 FIXED | `src/renderer/src/components/Bar.test.tsx` | FIXED | `src/main/screen-preprocess.test.ts` | FIXED | `src/main/brain/verified-numbers.test.ts` | FIXED | `src/main/win-security.test.ts` |# Métis Bug Ledger

The durable registry of defects found in QA. One row per defect, one id per defect, forever.

**This file is mechanically enforced by `npm run check:bugs` (`scripts/check-bug-ledger.mjs`).** The gate
fails the build if an entry marked `FIXED` does not name a regression test that exists *and* literally
contains its `MQA-###` id. That is the whole point: a fixed bug that regresses must break a test whose
name leads straight back to the row explaining what went wrong the first time. A prose bug list rots;
this one cannot.

## How to use it

1. **Found a defect?** Claim the next id, add a row with status `OPEN`, and write a `### MQA-###` detail
   section below with the concrete repro (inputs/state → wrong result) and both-sides citations
   (intended behavior quoted from a comment/doc/test, actual behavior at `file:line`).
2. **Fixing it?** Write the regression test *first* — it must fail before the fix and pass after — and
   put the bug id in the test's name or a comment beside it. Then flip the row to `FIXED` and name the
   test file in the Regression test column.
3. **Not fixing it?** `WONTFIX` (deliberate) or `ACCEPTED` (known, tracked in
   `docs/asktoto-hardening-backlog.md`) with the reason in the detail section. Never delete a row —
   deleting loses the memory this ledger exists to hold. Reusing an id is likewise forbidden.

Severity: `critical` = data loss / security / crash on a common path · `high` = core workflow broken or
silently wrong · `medium` = degraded or confusing in a real scenario · `low` = edge case.

## Details

> MQA-124 .. MQA-130 came from a 178-agent DEEP audit (2026-08-10): 36 Sonnet finders across 18 subsystems
> × 2 lenses, each finding adversarially verified by 2 independent skeptics. 56 findings were confirmed;
> the highest-value + all resilience-code regressions were fixed here, and the full triage (including
> deferred + false-positive findings) is recorded in `docs/qa/audit-2026-08-10.md`. The blocker (MQA-124)
> was a genuine privacy bypass in the resilience code shipped the day before.

> MQA-008 .. MQA-099 came from a 16-domain adversarial sweep (2026-08-08): 16 hunter agents, one per
> workflow domain, each finding independently attacked by a skeptic agent instructed to refute it.
> 101 candidate findings, 9 refuted, 92 confirmed. They are recorded here in full BEFORE being fixed,
> so the backlog is durable rather than living in a chat transcript.


### MQA-001 — DeepSeek shipped retired model ids as its defaults

**Intended.** `src/shared/providers.ts` documents `defaultModel`/`fastModel`/`thinkModel` as the ids the
app sends when the user has not overridden them, i.e. ids that must actually resolve at the provider.

**Actual.** The registry pinned `deepseek-chat` (default + fast) and `deepseek-reasoner` (think). DeepSeek
announced both for discontinuation on **2026-07-24** — a date already past — replacing them with the V4
generation (`deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`).

**Repro.** Configure DeepSeek with a valid API key and ask anything. Once the provider completes the
sunset, every request returns a model-not-found error. Worse for anyone who ever *picked* a model in
Settings: `providerModels.deepseek = 'deepseek-chat'` is persisted, and a persisted override beats every
registry default in `resolveModelTier` (`src/shared/providers.ts`), so updating the app alone would not
have healed those profiles. The user experiences this as "my API key stopped working" and re-enters a
perfectly valid key, which changes nothing.

**Fix.** Registry moved to `deepseek-v4-flash` (base) / `deepseek-v4-pro` (think + deep), DeepSeek
promoted to a `featured` tier provider. `migrateRetiredModelId`/`migrateRetiredModelMap` in
`src/shared/providers.ts` map the retired ids to V4 Flash — deliberately Flash, not Pro, since DeepSeek
documents both old ids as aliases for V4 Flash's non-thinking/thinking modes and promoting to Pro would
silently triple a user's token cost. `src/main/store.ts` `getSettings()` applies the migration on **read**,
so existing profiles heal without waiting for a settings save. `reasoningEffortFor()` keeps the base tier
at low effort because V4 defaults to thinking mode, which would otherwise blow the 15s live-suggest idle
budget in `askStart`.

### MQA-002 — Windows setup readiness was macOS-only

**Intended.** `src/main/index.ts` describes the upfront pass as "Front-load the OS permission prompts
during onboarding … so the first real meeting isn't interrupted by them", and `platform-perms.ts` opens
with "macOS needs Screen Recording + Mic permissions. Windows needs Mic permission".

**Actual.** `permissionsRequestUpfront` was wrapped entirely in `if (process.platform === 'darwin')`, so
on Windows it did nothing at all. `windowsScreenStatus()` returned a hardcoded `'unknown'`, so no code
path could ever establish whether screen capture worked on Windows.

**Repro.** Install on Windows, complete onboarding, ask a screenshot question in the first meeting. If
capture is blocked by the graphics-capture privacy setting, the failure surfaces mid-meeting — the setup
checklist reported `screenRecording: 'unknown'` throughout and could not warn. Confirmed live: the QA
suite's boot group observed `{"mic":"granted","screen":"unknown"}` on Windows.

**Fix.** `probeScreenCapture()` performs a 1px `desktopCapturer` capture and records the outcome as real
evidence; `windowsScreenStatus()` returns that instead of a constant. The probe runs at boot on Windows
(where it raises **no** prompt) and stays inside onboarding on macOS (where it *does* raise the TCC
prompt and needs explaining first). `permissionsRequestUpfront` now has a win32 branch. macOS still
treats TCC as authoritative and consults probe evidence only when TCC is undecided.

### MQA-003 — a dead provider is retried first on every ask (no circuit breaker)

**Intended.** `src/main/index.ts` justifies capping same-provider retries when a failover target exists
so "the API answers in seconds instead of after the full ~30s of retrying a dead primary" — i.e. the
design explicitly values not burning the user's time on a provider that cannot answer.

**Actual.** Nothing remembers that a provider just failed. `pickPrimaryProvider` selects the configured
provider again on the very next ask, so every request re-pays the dead provider's round trip.

**Repro (measured, not theoretical).** With a revoked DeepSeek key configured, three consecutive suggest
asks each produced the walk `["deepseek","nvidia","local"]`, costing 6.5s / 9.3s / 9.2s before the local
model answered. Live suggestions have a 15s idle budget, so on a slower network this alone can exhaust
it — the user sees "no suggestion" rather than a fast local one.

**Suggested fix.** A short in-memory per-provider cooldown (e.g. skip a provider for N minutes after M
consecutive pre-token auth failures), cleared whenever its key changes or the app restarts. Must not
persist to disk — a provider outage should not outlive the session.

### MQA-004 — nothing ever marks a provider whose key died as not-ready

**Intended.** `publicSettings()` documents `providerReady` as "Active provider is usable: key present AND
any provider-specific setup done … Drives the add-key CTA so it only shows when the app genuinely can't
answer yet."

**Actual.** `providerReady` is derived purely from a key *string existing* (`hasApiKey`), never from
whether that key *works*. No failure counter, no health state, nothing downgrades it.

**Repro (measured).** With a revoked DeepSeek key that had just 401'd on three consecutive asks, the
settings snapshot still reported `providerReady: true`. The user is told everything is fine while every
cloud ask silently degrades to the on-device model, and there is no banner, badge, or CTA pointing at
the real problem. `testApiKey` *does* correctly reject the dead key (`401 … your api key … is invalid`),
so the detection capability exists — it is simply never invoked automatically.

**Suggested fix.** Track consecutive pre-token auth failures per provider; after a threshold, surface a
dismissible "Your <provider> key stopped working — re-enter it" banner deep-linking to Settings → AI,
and reflect it in `providerReady`. Pairs naturally with the MQA-003 cooldown (same signal drives both).

### MQA-005 — raw provider error text reaches the user

**Intended.** `askStart`'s error path replaces transport strings with clean copy — "Replace raw client
transport strings … with a clean message" — and the no-key path produces the well-formed
"No API key for Claude · Anthropic. Open Settings (gear) and add it."

**Actual.** A non-transient, non-Dust-auth failure falls through to `: message`, passing the provider's
raw string straight to the UI.

**Repro (measured).** Dead DeepSeek + dead NVIDIA keys with the local fallback disabled produced exactly
`403 status code (no body)` in the renderer. That tells the user nothing about what to do.

**Suggested fix.** Map auth-shaped failures (401/403/402, "invalid api key", "insufficient credit") to an
actionable message naming the provider and pointing at Settings, the same way the no-key path already does.

### MQA-006 — the first on-device answer after launch times out

**Intended.** Métis Local exists so that "a zero-API-key install still gets a working assistant"
(`src/shared/ipc.ts`, `localLlm.fallback`). `local-routing.ts` describes prewarm as warming the sidecar
so a real suggest does not pay the spin-up.

**Actual.** `localPrewarmEligible` required `useFor.suggest`, which now defaults to **false** (it must, or
local would preempt a configured cloud provider — see the non-preemption contract). So on exactly the
install this feature targets, prewarm never ran, the sidecar was always cold when the fallback finally
routed to it, and a cold ~730 MB GGUF load routinely exceeds `askStart`'s 15s suggest idle budget.

**Repro (measured, physical).** Fresh profile, zero API keys, `scripts/qa/e2e-workflows.mjs --only=ask`
immediately after launch: `suggest answers on-device with zero API keys configured` failed with
`Stream timed out — no response from the model.` The same check passed on a warm run — this is a
first-use-only failure, i.e. precisely a new user's first impression. It was introduced by the
`useFor`-defaults-off change and is therefore a regression of that change, caught by physical QA rather
than by any unit test.

**Fix.** Two complementary changes. (1) `localPrewarmEligible` gained a `cloudReady` argument and now
also engages when the fallback is armed and **no** cloud/CLI provider is ready — local is then the likely
server, so warming it is justified; with a healthy cloud provider configured the gate stays false and no
sidecar is spawned for its standing RAM cost. (2) `askStart` applies a 90s idle floor when routing to
local while the sidecar is not yet running, so a legitimate cold load is never mistaken for a hang. Once
warm, local keeps the normal tighter budgets.

### MQA-007 — suite flakiness under heavy parallel load

**Intended.** A green suite should mean the code is correct; a run's result should not depend on what
else the machine is doing.

**Actual.** With ~16 concurrent vitest processes running (a multi-agent QA sweep), individual runs failed
non-deterministically in `src/main/brain/corrections.test.ts` with
`ENOENT: … rename '….brain\index.json.<hash>.tmp' -> '….brain\index.json'` — the tmp+rename durability
path racing its own teardown. Different runs of identical code failed different tests.

**Evidence both ways.** Three consecutive full runs of the same tree gave 1 failure, 4 failures, then
**0 failures / 1925 passed / `success: true`**. Isolated runs of the implicated files pass consistently.
So this is a test-harness race under abnormal load, not a product defect — but it is exactly the kind of
flake that erodes trust in the gate, and this repo has a documented history of teardown races masking
real failures.

**Not fixed (2026-08-08).** Left OPEN deliberately rather than papered over: the honest fix is to make the brain
tests' temp-profile teardown await in-flight index writes (an exported settle hook already exists,
`whenIndexWritesSettle`), which is a focused change that deserves its own pass rather than being bundled
into a QA sweep. CI runs a single suite at a time and is unaffected today.

**FIXED (2026-08-17).** Three real test defects, found by reproducing the condition rather than reasoning about it — 8 then 16 concurrent `vitest run src/main/brain/` processes, which failed 8/8 before any change.

1. **A shared fixed path.** `corrections.test.ts`'s path-traversal case wrote its decoy to `join(folder, '..', 'evil.json')`. One level above a `mkdtemp` profile is the shared OS temp root, so that is the SAME file in every concurrent vitest process — each one's `finally` rmSync deleted the others' decoy and whoever read it next failed with ENOENT. Now named after the run's own profile dir. A test that fails because another test run exists is the purest form of this row.
2. **Teardown racing an in-flight index write.** Every brain suite that can queue an `updateIndex` now awaits `whenIndexWritesSettle()` before `rmSync`-ing the profile — the hook the ledger itself pointed at, which already existed and had no caller in half the files. This is the tmp+rename ENOENT the original evidence names.
3. **`running: false` is not "writes are done".** `waitForIdle` in four suites waited on `brainBackfillProgress().running` and then read index.json, which `whenIndexWritesSettle`'s own doc comment says is exactly wrong: the last job's record is still queued on the serialized lane at that moment. Under load the window widens enough to lose. All idle waits now settle.

Plus the timing class, which is not a defect but does decide the verdict: vitest's 5s test default and 1s `vi.waitFor` default are sized for in-memory unit tests, while a large part of this suite stands up a real temp profile and drives the production tmp+rename path on a Windows checkout under OneDrive/AV. `testTimeout`/`hookTimeout` are 30s, every `vi.waitFor` carries an explicit 10s, and the one genuine outlier (`brain.test.ts`'s 6-permutation determinism proof, 18 full ingest round trips) carries 90s. None of this weakens the gate: a hung test still fails, just later. Two tests over live OS facilities also needed the same honesty — the MQA-028 memo burst now freezes the clock (it must prove memoization, not that the machine is fast, and the memo TTL is a deliberate 5s security bound), and the MQA-008 live ACL probe retries with backoff.

**Verified, not asserted.** 16/16 concurrent brain suites green (the condition this row documents; 8/8 failed before). 6/6 concurrent FULL suites green. 10/10 concurrent full suites reaches 8-9 green.

**Known residual, deliberately not "fixed":** at 10 concurrent full suites the live ACL probe in `win-security.test.ts` can still return null. Its cause is not a race — `readAcl` spawns `powershell.exe` under a **production** 8s `execFileSync` cap, and on a machine running ten full suites PowerShell cannot finish starting inside it, so retries cannot help. The two ways to make it green would be to lower a security-relevant production timeout to suit a test machine, or to let the test accept a null probe — which is precisely the evidence MQA-008 exists to demand. Neither is worth it; the honest statement is that this one assertion needs a machine that can start PowerShell in 8s.

### MQA-001 (continued)

**Not verified.** The exact live behavior of `reasoning_effort` on DeepSeek V4 (whether `low` fully
suppresses thinking, vs. the separate documented `thinking: {type}` parameter) has **not** been confirmed
against the live API — no DeepSeek key was available. `openai.ts`'s param-rejection retry means a
rejected `reasoning_effort` degrades safely rather than failing the request, but latency on the base tier
should be measured with a real key before relying on DeepSeek for live suggestions.

### MQA-008 — Windows machine managed-config is NEVER trusted: Get-Acl's .Owner is a String, so SidOf() returns null and evaluateAclTrust always fails

**Where.** `src/main/win-security.ts:96` · workflow: Enterprise policy enforcement on Windows (requireAuth / allowedProviders / lockedKeys / managed defaults / disableAutoUpdate kill-switch) · fix size: small

**Intended.** win-security.ts:141-143 — "* - win32: yes only if the file is owned by SYSTEM/Administrators/TrustedInstaller AND no broad\n *   non-admin principal (Users, Authenticated Users, Everyone, Domain Users…) has a write ACE." Locked by src/main/win-security.test.ts:44-54: `it('trusts a SYSTEM-owned policy whose only write ACEs are admin principals', () => { ... expect(evaluateAclTrust(acl)).toBe(true) })`. docs/ENTERPRISE-DEPLOY-WINDOWS.md:80 — "On Windows the machine-level file is only honored when its ACL is admin-owned".

**Actual.** src/main/win-security.ts:96 builds the probe as `$out = [ordered]@{ owner = (SidOf $a.Owner); aces = @() }`, but `Get-Acl` returns `FileSecurity` whose `.Owner` is a `System.String`, not an `IdentityReference`. `SidOf` (line 95) calls `$ref.Translate(...)` → RuntimeException → catch → `$ref.Value` on a String → `$null`. The probe therefore always emits `"owner":null`; win-security.ts:112 coerces it to `''`; evaluateAclTrust (line 82) does `ADMIN_OWNER_SIDS.has('')` → false. `isAdminManagedTrusted()` and `readTrustedAdminManaged()` return false/null for EVERY file on win32, including a correctly SYSTEM-owned GPO/Intune-deployed policy. The ACE SIDs translate fine (they are NTAccount objects) — only the owner is broken, so the failure is invisible in the ACE-focused tests.

**Repro.** Verified on this Windows 11 host. Running the exact readAcl PowerShell block from win-security.ts:91-101 against D:\Asktoto\package.json returns `{"owner":null,"aces":[{"sid":"S-1-5-32-544",...},{"sid":"S-1-5-18",...},...]}`. Direct type probe: `Get-Acl -LiteralPath 'D:\Asktoto\package.json'` → `Owner value: DESKTOP-IK7QQ0E\Tony`, `Owner type : System.String`, `Ace0 type : System.Security.Principal.NTAccount`, and `$a.Owner.Translate([SecurityIdentifier])` → `THREW: RuntimeException -> fallback .Value = []`. Consequence chain: deploy `%ProgramData%\Métis\managed-config.json` as SYSTEM with a Users:Read-only ACL (the documented IT deployment) containing `{"requireAuth":true,"allowedProviders":["anthropic"],"disableAutoUpdate":true}` → auth.ts:606 gets null (SSO never forced), store.ts:210 gets null (provider allowlist never applied — Kimi/Dust egress is not blocked), store.ts:186/197 get null (locked keys and managed defaults never applied), updater.ts:26 `autoUpdateDisabledByPolicy()` returns false (fleet version freeze never takes effect). The only visible signal is one warn line per process from warnUntrusted (win-security.ts:132) telling IT their correctly-deployed file is "not admin-owned".

**Suggested fix.** In readAcl's PowerShell, resolve the owner through the ACL object rather than the string NoteProperty: `$ownerSid = $a.GetOwner([System.Security.Principal.SecurityIdentifier]).Value` (with a fallback to `(New-Object System.Security.Principal.NTAccount($a.Owner)).Translate([System.Security.Principal.SecurityIdentifier]).Value`). Then add the missing positive-direction coverage: a win32 test that builds a SYSTEM-owned file (or injects a fake readAcl) and asserts isAdminManagedTrusted() === true — today every real-PowerShell test only asserts the reject direction, which is why this is green.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; reproduced the full chain independently on this Windows host.

TYPE CLAIM CONFIRMED: src/main/win-security.ts:96 does `owner = (SidOf $a.Owner)`, but Get-Acl returns System.Security.AccessControl.FileSecurity whose `.Owner` is a System.String (PowerShell ETS CodeProperty), not an IdentityReference. Live probe (pinned interpreter, PS 5.1.26100.7019): `Owner type : System.String`, `Owner.Translate THREW: RuntimeException`, `.Value is null? True`. SidOf (line 95) therefore returns $null.

PROBE ALWAYS EMITS owner:null, INCLUDING FOR ADMIN-OWNED FILES: running the exact block from win-security.ts:91-101 gave `{"owner":null,...}` for C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe (owner NT SERVICE\TrustedInstaller), C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts (owner BUILTIN\Administrators), and C:\ProgramData (owner NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM). ACE SIDs translate fine (S-1-5-18, S-1-5-32-544, S-1-5-32-545) because IdentityReference is an NTAccount — only the owner is broken, exactly as claimed. Chain: win-security.ts:112 `String(parsed.owner || '')` -> '', evaluateAclTrust:82 `ADMIN_OWNER_SIDS.has('')` -> false.

DECISIVE END-TO-END PROOF ON THE UNMODIFIED MODULE (no repo edits): drove the real module via node --experimental-strip-types against C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts — `isAdminManagedTrusted(hosts) = false`, `readTrustedAdminManaged(hosts)` = null. That file's probed ACL is owner=Administrators with write ACEs only S-1-5-18 and S-1-5-32-544 (Users and AppContainer entries are 0x1200A9, zero overlap with WRITE_MASK 0x500D0116), i.e. structurally the ACL that win-security.test.ts:44-57 asserts must be true. Root cause pinned by differential: `$a.GetOwner([SecurityIdentifier]).Value` -> S-1-5-32-544 and `([NTAccount]$a.Owner).Translate([SecurityIdentifier]).Value` -> S-1-5-32-544, while the shipped form -> empty.

REFUTATIONS ATTEMPTED AND FAILED:
- Guard/caller fallback? None. All consumers route through readTrustedAdminManaged(): updater.ts:26 (no fallback at all — disableAutoUpdate fleet freeze fully dead), transcripts.ts:96 (per-user tier "deliberately NOT consulted", comment at :88 — escrow pubkey dead), store.ts:186/197 (machine tier dead), store.ts:210-211 (falls back only to the per-user userData file, never the machine path), auth.ts:606 (per-user fallback at :612 only). No registry/GPO alternate path exists (grep for HKLM/registry/Policies in src/main found nothing).
- Test already covers it? No. `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/win-security.test.ts` -> 16 passed. The live win32 describe (win-security.test.ts:177-206) asserts only rejection, which passes vacuously when owner is always ''. The positive case (44-54) feeds a hand-built AclProbe straight into evaluateAclTrust, bypassing readAcl.
- "Intended behavior" quote accurate? Yes — win-security.ts:141-143 and docs/ENTERPRISE-DEPLOY-WINDOWS.md:80 ("On Windows the machine-level file is only honored when its ACL is admin-owned").
- Already fixed in tree / unreachable path? No — win-security.ts is unmodified in the working tree, and the win32 branch is the production path on Windows.

SEVERITY: keeping critical, with one framing correction — it fails CLOSED against forgery (a standard user still cannot plant policy), so this is not privilege escalation. Criticality is that the entire documented Windows enterprise control plane is 100% inert on every Windows deployment: requireAuth (auth.ts:606), allowedProviders egress allowlist (store.ts:210), lockedKeys/managed defaults (store.ts:186/197), transcript escrow pubkey (transcripts.ts:96), and the disableAutoUpdate kill-switch (updater.ts:26) — the last two with no fallback tier at all. The only signal is warnUntrusted (win-security.ts:132) telling IT their correctly SYSTEM-owned GPO/Intune file is "not admin-owned", which guarantees misdiagnosis.

FIX: one PowerShell expression (use `$a.GetOwner([System.Security.Principal.SecurityIdentifier]).Value`, or cast `[NTAccount]$a.Owner` before Translate; keep SidOf for the ACE path). Sized "small" rather than "trivial" because the regression test that would have caught it needs a non-elevated positive case — e.g. probing a known Administrators-owned system file such as the hosts file, as done here.

### MQA-009 — Fact-check-on-screen sends the model ZERO screen data — the screenContext injector is nested inside the `kind !== 'factcheck'` gate

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:2749` · workflow: Fact-check what's on my screen (the Fact-check quick action with an empty input box and no live transcript) · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:2745-2748 — "Screen fast-path (M13): the renderer asked to answer from the pre-analyzed on-device screen context. Inject main's OWN cached description (re-validated for freshness/window match), plus a short recent-conversation tail so the answer fuses what's on screen with what's being said." The factcheck exclusion one block above is scoped ONLY to brainContext and says why: src/main/index.ts:2735-2737 — "Excludes fact-check (mode:'answer', kind:'factcheck'): personas.ts strips GROUNDING_RAIL for it (its contract is a VERDICT-only response), so injecting brainContext here would add citable material with no citation/anti-fabrication guardrail attached — gate identically to the rail." The screen block carries its OWN untrusted-data guard (src/main/llm/shared.ts:151-157 screenContextBlock), so the GROUNDING_RAIL rationale does not apply to it.

**Actual.** The `if (req.wantsScreenContext)` injector (src/main/index.ts:2749-2762) is nested INSIDE the gate opened at src/main/index.ts:2738 `if (req.mode === 'answer' && req.kind !== 'factcheck') {`. For a factcheck request the gate is false, so the injector never runs and `req.screenContext` stays `undefined` from the unconditional clear at src/main/index.ts:2725. These are the only two `req.screenContext` assignments in the whole main process (verified by grep).

**Repro.** Settings: enable background screen context (`backgroundScreenContext`) with Métis Local provisioned, and configure any cloud provider so `providerReady` is true. Not in a meeting, chat input empty. Click Fact-check -> chooseQuickActionRoute returns transport 'screen' (src/shared/quick-actions.ts:133-136) -> App.tsx:1081-1086 calls askScreen(FACT_CHECK_SCREEN_PROMPT, { kind: 'factcheck', label: 'Claims on your screen' }) -> the fast path at App.tsx:841-852 gets a fresh on-device description and fires `ask.run({ mode:'answer', kind:'factcheck', wantsScreenContext:true })`. Main skips the injector, so the provider receives ONLY the prompt text "Fact-check the most prominent claim visible on my screen…" (src/shared/quick-actions.ts:39-42) with no description of the screen at all. Result: a verdict card labelled "Claims on your screen" that is either a hallucinated verdict about a screen the model never saw, or "I can't see your screen" — while the non-fast path (background screen context OFF) captures a real screenshot and works correctly.

**Suggested fix.** Move the `if (req.wantsScreenContext) { … }` block out of the `req.kind !== 'factcheck'` gate — e.g. keep the brainContext assembly under `req.mode === 'answer' && req.kind !== 'factcheck'`, and run the screen injection under a sibling `if (req.mode === 'answer' && req.wantsScreenContext)`. Alternatively make askScreen skip the fast path for `kind === 'factcheck'` so it always captures a real image; the first fix is better since the fast path exists to avoid the upload.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED. Structure verified at current HEAD (finder's line numbers are ~15 low but the code matches): src/main/index.ts:2751 unconditionally clears `req.screenContext`; src/main/index.ts:2764 opens `if (req.mode === 'answer' && req.kind !== 'factcheck') {`; the screen injector `if (req.wantsScreenContext) {` sits at 2775-2792 INSIDE that gate, closed by the outer `}` at 2793. Grep confirms 2751 and 2785 are the only two `req.screenContext` writes in the whole main process, and `wantsScreenContext` appears nowhere else in main.

The "intended behavior" quote checks out: the exclusion comment at 2761-2763 justifies the factcheck gate purely by GROUNDING_RAIL/brainContext ("personas.ts strips GROUNDING_RAIL for it ... injecting brainContext here would add citable material with no citation guardrail"), and the screen block carries its own untrusted-data guard at src/main/llm/shared.ts:151-157. Git archaeology proves the coupling is accidental: at 4b2a98a~1 the injector was already nested inside a plain `if (req.mode === 'answer') {` (rev lines 2447-2476), and commit 4b2a98a ("fix(r3) 35 a11y/UX bugs") changed only the condition to add `&& req.kind !== 'factcheck'` for the brainContext reason, sweeping the screen injector in.

Refutation attempts all failed: (1) no other injector — `req.screenContext` is consumed only at src/main/llm/shared.ts:143 in userText's answer branch, and src/main/personas.ts:98-116 only REMOVES material for kind==='factcheck'; (2) the renderer does not compensate — App.tsx:841-843 uses the probed ctx solely for setScreenCapturedAt, state.ts:407-420 forwards the boolean only; (3) the route is reachable — src/shared/quick-actions.ts:133-136 returns transport 'screen' for factcheck with empty input+transcript, App.tsx:1080-1088 calls askScreen(FACT_CHECK_SCREEN_PROMPT, {kind:'factcheck'}), the fast path at App.tsx:844-852 fires mode:'answer'+kind:'factcheck'+wantsScreenContext:true, and the schema preserves both fields (src/shared/ipc.ts:579, 600); (4) no test guards it — ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/local-cloud-boundary.contract.test.ts src/main/llm/shared.test.ts src/shared/ipc.test.ts: 71 passed WITH the bug present; the contract test (local-cloud-boundary.contract.test.ts:29-46) only asserts redaction inside the block.

Two aggravators the finder missed: src/main/cahe-embedded-key.ts:54 seeds `backgroundScreenContext: true` once per profile for the entire Cahê edition, so the broken fast path is the default there (not merely opt-in; DEFAULT_SETTINGS has it false at src/shared/ipc.ts:801/1128). And src/renderer/src/state.ts:403 sets `usedScreen: !!req.wantsScreenContext`, which drives the "Viewed screen" trust badge at src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:129-153 — the UI asserts the model saw a screen it got zero data about. Mitigating: EPISTEMIC_HUMILITY_LINE (src/shared/quick-actions.ts:26-27) makes VERDICT: UNVERIFIABLE more likely than a fabricated verdict, so it is a dead feature plus false trust signal rather than confident hallucination. Severity high stands. Fix is a dedent of the wantsScreenContext block to sibling scope of the brainContext gate.

### MQA-010 — buildBrainContext reads and Zod-parses EVERY person/account/deal file off disk on every answer-mode ask, synchronously on the main process

**Where.** `src/main/brain/context.ts:139` · workflow: Ask a question (every typed question, screen fast-path ask, Spotlight Ref, follow-up — any mode:'answer' request) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/brain/context.ts:14-18 — "Relevance is entity-name matching against the question text. It is deliberately cheap: we match the ENTITY SLUG (already the name reduced to lowercase hyphen-joined tokens) against the same-normalized question tokens, so only the handful of entities the user actually named get read off disk. This runs once per user question on the answer path — never per keystroke — and is bounded hard on entity count and total size so it can never balloon the prompt or the latency." Reinforced at the call site, src/main/index.ts:2734 — "Best-effort: a brain read must never block an answer."

**Actual.** src/main/brain/context.ts:138-156 reads first and filters second: `listEntities(s,'person').map((slug) => readPerson(s, slug)).filter((p) => … matchesEntity(p.id, p.aliases, hay)).slice(0, MAX_PEOPLE)` — and identically for accounts (147) and deals (153). `readPerson`/`readAccount`/`readDeal` (src/main/brain/store.ts:418-431) go through `readJson` (store.ts:214-237), which does a `statSync` + `readSavedFile` + `JSON.parse` + Zod `parse` per file. The whole thing runs inside the synchronous `ipcMain.handle(IPC.askStart, (e, raw) => {…})` body (src/main/index.ts:2740), before `createStream` is ever reached, so it blocks the Electron main-process event loop. `brainDir` is `<meetingsFolder>/.brain` (src/main/brain/store.ts:32-34) — i.e. the OneDrive-synced meetings folder by default.

**Repro.** A user with a year of indexed meetings has ~400 `.brain/entities/person/*.json`, ~120 account and ~80 deal files. They type "what's the weather in Paris" (names no entity). `tokenString` is non-empty so the early return at context.ts:134 does not fire; the function then stats+reads+parses ~600 JSON files and returns `{ block:'', matched:false }` — zero of them matched. On a OneDrive Files-On-Demand `.brain`, each cold file's `readFileSync` blocks on a network hydration, so the overlay freezes (no drag, no tray, no other IPC) and that time is added to TTFT before the request is even sent. The `jsonCache` does not save it: `statSync` still hits the filesystem for every file each ask, and once `jsonCache.size >= 2000` the cache is flushed wholesale with `jsonCache.clear()` (store.ts:234), so a brain larger than the cache re-reads everything on every ask.

**Suggested fix.** Filter on the slug BEFORE touching disk, exactly as the doc describes: `listEntities(s,'person').filter((slug) => slugInText(slug, hay)).slice(0, MAX_PEOPLE).map((slug) => readPerson(s, slug)).filter(Boolean)`. To keep the alias half of `matchesEntity`, maintain a small alias->slug map in the brain index (written at ingest time) and consult that instead of opening every entity file. Failing that, move the assembly off the synchronous IPC handler.

**Verifier.** SURVIVES. I tried to kill this four ways and could not.

1) The code shape is exactly as claimed. `src/main/brain/context.ts:138-141` is `listEntities(s,'person').map((slug) => readPerson(s, slug)).filter((p) => !!p && matchesEntity(p.id, p.aliases, hay)).slice(0, MAX_PEOPLE)` — map (read) BEFORE filter, and `.slice()` after the read, so the MAX_* constants bound the output lines, not the number of files opened. Identical at :146-149 (accounts) and :152-156 (deals). `readPerson`/`readAccount`/`readDeal` (store.ts:418-433) each go through `readJson` (store.ts:214-237): `statSync` + `readSavedFile` (a plain `readFileSync` + decrypt, transcripts.ts:261-263) + `JSON.parse` + Zod `.parse` + a migrate pass. No guard, no early exit, no cap on N.

2) The "intended behavior" quote is not just accurate — it is provably the prior implementation. `git show e656201:src/main/brain/context.ts` (the original Receipt Mode commit) reads `.filter((slug) => slugInText(slug, hay)).slice(0, MAX_PEOPLE).map((slug) => readPerson(s, slug))` — filter-then-read, exactly what the doc comment at context.ts:14-18 describes ("only the handful of entities the user actually named get read off disk... bounded hard on entity count"). Commit `1fd6c7c feat(brain): graphify inheritance + alias-expanded retrieval (MI-5)` inverted it to read-then-filter to gain `aliases[]` matching (aliases only exist inside the entity file) and left the doc comment untouched. This is a documented-invariant regression with clean git provenance, not a misread comment.

3) It really is synchronous on the main process. `ipcMain.handle(IPC.askStart, (e, raw) => {` (index.ts:2712) is a non-async arrow; `buildBrainContext` is called at index.ts:2766 inside that body, gated only by `req.mode === 'answer' && req.kind !== 'factcheck'` (index.ts:2764). No settings gate exists at all (grep for brainEnabled/meetingBrain: zero hits), so it fires on every answer-mode ask before any streaming starts.

4) Refutation attempts that failed:
- No pre-warm. I checked the frequent poller: `brainStatusCounts` (index.ts:379-393) only does `listBrainEntities(...).length` (a readdir) and is revision-cached — it never reads entity files, so it does not populate `jsonCache`. `brainRead` (index.ts:3307) does read them all but only while BrainView is open. So for a user who never opens the brain view, the first ask after every app launch is a fully cold read+decrypt+parse of every person/account/deal file.
- No cheap alias index exists to make this avoidable today: `readAliasMap` (corrections.ts:628) delegates to `readEntityAliasMap` (corrections.ts:505-531), which itself iterates `listEntities` and reads every entity file.
- The OneDrive framing checks out: `brainDir` = `<meetingsFolder>/.brain` (store.ts:32-34) and `resolveMeetingsFolder` defaults to `detectOneDrive() || app.getPath('documents')` (transcripts.ts:515-529), so on the default Windows install `.brain` sits in a cloud-synced folder with Files-On-Demand on.
- Tests do not cover it and do not block the fix, but they do constrain it: `src/main/brain/brain.test.ts:255-272` writes a person with `aliases: ['Acme Corp']` directly to disk (no journal entry) and asserts the alias matches, so a naive revert to slug-only pre-filtering would fail it. Ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/brain.test.ts` — 56/56 pass, confirming current behavior.

Severity kept at high, but two parts of the repro are overstated and I want that on record: `jsonCache` does blunt the steady state to an N-times-`statSync` storm rather than N full parses (the finder concedes the stat cost but implies re-parsing every ask), and the `jsonCache.clear()` at store.ts:234 needs >2000 cached brain paths, which ~600 entities plus ~250 meeting extractions would not reach. High still holds because it is the app's hottest path (every question), it blocks the Electron main-process event loop, the read count is genuinely unbounded and grows with usage, at-rest encryption adds a decrypt per file, and the cold-cache full read is guaranteed once per app launch on a OneDrive-backed folder — all against a comment that explicitly promises the opposite.

Fix: restore filter-before-read (derive candidate slugs from the question's token n-grams and intersect with `listEntities`, or re-apply `slugInText(slug, hay)` before `.map`), then recover alias matching from a cheap source — `aliasMapFromJournal(readCorrectionsJournal(s))` is one file read — or a small persisted alias index written on entity write. Contained to `buildBrainContext`, though the brain.test.ts:255 case (aliases on the file with no journal entry) means a journal-only fix needs an accompanying index or test change, which is what keeps this small rather than trivial.

### MQA-011 — A 'them' channel that goes silent without ending its track is never detected or recovered — the watchdog is permanently disarmed after the first window

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts:942` · workflow: Live meeting capture — keeping the remote (system-audio) side alive across a mid-meeting audio-device change · fix size: small

**Intended.** listen.ts:801-803 — "Both sides now surface a \"reconnecting…\" note and re-acquire automatically — mic via recoverMicRef, system audio via recoverSystemAudioRef (which re-runs the programmatic arm-dance getDisplayMedia; no user gesture is needed, so a blip no longer forces a \"Toggle Listen\" restart)." and listen.ts:936-938 — "A Bluetooth switch often leaves the old track \"alive\" but permanently silent (no 'ended' event) — the classic silent death."

**Actual.** The `devicechange` handler that exists specifically for the no-'ended' silent death covers only the microphone: listen.ts:942 `if (!liveRef.current || !channels.current.you) return` and listen.ts:946 `void recoverMicRef.current?.()`. There is no equivalent for 'them'. The only other 'them' detector, `armThemWatchdog`, self-disables forever after the first window: listen.ts:723-725 `if (themWatchdogRef.current) clearTimeout(...); if (themHeardRef.current) return`, and `themHeardRef` is set true on the first 'them' emission at listen.ts:772-773 and is only reset inside `openChannel` for a NEW 'them' channel (listen.ts:833).

**Repro.** Windows or macOS, audioSource 'both'. Meeting starts, the other side is audible → `themHeardRef=true`, the 20 s watchdog is cleared (listen.ts:774-777). 25 minutes in, plug in USB/Bluetooth headphones so the OS default render endpoint changes; the loopback capture keeps `readyState==='live'` but delivers silence (the exact mode listen.ts:936-938 names). `devicechange` fires → listen.ts:942 sees `channels.current.you` and re-acquires only the mic. `onended` never fires, so `recoverSystemAudioRef` is never called; `armThemWatchdog` is never called again and would no-op anyway. Result: every remaining minute of the meeting has zero THEM lines, `captureDegraded` stays null, the Bar keeps showing the healthy 'Heard live' chip and the red rec-dot — the exact failure the CaptureDegraded doc block (listen.ts:141-147, the 2026-07-20 incident) exists to prevent.

**Suggested fix.** (a) In `onDeviceChange`, also re-check the them side: if `wantsSystemRef.current` and either no 'them' channel exists or no 'them' window has arrived in the last N seconds, call `recoverSystemAudioRef.current?.()`. (b) Replace the one-shot `themHeardRef` latch with a rolling last-'them'-window timestamp so the watchdog can re-fire (set THEM_SILENT_MSG + captureDegraded) after N seconds of silence at any point in the meeting, not only before the first window.

**Verifier.** Could not refute it; every cited line checks out and no other code path covers the case.

CONFIRMED CHAIN:
1. src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts:940-954 — the devicechange effect is mic-only: :942 `if (!liveRef.current || !channels.current.you) return` and :946 `void recoverMicRef.current?.()`. There is no 'them' branch. `grep -rn devicechange src/` returns only this listener plus an unrelated device-list refresh at Settings.tsx:3336.
2. listen.ts:723-731 — `armThemWatchdog` returns early at :725 when `themHeardRef.current` is true. `themHeardRef` flips true on the first 'them' emission (:772-773) and is reset to false in exactly one place, `openChannel` for a NEW 'them' channel (:833). Its only call sites are :834 (openChannel) and :1366 (resume); resume's own comment at :1364-1365 admits it is a no-op once audio was already heard. So after the first them window the watchdog is permanently disarmed for the life of that channel.
3. No alternate detector exists. `recoverSystemAudioRef` self-blocks on a still-registered channel (listen.ts:884 `if (channels.current.them) return`), so a zombie 'them' channel can never be recovered through it. The permission-poll watcher (listen.ts:962-982) is skipped entirely on Windows (`if (isWindows || !state.listening || !wantsSystemRef.current) return`) and also early-returns on `channels.current.them || sysRecoveringRef.current` — so the zombie channel blocks it on macOS as well. The only route to `recoverSystemAudioRef` from a live session is the `onended` handler (listen.ts:804-816), which by hypothesis never fires. Main process (src/main/index.ts:4100-4137) only returns `audio: 'loopback'`; no device-follow/re-bind logic. No heartbeat or global silence check exists — `parakeetEmptyRunRef` counts empty ASR returns on flowing audio, and a silent worklet emits no windows at all (VAD-gated), so nothing increments.
4. Result: `captureDegraded` stays null, so Bar.tsx:439-456 keeps showing the "Heard live" chip and ControlPill keeps the confident red dot — the exact false-health state the CaptureDegraded doc block (listen.ts:141-147, the 2026-07-20 incident) was written to prevent.
5. No test guards this. Ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/lib/listen.test.ts src/renderer/src/App.mic-only-visibility.test.ts` — 16/16 pass, but they only cover isQuestion/looksLikeNetworkError and source-text anchors for the captureDegraded UI; nothing exercises a mid-session 'them' silence.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED: (a) recoverMic does not touch 'them'; (b) the macOS permission watcher is gated out by the registered channel; (c) start()/resume() do not reset themHeardRef; (d) main-process loopback handler has no endpoint-change handling.

PARTIAL CORRECTION TO THE FINDER: the listen.ts:936-938 comment is quoted verbatim but self-scopes to "the default input … while the mic channel is live" — it does not itself promise a them-side equivalent, so the "intended behavior" framing leans on the broader CaptureDegraded contract at :141-147 rather than on a direct promise. Also, the repro is strongest on Windows (the old WASAPI render endpoint stays valid after a default-output change, so loopback keeps delivering zero-filled buffers with no error and no 'ended'); on macOS ScreenCaptureKit taps the system mix rather than an endpoint, so the device-swap trigger is less certain there. Neither weakens the code-level gap: any 'them' silence without an 'ended' event is undetected and unrecoverable for the rest of the session.

SEVERITY: high stands — silent, total loss of the remote side of a meeting transcript while the UI actively asserts health is the same incident class the file documents. FIX COMPLEXITY: small — either add a 'them' arm to the devicechange handler (recycle via closeChannel('them') + recoverSystemAudio) or make the watchdog rolling (re-arm on each window instead of one-shot); the only care needed is avoiding a gratuitous macOS SCStream restart on every device blip.

### MQA-012 — 'auto' spoken language: the Parakeet probe retires permanently after 5 windows, so a non-English meeting whose opening lines are short is transcribed in English for its entire duration

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts:537` · workflow: Live transcription of a non-English meeting with Settings → Audio → Spoken language = 'auto' (the shipped default) · fix size: small

**Intended.** listen.ts:34 — "const PROBE_WINDOW_BUDGET = 5 // give up pinning off the opening windows after this many and stay 'auto'", together with whisper.worker.ts:49-50 — "In 'auto' mode the same machinery CONVERGES onto the conversation's language, giving pin-quality decoding without a setting."

**Actual.** listen.ts:537 `const due = probePinnedRef.current ? n % PROBE_EVERY === 0 : n <= PROBE_WINDOW_BUDGET` — once `n > 5` with `probePinnedRef` still false, `due` is false for every remaining window of the meeting, so no further `pinLanguage` message can ever be produced. Each of those 5 slots is consumed at dispatch time (listen.ts:535-538) but is then thrown away by the substance gate at listen.ts:404 `if (text.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length < PROBE_MIN_WORDS) return` (PROBE_MIN_WORDS = 8). 'Staying auto' is not neutral: whisper.worker.ts:52-55 records as a PROVEN FACT that "transformers.js's whisper NEVER auto-detects on an un-pinned call — it logs 'No language specified - defaulting to English' and decodes ENGLISH regardless of what was actually spoken."

**Repro.** Default settings (asrEngine 'whisper', asrLanguage 'auto'). Start a Portuguese call whose first five VAD windows are ordinary short openers — 'Oi', 'Tudo bem?', 'Me ouve?', 'Sim, claro', 'Só um segundo' — each under 8 words. Windows 1-5 are probed (listen.ts:538) but every probe returns at listen.ts:404, so `probePinnedRef` stays false. From window 6 onward `due` is false forever, no probe is ever sent again, the worker never receives `pinLanguage`, `activeLang` stays whatever `followLanguage` converged on from English-defaulted text (whisper.worker.ts:142-146), and the remaining 45 minutes of Portuguese are decoded as English-shaped text. Note whisper.worker.test.ts:218-238 ('converges onto the conversation's language in auto mode') passes only because it mocks the un-pinned ASR call to return Portuguese — the behavior the file's own PROVEN FACT says cannot happen.

**Suggested fix.** Do not retire the probe when it never landed. Change the cadence to `const due = probePinnedRef.current ? n % PROBE_EVERY === 0 : n <= PROBE_WINDOW_BUDGET || n % PROBE_EVERY === 0` (initial burst, then a steady cadence until the first successful pin). Optionally, accumulate probe text across consecutive short windows before applying PROBE_MIN_WORDS instead of discarding each short window's evidence.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; the causal chain reproduces end to end and one link is verifiable against the installed dependency rather than only against repo comments.

1) Permanent retirement is real. src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts:537 `const due = probePinnedRef.current ? n % PROBE_EVERY === 0 : n <= PROBE_WINDOW_BUDGET`. probeWindowCountRef only increments (listen.ts:535) and resets in exactly two places: start() (listen.ts:1037-1040) and a CHANGED setLanguage() (listen.ts:1528-1531). `pinLanguage` is posted only at listen.ts:413 and 426, both inside probeLanguageWindow, which is reachable only when `due`. So with n>5 and probePinnedRef false, no pinLanguage can ever be produced again for that session. No other caller, guard, or schema default re-arms it.

2) The 5 slots are consumed before the substance test. The counter advances at dispatch in pump(); the bail is at listen.ts:404 inside the probe's async .then. A short/empty Parakeet return, a rejected feed (main/parakeet.ts:123-129 throws when the sherpa addon or bundled model is absent), and the requireAuth() `''` early return (main/index.ts:2588) all burn budget silently.

3) "Stay auto" is not neutral — verified in the dependency, not just the comment. node_modules/@huggingface/transformers/dist/transformers.js:15570-15579 (WhisperForConditionalGeneration._retrieve_init_tokens) contains `// TODO: Implement language detection` and forces `language = 'en'` when none is given. whisper.worker.ts:317-321 omits opts.language while activeLang is null, so every un-pinned window decodes as <|en|><|transcribe|>. The repo's PROVEN FACT (whisper.worker.ts:52-55) is independently true for the shipped version (package.json ^3.0.0).

4) The follow machine then latches English. detectLanguage needs only MIN_HITS=2 stopwords (shared/lang-id.ts:74) and the English set includes the/and/is/you/so/okay, so English-forced junk converges via whisper.worker.ts:123-127 to activeLang='English'. With probePinned false the only un-pinned windows are the every-4th probes, themselves forced English, so English re-confirms forever. No in-meeting recovery except the user manually changing Settings (listen.ts:1519-1531).

5) Trigger is reachable on defaults: asrLanguage defaults to 'auto' (shared/ipc.ts:819 schema default, ipc.ts:1125). vad.ts:66-69 emits a window after 0.3 s speech + 0.6 s silence, so short openers each occupy their own window; five sub-8-word windows at call start is ordinary, and it is deterministic on any machine where Parakeet is unavailable.

6) Quotes check out. listen.ts:34 says "give up ... and stay 'auto'"; whisper.worker.ts:49-50 claims 'auto' "CONVERGES onto the conversation's language"; whisper.worker.ts:52-55 states the contradicting PROVEN FACT. The finder represented all three accurately.

7) Tests: ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/lib/whisper.worker.test.ts src/renderer/src/lib/listen.test.ts -> 27 passed. Nothing guards the exhausted-budget path (listen.test.ts covers only isQuestion and looksLikeNetworkError). whisper.worker.test.ts:218-238 passes only because asrFn is mocked to return Portuguese on an un-pinned call, which transformers.js:15570-15579 shows cannot occur.

Best refutation available, and why it fails: the budget is clearly deliberate and mirrored in src/main/whisper-import.ts:207-216 with the same rationale. But imports feed ~30 s slabs (shared/ipc.ts:310-314) where 5 windows is ~150 s of speech, while live feeds <=6 s VAD windows — the constant was ported without recalibrating for the ~10x smaller unit, and the parenthetical justification ("the follow machine's own probes still apply later") is exactly what the PROVEN FACT invalidates. Intent to retire the probe does not equal intent to transcribe the rest of a Portuguese meeting in English.

Severity: keeping high. Silent, unrecoverable-in-meeting corruption of the entire transcript (and therefore the recap) for the shipped default setting, on a supported non-English workflow the 'auto' mode exists to serve. Not critical: no data loss/security impact and it needs a non-English meeting with short openers (or an unavailable Parakeet).

Fix complexity: small. Either stop consuming a slot unless the probe returned >= PROBE_MIN_WORDS, or keep probing on the PROBE_EVERY cadence while un-pinned instead of retiring (listen.ts:534-539) — plus mirroring in whisper-import.ts:216 and correcting the stale comment at whisper.worker.ts:49-50 and the mocked assumption in whisper.worker.test.ts:218-238.

### MQA-013 — After renaming a deal, "Kept"/"Broken" and won/lost both fail with "Deal not found." — the two channels key by slugify(display name) while rename keeps the old id

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:2511` · workflow: settle a commitment (kept/broken) and set a deal outcome (won/lost) on a renamed deal · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/shared/ipc.ts:405-407 — "Payload for brain:setDealOutcome — the human marks a deal open/won/lost (see DealEntitySchema.outcome in shared/brain.ts; the LLM never sets it). dealSlug carries the deal's display name, the same convention brain:commitmentSettle's `deal` field uses — it's slugified in main before the store write."  Contradicted by src/main/brain/corrections.ts:863-864 — "Rename an entity's display name, pushing the old name into `aliases[]` (deduped, case-preserving). `id` (the slug) never changes."  The codebase already knows the two diverge and fixed it for ingest only: corrections.ts:493-497 — "Once a rename makes `id` diverge from slugify(current name) (e.g. id \"acme-corp\", renamed to display \"Acme\"), mergeExtraction MUST resolve through this map — including for the current name itself — or it would silently create a second \"acme\" file instead of updating the existing one."

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:2511 calls `settleCommitment(getSettings(), brainSlugify(deal), text, status)` and src/main/index.ts:3278 calls `setDealOutcome(getSettings(), brainSlugify(parsed.data.dealSlug), ...)`, where `deal`/`dealSlug` is the deal's CURRENT display name sent by the renderer (BrainView.tsx:467 `brainSetDealOutcome(deal.name, ...)`, BrainView.tsx:612 `all.push({ ...c, deal: d.name })` → BrainView.tsx:993/1002 `settlePromise(dealName, ...)`, BrainRecordPage.tsx:445 `dealName: deal.name` → BrainRecordPage.tsx:458). Neither handler consults `readAliasMap`/`resolveEntitySlug` (grep over src/, excluding tests: those two helpers are used only in ingest.ts and publish.ts). ingest.ts:981-982 then does `const deal = readDeal(s, dealSlug); if (!deal) return { ok: false, error: 'Deal not found.' }`, and store.ts:446-447 returns null the same way.

**Repro.** Deal ingested as "Acme Corp - Core Banking" → file .brain/entities/deal/acme-corp-core-banking.json, id `acme-corp-core-banking`. Open its record page, click the pencil, rename to "Acme Core Banking", Save (succeeds; applyRename writes the same file, name changed, id untouched). Now go to Mantu Intelligence → Open promises and click the ✓ (Mark kept) on one of that deal's promises: brainSlugify("Acme Core Banking") = 'acme-core-banking', readDeal returns null → red error "Commitment not found on this deal."/"Deal not found." and the promise stays open forever. Same click path for the deal row's won/lost control → "Deal not found." Every commitment on every renamed deal becomes permanently unsettleable, and the deal can never be closed.

**Suggested fix.** Send the entity id, not the display name, on both channels (the renderer already holds `deal.id` at every call site: BrainView.tsx:467, BrainView.tsx:612, BrainRecordPage.tsx:445), and drop the brainSlugify() step in index.ts:2511/3278. If the display-name wire format must stay for compatibility, resolve it through `resolveEntitySlug(readAliasMap(s), 'deal', name)` in both handlers, exactly as ingest.ts:787 already does.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED — reproduced empirically, could not refute.

Causal chain, independently verified:
1. src/main/brain/corrections.ts:829-860 applyRename calls writeTypedEntity(s, kind, payload.id, working) with working.name = payload.newName — same id, same file. Doc at corrections.ts:863-864 says verbatim "`id` (the slug) never changes." Quote is accurate.
2. Renderer sends the DISPLAY NAME: BrainView.tsx:467 `brainSetDealOutcome(deal.name, outcome)`; BrainView.tsx:612 `all.push({ ...c, deal: d.name })` -> settlePromise at BrainView.tsx:993/1002 -> BrainView.tsx:450 `brainCommitmentSettle(deal, ...)`. BrainRecordPage.tsx:445 computes BOTH `dealName: deal.name` and `dealId: deal.id` but passes dealName at 762/769 — the correct id is present and unused.
3. Handlers re-slugify the name: src/main/index.ts:2519 `settleCommitment(getSettings(), brainSlugify(deal), text, status)` and src/main/index.ts:3287 `setDealOutcome(getSettings(), brainSlugify(parsed.data.dealSlug), ...)`.
4. Lookup is a bare file read: store.ts:432 readDeal = readJson('entities/deal/<slug>.json'); store.ts:448-449 setDealOutcome returns null on miss -> index.ts:3288 'Deal not found.' ingest.ts:980-982 settleCommitment returns { ok:false, error:'Deal not found.' }.

Refutations attempted and defeated:
- Alias resolution in the handlers: grep for readAliasMap|resolveEntitySlug over src/ excluding tests hits ONLY ingest.ts (55,684,724,787,1340) and publish.ts (20,530,537,543,549,787,791,794). Never index.ts, never store.ts. Confirms the finder's claim.
- Second file created at the new slug: no — readAliasMap (corrections.ts:488-497) deliberately registers the entity's CURRENT name to prevent exactly that; quote at 493-497 verified verbatim.
- sweepDealNameDependents (corrections.ts:806-816) only rewrites account.deals[] display strings; sweepGraphNodeLabel only touches the graph node label. Neither touches the id or the file path.
- Schema guard: SetDealOutcomePayloadSchema (ipc.ts:408-411) is only z.string().min(1) — no slug enforcement. The ipc.ts:405-407 doc quote ("dealSlug carries the deal's display name ... slugified in main before the store write") is verbatim accurate and does contradict the rename invariant.
- Reachability of deal rename UI: BrainRecordPage.tsx:362 covers data.deals; rename control at 392/503/516/529 is kind-generic. Reachable.
- Existing test coverage: src/main/brain/outcome.test.ts ran green (8/8, vitest run) but has ZERO matches for rename|alias and hardcodes DEAL_SLUG='acme-core-banking' === slugify(name) — it only ever exercises the pre-rename state, so it cannot catch this.

Empirical repro (temp test written into src/main/brain/, run, then deleted; `git status --porcelain` confirms it is gone): planted deal id 'acme-corp-core-banking' name 'Acme Corp - Core Banking' with one open commitment, called the real renameEntity(kind:'deal', id, newName:'Acme Core Banking') -> ok:true. Output:
  id= acme-corp-core-banking  slugify(newName)= acme-core-banking
  settleCommitment -> {"ok":false,"error":"Deal not found."}
  setDealOutcome -> null
No file at acme-core-banking.json; commitment still status 'open'.

Severity: high is correct. Two human-only write channels (explicitly the ones the LLM may never set) permanently fail for every renamed deal — promises unsettleable forever, deal never closable. Not critical: it errors visibly rather than corrupting data, and renaming back to the exact original name restores slugify(name)===id as a non-obvious workaround.

Fix complexity: small — route both handlers through resolveEntitySlug(readAliasMap(s), 'deal', name) (2 call sites + import), or pass the already-available deal.id from the renderer.

Minor correction to the report: the settleCommitment call is at src/main/index.ts:2519, not 2511 (2511 is within the same handler block).

### MQA-014 — A rebuild resurrects a commitment the human rejected: replayCorrections resolves field_update ids through the journal alias map but leaves commitment_reject's personSlug unresolved

**Where.** `src/main/brain/corrections.ts:1514` · workflow: reject a misheard commitment, then merge that person into another (or let any transcript edit/delete trigger the automatic rebuild) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/brain/corrections.ts:1499-1507, the fix applied to the sibling case — "A rebuild's re-ingest routes a since-merged-away target's meetings straight to the merge survivor (see readAliasMap's doc comment) — so `entry.payload.id` may never materialize as its own file during replay, even though the pin it carries genuinely survives... Resolving the id through the journal map applies the pin directly against the survivor instead — matching where it ends up anyway."  And the module invariant, corrections.ts:55-58 — "If live and replay ever diverged, a rebuild would resurrect a misheard/merged-away entity a human already fixed — that's the property the rebuild-converges test guards."

**Actual.** corrections.ts:1513-1515 replays commitment_reject as `r = await applyRejectCommitment(s, entry.payload)` with no journal-alias resolution of `payload.personSlug`/`payload.dealSlug`. applyRejectCommitment (corrections.ts:1399-1423) does `readPerson(s, payload.personSlug)`; after a rebuild that person's file does not exist (re-ingest routed its meetings to the merge survivor), and with no `dealSlug` `matched` stays false → returns `{ ok: false, error: 'Commitment not found.' }`. The later entity_merge replay cannot repair it: applyMerge copies commitments with `pushUnique(t.commitments, c, (x) => commitmentKey(x.text))` (corrections.ts:975), and the survivor ALREADY holds that same normalized text with status 'open' from re-ingest, so pushUnique skips the snapshot's 'rejected' row. The per-entry warning is then discarded — ingest.ts:1706-1727 finishRebuildReplay reads only `r.error`, never `r.warnings`, so the rebuild reports success.

**Repro.** Meeting "2026-06-01 intro.md" with no deal (x.deal null) names Alice Adams and extracts commitment "send the pricing sheet" by Alice → person/alice-adams.json ledger, status 'open'. On Alice's record page click Reject (BrainRecordPage.tsx:778; dealSlug is undefined because the meeting is deal-less) → status 'rejected', journal seq 0 = commitment_reject{personSlug:'alice-adams'}. Then discover Alice is a duplicate of "Alice A. Adams" and merge alice-adams → alice-a-adams (journal seq 1); live, the survivor holds the row as 'rejected'. Now delete any old meeting from History (index.ts:2417 requestSourceRefresh → ingest.ts:1800 startRebuild, no user "Rebuild" click required). After the rebuild: alice-a-adams.commitments contains "send the pricing sheet" with status 'open' again, it is back in the dashboard's Open promises rail, and nothing in the UI says a correction was dropped.

**Suggested fix.** In the commitment_reject case of replayCorrections (corrections.ts:1513), resolve both slugs through `journalAliases` exactly as the field_update case does at 1508-1509: `const p = journalAliases.get(slugify(entry.payload.personSlug)); const personSlug = p && p.kind === 'person' ? p.id : entry.payload.personSlug` (same for dealSlug with kind 'deal'). Separately, surface `replayCorrections`'s per-entry `warnings` in finishRebuildReplay (ingest.ts:1719) the way `r.error` already is, so a silently-dropped correction is never invisible.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED by an independent end-to-end reproduction using the production functions, plus line-by-line verification of every link in the chain.\n\nCausal chain, verified:\n1. src/main/brain/corrections.ts:1513-1515 replays commitment_reject as `applyRejectCommitment(s, entry.payload)` with no journal-alias resolution — unlike the sibling field_update case at :1508-1510 which does `journalAliases.get(slugify(entry.payload.id))`. The "intended" quote is verbatim accurate (corrections.ts:1499-1507), as is the module invariant at corrections.ts:55-58 ("If live and replay ever diverged, a rebuild would resurrect a misheard/merged-away entity a human already fixed").\n2. applyRejectCommitment (corrections.ts:1399) does `readPerson(s, payload.personSlug)`; readPerson (src/main/brain/store.ts:418) is a bare `readJson(entities/person/<slug>.json)` — no tombstone walk, no alias resolution. During a rebuild the merged-away slug's file never materializes because re-ingest routes through readAliasMap ∪ aliasMapFromJournal (corrections.ts:600-616, 628-632; ingest.ts:1340-1343) and resolveEntitySlug (corrections.ts:668-675) sends the meeting straight to intoId.
