### MQA-015 — A rebuild inverts foldProvenant's merge precedence: a pin made on the merged-AWAY entity overwrites the survivor's own pin

**Where.** `src/main/brain/corrections.ts:1510` · workflow: pin a field on two duplicate records, then merge one into the other, then rebuild · fix size: medium

**Intended.** src/main/brain/corrections.ts:902-907, foldProvenant's stated precedence — "2. pinned/edited beats extracted/verified — a human's judgement beats the machine's. 3. BOTH pinned/edited → `into` wins: the human chose the merge direction, so the surviving entity's own pin is the one they kept." — implemented at corrections.ts:920-922. And shared/brain.ts:273-274 — "brain:rebuildAll's replay calls those SAME functions in `seq` order, never a parallel reimplementation — that single-mutation invariant is what makes \"rebuild + replay\" reproduce the live-corrected state byte-for-byte."

**Actual.** corrections.ts:1508-1510 rewrites a field_update's target to the merge survivor (`const hit = journalAliases.get(slugify(entry.payload.id)); const resolvedId = hit && hit.kind === entry.payload.kind ? hit.id : entry.payload.id`) BEFORE the entity_merge entry replays. So the source's pin is applied straight onto the survivor's own field via pinProvenant (corrections.ts:1195-1210), clobbering the survivor's pin. When applyMerge then replays (corrections.ts:1493), `into` already carries the source's value, `from` comes from the snapshot with the same value, both are `state:'pinned'`, and rule 3 elects `into` — which is now the WRONG value. Rule 3's whole purpose (the survivor's own pin wins) is defeated because the survivor's pin was already overwritten.

**Repro.** Two account records: "Acme Corp" (id acme-corp) and duplicate "Acme Corportation" (id acme-corportation). (1) On acme-corp's record page edit Sector → save 'financial-services' (journal seq 0, state 'pinned'). (2) On acme-corportation's page edit Sector → save 'technology' (journal seq 1, state 'pinned'). (3) On acme-corportation's page use "Same as…" → merge into "Acme Corp" (journal seq 2). Live result is correct: acme-corp.sector = 'financial-services' (foldProvenant rule 3 — into wins). (4) Delete any old meeting from History, which auto-fires startRebuild (ingest.ts:1800), or click Rebuild. After the rebuild acme-corp.sector = 'technology' — the human's surviving pin has been silently replaced by the pin they merged away. The existing regression test at corrections.test.ts:466 misses this because its merge target (Bob Baker) has `role: null`, so both sides end up with the same value.

**Suggested fix.** Do not redirect a field_update onto the survivor when a LATER entity_merge entry will fold that same snapshot in anyway. Either (a) skip the redirect and treat a 'not found' target as a tolerated no-op when journalAliases shows the id was merged away (the merge's own snapshot fold already carries the pin — that is what the code comment at 1502-1505 says happens), or (b) keep the redirect but replay it through foldProvenant against the survivor's current field instead of pinProvenant's unconditional overwrite, so rule 3 still elects the survivor's own pin. Add a rebuild-converges test for the both-sides-pinned-with-different-values permutation.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED by execution, not just reading. (1) Code trace: corrections.ts:1508-1510 rewrites EVERY field_update's target through aliasMapFromJournal unconditionally — no existence check, no seq/ordering guard, and the map is built from the FULL journal (corrections.ts:1478), so a pin journaled BEFORE the merge is still redirected. aliasMapFromJournal maps fromId->intoId at corrections.ts:600-615. applyFieldUpdate then calls pinProvenant (corrections.ts:1195-1210), which unconditionally overwrites `value` (old value only survives in `superseded`). So the merged-away entity's pin is written straight onto the survivor's own field BEFORE applyMerge replays (corrections.ts:1493). applyMerge reads `into` from the file (corrections.ts:958), which now carries the source's value; `from` comes from the snapshot with the same value; both state:'pinned', so foldProvenant rule 3 (corrections.ts:920-922) elects `into` — now the wrong value. Rule 3 is defeated, not applied. (2) Intended-behavior quotes verified verbatim: corrections.ts:904-906 states rules 2 and 3 exactly as quoted; src/shared/brain.ts:272-274 states the byte-for-byte rebuild+replay invariant exactly as quoted. (3) Executed repro (temp test in gitignored out/repro, since deleted; ran via ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run with a throwaway config): ingest two people with roles, seq0 pin role='Survivor Pin' on Bob, seq1 pin role='Source Pin' on Alice, seq2 merge Alice->Bob; then purgeBrain({preserveCorrections:true}) + re-ingest + replayCorrections (the exact sequence startRebuild performs, ingest.ts:1763-1782). Output: LIVE role = 'Survivor Pin' (rule 3 correct), REBUILT role = 'Source Pin' — AssertionError: expected 'Source Pin' to be 'Survivor Pin'. replay.warnings was empty, so the corruption is silent. The remaining 1880 tests passed in the same run, confirming no existing coverage; corrections.test.ts:466 misses it because Bob Baker has role:null so the survivor has no competing pin. (4) Searched for anything that already handles it — nothing does: no guard at the call site, withEntityLock is irrelevant, applyUnmerge only fires on explicit unmerge entries, readFieldProvenance is read-only (dashboard accept-suggestion only), pinProvenant has no rank gate by design. Two refinements, neither refuting: (a) the bug is ORDER-DEPENDENT — it manifests only when the survivor's pin has a LOWER seq than the merged-away entity's pin; in the reverse order replay's last-write-wins accidentally converges. The finder's repro uses the failing order. (b) the clobbered value is not fully destroyed (pinProvenant pushes it to `superseded`), but the surfaced value is wrong and the byte-for-byte invariant is broken. Severity high stands: silent corruption of an explicit human correction on a path that fires automatically (maybeStartSourceRefresh -> startRebuild, ingest.ts:1794-1806) after an ordinary meeting delete/edit, with zero warning. Fix complexity medium, not trivial: the redirect cannot simply be removed (that reintroduces the 'not found' warning FIX 2 closed), so the redirected pin must be applied with foldProvenant precedence — yield to a survivor field already pinned/edited and fold into superseded instead of overwriting — i.e. a new fold-aware path alongside applyFieldUpdate plus a regression test covering both sides pinned in both seq orders. READ-ONLY honored: no project file was modified; the only files created were in gitignored out/repro/ and the scratchpad, and out/repro/ was deleted (the modified files now in git status belong to a concurrent session, none under src/main/brain/).

### MQA-016 — appendCorrectionEntry deletes forward-compat journal entries and reuses their seq, so "Undo" on a merge can restore a different, unrelated pair of entities

**Where.** `src/main/brain/corrections.ts:409` · workflow: undo a merge (and cross-device/version-skew correction sync) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/shared/brain.ts:336-338 — "(The on-disk journal is read/validated per-entry in corrections.ts's parseJournalFile — tolerant of a single forward-compat unknown-kind entry — so there is no whole-array schema; a z.array() gate here would fail-closed on exactly the version-skew case that must be tolerated.)"  And corrections.ts:399-400 — "Append one entry, assigning it the next `seq` (the journal's own length — append-only, so entries are always contiguous 0..n-1)."

**Actual.** parseJournalFile (corrections.ts:176-182) DROPS every entry that fails CorrectionEntrySchema.safeParse from the returned array, keeping the surviving entries' original `seq` values. readCorrectionsJournalSafe hands that filtered array back as `gate.entries` (corrections.ts:366). appendCorrectionEntry then does `const withSeq = { ...entry, seq: currentEntries.length }` and `await writeJson(s, CORRECTIONS_REL, [...currentEntries, withSeq])` (corrections.ts:409-410) — which (a) rewrites the file WITHOUT the skipped entry, permanently erasing a correction another build wrote, and (b) assigns a seq that is no longer unique whenever a skipped entry sat before a surviving one. resolveUnmergeRestore then resolves by seq alone: `journal.find((e) => e.seq === payload.targetSeq && e.kind === 'entity_merge')` (corrections.ts:1132-1134) — first match wins. aliasMapFromJournal's `annulled.add(e.payload.targetSeq)` (corrections.ts:588) likewise annuls every merge sharing that seq.

**Repro.** OneDrive-shared .brain, machine B on a newer build. corrections.json = [ {seq:0, kind:'entity_relabel', …} (kind unknown to this build), {seq:1, kind:'entity_merge', fromId:'jon-smith', intoId:'john-smith', snapshot:{…}} ]. This build reads it as ONE entry (the merge, still carrying seq 1) — corrections.test.ts:885 proves exactly this skip. The user now merges account 'acme-corportation' into 'acme-corp': appendCorrectionEntry assigns seq = currentEntries.length = 1, writes [merge(seq 1, persons), merge(seq 1, accounts)] and the 'entity_relabel' entry is gone from disk. mergeEntities returns seq 1, BrainRecordPage shows "Merged Acme Corportation into Acme Corp. [Undo]". Click Undo → unmergeEntities({targetSeq:1}) → find() returns the FIRST seq-1 merge (the person one) → both person files are overwritten from a months-old snapshot, discarding every meeting, pin and commitment john-smith accumulated since that merge, while acme-corportation stays merged into acme-corp.

**Suggested fix.** Stop deriving seq from array length. Use `Math.max(-1, ...currentEntries.map((e) => e.seq)) + 1` in appendCorrectionEntry (corrections.ts:409) so a skipped entry can never cause a collision, and preserve unrecognized entries: have parseJournalFile return them alongside the typed ones (e.g. `{ entries, unrecognized }`) and write them back through in appendCorrectionEntry/readCorrectionsJournalSafe's merge write (corrections.ts:388), which is what "forward-compat" requires. Add a duplicate-seq assertion to resolveUnmergeRestore so a collision refuses rather than restoring an arbitrary match.

**Verifier.** Confirmed end to end; could not refute. (1) src/main/brain/corrections.ts:176-182 — parseJournalFile drops every item failing CorrectionEntrySchema.safeParse regardless of position and returns survivors with their ORIGINAL on-disk seq (parsed.data verbatim). (2) corrections.ts:364-367 — with no OneDrive conflict copy, readCorrectionsJournalSafe returns that filtered array unchanged; the only re-sequencer (mergeJournalSources, corrections.ts:265-270, `{...t.entry, seq: i}`) is on the conflict-copy branch only, so it does not rescue the plain shared-folder/version-skew case. (3) corrections.ts:409 — `seq: currentEntries.length` then `writeJson(..., [...currentEntries, withSeq])`: with [{seq:1}] (seq 0 dropped) the new entry also gets seq 1, and the rewritten file permanently loses the dropped entry. I grepped every seq site in the file: appendCorrectionEntry and mergeJournalSources are the only assigners — no max(seq)+1, no uniqueness check, no dedup. (4) corrections.ts:1132-1134 — resolveUnmergeRestore's `journal.find(e => e.seq === targetSeq && e.kind === 'entity_merge')` takes the FIRST match, and applyUnmerge (1150-1153) does whole-file writeTypedEntity on both sides from that snapshot. src/main/index.ts:3368 and BrainView.tsx:552-555 confirm Undo passes exactly the seq returned by mergeEntities (corrections.ts:1107). (5) corrections.ts:587-588/600 — annulled.add(payload.targetSeq) / !annulled.has(e.seq) annuls every merge sharing that seq, so the alias map diverges from disk too. Refutations attempted and failed: the gate does NOT treat an unknown-kind entry as corrupt (parseJournalFile returns status 'ok'; doc at 301-302 says so explicitly); the conflict-copy renumbering only runs when listConflictCopyNames is non-empty; the quoted intent is accurate — src/shared/brain.ts:336-338 verbatim requires tolerating forward-compat entries, and corrections.ts:399-400 verbatim asserts "append-only, so entries are always contiguous 0..n-1", the exact invariant the tolerant filter breaks. Reachability is proven by the repo's own test: I ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/corrections.test.ts -t "unknown-kind"` — it passes, logging "[brain] corrections journal: skipping one unrecognized/malformed entry", then performs a further mutation that rewrites the file without that entry. That test only places the unknown entry LAST, so it never exercises the collision; the mid-journal case is untested, not guarded. Extra manifestation the finder missed: mergeJournalSources' unmerge remap indexes by array position (corrections.ts:244, `entriesBySource.get(t.sourceId)?.[t.entry.payload.targetSeq]`), also wrong once a drop makes index != seq. Severity high (silent unrecoverable overwrite of two entity files from a stale snapshot plus erasure of another build's journal entry) rather than critical, because it needs cross-version multi-device journal sharing — a configuration this file is explicitly engineered for, but still a precondition. Fix is small: assign max(seq)+1 (or carry unrecognized entries through opaquely).

### MQA-017 — splitIntoWindows never advances `i` when one window's overlap seed plus the next line exceeds the window size — infinite loop + unbounded array growth wedges the main process

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:284` · workflow: index meetings / ingest a saved meeting (both the live save path and the 60s automatic reconcile backfill) · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:269-273 — "Split `text` into sequential windows of at most `size` chars, cut at line boundaries so a window never splits a transcript line, with `overlap` chars of trailing context carried into the next window. Returns `[text]` UNCHANGED when `text.length <= size` …" (i.e. the function is contracted to terminate and return a finite window list for any input). The `continue` at :295 is commented "re-evaluate this same line against the freshly-seeded (overlap-only) window", assuming the reseeded window is always small enough to accept the line.

**Actual.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:284-295 — the loop only advances `i` on the push path (:297-299). When the overlap seed (:287-293) reproduces a `cur` whose length plus the next line's length still exceeds `size`, the branch at :284 fires again on the same `i`, pushes the same window text again, and reseeds the identical `cur` — `i` is never incremented. `windows` grows without bound. This is reached synchronously from prepareMeetingWindows (:526) → extractMeeting (:484) → runExtractionStage (:1378) on the main process thread.

**Repro.** Verified by executing the exact function body under Node with a loop guard. Input A: a meetings-folder `.md` of 24,009 chars whose first two lines are 12,000 and 12,001 chars → guard tripped at 200,000 iterations with 199,999 duplicate windows and `i` still 1 of 3. Input B: a 30,000-char first line followed by `You: ok` → same. Control C (3,000 short lines, 106,889 chars) → 5 windows, correct. Concretely: drop any `.md` into the meetings folder (or a configured teamTranscriptFolders shared folder) containing an unwrapped pasted paragraph ≥ ~23k chars — e.g. a pasted email thread or contract — then either save a meeting, open Mantu Intelligence, or simply wait for the 60s reconcile tick (index.ts:4338). The main process pins a core and allocates until OOM: all IPC hangs, the overlay stops responding. Because `backfillRequested` is durable and resumeBackfillIfPending()/reconcileMeetingsInBackground() re-queue the same file, the hang recurs on every relaunch.

**Suggested fix.** Make the reseed path unconditionally forward-progressing: when `cur.length > 0` and the reseeded window still cannot accept `lines[i]`, emit `lines[i]` as its own oversized window and `i++` (or hard-split any line longer than `size - overlap` into `size`-sized pieces before the loop). Add a regression test with two adjacent lines whose combined length exceeds `size` asserting the call returns.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED — I tried to kill it four ways (upstream size cap, line normalization, caller guard, existing test) and all four failed.

1. The loop is non-terminating, and it is a provable fixed point, not just slow. src/main/brain/ingest.ts:281-300: `i` is incremented ONLY on the push path (:297-299). The overflow branch at :284 pushes `cur`, reseeds `cur` from its own tail (:287-293), and `continue`s (:295) without touching `i`. The reseed loop tests `ovLen < overlap` BEFORE adding, so it always keeps at least the last line of the closed window, and it produces the MINIMAL suffix whose length >= overlap. Re-running that same rule on `cur = ov` returns `ov` unchanged — so once a reseed happens and `curLen + lineLen > size` is still true, state (`cur`, `curLen`, `i`) is identical on every subsequent iteration. Infinite loop + one `cur.join('\n')` string pushed into `windows` per iteration = unbounded heap growth.

2. Reproduced by running the exact body (types stripped, iteration guard added) under Node:
 - two ~12k lines + a short line (24,010 chars): guard tripped at 200,001 iterations, 199,999 duplicate windows, `i` stuck at 1 of 3.
 - a 30,000-char line + `You: ok`: same, `i` stuck at 1 of 2.
 - the realistic one — 500 normal transcript lines followed by ONE 23,000-char unwrapped paragraph (37,390 chars): guard tripped with 199,500 duplicate ~1,014-char windows, `i` stuck at 500 of 501.
 - controls terminate correctly: 3,000 short lines -> 7 windows; a 22,800-char line among short lines -> 2 windows (the threshold is ~`size - overlapSeed`, i.e. any line longer than ~22.95k with a ~1k seed). A file with no newline at all also terminates (single line, `cur` empty on entry), so the trigger needs the long line plus at least one more line.

3. No guard exists anywhere on the path. `prepareMeetingWindows` (src/main/brain/ingest.ts:525-526) passes the transcript straight through (only optional `redactSecrets`, which does regex replacement and never rewraps lines — src/shared/redact.ts:31-53). `runExtractionStage` (ingest.ts:1369-1378) calls it synchronously via `extractMeeting` (:484) — and also via `prepareMeetingText` on the reconcile/no-LLM path (:1376). `readSavedFile` applies no size cap; the only byte caps in src/main are for audio imports (import-audio.ts:24) and the 8,000-char debrief (index.ts:2521), neither of which bounds this input. The `try/catch` at :1368-1382 cannot help — a hang throws nothing, so no `ingested[key].ok:false`, no `attempts`, no `exhausted`, no `retryAfter`.

4. Reachability is real and durable. `isMeetingTranscriptFile` (ingest.ts:1481-1483) accepts ANY `.md` that is not dot-prefixed / `index.md` / `README.md` — there is no `type: meeting-transcript` frontmatter gate in ingest.ts (grep: 0 matches), unlike appendDebrief (transcripts.ts:758). `startBackfill` enumerates the whole meetings folder (ingest.ts:1903-1944) and every configured `teamTranscriptFolders` shared folder (:1952-1961). index.ts:4390-4395 runs `reconcileMeetingsInBackground` 15s after boot and every 60s thereafter, and `backfillRequested` is durable (ingest.ts:1870), so the file is re-selected on every launch — the wedge recurs permanently until the user finds and deletes the file. Since it runs on the main-process thread, all IPC stops.

5. No existing test covers it. `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/verified-numbers.test.ts` -> 22 passed; its three `splitIntoWindows` cases (verified-numbers.test.ts:45-74) all use short lines, and the multi-window fixture at :327 uses `filler(...)` short lines too. Nothing asserts termination.

Severity corrected critical -> high: the consequence is exactly as described (main-process hang + OOM, recurring across relaunches, triggerable by a file a colleague drops in a shared team folder), but it is NOT reachable from app-authored content in ordinary use — ASR writes one short line per segment (transcripts.ts:602-610), the debrief is capped at 8k, and recap/note bodies are model text. It needs user-supplied markdown carrying a >~23k single line (a base64 data-URI image line, a minified/JSON blob, or a very long unwrapped pasted paragraph), which is an atypical rather than default input.

Fix is a few lines: track whether `cur` was already an overlap-only reseed and, if so, accept the oversized line into it (or clear the seed) instead of `continue`-ing — e.g. skip the reseed/`continue` when `cur` is byte-identical to the seed just produced.

### MQA-018 — startRebuild's "don't wipe what no provider can recreate" guard is defeated by the default-on local fallback — an automatic OneDrive-drift rebuild purges the whole brain and then fails every re-extraction

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1752` · workflow: automatic source-refresh rebuild of Mantu Intelligence (triggered by meeting-file drift, no user action) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1751-1753 — "// Do not wipe usable derived data just to discover that no configured provider can recreate it. if (!hasUsableProvider(s)) { return { queued: 0, error: 'Connect an AI provider …' } }". The eligibility helper it depends on documents its own limit at src/main/llm/local-routing.ts:26-30: "Doesn't prove it can actually spawn or load a model — a genuine spawn failure still fails over via local-runtime.ts's own crash/restart-budget handling; this only gates whether Métis Local is offered as a route at all".

**Actual.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:119-121 (new on this branch) makes `local` a candidate whenever `s.localLlm.fallback && localBaseReady(s, allowed)`, and src/shared/ipc.ts:879-911 defaults BOTH `localLlm.enabled` and `localLlm.fallback` to true. localBaseReady (src/main/llm/local-routing.ts:52-58) only checks enabled + org allowlist + binary-on-disk + model-downloaded — it never consults localRuntimeState, whose 'unavailable' value src/shared/ipc.ts:1016-1018 documents as a "session-long 'unavailable' lockout (restart-budget exhausted, cleared only by relaunch)". So hasUsableProvider() returns true on a machine where llama-server provably cannot run, the guard at :1752 passes, and purgeBrain(s, {preserveCorrections:true}) at :1763 rmSync's the entire `.brain/` tree (store.ts:503). The failover "mitigation" local-routing.ts cites does not exist here: the fallback is appended as the LAST candidate (:119), so there is nothing after it to fail over to.

**Repro.** Zero cloud/CLI providers keyed (the Cahê single-Kimi-key pilot with the key removed), stock settings (localLlm.enabled=true, fallback=true, model+binary shipped in the installer), and llama-server unable to spawn on this box (Windows Vulkan/CPU spawn failure exhausting the restart budget → localRuntimeState 'unavailable'). OneDrive touches the mtime of any already-indexed meeting → hasMeetingSourceDrift (:1508) → requestSourceRefresh (:1786) → maybeStartSourceRefresh (:1798, hasUsableProvider now true) → startRebuild → purgeBrain deletes every entity/graph/meeting-extraction file → all N re-extractions throw on the dead sidecar → each source ends at MAX_INGEST_ATTEMPTS with exhausted:true, which the automatic reconcile tick then skips forever (:1924). Net: Mantu Intelligence goes from a populated graph to 0 people / 0 accounts / 0 deals, unrecoverable without a manual Retry index. Before this branch the same machine returned hasUsableProvider()=false and the guard refused the purge.

**Suggested fix.** Have the local fallback candidate require live runtime health, not just on-disk provisioning: gate ingest.ts:119 on localRuntimeState !== 'unavailable' (and ideally a successful ensureLocalRuntimeStarted probe) before local counts toward hasUsableProvider(); alternatively make startRebuild's precondition stricter than the extraction waterfall's — a candidate that only exists as a last-resort fallback should not by itself authorize a destructive purge.

**Verifier.** I tried to kill this on five fronts and every one held.

VERIFIED CHAIN
1. The quote is accurate and literal. `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1751-1753` is verbatim "Do not wipe usable derived data just to discover that no configured provider can recreate it" guarded by `if (!hasUsableProvider(s))`. `hasUsableProvider` = `pickProvider(s) !== null` = first element of `pickProviderCandidates` (ingest.ts:71-73, 127-129).
2. The local candidate at ingest.ts:119-121 is genuinely new on this branch: `git diff main...HEAD -- src/main/brain/ingest.ts` shows `+ if (s.localLlm.fallback && localBaseReady(s, allowed)) candidates.push({provider:'local',...})` as an addition. And `git diff main...HEAD -- src/shared/ipc.ts` shows `enabled: false → true` and `fallback` newly added `.default(true)` (ipc.ts:879, :911, plus DEFAULT_SETTINGS at ipc.ts:1139-1145). So on a zero-cloud-key machine `hasUsableProvider()` flipped false→true on this branch.
3. `localBaseReady` (src/main/llm/local-routing.ts:51-57) is enabled + org allowlist + `localRuntimeBinaryPresent()` (existsSync) + `safeIsDownloaded()`. `isDownloaded` (src/main/llm/local-models.ts:122-126) is a *file-size* comparison only. Zero runtime-health input. I grepped every `localRuntimeState` use: only `src/main/index.ts:912` (snapshot) and `Settings.tsx:1403-1407` (status line). It is display-only — nothing in routing reads it. Confirmed.
4. The purge is total: `purgeBrain` (src/main/brain/store.ts:495-513) `rmSync(root, {recursive:true, force:true})` on `brainDir` = `join(resolveMeetingsFolder(s), '.brain')` (store.ts:32-34), escrowing only `corrections.json`. That directory holds index.json, entities, graph AND every saved meeting extraction — so `startBackfill`'s no-LLM repair path (`strategy: 'reconcile'`, ingest.ts:1930-1931, driven by `listMeetingExtractions`) cannot apply afterwards. Every source needs a live LLM call.
5. Local really is terminal when it can't run. `runCompletion` (ingest.ts:200-213) only fails over `if (hasNext)`, and local is pushed last, so there is no next. The local call goes `createStream({providerId:'local'})` → `streamLocal` → `runLlama` (src/main/llm/local.ts:162-163) → `ensureLocalRuntimeStarted` (local.ts:69-75) → `verifyIntegrity` → `localRuntime.start`, which throws unconditionally at `src/main/llm/local-runtime.ts:511` once `state==='unavailable'`, a session-long latch set at :429/:437.
6. Trigger is fully automatic. `reconcileMeetingsInBackground` (ingest.ts:2066-2076) runs on `setInterval(..., 60_000)` from `src/main/index.ts:4395`; `hasMeetingSourceDrift` (ingest.ts:1508-1521) compares `meetingSourceVersion` = `` `${mtimeMs}:${size}` `` (ingest.ts:1234-1241), so a OneDrive mtime touch (or a sync to a second machine — `.brain` lives *inside* the synced meetings folder) trips it → `requestSourceRefresh` → `maybeStartSourceRefresh` (:1798, same `hasUsableProvider` gate) → `startRebuild` → purge. No user action anywhere.
7. Not self-healing: after `MAX_INGEST_ATTEMPTS` the record is `exhausted` and the automatic tick skips it forever (ingest.ts:1923-1924); only a manual Retry/Index re-arms it. No existing test covers the rebuild-guard/local-fallback interaction — `ingest-index-fallback.test.ts` only proves the waterfall ordering. I ran `vitest run src/main/brain/ingest-index-fallback.test.ts src/main/brain/ingest-rebuild-resume.test.ts` — 16/16 pass, and nothing there contradicts this.

STRONGER REPRO THAN THE FINDER'S (found while trying to refute): the 'unavailable' latch is only reachable via `maybeAutoRestart`, which fires only `if (wasRunning)` (local-runtime.ts:407-418) — i.e. it needs a sidecar that reached 'running' then crashed twice in 10 min. But two *deterministic* machine classes defeat the guard without any of that: (a) `verifyIntegrity` calls `assertRamOk` (local-models.ts:176-177, 84-89) and the bundled model declares `minTotalRamGB: 8`, while `isDownloaded` has no RAM check — on a <8 GB box `localBaseReady()` is true forever and every local call throws `InsufficientRamError`; (b) a partially-synced/corrupt model file with a matching byte size but wrong sha256 passes `isDownloaded` and throws `ChecksumMismatchError` on every call. Both purge and then fail 100% of re-extractions.

WHY I DOWNGRADED critical → high. Two things the finder overstates. (i) The guard was never a capability check even on `main` — a configured-but-401/expired cloud key already passed it and already produced purge-then-fail. This branch widens an existing hole rather than opening a new class; what's new (and real) is that it widens it to exactly the population the guard uniquely protected, by default, with no user action. (ii) Nothing unrecoverable is destroyed: the transcripts are untouched (purge is scoped to `.brain`) and corrections are escrowed, so the graph is fully reconstructible once any provider works, via one manual Retry. Combined with the compound precondition (populated brain AND zero eligible cloud candidates AND a local runtime that cannot run), that is high, not critical.

FIX SIZE: small. The rebuild path needs a stricter predicate than the ingest path — e.g. `startRebuild` gating on a "can actually recreate" check that excludes an unproven local fallback (`localRuntime.getState() !== 'unavailable'` plus a cheap `assertRamOk`/integrity precheck), or deferring the purge until the first extraction actually succeeds. A few lines in ingest.ts around :1750-1763 plus a test; must stay scoped so it does not undo the intended fallback indexing at ingest.ts:119.

**PARTIAL (2026-08-08).** The restart-budget lockout path from the repro above is fixed and pinned by `src/main/brain/ingest-degradation.test.ts`, but the row stays OPEN deliberately: the verifier also identified variants that still purge-then-fail — a machine under the model's RAM floor, and a corrupted/checksum-mismatched model file. Closing those needs `src/main/llm/local-models.ts` (RAM + integrity are known there, not in ingest) or a purge-deferral redesign, so the guard would have to ask "can local actually LOAD right now", not merely "is local configured". Marking this FIXED on the strength of the one covered path would overstate it.

**FIXED (2026-08-17).** The remaining two variants are closed by making the destructive path ask the stronger question, split across the two places that can actually answer it. **RAM floor → eligibility:** `localBaseReady` (src/main/llm/local-routing.ts) now also runs `assertRamOk`. `isDownloaded` is a file-SIZE check, so below `minTotalRamGB` it stayed true forever while every load threw `InsufficientRamError` — and `listModels()` was already reporting that same machine as `unavailableReason: 'insufficient-ram'`. The snapshot and the routing decision were asserting opposite things about one machine; now there is one answer. Wrapped like `safeIsDownloaded`, so an unknown model id degrades to "not ready" rather than throwing into a routing decision. **Corrupt model → the purge precondition:** `startRebuild` calls `localOnlyRebuildBlocked` before `purgeBrain` — when EVERY candidate is `local` it awaits `verifyIntegrity(modelId)` and refuses the rebuild, naming the reason, when that throws. A checksum mismatch cannot be seen from a size check and cannot be hashed cheaply on the ask path, but a rebuild is rare and destructive, and this is not extra work: it is the SAME `verifyIntegrity` the first extraction's cold start would run anyway (`ensureLocalRuntimeStarted`), moved to before the deletion instead of after it. A keyed cloud candidate skips it entirely, so the common path pays nothing. Net: local authorizes a purge only once it has been shown loadable this session. The intended fallback indexing at ingest.ts's candidate list is untouched — this is strictly the rebuild precondition, exactly the "stricter than the extraction waterfall's" split the verifier called for. Regression tests name MQA-018 for both variants, for the cloud-candidate fast path (proving no gigabyte re-hash on the common path), and for the RAM gate in `local-routing.test.ts`.

### MQA-019 — `dust status` timeout kills only cmd.exe on Windows, orphaning the real `dust` process — which then rotates the single-use OAuth refresh token concurrently with the next refresh and invalidates the whole Dust CLI session

**Where.** `src/main/dustcli.ts:109` · workflow: Dust token refresh (startup, Connect from Dust CLI, and on-401 self-heal) on Windows · fix size: small

**Intended.** dustcli.ts:83-87 — "Overlapping refreshes are dangerous, not just wasteful: Dust's OAuth refresh tokens rotate and are single-use, so two concurrent `dust status` runs (startup refresh racing a 401-triggered one) can burn a stale refresh token and invalidate the whole CLI session — the exact 'why am I running `dust login` again' failure. Single-flight collapses concurrent callers onto one mint." cli.ts:73-79 — "Aborting/killing only the immediate child (cmd.exe) does not cascade to that grandchild — it keeps running to completion, orphaned. `taskkill /T` recurses the whole process tree rooted at pid."

**Actual.** src/main/dustcli.ts:107-114 routes the refresh through `resolveSpawnTarget(bin, ['status'])` — i.e. it knows it is on the Windows cmd.exe shim path — but then relies on `exec(..., { timeout: 25_000 })`. execFile's timeout sends a kill to the IMMEDIATE child only, which on that path is cmd.exe; the `node …dust-cli status` grandchild is not touched. cli.ts's `killWindowsProcessTree` (cli.ts:80-85) exists for exactly this and is applied at every cli.ts spawn site (cli.ts:504, cli.ts:684) but never here. The `refreshInflight` single-flight guard (dustcli.ts:88-97) only tracks Métis's own promise, so it is blind to an orphan it can no longer see.

**Repro.** Windows, `dust` installed via npm (dust.cmd). Network stalls (captive portal / VPN reconnect). A Dust ask 401s → refreshDustAuth → refreshDustCliSession spawns cmd.exe → dust.cmd → node. At 25s exec times out and kills cmd.exe only; refreshInflight is cleared and importDustCliSession re-reads the OLD token from Credential Manager, so the ask fails. The orphaned `dust status` is still mid-flight holding refresh token R1. The user retries ~30s later (past REFRESH_RESULT_TTL_MS): a SECOND `dust status` starts and also presents R1. Both rotate; one rotation invalidates the other → Credential Manager ends up with a token pair Dust rejects → every subsequent Dust ask 401s and no refresh can recover it. The user has to run `dust login` again — precisely the failure dustcli.ts:83-87 says the design must prevent.

**Suggested fix.** Export `killWindowsProcessTree` from cli.ts and stop using execFile's `timeout` here: spawn the target, arm your own timer, and on expiry call `killWindowsProcessTree(child.pid)` on win32 (SIGTERM elsewhere) before resolving. Cheap extra safety: keep a module-level `lastStatusRunAt` and refuse to start a new `dust status` until the previous one has actually been reaped or a hard grace period has passed.

**Verifier.** I tried to refute this four ways and it survived all four, including an empirical repro on this Windows machine.

MECHANISM — confirmed in code and by execution.
`D:\Asktoto\src\main\dustcli.ts:107` calls `resolveSpawnTarget(bin, ['status'])`. On Windows `resolveBin('dust')` returns `dust.cmd` (`cli.ts:97` parseWhereOutput matches `.cmd`; `cli.ts:107` npmGlobalBinCandidates emits `dust.cmd`; the in-app installer WIN_SETUP_SCRIPT at `dustcli.ts:188` does `npm i -g @dust-tt/dust-cli`). `resolveSpawnTarget` (`cli.ts:290`) routes `.cmd` to `cmdShimSpawn`, which returns `{command: cmd.exe, args:['/d','/s','/c', ...]}`. So the immediate child at `dustcli.ts:108` IS cmd.exe, and the real `node dust-cli status` is a grandchild. `exec` there is `promisify(execFile)` (`dustcli.ts:12`) with `timeout: 25_000`; Node's execFile timeout calls `child.kill('SIGTERM')`, which on Windows is `TerminateProcess` on that one pid only.

I reproduced it verbatim in scratchpad (`orphan/driver.js`, a byte-identical copy of the cmdShimSpawn target shape + the same execFile options, timeout shortened to 5s): `EXEC REJECTED at 5062 ms killed=true signal=SIGTERM`, and 20s later the grandchild had written its `.finished` marker — it survived the kill and ran to completion, orphaned. I specifically tested my best refutation, that execFile's `close` would be held open by the grandchild's inherited pipe handles and thus keep `refreshInflight` set (which would have preserved single-flight): it does not — execFile destroys stdout/stderr before killing, so the promise settled at the timeout and `refreshInflight` (`dustcli.ts:123`, in `finally`) was cleared while the process was still alive.

The guard is genuinely blind afterwards: `dustcli.ts:119-120` runs unconditionally after the swallowed catch, so `lastRefresh` is cached with `ok:true` (the stale-but-present token/workspace still read fine), the 30s `REFRESH_RESULT_TTL_MS` expires, and the next caller spawns a second `dust status` against the same Credential Manager refresh token the orphan is still holding. `refreshInflight`/`lastRefresh` (dustcli.ts:88-90) are the ONLY serialization anywhere in the repo — grep confirms no lock file, mutex, or caller-side gate.

INTENDED-BEHAVIOR QUOTES — both accurate. `dustcli.ts:83-87` says verbatim that overlapping refreshes can "burn a stale refresh token and invalidate the whole CLI session — the exact 'why am I running `dust login` again' failure," and that single-flight exists to prevent it. `cli.ts:73-79` says verbatim that killing only cmd.exe "does not cascade to that grandchild — it keeps running to completion, orphaned" and that `taskkill /T` is the remedy. `killWindowsProcessTree` (cli.ts:80-85) is applied at cli.ts:504 and cli.ts:684 — and cli.ts:475-481 even disables spawn's built-in signal wiring so nothing races the taskkill — but it is not exported and never used in dustcli.ts. This is a real inconsistency, not a design choice.

CORRECTION TO THE FINDER. The claimed workflow "startup refresh racing a 401-triggered one" cannot happen on Windows: `index.ts:4265` gates `refreshAndPersistDust` (both the startup call at 4285 and the 10-min keep-warm at 4289) behind `process.platform !== 'darwin' → return`. That removes the highest-frequency collision source the finder cites. It does not save the finding — three ungated Windows triggers remain: `refreshDustAuth` on a stream 401 (index.ts:703 and index.ts:2998), `dustListAgents` on-401 self-heal (index.ts:2140), and `dustImportCli` / "Connect from Dust CLI" (index.ts:2158), which Settings.tsx:2434 confirms is live cross-platform. The realistic collision is: ask 401s → refresh times out at 25s leaving the orphan → user opens Settings and clicks "Connect from Dust CLI" past the 30s TTL → second `dust status` presents the same refresh token.

SEVERITY. Keeping high. The mechanism is certain and proven; only the worst-case consequence (server-side reuse detection revoking the whole token family) rests on Dust's OAuth semantics I can't verify from this repo — but the milder outcome is still corruption, since the orphan finishes last and writes an older token pair over the newer one in Credential Manager (last-writer-wins on a shared secret store). The repo's own bar supports high: it built dedicated plumbing for this exact orphaning class at every cli.ts spawn site, and the blast radius here (auth session destruction requiring `dust login`) is worse than a stray CLI process. No test covers it — `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/dustcli.test.ts` reports 6 tests, all skipped (keychain-gated), and cli-win.test.ts tests `resolveSpawnTarget` shape only, never the timeout/kill path.

FIX. Small: export `killWindowsProcessTree` from cli.ts and, in dustcli.ts, replace `exec` with `spawn` plus a 25s timer that calls it on `child.pid` (mirroring cli.ts:501-510), or reuse the existing abort-listener pattern. ~20-30 lines, no behavior change off Windows.

### MQA-020 — claude-cli's `is_error: true` terminal line is settled as SUCCESS, so a failed CLI failover target returns a blank answer and stops the waterfall

**Where.** `src/main/cli.ts:357` · workflow: ask a question (any mode) after the primary cloud key dies and the waterfall reaches Claude Code CLI · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/cli.ts:559-570 — `child.on('close', (code) => { rl.close(); void cleanup(); if (settled || controller.signal.aborted) return; if (code === 0) { settled = true; wd.clear(); opts.handlers.onDone({}) } else { const stderr = ...; fail(stderr.slice(-500) || `${label}: exited with code ${code}`) } })`, i.e. a non-zero CLI run must reach `fail()`. Reinforced by src/main/llm/openai.ts:180-181: "onDone with empty content would render as the idle \"Ask a question…\" placeholder — indistinguishable from never having asked — so surface it as a real, actionable error instead", and by the contract test src/main/ask-freshness.contract.test.ts:133-135 ("the pre-token failover seam hands ANY exhausted-retry error to the next provider").

**Actual.** src/main/cli.ts:357-364 `isResultLine(line) { ... return obj.type === 'result' || (obj.type === 'stream_event' && obj.event?.type === 'message_stop') }` matches a result line regardless of `is_error` / `subtype`. src/main/cli.ts:546-551 then does `settled = true; wd.clear(); opts.handlers.onDone({}); controller.abort()`, so the non-zero-exit branch at cli.ts:562 short-circuits on `if (settled ...) return`. index.ts:3015 `onDone` never checks whether a single token arrived.

**Repro.** DeepSeek key revoked; Claude Code CLI connected as the next waterfall target. Ask any question. DeepSeek 401 -> retry.ts isTransient=false -> index.ts:3055 failover -> attempt('claude-cli'). The user's Claude subscription limit is already reached, so `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages` (cli.ts:320-334) emits zero `stream_event`/`text_delta` lines and one `{"type":"result","subtype":"error_during_execution","is_error":true,"result":"Claude AI usage limit reached|..."}`, then exits 1. cli.ts:546-551 calls onDone({}) -> index.ts:3029 sends IPC.streamDone -> state.ts:327-329 `text: noOutput ? '' : a.text` blanks the answer -> Answer.tsx:329-338 renders the empty "Ask a question or press …" placeholder. No error, no hint, and codex-cli / NVIDIA NIM / Métis Local are never tried because index.ts:3055's failover line only runs from onError.

**Suggested fix.** Make `isResultLine` a SUCCESS-only marker: `return (obj.type === 'result' && obj.is_error !== true && !String(obj.subtype ?? '').startsWith('error_')) || (obj.type === 'stream_event' && obj.event?.type === 'message_stop')`. Add an `isErrorResultLine` sibling that routes `is_error === true` (and `error_*` subtypes) through `fail(obj.result || obj.subtype || label + ' failed')` so the ask reaches index.ts's failover seam. Belt-and-braces: in index.ts:3015 treat `onDone` with `gotToken === false` as a pre-token failure and run the same failover path. Extend src/main/cli.test.ts:217-240 (which only ever asserts `subtype: 'success'`) with an `is_error: true` case.

**Verifier.** Could not refute. Every link in the chain reproduces.

1) src/main/cli.ts:357-364 — `isResultLine(line)` returns `obj.type === 'result' || (obj.type === 'stream_event' && obj.event?.type === 'message_stop')`. No `is_error` / `subtype` check. Grepping `is_error|error_during_execution|usage limit` across src/ and docs/ returns ZERO hits, so no other layer inspects it either.

2) src/main/cli.ts:546-551 — on a match: `settled = true; wd.clear(); opts.handlers.onDone({}); controller.abort()`. That makes cli.ts:562's `if (settled || controller.signal.aborted) return` skip the intended `code !== 0` -> `fail(stderr...)` branch at cli.ts:567-570, discarding stderr entirely. The intended-behavior quote is verbatim-correct at cli.ts:559-570.

3) The behavior is actively codified by the existing suite, not guarded against: src/main/cli.test.ts:283-306 writes `{"type":"result"}`, then `child.emit('close', 1)`, and asserts `onError` was never called. cli.test.ts:220 only pins `subtype:'success'`. `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/cli.test.ts` -> 19/19 pass, i.e. the tests bless the defect.

4) No wrapper guard: src/main/llm.ts:17-30 `createStream` and src/main/llm/cli.ts:11-18 `streamCli` pass handlers through untouched.

5) src/main/index.ts:3022-3037 `onDone` never consults `gotToken` (declared 2984, set only in onDelta at 3018-3019); it just sends IPC.streamDone. Failover exists only inside `onError` (index.ts:3062), so the waterfall stops dead — codex-cli / NIM / Métis Local are never tried.

6) src/renderer/src/state.ts:321-329 — onDone with zero deltas has `noOutput = pendingReplaceRef.current === true`, so `text: ''` and no `error`. src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:329-338 then renders the idle "Ask a question or press …" placeholder. The `notice` slot (Answer.tsx:164) is screen-capture-permission-only, so nothing else surfaces.

Refutations I tried and that failed:
- "claude-cli can't be a failover target": false. index.ts:2802-2820 `pickFailover` admits CLI providers on `!!s.cliConnected[p]`; index.ts:3083-3088 also makes it PRIMARY when providerPriority==='cli'.
- "a connection re-test would disconnect a limit-exhausted CLI": false. `cliConnected` is persisted once on connect (index.ts:2245) and is never re-run per ask; askStart only reads it (index.ts:2910, 3095).
- "some empty-output guard exists": false. The only precedent is the opposite one — src/main/llm/openai.ts:176-183 routes zero-content-terminal through `onError` with exactly the quoted rationale, and src/main/ask-freshness.contract.test.ts:133-135 + 137-143 pin that the pre-token seam must hand such cases to the next provider. Both cited quotes are accurate.

The only unverifiable element is the CLI's exact bytes under a subscription limit, which I cannot exercise here. It is not load-bearing: the defect is schema-level — ANY error-shaped `type:'result'` line (error_during_execution, error_max_turns, API rejection) with zero text deltas is settled as success, and cli.ts:336-349 `parseLine` only emits text from `text_delta`, so the error string in `result` is never shown either.

Severity: high is right. Silent success on a failed provider, blank panel with no error and no hint, plus suppression of the entire remaining waterfall — the classic degrade-ask failure. Not critical (no data loss / security exposure). Fix is small: have `isResultLine` reject `is_error === true` (or better, surface the result line's `result` text through `fail()`), plus a regression test.

### MQA-021 — No per-provider cooldown or circuit breaker: a revoked/rate-limited primary is re-attempted (and, on a 429, retried) on every single ask, forever

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:3037` · workflow: every live ask after the primary key dies — typed answer, screen vision, and the live-meeting suggest loop · fix size: medium

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:3037-3039 states the goal explicitly: "Waterfall: when another configured provider can take over (e.g. Dust down but a Claude/GPT key is set), cap same-provider retries at ONE so the API answers in seconds instead of after the full ~30s of retrying a dead primary." docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1875 states the design as "Provider health: on StreamError with code 429/503 → fallback to next healthy provider in settings.fallbackChain (if configured); log to audit.log".

**Actual.** There is no provider-health state anywhere in src/main (grep for `cooldown|deadUntil|unhealthy|failCount|lastFailure|providerFail` over src/main -> no matches). src/main/llm/local-routing.ts:140-152 `pickPrimaryProvider` is pure and always returns `s.provider` (or the local/CLI precedence); index.ts:2779-2822 `pickFailover` gates only on `getApiKey(p).length > 0` / `s.cliConnected[p]`, i.e. key PRESENCE, never key validity. `auditLog('provider.failed', ...)` (index.ts:3033) is write-only for routing — it is read only by metrics.ts:62-63 for the Diagnostics counters.

**Repro.** DeepSeek key hits its monthly quota and returns `429 Too Many Requests` on every call; NVIDIA NIM is configured. Every ask runs: attempt('deepseek') -> 429 -> retry.ts isTransient=true (TRANSIENT_PATTERN `\b429\b`) -> index.ts:3046 retryBudget=1 -> nextBackoff(0)=250-500ms -> attempt('deepseek') again -> 429 -> index.ts:3055 failover -> NVIDIA answers. Every ask, in every session, pays two dead DeepSeek round trips plus ~0.4s of added latency, and each of those two requests is another hit against the already-rate-limited key. In a live meeting the shadow-suggest loop (src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1189-1205, ~every 15s while the other side is speaking) plus each "What to say next" click repeats this continuously.

**Suggested fix.** Add a module-level `Map<ProviderId, { until: number; reason: 'auth' | 'quota' }>` in index.ts. On a pre-token failure that is auth-shaped (401/403) or quota-shaped (402/429/insufficient-credit), mark the provider unavailable for a bounded window (e.g. 15 min for auth, honor Retry-After for quota). Have `pickPrimaryProvider`/`pickFailover` skip providers inside their cooldown window, and clear a provider's entry on any successful onDone or on a Settings key change (`key.set`).

**Verifier.** SURVIVES — I could not refute the causal chain; it reproduces exactly at HEAD (2db18a7), and the repo's own QA has independently measured it.

What I verified independently at HEAD (`git show HEAD:src/main/index.ts`):
- No provider-health state exists anywhere: `grep -cE "isCoolingDown|provider-health|recordAuthFailure"` over HEAD's index.ts = 0; my own grep for `cooldown|deadUntil|unhealthy|failCount|lastFailure|providerFail|breaker|backoffUntil` over src/main returned only unrelated brain-journal "quarantine" hits.
- `pickPrimaryProvider` (D:\Asktoto\src\main\llm\local-routing.ts:140-152) is pure: `if (localVisionRequired) return 'local'; if (providerOverride) …; if (localEligible) …; if (cliPrimary) …; return activeProvider`. It takes no failure history, so every ask re-selects the same dead `s.provider`. HEAD calls it at index.ts:3079 with no health input.
- `pickFailover`'s candidate filter (HEAD index.ts ~2786-2829) gates on `getApiKey(p).length > 0` / `s.cliConnected[p]` — key PRESENCE only, never validity.
- The retry math checks out: HEAD index.ts:3036-3037 `hasFailoverTarget → retryBudget = 1`; `isTransient` returns true for 429 both via `status === 429` and via TRANSIENT_PATTERN's `\b429\b` / `too many requests` (D:\Asktoto\src\main\llm\retry.ts:53-66); `nextBackoff(0)` = min(8000, 500)/2 + rand*250 = 250-500ms (retry.ts:84-90). Ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/llm/retry.test.ts` — 9/9 pass, confirming that classification. So: 2 dead primary round trips + ~0.4s per ask, forever. Worse than the finder states, actually: `new OpenAI({apiKey, baseURL})` (openai.ts:65) sets no `maxRetries`, so the SDK's default 2 internal retries (429 is in its retry set, honoring Retry-After) multiply each app-level attempt.
- No mitigation elsewhere: the ask path never persists a successful failover (no `setSettings({provider})` anywhere in index.ts), the renderer has no sticky provider (`streamMeta` is consumed only for the waiting-state label, state.ts:226; `providerOverride` is only ever set to 'dust'), and `provider.failed` is read only by metrics.ts:62 for a Diagnostics counter — exactly as claimed. The App.tsx speculative-suggest effect (~line 1189-1205) does re-fire the whole walk every ≥15s while the other side is speaking.
- Corroboration, not my basis: docs/qa/BUG-LEDGER.md already carries this as **MQA-003 (high, OPEN)** with a measured repro — a revoked DeepSeek key produced the walk ["deepseek","nvidia","local"] on three consecutive suggest asks costing 6.5s / 9.3s / 9.2s against a 15s live-suggest budget. A sibling agent is wiring the fix in the working tree right now (untracked src/main/llm/provider-health.ts + index.ts:2842 and :3141) — so this is a DUPLICATE of MQA-003 and is already being fixed.

Where the finder overreached (does not kill it, but should be corrected):
1. The docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1875 citation does NOT say what the finder claims. It is pseudocode for an unbuilt design (`settings.fallbackChain` does not exist in src/shared/ipc.ts — it appears only in docs), and that doc defines "healthy" as *connected*, not *not-recently-failed*: line 877 says "selectRoute builds fallbackChain at call time from the set of connected providers". Read straight, the shipped `pickFailover` satisfies it. Only the index.ts:3044-3046 comment genuinely supports the intent, and even that is scoped to the within-one-ask retry budget, not cross-ask memory.
2. The 429 framing is the weakest sub-case. A bare rate-limit 429 is often genuinely per-minute-transient, and DeepSeek's exhausted-balance response is 402 "Insufficient Balance", not a bare 429. The in-flight fix deliberately excludes non-auth failures for exactly this reason (provider-health.ts:13-15: "Auth failures only… A 500 or a dropped socket is the provider having a bad minute"), so the 429 half will still re-attempt every ask even after MQA-003 lands. The finding's load-bearing half is the revoked/dead-key case in its own title, which is real and unambiguous.

Severity corrected medium → high, matching the ledger's own rubric ("high = core workflow broken or silently wrong"): the wasted walk is measured at 6.5-9.3s against the 15s live-suggest idle budget, so on a slower network the headline live-meeting suggestion silently never appears, and MQA-004 means the user is simultaneously told providerReady: true.

### MQA-022 — isIngestTransportFailure() classifies every credential error without an HTTP status number as PERMANENT, halting the failover walk before the local last-resort candidate

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:143` · workflow: index meetings (brain ingest / entity extraction) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:136-138 — "this pipeline's known failure mode (a provider consistently returning e.g. HTTP 404 for a misconfigured/retired model) is exactly that kind of permanent-looking 4xx, and a DIFFERENT eligible provider can still serve the request. Anything that isn't a deliberate cancel is worth one hop to the next candidate; MAX_INGEST_ATTEMPTS is what stops a transcript with every provider down from retrying forever, not this gate." Reinforced by docs/cahe-windows-edition.md:10 — "if Kimi (or whichever cloud provider is active) is unreachable or unconfigured, meeting indexing (Mantu Intelligence extraction) ... run on-device as a last resort instead of failing — meetings still get indexed".

**Actual.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:143 `return /timed out|\b4\d\d\b/i.test(message)`. isTransient() (src/main/llm/retry.ts:58) has already returned false for anything matching AUTH_PATTERN, so line 143 is the only remaining chance to classify a credential failure as failover-worthy — and it needs literal HTTP-status digits in the message text. Dust surfaces auth failures as prose with no digits: src/main/llm/dust.ts:370 calls `fail(created.error.message)`, passing only `.message`, and the phrasings pinned in src/main/llm/dust.test.ts:204-210 are "The user request does not have a valid authenticated credential.", "The request does not have valid authentication credentials.", "Unauthorized", "Invalid API token", "expired_oauth_token_error". CLI providers are the same: src/main/cli.ts:569 fails with raw stderr or `${label}: exited with code ${code}`.

**Repro.** Cahê/Windows-shaped profile: settings.provider='kimi' (key present), Dust connected, localLlm.fallback=true with the bundled model provisioned (defaults, src/shared/ipc.ts:905). Kimi returns 503; the walk in runCompletion (ingest.ts:203-213) fails over to the next candidate and reaches 'dust' (PROVIDERS order, src/shared/providers.ts:243, before 'local' which is appended last at ingest.ts:119-121). Dust's ~1h OAuth token has expired, so createStream errors with `The user request does not have a valid authenticated credential.` -> isIngestTransportFailure() returns false (verified by evaluating the exact regexes from ingest.ts:141-143 and retry.ts:41-65 against those strings) -> runCompletion rethrows at ingest.ts:210 instead of hopping -> 'local' is never attempted. finishJob (ingest.ts:1400-1414) writes ingested[file] = {ok:false, error:'The user request does not have a valid authenticated credential.', attempts:n} and after 6 reconcile ticks (~30 min) exhausted:true. The meeting is never indexed even though a ready on-device model was the very next candidate in the pool. Existing coverage misses this: every failover test uses digit-bearing messages ('503 Service Unavailable', '404 page not found', 'network error') — src/main/brain/ingest-resilience.test.ts:85,101,132,152 and src/main/brain/ingest-index-fallback.test.ts:137,213,236,288 — and all 19 tests pass today.

**Suggested fix.** Make the gate structural rather than string-shaped: treat auth/credential failures as failover-worthy in this pipeline (the opposite of the interactive path, where retrying the SAME provider is pointless but hopping to a DIFFERENT one is exactly right). E.g. `if (isDustAuthError(err) || AUTH_SHAPED.test(message)) return true` before the digit test, or invert the predicate to `return !isDeliberateCancel(err)` to match the stated "anything that isn't a deliberate cancel is worth one hop" contract, and add a regression test asserting the walk reaches 'local' after a Dust-phrasing auth error.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED. Independently reproduced the causal chain.

CLASSIFICATION: src/main/brain/ingest.ts:162-182 rejects with `new Error(m)` where m is a bare string from onError, so errorBlob (src/main/llm/retry.ts:16-33) always sees status===null in this path. Evaluating the actual regexes (retry.ts:41-47 + ingest.ts:141-143) in node: "The user request does not have a valid authenticated credential." / "The request does not have valid authentication credentials." / "Unauthorized" / "Invalid API token" / "expired_oauth_token_error" all hit AUTH_PATTERN -> isTransient false (retry.ts:58), then ingest.ts:143 needs literal HTTP digits -> false. Digit-bearing controls ("503 Service Unavailable", "404 page not found", "network error") return true, so the gate really does turn on digits. Result: runCompletion rethrows at ingest.ts:210 despite hasNext===true; local (appended strictly last at ingest.ts:119-121) is never attempted; finishJob (ingest.ts:1392-1414) records ok:false and exhausted:true after MAX_INGEST_ATTEMPTS (ingest.ts:1250).

NO EXISTING GUARD — this is the check that could have killed the finding and did not. Dust's auth self-heal cannot fire here: refreshDustAuth is passed at only two call sites, src/main/index.ts:708 and :3031 (both ask-path). runCompletionOnce never passes it, so retryIfAuth short-circuits on !opts.refreshDustAuth (src/main/llm/dust.ts:258) and falls to fail(created.error.message) (dust.ts:370) — .message only, the 401 status is discarded before ingest ever sees it. The launch-time eager refresh is darwin-gated (index.ts:4318), so on the Windows edition the ~1h token is never proactively re-minted either. pickProviderCandidates does not consult provider-health (no such import in ingest.ts:1-29). runWindow's reminder retry (ingest.ts:499-508) re-walks with servedBy undefined and halts identically.

INTENT QUOTE IS ACCURATE: ingest.ts:136-138 says verbatim "Anything that isn't a deliberate cancel is worth one hop to the next candidate; MAX_INGEST_ATTEMPTS is what stops a transcript ... not this gate." The sibling ask path confirms the asymmetry: src/main/index.ts:3105 fails over on ANY pre-token error with no classification gate at all, so the ingest gate — documented as "deliberately BROADER than the interactive ask path" — is strictly narrower than what the ask path does.

REPRO IS REACHABLE AND STRONGER THAN CLAIMED: localLlm.fallback defaults true (src/shared/ipc.ts:905); docs/cahe-windows-edition.md:10 promises on-device last-resort indexing; that same doc's step 4 instructs the Windows pilot to connect Dust, and src/main/dustcli.ts:202 supports win32. With s.provider==='dust' Dust is candidate #0, so an expired token halts the walk on the first hop — even a healthy later cloud key is skipped, not just local. Same shape for CLI providers (src/main/cli.ts:569, "exited with code 1" has no 4xx match).

TESTS: ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/ingest-index-fallback.test.ts src/main/brain/ingest-resilience.test.ts — 19 passed. Every failover assertion uses digit-bearing messages (ingest-resilience.test.ts:85,101,132,152; ingest-index-fallback.test.ts:137,213,236,288). ingest-index-fallback.test.ts:285-287 explicitly concedes that an unrecognizable message "would read as PERMANENT and stop the walk after one hop" — it documents the gap to avoid a confound, it does not assert the behavior is intended for credential errors.

SEVERITY: high stands. Silent, repeating failure of a core background feature under a default-on, documented configuration, contradicting both the in-code intent and the shipped Windows-edition promise. Not security/data-corruption, and the failure is surfaced in ingestFailureDetails, which is the only thing keeping it below critical.

FIX: small. Widen the gate to match its documented contract (fail over on anything that is not an abort, letting MAX_INGEST_ATTEMPTS bound it) or add the auth family to line 143, plus a regression test using a digit-free credential message asserting the walk reaches 'local'.

### MQA-023 — A backfill queue stalled by provider loss is never re-pumped — indexing freezes permanently, "Retry index" becomes a no-op, and the progress bar sticks

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:2041` · workflow: index meetings (backfill / Mantu Intelligence) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1611-1613 — the stall path logs `'[brain] backfill paused: no configured AI provider — will resume next time one is available'`. src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1597-1601 states the design: "A provider can be removed (cleared key, CLI disconnected) after startBackfill() already queued jobs — re-checking here, not just at queue time, stops a mid-backfill provider loss from burning every remaining job... Backfill jobs stay AT THE FRONT of the queue (never removed here)".

**Actual.** pump() has exactly four call sites: ingest.ts:1623 and 1634 (both only reachable from inside an already-running job), 1684 (enqueueIngest), and 2014 (startBackfill). With every remaining job stalled in `queue`, no job is running, so 1623/1634 can never fire. `hasActiveBackfill()` (ingest.ts:1129) is permanently true because the stalled jobs are still in `queue`, which makes both automatic recovery paths bail before they reach startBackfill/pump: reconcileMeetingsInBackground returns at ingest.ts:2069 (`if (backfillPreparing || sourceRefreshRunning || hasActiveBackfill()) return`) and requestBackfill returns at ingest.ts:2041 (`if (hasActiveBackfill() || backfillLintPending) return { queued: 0 }`). Neither IPC.setApiKey (src/main/index.ts:2085-2097) nor IPC.settingsSet (src/main/index.ts:1907+) touches the brain queue.

**Repro.** Org profile with allowedProviders pinned so 'local' is excluded (or localLlm.enabled=false), one cloud key. Click Index meetings with 40 saved meetings -> startBackfill queues 40 backfill jobs, backfillTotal=40. Three complete. The user, seeing 401s, opens Settings -> AI and clears the dead key (IPC.clearApiKey, index.ts:2099) intending to paste a new one. pump()'s per-iteration `hasUsableProvider` check (ingest.ts:1604-1608) now returns -1, breaks, and leaves 37 jobs in `queue` forever. The user pastes the fresh, working key: the 60-second reconcile timer (index.ts:4338) returns at ingest.ts:2069 on every tick; the Mantu Intelligence "Retry index" button (src/renderer/src/components/BrainView.tsx:726 -> window.toto.brainBackfill -> index.ts:3209 -> requestBackfill) returns {queued:0} at ingest.ts:2041 and does nothing; brainBackfillProgress().running stays true (ingest.ts:1151), so BrainView freezes at "Mapping 3 of 40 meetings · 7%" AND suppresses the failure banner, which is gated on `!bf?.running` (BrainView.tsx:697). Only an app restart (resumeBackfillIfPending, ingest.ts:1838), saving a new meeting (enqueueIngest -> pump, ingest.ts:1684), or a destructive full Rebuild recovers.

**Suggested fix.** Let a re-entrant request re-pump instead of short-circuiting: in requestBackfill, when `hasActiveBackfill()` is true but nothing is actually in flight (`inFlightJobs.size === 0 && extracting.size === 0`), call pump() before returning; and drop `hasActiveBackfill()` from reconcileMeetingsInBackground's guard (ingest.ts:2069) in favour of an in-flight check, so the 60s tick can revive a stalled queue. Add a regression test: queue N backfill jobs, remove the provider mid-run, restore it, tick reconcile, assert the remaining jobs complete without a restart.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; every link reproduces in code.\n\nSTALL: pump() re-checks hasUsableProvider per iteration (src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1602-1608); when all queued jobs are origin:'backfill' without strategy:'reconcile' and no provider resolves, findIndex returns -1 and it breaks (ingest.ts:1609-1616), leaving jobs in `queue`. `queue` is mutated in only three places in the file — splice in pump (ingest.ts:1618), push in enqueueIngest (ingest.ts:1683), push in startBackfill (ingest.ts:2013) — so there is no flush/cancel path.\n\nNO RE-PUMP: pump()'s only call sites are ingest.ts:1623 and 1634 (both inside runExtractionStage().then/.finally, reachable only while a job runs), 1684 (enqueueIngest) and 2014 (startBackfill). With zero in-flight jobs, 1623/1634 are unreachable.\n\nBOTH AUTOMATIC PATHS BLOCKED: hasActiveBackfill() = queue.some(j => j.origin==='backfill') (ingest.ts:1129) is permanently true. reconcileMeetingsInBackground returns at ingest.ts:2069 on every 60s tick (timer at src/main/index.ts:4409). requestBackfill returns {queued:0} at ingest.ts:2041 — and once the user restores a provider the earlier escape hatch at ingest.ts:2037 (`if (!hasUsableProvider) return startBackfill(...)`) no longer fires, so 2041 is what executes. The Retry-index IPC (src/main/index.ts:3269) and the dashboard-open pass (src/main/index.ts:3224) both route through requestBackfill, so both are no-ops. resumeBackfillIfPending is invoked only at boot (src/main/index.ts:4406).\n\nNO SETTINGS-SIDE RECOVERY: IPC.setApiKey (src/main/index.ts:2103-2119) and IPC.clearApiKey (src/main/index.ts:2121-2130) only write the key store and call resetProviderHealth; IPC.settingsSet (src/main/index.ts:1925+) touches screen preprocess, wiki publish, login item, content protection — never the brain queue.\n\nINTENDED-BEHAVIOR QUOTES ARE ACCURATE: ingest.ts:1613 logs 'backfill paused: no configured AI provider — will resume next time one is available', and the design comment at ingest.ts:1596-1601 states backfill jobs 'stay AT THE FRONT of the queue (never removed here)'. The promised auto-resume does not exist for the in-session case.\n\nUI IMPACT IS WORSE THAN CLAIMED: brainBackfillProgress().running stays true via hasActiveBackfill() AND backfillLintPending (ingest.ts:1151; maybeFinishBackfill at ingest.ts:1464 requires !hasActiveBackfill() to clear it). In src/renderer/src/components/BrainView.tsx the bf?.running branch (:803) renders the frozen 'Mapping N of M' meter, and that same flag suppresses the failure banner at :697 (`durableFailed > 0 && !bf?.running`) which is the only place the 'Retry index' button (:726) renders, plus the 'Ingest now' row (:826-841). So the user sees a lying progress bar and has no visible recovery control at all.\n\nREACHABILITY: clearApiKey is wired to a real renderer action (src/renderer/src/state.ts:563-569). Other realistic triggers that flip pickProviderCandidates (ingest.ts:84-123) to empty mid-run: a local-only setup where localBaseReady goes false, or an org allowedProviders policy change.\n\nNO EXISTING COVERAGE: src/main/brain/ingest-backfill.test.ts only tests the queue-time no-provider guard (lines 78-134); nothing exercises provider loss AFTER jobs are queued followed by provider restoration. Its own afterEach comment (lines 65-68) independently documents this mechanism as the cause of a ~1-in-4 suite flake.\n\nSeverity high stands: core Mantu Intelligence indexing freezes for the rest of the session, every in-app recovery affordance is either hidden or a silent no-op, and the progress UI actively misreports.
