### MQA-024 — Cancelling an import while it is generating the summary leaves the saved meeting file (and its index.md row) on disk, with the job card gone

**Where.** `src/main/import-jobs.ts:349` · workflow: cancel an in-flight import · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/import-jobs.ts:337-342 states the invariant and implements it for the save window: "cancel() flipped the job to 'cancelled' while saveMeeting() was in flight. The meeting file already landed on disk but job.file was never recorded — delete it here so a cancelled import never leaves an orphaned meeting behind." `deleteMeeting` is wired for exactly this (index.ts:789) and correctly removes both the .md and its index.md row (recall.ts:256-289).

**Actual.** The three later cancellation checkpoints inside finishDecoding — src/main/import-jobs.ts:349 (after generateRecap), :352 (after updateRecap) and :362 (before enqueueIngest) — are bare `if (this.isCancelled(job)) return` with no `deleteOrphanedFile(file)` call. `deleteOrphanedFile` is referenced exactly once in the file, at line 341. Meanwhile cancel() (import-jobs.ts:216-230) has already deleted the durable checkpoint (line 222) and the renderer filters state 'cancelled' out of the card list (RecallView.tsx:1125), so no trace remains.

**Repro.** Import any recording. The card renders a Cancel button for every non-done state (RecallView.tsx:1157-1158), including the multi-second-to-multi-minute 'recapping' phase shown as the wrapping-up pulse. Click Cancel while the summary is being generated (state 'recapping'). Result: the card disappears, the checkpoint is deleted, and `<meetings folder>/<stamp>-<slug>.md` written at import-jobs.ts:330 stays on disk plus its index.md row (transcripts.ts:704-710) — a transcript of the recording the user explicitly cancelled silently appears in History/Recall (and syncs to OneDrive) with an empty "Notes & follow-ups" section and no brain ingest. Existing test import-jobs.test.ts:218-232 drives this exact window but only asserts state==='cancelled' and enqueueIngest not called, so the orphan slips through.

**Suggested fix.** Route all four cancellation checkpoints through one helper that calls `await this.deleteOrphanedFile(job.file ?? file)` before returning (import-jobs.ts:349, 352, 362), matching line 341. If keeping the transcript is actually preferred, invert it instead: leave the job visible as 'done' with an explicit "summary cancelled" note rather than silently vanishing the card.

**Verifier.** I tried to refute this three ways (a guard elsewhere, a caller that cleans up, an intent to keep the saved transcript) and it survived all three; I also reproduced it with a runnable test.

1) The quoted intent is accurate, verbatim. src/main/import-jobs.ts:337-343: `if (this.isCancelled(job)) { // cancel() flipped the job to 'cancelled' while saveMeeting() was in flight. The meeting file already landed on disk but job.file was never recorded - delete it here so a cancelled import never leaves an orphaned meeting behind. await this.deleteOrphanedFile(file); return }`. The stated invariant is general.

2) The three later checkpoints are bare returns. import-jobs.ts:349 (after generateRecap), :352 (after updateRecap), :362 (before enqueueIngest). `deleteOrphanedFile` appears exactly twice in the file: definition at :445, single call site at :341. Nothing compensates: `deleteMeeting` is referenced only at index.ts:215/805 (dep wiring), index.ts:2438 (user-initiated recallDelete IPC) and recall.ts:654 (retention sweep). The cancel IPC handler (index.ts:3549-3555) only calls `importJobs.cancel(jobId)`; onCancel -> closeImportDecoder (index.ts:505-518) only tears down the decoder. cancel() (import-jobs.ts:216-230) never inspects `job.file` and deletes the durable checkpoint at :222, so after a restart the job is gone from memory entirely and nothing can ever reconcile the file.

3) Reproduced. Throwaway vitest suite in my scratchpad (C:\Users\Tony\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--Asktoto\b531604d-ab95-48b1-bb9f-c07c78393874\scratchpad\orphan.verify.test.ts) against the real ImportJobManager — no project files touched. All three pass: (a) BASELINE — cancel while saveMeeting is in flight DOES call deleteMeeting('saved-import.md'), so the dep is live and the harness is sound; (b) REPRO — cancel while generateRecap is in flight: job observed at state 'recapping' with file='saved-import.md'; after cancel, state 'cancelled', checkpoint gone from the store, enqueueIngest never called, deleteMeeting.mock.calls.length === 0; (c) REPRO 2 — same orphan for cancel during updateRecap/before enqueueIngest. Existing suite: ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/import-jobs.test.ts -> 21 passed. No test in that file (nor import-jobs.verify-cascade.scratch.test.ts / import-recap.contract.test.ts) references deleteMeeting at all, so the existing cancel-during-recap test (import-jobs.test.ts:218-232) asserts only state + enqueueIngest and lets the orphan through.

4) The file is genuinely user-visible and the window genuinely reachable. saveMeeting writes the .md and, when encryptTranscripts is off, appends the index.md row (src/main/transcripts.ts:704-710), so the cancelled recording shows up in History/Recall with an empty "Notes & follow-ups" section. The renderer filters `job.state !== 'cancelled'` out of the card list (RecallView.tsx:1125) and renders Cancel for every non-done state (RecallView.tsx:1157-1158), including 'recapping' — which work-progress.ts:169-178 itself documents as "the stretch that can legitimately take a while (an LLM call)". So the app offers Cancel during a multi-minute phase, then on click removes the card, removes the checkpoint, and keeps the transcript.

5) The strongest counter-argument — that a saved transcript is deliberately durable — does not save the code. recover() (import-jobs.ts:154-160) implements that alternative for the CRASH path: file + 'recapping' becomes 'done' with a recapError and a visible "Open meeting" card (RecallView.tsx:1146-1155). The cancel path does neither: it neither deletes the file nor keeps a visible done card. Whichever resolution is preferred, the current state is inconsistent, so the defect stands.

Severity: keeping 'high'. Not a narrow race — it is a mandatory, long, cancel-inviting phase of every import; the outcome is silent retention of exactly the recording the user asked to discard (privacy-relevant in a meeting-transcription app, and it lands in the synced meetings folder), plus an artifact that was never ingested so Ask/brain cannot see it. Short of critical: nothing lost or corrupted, and the user can delete the meeting once they notice.

Fix: `await this.deleteOrphanedFile(file)` at import-jobs.ts:349, :352, :362, plus clearing/persisting `job.file` (already recorded by then), plus the missing assertions in import-jobs.test.ts:218-232.

### MQA-025 — The Resume button re-saves an already-saved meeting, creating a duplicate meeting file, a duplicate index.md row and a duplicate brain ingest

**Where.** `src/main/import-jobs.ts:204` · workflow: resume a failed import · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/import-jobs.ts:151-153 states the invariant: "The meeting file is already durable once `file` is present. A crash during recap must not replay the decoder and create a duplicate meeting; surface it as a completed transcript so the user can open the note and retry its summary manually." It is locked by import-jobs.test.ts:234 — `it('does not decode or duplicate a meeting after a crash during recap', ...)` asserting `expect(second.decode).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`.

**Actual.** `resume()` at src/main/import-jobs.ts:204-214 checks only `if (job.state !== 'failed')`; it never consults `job.file`, does not clear it, and re-enqueues the job for a full decoder replay. finishDecoding then calls `this.deps.saveMeeting(...)` unconditionally at import-jobs.ts:330, and saveMeeting picks a fresh non-colliding filename (`for (let n = 2; existsSync(file); n++) file = ...-${n}.md`, transcripts.ts:671-674) — so the second run writes a SECOND meeting rather than overwriting. recover() has the same hole for a checkpoint persisted in state 'saving' (import-jobs.ts:328-329): its guard at line 154 only matches `job.file && job.state === 'recapping'`, so a 'saving' checkpoint whose saveMeeting had already landed is re-queued at line 174 and re-saved.

**Repro.** A job that already wrote its meeting then fails inside finishDecoding's OUTER try after line 344 — reachable when the checkpoint write at import-jobs.ts:367 throws: writeSaved re-throws EPERM/EBUSY after 5 bounded retries under an AV/EDR or OneDrive lock (transcripts.ts:296-305), and encryptEnvelopeV2 is deliberately fail-closed when the credential store is momentarily unavailable (transcripts.ts:280-285). The card then shows state 'failed' with a Resume button labelled "Resume this import from its last saved transcript checkpoint" (RecallView.tsx:1137-1139). Click Resume -> ffmpeg replays the source with skipThrough = cursor = totalChunks so every chunk is skipped -> finishDecoding -> saveMeeting again -> `<stamp>-<slug>-2.md` with byte-identical content next to `<stamp>-<slug>.md`, a second index.md row, and a second enqueueIngest so the same meeting is double-counted in Mantu Intelligence (two people/account/deal merges from one conversation).

**Suggested fix.** In `resume()` (and in recover()'s non-terminal branch), treat `job.file` as the terminal marker the recapping guard already does: if `job.file` is set, do not re-enqueue the decoder — retry only the recap/ingest tail (or mark the job 'done' with a recapError telling the user to open the meeting). Extend import-jobs.test.ts:234's assertion to the resume() entry point and to a 'saving'+file checkpoint.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; reproduced end-to-end with a scratch vitest run (since deleted, tree clean of my changes).

INTENT QUOTE IS ACCURATE. src/main/import-jobs.ts:151-153 literally states "The meeting file is already durable once `file` is present. A crash during recap must not replay the decoder and create a duplicate meeting…", and src/main/import-jobs.test.ts:234-251 locks it ONLY for recover() (`expect(second.decode).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`).

CAUSAL CHAIN VERIFIED LINK BY LINK:
1) src/main/import-jobs.ts:204-214 — resume() guards only `job.state !== 'failed'`; it never reads or clears `job.file`, then enqueue()+pump().
2) 'failed' WITH `file` set is reachable and durable: `job.file = file` is set at import-jobs.ts:344, and everything after it is still inside the outer try — persist at :346, `await this.deps.enqueueIngest(file)` at :363, persist at :367. Any throw lands in the outer catch at :369 -> fail() -> state 'failed' while `file` survives. writeSaved (src/main/transcripts.ts ~:288-305) genuinely re-throws EPERM/EBUSY after 5 bounded retries, and encryptEnvelopeV2 is documented fail-closed ("Any error propagates to the caller … plaintext is never silently written"), so the trigger class is real — and is exactly the Windows AV/lock class this branch is hardening.
3) UI offers the button unconditionally: RecallView.tsx:1136-1139 renders Resume inside a bare `job.state === 'failed'` branch (no `job.file` check), and the list filter at :1124 keeps failed cards. IPC handler src/main/index.ts:3557-3563 (IPC.importJobResume) adds no guard.
4) Replay really re-saves: startImportDecoder (src/main/index.ts:566) passes `job.cursor` as skipThrough; src/main/ffmpeg-decoder.ts:145 and :162 skip every chunk when seq < skipThrough and :170 calls onComplete(seq) with the full count -> finishDecoding's totalChunks/cursor/lines checks all pass -> saveMeeting at :330 -> transcripts.ts:670-673 `for (let n = 2; existsSync(file); n++)` picks `<stamp>-<slug>-2.md` (a SECOND file, not an overwrite) and appendIndexRow adds a second index.md row.

EMPIRICAL RUN (scratch test, ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run): store throws once on the state:'done' checkpoint write -> job persists durably as {state:'failed', file:'…interview.md'} (fail()'s own persist succeeds after the transient lock clears) -> manager.resume('job-1') -> decode called a 2nd time with cursor 1 of 1 -> finishDecoding -> saveMeeting calls: 2, returning ['…interview.md','…interview-2.md']; enqueueIngest calls: 2, with the two DIFFERENT paths (so the brain double-ingests the same conversation under two basenames — enqueueIngest keys by basename, ingest.ts:1649, so no dedupe saves it). Baseline src/main/import-jobs.test.ts is 21/21 green — nothing covers the resume-with-file path.

SECONDARY HOLE ALSO CONFIRMED: recover()'s guard at import-jobs.ts:154 is `job.file && job.state === 'recapping'`. The 'saving' checkpoint is persisted at :328-329 BEFORE saveMeeting, so a kill anywhere in saveMeeting's tail (meeting file already renamed into place + index row appended) leaves a durable 'saving' checkpoint with no `file` -> non-terminal -> requeued at :174 -> full decoder replay -> duplicate. Narrower crash window, same defect.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED: no guard in the IPC layer; no `file` check in the renderer; recover()'s guard does not cover resume() (different code path, and 'failed' is terminal so recover() never revisits it); saveMeeting does not overwrite; enqueueIngest does not dedupe across differing basenames; deleteMeeting is only wired to the cancel path (:341).

SEVERITY: keeping 'high'. Silent duplicate meeting file + duplicate index.md row + double brain ingest (double-counted people/account/deal merges), durable across restarts, and actively invited by a prominent button whose tooltip promises a resume "from its last saved transcript checkpoint". Not a security issue, so not critical.

FIX: small — in resume(), mirror recover()'s invariant (`if (job.file) { state='done'; recapError=…; removeCheckpoint; return }`), and widen recover()'s guard to `job.file && (state === 'recapping' || state === 'saving')`; plus record job.file before saveMeeting or make finishDecoding no-op when job.file is already set.

### MQA-026 — "Today's agenda" queries a UTC-midnight window, not the user's local day — Graph ignores Prefer: outlook.timezone for request bounds

**Where.** `src/main/calendar.ts:24` · workflow: view today's agenda / get "meeting starting soon" notifications · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/calendar.ts:15-16 — "/** Today's [00:00, next-00:00) as naive ISO strings in the given IANA timezone (Graph reads them with the Prefer: outlook.timezone header, so no offset math is needed here). */". The sibling Graph call in the same repo does it the other way: src/main/graph-transcript.ts:44-45 — `const start = new Date(startedAt - CALENDAR_LOOKUP_PAD_MS).toISOString()` (offset-bearing, ends in `Z`), with the comment at :42 saying it "Mirrors calendarToday's own calendarView + fetch pattern".

**Actual.** src/main/calendar.ts:24 builds `const start = `${parts}T00:00:00`` and :27 `const end = `${next.toISOString().slice(0,10)}T00:00:00`` — naive, no timezone designator — and passes them as `startDateTime`/`endDateTime` at :54. Microsoft Graph documents that calendarView's startDateTime/endDateTime "are interpreted using the timezone offset specified in the value and are not impacted by the value of the Prefer: outlook.timezone header if present. If no timezone offset is included in the value, it is interpreted as UTC." The Prefer header sent at :57 only controls the timezone of the *returned* start/end values, which is why AgendaView's `fmtTime` (AgendaView.tsx:6-11, `new Date(iso)` on a naive string = local) renders correctly while the window itself is wrong.

**Repro.** I executed the exact todayBounds() body under several zones on 2026-08-08. Asia/Tokyo -> start `2026-08-09T00:00:00`, end `2026-08-10T00:00:00`; interpreted as UTC that is Aug 9 09:00 JST -> Aug 10 09:00 JST. So a Tokyo user with an 08:30 JST standup today sees "No meetings today" for it, while tomorrow's 07:00 meeting is listed as today's. Pacific/Auckland gives a noon->noon window (the entire morning agenda is missing). America/Los_Angeles gives Aug 7 17:00 -> Aug 8 17:00 PDT: today's 17:30 call is absent and yesterday's 18:00 call is shown as today's. The same wrong list feeds startMeetingNotifier (src/main/index.ts:1600-1611), so those meetings also get no "starting soon" notification.

**Suggested fix.** Emit offset-bearing bounds instead of relying on the Prefer header — e.g. derive the tz offset for the target date (Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZoneName:'longOffset', or format the local midnight and convert) and send `${date}T00:00:00${offset}` / `${nextDate}T00:00:00${offset}`, matching graph-transcript.ts's `.toISOString()` pattern. Add a unit test that pins todayBounds for Asia/Tokyo and America/Los_Angeles.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED — I attacked this from four angles and it survived all of them.

1) Code path is exactly as claimed. src/main/calendar.ts:18-23 formats "YYYY-MM-DD" for the given IANA zone via Intl(en-CA); :24 `const start = `${parts}T00:00:00`` and :27 `const end = `${next.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}T00:00:00`` — both naive, no `Z` and no `±HH:MM`. They are passed verbatim as `startDateTime`/`endDateTime` at :53-55, with `Prefer: outlook.timezone="${zone}"` set at :57. The UTC date arithmetic at :25-26 is only computing "next calendar date" and is fine; the defect is solely the missing offset designator.

2) The "intended behavior" quote is real and is contradicted by the vendor. The comment at calendar.ts:15-16 literally says the bounds are read "with the Prefer: outlook.timezone header, so no offset math is needed here". I fetched the live Microsoft Graph reference (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/user-list-calendarview, v1.0) and it states verbatim: "The values of `startDateTime` and `endDateTime` are interpreted using the timezone offset specified in the value and aren't impacted by the value of the `Prefer: outlook.timezone` header if present. If no timezone offset is included in the value, it is interpreted as UTC." The same page defines the header as response-only: "Prefer: outlook.timezone — Use this to specify the time zone for start and end times in the response." So the code's stated premise is false at the source of truth, and the window is a UTC-midnight window.

3) Repro reproduced independently. I ran the exact todayBounds() body (real clock, UTC 2026-08-08T19:15Z): Asia/Tokyo -> {"2026-08-09T00:00:00","2026-08-10T00:00:00"} = 09/08 09:00 -> 10/08 09:00 JST (today's pre-09:00 meetings absent, tomorrow's early ones shown as today's). Pacific/Auckland -> 12:00 -> 12:00 (whole morning missing). America/Los_Angeles -> 07/08 17:00 -> 08/08 17:00 PDT (today's evening calls absent, yesterday evening's shown as today's). Europe/Paris -> 02:00 -> 02:00, i.e. near-harmless for CEST users, which is why this can hide in a Paris-HQ product; UTC users are unaffected entirely.

4) No guard, caller, default, or test rescues it. There is no calendar test file anywhere (`grep -l calendar` over all src/**/*.test.ts* returns nothing; no `todayBounds` reference outside calendar.ts), and `grep` for `timeZoneName|longOffset|getTimezoneOffset` across all of src/ returns zero hits — no offset helper exists in the codebase. Both callers pass a real zone, not UTC: src/renderer/src/components/AgendaView.tsx:60 and src/main/index.ts:1615-1617 both use `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, and the IPC handler at src/main/index.ts:2370-2373 forwards it unchanged. The renderer does no post-filtering — AgendaView.tsx:119-128 renders `res.events` as-is and prints "No meetings today." on an empty array. startMeetingNotifier (src/main/index.ts:1628-1644) iterates the same list, so events outside the shifted window simply never get a "starting soon" notification; the 30s cache at :1595 just propagates the same wrong list.

The finder's internal-inconsistency evidence also holds: the sibling call at src/main/graph-transcript.ts:44-45 builds `new Date(...).toISOString()` (offset-bearing, ends in `Z`) with no Prefer header, while its comment at :42 claims it "Mirrors calendarToday's own calendarView + fetch pattern" — the two Graph calls in this repo disagree, and graph-transcript.ts is the correct one.

Severity: keeping high, not raising or lowering. It is read-only convenience data (no corruption, no security exposure), but it silently produces wrong output on two headline workflows for every user whose UTC offset is non-zero — a real meeting rendered as "No meetings today" and a missing meeting-start notification, with no error state to signal it. Fix complexity is small rather than trivial: the bounds need a real DST-aware offset for the zone appended (e.g. Intl formatToParts with timeZoneName:'longOffset', or compute the offset at that instant) rather than a one-token edit, and the comment at :15-16 must be corrected.

READ-ONLY: I changed nothing. Files examined: D:\Asktoto\src\main\calendar.ts, D:\Asktoto\src\main\graph-transcript.ts, D:\Asktoto\src\main\index.ts, D:\Asktoto\src\renderer\src\components\AgendaView.tsx, D:\Asktoto\src\preload\index.ts.

### MQA-027 — A non-GUID / placeholder Entra tenant ID passes validation and permanently bricks the app — SignInWall has no escape and the Settings form self-locks

**Where.** `src/main/auth.ts:120` · workflow: first-run sign-in / enabling Microsoft SSO (self-serve or managed enterprise rollout) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/auth.ts:112-119 (isPlausibleAzureConfig doc comment): "NOTE for the auth owner: although the MSAL authority URL accepts a domain-form tenantId, the runtime tenant gate in signIn() compares against the id-token `tid` claim, which Entra always issues as the tenant GUID — so a domain-form tenantId would authenticate then be rejected as \"outside your organization\" on every sign-in. **Actual.** Neither remedy was implemented. src/main/auth.ts:120-122 `isPlausibleAzureConfig` only calls `isSafeConfigValue`, whose test is `/^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$/` (src/main/auth.ts:109) — so `mantu.onmicrosoft.com` AND the placeholder shipped in build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json (`"azureTenantId": "REPLACE-WITH-AZURE-TENANT-ID"`) both pass. readConfig() then reports configured:true, and every sign-in dies at src/main/auth.ts:754 `if (tid !== cfg.tenantId)` → 'That account is outside your organization.' There is no recovery: App.tsx:2535-2541 renders <SignInWall/> instead of the whole app whenever `configured && !signedIn`; App.tsx:1950-1952 blocks every hotkey except 'hide' while that gate is up (so tray → 'Settings…' at index.ts:1672-1675, which routes through sendHotkey('settings'), is dead too); and Settings.tsx:5887-5891 sets `azureLocked = ... || !!authStatus?.configured`, disabling the three ID inputs and the Save button forever once any config resolves. settingsSet in main also refuses the write (index.ts:2022 `if (!requireAuth()) return publicSettings()`).

**Repro.** Fresh install, Settings → Account → Change IDs. Enter a valid clientId, put the Entra *primary domain* (e.g. `mantu.onmicrosoft.com`) in "Directory (tenant) ID" instead of the GUID, allowed domain `mantu.com`, Save. Within one auth poll (≤5 min) or on next launch the app renders only the SignInWall. Click "Sign in with Microsoft" → browser auth succeeds at Microsoft → Métis returns "That account isn't part of @mantu.com…". Every retry gives the same result; Settings, the tray Settings item, and all hotkeys are blocked. The app is unusable until userData/settings.json is hand-edited or the profile deleted. Fleet-scale variant: deploy build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json with `requireAuth: true` and the REPLACE-WITH-* placeholders unedited → every machine that receives the policy is bricked identically.

**Suggested fix.** (1) In isPlausibleAzureConfig, require tenantId to match a GUID (`/^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$/`) or resolve the domain form to a GUID before the auth.ts:754 compare; reject the literal `REPLACE-WITH-*` placeholders outright. (3) Make signIn()'s tenant rejection say which tenant was expected vs. returned, so the misconfiguration is diagnosable.

Neither remedy exists: `isPlausibleAzureConfig` at `src/main/auth.ts:120-122` is a three-way `isSafeConfigValue` call, and `isSafeConfigValue` (`src/main/auth.ts:105-110`) is only `v.length > 0 && v.length <= 253 && /^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$/.test(v)`. Both `mantu.onmicrosoft.com` (letters + dots) and `REPLACE-WITH-AZURE-TENANT-ID` (letters + hyphens) pass.

The compare has no normalization at all, so this also fires on any GUID typo or an uppercase-pasted GUID — a wider trigger than the finder claimed.

No sign-out, no settings link, no reset. Grepping the whole tree for "Reset SSO"/resetSso/clearAzure returns only three comments inside auth.ts — that UI does not exist.

I checked whether the `body` memo at App.tsx:2456-2471 (which does contain `view === 'settings' ? settingsBody`) offers a way in — it does not; `body` is only consumed at App.tsx:2796, far below the 2536 early return. The onboarding gate at 2550 has a special `view === 'settings'` branch, but it sits after the SSO gate, so it is unreachable. `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1948-1952` blocks every hotkey but 'hide', and tray → 'Settings…' at `src/main/index.ts:1681-1684` routes through `sendHotkey('settings')`, so it is dead too.
