Main refuses the write independently: `src/main/index.ts:1930` `if (!requireAuth()) return publicSettings()` (the finder cited 2022 — line drift, the guard is real). I traced `requireAuth()` (`src/main/auth.ts:633-638`) for this exact state: authEnforced=false, sticky=false (never signed in successfully, so `writeStickyConfigured()` at auth.ts:780 never ran), so it falls to `!s.configured || s.signedIn` = `!true || false` = false. Blocked.

REFUTATION ATTEMPT 4 (LKG recovery saves it): failed. `readConfig()` only consults LKG when `isStickyConfigured()` (auth.ts:161), and sticky is only written in signIn()'s success branch — which is unreachable here. The documented recovery mechanism is inert for a config that never once succeeded.

REFUTATION ATTEMPT 5 (a test or schema default catches it): failed. `src/shared/ipc.ts:697-699` is bare `z.string().default('')` — no format refinement. `saveOutlookIds` (Settings.tsx:5898-5901) only checks non-empty. No test anywhere references isPlausibleAzureConfig or tenant-ID shape; `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/auth.test.ts` passes 4/4 and covers only requireAuth/authStatus enforcement, not config format.

TWO CORRECTIONS to the finder. (a) The fleet variant works, but not by the route implied: `build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json:19-21` uses TOP-LEVEL `azureClientId/azureTenantId/azureAllowedDomain`, whereas `azureFromManagedContent` (auth.ts:52-62) requires a NESTED `{ azure: {...} }` block that the example lacks — so `readManagedAzure()` returns {}. The placeholders instead reach auth via `src/main/store.ts:445-446` (`base = { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, ...validatedManaged() }`) and then `readSettingsAzure()`. Same brick, different path. It is also mitigated: that file's own `_comment` says "Replace placeholder IDs and URLs before rollout." (b) Severity: the code's own comment is right that this is fail-closed — no bypass, no data loss, no unauthorized access, and it requires an operator misconfiguration. Recovery exists outside the app (edit userData/settings.json, delete the profile, or set all three AZURE_*/ASKTOTO_ALLOWED_DOMAIN env vars, which outrank Settings at auth.ts:149-154). That is an unrecoverable-in-app brick for misconfigured installs, not an all-users or security-class defect, so high rather than critical.

Fix is small: enforce `/^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-([0-9a-fA-F]{4}-){3}[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$/` on tenantId in isPlausibleAzureConfig (trivial on its own), plus a case-insensitive compare at auth.ts:754 and an escape hatch on the wall for the already-bricked population.

### MQA-028 — Every privileged IPC call spawns 3+ synchronous PowerShell Get-Acl probes on a managed Windows install, blocking the main process

**Where.** `src/main/win-security.ts:103` · workflow: change any setting / ask a question / index meetings on an IT-managed Windows install · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/win-security.ts:118-126 — "The ACL verdict is deliberately NOT cached. ... Since the ACL check IS the security gate, and callers do a separate readFileSync for content after calling this, the verdict must be fresh on every call. Perf is fine: callers already sit behind getSettings()'s own mtime-keyed cache (store.ts), so this doesn't run on every settings read."

**Actual.** That premise is false for four hot callers, which each invoke readTrustedAdminManaged() OUTSIDE getSettings()'s cache, and each call runs execFileSync(WINDOWS_POWERSHELL, ['-NoProfile','-NonInteractive','-Command', <Get-Acl script>], { timeout: 8000 }) at src/main/win-security.ts:103 (via readAcl at :220): src/main/store.ts:197 (getLockedKeys), src/main/store.ts:210 (getAllowedProviders), src/main/auth.ts:68 (readManagedAzure), src/main/auth.ts:606 (authEnforced). requireAuth() at src/main/auth.ts:633-638 fires three of them by itself — authStatus()->readConfig()->readManagedAzure() (auth.ts:572/68), authStatus()'s `enforced: authEnforced()` (auth.ts:595), then authEnforced() again (auth.ts:635) — and requireAuth() is the first line of every privileged handler.

**Repro.** Windows install with the machine policy file deployed at C:\ProgramData\Métis\managed-config.json (the enterprise path adminManagedConfigPath() returns, win-security.ts:40-41). Flip one toggle in Settings: IPC.settingsSet (src/main/index.ts:1907) runs requireAuth() = 3 PowerShell launches, then setSettings -> getLockedKeys = 1, then getSettings (cache just invalidated) -> validatedManaged + getLockedKeys = 2, then publicSettings -> getAllowedProviders (index.ts:843) + getLockedKeys (index.ts:908) = 2 → 8 blocking powershell.exe spawns, each with an 8 s timeout budget, before the handler returns. At a typical 300-600 ms cold PowerShell start that is ~2.5-5 s with the entire main process frozen (overlay, global hotkeys, an in-flight meeting stream). Same shape per question (askStart: requireAuth + getAllowedProviders at index.ts:2768) and per brain-ingest queue tick (brain/ingest.ts:85 and :92 call getAllowedProviders twice per pickProviderCandidates, and pump() calls hasUsableProvider per tick at ingest.ts:1607). On a machine with no ProgramData policy file openSync throws first (win-security.ts:212) and zero probes run — which is exactly why this never shows up outside the managed deployment the branch is hardening.

**Suggested fix.** Resolve the machine policy ONCE per IPC turn and pass the parsed object down (validatedManaged / getLockedKeys / getAllowedProviders / authEnforced / readManagedAzure all re-derive it from the same bytes), or add a short-lived verdict+content memo in win-security.ts keyed on a cheap freshness signal (e.g. re-probe at most every N seconds and on window focus) instead of on file content metadata — the reason the old mtime+size key was removed does not apply to a time-bounded memo. Failing that, make the ACL probe async so it can never block the main process.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; reproduced the full causal chain and found the repo's own tests confirm the cost.

NO CACHE EXISTS. src/main/win-security.ts has exactly one piece of module state, `let warnedUntrusted = false` (win-security.ts:127), which latches only the log line in warnUntrusted(), not the probe. readAcl() runs execFileSync(WINDOWS_POWERSHELL, ['-NoProfile','-NonInteractive','-Command', <Get-Acl>], { timeout: 8000 }) at win-security.ts:103 on every call, and readTrustedAdminManaged() calls it unconditionally at win-security.ts:220 once openSync (win-security.ts:212) succeeds.

THE "INTENDED" QUOTE IS VERBATIM AND ITS PREMISE IS FALSE. win-security.ts:124-126 states "Perf is fine: callers already sit behind getSettings()'s own mtime-keyed cache (store.ts), so this doesn't run on every settings read." getSettings() (store.ts:432) does key its cache on safeMtime(adminManagedConfigPath()) — a statSync, no PowerShell — and only calls validatedManaged() on a miss. But six callers sit OUTSIDE that cache and each calls readTrustedAdminManaged() with zero memoization: getLockedKeys (store.ts:195-200), getAllowedProviders (store.ts:207-217, first statement, no early return above it), readManagedAzure (auth.ts:68), authEnforced (auth.ts:606), plus two the finder missed — updater.ts:26 and transcripts.ts:96.

requireAuth() = 3 PROBES, CONFIRMED BY TRACE. requireAuth (auth.ts:633) -> authStatus() -> readConfig() (auth.ts:572/140); env tier misses on a managed install -> readManagedAzure() (auth.ts:155/68) = probe 1. authStatus()'s `enforced: authEnforced()` (auth.ts:595) -> ASKTOTO_REQUIRE_AUTH unset -> readTrustedAdminManaged() (auth.ts:606) = probe 2. requireAuth line 635 calls authEnforced() again = probe 3. Only an all-env deployment (AZURE_CLIENT_ID/AZURE_TENANT_ID/ASKTOTO_ALLOWED_DOMAIN and ASKTOTO_REQUIRE_AUTH) short-circuits both — an alternative deployment style, not a guard. requireAuth() appears at 82 call sites in src/main/index.ts.

SETTINGS-SET COUNT VERIFIED ~8. index.ts:1912 requireAuth() = 3; store.ts:536 getLockedKeys in setSettings = 1; publicSettings' getSettings() now cache-missed (settings.json mtime changed) -> validatedManaged() (store.ts:186) + getLockedKeys (store.ts:476) = 2; index.ts:843 getAllowedProviders + index.ts:908 getLockedKeys = 2. Same shape per ask (index.ts:2775 getAllowedProviders after requireAuth).

MEASURED COST FROM THE REPO'S OWN TESTS. ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/win-security.test.ts passes 16/16 on this Windows box; the two live-ACL cases take ~1.6 s EACH for a SINGLE probe (1572 ms / 1643 ms). src/main/win-security.test.ts:193-196 admits "the ACL read spawns System32 powershell.exe with an 8s execFileSync timeout, which already exceeds vitest's 5s per-test default", and both cases carry an explicit 20_000 ms budget. At that rate the ~8 probes per settings change block the main process substantially longer than the finder's 2.5-5 s estimate. execFileSync is synchronous, so the whole main process (overlay, global hotkeys, in-flight meeting stream) is frozen.

SCOPE (the only real mitigation): openSync at win-security.ts:212 throws when %ProgramData%\Métis\managed-config.json is absent, so zero probes run outside a managed install — which is why this is invisible except in the enterprise deployment this branch hardens. Bounds blast radius to enterprise installs; does not refute.

MINOR CORRECTION TO THE FINDER: pump() (brain/ingest.ts:1602-1607) short-circuits via `if (j.origin !== 'backfill' || j.strategy === 'reconcile') return true`, so hasUsableProvider -> pickProviderCandidates -> getAllowedProviders (ingest.ts:85, :92) only fires for backfill jobs, not every tick. Real but narrower.

SEVERITY: high, not critical — availability/perf degradation confined to managed Windows installs, no data loss or security bypass (the gate still fails closed correctly). FIX: small, and it need not weaken the correct security argument at win-security.ts:118-123 (an mtime+size key is genuinely blind to Set-Acl); a short wall-clock TTL memo or a single per-IPC read threaded through requireAuth()/publicSettings() collapses 8 spawns to 1.

### MQA-029 — Codex CLI is silently dropped from the meeting-index provider waterfall because it has no configured model id

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:108` · workflow: index meetings / Mantu Intelligence brain extraction · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:2806-2809 — "CLI providers (e.g. codex-cli) may have no configured model at all — attempt() below already exempts kind==='cli' from the \"no model\" ineligibility check (the CLI just uses its own default), so a failover candidate must be exempted the same way or a fully default-configured CLI provider can never be selected." The same exemption is honoured in the imported-recap waterfall at src/main/index.ts:670 (`if (def.kind === 'cli') return !!settings.cliConnected[provider]`, returning before the model check), and src/main/cli.ts:379 explicitly supports an empty model for codex (`...(model ? ['-m', model] : [])`).

**Actual.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:107-108 applies the model check to EVERY provider with no CLI exemption: `const model = resolveModelTier(p, s.providerModels, s.providerModelsThinking, 'deep', s.providerModelsDeep); if (!model) continue`. PROVIDERS['codex-cli'] (src/shared/providers.ts:275-290) has models: [], defaultModel: '', fastModel: '', thinkModel: '' and no deepModel, so resolveModelTier returns '' for every tier and codex-cli is skipped even when s.cliConnected['codex-cli'] is true.

**Repro.** Install where the only AI connection is Codex CLI (onboarding step 5's "Claude Code or Codex" tile sets provider='codex-cli' via chooseCli, Onboarding.tsx:565), no API keys. Click Index meetings with a saved meeting. pickProviderCandidates walks p='codex-cli': connected=true (ingest.ts:104), model='' → `continue`. With the shipped defaults (localLlm.enabled/fallback true, ipc.ts:881/905) the meeting is instead extracted by the bundled 0.8B on-device model appended at ingest.ts:119-121 — the user's Codex subscription is never used and extraction quality silently drops to the small model. Turn Local AI off in Settings (localLlm.enabled=false), or deploy an allowedProviders policy that omits 'local', and hasUsableProvider() (ingest.ts:71-73) returns false → startBackfill returns { queued: 0, deferred: 'no-provider' } (ingest.ts:1868) and startRebuild returns "Connect an AI provider in Settings → AI..." (ingest.ts:1753) while Codex CLI is connected and happily answering chat questions.

**Suggested fix.** Mirror the ask path's exemption in pickProviderCandidates: `if (def.kind !== 'cli' && !model) continue` (keep pushing `model` as-is so cli.ts falls back to the CLI's own default for codex and to 'sonnet' for claude-cli per cli.ts:333). Add a regression test alongside src/main/brain/ingest-index-fallback.test.ts asserting a codex-cli-only, local-disabled profile yields one candidate rather than deferred:'no-provider'.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; every link reproduces from source.

CAUSAL CHAIN VERIFIED:
1. src/shared/providers.ts:275-290 — PROVIDERS['codex-cli'] has models: [], defaultModel: '', fastModel: '', thinkModel: '', and NO deepModel key.
2. src/shared/providers.ts:497-515 — resolveModelTier tier 'deep' returns `deep || def.deepModel || think || base || def.defaultModel || ''`; all terms empty/undefined for codex-cli → ''. Corroborated by the existing assertion src/shared/providers.test.ts:172 (applyInteractiveGuardrail('codex-cli','base','') === ''); ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/shared/providers.test.ts → 36/36 pass.
3. src/main/brain/ingest.ts:104 correctly branches on def.kind === 'cli' for connectivity (!!s.cliConnected[p]), then line 107-108 applies `if (!model) continue` with NO cli exemption → codex-cli passes the connect gate and is dropped one line later. claude-cli survives only because its deepModel is 'opus', so this is not a deliberate "no CLI in ingest" policy.

INTENDED-BEHAVIOR QUOTE IS ACCURATE and load-bearing in two independent places, not one: src/main/index.ts:2806-2811 (failover filter: `PROVIDERS[p].kind === 'cli' || !!resolveModelTier(...)`) and the ineligibility chain it cites at src/main/index.ts:2907 (`def.kind !== 'cli' && !model`). The imported-recap waterfall exempts CLI the same way at src/main/index.ts:670, returning before its resolveModelTier check at line 673. src/main/cli.ts:368-380 omits -m when model is empty, and src/main/cli.ts:220 documents that "the brain-ingest path can deliver a model string without going through the interactive guardrail" — brain ingest is expected to reach CLI providers.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED (no guard/caller/default/test covers it):
- Schema default: src/shared/ipc.ts:1068-1070 — providerModels = { dust: ... } only; Thinking/Deep = {}.
- No code seeds a codex-cli model: the only providerModels writes in src/main are Dust-specific (index.ts:888, 2781, 2896, 3772). IPC.cliTest (src/main/index.ts:2271-2276) writes only cliConnected. Onboarding choose() (Onboarding.tsx:538-541) patches only { provider }.
- No UI can supply one: CLI_PROVIDERS (Settings.tsx:138) excludes claude-cli/codex-cli from the generic model+key section; renderCliCard (Settings.tsx:1694-1800) offers connect/disconnect only, no model field.
- No test guards it: no test under src/main/brain sets cliConnected; ingest-backfill.test.ts:53 and ingest-team.test.ts:41 stub CLI env keys to '' and never exercise the CLI branch.

IMPACT, both branches confirmed: with shipped defaults (localLlm.enabled/fallback default true, useFor.summary default false — src/shared/ipc.ts:881,905,908-913) the bundled 0.8B appended at ingest.ts:119-121 silently serves every meeting extraction instead of the user's Codex subscription, with no user-visible signal. With Local AI off, or an allowedProviders policy omitting 'local', pickProviderCandidates returns [] → hasUsableProvider false (ingest.ts:71-73) → startBackfill returns { queued: 0, deferred: 'no-provider' } (ingest.ts:1865-1869) and startRebuild returns "Connect an AI provider in Settings → AI..." (ingest.ts:1752-1754) while codex-cli is connected and answering interactive asks normally.

Severity kept at high: a whole intended user segment (the ChatGPT/Codex-only install the codex-cli tile is marketed for, Onboarding.tsx:562-565) never gets their paid provider used for the core Mantu Intelligence pipeline, and one settings toggle away it becomes a hard block behind a message that contradicts reality.

Fix: one line — `if (def.kind !== 'cli' && !model) continue` at ingest.ts:107-108, mirroring index.ts:2810 and index.ts:670; runCompletionOnce/streamCli already tolerate model === '' (src/main/llm/cli.ts:5-18 → src/main/cli.ts:370-379).

### MQA-030 — "Disregard" silently keeps the meeting on a profile with no AI provider — the transcript stays on disk and is ingested/published

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1701` · workflow: discard a just-finished meeting · fix size: small · **regression**

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/Review.tsx:129-131 — "Discard this meeting instead of keeping it — deletes the saved file (main pops a native confirm) then leaves the review. Sits next to Save so 'keep' vs 'throw away' is one clear choice."  src/renderer/src/App.tsx:528-533 — "…a click landing in that window used to read savedPath as still null, skip the delete branch entirely, and let the save land moments later anyway."  Pinned by src/renderer/src/App.local-gates.test.ts:179-200 ("Disregard-vs-autosave race (finding 7)").

**Actual.** src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1491-1498: when `!settings?.providerReady`, maybeFireRecap calls `ask.clear()` and persists the meeting via `void saveMeetingNowRef.current?.(...)` (line 1497). saveMeetingNow (App.tsx:1544-1575) deliberately writes NEITHER savedPath NOR savingPromiseRef NOR savedRef ("deliberately does NOT write the live session's savedRef/savedPath", App.tsx:1552-1554). discardMeeting (App.tsx:1695-1708) only inspects `savingPromiseRef.current` and `savedPath`, so `path` is null (line 1701), the `if (path)` delete branch at 1702 is skipped entirely, no confirm dialog appears, and reset() runs.

**Repro.** Profile with no AI provider connected (onboarding "Decide later" — settings.providerReady === false). Start a meeting, speak a few lines, press Stop. Review shows "Connect a provider to get an AI summary. Your transcript is saved either way." The transcript file has already been written by App.tsx:1497. Click **Disregard**. Expected: native confirm, then the .md is deleted. Actual: no dialog at all, Review closes, and the .md (plus its index.md row) is still in the meetings folder, gets brain-ingested and, when publishing is on, published to wiki/meetings/<slug>.md — a recording the user explicitly threw away.

**Suggested fix.** Make saveMeetingNow report its outcome: have it resolve to the saved path, store the promise in savingPromiseRef (and set savedRef on success) whenever it is saving the CURRENT live session (as opposed to the exit-path rescue). Minimally, in the keyless branch at App.tsx:1497 assign `savingPromiseRef.current = saveMeetingNow(...)` and set savedPath from its result so discardMeeting's existing await-then-delete path covers it.

**Verifier.** I tried to refute this on four fronts (a guard in Review, a second savedPath writer, the autosave effect firing anyway, an existing test/regression pin) and all four failed.

1. The keyless save really does happen and really does bypass every handle discardMeeting reads. D:\Asktoto\src\renderer\src\App.tsx:1491-1498 — on `!settings?.providerReady`, maybeFireRecap sets recapSkipped, calls `ask.clear()`, then `void saveMeetingNowRef.current?.(listen.lines, meetingStartRef.current, '')`. saveMeetingNow (App.tsx:1544-1575) calls `await window.toto.saveTranscript(payload)` (line 1563) and discards the returned path; its own comment (1551-1557) states it "deliberately does NOT write the live session's savedRef/savedPath". I grepped every writer: `setSavedPath` occurs at only App.tsx:382 (declaration), :514 (manualSave), :568 (doSave inside the recap autosave effect), and :1430 (reset-to-null in startListen). `savingPromiseRef.current` is assigned at only :585 and :589 (both inside doSave's effect) and :1431 (null in startListen). So in the keyless flow both are null.

2. The recap autosave effect cannot rescue it. App.tsx:535-593 requires `settled = !answerStreaming && (!!answerText || !!answerError)` (line 543). maybeFireRecap's keyless branch calls `ask.clear()` before returning and never calls `ask.run`, so ask.answer is null → answerText '' and answerError null → `settled` false → doSave never runs → savedPath/savingPromiseRef stay null.

3. discardMeeting (App.tsx:1695-1708) reads exactly those two: `const inFlightPath = savingPromiseRef.current ? await savingPromiseRef.current : null` (1700) and `const path = inFlightPath ?? savedPath` (1701). Both null → the `if (path)` block at 1702-1705 (the only call to `window.toto.recallDelete`, i.e. the only thing that pops main's native confirm at src\main\index.ts:2422-2432) is skipped entirely → savedRef pinned, reset() runs, review closes with zero feedback. The function's own doc comment at App.tsx:1693-1694 asserts the now-false invariant: "A session that never saved (no savedPath) has nothing on disk — just leave."

4. No guard hides the button and no test pins this. App.tsx:2371 passes `onDiscard={pm ? undefined : discardMeeting}` — unconditional for a live session, independent of savedPath — and Review.tsx:507-509 renders it with no disabled/gating condition (contrast the Save button at :502, which does gate on savedPath). The cited intended-behavior quote at Review.tsx:129-131 is verbatim and does say the file is deleted with a native confirm. I ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/App.local-gates.test.ts — 35/35 pass; the "Disregard-vs-autosave race (finding 7)" block (test:179-200) only asserts source-text shape of the doSave-promise handshake and never touches the keyless/saveMeetingNow path, so it passes while the hole is open.

Consequence is confirmed downstream, not speculative: src\main\index.ts:3175-3196 (IPC.saveTranscript) writes the meeting, then `scheduleRebuild()` (3187) and `await enqueueIngest(r.path)` (3190) — so ingestion is already queued at save time and the wiki mirror publishes to `meetings/<slug>.md` when publishBrainPages is on (src\main\brain\publish.ts:193, 269, 409/499/719 gates). Discarding afterwards removes nothing.

Severity stays high: a user's explicit "throw this away" is silently ignored (no dialog, no error, no toast) for any keyless profile — the exact profile the onboarding "Decide later" path creates — and the retained transcript flows into the brain index and, with publishing on, into the wiki. Not critical only because it needs providerReady === false. Fix is small: have the keyless branch capture the save (assign `savingPromiseRef.current` to a promise resolving to the saved path, or set savedPath) rather than fire-and-forget through the leave-path saver — the only care needed is preserving saveMeetingNow's deliberate "don't pollute the next session" contract, e.g. via a live-session variant/flag instead of changing saveMeetingNow itself.

### MQA-031 — publishAll re-reads and re-decrypts every saved meeting once per entity AND once per note card — synchronous main-process freeze on a real corpus

**Where.** `src/main/brain/publish.ts:411` · workflow: flag a meeting confidential / enable wiki publishing · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/brain/publish.ts:126-129 — "basenames of every saved meeting flagged `confidential: true`… Read fresh on every publish call (no cache) — **this runs once per publish/index-regen, not per keystroke**, and correctness… matters far more than the cost of a handful of extra file reads at this app's single-exec scale."

**Actual.** It does not run once per publish. publishAll (publish.ts:803-814) calls publishEntity for every person/account/deal and publishMeetingCard for every meeting extraction; publishEntity calls readConfidentialMeetings at publish.ts:411, publishMeetingCard at publish.ts:503, publishIndexes at publish.ts:721. readConfidentialMeetings (publish.ts:131-143) does a full `readdirSync` plus a synchronous `readSavedFile` (readFileSync + AES-GCM decrypt when encryptTranscripts is on, src/main/transcripts.ts:261-263) of EVERY meeting .md. Total = (entities + meetings + 1) x meetings blocking reads. publishForExtraction (publish.ts:780-798) multiplies it again: ~5-10 full scans per ingested meeting.

**Repro.** Profile with 300 saved meetings (so ~700-1000 brain entities). Open a meeting in Review and click the **Confidential** toggle -> src/main/index.ts:2472 fires `void publishAll(s)` -> roughly 1000 x 300 = 300,000 synchronous full-file reads/decrypts on the main process. The overlay, global hotkeys, tray and every IPC handler are frozen for minutes; the Confidential chip stays in its optimistic state with no progress indication. The same storm runs for every meeting ingested during a brain backfill via publishForExtraction.

**Suggested fix.** Compute the confidential set once per publish operation and thread it through: give publishEntity/publishMeetingCard an optional `confidential: Set<string>` parameter that publishAll/publishForExtraction/publishIndexes build a single time, falling back to readConfidentialMeetings(s) only when the caller supplies nothing.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED — I could not refute it.

Chain verified line by line:
1. src/main/brain/publish.ts:131-143 `readConfidentialMeetings` has no cache and no early exit. It calls `listSavedMeetingFiles` (110-114, a `readdirSync` of the flat meetings folder returned by `resolveMeetingsFolder`, transcripts.ts:515-530) and then `readSavedFile(join(folder, f))` for EVERY saved meeting `.md`.
2. src/main/transcripts.ts:261-263 `readSavedFile` = `decodeSaved(readFileSync(path))` — a fully synchronous whole-file read. The meeting `.md` contains the entire `## Full transcript` body, so these are large files. With `encryptTranscripts` on, each read also runs `decryptEnvelopeV2` (transcripts.ts:171-216): a per-file `safeStorage.decryptString` DPAPI unwrap on packaged Windows (`S:` envelopes) plus a full AES-256-GCM decrypt of the ciphertext. Only the frontmatter is then used (readFrontmatterFlag, 119-124).
3. It is invoked unconditionally at the top of publishEntity (publish.ts:411 — BEFORE `readPerson`/`readAccount`/`readDeal`), publishMeetingCard (503 — BEFORE the `existsSync(path)` guard at 510), and publishIndexes (721). The only earlier bail is `!s.publishBrainPages || !id`.
4. publishAll (803-814) iterates `listEntities` for person/account/deal (store.ts:459-466, unbounded `readdirSync`) calling publishEntity for each, then `listMeetingExtractions` (store.ts:468-474) calling publishMeetingCard for each, then publishIndexes. So full-corpus scans = (#entities + #meeting-extractions + 1), each scan = M synchronous read+decrypts. O(N x M).
5. publishForExtraction (780-798) does ~(1 account + N people + 1 deal + 1 card) scans per merge and is called from src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1348 on every merge, live AND backfill — so a 300-meeting backfill repeats the storm ~5x per meeting.

Refutations I tried and that failed:
- No cache/memo anywhere: repo-wide grep shows only 4 call sites of readConfidentialMeetings (publish.ts:411/503/721, graphify.ts:268). No TTL, no module-level Set, no mtime cache. store.ts's JSON cache (referenced at corrections.ts:442) covers entity JSON reads only, not readSavedFile.
- No sidecar index of confidential state that would avoid the scan: setMeetingConfidential (src/main/recall.ts:554+) writes `confidential:` into the meeting file's own frontmatter and nowhere else, so scanning every meeting file really is the only current source of truth.
- Not offloaded: grep for `utilityProcess|new Worker|worker_threads|child_process.fork` under src/main/ returns nothing. This is all main-process.
- No throttle/dedupe on the caller: src/main/index.ts:2496 is a bare `void publishAll(s)` inside the recallSetConfidential handler (and index.ts:1993 on enabling the setting) — no debounce, no in-flight guard, so two rapid toggles run two concurrent storms.
- No existing test guards it: `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/publish.test.ts` = 20/20 passing, but the largest fixture (publish.test.ts:361-386) is 2 meetings / 3 entities ≈ 12 reads. Correctness tests pass because this is purely a cost defect.

Corrections to the finder:
- Line cite: the publishAll call is src/main/index.ts:2496, not 2472 (2472 is the recallUpdateRecap zod parse).
- "Frozen for minutes" overstates the shape: writeWikiFile -> writeSaved uses fs/promises, so real async I/O yields between iterations. It is a back-to-back storm of blocking chunks (one full corpus scan each, hundreds of ms on a 300-meeting corpus) rather than one uninterrupted block; cumulative main-thread block time is unchanged. Note the very first publishEntity's scan runs synchronously before the IPC handler returns.
- The 1000-entity figure is an assumption, but even a conservative 150 entities + 300 cards + 1 gives ~450 scans x 300 files = 135,000 blocking read+decrypts per toggle.
- The "intended" quote is directionally supported but slightly loose: "Read fresh on every publish call" is literally accurate; the mischaracterization is in the cost estimate ("a handful of extra file reads at this app's single-exec scale"), which is wrong by 4-5 orders of magnitude under publishAll/publishForExtraction.

Severity kept at high: gated behind an opt-in `publishBrainPages` (default false, src/shared/ipc.ts:723/1094) and needing a real corpus, but for the users of that feature it is 100% deterministic, sits on the core ingest path too, and blocks the process that owns the capture overlay, global hotkeys, tray and every IPC handler on a live meeting recorder. No data loss or security impact, which is what keeps it off critical.

Fix is small and surgical: compute the Set once and thread it as an optional param, e.g. publishEntity(s, kind, id, confidential?) / publishMeetingCard(s, file, confidential?) defaulting to readConfidentialMeetings(s), with publishAll, publishIndexes and publishForExtraction each computing it once and passing it down. ~10-15 lines plus call-site updates; the existing determinism and confidentiality tests already cover the behavior it must preserve.

### MQA-032 — "Delete all Métis data" unlinks EVERY .md in the meetings folder, including the user's own unrelated markdown files, while the confirm dialog only counts real meetings

**Where.** `src/main/recall.ts:612` · workflow: Delete all my data (GDPR/CCPA erasure) from Settings · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/recall.ts:650 (sweepExpiredMeetings, the sibling bulk-delete path) states the rule this file follows elsewhere: `if (!m) continue // unrecognized filename shape — never guess an age, skip rather than risk deleting the wrong file`. src/main/index.ts:2526-2533 builds the confirmation from the parsed-meeting count only — `const meetings = await listMeetings()` … `message: \`Delete all ${meetings.length} saved meeting${meetings.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}?\``, with detail `'This permanently removes every saved transcript, note, and the knowledge graph from this device.'` — and listMeetings drops anything that is not a Métis file at src/main/recall.ts:126 `if (fm.type && fm.type !== 'meeting-transcript') return null`.

**Actual.** src/main/recall.ts:612 `const files = await meetingFiles(folder)` and the unlink loop at src/main/recall.ts:615-622 delete by FILE EXTENSION only. meetingFiles (src/main/recall.ts:23-32) returns every `e.isFile() && e.name.endsWith('.md')` except README.md/index.md — no frontmatter check, no `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS-` filename check, unlike sweepExpiredMeetings. The meetings folder is an arbitrary user-chosen directory: src/main/index.ts:3661-3666 `properties: ['openDirectory', 'createDirectory']` … `setSettings({ meetingsFolder: r.filePaths[0] })`.

**Repro.** 1. Settings → Meetings & transcripts → Change folder → pick an existing notes directory, e.g. `D:\Notes`, which already contains `ideas.md`, `todo.md`, `2026-budget.md` (the user's own files, not Métis's). 2. Record/save one meeting there, so `2026-08-07_101500-standup.md` exists. 3. Settings → Delete all my data. The dialog reads "Delete all 1 saved meeting?" (listMeetings parsed exactly one `type: meeting-transcript`). 4. Confirm. Result: `ideas.md`, `todo.md` and `2026-budget.md` are also permanently unlinked (recall.ts:617), the returned `deleted` count is 4, and there is no undo and no backup. The user was told 1 file would go and lost 4.

**Suggested fix.** Give deleteAllMeetings the same identity gate the rest of the module already uses: iterate meetingFiles(folder) but only unlink a file that either matches `FILENAME_TIMESTAMP` / the `.autosave-draft-` prefix, or whose decoded frontmatter carries `type: meeting-transcript` / `type: note` / `type: meeting-transcript-draft` (reuse readMeeting, and treat `isEncryptedFile(path) === true` as "ours" for undecryptable envelopes). Report skipped foreign files in the result so the dialog count and the deletion set can never diverge.

**Verifier.** CORE MECHANISM CONFIRMED — could not refute. src/main/recall.ts:23-32 `meetingFiles()` returns every `e.isFile() && e.name.endsWith('.md')` except README.md/index.md, with no frontmatter, filename, or ownership check. src/main/recall.ts:610-622 `deleteAllMeetings()` iterates exactly that list and calls `unlink(join(folder, file))` on each — permanent (unlink, not shell.trashItem), no backup, no undo. The sibling rule the finder cites is verbatim at recall.ts:650: `if (!m) continue // unrecognized filename shape — never guess an age, skip rather than risk deleting the wrong file`. The folder really is arbitrary: index.ts:3722-3736 persists `r.filePaths[0]` raw (`setSettings({ meetingsFolder: r.filePaths[0] })`, no subfolder appended), src/shared/ipc.ts:769 is `meetingsFolder: z.string().default('')` with no validation, resolveMeetingsFolder (transcripts.ts:515-518) returns it unchanged, and Settings.tsx:4830-4843 offers no warning that Métis will own the folder. No guard, caller, or schema default prevents it. src/main/recall.test.ts:141-179 covers only Métis-authored files; ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/recall.test.ts — 27/27 pass, so this is live code, nothing stubbed.

PARTIALLY REFUTED — the finder's repro narrative is wrong as written. The claim that listMeetings "drops anything that is not a Métis file at recall.ts:126" overstates that line. tryDecodeSaved (transcripts.ts:251) returns `buf.toString('utf8')` for any non-encrypted file; frontmatter() (recall.ts:12-21) returns {} when there is no `---` block; the filter is `if (fm.type && fm.type !== 'meeting-transcript') return null` — it only drops files carrying an EXPLICIT `type:` key. Plain notes like `ideas.md`, `todo.md`, `2026-budget.md` have no frontmatter, so fm.type is undefined and they ARE returned as summaries (title = filename, date = ''), with no further filter in listMeetings (recall.ts:147-154). The dialog at index.ts:2558-2565 would read "Delete all 4 saved meetings?", not "Delete all 1 saved meeting?". The stated "told 1, lost 4" undercount only occurs for user files carrying a `type:` key with another value (e.g. Obsidian/Dataview `type: book`), and even then only with LF line endings, since the frontmatter regex /^---\n/ will not match a CRLF file. So the misleading-count amplifier is a narrow subcase, not the general case.

WHAT SURVIVES: the destructive half. The user's own unrelated .md files in the chosen folder are permanently unlinked by an action whose dialog only promises to remove "every saved transcript, note, and the knowledge graph" (index.ts:2564-2565) — nothing puts non-Métis markdown in scope — and deleteAllMeetings has no ownership predicate while its sibling sweep at recall.ts:650 explicitly does.

SEVERITY CORRECTED critical -> high. Permanent unrecoverable loss of data outside the app's ownership is genuine, but gated on an off-path precondition (pointing the transcripts folder at a directory already holding the user's markdown; default is a dedicated `Métis Meetings` folder, transcripts.ts:527) plus a deliberate "Danger zone" erase behind a two-step, defaultId/cancelId=1 confirm saying "This cannot be undone." In the common no-frontmatter case the count shown is accurate, so the user is misled about which files qualify, not about volume.

FIX small: give deleteAllMeetings the ownership predicate the file already uses (FILENAME_TIMESTAMP / DRAFT_FILENAME shape, or delete only what listMeetings/lockedStub resolved) and report the real count. Not trivial only because the predicate must still erase locked/undecryptable meetings and `.autosave-draft-*.md` drafts to remain a genuine GDPR wipe.

### MQA-033 — A transient read error on one meeting file makes it vanish from History and Search, and the failure is cached so it stays invisible for the rest of the session

**Where.** `src/main/recall.ts:141` · workflow: Browse / search past meetings in History · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/recall.ts:61-63: `/** Best-effort display stub for an undecryptable-but-real meeting file, so it stays visible (instead of silently vanishing) with a lock affordance. …*/`, and src/main/recall.ts:117-121: `// decodeSaved returns '' both for "not a meeting file" and for a REAL meeting encrypted at rest that this device's keychain can't decrypt … Only the latter should still show up, as a locked stub, so it never just vanishes`. src/main/transcripts.ts:292-295 documents that this exact folder routinely produces transient I/O errors and that they must not lose data: `The default meetings folder lives under OneDrive, which routinely holds a just-written file open (upload hashing) or gets grabbed by AV/EDR real-time scanning — rename() then throws EPERM/EBUSY on Windows even though nothing is actually wrong. Bounded retry rides out that transient lock instead of losing the save`.

**Actual.** readMeetingUncached wraps the whole read in `try { const text = decodeSaved(await readFile(path)) … } catch { return null }` (src/main/recall.ts:114-143, catch at 141-143). An I/O failure is indistinguishable from "not a meeting" — it returns null, so listMeetings (recall.ts:150-151) and searchMeetings (recall.ts:667-668) filter the meeting out entirely, and the locked-stub fallback at recall.ts:121 can never fire because `isEncryptedFile` (transcripts.ts:266-272) also swallows its own read error and returns false. Worse, readMeeting caches that null: `readCache.set(path, { mtimeMs, size, read })` at src/main/recall.ts:109, keyed on the stat() that already succeeded. The write path retries EPERM/EBUSY 5 times (transcripts.ts:296-305); the read path does not retry at all.

**Repro.** Windows, meetings folder under OneDrive with Files On-Demand. `2026-08-01_140000-renault.md` is a dehydrated cloud placeholder. Go offline (or let Defender hold the file open right after a sync). Open History: stat() succeeds (placeholder metadata is local, mtimeMs and size unchanged), readFile throws → recall.ts:141 returns null → the Renault meeting is absent from the list and returns zero hits for the search "renault", with no error, no Locked chip, no row. Reconnect: hydration does not change mtimeMs or size, so readMeeting hits the cached `{read: null}` at recall.ts:106 and the meeting stays invisible until the app is restarted (or 2000 other files evict the cache at recall.ts:108).

**Suggested fix.** Separate "cannot read" from "not a meeting". Catch the readFile/stat error explicitly, and (a) do not write it into readCache, (b) return a stub — reuse lockedStub() with an 'unreadable' reason, or a new `unavailable: true` flag on MeetingSummary — so the row stays in History with an explanatory affordance. Optionally give readFile the same bounded EPERM/EBUSY retry writeSaved already has.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED. I attempted four refutations; all failed.

1) Code chain verified verbatim. `readMeetingUncached` (D:\Asktoto\src\main\recall.ts:113-144) wraps `decodeSaved(await readFile(path))` in a try whose `catch { return null }` sits at 141-143. A rejected `readFile` short-circuits *before* line 116, so it never even reaches the locked-stub branch at 121 — it is indistinguishable from "not a meeting file". `listMeetings` (147-154) filters `r !== null`; `searchMeetings` (661-691) does `if (!r) continue`. Both IPC handlers (src\main\index.ts:3755-3762) return the array with no error channel, so the row and the search hit vanish with zero signal.

2) The null IS cached, keyed on a stat that already succeeded. `readMeetingUncached` resolves (never rejects), so recall.ts:107-109 unconditionally runs `readCache.set(path, { mtimeMs, size, read: null })`. Line 106 then serves that null on every later call while (mtimeMs, size) match. The comment at 85 only contemplates caching nulls for "non-meeting or undecryptable files" — the I/O-error null is an unintended member of that set.

3) Refutation attempt "some other path clears the cache": grep across src/ shows `readCache` is module-private, never exported, and mutated in exactly one function. The only invalidations are a *failed* stat (102, deletes the entry) and the 2000-entry `clear()` (108). No watcher, no settings-change hook, no post-save flush. Saved meetings are immutable-after-write, so mtime/size never move on their own — the poisoned entry survives until process exit.

4) Refutation attempt "stat and readFile fail together, so line 102 deletes the entry and it self-heals": disproved empirically on this Windows 11 box. I locked a file with FileShare.None and ran Node against it:
   `stat OK mtimeMs=1786216176856.5132 size=53` / `read FAIL EBUSY: resource busy or locked, open ...`
   and after releasing the lock: `after unlock: stat mtimeMs=1786216176856.5132 size=53 read len=53` — byte-identical mtimeMs and size. So the exact sequence the finder describes reproduces: stat succeeds, read throws EBUSY, null is cached, and recovery does not change the cache key, so recall.ts:106 keeps returning the cached null.

5) Refutation attempt "already-handled elsewhere": `isEncryptedFile` (src\main\transcripts.ts:266-273) does `catch { return false }`, so even a fixed catch that fell through to the stub would still drop the file. No retry exists on the read path, while the *same folder's* write paths retry EPERM/EBUSY five times at transcripts.ts:296-305 and 865-871, and the comment at 292-295 states these errors are routine there. `recallRead` (161-175) does return a proper error, but that path is only reachable by clicking a row that no longer renders.

6) Intended-behavior quotes check out verbatim at recall.ts:61-63, 117-121 and transcripts.ts:292-295. `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/recall.test.ts` passes 27/27; the locked-stub test at recall.test.ts:528-538 covers decode failure only (readFile succeeds), never a read throw — no existing test guards this.

Minor imprecision in the finding, not fatal: the stub at line 121 is unreachable because the throw skips it, not (only) because isEncryptedFile swallows its error — the finder's point holds as an "even then".

Severity high stands. Silent disappearance of a saved meeting from the product's core browse/search workflow, no error, no chip, no row, sticky for the whole session and recoverable only by an app restart the user has no reason to attempt. Realistic trigger: default meetings folder under OneDrive with Files On-Demand, an old meeting dehydrated by Storage Sense, user offline reviewing history — or a momentary AV/EDR share-lock, the exact condition this repo already retries around on write. Fix is small: return a distinct sentinel (or rethrow) for a thrown read so recall.ts:109 skips caching, plus an EPERM/EBUSY bounded retry mirroring transcripts.ts:296-305. Note the same cache pattern was copied into src\main\brain\store.ts:201, worth checking for the same defect.

### MQA-034 — Every ask and a 6-second background timer synchronously spawn PowerShell for the managed-config ACL probe (measured 1.5-1.9s per call)

**Where.** `src/main/store.ts:210` · workflow: Asking a question / background screen context / settings poll on a Windows machine with an admin managed-config deployed · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/win-security.ts:124-126 — "Since the ACL check IS the security gate, and callers do a separate readFileSync for content after calling this, the verdict must be fresh on every call. Perf is fine: callers already sit behind getSettings()'s own mtime-keyed cache (store.ts), so this doesn't run on every settings read."

**Actual.** `getAllowedProviders()` (src/main/store.ts:210) and `getLockedKeys()` (src/main/store.ts:197) call `readTrustedAdminManaged()` directly — they are NOT behind the getSettings() mtime cache (that cache only wraps `validatedManaged()`, store.ts:186). Those two are invoked outside the cache from: src/main/index.ts:2768 (`const allowed = getAllowedProviders()` inside the ask path), src/main/index.ts:843 + 908 (`publicSettings()`, which index.ts:1822 documents as running "on every renderer settings fetch"), and src/main/index.ts:1367 (`localReady: () => localBaseReady(getSettings(), getAllowedProviders())`), which src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:149 calls from `eligible()` on the `setInterval(onRefreshTick, REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS)` tick at screen-preprocess.ts:282/106 — every 6000 ms. Each call, when the policy file exists, runs `execFileSync(WINDOWS_POWERSHELL, ...)` (win-security.ts:103, 8000 ms timeout) synchronously on the main process.

**Repro.** Measured on this host: the repo's own live-ACL tests take 1857 ms and 1514 ms for a single isAdminManagedTrusted / readTrustedAdminManaged call (`./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/win-security.test.ts` → 'rejects a policy file planted by the current non-admin user' 1857ms, 'readTrustedAdminManaged never returns content' 1514ms); a bare Get-Acl round-trip measured 531-825 ms. So: Windows install + `%ProgramData%\Métis\managed-config.json` present (the documented enterprise deployment) + backgroundScreenContext on (explicitly seeded true for the Cahê pilot at src/main/cahe-embedded-key.ts:53) → the main process blocks for ~0.5-1.9 s every 6 s, forever: hotkeys, IPC, window paints and the update/audio main-side work all stall for 10-30% of wall-clock. Independently, every single ask pays one more blocking PowerShell spawn at index.ts:2768 before the request is sent.

**Suggested fix.** Cache the ACL verdict keyed on something that actually changes when the DACL changes — e.g. `(dev, ino, mtimeMs, size, ownerSid+DACL revision from a cheap probe)` — or, simpler and safe: keep the verdict fresh but make the probe cheap by replacing the PowerShell round-trip with a single long-lived helper/native call, and route getAllowedProviders()/getLockedKeys() through the same memoized `validatedManaged()` snapshot that getSettings() already invalidates. At minimum, do not call it from the 6 s screen-preprocess tick — hoist the allowlist into the cached settings snapshot.

**Verifier.** Reproduced the full chain; could not refute it.

1. The uncached path is real. src/main/store.ts:207-217 getAllowedProviders() and store.ts:195-200 getLockedKeys() call readTrustedAdminManaged() directly (store.ts:210 / :197), unconditionally and before any edition short-circuit. getSettings()'s mtime-keyed cache (store.ts:432-442) only wraps validatedManaged() (store.ts:185-192) and the getLockedKeys() call at store.ts:476 that sits inside the cache-miss body. Neither of the two exported accessors is behind it.

2. The "intended" quote is verbatim and does say what the finder claims: src/main/win-security.ts:124-126 — "Perf is fine: callers already sit behind getSettings()'s own mtime-keyed cache (store.ts), so this doesn't run on every settings read." That assumption is factually wrong for getAllowedProviders() (never behind the cache) and for getLockedKeys() when called from publicSettings()/setSettings().

3. Cost per call is a synchronous PowerShell spawn: win-security.ts:220 readAcl -> win-security.ts:103 execFileSync(WINDOWS_POWERSHELL, ['-NoProfile','-NonInteractive','-Command', ps], timeout 8000). execFileSync blocks the Electron main thread. Measured on this host with the byte-identical script: 1177/899/691/778/937 ms over 5 runs. The repo's own live-ACL tests in my run: 'rejects a policy file planted by the current non-admin user' 1438 ms, 'readTrustedAdminManaged never returns content' 1099 ms (./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/win-security.test.ts -> 16/16 pass).

4. Hot call sites confirmed (current worktree numbers; the finder's are ~10-26 lines off from a slightly older snapshot, same functions): publicSettings() calls getAllowedProviders() at src/main/index.ts:851 AND getLockedKeys() at index.ts:919 = 2 spawns per settingsGet, the handler index.ts:1838 documents as running "on every renderer settings fetch"; the ask path at index.ts:2794; index.ts:1378 localReady: () => localBaseReady(getSettings(), getAllowedProviders()) — the argument is evaluated eagerly, so localBaseReady's own `enabled` short-circuit (llm/local-routing.ts:52) does NOT avoid the spawn; src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:148-149 eligible() is the first statement of describeForWindow (line 197), fired by setInterval(onRefreshTick, REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS=6000) at screen-preprocess.ts:282/106. Plus store.ts:536, store.ts:724, brain/ingest.ts:85,92, graphify.ts:186.

5. Nothing already handles it: no guard, no cache, no schema default, no test asserting call counts. The single precondition is that %ProgramData%\Métis\managed-config.json exists (openSync at win-security.ts:212 throws -> null -> no spawn otherwise). That path is exactly what docs/ENTERPRISE-DEPLOY-WINDOWS.md:73 instructs IT to deploy and what build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json ships for, and cahe-embedded-key.ts:53-54 does seed backgroundScreenContext: true.

6. Detail the finder MISSED that strengthens it: readAcl runs BEFORE the trust verdict (win-security.ts:220-225), so an UNTRUSTED file triggers the spawn too, every call, with no negative caching. Since %ProgramData% grants BUILTIN\Users:Write (the entire premise of this module, win-security.ts:6-11), any standard user can plant that file and force ~1 s main-thread stalls per ask and per 6 s tick with zero elevation.

Minor overstatements in the report, not disqualifying: renderer window paints do not stall (separate process — only main-side IPC/hotkey/tray/update work does); and on Windows the 6 s tick also requires localLlm.enabled + runtime binary + model downloaded (local-routing.ts:51-56), because ocrAvailable() is false there (index.ts:1396), so the periodic path is narrower than "backgroundScreenContext on".

Severity: high stands. Not critical (no security or data-integrity impact, and it needs the policy file present), but within the deployment posture the product documents it is a continuous main-process freeze (~0.7-1.9 s) on every ask, every settings fetch (x2), and every 6 s under background screen context, on a real-time hotkey-driven assistant.

Fix complexity: small — but not a naive cache, since win-security.ts:118-126 correctly rejects a content-mtime-keyed verdict cache (Set-Acl changes the DACL without touching mtime/size). Contained options: route getAllowedProviders()/getLockedKeys() through the same mtime+cache envelope as getSettings(), coalesce the probe per operation, or give it a very short time-based TTL — all local to store.ts/win-security.ts.

### MQA-035 — Private View does not block the cached on-device screen description — screen:context and askStart hand it to a cloud provider for up to ~6s after the toggle

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:2681` · workflow: ask a screen question with Private View on · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:15 — "Private View hard-blocks it: getScreenshot() throws while it's on, and any cached description is dropped."  Reinforced by src/main/index.ts:1305-1307 — "Private View promises Métis won't look at (or send) the screen while it's on — that has to mean this app's own capture pipeline refuses to run" and index.ts:1334-1336 — "Without this second check, a frame grabbed a moment before the toggle would still be cached and sent to the model — breaking the Private View guarantee on a mid-capture toggle."

**Actual.** Neither read path checks Private View. `ipcMain.handle(IPC.screenContext, ...)` (src/main/index.ts:2678-2682) returns `screenPreprocess.currentFreshContext()` with no `privateViewOn()` gate, and the askStart injection at src/main/index.ts:2758 does the same. `currentFreshContext()` (src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:311-320) only checks TTL + window id. The cache is dropped ONLY when `describeForWindow` next runs (screen-preprocess.ts:198-201), i.e. on the 6s `REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` tick (screen-preprocess.ts:106, 282). `refreshScreenPreprocess()` on settings save (src/main/index.ts:1965) only calls `refresh()`, whose `eligible()` (screen-preprocess.ts:148-149) does not consider privateView, so flipping Private View neither stops the engine nor clears the cache.

**Repro.** Settings → AI: enable Métis Local (provisioned) and Settings → Privacy: turn on background screen context (`backgroundScreenContext`). Have any cloud provider keyed (`providerReady`). Let the engine cache a description of the current window at T=0. At T=1s turn Settings → Privacy → "Private View" ON. At T=2s type "what's on my screen?" → App.tsx:841 `window.toto.screenContext()` returns the cached description (age 2s < CONTEXT_TTL_MS 12000, same windowId) → App.tsx:844 runs `ask.run({mode:'answer', wantsScreenContext:true})` → index.ts:2758-2761 injects that description into the cloud request. On macOS that text can be a verbatim Vision-framework OCR extract of the screen (index.ts:2753-2755). Result: screen content leaves the device while Private View is on. Same leak for the whole ~6s window until the next refresh tick.

**Suggested fix.** Gate both read paths on `privateViewOn()`: return null from the `IPC.screenContext` handler and skip the `req.screenContext` injection in askStart when Private View is on. Better, make it structural — pass `privateViewOn` into `currentFreshContext()` (or have it consult `deps.privateViewOn()` directly) so every current and future caller inherits the block — and clear the cache eagerly by calling `screenPreprocess` on the `privateView` transition in `settingsSet` instead of waiting for the 6s tick. Add a regression test: `h.state.privateView = true; expect(h.sp.currentFreshContext()).toBeNull()` (the existing test at screen-preprocess.test.ts:173-184 only proves the cache is cleared by the NEXT describe, never that the read path is blocked).

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED after failing four refutation attempts.

1. Read paths ungated: src/main/index.ts:2697-2701 (IPC.screenContext handler) returns screenPreprocess.currentFreshContext() behind only assertMainWindow + requireAuth; the askStart injection reads the same accessor at src/main/index.ts:2777 inside the wantsScreenContext block (2775-2792). Neither calls privateViewOn(). A repo-wide grep for `privateView` shows it in screen-preprocess.ts ONLY at line 47 (dep declaration) and line 198 (inside describeForWindow) — the drop is structurally reachable only on a describe pass.

2. currentFreshContext() (src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:311-320) checks only non-empty description, CONTEXT_TTL_MS=12000, and window-id match. No privateView term.

3. Settings-save path does not help: refreshScreenPreprocess() (src/main/index.ts:1403-1409, called at src/main/index.ts:1976) calls refresh(), whose eligible() (screen-preprocess.ts:148-149) tests only backgroundScreenContext && (localReady() || ocrAvailable()). Engine is already `started`, so start() returns early — no stop, no cache clear.

4. No renderer gate: App.tsx references privateView only in a comment at line 1781. The screen-ask fast path (App.tsx:839-855) gates on backgroundScreenContext && providerReady and calls window.toto.screenContext() directly; only the FALLBACK window.toto.capture() throws PrivateViewBlockedError.

5. No test covers it: screen-preprocess.test.ts:172-184 asserts the drop only by explicitly invoking _test.describeForWindow. No test exercises currentFreshContext() under Private View. Existing suite passes 22/22 (./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/screen-preprocess.test.ts).

INDEPENDENT REPRO (temp dir outside the repo, since deleted; repo untouched): harness whose getScreenshot throws under Private View exactly like index.ts:1321. Cache a description at T=0; at T=1s set privateView=true and call refresh() (mirrors index.ts:1976); at T=2s currentFreshContext() returned {"description":"VS Code showing AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=abc123"} and isActive() was still true. A second test confirmed the cache clears only when describeForWindow runs again, i.e. on the REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS=6000 tick (screen-preprocess.ts:106, 282).

EGRESS CONFIRMED: req.screenContext is rendered into the user turn via screenContextBlock() at src/main/llm/shared.ts:143,151; providerReady (src/main/index.ts:852-861) means the active provider is a keyed API or connected CLI provider — off-device by construction.

INTENDED-BEHAVIOR QUOTES ARE ACCURATE: screen-preprocess.ts:15 states the invariant, and index.ts:1345-1352 is decisive — the code already treats "a frame grabbed a moment before the toggle would still be cached and sent to the model" as breaking the Private View guarantee and hardens getScreenshot against exactly that race. The preprocess cache is the same hazard class, unguarded, and unlike the capture path emits no `capture.blocked` audit event, so the violation is silent.

SEVERITY high (finder's rating stands, not critical). Narrowing factors: backgroundScreenContext defaults false (src/shared/ipc.ts:801); Windows has no OCR so localReady (Métis Local provisioned) is mandatory; a cloud/CLI provider must be active; window bounded to ~6s (12s TTL ceiling) and requires staying in the same window since handleWindowChange (screen-preprocess.ts:263-271) clears on focus change; redactSecrets at index.ts:2783 strips high-confidence secrets but not general screen content. Against that: a silent, unaudited breach of an explicit user-facing privacy switch on a plausible sequence (flip Private View, then hit the screen-ask hotkey and get a screen-grounded answer instead of the block notice).

FIX trivial: both read paths funnel through one accessor, so `if (deps.privateViewOn()) { cache = null; return null }` at the head of currentFreshContext() (src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:311) closes both seams at once — consistent with the module's own "one authority" comment at line 87.

NOTE: finder cited src/main/index.ts:2681 as the location; the handler is actually at src/main/index.ts:2697-2701 in the working tree (~16-line drift). Substance unaffected.

And src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1781-1782 — "It does NOT touch privateView (whether Métis captures YOUR screen for screen questions) — that's a separate, less-frequent switch in Settings → Privacy, kept off the bar to avoid conflating the two."  And src/renderer/src/components/Bar.tsx:163 — "eye button toggles this. Separate from Private View (whether Métis captures the user's screen)."

**Actual.** The eye button's tooltip is literally the Private View wording — Bar.tsx:603-606 renders `'Private view: managed by your organization'` / `'Private view on'` / `'Private view off'` — while its `onClick` (Bar.tsx:608) is `onToggleStealth`, which patches `contentProtection` (src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1783-1785), and its `active`/icon state comes from `stealth={settings?.contentProtection ?? true}` (App.tsx:2726). Settings then claims the two controls are the same one: src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:4730-4733 renders a toggle labelled "Private View" bound to `settings.privateView` whose description ends "Same switch as the eye button on the bar." They are two different flags with different defaults (`contentProtection: true`, `privateView: false` — src/shared/ipc.ts:1097-1098).

**Repro.** Fresh install (contentProtection=true, privateView=false). Open Settings → Privacy: "Private View" reads OFF. Hover the bar's eye: tooltip reads "Private view on" — opposite state, same name. Add a Settings.contract test that asserts no two controls bound to different setting keys carry the string "Private view".

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED. Every cited fact reproduces, and the intent quotes are verbatim.

Wiring: src/renderer/src/components/Bar.tsx:602-607 renders the eye's tooltip as 'Private view: managed by your organization' / 'Private view on' / 'Private view off', with onClick={props.onToggleStealth} (Bar.tsx:608). src/renderer/src/App.tsx:2726 feeds it stealth={settings?.contentProtection ?? true}, and App.tsx:1783-1788 patches ONLY { contentProtection: nextHidden }. Main then applies it: src/main/index.ts:1843 / 1995 call win.setContentProtection(contentProtectionOn()). privateView is never touched by this path.

Two controls, one name, opposite defaults: src/shared/ipc.ts:1097-1098 sets contentProtection: true, privateView: false. src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:4729-4735 renders a SECOND toggle labelled "Private View" bound to settings.privateView, whose desc (Settings.tsx:4731) ends "Same switch as the eye button on the bar." — that sentence is false. On a fresh install Settings shows Private View OFF while the bar's tooltip for the same name reads "Private view on".

Intent quotes check out verbatim: ipc.ts:746-754 ("Purely about the window — it never blocks Métis's own screen capture" vs "Private View: Métis itself won't look at (or send) YOUR screen"), App.tsx:1780-1782 ("It does NOT touch privateView ... kept off the bar to avoid conflating the two"), Bar.tsx:163 ("Separate from Private View").

Refutations attempted and defeated:

The eye now controls contentProtection again"). The label is orphaned by that revert.
2. "A guard blocks unhiding during a live share." None exists — App.tsx:1783-1785 patches unconditionally; no listening/sharing check anywhere in the path.
3. "A test pins the copy." src/renderer/src/components/Bar.test.tsx contains no stealth/tooltip assertion at all; src/main/store.test.ts only covers flag persistence. Nothing pins it.
4. "The toast prevents the exposure." src/renderer/src/components/VisibilityToast.tsx:41-48 fires AFTER the click ("Visible on shared screens" / "Métis will now appear if you share or record your screen") and auto-dismisses after 2600ms. Additional evidence the finder missed, which makes the repro app-guided rather than hypothetical: src/renderer/src/App.tsx:894 and :967 tell the user "Private View is on, so Métis couldn't see your screen. Turn Private View off to include the screen." The only control named "Private view" that is visible during a meeting is the bar eye. Clicking it leaves privateView untouched (the screen ask still fails) and sets contentProtection:false, making the overlay with the live transcript visible to everyone in the Teams/Zoom share. ### MQA-037 — The zero-config "answer it on-device" local fallback is dispatched with the 20s retry idle cap instead of its mode budget, so local summary/vision answers time out

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:2975` · workflow: Answer an in-scope ask on the bundled local model when no cloud provider is configured (localLlm.fallback safety net) — post-meeting summary and screen questions · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:2955-2956 — "Per-tier idle budget: a live suggest gives up fast to stay real-time; recaps + deep answers get the full headroom. Bounds time-to-first-token and triggers failover when a provider stalls before a token." (summary/recap = 120_000 ms, vision = 60_000 ms at src/main/index.ts:2957-2968.) The short cap is justified ONLY for network retries: src/main/index.ts:2969-2973 — "Each failover attempt re-derives a fresh, full idle budget with no shared cross-provider deadline — on a silent-drop offline network (captive portal / dead-gateway WiFi that accepts the connection then black-holes packets) that compounds into N x the base budget of blank spinner… Retries (attempted.length > 0) get a much shorter cap: a healthy provider still answers well inside it, while a silent-drop network surfaces the 'Connection error.' in seconds." And the fallback's own purpose, src/main/index.ts:2924-2930: "With a provisioned on-device model and fallback on, answer the in-scope ask locally instead: a fresh zero-API-key install gets a working assistant."

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:2975 `const idleMs = attempted.length > 0 ? Math.min(baseIdleMs, RETRY_IDLE_CAP_MS) : baseIdleMs` keys the cap purely on `attempted.length`. The zero-config safety net dispatches local as `attempt('local', attempted.concat(provider))` (src/main/index.ts:2940) and pickFailover's last-resort local target (src/main/index.ts:2820) likewise always arrives with `attempted.length >= 1` — so the on-device model is ALWAYS given 20_000 ms, never its mode budget, even though nothing about that attempt is a network retry (the preceding step was a pure in-memory config check that took ~0 ms and never touched a socket).

**Repro.** Keyless install, Métis Local provisioned, `localLlm.fallback` on, `localLlm.useFor.summary` off. End a 60-minute meeting; the summary ask (mode:'summary', baseIdleMs 120_000) tries `s.provider` ('anthropic') -> ineligible "No API key for Claude · Anthropic" -> attempt('local', ['anthropic']) -> idleMs 20_000. The local strategy feeds up to LOCAL_SUMMARY_TRANSCRIPT_CHAR_CAP = 80_000 chars (~20k tokens, src/main/llm/local.ts:15) to the bundled 0.8B model; prefill of that prompt on the Windows CPU sidecar does not produce a first token within 20 s, so openai.ts's watchdog fires 'Stream timed out — no response from the model.' Because `provider === 'local'` there is no failover (src/main/index.ts:3054), so the user gets a hard error. The IDENTICAL request with `useFor.summary` ON routes local as PRIMARY (attempted.length === 0) and gets the full 120 s — 6x more budget for the same work. Same asymmetry for vision: 60 s as primary vs 20 s via the fallback seam.

**Suggested fix.** Cap on the reason for the extra attempt, not on `attempted.length`. E.g. thread a `viaTransportFailure` flag into `attempt()` (set only from the `onError` failover/retry seams) and use `const idleMs = viaTransportFailure ? Math.min(baseIdleMs, RETRY_IDLE_CAP_MS) : baseIdleMs`; or at minimum exempt `provider === 'local'` from RETRY_IDLE_CAP_MS, since a local attempt cannot be a silent-drop-network victim.

**Verifier.** SURVIVES, but the finder's line numbers are ~30 off and its headline claim ("ALWAYS 20s") plus its literal repro are refuted.

CONFIRMED MECHANISM. src/main/index.ts:3014-3018 keys the cap on attempted.length alone: `localColdStart ? Math.max(baseIdleMs, LOCAL_COLD_START_IDLE_MS) : attempted.length > 0 ? Math.min(baseIdleMs, RETRY_IDLE_CAP_MS) : baseIdleMs`. The fallback seam can never produce attempted.length===0 for local: src/main/index.ts:2971 dispatches `attempt('local', attempted.concat(provider))`, src/main/index.ts:2851 returns 'local' only from inside failover(attempted.concat(provider)), and src/main/index.ts:3142 feeds pickPrimaryProvider only `localEligibleFor` (useFor-driven), never `localFallbackEligibleFor` (src/main/llm/local-routing.ts:93-103, 158-168). The intended-behavior quotes are verbatim-accurate at index.ts:2986-2999 (mode budgets: summary/recap 120_000, vision 60_000) and index.ts:3000-3004 (retry cap justified solely as silent-drop NETWORK detection — inapplicable to a 127.0.0.1 sidecar). idleMs reaches the watchdog unmodified: llm/local.ts:175-185 spreads ...opts into streamOpenAI; llm/openai.ts:66-70 arms idleWatchdog(opts.idleMs) and only pings on truthy delta.content/reasoning_content (openai.ts:138-146), so it is a pure TTFT bound covering the whole server-side prefill. On fire, the user is dead-ended: "Stream timed out" is deliberately excluded from TRANSIENT_PATTERN (llm/retry.ts:39-42 — "Bare 'timeout' is intentionally omitted"), so no same-provider retry, and index.ts:3107 blocks failover for provider==='local'. Default settings put every keyless install on this seam (shared/ipc.ts:881 enabled:true, :905 fallback:true, :910 useFor all false). No guard/schema/test covers it — local-routing.test.ts (80 tests) passes and never references idleMs; the only idle assertion in the suite is src/main/llm.test.ts:119 (anthropic 120s).

REFUTED PART. index.ts:3012-3015 (MQA-006) already floors a COLD local attempt at Math.max(baseIdleMs, 90_000), so local is not "always" capped at 20s. The finder's own repro lands on that cold path: on a default keyless install nothing warms the sidecar before the summary — the renderer prewarm effect is gated on settings.localSuggestReady (App.tsx:1226), which is localReady && useFor.suggest = false (index.ts:866), and the speculative-suggest effect is gated on providerReady || localSuggestReady (App.tsx:1190-1196), both false (providerReady excludes localFallbackReady, index.ts:872-884). So "end a 60-min meeting, summary is the first local ask" actually gets 120_000 ms.

RESIDUAL DEFECT (why it still stands). Whenever the sidecar is WARM — any prior local fallback ask (a "What to say next" click, screen ask, or brain indexing) within the 15-minute idle stop (local-runtime.ts:52 IDLE_STOP_MS) — localColdStart is false and the summary/vision fallback ask drops to 20s while the byte-identical request with useFor.summary ON gets 120s. That prefill is up to LOCAL_SUMMARY_TRANSCRIPT_CHAR_CAP = 80_000 chars (~20k tokens, llm/local.ts:15) with no cached prefix (prewarm warms slot 0/suggest; summary pins slot 1, local.ts:167-172), on the bundled Qwen3.5 0.8B (llm/local-models.ts:26-38) against the project's own documented reference hardware "Ryzen 5 5600U ... Windows CPU/WASM is mandatory" (docs/design/2026-07-10-packaged-local-ai-design.md) — well outside 20s. Incidentally immune on macOS Apple-FM (localRuntime.isRunning() is false there, so the 90s floor always applies), making this a Windows/llama-engine exposure.

SEVERITY. Kept at medium rather than raised: it is a hard, no-failover, user-visible error on a default-on zero-config path and a core feature (post-meeting summary), but it is conditional on a warm sidecar rather than universal as claimed. FIX: trivial — one predicate at index.ts:3016 (e.g. `attempted.length > 0 && provider !== 'local'`, or gate the cap on the prior attempt having actually opened a socket).

### MQA-038 — A renderer crash mid-meeting leaves main's `listeningActive` true forever, permanently disabling the fresh-question boundary so every later plain ask inherits the dead meeting's Dust conversation

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:1050` · workflow: Ask a plain typed question outside a meeting (the fresh-question boundary / follow-up-memory contract) · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:3751 — "listeningActive = !!on // fresh-question boundary (askStart) is suspended while a meeting is live", i.e. the suspension is meant to last exactly as long as the meeting. The contamination it guards is spelled out in src/main/llm/dust.ts:114-117 — "Also time-bounded (DUST_CONVERSATION_TTL_MS): without this, an unrelated ad-hoc question asked hours or days later — with no new meeting having started in between — would silently inherit that old meeting's private conversation history." And the codebase already treats module state surviving a renderer crash as a bug class it fixes: src/main/index.ts:925-931 — "Crash/recovery guard: render-process-gone recovery and the boot-retry path both rebuild the window from scratch, but isMinimized/currentWidth are module-level state that otherwise survives from before the crash… Reset both so a recovered window always starts full-size."

**Actual.** `listeningActive` is declared at src/main/index.ts:2684 and assigned in exactly ONE place — src/main/index.ts:3751, from the renderer's `IPC.listeningState` IPC (verified by grep: only 2684 and 3751). The render-process-gone handler at src/main/index.ts:1050-1056 recovers by reloading the SAME BrowserWindow (`win.loadURL(...)` / `win.loadFile(...)`), so `createWindow()` never re-runs and the crash/recovery guard at 925-931 never executes. Nothing anywhere resets `listeningActive` (or `audioArmed`, index.ts:349) after the renderer that set it dies.

**Repro.** Start a meeting -> renderer calls listeningState(true) -> main sets `listeningActive = true`, calls resetDustConversation() and prewarms Dust conversation C1 (index.ts:3757-3771); mid-meeting chat/fact-checks accumulate the private transcript inside C1. The renderer process then dies (the handler's own comment at index.ts:1044-1045 names a worker crash as the motivating case) and main reloads index.html. The remounted renderer starts with listening=false and never calls listeningState(false), so `listeningActive` stays true for the rest of the app session. The user now types an unrelated question ("what's the weather in Paris"): the gate at src/main/index.ts:2705-2718 requires `!listeningActive`, so it is skipped entirely — `req.history = []` and `resetDustConversation()` never run, and `lastPlainAskAt` never advances so the ASK_MEMORY_IDLE_MS expiry can never fire either. streamDust's `isFresh(C1)` is still true (same workspace, same base agent, < 2 h) so the question is posted into C1 and the agent answers with the dead meeting's full private conversation in context — exactly the leak the TTL was added to bound.

**Suggested fix.** Reset the renderer-owned module state in the render-process-gone handler (src/main/index.ts:1050): `listeningActive = false; audioArmed = false; lastPlainAskAt = 0; resetDustConversation(); setTrayRecording(false); setRecordingPowerSaveBlock(false)` before reloading. Better still, hang that reset off `win.webContents.on('did-start-navigation'/'did-finish-load')` so ANY renderer reload re-syncs, since main can never observe a listeningState(false) the dead renderer owed it.

**Verifier.** I could not refute it. (Note: the finder's line numbers are ~26 low vs. HEAD — index.ts is unmodified in the worktree — but every quoted string is verbatim present, so this is cosmetic drift, not a misquote.)

CHAIN VERIFIED, LINK BY LINK:

1. `listeningActive` really has exactly two mentions plus one assignment. `src/main/index.ts:2710` (declaration `let listeningActive = false`), `:2737` (the read, inside the fresh-question gate), `:3811` (the ONLY assignment, `listeningActive = !!on`, in `ipcMain.handle(IPC.listeningState, …)`). Repo-wide grep for `listeningActive` returns hits only in `src/main/index.ts` and in the source-contract test. Nothing else writes it.

2. Renderer-crash recovery does NOT re-run `createWindow()`. `src/main/index.ts:1061-1067` reloads the SAME window (`win.loadURL(...)` / `win.loadFile(...)`). This is not incidental — `src/main/c-main-fixes.contract.test.ts:93-103` explicitly pins that body to `win.loadURL(...)` / `win.loadFile(...)`, i.e. reload-in-place is the locked-in contract. So the "Crash/recovery guard" the finder cites at `src/main/index.ts:936-943` (which resets `isMinimized`/`currentWidth`) never executes on `render-process-gone` — its own comment claiming render-process-gone "rebuilds the window from scratch" is stale. `createWindow()` is only called at :452, :1158, :4412 (activate / boot-retry / startup).

3. Nothing re-syncs the state on reload. The only `did-finish-load` hook (:1070) is gated behind `ASKTOTO_SHOT` (dev screenshot). No `dom-ready`/`did-navigate` handler exists. The renderer's four `setListeningState` call sites (`src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts:605, 1043, 1224, 1433`) are all inside start/stop/teardown paths — none runs on mount. The worker-`onerror` path at listen.ts:605 does call `setListeningState(false)`, but that only covers an in-renderer *worker* crash, not the whole-renderer death that `render-process-gone` handles. `app.relaunch()` at :1221 is the main-process `onFatal` handler, irrelevant here.

4. The leak lands. `streamDust`'s `isFresh` (`src/main/llm/dust.ts:278-283`) reuses `activeConversation` on workspace+agent match within `DUST_CONVERSATION_TTL_MS`; a plain renderer ask never sets `opts.freshConversation` (only `index.ts:725`, brain ingest, does). `resetDustConversation()` is called from only :1971 (askFollowUpMemory flip), :2741 (the dead gate), :3177 (New chat), :3819 (meeting start) — none at boot, and module state outlives the renderer.

STRONGER THAN CLAIMED, actually: the finder frames the impact as Dust-only and TTL-bounded, but `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:612-613` says the history refs "accumulate regardless of the setting", and main's gate is the sole enforcement. With `listeningActive` stuck true, `req.history = []` never runs either, so `askFollowUpMemory` (default OFF, pinned at ask-freshness.contract.test.ts:22-25) is silently ignored for every plain ask for the rest of the app session — not bounded by the 2h TTL, and provider-agnostic. Same root cause also strands `setTrayRecording(true)` and `setRecordingPowerSaveBlock(true)` (:3812-3813), which `app.on('before-quit')` at :4438 then reads as "meeting in progress" forever.

NO TEST COVERS IT: `src/main/ask-freshness.contract.test.ts` passes (18/18, run via ./node_modules/.bin/vitest) but is purely a source-regex contract lock — its listeningState test only asserts `listeningActive = !!on` exists. `c-main-fixes.contract.test.ts` covers crash recovery but asserts only logging + reload, never state reset.

SEVERITY: medium confirmed. Precondition is a real crash, and mitigations exist (starting a new meeting resets everything; New chat clears renderer history and the Dust conversation), but neither New chat nor the settings flip resets `listeningActive`, so the gate stays dead until app restart.

FIX: trivial — reset `listeningActive` (and `audioArmed` at :357, plus `setTrayRecording(false)` / `setRecordingPowerSaveBlock(false)`) inside the `render-process-gone` handler at src/main/index.ts:1061, mirroring the intent already stated at :936-941. READ-ONLY: I changed nothing.

### MQA-039 — Clicking Spotlight Ref evicts the meeting's cached Dust conversation, so the next mid-meeting ask starts cold and loses all accumulated meeting context

**Where.** `src/main/llm/dust.ts:380` · workflow: Mid-meeting Dust quick actions (chat, Explain, Fact-check) sharing one conversation with the agent · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/llm/dust.ts:108-111 — "One Dust conversation per meeting, not one per request. Fact-check, Explain, Spotlight Ref, and every other Dust-routed quick-action fired during the SAME meeting reuse this conversation, so the agent sees the accumulated back-and-forth instead of a cold start on every call. Reset exactly once, when a NEW meeting/listening session begins."

**Actual.** There is a single `activeConversation` cache slot (src/main/llm/dust.ts:121) and `isFresh` requires `c.agentId === opts.model` (src/main/llm/dust.ts:278-283). Spotlight Ref pins `opts.model` to a DIFFERENT agent: the renderer sends `agentOverride: refAgent` = DUST_SPOTLIGHT_REF_AGENT_ID 'GOr913Zr5V' (src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1343, src/shared/ipc.ts:1063), and src/main/index.ts:2873 resolves `model` to that override for Dust. So Spotlight Ref can never reuse the meeting conversation — and worse, on creation it OVERWRITES the shared slot: src/main/llm/dust.ts:380 `activeConversation = { conversationId: sId, workspaceId, agentId: opts.model, createdAt: Date.now() }` runs for every non-`freshConversation` request, including the pinned one.
