**Repro.** Start a meeting -> resetDustConversation() + prewarm creates C1 (agentId = base agent). Ask three chat questions and one Explain -> all land in C1, agent has the accumulated meeting thread. Click Spotlight Ref -> isFresh(C1) is false (agentId 'GOr913Zr5V' != base) -> createConversation C2 -> dust.ts:380 replaces the cache with { C2, agentId: 'GOr913Zr5V' }. Ask the next chat question (base agent) -> isFresh(C2) is false -> a THIRD conversation C3 is created and cached. From that ask on the agent has none of the earlier meeting back-and-forth; every Spotlight Ref click repeats the eviction. Contrast: without the Spotlight Ref click, every one of those asks stays in C1 as documented.

**Suggested fix.** Make the cache a small per-agent map instead of one slot — `Map<`${workspaceId}:${agentId}`, DustConversationRef>` cleared wholesale by resetDustConversation() — so the pinned Spotlight Ref agent keeps its own meeting-scoped thread without evicting the base agent's. Cheapest alternative: have the pinned (agentOverride) path set `freshConversation: true` so it neither joins nor overwrites the shared slot, and correct the module doc, which currently promises Spotlight Ref reuses the meeting conversation.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED, and reproduced. Code chain: src/main/llm/dust.ts:121 holds ONE `activeConversation` slot; isFresh at dust.ts:278-283 requires `c.agentId === opts.model`; dust.ts:379-381 unconditionally overwrites that slot for any non-freshConversation creation. Spotlight Ref pins a different agent: src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1340-1346 sends `agentOverride: refAgent` (= providerModelsSpotlightRef.dust = DUST_SPOTLIGHT_REF_AGENT_ID 'GOr913Zr5V', src/shared/ipc.ts:1071/1079) vs DUST_BASE_AGENT_ID 'vJxYHvTRBT' (ipc.ts:1070), and src/main/index.ts:2904-2906 resolves `model = req.agentOverride` for provider 'dust'. Empirical repro with a temporary vitest file using dust.test.ts's mocked @dust-tt/client (file deleted after the run, tree left clean): base -> base -> spotlight -> base -> base yielded create=3, created ["conv-1","conv-2","conv-3"], posted ["conv-1","conv-3"] — conv-1 (the meeting thread) is evicted by the Spotlight click and the next base ask starts cold in a new conversation. Alternating base/spotlight 4x yielded 4 creates and 0 posts (every ask cold). Refutations attempted and defeated: (1) freshConversation would exempt it, but it is set only at src/main/index.ts:725 (import recap) and src/main/brain/ingest.ts:172 (brain ingest) — the live ask path createStream at index.ts:3022 does not set it, and App.tsx's spotlightRef does not either; (2) creationInFlight and the conversationEpoch guard are orthogonal (concurrency / meeting-boundary) and do not stop the overwrite; (3) the existing test dust.test.ts:152 pins only non-reuse across agents (create===2) and never asserts the base conversation survives, so nothing sanctions or prevents the eviction; (4) no history fallback — src/main/llm/shared.ts userText/baseUserText never use req.history for Dust (only anthropic.ts:6 replays history), so the Dust conversation IS the sole memory. The quoted intent at dust.ts:108-111 is verbatim and does name "Spotlight Ref" as reusing the meeting conversation, so the doc is genuinely contradicted; the later "Scoped to (workspaceId, agentId)" clause explains non-reuse but never authorizes destroying the base agent's cached thread. Partial mitigation that caps severity at medium (not high): App.tsx:56-57 withContext re-sends the last 3000 transcript chars on every mid-meeting ask, so the recent transcript survives — only the accumulated Q&A turns and older context are lost, plus the prewarmed-conversation latency benefit (dust.ts:149-188). Fix is small: replace the single slot with a per-agent map keyed by (workspaceId, agentId), keeping the same TTL, epoch and reset semantics.

### MQA-040 — codex-cli's idle watchdog can never be pinged, turning the per-tier idle budget into a hard total-runtime deadline that kills healthy runs

**Where.** `src/main/cli.ts:536` · workflow: Ask a question routed to a CLI provider (providerPriority 'cli' with Codex connected, or Codex reached by failover) · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/llm/shared.ts:63-66 — "Abort a stream that produces no token for `ms` (provider hang / slow first token). Call ping() on each chunk to reset it. The budget is per-tier/mode (see the ask handler): a live suggest gives up fast so it stays real-time; a deep answer or a recap gets the full headroom." And src/main/cli.ts:432-433 — "Per-tier idle budget from the caller (a live suggest gives up in seconds so failover can fire; recaps get full headroom) — a hung CLI must not block the real-time path for the full 120s." openai.ts implements the contract properly, pinging on reasoning chunks so the watchdog "doesn't abort the stream while the model is reasoning" (src/main/llm/openai.ts:135-141).

**Actual.** src/main/cli.ts:531-541 only calls `wd.ping()` when `cfg.parseLine(line)` returns non-null. codex-cli's parseLine (src/main/cli.ts:382-392) returns non-null ONLY for `obj.type === 'item.completed' && obj.item?.type === 'agent_message'` — the complete final answer. Every other JSON line codex emits on `--json` (thread/turn/item.started, reasoning items, status) is discarded and does NOT ping. So ping() can only ever fire at the moment the run is already finished: the "idle" budget is in fact a ceiling on the codex process's entire runtime.

**Repro.** Settings -> providerPriority 'cli' with codex-cli connected. Ask a plain question that routes to the base tier (routeTier -> 'base', so baseIdleMs = 45_000 at src/main/index.ts:2968). `codex exec --json` boots node, authenticates and reasons; no line it emits before the final agent_message can reset the watchdog, so at t=45s the watchdog fires `fail('Codex · OpenAI CLI: stream timed out — no output for 45s.')` and controller.abort() taskkills the process tree, discarding an answer that was actively being produced. index.ts's onError sees `!gotToken` (gotToken is only set by a content delta) and fails the request over to another provider — 45 wasted seconds. A live `suggest` routed to codex-cli gets only 15_000 ms (src/main/index.ts:2958), which a cold `codex exec` spawn essentially never beats, so that path fails over every single time.

**Suggested fix.** Ping the watchdog on ANY parsed line from the child, not just answer text: in src/main/cli.ts:531 call `wd.ping()` once per non-empty line before the parseLine branch (keep onDelta gated on parseLine). That restores the documented "no output for ms" semantics for both CLIs and still catches a genuinely hung child, which emits nothing at all.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; chain independently reproduced. (1) src/main/cli.ts:536 is the ONLY wd.ping() in the file (verified by grep across cli.ts + all llm/*.ts providers) and it sits inside `if (text !== null)` at cli.ts:535, so only answer-text lines reset the watchdog. (2) codex-cli's parseLine (src/main/cli.ts:382-392) returns non-null solely for `type==='item.completed' && item.type==='agent_message'` — the finished answer; cli.test.ts:102-108 pins that reasoning items return null. codex-cli also has no isResultLine (cli.test.ts:237-238 asserts undefined), so nothing else touches the timer mid-run. Therefore the timer armed at cli.ts:435-438 is a wall-clock ceiling on the whole `codex exec` run, not an idle detector. claude-cli is unaffected because its parseLine returns text_delta per chunk (cli.ts:336-344), so identical code is correct there and broken for codex.

Intended-behavior quotes check out verbatim: shared.ts:62-66 "Call ping() on each chunk to reset it"; cli.ts:432-433 "a hung CLI must not block the real-time path". Every other provider honors it — anthropic.ts:53-56, dust.ts:419, and openai.ts:138-147 which pings on reasoning_content explicitly so it "doesn't abort the stream while the model is reasoning". codex-cli is the sole provider whose ping site is unreachable during the run.

Refutations attempted and failed: (a) no CLI-specific budget override — index.ts:2988-3018 derives baseIdleMs from mode/tier only; the sole overrides are LOCAL_COLD_START_IDLE_MS (gated on provider==='local') and RETRY_IDLE_CAP_MS=20_000, which makes a failover INTO codex worse; llm/cli.ts:16 passes idleMs through unchanged. (b) codex-cli is live, not vestigial — index.ts:3133-3138 makes it cliPrimary when providerPriority==='cli' and claude-cli is absent, pickFailover at index.ts:2832-2838 deliberately exempts CLI kinds from the no-model filter so it CAN be chosen, and Settings.tsx:1905 renders its connect card. (c) no mode gate blocks suggest/recap from CLI — index.ts:2934-2946 checks only cliConnected + vision for kind==='cli'. (d) no downstream guard — gotToken is set only in onDelta (index.ts:3060), so index.ts:3097-3107 sees !gotToken and burns the budget before failing over, or surfaces "stream timed out" outright for a codex-only user. (e) no test pins this as intended: ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/cli.test.ts passes 19/19, but the watchdog tests (cli.test.ts:168-199) exercise idleWatchdog in isolation and the runCliStream contract test (201-215) never feeds lines — the ping path is uncovered.

Line-number nit only: finder cites index.ts:2958/2968 for the 15s/45s budgets; actual is 2990/2999. Values and logic correct.

Severity medium confirmed: degrades rather than breaks in the common case (45s base often suffices; failover usually rescues), but the 15s live-suggest budget and the 20s retry cap are near-unwinnable for a cold codex exec, and a 120s recap emitted in one shot at end-of-run can be killed mid-production. A codex-only user gets no answer at all on those paths. Fix is trivial: hoist wd.ping() out of the text!==null branch (ideally gated on "line parsed as JSON" rather than "any line", so claude-cli hook chatter can still time out).

### MQA-041 — Windows system-audio auto-recovery is unreachable: the `isWindows` early return kills the very retry the code below it was written to add

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts:966` · workflow: Live meeting capture on Windows — recovering the 'them' (system audio) side after a start-time loopback failure · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** listen.ts:972-975 — "Windows never reports 'granted' here (windowsScreenStatus() hard-codes 'unknown' — there is no OS permission gate to poll), which made this watcher dead code there: a transient start-time loopback failure was never retried. Drive the retry off actual capture state on Windows instead of a permission string that will never flip." (added by commit 7691b94 as a shipped fix)

**Actual.** listen.ts:966 `if (isWindows || !state.listening || !wantsSystemRef.current) return` — added earlier by commit e09368d — returns before `setInterval` is ever created on Windows, so the `(isWindows || p?.screenRecording === 'granted')` branch at listen.ts:976 can never execute. `git log -L 955,985:src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts` shows both edits landing in the same function with opposite intent.

**Repro.** Windows, Settings → audioSource 'both' (the default). Press Listen while the meeting audio device is momentarily unavailable (another app holds the render endpoint exclusively, or the default output is mid-switch) → `getDisplayMedia` throws, `sysOk=false`, UI shows 'System audio unavailable. Listening to your microphone only.' (listen.ts:1256-1257). Fix the output device 5 seconds later. Expected (per listen.ts:972-975): the 3 s watcher calls `recoverSystemAudioRef` and the 'them' channel comes up in place. Actual: the effect returned at listen.ts:966 so no interval exists; `onDeviceChange` (listen.ts:941-948) only re-acquires the mic; no 'them' track exists so `onended` can't fire. The whole meeting runs mic-only and the remote side is never transcribed until the user stops and restarts Listen (which splits the meeting into two transcripts).

**Suggested fix.** Split the guard: keep the `getPermissions()` poll macOS-only, but on Windows run the same 3 s interval with the poll skipped — e.g. `if (!state.listening || !wantsSystemRef.current) return` and inside the tick, `if (isWindows) { void recoverSystemAudioRef.current?.(); return }` before the `getPermissions()` call. Add a regression test asserting `recoverSystemAudio` is invoked on Windows when `channels.current.them` is absent.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED — I tried to kill this four ways and it survived.

1) The unreachability is literal, not inferred. `src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts:966` is `if (isWindows || !state.listening || !wantsSystemRef.current) return`, and it sits ABOVE `const iv = setInterval(...)` at :967. The Windows branch the finder cites, `if ((isWindows || p?.screenRecording === 'granted') && !channels.current.them)` at :976, lives inside that interval callback. `isWindows` is a module-level const computed once (`src/renderer/src/lib/keys.ts:9`, `navigator.platform.toLowerCase().includes('win')` — Electron reports "Win32"), so it cannot flip; the effect deps are `[state.listening]` only. On win32 the effect returns before any interval exists, so :976 is dead code in every reachable state.

2) The "intended" quote is verbatim. listen.ts:972-975 says exactly what the finder quoted, including "which made this watcher dead code there: a transient start-time loopback failure was never retried. Drive the retry off actual capture state on Windows instead of a permission string that will never flip." `git log -L 960,984:src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts` confirms the ordering: e09368d added `isWindows ||` to the early return; 7691b94 later added `isWindows ||` inside the poll callback without removing the guard above it. The shipped "fix" is a no-op on Windows.
(One nit that does NOT save the finding: the comment's premise is itself stale — `windowsScreenStatus()` at `src/main/platform-perms.ts:73-77` returns `screenProbeResult ?? 'unknown'`, so it CAN return 'granted' after a successful startup probe. That only weakens the rationale for the fix's design; the early return still kills the interval either way.)

3) No other code path recovers 'them' on Windows. I checked every candidate: `recoverSystemAudioRef` has exactly two call sites (listen.ts:814 and :977). :814 is the `track.onended` handler installed inside `openChannel` (:804-817) — it requires a 'them' channel that already opened, which is precisely what did not happen at start time. The devicechange effect (:940-954) bails unless `channels.current.you` exists and only calls `recoverMicRef`. `armThemWatchdog` is only armed from `openChannel` when `sp === 'them'` (:832-834) and only surfaces a soft note. Bar.tsx's degraded chip (:433-462) is display-only — no retry action. `startListen()` in App.tsx (:1539, :1586, :1925) is toggle / new-meeting / resume, all user-driven. No test pins the guard: the only test touching this file, `src/renderer/src/App.mic-only-visibility.test.ts`, asserts nothing about the watcher (ran it: 6/6 pass, so it neither catches nor blesses this).

4) The repro preconditions hold. `audioSource` defaults to `'both'` (`src/shared/ipc.ts:1099`, enum at :755). With source 'both', a `getDisplayMedia` failure sets `sysOk=false` (listen.ts:1201-1204), start still reaches `listening: true` with the Windows note at :1256-1257, and `wantsSystemRef.current` is true (:1026) — i.e. exactly the state the watcher was written for, on the one platform where it is switched off.

Bonus consequence the finder understated: the catch inside `recoverSystemAudioRef` (:922-930) explicitly leaves the sticky note "so the live permission watcher / a devicechange can retrigger recovery later". On Windows neither exists, so even a mid-session 'them' death gets exactly ONE recovery attempt and is permanently mic-only if that attempt loses the race.

Severity corrected high → medium: the failure is degraded, not broken, and is user-visible (amber "Mic only" chip + platform-specific cause in Bar.tsx:439/452-457) with a working manual workaround (stop/restart Listen, at the cost of a split transcript). It also requires a transient start-time loopback failure that later self-heals, which is narrower than a routine path. It is still a genuine correctness bug on the branch's own target platform.

Fix is a one-token deletion at listen.ts:966 (drop `isWindows ||`); optionally skip the `getPermissions()` IPC on Windows and call `recoverSystemAudioRef` straight from the interval, since the permission read is meaningless there.

### MQA-042 — parakeetRelease() frees nothing — sherpa's OfflineRecognizer has no free(), so ~487 MB of native memory is retained after every meeting, including default whisper+auto meetings

**Where.** `src/main/parakeet.ts:145` · workflow: Ending a meeting / running several meetings back-to-back in one app session · fix size: small

**Intended.** parakeet.ts:142 — "/** Free the recognizer (between meetings / on idle) to release memory. */" and main/index.ts:3747-3748 — "It's also the clean boundary to free Parakeet's ~487MB native recognizer between meetings/on idle, instead of leaving it resident in the main process for the rest of the app's life."

**Actual.** parakeet.ts:145 `recognizer?.free?.()` — `OfflineRecognizer` in node_modules/sherpa-onnx-node/non-streaming-asr.js exposes only `constructor`, `createAsync`, `createStream`, `setConfig`, `decode`, `decodeAsync`, `getResult`. There is no `free`, so the optional call silently no-ops and parakeet.ts:149 `recognizer = null` merely drops the JS reference. The native allocation is not registered with V8 (no `napi_adjust_external_memory` in the wrapper), so it is only reclaimed whenever a full GC happens to finalize the wrapper — unbounded in a low-JS-allocation main process. Worse, this is on the DEFAULT path: with `asrEngine: 'whisper'` and `asrLanguage: 'auto'` (shared/ipc.ts:1124-1125), listen.ts:538 `probeLanguageWindow` calls `parakeetFeed` on window 1, which constructs the recognizer via main/index.ts:2581 → parakeet.ts:99.

**Repro.** Fresh app, all defaults. Run meeting 1 (whisper engine, auto language) — the first VAD window triggers a language probe, which builds the Parakeet OfflineRecognizer in the main process (+~487 MB RSS). Press Stop → `setListeningState(false)` → main/index.ts:3763 `} else parakeetRelease()` → `free` is undefined, nothing is released, RSS stays elevated. Start meeting 2 → `getRecognizer()` sees `recognizer === null` and constructs a SECOND recognizer while the first is still un-finalized → ~974 MB. Three back-to-back meetings can hold ~1.5 GB of native memory in the main process on an 8 GB Windows machine.

**Suggested fix.** Stop pretending the release happened. Either (a) call the addon's real teardown if one exists (`addon.destroyOfflineRecognizer(this.handle)` via a thin wrapper) instead of the non-existent `free`, or (b) keep one memoized recognizer for the app's lifetime rather than repeatedly constructing new ones, and (c) do not build Parakeet at all for a whisper-engine session — gate `probeLanguageWindow` behind a cheap `parakeetStatus()`/settings check, or run the language probe only when the Parakeet engine is already loaded. Add a test asserting `parakeetRelease` invokes a method that actually exists on the recognizer object.

**Verifier.** SURVIVES. I verified the core mechanism at runtime, not just by reading.

1) The no-op is real and runtime-proven. `node -e "require('sherpa-onnx-node').OfflineRecognizer.prototype"` returns own props [constructor, createStream, setConfig, decode, decodeAsync, getResult], `typeof ...prototype.free === 'undefined'`, statics [length, name, prototype, createAsync]. Source confirms: node_modules/sherpa-onnx-node/non-streaming-asr.js:52-139 defines no free/destroy/dispose, and node_modules/sherpa-onnx-node/sherpa-onnx.js:26 re-exports that exact class unmodified. So src/main/parakeet.ts:145 `recognizer?.free?.()` short-circuits on the optional call and silently does nothing; only parakeet.ts:149 `recognizer = null` has any effect.

2) The intended-behavior quotes are accurate verbatim. parakeet.ts:142 "Free the recognizer (between meetings / on idle) to release memory." src/main/index.ts (comment at ~3763-3764) "It's also the clean boundary to free Parakeet's ~487MB native recognizer between meetings/on idle, instead of leaving it resident in the main process for the rest of the app's life." The code does not deliver the deterministic release the comment promises.

3) The default path is confirmed. src/shared/ipc.ts:814 asrEngine defaults 'whisper'; :819 asrLanguage defaults 'auto'. src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts:528-539 is the whisper fall-through (parakeet/apple both return earlier), and with asrLanguageRef === 'auto' it calls probeLanguageWindow on windows 1..5 (PROBE_WINDOW_BUDGET=5, listen.ts:34). probeLanguageWindow (listen.ts:395-397) invokes window.toto.parakeetFeed -> IPC.parakeetFeed handler in src/main/index.ts (~2586-2596) -> parakeetTranscribe -> parakeet.ts:92 getRecognizer() -> parakeet.ts:99 `new sherpa.OfflineRecognizer(...)`. Model assets ship bundled (electron-builder.yml extraResources maps resources/asr -> asr; resources/asr/sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8/encoder.int8.onnx is 622 MB on disk), so parakeetModelReady() is true in a shipped build and the construction actually happens. requireAuth() at the handler does not block it during a live meeting.

4) No guard, caller, or test prevents it. grep shows exactly one parakeetRelease() call site (src/main/index.ts, `} else parakeetRelease()` in the IPC.listeningState handler). setListeningState(false) is genuinely fired on stop (listen.ts:605, 1224, 1433). src/main/parakeet.test.ts is the only parakeet test file; I ran it (./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/parakeet.test.ts) - 2 tests pass - and it only covers parakeetModelReady/ensureParakeetModel with no coverage of release. Nothing refutes the chain.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDER (why I downgrade high -> medium):
- It is NOT a permanent leak. node_modules/sherpa-onnx-win-x64/sherpa-onnx.node contains `napi_add_finalizer` and imports `SherpaOnnxDestroyOfflineRecognizer`, and no destroy is exported to JS - so the External handle is destroyed by a napi finalizer when V8 collects the dropped wrapper. The title's "~487 MB of native memory is retained after every meeting" / "rest of the app's life" framing overstates it; the accurate defect is "non-deterministic reclamation where the code and its comment promise a deterministic free at the meeting boundary."
- The finder's supporting sub-claim about V8 pressure IS correct and is what makes this more than cosmetic: I grepped the binary for `adjust_external` and got 0 matches, so V8 sees only a tiny JS wrapper and has no allocation-pressure link to ~600 MB of native ONNX weights. GC timing is therefore uncorrelated with the real cost, and getRecognizer() rebuilding on meeting 2 while the meeting-1 wrapper is still unfinalized (transient ~2x) is plausible.
- The magnitude figure is off in the code's own favour-against: encoder.int8.onnx alone is 622 MB on disk, so the "~487MB" comment likely understates resident cost.

Net: real defect, real user impact on low-RAM machines, on the default whisper+auto path - but no correctness/security consequence and the memory is eventually reclaimable, so medium rather than high. Fix is small but not trivial: there is no free() to call, so the honest options are (a) fix the misleading comments and force a major GC at the meeting boundary, or (b) stop constructing the recognizer on the whisper+auto probe path / move it to a terminable utility process.

### MQA-043 — Speaker Intelligence session labels never reset at a meeting boundary — resetSession() has no production caller, so back-to-back meetings share cluster identities

**Where.** `src/main/speaker-id.ts:231` · workflow: Live speaker labelling ('Speaker N' names on THEM lines) across two meetings less than 30 minutes apart · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** speaker-id.ts:32-33 — "/** A silence gap this long between THEM windows means a new meeting — session labels reset. */"; speaker-cluster.ts:17 — "Stable session label, 'Speaker N' (1-based, in order of first appearance)" (per session); and the `resetSession: () => void` member declared on the SpeakerId contract at speaker-id.ts:122, exercised by speaker-id.test.ts:83-91 ('a >30min silence gap resets session labels (new meeting)' … 'numbering restarted').

**Actual.** `resetSession` (speaker-id.ts:231-234) has no caller anywhere in src/ outside speaker-id.test.ts. The real meeting boundary — main/index.ts:3749 `if (on) { resetDustConversation(); … } else parakeetRelease()` — resets the Dust conversation and (attempts to) release Parakeet but never touches the speaker session. The only reset in production is the idle heuristic at speaker-id.ts:186 `if (lastWindowAt && t - lastWindowAt > SESSION_GAP_MS) clusterer.reset()` with SESSION_GAP_MS = 30 min (speaker-id.ts:33).

**Repro.** Settings → Speaker Intelligence enabled, asrEngine 'parakeet' (or 'apple'). Meeting A, 14:00-14:30, two remote participants → clusters 'Speaker 1' and 'Speaker 2' (speaker-cluster.ts:113). Stop. Meeting B starts 14:35 with one completely different remote participant. `labelWindow` computes `t - lastWindowAt = 5 min < 30 min`, so `clusterer.reset()` is skipped; the new voice is scored against meeting A's centroids (speaker-id.ts:192 → speaker-cluster.ts:108-112). If cosine ≥ 0.5 (DEFAULT_THRESHOLD, plausible for two same-gender speakers over the same VoIP codec) meeting B's lines are stamped with meeting A's 'Speaker 1' identity and the EMA update pollutes that centroid; if not, meeting B's first speaker is labelled 'Speaker 3'. Either way the saved transcript's `name` field is wrong for meeting B.

**Suggested fix.** Call `getSpeakerId().resetSession()` from the `IPC.listeningState` handler's `if (on)` branch in main/index.ts (alongside `resetDustConversation()`), which is already documented there as "the one clean boundary" for a new meeting. Add a contract test that a listening:true transition resets the clusterer.

**Verifier.** SURVIVES. I tried four refutations; none held.

1) "resetSession has a caller somewhere." Refuted in the finder's favor: grep over the whole repo (excluding node_modules) returns exactly two hits — the contract declaration at D:\Asktoto\src\main\speaker-id.ts:122 and the implementation at :231-234. Zero callers, including tests. (The finder's own claim that it is "exercised by speaker-id.test.ts:83-91" is WRONG — I read D:\Asktoto\src\main\speaker-id.test.ts:83-91 and that test drives the idle-gap path by injecting `now`, never calling resetSession. That mis-citation makes the code deader than claimed, not less dead.)

2) "Something else resets the session at a meeting boundary." No. `speakerIdInstance` (D:\Asktoto\src\main\index.ts:103-107) is a module-level singleton with exactly three references — declaration, lazy init, return — and is never nulled. `clusterer.reset()` has only two call sites (speaker-id.ts:186 idle heuristic, :232 the dead resetSession). The real meeting boundary is IPC.listeningState at D:\Asktoto\src\main\index.ts:3756 (finder said 3749 — 7 lines off, but the quoted body matches 3765-3779): `if (on) { resetDustConversation(); prewarmDustConversation(...) } else parakeetRelease()`. It resets Dust conversation state and releases Parakeet — every other piece of per-meeting state — and never touches the speaker session. The renderer fires it on every real start/stop: D:\Asktoto\src\renderer\src\lib\listen.ts:1043 (`setListeningState(true)`), :1224 and :1433 (`false`). So main has ground-truth meeting boundaries and uses a 30-min idle proxy instead.

3) "The idle heuristic covers it." It cannot. `lastWindowAt` (speaker-id.ts:187) is bumped on every THEM window, so the >SESSION_GAP_MS branch at :186 only fires after 30 min of silence. Two meetings 5 min apart never trip it, exactly as the repro says.

4) "It's intended — the gap IS the meeting detector and resetSession is a reserved P2 hook." Strongest counter, still fails. The cited comment (speaker-id.ts:32-33) does not merely describe a heuristic, it asserts the semantics: "A silence gap this long between THEM windows means a new meeting — session labels reset." speaker-cluster.ts:17 promises "Speaker N (1-based, in order of first appearance)" per session, and the listeningState handler's own comment calls `on` "the one clean boundary". Meeting B's first speaker being stamped "Speaker 3" breaks the 1-based contract on the boundary the code already knows about.

Causal chain reproduced in code: labelWindow (speaker-id.ts:182-193) -> profile match first (unaffected, so no real-name misattribution) -> clusterer.assign (speaker-cluster.ts:107-116) against meeting A's surviving centroids. Two saved-to-disk harms, since the label rides into the transcript line (index.ts:2604/2628 -> listen.ts:459/501 -> commitLine at :336/364): numbering never restarts, and — the amplifier the finder missed — speaker-cluster.ts:109 force-assigns to the nearest centroid regardless of similarity once `clusters.length >= maxSpeakers` (8). After a workday of back-to-back meetings the accumulated cluster list saturates and every subsequent window is stamped with an arbitrary stale identity, collapsing distinct people onto one label WITHIN a single later meeting.

Severity held at medium. Against raising: opt-in and default-off (`speakerId: { enabled: false }`, D:\Asktoto\src\shared\ipc.ts:1147); labels are anonymous "Speaker N" so no PII is misattributed; enrolled profiles are matched before clustering and are immune; and the post-save Teams-VTT backfill overwrites `name` outright (applySpeakerNames, D:\Asktoto\src\shared\transcript-align.ts:152-154, called from index.ts:3155) whenever a VTT exists, silently repairing the Teams-with-transcription case. Against lowering: with VTT off or on Zoom/Meet the wrong labels persist into the saved .md, recall, and brain, and the maxSpeakers saturation makes them genuinely wrong rather than merely oddly numbered.

Fix is one line: call `speakerIdInstance?.resetSession()` inside the `if (on)` branch at D:\Asktoto\src\main\index.ts:3765 (use the nullable ref, not getSpeakerId(), so the boundary never force-probes the sherpa addon on meeting start). Tests are green as-is: ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/speaker-id.test.ts src/main/speaker-cluster.test.ts -> 16 passed, which is itself the point: no existing test covers the meeting-boundary reset.

### MQA-044 — On the 3× boosted 'them' channel the VAD latches into the speech state and never endpoints, so remote turns are only cut by the 6 s hard cap

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/lib/vad.ts:79` · workflow: Live transcription of the remote side during a call with any steady background (hold music, conference-bridge comfort noise, a fan on the far end) · fix size: medium

**Intended.** vad.ts:10-12 — "Decision: emit the window when there has been enough REAL speech (rejects coughs/clicks) followed by a continuous trailing silence (end of turn)." and vad.ts:66-68 — "const ENDPOINT = Math.round(SR * 0.6) // continuous trailing silence that ends a turn (~0.6s). Tuned for low turn-detection latency … ~0.2s snappier than a conservative 0.8s — the dominant slice of perceived live-caption lag."

**Actual.** The only exit from the speech state is vad.ts:79 `if (rms < OFF) active = false` (OFF = 0.006, ON = 0.012, vad.ts:70-71). listen.ts:764 `gain.gain.value = 3.0` multiplies the 'them' channel, so any far-end bed at raw RMS 0.002-0.004 lands at 0.006-0.012 — inside the OFF..ON dead band. Once real speech has set `active`, the bed keeps it set forever: `silence` is reset to 0 every quantum (vad.ts:85) and `step()` never returns true, so the only emit left is the hard cap at whisper-worklet-src.ts:72 `if (this.fill >= MAX_SAMPLES) this.emit()`. The repo already records the latch itself at vad.ts:20-22 ("the VAD never leaves the speech state and the 6s hard cap force-emits non-speech windows to the ASR continuously") but the fix that was applied — `isSpeechLikeWindow` — only discards non-speech windows; it does nothing about endpointing.

**Repro.** 'them' loopback carrying a steady bed at raw RMS 0.003 (typical conference-bridge comfort noise / hold music, i.e. the exact case vad.ts:18-22 describes) → boosted to 0.009. The remote party speaks once, setting `active=true`. From then on every remote turn is emitted only when `this.fill` reaches 96 000 samples: (1) turn-detection latency becomes up to 6 s instead of the designed ~0.6 s, so `isQuestion`/auto-answer fires up to 6 s after the question ends; (2) sentences are cut at arbitrary 6 s boundaries mid-word, degrading decode quality; (3) a short remote reply ('Sure.', ~0.5 s = 10 of the 120 50 ms frames) inside such a window makes `isSpeechLikeWindow`'s p90 index (vad.ts:59, `rms[Math.floor(120*0.9)] = rms[108]`) land on a bed frame, so hi/lo ≈ 1 < SPREAD 2.5 and the whole window — including the real utterance — is dropped at whisper-worklet-src.ts:53, contradicting that function's own 'Fail-open by design' contract (vad.ts:30-32).

**Suggested fix.** Make the endpoint adaptive instead of a fixed absolute pair: track a rolling noise floor per channel (e.g. a slow minimum/percentile of quantum RMS) and set OFF/ON relative to it, so a 0.009 bed cannot hold `active` true. A cheap interim guard: in `makeVad`, force `active = false` once `speech` exceeds a ceiling (e.g. 4 s) with no quantum above, say, 1.5×ON, so the latch can break on its own; and raise `MIN_FRAMES`/use a lower percentile in `isSpeechLikeWindow` so a hard-cap window containing any high-energy frame run is not judged purely on p90/p10.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED — reproduced the full causal chain and could not refute it.

MECHANISM (read): vad.ts:78-82, the only exit from the speech state is `if (rms < OFF) active = false` (OFF=0.006, ON=0.012 at vad.ts:70-71). While `active`, vad.ts:85 resets `silence = 0` every quantum, so the endpoint return at vad.ts:89 (`speech >= MIN_SPEECH && silence >= ENDPOINT`) can never fire. listen.ts:764 `gain.gain.value = 3.0` applies to the 'them' channel only.

ADVERSARIAL CHECKS THAT FAILED TO KILL IT:
- Upstream suppression? No. The mic gets `noiseSuppression: true` (listen.ts:209) but 'them' is `getDisplayMedia({ audio: true })` (listen.ts:894, 1177) with no audio-processing constraints, and the graph is src -> gain -> worklet with no filter (listen.ts:779-784). The raw bed reaches the boost.
- Another emit path? No. `'flush'` is posted only from pause() (listen.ts:1333) and stop() (listen.ts:1400); the sole setInterval (listen.ts:967) is an unrelated screen-permission poll. That leaves only the hard cap at whisper-worklet-src.ts:72.
- Does the applied fix cover it? No. isSpeechLikeWindow (vad.ts:37) runs at emit time (whisper-worklet-src.ts:53) and never touches `active`/`silence`, so it structurally cannot restore endpointing.
- Existing test coverage? `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/lib/vad.test.ts` -> 17/17 pass. No test covers speech-over-a-bed endpointing. vad.test.ts:77 tests only ENTRY from the inactive state (a 0.009 value does not START a turn); it never exercises the EXIT after real speech has set active. vad.test.ts:222 actually encodes the latch as accepted behavior, asserting only that the resulting non-speech window is swallowed.

EMPIRICAL REPRO (VAD + worklet logic transplanted verbatim into a standalone sim, 128-sample quanta):
- No bed, 1.2s utterance -> EMIT at t=3.00s, 3.00s window (0.6s after speech ends) = the designed behavior at vad.ts:66-68.
- Bed 0.009 (dead band) AND bed 0.015 (above ON), same utterance -> single EMIT at t=6.00s, 6.00s window. Turn-detection latency 3.8s instead of 0.6s.
- 10s turn over a bed -> EMIT at exactly t=6.00s and t=12.00s, cut mid-word.
- Realistic 5 Hz syllabic 0.5s "Sure." over a bed -> window t=6-12s returns DROP not-speech-like (p90 index 108 of 120 frames lands on a bed frame, ratio ~1 < SPREAD 2.5). The identical utterance with no bed -> EMIT at t=2.12s. Real remote speech is silently lost, contradicting the "Fail-open by design" contract at vad.ts:30-32.

INTENDED-BEHAVIOR QUOTES VERIFIED VERBATIM at vad.ts:10-12 and vad.ts:66-68. The repo's own vad.ts:19-22 already states the latch ("the VAD never leaves the speech state and the 6s hard cap force-emits non-speech windows"), so the finder did not invent the chain; the finder's point that the shipped fix addressed only the hallucination symptom and not endpointing is correct.

CORRECTION TO THE FINDER (broadens, does not refute): the OFF..ON dead band is not required. The latch fires for ANY boosted bed >= OFF (0.006), i.e. raw >= 0.002. Above ON it is worse, since the VAD then self-activates on the bed alone. My sim confirmed identical 6.00s behavior at both 0.009 and 0.015.

SEVERITY: medium is correct. It degrades a core product function (live remote captions + isQuestion/auto-answer timing) in a common scenario (hold music, conference-bridge comfort noise, far-end fan), and can silently drop short remote utterances. It is not a crash, security, or persistent-data-integrity issue, it requires a steady far-end bed, and downstream text filters partially backstop the hallucination side. Not high.

FIX COMPLEXITY: medium. The clean fix is a relative/adaptive noise floor inside makeVad (track a rolling low percentile of quantum RMS and endpoint on rms < max(OFF, floor * k)) rather than the fixed absolute OFF. That is ~20-30 lines, but it must preserve the strict transplant contract at vad.ts:6-8 (pure, Math + literals only, embedded via .toString()), needs retuning against the existing 17 tests, and needs new tests for the speech-over-bed case that no test currently covers.

READ-ONLY respected: no repo files were modified; simulation scripts were written only to the session scratchpad.

### MQA-045 — The post-merge "Undo" banner follows the user onto unrelated records, offering to revert a merge from a page that has nothing to do with it

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/BrainRecordPage.tsx:470` · workflow: undo a merge / browse entity records after merging · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/BrainRecordPage.tsx:304-306 — "A just-completed merge, tracked by the PARENT (BrainView) rather than this component — the record page remounts fresh on every navigation (including the one confirmMerge itself triggers), so anything that must survive that navigation (the \"Undo\" banner) has to live one level up." The stated scope is surviving the one navigation confirmMerge triggers (to the survivor), not every subsequent navigation.

**Actual.** BrainRecordPage.tsx:470 renders the banner on `{recentMerge && (…)}` with no comparison against the currently-displayed `recordRef`, and BrainView.tsx:766-769 passes `recentMerge` to every record page unconditionally. `recentMerge` is BrainView-level state (BrainView.tsx:362) cleared only by Undo (BrainView.tsx:557), Dismiss (BrainView.tsx:769) or the next merge — the Back button only does `setRecord(null)` (BrainView.tsx:667), leaving it set for the rest of the dashboard session.

**Repro.** On account record "Acme Corportation", Same as… → merge into "Acme Corp". The page navigates to Acme Corp and shows "Merged Acme Corportation into Acme Corp. [Undo] [x]". Press Back (returns to the dashboard), then click any unrelated record — e.g. person "Bob Baker" in the People list. Bob Baker's record page renders the same "Merged Acme Corportation into Acme Corp. [Undo]" banner. Clicking Undo there restores the two ACCOUNTS from the merge snapshot (discarding anything either accumulated since, per unmergeEntities' documented point-in-time semantics) and jumps the user to the account record — from a person page that never mentioned them.

**Suggested fix.** Scope the banner to the record it belongs to: pass it through only when it matches, e.g. in BrainView.tsx:767 `recentMerge={recentMerge && record && recentMerge.kind === record.kind && recentMerge.intoId === record.id ? recentMerge : null}` (capture `intoId` in RecentMerge at BrainRecordPage.tsx:307-313 and BrainRecordPage.tsx:421, which currently stores only `fromId` and the two labels), and clear `recentMerge` when the Back button pops to the dashboard (BrainView.tsx:667).

**Verifier.** Could not refute — every link reproduces. (1) BrainRecordPage.tsx:470 renders the banner on `{recentMerge && (` with zero comparison against recordRef/kind/id. (2) BrainView.tsx:753-769 is the SOLE render site (grepped: no other parent renders BrainRecordPage) and passes `recentMerge={recentMerge}` unconditionally to whatever record is open. (3) BrainView.tsx:362 holds it as parent state; I enumerated every `setRecentMerge` occurrence — only 4 exist: declaration (362), Undo (557), onMerged setter (766), Dismiss (769). No useEffect clears it (checked all five: 238, 423, 494, 500, 532); no auto-dismiss timer. (4) BrainView.tsx:667 Back is `record ? setRecord(null) : onBack()` — BrainView stays mounted, so the state survives for the rest of the dashboard session and reappears on the next record opened.

The intended-behavior quote is verbatim-accurate and does say what the finder claims: BrainRecordPage.tsx:304-306 scopes the lift-up to surviving "the one navigation confirmMerge itself triggers." An independent second comment at BrainView.tsx:360-361 narrows it further — "Survives ACROSS a post-merge navigation (record changes to the surviving entity)."

A guard is not just missing but impossible as written: the RecentMerge interface (BrainRecordPage.tsx:307-313) carries seq/kind/fromId/fromLabel/intoLabel with NO intoId, so the component has nothing to compare the open record against — evidence the check was never authored.

Refutations attempted and failed: it is not an intentional global toast (it renders only inside record pages, never on the dashboard — incoherent for a session-level notice); BrainView does not unmount on Back; the `!entity` early-return at :373-379 suppresses the banner only on deleted records, not unrelated ones; BrainRecordPage.test.ts passes 27/27 but covers only pure helpers (provenanceChipLabel, moneyFieldMode, filterMergeCandidates, recordKey) and no test in the repo references recentMerge.

Severity amplifier verified: corrections.ts:1167-1171 documents "POINT-IN-TIME snapshots" where "any correction applied to EITHER side between the merge and the unmerge… is intentionally discarded," so a stale Undo is genuinely destructive. Held at medium (not high) because the banner text remains truthful about which entities it would revert, so the user is misled about where the action is offered rather than what it does, and destruction requires a deliberate click on a correctly-labeled button. Fix is small and confined to BrainRecordPage.tsx: add `intoId` to RecentMerge, populate at :421 (target.id already in scope at :416), gate :470 on `recentMerge.kind === kind && recentMerge.intoId === id`.

### MQA-046 — purgeBrain rmSync's `.brain/` while a fire-and-forget index write is in flight — index.json is resurrected with the pre-purge ledger, so the rebuild queues 0 candidates and reports an empty brain as fully indexed

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1589` · workflow: automatic source-refresh rebuild of Mantu Intelligence · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1104-1111 — "Resolve once every queued index.json mutation has settled… `brainBackfillProgress().running` going false is NOT the same as 'all writes are done': the last job's own index record is still queued on the serialized lane above at that moment. Anything that tears down or moves the profile — app shutdown, a test's teardown — needs this instead, or it deletes the directory out from under an in-flight tmp+rename."

**Actual.** `whenIndexWritesSettle` (:1112) has ZERO production callers — grep across src/ finds it only in seven test files. maybeFinishDrain fires an explicitly un-awaited index write at :1575 (updateIndexDetached, doc at :1091 "deliberately not awaited"), and maybeFinishBackfill does the same at :1467 plus `void publishIndexes(sx)` at :1475 — then, on the very next statement at :1589, calls maybeStartSourceRefresh() which enters startRebuild and reaches purgeBrain (:1763) → store.ts:503 `rmSync(root, {recursive:true, force:true})` after a single await. The detached callback has already read the full pre-purge index into memory (updateIndex :1082) before the rmSync runs; purgeBrain then recreates `.brain/` (store.ts:505) for the preserved journal, so the pending tmp-write+rename lands in the recreated directory.

**Repro.** A backfill drains while idx.sourceRefreshRequested is set (a meeting file drifted). maybeFinishDrain (:1567) queues the detached updateIndex (its readIndex at :1082 captures ingested={20 files, all ok:true}), then synchronously calls maybeStartSourceRefresh → startRebuild → purgeBrain deletes `.brain/` and immediately re-creates it. The detached write's rename then restores `.brain/index.json` holding all 20 ok:true records. startRebuild's own updateIndex (:1772) is chained behind it on indexLock so it preserves that map, and startBackfill (:1871) computes `already` from it → candidates=[] → `{queued: 0}`. Every entity/graph/meeting-extraction file is gone, yet brainStatus reports `meetings: 20` (index.ts:3186) and hasIncompleteMeetingSource (:1533) returns false so backfillRequested is cleared. The dashboard shows an empty graph with no failure banner and nothing ever re-extracts. (If the write instead loses the race, the outcome is the milder one: the detached mutation is silently swallowed by the .catch at :1101.)

**Suggested fix.** `await whenIndexWritesSettle()` (and await the publish writes) immediately before purgeBrain in startRebuild, and make maybeStartSourceRefresh async so maybeFinishDrain's detached write is awaited before it can fire. Belt-and-braces: have purgeBrain take the same indexLock lane so no index mutation can straddle the wipe.

**Verifier.** MECHANISM CONFIRMED, CONSEQUENCE OVERSTATED.

Confirmed by reading + empirical probe:
- src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1575 fires updateIndexDetached (and :1467 another), then :1589 calls maybeStartSourceRefresh() on the very next statement.
- updateIndex (:1080) runs in a microtask: readIndex (full pre-purge ledger) -> writeIndex -> writeJson -> writeSaved (src/main/transcripts.ts:289-291) dispatches fsPromises.writeFile(<root>/index.json.<hex>.tmp) to the threadpool and suspends.
- startRebuild's only await before the purge is `await readCorrectionsJournalSafe(s)` (:1758); that function's no-conflict-copy path (src/main/brain/corrections.ts:316-366) has ZERO awaits, so it resolves in one microtask tick and purgeBrain -> rmSync(root,{recursive,force}) (src/main/brain/store.ts:503) runs synchronously with the tmp open still in flight. Ordering is exactly as claimed.
- whenIndexWritesSettle (:1112) really does have zero production callers (grep: 7 test files only), and its doc at :1104-1111 says what the finder quotes.
- I ran a 600-trial Node probe modeling writeSaved + purgeBrain's exact sync block on this Windows machine (with and without libuv threadpool pressure): 597 benign (writeFile fails ENOENT, swallowed by the .catch at :1101), 3 races where the tmp survived the purge and index.json was resurrected with the pre-purge ledger. The primitive is real.

But the claimed chain dies twice:
1. In 3/3 observed races the resurrection came with purgeOk=false (ENOTEMPTY). purgeBrain's own post-purge check at store.ts:510-511 (`remaining.length === 1 && remaining[0] === 'corrections.json'`) sees the stray tmp and fails the purge, so startRebuild:1764-1770 ABORTS with a typed error rather than reaching startBackfill with queued:0. I could not produce the purgeOk=true + resurrected-ledger branch the finder's "reports 20 meetings, no failure banner" headline requires.
2. Even granting that branch, finishRebuildReplay:1726 recomputes `i.sourceRefreshRequested = hasMeetingSourceDrift(s, i)` against the RESURRECTED ledger, whose records still carry the stale sourceVersion (or name the deleted file) that set the flag. Every setter of the flag (ingest.ts:1662, :1668, :1867, :2072; index.ts:2441, :4036) is a drift or a deletion, so drift is still true -> flag stays set -> onFinished (:1802-1805) re-enters maybeStartSourceRefresh, and independently reconcileMeetingsInBackground on its 60s timer (index.ts:4390-4395) calls requestSourceRefresh, whose index write IS awaited (:1787) -> clean purge + full re-extraction. "Nothing ever re-extracts" is false.

Net: a genuine fire-and-forget-write vs. synchronous rmSync race that can resurrect a pre-purge index.json and/or fail the purge outright, leaving a wiped derived store reported as fully indexed — but bounded to roughly one 60s reconcile tick and one wasted purge cycle, with the corrections journal protected by purgeBrain's escrow restore (store.ts:522-532). Not high (no permanent silent data loss); medium. Fix is one line: await whenIndexWritesSettle() before purgeBrain in startRebuild (or in maybeStartSourceRefresh).

### MQA-047 — A backfill stalled by mid-run provider loss never resumes — the progress bar stays frozen at N of M forever because every re-entry point short-circuits on hasActiveBackfill()

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:2041` · workflow: index meetings (historical backfill) + the automatic reconcile tick · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1611-1614 — the stall is logged as `'[brain] backfill paused: no configured AI provider — will resume next time one is available'`, and :1596-1601 states the design: "A provider can be removed (cleared key, CLI disconnected) after startBackfill() already queued jobs — re-checking here, not just at queue time, stops a mid-backfill provider loss from burning every remaining job… Backfill jobs stay AT THE FRONT of the queue (never removed here)".

**Actual.** Nothing ever re-runs pump() when a provider returns. pump() is called only from inside itself (:1623, :1634), from enqueueIngest (:1684) and from startBackfill (:2014). Both paths that would reach startBackfill after a stall bail first: requestBackfill returns `{ queued: 0 }` at :2041 on `hasActiveBackfill() || backfillLintPending`, and reconcileMeetingsInBackground returns at :2069 on `hasActiveBackfill()`. Because the stalled jobs are still in `queue`, hasActiveBackfill() (:1129) stays true permanently, so brainBackfillProgress().running (:1151) also stays true.

**Repro.** With one cloud provider keyed, click Index meetings on 20 saved meetings. After ~5 complete, open Settings and turn Métis Local off / clear the provider key (or an admin pushes a managed-config allowlist change). pump()'s findIndex (:1604-1608) now rejects all 15 remaining backfill jobs and breaks. Re-key the provider a minute later: the Index button (index.ts:3209 → requestBackfill) returns `{queued:0}` with no work started, the 60s reconcile tick returns at :2069, and the dashboard keeps rendering `Mapping 5 of 20 meetings · 25%` (brainBackfillProgress total=20, done=5, running=true) indefinitely. The queue only unwedges if the user happens to save another meeting (enqueueIngest → pump at :1684) or restarts the app.

**Suggested fix.** Give requestBackfill/reconcileMeetingsInBackground a re-pump path: when hasActiveBackfill() is true but nothing is in `extracting`/`inFlightJobs`, call pump() instead of returning `{queued:0}`. Optionally have brainBackfillProgress expose a `stalled: true` flag so the renderer stops claiming active progress.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; every link in the chain reproduces in the code.\n\n1) The stall leaves jobs in the queue: src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1604-1616 — findIndex accepts a backfill job only when hasUsableProvider(s) is re-checked true (1606-1607); on idx === -1 it logs once and `break`s (1611-1615). Jobs are never spliced or failed, so they persist in the module-level `queue` (declared :1017, pushed only at :1683 enqueueIngest and :2013 startBackfill).\n\n2) That makes hasActiveBackfill() (:1128-1130) permanently true, so brainBackfillProgress().running (:1151) is permanently true.\n\n3) Nothing re-enters pump(). Grep over src confirms pump() in ingest.ts is called only at :1623, :1634 (self, from a finishing job), :1684 (enqueueIngest) and :2014 (startBackfill). ingest.ts has no timers (only queueMicrotask at :1732 and setImmediate at :2046). maybeStartSourceRefresh (:1795) and maybeFinishDrain (:1569) both require an empty queue, so they no-op — which also means backfillLintPending is never cleared by maybeFinishBackfill (:1463-1476).\n\n4) Both automatic/manual re-entry points bail exactly as claimed: requestBackfill returns {queued:0} at :2041 on `hasActiveBackfill() || backfillLintPending` (the !hasUsableProvider branch at :2037 is not taken once the provider is back), and reconcileMeetingsInBackground returns at :2069 on hasActiveBackfill(). The 60s tick (src/main/index.ts:4392) is the only automatic driver and it hits :2069.\n\n5) The unguarded startBackfill callers that WOULD top up the queue and pump() are unreachable mid-session: resumeBackfillIfPending is called once at boot (src/main/index.ts:4389) and startRebuild is only reachable via IPC.brainRebuildAll (src/main/index.ts:3262) which has no renderer call site at all (grep for brainRebuildAll in src/renderer: no matches; it exists only in src/preload/index.ts:112).\n\n6) No side door: IPC.setApiKey (src/main/index.ts:2100-2116) and settingsSet/settingsGet do not touch brain/ingest.\n\n7) UI cannot self-rescue: src/renderer/src/components/BrainView.tsx:803 renders the frozen spinner while bf.running; the "Ingest now" row (:826) and the "Retry index" banner (:697, gated on !bf?.running) are hidden in that state, and both would route to brainBackfill -> requestBackfill -> {queued:0} anyway.\n\n8) Intended-behavior quote is accurate: ingest.ts:1613 is verbatim '[brain] backfill paused: no configured AI provider — will resume next time one is available', and the :1596-1601 comment states the mid-backfill provider-loss design and that backfill jobs stay at the front of the queue.\n\n9) No existing coverage: ingest-backfill.test.ts only covers no-provider AT QUEUE TIME; ingest-progress.test.ts reconcile tests run on an idle module. No test exercises provider-loss-then-return mid-run. (I did not add a repro test: task is read-only and vitest.config.ts restricts include to src/**, so a scratchpad test would not run.)\n\nSeverity corrected high -> medium: recovery is guaranteed on app restart (queue is in-memory; idx.backfillRequested stays durable so resumeBackfillIfPending re-queues) or on the next meeting save (enqueueIngest -> pump at :1684), and no data is lost. Trigger requires a mid-run provider flip (key rotation during indexing, Métis Local summary toggled off, an admin allowedProviders push read live by getAllowedProviders, or getApiKey caching '' after a transient read failure at src/main/store.ts:883-888). It stays above low because when hit, the entire ingest pipeline plus source-drift reconciliation is dead for the whole session behind a permanently spinning "Mapping N of M" with no in-app recovery control.\n\nFix complexity small: a nudge (e.g. export a resumeStalledQueue() that calls pump(), invoked from the reconcile tick before the hasActiveBackfill guard, or gate that guard on "backfill jobs actually progressing"), plus a regression test.

### MQA-048 — Local-served brain extraction runs 3 concurrent streams all pinned to llama-server id_slot 1 on a 2-slot sidecar, and never yields to live user-facing local streams

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1040` · workflow: live meeting suggestions/summary on Métis Local while a background meeting index runs · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:204-205 — "// Yield to real user-facing local streams (live suggest/summary) — don't make them wait for a slot. if (deps.runtime.activeStreams() > 0) return", and src/main/llm/local-runtime.ts:266-269 — "How many local streams are currently attached to the sidecar. The background screen-preprocess describe reads this to yield to real user-facing streams (live suggest/summary) rather than compete for a slot." The sidecar contract at local-runtime.ts:112-113 is explicit: "Two slots share the total context" (`'--parallel', '2'` at :130).

**Actual.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1040 `const EXTRACT_CONCURRENCY = 3` — pump() (:1602) starts up to three runExtractionStage calls at once, and with the new fallback (:119-121) each one can be served by `local`. runCompletionOnce (:157-158) sends every local extraction as `mode: 'summary'`, and src/main/llm/local.ts:172-173 pins every summary request to `{ id_slot: 1, cache_prompt: true }`. So three concurrent brain streams contend for a single named slot on a two-slot server, and neither pickProviderCandidates nor pump ever consults localRuntime.activeStreams() the way screen-preprocess.ts:205 requires of background local work.

**Repro.** Zero cloud providers keyed (default install: localLlm.enabled=true, fallback=true). User is in a live meeting with Métis Local suggestions on. The 60s reconcile tick (index.ts:4338 → reconcileMeetingsInBackground → requestBackfill) queues 20 unindexed meetings; pump immediately attaches 3 local streams, each holding id_slot 1 for the whole extraction (a >24k-char transcript runs its windows sequentially at :514, so one job can hold the slot for minutes). The live meeting's own summary/recap request also pins id_slot 1 and now queues behind (or is rejected by) the background work, and screen-preprocess's describeForWindow is suppressed for the entire backfill because activeStreams() stays > 0. The background job wins the slot the live meeting needs — the exact inversion screen-preprocess.ts:205 exists to prevent.

**Suggested fix.** Apply the same yield rule to brain ingest: before starting a local-served extraction, skip/defer when localRuntime.activeStreams() > 0, and clamp the effective concurrency to 1 whenever the picked candidate is `local` (the sidecar has 2 slots, one of which is reserved for live suggest at id_slot 0). Consider giving background extraction its own slot id rather than reusing the live summary slot.

**Verifier.** I tried to kill this on five fronts and it survived all of them.

CHAIN, VERIFIED LINK BY LINK
1. `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1040` is literally `const EXTRACT_CONCURRENCY = 3`, and `pump()` at :1602 is `while (extracting.size < EXTRACT_CONCURRENCY)` — it splices up to three jobs and fires `runExtractionStage` on each with no provider-aware cap.
2. `local` really can serve those extractions: `pickProviderCandidates` returns local exclusively when `useFor.summary` (:85-86) and appends it last when `s.localLlm.fallback && localBaseReady(...)` (:119-121). Schema defaults confirm this is the out-of-box config on a zero-key install — `src/shared/ipc.ts:881` `enabled: z.boolean().default(true)` and `:905` `fallback: z.boolean().default(true)`.
3. `runCompletionOnce` (`ingest.ts:157-158`) sends every local extraction as `mode: 'summary'`. Not inferred — `src/main/brain/ingest-local.test.ts:95` asserts `expect(request.req.mode).toBe('summary')`, and I ran it: `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/ingest-local.test.ts` → 5 passed.
4. `src/main/llm/local.ts:172-173` pins that mode to `{ id_slot: 1, cache_prompt: true }`, and `src/main/llm/openai.ts:119-121` actually copies `id_slot` onto the request body. `src/main/llm/local-runtime.ts:130` is `'--parallel', '2'` — slots 0 and 1 only. Three concurrent requests naming `id_slot: 1` cannot execute in parallel on one slot regardless of llama.cpp's version-specific policy (defer vs. reject), so contention is structural, not speculative.
5. `grep -rn activeStreams src/` returns exactly two non-test call sites: `src/main/index.ts:1387` (wiring) and `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:205`. Nothing in `brain/` reads it. `grep -n "local" src/main/brain/ingest.ts` shows ingest imports only `localBaseReady` from local-routing — no runtime/slot awareness at all.

REFUTATIONS I ATTEMPTED AND WHY THEY FAILED
- Serialization downstream? No. `beginStream()` (`local-runtime.ts:251-253`) is a bare counter for switch-kill/drain, not admission control. `local.ts` has no mutex/queue. `createStream` (`src/main/llm.ts:17-30`) is a plain switch.
- A live-meeting gate on the tick? None. `index.ts:4395` `setInterval(reconcileMeetingsInBackground, 60_000)`; `ingest.ts:2066-2080` gates only on `backfillPreparing / sourceRefreshRunning / hasActiveBackfill / hasUsableProvider`. No recording-state check anywhere in `src/main/brain/`.
- An existing test encoding the opposite decision? No. `ingest-local.test.ts`, `ingest-index-fallback.test.ts`, and `local-runtime.concurrency.test.ts` contain zero references to slots, `activeStreams`, or extraction concurrency.
- Windows-per-file give it back? Partially — `ingest.ts:511-514` runs windows sequentially per file, each its own stream, so the slot is released between windows. That weakens "one job holds the slot for minutes" but not the aggregate: three jobs looping windows keep slot 1 effectively saturated for the backfill's duration.
- Does the intended-behavior quote say what the finder claims? Verbatim yes — `screen-preprocess.ts:204-205` and `local-runtime.ts:266-267` and `local-runtime.ts:112` (`Two slots share the total context`) all match character-for-character.

WHY I DOWNGRADE high → medium
The one place the finder overreaches: `local-runtime.ts:266-267` says "The background screen-preprocess describe reads this" — it documents the one existing consumer, it does not state a cross-cutting "all background local work must yield" invariant. So this is a design-consistency + priority-inversion defect, not a violated contract. Impact is degradation, not corruption: no data loss, no wrong output, retries intact. Live *suggest* — the highest-frequency live surface — pins `id_slot: 0` (`local.ts:170-171`) and is not blocked, only compute-contended; only summary/recap-shaped local requests actually queue behind the background work. That said it is squarely real and user-visible, and the sharpest part of it is that `EXTRACT_CONCURRENCY = 3` buys *zero* throughput on local (all three serialize on slot 1 anyway) while costing the live path its slot — pure harm, no benefit.

FIX: localized — cap concurrency to 1 when the served candidate is `local`, and/or stop pinning `id_slot` for background extraction so llama picks a free slot. A true yield-to-live also needs a wake-up on `endStream()` so backfill doesn't stall, which is the only reason this isn't trivial.

**FIXED (2026-08-08, ledger row flipped 2026-08-17).** The fix landed in c481051 and the row was never flipped with it. `extractConcurrency(s)` clamps the pump to ONE in-flight extraction whenever the first candidate is `local` — three concurrent summary-mode requests all pin `id_slot: 1` and therefore buy zero throughput while costing the live path its slot — and cloud batches keep the full `EXTRACT_CONCURRENCY`. `localExtractionShouldYield(s)` applies screen-preprocess.ts's own rule to brain ingest: a BACKFILL-origin job stands aside while `localActiveStreams()` shows a real user-facing local stream attached. Only backfill yields — a just-saved meeting's own ingest is the user's action, not background work — and a yielded job stays at the FRONT of the queue, revived by the same three paths that revive a no-provider stall (a finishing job's pump, the 60s reconcile tick, Retry index), so it degrades to latency, never to a stall. Regression tests name MQA-048 for all three: cloud keeps 3-wide, local runs 1-wide, and a parked backfill resumes once the live stream ends.

### MQA-049 — A just-saved meeting's durable pending record is counted and rendered as a failed ingest — dashboard shows a red "needs attention" banner and an attention item reading "Failed to index: Unknown error"

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1676` · workflow: save/end a meeting (live ingest), then open Mantu Intelligence · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1160-1164 — "a record with ok:false stays that way until it either succeeds or is deleted… No separate storage: every ok:false record IS a currently live, unresolved failure (a fixed source overwrites its record with ok:true), so there is nothing stale to filter by a time window." ingestFailureCounts (:1171-1176) and ingestFailureDetails (:1208-1216) are both built on that assumption.

**Actual.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1672-1677 — enqueueIngest deliberately writes a NON-failure ok:false record before extraction starts: `idx.ingested[key] = { at: Date.now(), ok: false, …, attempts: 0 }`, commented at :1674-1675 as "a retry must clear the previous error while leaving an honest durable pending record". That record has no `error`, so ingestFailureCounts increments `failed` (:1174) and ingestFailureDetails emits `error: 'Unknown error'` (:1214). This branch then wires both into two new user-facing surfaces: src/main/brain/attention.ts:107-116 pushes `kind: 'ingest_failed'` with `detail: 'Failed to index: Unknown error'`, and index.ts:3184/3191 ships `failedDetails` to the dashboard.

**Repro.** With a working provider, end and save a meeting `2026-08-08-1200-acme.md`. enqueueIngest writes the pending ok:false record and queues the job; extraction takes seconds-to-a-minute (longer with multiple 24k windows, or while EXTRACT_CONCURRENCY is saturated by a backfill). Open Mantu Intelligence in that window: `durableFailed = failed + exhausted` is 1 and `bf.running` is false (a live job is not a backfill — brainBackfillProgress at :1146-1152), so BrainView.tsx:697 renders the red role="alert" banner with a "Retry index" button, Details lists `2026-08-08-1200-acme.md: Unknown error`, and the Attention list shows `Failed to index: Unknown error` — for a meeting that is indexing normally and succeeds moments later. Quitting right after a save makes the same false state persist across the next launch until the resumed backfill re-processes the file.

**Suggested fix.** Distinguish pending from failed in the ledger: either have enqueueIngest write `pending: true` (or omit the record until the first real attempt) and have ingestFailureCounts/ingestFailureDetails skip records with `attempts === 0 && !error`, or key the failure surfaces on `record.error !== undefined` instead of `!record.ok`.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED — could not refute. Chain reproduced end to end: src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1671-1677 has enqueueIngest write `idx.ingested[key] = { at, ok:false, sourceVersion?, attempts:0 }` BEFORE queueing the job (:1683) and before any extraction; the record carries no `error`, no `exhausted`, no `retryAfter`. src/main/index.ts:3190 awaits enqueueIngest inside saveTranscript, so the record is durable the moment Save returns. ingestFailureCounts (ingest.ts:1171-1176) only skips `record.ok`, so it increments `failed`; ingestFailureDetails (:1208-1216) only filters `!record.ok` and emits `record.error ?? 'Unknown error'`. Both are shipped by brain:status (index.ts:3227,3230,3237,3244-3245) and computeAttention pushes kind:'ingest_failed' with detail 'Failed to index: Unknown error' (src/main/brain/attention.ts:109-117). BrainView.tsx:655,697 renders the red role="alert" banner + "Retry index" whenever durableFailed>0 && !bf?.running, with the Details list at :714/:736.

The `!bf?.running` gate does NOT suppress it, and this is proven by an existing test rather than by my reasoning alone: src/main/brain/ingest-progress.test.ts:173 asserts `brainBackfillProgress().running === false` while a live extraction is in flight (live jobs are origin:'live'; hasActiveBackfill at ingest.ts:1128-1130 only counts origin==='backfill'). I ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/ingest-progress.test.ts — 10/10 pass, including that assertion and "persists a live meeting as pending background work..." (:185-214), which shows the ok:false record is written atomically with backfillRequested and only flips to ok:true after extraction.

Refutations attempted and killed: (1) a dashboard-open requestBackfill would set bf.running — no, startBackfill's scan skips files already in `inFlight` (ingest.ts:1904), so candidates.length===0, backfillLintPending stays false (:2011) and backfillPreparing clears in the same setImmediate (:2054); (2) the periodic reconcile would set sourceRefreshRunning — no, hasMeetingSourceDrift explicitly `continue`s on !record.ok (ingest.ts:1512); (3) some consumer discriminates pending via `attempts` or the absent `error` — grep over src/main/brain shows `attempts` is only read in finishJob (:1402) and the un-exhaust loop (:2003), never as a pending discriminator; (4) the renderer filters the kind — no, BrainRecordPage.tsx:78-85 explicitly ranks `ingest_failed: 3` and BrainView.tsx:887+ renders it; (5) a test pins the intended behavior — attention.test.ts:132-158 and ingest-resilience.test.ts:216-242 only ever build records that carry an `error`; the pending shape is untested.

The cited intended-behavior quote is verbatim accurate (ingest.ts:1159-1161: "every ok:false record IS a currently live, unresolved failure ... so there is nothing stale to filter"). A second independent contradiction the finder missed: RecallView.tsx:117-127's meetingIndexStatus documents 'pending' as "a backfill/live ingest was requested but this file hasn't settled either way yet" but checks `failed` before `pending`, so the pending record makes that documented state unreachable for exactly the case it exists for.

One correction to the finder's framing (does not refute): the red banner, the `failed` count and RecallView's failed dot are PRE-EXISTING on main — `git show main:src/main/index.ts` already has failedFiles (:3140) and `failed: failure.failed` (:3147). What this branch newly introduces is the 'Unknown error' text reaching the user, via failedDetails and the new ingest_failed attention item.

Severity medium is right: no data loss (the meeting indexes correctly moments later), but it fires on the app's most common workflow, survives a quit-after-save until the resumed backfill re-processes the file, and stacks one bogus item per pending save when EXTRACT_CONCURRENCY is saturated. Fix complexity small, not trivial: the pending record is uniquely identifiable (!ok && !error && !exhausted && attempts===0), but the guard must be applied in ingestFailureCounts, ingestFailureDetails AND the failedFiles derivation at index.ts:3236 so the RecallView dot agrees, plus a regression test.

### MQA-050 — Windows .cmd-shim path: an abort delivered before spawn() returns leaves the entire cmd.exe → claude/codex tree running, unkillable and surviving app quit

**Where.** `src/main/cli.ts:481` · workflow: ask / live suggest via a CLI provider on Windows, then Stop, New chat, or quit · fix size: trivial · **regression**

**Intended.** cli.ts:478-480 — "Making the explicit listener the single teardown path means nothing races taskkill to kill cmd.exe." and cli.ts:496-499 — "On that path spawn() was given no signal (above), so this listener is the whole teardown: taskkill /T reaps cmd.exe AND its descendants while cmd.exe is still alive and the tree is still walkable." Commit a97073f (20h ago) titles itself "stop an abort-signal race from orphaning child processes".

**Actual.** src/main/cli.ts:481 withholds `signal` from spawn() on the shim path (`signal: spawnTarget.windowsVerbatimArguments ? undefined : controller.signal`), and the replacement teardown is registered at src/main/cli.ts:501 — AFTER the spawn at 473. Per the DOM spec, `AbortSignal.addEventListener('abort')` on an ALREADY-aborted signal never fires (verified on this machine: listener fired = false; by contrast `spawn(…,{signal})` with an already-aborted signal does kill the child — exit sig=SIGTERM). So an abort() that lands between runCliStream() returning (line 585-590) and the listener registration at 501 produces ZERO teardown: `killWindowsProcessTree` is never called and `child.kill()` is unreachable (line 507 is guarded to non-win32). The window is real, not theoretical: line 445 awaits `resolveBin` (an actual `where.exe` exec, 50-300ms, whenever binCache is cold) and line 455 awaits `mkdtemp` for codex-cli — a genuine libuv/macrotask boundary on EVERY codex ask, so an IPC `askCancel` can interleave there.

**Repro.** Windows, Claude Code CLI installed via npm (resolveBin → C:\Users\<u>\AppData\Roaming\npm\claude.cmd), first ask of the session so binCache is cold. Renderer calls ask → runCliStream returns; ~150ms later `where.exe` resolves. Press Stop / open a new chat / close the overlay during that window → index.ts:3098 `streams.get(id)?.abort()` (or index.ts:1011 on window close) sets controller.aborted. The async body then still reaches spawn at cli.ts:473, and the listener at 501 attaches to an already-aborted signal so it never fires. Result: cmd.exe + the real `node …claude cli.js` grandchild run the full turn to completion, with the meeting transcript already written to their stdin (line 521), and survive Métis quitting — nothing ever kills them. Same on every codex-cli ask (the mkdtemp macrotask gap is unconditional). No test covers this: cli-win.test.ts (34 tests, all passing) only asserts the built command line, never abort ordering.

**Suggested fix.** Re-check the signal after the awaits and before spawning — `if (controller.signal.aborted) { void cleanup(); return }` right after line 461 — and make the teardown idempotent by hoisting it into a named `teardown()` that is called directly when `controller.signal.aborted` is already true at registration time instead of relying on addEventListener: `if (controller.signal.aborted) teardown(); else controller.signal.addEventListener('abort', teardown, { once: true })`.

**Verifier.** Could not refute. Chain verified line by line. (1) src/main/cli.ts:481 withholds the signal exactly when spawnTarget.windowsVerbatimArguments is truthy, which is set only by cmdShimSpawn (cli.ts:269) reached via resolveSpawnTarget->isCmdShim (cli.ts:203-205, /\.cmd$/i) - i.e. the mainstream Windows npm claude.cmd/codex.cmd install. (2) The sole replacement teardown is registered at cli.ts:501, AFTER the spawn at cli.ts:473, and there is no controller.signal.aborted guard anywhere between the async IIFE start (cli.ts:440) and the spawn - I read every line of 440-494. (3) Node semantics confirmed on this machine: a listener added to an already-aborted signal never fires (listener fired = false), while spawn(...,{signal}) with an already-aborted signal DOES kill (exit code=null sig=SIGTERM) - so the asymmetry the finder claims is real, and the kept-signal branch is the safe one. (4) Full-shape repro (async body -> mkdtemp macrotask boundary -> abort lands -> spawn without signal -> addEventListener after spawn) printed: controller.aborted=true, teardown listener fired=false, child ran its full 2.5s and exited 0. killWindowsProcessTree is never called and child.kill() at cli.ts:507 is guarded to non-win32. (5) No other reaper exists: child.on('close') early-returns on aborted (cli.ts:562), fail() early-returns (cli.ts:427), and app.on('will-quit') (src/main/index.ts:4433-4479) reaps only localRuntime/fmRuntime/screenPreprocess - nothing walks CLI process trees. (6) Abort callers are real: IPC.askCancel (src/main/index.ts:3112-3115), window 'closed' (src/main/index.ts:1019), and renderer src/renderer/src/state.ts:376 which cancels any prior in-flight stream on every new run(). (7) Test coverage: src/main/cli-win.test.ts contains zero occurrences of 'abort' or 'signal'; src/main/cli.test.ts only asserts post-spawn abort. Both pass (53/53) and neither covers this ordering. The intended-behavior quotes at cli.ts:478-480 and 496-499 are verbatim, and commit a97073f is titled "stop an abort-signal race from orphaning child processes" - so the code contradicts its own stated contract, and this is a regression: before a97073f the already-aborted signal at least killed cmd.exe. SEVERITY CORRECTED high -> medium. The finder overstates three things. (a) "on EVERY codex ask" conflates the boundary with the hit: the mkdtemp gap (cli.ts:455) exists on every codex ask but the abort must land inside a ~1-5ms window - it is a race, not a deterministic orphan. (b) The cold-binCache repro is real but not the common case: prewarmCli() (cli.ts:1164) is fired at index.ts:2343 and index.ts:3920 and Windows `where` hits are cached (cli.ts:130); with a warm cache the only await is a microtask boundary, which drains before any IPC macrotask, closing the window entirely - it reopens only on a first-ask/prewarm race or after binCache.delete on re-setup (cli.ts:1022). (c) "unkillable" overreaches: nothing kills the tree, but it self-terminates when the CLI turn finishes. Real harm is bounded: Stop silently does not stop, subscription/quota burn, transcript written to stdin at cli.ts:521 after cancel, orphan outliving app quit until the turn ends - no data loss, no security boundary crossed. Also note managed-CLI installs are NOT affected (resolveSpawnTarget returns process.execPath with no windowsVerbatimArguments, cli.ts:288, so they keep the signal). Fix is one line: an aborted check before spawn, or `if (controller.signal.aborted) killWindowsProcessTree(child.pid)` immediately after registering the listener at cli.ts:501.

### MQA-051 — Dust OAuth keep-warm refresh is gated to macOS, so on Windows the ~1h token is never proactively re-minted and the first post-expiry live suggest dies on the 15s idle watchdog

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:4258` · workflow: ask a Dust agent (live suggest / Spotlight Ref / chat) more than ~1h after connecting Dust, on Windows · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** index.ts:4279-4281 — "Keep the session warm for the app's whole lifetime: re-mint whenever the token passes 45 min of its ~1h life, so it never expires mid-meeting and the user never sees a Dust reconnect." dustcli.ts:20-22 — "The per-OS read lives in dust-secret-store.ts (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux libsecret) … This module orchestrates import, refresh, and first-run setup on top, identically on every platform." dustcli.ts:104-106 explicitly handles the Windows shim inside the refresh itself: "On Windows the resolved bin is `dust.cmd`, a shim that can't be exec'd directly".

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:4258 — `if (process.platform !== 'darwin' || !hasApiKey('dust')) return` makes BOTH the startup call (index.ts:4278) and the 10-minute keep-warm interval (index.ts:4282) unconditional no-ops on Windows and Linux. The gate is inverted relative to its own documented rationale, which is macOS-specific prompt cost (index.ts:4252-4256: "the keychain read behind refreshDustCliSession can cost a macOS keychain password prompt") — dust-secret-store.ts:17 states "Reading the CURRENT user's own credential never prompts on Windows/Linux", so Windows is the platform with no reason to be skipped.

**Repro.** Windows. Connect Dust (Settings → Connect from Dust CLI) at t=0; dustTokenMintedAt=now. Leave Métis running (it is an always-on overlay). At t=70min start a meeting and let a live suggest fire: index.ts:2957-2959 sets idleMs=15_000 for `req.mode === 'suggest'`. streamDust arms its watchdog at dust.ts:227 before any network call, hits a 401 on createConversation, and dust.ts:257-262 `retryIfAuth` awaits `refreshDustCliSession()`, which spawns `dust status` with a 25s exec timeout (dustcli.ts:109). 15s < the refresh budget, so the watchdog fires first: the user sees "Timed out — no response from the agent." on a stream that was never given a chance.
