On macOS the same profile never reaches this state because refreshAndPersistDust re-mints at the 45-minute mark.

**Suggested fix.** Drop `process.platform !== 'darwin'` from the guard at index.ts:4258 (keep the `hasApiKey('dust')` and the DUST_TOKEN_FRESH_MS freshness check), and move the macOS prompt-cost concern into the freshness window it already has. Separately, exclude the pre-token `refreshDustAuth` await from the idle-watchdog budget (clear/re-arm `wd` around it in dust.ts:259) so a legitimate refresh can never be reported as an agent timeout.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED as a real platform-parity defect, but the severity is medium, not high.

Verified: src/main/index.ts:4295 (HEAD 4249; file is being concurrently edited, hence the drift from the cited 4258) contains verbatim `if (process.platform !== 'darwin' || !hasApiKey('dust')) return`, and it guards the shared `refreshAndPersistDust` used by BOTH the startup `runStep('refreshDustSession', ...)` and `trackTimer(setInterval(() => refreshAndPersistDust('interval'), 10 * 60 * 1000))`. So the proactive re-mint is a no-op on Windows and Linux.

The "intended behavior" quotes are accurate, not paraphrased: index.ts:4286-4292 states the keep-warm intent and justifies the freshness skip solely by "the keychain read behind refreshDustCliSession can cost a macOS keychain password prompt"; dustcli.ts:18-21 says the module orchestrates "import, refresh, and first-run setup ... identically on every platform"; dustcli.ts:103-106 handles the Windows `dust.cmd` shim inside the refresh itself; dust-secret-store.ts:17 says "Reading the CURRENT user's own credential never prompts on Windows/Linux". The gate therefore excludes exactly the platforms its own rationale does not cover.

I searched for an alternative path and found none. Every other refreshDustCliSession caller is reactive/on-demand: index.ts:2140 (dustListAgents on-401), 2158 (dustImportCli), 2995 (stream refreshDustAuth). index.ts:2171 dustProbeSession deliberately only READS (no rotation), and the dustSetupPoll at 2191 is a 5-minute post-login window that also only reads. No schema default, caller, or test compensates; no test references refreshAndPersistDust or this gate (windows-keystore-dpapi.test.ts's darwin assertions target index.ts:275 ASKTOTO_LOCAL_KEYSTORE, unrelated).

Consequence chain is mechanically sound: idleMs=15_000 for req.mode==='suggest' (index.ts ~2964); dust.ts:227-230 arms the watchdog before any network call; `wd.ping()` occurs exactly once in dust.ts (line 419, on a token delta), so nothing resets it while dust.ts:257-263 retryIfAuth awaits refreshDustAuth -> refreshDustCliSession (dustcli.ts:107-114, cmd.exe -> node `dust status`, then three sequential PowerShell Add-Type CredRead spawns in importDustCliSession). retry.ts:39-42 explicitly excludes "Timed out — no response from the agent." from TRANSIENT_PATTERN, so there is no same-provider retry; index.ts:3062 falls over instead, and failover is suppressed for pinned-agent requests (local-routing.ts:169 allowCrossProviderFailover), so Spotlight Ref gets a hard error.

Severity corrected down for three reasons the finder omitted: (1) the 25s exec timeout is a CAP, not expected latency — whether the refresh exceeds the 15s budget is plausible on Windows but not proven, so "the watchdog fires first" is an over-claim; (2) the failure is one-shot per expiry — the aborted stream's refreshDustAuth closure still completes and persists the fresh token, and attempt() re-reads getApiKey(provider) at each entry, so the next ask succeeds; longer modes (answer 45s, recap 120s, index.ts 2964-2975) absorb the lazy refresh comfortably; (3) docs/cahe-windows-edition.md:9 makes Kimi Code, not Dust, the default provider on the Windows edition, so most Windows users hit failover-degradation rather than a dead end.

Fix is one line: drop `process.platform !== 'darwin' ||` from index.ts:4295 (the freshness check on the next line already bounds how often `dust status` is spawned, and it is the same spawn the on-401 path already performs on Windows).

### MQA-052 — The per-meeting Dust conversation is a single slot keyed by agentId, so every Spotlight Ref click evicts the meeting thread and the next normal ask cold-starts with no accumulated context

**Where.** `src/main/llm/dust.ts:121` · workflow: mixing Spotlight Ref with normal Dust questions inside one meeting · fix size: small

**Intended.** dust.ts:108-113 — "One Dust conversation per meeting, not one per request. Fact-check, Explain, Spotlight Ref, and every other Dust-routed quick-action fired during the SAME meeting reuse this conversation, so the agent sees the accumulated back-and-forth instead of a cold start on every call. Reset exactly once, when a NEW meeting/listening session begins."

**Actual.** src/main/llm/dust.ts:121 stores exactly one `activeConversation`, and dust.ts:278-283 `isFresh` requires `c.agentId === opts.model`. Spotlight Ref runs with `opts.model = req.agentOverride` (index.ts:2874), a DIFFERENT agent id from the base agent used by chat/quick actions, so it can never match. dust.ts:379-381 then unconditionally OVERWRITES the single slot with the Spotlight conversation (the guard there only excludes `opts.freshConversation` and epoch changes, not a different agentId). Reset is therefore not "exactly once per meeting" — it happens on every agent alternation.

**Repro.** During one meeting with Dust connected: (1) ask "what did they say about pricing?" → conversation C1 created, activeConversation = {C1, agentId: base}; (2) click Spotlight Ref → agentId mismatch → C2 created and activeConversation is overwritten to {C2, agentId: spotlight}, discarding C1; (3) ask a follow-up in chat → agentId mismatch again → C3 created cold, and the agent answers with none of step 1's context. Every subsequent alternation repeats the cold start, so the documented "accumulated back-and-forth" never accumulates for a user who uses Spotlight Ref at all.

**Suggested fix.** Replace the single `activeConversation` slot with a small `Map<string, DustConversationRef>` keyed by `${workspaceId}|${agentId}` (a handful of entries at most). `resetDustConversation()` clears the whole map and bumps the epoch exactly as today; `isFresh` becomes a map lookup + TTL check, and the create branch writes into its own key instead of evicting another agent's thread.

**Verifier.** I tried to kill this and could not. Reproduced it against the real module.

MECHANISM (verified by reading, not inference):
- `src/main/llm/dust.ts:121` — `let activeConversation: DustConversationRef | null` is literally ONE slot, not a map.
- `src/main/llm/dust.ts:278-283` — `isFresh` requires `c.agentId === opts.model`.
- `src/main/llm/dust.ts:379-381` — the create branch overwrites that single slot unconditionally: the guard is only `sId && !opts.freshConversation && epochAtStart === conversationEpoch && !controller.signal.aborted`. Nothing preserves the previous agent's entry.

AGENT IDS REALLY DIFFER (so the mismatch is the default state, not an edge case):
- `src/shared/ipc.ts:1070-1071` — `DUST_BASE_AGENT_ID = 'vJxYHvTRBT'`, `DUST_SPOTLIGHT_REF_AGENT_ID = 'GOr913Zr5V'`; `ipc.ts:1076/1079` make them the shipped defaults for `providerModels.dust` and `providerModelsSpotlightRef.dust`.
- `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1329-1345` — Spotlight Ref sends `agentOverride: providerModelsSpotlightRef.dust` + `providerOverride: 'dust'`.
- `src/main/index.ts:2904-2905` uses `req.agentOverride` as the model when provider === 'dust'; `index.ts:2915-2921` pins non-override interactive asks to `providerModels['dust']` (the base agent). So `opts.model` genuinely alternates.

GUARDS I CHECKED AND RULED OUT:
- `freshConversation` is NOT set for Spotlight Ref (only `src/main/index.ts:725` import-recap and `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:172`), so it does take the caching path and does overwrite the slot.
- `src/main/index.ts:2733-2743`'s fresh-question reset explicitly EXEMPTS `agentOverride`/`providerOverride`, so it neither causes nor masks this.
- No other writer repopulates the base slot; `prewarmDustConversation` (dust.ts:149-188) warms the BASE agent at meeting start, so a Spotlight click also throws away the prewarm for the rest of the meeting.
- Existing test `src/main/llm/dust.test.ts:152-162` ("does not reuse a conversation across different Dust agents") locks the *isolation*, not the *eviction* — it never fires a third call back to the first agent, so nothing in the suite covers or blesses the thrash.

REPRO (executed): I ran a mocked-API test (temp file under node_modules/.repro-verify, since drive-crossing scratchpad paths break vite's id resolution; removed afterwards — `git status` confirms dust.ts untouched). Sequence base, base, SPOT, base, SPOT, base → `creates=5`, `createdFor=[base, spot, base, spot, base]`, `postedTo=['conv-1']`. Only the pre-Spotlight base→base reuse ever happened; every alternation cold-starts. Existing `dust.test.ts` still passes (12/12).

WHY THE HARM IS REAL FOR DUST SPECIFICALLY: `req.history` is consumed only by `anthropic.ts:6`, `openai.ts:8`, `cli.ts:8` — `dust.ts` builds `messageBody` from `preamble + userText(req)` alone (dust.ts:299-303), so the server-side conversation is Dust's ONLY continuity carrier (`index.ts:2706-2708` says exactly that: "TWO independent carriers"). Losing the slot really does lose the prior Q&A.

WHERE THE FINDER OVERREACHED (doesn't kill it): the quoted intent block continues past line 113 with "Scoped to (workspaceId, agentId) so switching agents/workspaces mid-session can't leak one agent's conversation into another's" — the finder omitted that clause. But that clause only sanctions non-mixing; a `Map` keyed by `${workspaceId}:${agentId}` satisfies isolation AND the promised per-meeting accumulation, so it does not sanction eviction, and the comment's own "Spotlight Ref ... reuse this conversation" is still flatly false in code (both sentences date from the same commit edbca25, so the contradiction is original, not drift). Also overstated: "never accumulates" — context does accumulate between alternations, and each ask still carries the transcript tail (`App.tsx:56-57` withContext, last 3000 chars) plus the full system preamble, so the agent is degraded, not blind.

SEVERITY: medium stands. Plausible headline workflow (Spotlight Ref mid-meeting with Dust as the chat provider), silent loss of the feature's documented value, plus an extra createConversation round trip per alternation that the prewarm exists to avoid. No data loss (the orphaned Dust conversations still exist server-side), no security impact — so not high.

FIX: swap the single slot for a Map keyed by `${workspaceId}::${agentId}` and key `creationInFlight` the same way; touches dust.ts:121/127/133-136/154-159/278-283/289-297/336/379-381 only. Small.

### MQA-053 — A successful failover is invisible: the app never tells the user the primary key is broken, and the "who is answering" indicator is not rendered at all after the first ask of a session

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:305` · workflow: ask a question after the primary key is revoked — the user needs to learn their key is dead so they can fix it · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:2952-2954: "Tell the waiting UI WHO is answering (\"Asking your Dust agent…\") — re-sent on retry/failover so the display follows the live attempt." src/renderer/src/state.ts:226-228: "Who is answering (from streamMeta, sent before any token) ... Follows the latest retry/failover." docs/asktoto-architecture.md:2300: "Fallback suggestion: if settings.fallbackChain configured, auto-routes and shows \"Switched to [provider]\""; :2317: "Graceful degradation (provider slow → fall back a tier and say so)".

**Actual.** src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:310 (`const who = provider === 'dust' ? 'your Dust agent' : provider ? PROVIDERS[provider]?.label : undefined`) is the ONLY consumer of `AnswerState.provider`, and it sits inside `if (thinking)` at Answer.tsx:305, where `thinking = !text && streaming` (Answer.tsx:97). src/renderer/src/state.ts:397 deliberately keeps the previous answer on screen (`text: prev?.text ?? ''`), so from the second question of a session onward `text` is non-empty, `thinking` is false, and the provider name is never rendered. Nothing else surfaces a failover: no notice, no chip on the finished answer, no Settings badge, no "Switched to X" string anywhere in src (grep "Switched to" -> no matches).

**Repro.** DeepSeek key revoked, NVIDIA NIM keyed. Ask three questions in one session. Main sends streamMeta twice per ask (deepseek, then nvidia — index.ts:2954) and all three answers come from NVIDIA. The renderer shows "Asking DeepSeek…" for a fraction of a second on ask #1 only, and nothing at all on asks #2 and #3. Settings still shows DeepSeek as the active provider with a stored key. The user is never told the key is dead, so it is never fixed and the degradation is permanent and silent.

**Suggested fix.** Carry the failover fact to the renderer, not just the provider id: add `viaFailover: attempted.length > 0` to the IPC.streamMeta payload (index.ts:2954) and, when true, render a persistent one-line notice on the finished answer ("Answered by NVIDIA · NIM — your DeepSeek key failed. Check it in Settings → AI."), reusing the dismissible notice slot Answer.tsx already has for capture failures. Pair it with a Settings → AI badge on the failing provider driven by the same cooldown state as the previous finding.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; the causal chain reproduces exactly, and the repo's own test proves the key step.

CHAIN: (1) Answer.tsx:97 `const thinking = !text && streaming`. (2) Answer.tsx:310 (`const who = provider === 'dust' ? ... : PROVIDERS[provider]?.label`) sits inside `if (thinking)` at Answer.tsx:305 and is the ONLY use of the `provider` prop in the file (grep for "provider" in Answer.tsx hits only the import at :3, unrelated error-hint strings at :33-40, the prop decl at :56/:78, a comment at :93, and :310). (3) App.tsx:2425 `provider={ask.answer?.provider}` is the ONLY consumer of AnswerState.provider anywhere in src/renderer. (4) state.ts:395-405 `run()` sets `text: prev?.text ?? ''`, deliberately preserving the previous answer. (5) The repo's OWN passing test nails the consequence: state.useAsk.test.ts:225 asserts turn 2 is `{ id: id2, text: 'OK', streaming: true }` — non-empty text AND streaming, so `thinking === false`. Ran it (`./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/state.useAsk.test.ts`): 2 passed. From ask #2 onward the thinking branch — and with it the provider name AND the "Still working… (Ns)" elapsed-time reassurance — is unreachable; the only busy signal is the blinking caret after the STALE previous answer.

FAILOVER IS SILENT: main/index.ts:3062 returns as soon as `failover(...)` succeeds, before any streamError is sent, so the primary's 401 never reaches the renderer when a second keyed provider answers. streamMeta is re-sent per attempt (index.ts:2961) and stored (state.ts:331-334) but has no live consumer. grep "Switched to" in src/ -> no matches.

REFUTATIONS ATTEMPTED: (a) Intended-behavior quote — the docs citation (asktoto-architecture.md:2300) is WEAK/aspirational: that L10 section describes `AnswerCard.tsx` and `settings.fallbackChain`, neither of which exists in src/. But the SHIPPED comments do carry the intent: index.ts:2959-2960 "re-sent on retry/failover so the display follows the live attempt" and state.ts:227 "Follows the latest retry/failover" — the state follows, the display is never rendered. Product principle at :2317 ("fall back a tier and say so") also stands. (b) Another surface? Closest is Settings.tsx:5270, a metrics panel rendering a `Fallbacks` count + per-provider request breakdown + "N answers failed" (fed by provider.request{retry:true} / provider.failed, metrics.ts:60,62). Real but count-only diagnostics — never names the dead key, mixes in transient retries, requires the user to already suspect a problem. Mitigates, does not refute. (c) Key health? None — no keyStatus/keyError/health chip in Settings.tsx, and nothing flags or clears a stored key after a 401; Settings keeps showing the revoked provider as active with a key present. (d) Bar.tsx shows nothing about provider (zero matches). (e) Does the ask path clear the answer first? No — App.tsx:1036 and :1048 call ask.run() directly; only clearAnswer (App.tsx:1712)/reset/recap call ask.clear().

PRECISION FIX TO THE FINDING: the indicator DOES render whenever the surface is empty — first ask of a session, and after "New chat"/back. Also, during a screen capture App.tsx:2417 forces text='' so the thinking branch renders with the PREVIOUS turn's provider (stale) — a related wrinkle, not a rescue.

SEVERITY: medium is right. The app still answers (degradation works) and a buried metrics tab exists, so not high; but the routing change is permanent, invisible, and contradicts what Settings shows as active — including which vendor receives screenshots/transcripts — so not low. FIX: small (render the provider/"switched from X" chip outside the `thinking` guard, e.g. on the finished answer or as a one-time notice when streamMeta.provider differs from settings.provider).

**FIXED (attribution 2026-08-08, notice 2026-08-17).** Two halves, both needed. The BYLINE is computed outside the `thinking` branch now and renders on the finished answer as "Answered by <provider>" ("Asking <provider>…" while a request streams under a preserved previous answer), so from ask #2 onward the answering brain is still named — Answer.test.tsx pins all three states including the anonymous one. That alone still did not tell the user WHY the answer came from somewhere else, which is the half this row is really about: App.tsx now renders a standing notice whenever the provider Settings shows as ACTIVE appears in `settings.unhealthyProviders` for a reason the user must act on (`auth`, `quota-exhausted`), naming the provider, saying another one is answering, and opening Settings → AI with that message. Deliberately NOT shown for `rate-limit` or `usage-cap`: those are the transient cases "Backups & limits" already promises to ride out, and nagging about a 60s cooldown is how a notice gets trained-out. Not dismissible — it is a standing state, and it clears itself when that provider answers again or its key changes (provider-health's own reset paths). Paired with the settings re-fetch below so it does not wait for a window focus.

### MQA-054 — Dust OAuth token keep-warm is gated to macOS, so on Windows the ~1h token expires with nothing to re-mint it outside the interactive ask path

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:4258` · workflow: index meetings / any background Dust-routed work on Windows · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:4279-4281 — "Keep the session warm for the app's whole lifetime: re-mint whenever the token passes 45 min of its ~1h life, so it never expires mid-meeting and the user never sees a Dust reconnect." The macOS-only rationale in the comment above it (index.ts:4246-4249: the Keychain "allow access" prompt) does not apply to Windows: src/main/dust-secret-store.ts:17 states "Reading the CURRENT user's own credential never prompts on Windows/Linux; macOS shows a one-time...", and src/main/dustcli.ts:19-21 states the module "orchestrates import, refresh, and first-run setup on top, identically on every platform" (refreshDustCliSession explicitly handles the Windows `dust.cmd` shim at dustcli.ts:104-113).

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:4258 `if (process.platform !== 'darwin' || !hasApiKey('dust')) return` — refreshAndPersistDust is a no-op on win32, so neither the startup refresh (index.ts:4278) nor the 10-minute keep-warm interval (index.ts:4282) ever runs on Windows.

**Repro.** Windows (this branch's target; docs/cahe-windows-edition.md:18 makes Dust setup part of Cahê first-run). Connect Dust, leave Métis running. At T+0 the imported token is fresh. At T+70min no refresh has occurred on any path. The 60s brain reconcile tick (index.ts:4338) picks up a newly saved meeting and routes extraction to Dust -> 401/expired-token -> ingest has no refresh hook (see the runCompletionOnce finding) and the error string carries no status digits, so the walk halts. Every subsequent background index attempt fails identically until the user happens to make an interactive ask, whose lazy refreshDustAuth (index.ts:2988-2996) silently re-mints the token. Same Métis build on macOS never reaches this state because the 10-minute interval keeps the token under 45 minutes old.

**Suggested fix.** Drop `process.platform !== 'darwin'` from the guard at index.ts:4258 (keep `!hasApiKey('dust')`). dust-secret-store.ts already implements the Windows Credential Manager read and dustcli.ts already routes the `dust.cmd` shim, so the keep-warm works as-is cross-platform; the darwin gate only ever existed to avoid the macOS Keychain prompt, which Windows does not have.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED (line numbers in the finding are ~60 low; the code is at src/main/index.ts:4317-4342).

The code fact is exact. `src/main/index.ts:4318` is `if (process.platform !== 'darwin' || !hasApiKey('dust')) return`, so both the startup refresh (`runStep('refreshDustSession', ...)`, index.ts:4338) and the lifetime keep-warm (`trackTimer(setInterval(..., 10 * 60 * 1000))`, index.ts:4342) are no-ops on win32.

The "intended" quote checks out verbatim (index.ts:4339-4341: "Keep the session warm for the app's whole lifetime: re-mint whenever the token passes 45 min of its ~1h life, so it never expires mid-meeting and the user never sees a Dust reconnect") and is platform-neutral. The only macOS-specific rationale in the preceding block (index.ts:4306-4315) is the Keychain "allow access"/password prompt — a cost `src/main/dust-secret-store.ts:17` explicitly says does not exist on Windows ("Reading the CURRENT user's own credential never prompts on Windows/Linux").

Refutations I tried and why each failed:
1. "The gate is deliberate." Git history says otherwise. The gate landed 2026-07-05 in 168327a ("Dust CLI: one login that stays logged in"), when the whole Dust CLI path was darwin-only. The cross-platform commit 1258c8f (2026-07-10) says it "drops all three darwin-only gates" and the auto-import poll is "un-gated from darwin" — and its index.ts diff removes exactly one darwin gate (`if (r.ok && process.platform === 'darwin')` → `if (r.ok)`) while leaving this one untouched. Settings.tsx:2434-2435 states Dust setup is "cross-platform now ... no per-platform gating".
2. "Windows Dust can't refresh anyway." It can: dust-secret-store readWin (CredRead), setupDustCli win32 `.cmd` (dustcli.ts:201-221), `resolveSpawnTarget` for the `dust.cmd` shim (dustcli.ts:107-113), and `resolveBin` win32 via where.exe + %APPDATA%\npm probe (cli.ts:122-144). Ungating would work.
3. "Some other Windows path re-mints in background." Enumerated every caller: only dustImportCli (index.ts:2175), dustListAgents on-401 (2157), the 5-minute one-shot post-login setup poll (2208-2239), and the two `refreshDustAuth` closures. dustProbeSession (2190) deliberately uses read-only `importDustCliSession` and never persists. None is a background keep-warm.
4. "The on-401 refresh covers it, so nothing breaks." Only 3 `createStream` call sites exist repo-wide: index.ts:702 (import recap) and index.ts:3022 (ask) both pass `refreshDustAuth`; `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:162` does not. And a Dust 401 there does not fail over either: `isIngestTransportFailure` (ingest.ts:139-144) needs `isTransient` (retry.ts:57-59 returns false for auth by design) or a literal `\b4\d\d\b` in the message, and Dust's observed 401 wording carries no digits (dust.test.ts:205-209: "The user request does not have a valid authenticated credential.", "Unauthorized"). It throws, and 6 consecutive failures (MAX_INGEST_ATTEMPTS = 6, ingest.ts:1250, backoff capped at 30 min at ingest.ts:1243) mark the record `exhausted` — a terminal state the auto reconcile stops requeuing (ingest.ts:1245-1249). So the Windows-only delta is real: on macOS the keep-warm is what keeps that hookless path alive.

Severity corrected high → medium. It is a genuine platform-parity defect with a Windows-only dead-end, but: (a) the keep-warm is by the code's own comments a redundancy layer, and its loss only bites in combination with the separate missing-`refreshDustAuth` defect at ingest.ts:162 — fixing either makes the symptom vanish; (b) it needs Dust to be the first eligible ingest candidate, whereas this branch's stated Windows target defaults to Kimi Code with local fallback on (docs/cahe-windows-edition.md:10); (c) it is recoverable and lossless — the transcript persists, any interactive ask re-mints, and Retry / dashboard-open / boot resume clear `exhausted` (ingest.ts:1918-1925).

Fix is trivial: drop `process.platform !== 'darwin' ||` from index.ts:4318 (the `dustTokenMintedAt` freshness check at 4319 already suppresses needless mints). The stale "macOS only, matching importDustCliSession" comment at src/main/dustcli.ts:78 should go with it. No test asserts the gate (grep for `refreshAndPersistDust` hits no test file); `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/dustcli.test.ts src/main/llm/dust.test.ts` → 12 passed, 6 skipped (keychain-gated).

### MQA-055 — Brain ingest is the only Dust caller that omits refreshDustAuth, so an expired Dust token is never self-healed during background indexing

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:162` · workflow: index meetings (brain ingest / entity extraction) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/llm/shared.ts:25-28 documents the option as: "Called on a PRE-token Dust auth failure (expired OAuth token) to obtain fresh credentials. Returns the new creds (and persists them as a side effect)... Enables one transparent retry so an expired Dust token self-heals instead of surfacing a 401." src/main/llm/dust.ts:255 — "On a pre-token auth failure, refresh the token once and replay the same request."

**Actual.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:162-182 — runCompletionOnce's createStream({...}) options object passes providerId/kind/apiKey/baseURL/workspaceId/model/temperature/idleMs/maxOutputTokens/freshConversation/system/req/handlers, but no `refreshDustAuth`. Every other Dust caller supplies it: the ask path at src/main/index.ts:2988-2996 and the import recap cascade at src/main/index.ts:700-709. Without it, dust.ts:258 (`if (!allowRetry || gotToken || !opts.refreshDustAuth || !isAuthErr(err)) return false`) and dust.ts:393 both short-circuit and the raw 401 message is delivered to onError.

**Repro.** Dust-only org profile (managed-config allowedProviders: ['dust']) or Dust reached anywhere in the waterfall. The Dust CLI access token is ~1h-lived (src/main/dustcli.ts:24, src/shared/ipc.ts:853). After it lapses, the next background extraction calls runCompletionOnce with the stale token -> dust.ts createConversation returns an auth error -> retryIfAuth bails at dust.ts:258 because opts.refreshDustAuth is undefined -> fail(created.error.message) -> ingest records ok:false. The identical request issued a second later through the ask path succeeds, because that path refreshes and replays. The user sees Dust answering questions normally while every meeting silently fails to index, and after 6 ticks the records go `exhausted` (ingest.ts:1411), which the automatic reconcile tick then skips forever (ingest.ts:1924).

**Suggested fix.** Pass the same refreshDustAuth closure used at src/main/index.ts:2988-2996 into runCompletionOnce's createStream call (guarded on `provider === 'dust'`). refreshDustCliSession is already single-flighted with a 30s result cache (dustcli.ts:88-96), so concurrent backfill jobs cannot burn the rotating refresh token. Add a regression test asserting one transparent refresh+replay when a Dust ingest call returns an auth error.

**Verifier.** I tried to refute this four ways and could not kill the causal chain.

CODE FACTS (all verified by reading):
1. `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:162-182` — `runCompletionOnce` builds the `createStream({...})` options literal with providerId/kind/apiKey/baseURL/workspaceId/model/temperature/idleMs/maxOutputTokens/freshConversation/system/req/handlers. No `refreshDustAuth`. Grep for `refreshDustAuth` across `src/` returns exactly two production call sites, both in `src/main/index.ts` (line 708 ask/recap cascade, line 3031 main ask handler) plus `shared.ts:29` (the type) and two dust tests. Brain files contain zero occurrences.
2. Not injected downstream: `src/main/llm.ts:17-30` `createStream` is a bare `switch (opts.kind)` dispatcher — it passes `opts` through to `streamDust` unchanged, no defaulting.
3. `src/main/llm/dust.ts:258` (`if (!allowRetry || gotToken || !opts.refreshDustAuth || !isAuthErr(err)) return false`) and `dust.ts:393` both short-circuit on the undefined option, so `dust.ts:370 fail(created.error.message)` delivers the raw auth message to `onError` → `ingest.ts:180 reject(new Error(m))`. The quoted intent at `shared.ts:25-28` and `dust.ts:255` says exactly what the finder claims.
4. Dust is genuinely an ingest candidate: `ingest.ts:96-110` walks every allowed+keyed provider, with only `if (p === 'dust' && !s.dustWorkspaceId) continue` as a Dust-specific gate. `ingest-local.test.ts:126-129` sets Dust as the ingest provider in an existing regression test, confirming the path is live.
5. WORSE THAN CLAIMED — no failover rescue. `retry.ts:58` deliberately returns false for auth ("Auth is not transient — it has its own refresh-and-replay path"), and `ingest.ts:143` only widens to `/timed out|\b4\d\d\b/`. The Dust expired-token message is prose ("expired_oauth_token", "…does not have valid authentication credentials" — see `dust.ts:24-40`), carrying no 4xx digit, so `isIngestTransportFailure` is false and `runCompletion` (ingest.ts:210) throws instead of walking to the next cloud candidate or the appended local fallback. So it breaks multi-provider setups too, not just Dust-only orgs.

WHAT PARTLY DEFENDS IT (why I downgrade high → medium):
- `src/main/index.ts:4316-4342` runs a keep-warm: every 10 min, if the token is >45 min into its ~1h life, re-mint via `refreshDustCliSession()` and `setApiKey('dust', …)`. On macOS this means ingest essentially never sees a lapsed token. BUT line 4318 gates the whole thing on `process.platform !== 'darwin'` — on Windows/Linux there is NO proactive refresh at all, so the gap is fully live there (relevant on this Windows-audit branch).
- Any interactive Dust ask/recap refreshes and persists the token (`index.ts:713`, `index.ts:3036`); `getApiKey` reads that fresh value, so the window self-closes once the user asks anything. The bite case is unattended work: the 60s reconcile tick and a long backfill/team-folder scan spanning the token's expiry.
- The failure is durable, not invisible: `ingest.ts:1400-1414` records `ok:false` + error + exponential `retryDelayMs` (1→30 min), and `MAX_INGEST_ATTEMPTS = 6` (ingest.ts:1250) with backoff spans well over an hour, not "6 ticks". And `exhausted` is not permanent: `ingest.ts:1923-1926` only skips it when `respectRetryBackoff` is true (the automatic tick); the Index/Retry button, dashboard-open check, `resumeBackfillIfPending` at boot (ingest.ts:1838, no options) and rebuild all un-exhaust it. The finder's "skips forever" is overstated.

No guard, schema default, caller, or test prevents it — I checked every brain test file for `dust`/`refreshDustAuth`/`workspaceId` and found no coverage of these options. `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/llm/dust.stream-auth-retry.test.ts` passes (1/1), which only confirms the self-heal works when the callback IS supplied — it is opt-in per call site.

Fix: pass the same refresher into `ingest.ts:162`'s options for `provider === 'dust'` (extract the duplicated closure at index.ts:708/3031 into a shared helper over `refreshDustCliSession` + `setApiKey` + `setSettings`; `main/dustcli.ts` has no import cycle with `brain/ingest.ts`). Separately worth noting: the `!== 'darwin'` gate at index.ts:4318 is what makes this reachable at all on Windows.

### MQA-056 — Import-audio recap has no on-device fallback — a dead cloud key leaves the imported meeting with no summary even though the same meeting is indexed locally

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:659` · workflow: import an audio file (automatic summary after transcription) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:1491 (the Local AI → Fallback toggle description): "If every configured cloud provider is unreachable or none is set up, run meeting indexing, live suggestions, summaries and screenshot analysis on-device as a last resort — instead of failing. Cloud providers are always preferred when they work." src/main/llm/local-routing.ts:82-91 defines the gate for exactly this: "whether 'local' may serve THIS request as the strictly-LAST resort once every cloud/CLI route is exhausted... Deliberately ignores the per-mode useFor opt-in". src/main/index.ts:656 itself states "An imported recording is a summary task."

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:659 `const localSummaryReady = localEligibleFor({ mode: 'summary' }, settings, 'base', allowed)` and index.ts:669 `if (provider === 'local') return localSummaryReady`. runImportedRecap consults only localEligibleFor, which requires `s.localLlm.useFor.summary` (src/main/llm/local-routing.ts:76). It never consults localFallbackEligibleFor — the only two call sites are src/main/index.ts:2820 and 2938, both in the live-ask path.

**Repro.** Ship defaults: localLlm.enabled=true, fallback=true, useFor.summary=false (src/shared/ipc.ts:889-905), bundled model provisioned; one cloud key (e.g. Kimi) that has been revoked. Import a .wav. Transcription succeeds and the meeting is saved. generateRecap -> runImportedRecap builds candidates = ['kimi'] (local excluded because useFor.summary is false), the stream errors 401, the loop at index.ts:682-750 exhausts and throws at index.ts:751. import-jobs.ts:358 sets job.recapError and the card reads "Transcript saved. Open the meeting to retry the summary." Meanwhile the very same meeting IS indexed on-device, because brain ingest's pickProviderCandidates appends local under the same fallback flag (ingest.ts:119-121). Same setting, same meeting, two opposite behaviours.

**Suggested fix.** Build the candidate list with `localEligibleFor(...) || localFallbackEligibleFor({ mode: 'summary' }, settings, 'base', allowed)`, keeping the fallback-only case ordered LAST (after every cloud/CLI candidate) rather than first, so the existing useFor.summary=true precedence is unchanged. Add a test: fallback on, useFor.summary off, sole cloud provider 401s -> recap is produced by 'local' and job.recapError stays unset.

**Verifier.** SURVIVES. I tried four refutations; all failed.

Causal chain reproduced verbatim (line numbers are ~8 lower in the finder's snapshot but the text matches exactly):
- `D:\Asktoto\src\main\index.ts:667` — `const localSummaryReady = localEligibleFor({ mode: 'summary' }, settings, 'base', allowed)`; `index.ts:677` — `if (provider === 'local') return localSummaryReady`. That is the ONLY local gate in `runImportedRecap`.
- `D:\Asktoto\src\main\llm\local-routing.ts:76` — `localEligibleFor` requires `s.localLlm.useFor[req.mode]`, i.e. `useFor.summary`.
- `localFallbackEligibleFor` (`local-routing.ts:93`) is called only at `index.ts:2851`, `:2929`, `:2969` — all three inside `askStart`. (Finder said "two call sites at 2820/2938"; the count/lines are sloppy but the substance — all live-ask, none in the import path — is correct.)
- Defaults confirmed at `src/shared/ipc.ts` localLlm block: `enabled: true`, `useFor.{suggest,summary,vision}: false`, `fallback: true`.
- Failure path confirmed: candidates exhaust → `index.ts:759` throws → `import-jobs.ts:358` sets `job.recapError` → `work-progress.ts:184` renders "Transcript saved. Open the meeting to retry the summary."
- Asymmetry confirmed: `import-jobs.ts:363` `await this.deps.enqueueIngest(file)` runs for the same meeting, and `brain/ingest.ts:118` `if (s.localLlm.fallback && localBaseReady(s, allowed)) candidates.push({ provider: 'local', ... })`. Same flag, same meeting, opposite outcome.

Refutation attempts that failed:
1. "The retry recovers it." No — `App.tsx:1506` and `:1836` fire the manual recap with `mode: 'recap'`, and `local-routing.ts:18` `LOCAL_SCOPED_MODES = ['suggest','summary','vision']` excludes 'recap' in BOTH gates. So the UI's own advice ("Open the meeting to retry the summary") also cannot degrade on-device. There is no recovery path at all.
2. "The intended-behavior quote is misread." No — `src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:1491` is verbatim: "If every configured cloud provider is unreachable or none is set up, run meeting indexing, live suggestions, summaries and screenshot analysis on-device as a last resort — instead of failing." And `index.ts:664` really does say "An imported recording is a summary task." — the code itself classifies this task as `summary` (it sends `mode: local ? 'summary' : 'recap'` at `index.ts:693`), so 'recap is out of local's v1 scope' does not excuse it.
3. "A test/contract pins the current behavior as deliberate." No. `src/main/import-recap.contract.test.ts` only pins the trailing-stream-error salvage; `local-routing.test.ts` never touches the import path. Ran both: 83 passed, 2 files, no assertion about import + fallback.
4. "A schema default or guard covers it." No. The only partial counterweight is developer-facing scope prose: `ipc.ts` says the flag "Gates BOTH surfaces: the meeting-index waterfall … and in-scope live asks", and commit dda7c7a's message says the flag was "extended from meeting indexing to in-scope live asks". So the omission may have been an unnoticed gap rather than a considered exclusion — but that is an argument that the import surface was forgotten, not that it was deliberately denied. The user-facing promise, and the fact that `useFor.summary` (the Settings row literally labeled "Summaries") DOES gate this exact path local-first, make the one-directional coverage indefensible: the same toggle pair covers imports for local-first and abandons them for last-resort.

Worst case is stronger than the finder's repro: with zero API keys (the install this feature exists for — see docs/qa/BUG-LEDGER.md MQA-006 "a zero-API-key install still gets a working assistant"), `candidates.length === 0` at `index.ts:683`, so `runImportedRecap` returns undefined and `import-jobs.ts:354` writes "No AI provider is configured to create the automatic summary." while a provisioned on-device model sits idle and indexes the very same file.

Severity medium is correct: the transcript is saved (no data loss) and a working cloud key fixes it, but the auto-summary silently never happens on default settings and no on-device retry exists.

Fix is small, not trivial: `local` sits second-to-last in `PROVIDERS` (`src/shared/providers.ts:307`, before only `custom`), so adding `|| localFallbackEligibleFor({ mode: 'summary' }, settings, 'base', allowed)` to the `index.ts:677` filter nearly gets the ordering right, but making local strictly last requires also handling the `custom` position (and the dedupe at `index.ts:674`), plus a test. Note an adjacent, separate issue I did not report: unlike `ingest.ts:85-87`, `runImportedRecap` waterfalls from local into cloud even when `useFor.summary` is on — uploading a transcript the user chose to keep on-device.

READ-ONLY: nothing changed.

### MQA-057 — codex-cli can never be a brain-ingest candidate (empty model id), so a Codex-CLI-only user's meetings are silently indexed by the 0.8B on-device model or not at all

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:108` · workflow: index meetings (brain ingest) with a CLI subscription instead of an API key · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:2905-2910 — the ask path deliberately exempts CLI providers from the model check: `def.kind !== 'cli' && !model ? ... : ''`, i.e. an empty model is an expected, handled state for a CLI provider, never a disqualifier. src/main/cli.ts:318-319 confirms it is handled downstream: "'--model' is unconditional: an empty model must never silently inherit the user's own CLI default (which can be a premium model) — floor to the cheapest current model instead."

**Actual.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:107-108 applies `const model = resolveModelTier(p, ...,'deep', ...); if (!model) continue` unconditionally, including for `def.kind === 'cli'`. PROVIDERS['codex-cli'] (src/shared/providers.ts:275-290) has defaultModel:'', fastModel:'', thinkModel:'' and no deepModel, and the shipped providerModels default is `{ dust: DUST_BASE_AGENT_ID }` (src/shared/ipc.ts:1068) — so resolveModelTier (src/shared/providers.ts:507-514) returns '' and codex-cli is dropped from the candidate list. ('claude-cli' survives only because it declares deepModel:'opus'.)

**Repro.** Profile whose only provider is a connected Codex CLI (Settings → CLI Integration; cliConnected['codex-cli']=true, no API keys, providerModels['codex-cli'] left blank). Asking questions works. Click Index meetings: pickProviderCandidates skips codex-cli at ingest.ts:108, so with localLlm.fallback on (default) every meeting is extracted by the bundled 0.8B Qwen (ingest.ts:119-121) while the user's frontier CLI subscription sits idle and unused — with nothing in the index record or the UI naming the model that produced the extraction. With local disabled or org-excluded, hasUsableProvider() is false and startBackfill returns {queued:0, deferred:'no-provider'}, and BrainView.tsx:518 tells the user to "Connect an AI provider in Settings → AI" when one is already connected and working.

**Suggested fix.** Mirror the ask path's exemption: `if (def.kind !== 'cli' && !model) continue`, and pass the (possibly empty) model through to createStream — cli.ts:315-330 already floors an empty model to the cheapest option. Add a test asserting a connected codex-cli appears in pickProviderCandidates ahead of the local fallback.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; independently reproduced. (1) src/main/brain/ingest.ts:107-108 applies `const model = resolveModelTier(p,...,'deep',...); if (!model) continue` with no `def.kind === 'cli'` exemption, even though line 104 immediately above DOES branch on `def.kind === 'cli'` for the connected check. (2) src/shared/providers.ts:275-290 confirms codex-cli has models:[], defaultModel:'', fastModel:'', thinkModel:'' and NO deepModel key. (3) Empirically proven, not just read: I transpiled src/shared/providers.ts with the repo's own esbuild and evaluated resolveModelTier against the shipped default providerModels ({dust: DUST_BASE_AGENT_ID}, src/shared/ipc.ts:1076) — codex-cli returns deep="" / base="" (def.deepModel undefined), claude-cli returns deep="opus". So codex-cli is unconditionally dropped at ingest.ts:108. (4) The "intended behavior" claim is accurate and in fact understated: THREE other main-process sites deliberately exempt CLI from the model check — index.ts:2938 (`def.kind !== 'cli' && !model`), index.ts:677-681 in runImportedRecap (`if (def.kind === 'cli') return !!settings.cliConnected[provider]`, returning before the resolveModelTier check), and most damningly index.ts:2832-2838, whose comment states "CLI providers (e.g. codex-cli) may have no configured model at all ... a failover candidate must be exempted the same way or a fully default-configured CLI provider can never be selected." brain/ingest.ts is the lone outlier, and its own docstring (lines 75-83) falsely claims it runs "the SAME eligibility checks". (5) Empty model is genuinely handled downstream — better than the finder's citation: cli.ts:377 `...(model ? ['-m', model] : [])` in codex-cli's own buildArgs. (The finder's cli.ts:318-319 quote is real text but describes claude-cli's --model floor, a different policy; substance survives via cli.ts:377.) Refutations attempted and failed: no schema default or migration fills providerModels['codex-cli'] (DEFAULT_SETTINGS.providerModels is {dust:...} only; store.ts:456-465 only rewrites retired ids in already-persisted maps); no UI prompts for a CLI model (Settings.tsx:138 puts codex-cli in CLI_PROVIDERS, excluded from the generic tiles/key section, and renderCliCard 1694-1830 has no model field — only the collapsed Advanced base-model free-text input at Settings.tsx:1068 could set one); it is not a deliberate cost policy since line 104 explicitly admits CLI providers and claude-cli is a working ingest candidate today; no test pins it (ingest-backfill.test.ts:53 / ingest-team.test.ts:41 list 'codex-cli':'' as an API-key env entry but never set cliConnected; c-main-fixes.contract.test.ts:38 covers index.ts's cliPrimary, not ingest) — I ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/ingest-index-fallback.test.ts src/main/brain/ingest-backfill.test.ts, 17/17 pass, none exercises a CLI-connected profile; and the UI does not save the user, since index.ts:852-856 reports providerReady:true for a connected CLI provider, so BrainView.tsx:645 canIndex is true while startBackfill returns deferred:'no-provider' and BrainView.tsx:518 wrongly says "Connect an AI provider in Settings → AI". Defaults (localLlm.enabled:true, fallback:true in ipc.ts DEFAULT_SETTINGS) make the default outcome the silent 0.8B substitution at ingest.ts:119-121 rather than a hard failure — that is the degrade, not a rescue. Severity stays medium, not high: Onboarding.tsx:549-565 prefers claude-cli when Claude Code is installed and only falls back to codex-cli, so the affected segment is Codex-CLI-without-Claude-Code users plus explicit Settings connections, and the local fallback keeps indexing functional (just silently downgraded and unattributed). Fix is one condition at ingest.ts:108 mirroring index.ts:2836-2838: `if (def.kind !== 'cli' && !model) continue`.

### MQA-058 — An explicit graphify engine choice silently falls through to a different provider when its key stops working, sending the whole meetings folder somewhere the user did not pick

**Where.** `src/main/graphify.ts:191` · workflow: knowledge graph auto-rebuild after each saved meeting · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/graphify.ts:190 labels the cascade as the AUTO path only: "// auto: local Claude Code → stored Claude key → stored OpenAI key". The Settings UI presents the three options as exclusive contracts — src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:5553-5555: "Auto · Claude Code, then your Claude or OpenAI key" / "Claude · uses your Anthropic key" / "OpenAI · uses your OpenAI key". graphify.ts:184-185 also states the file's own discipline: "graphify streams the full transcript to its backend, so a pinned data-residency policy must gate the backend choice".

**Actual.** src/main/graphify.ts:188-193 — the two pref-specific returns are plain `if`s with no `else`/early-exit, so when the chosen provider's key is absent, control falls straight into the auto cascade at lines 191-193 and returns a DIFFERENT backend instead of null.

**Repro.** settings.graphifyBackend='openai' ("OpenAI · uses your OpenAI key"), graphifyEnabled + graphifyAutoRebuild on (both default true, src/shared/ipc.ts:703-705). The user's OpenAI key is revoked and they delete it in Settings → AI; an Anthropic key remains. Save any meeting -> scheduleRebuild (graphify.ts:340) -> 20s later buildGraph(true) -> pickBackend(): line 188 fails (pref!=='claude'), line 189 fails (hasApiKey('openai') false), line 191/192 returns { backend:'claude-cli' } or { backend:'claude', apiKey:<anthropic key> } -> graphify.ts:314 spawns the runner and the entire meetings (or wiki/) folder is extracted through Anthropic/Claude Code, with no error and no prompt. The only signal is the small `backend` label in graphifyStatus (graphify.ts:226).

**Suggested fix.** Make an explicit preference exclusive: `if (pref === 'claude') return hasApiKey('anthropic') && ok('anthropic') ? { backend:'claude', apiKey:getApiKey('anthropic') } : null` (and likewise for 'openai'), so a dead/removed key yields the existing actionable "No extraction backend. Install Claude Code, or add a Claude/OpenAI key in Settings → AI." (graphify.ts:300) instead of a silent provider swap. Run the cascade at 191-193 only when pref === 'auto'.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED. src/main/graphify.ts:188-193: the two pref-specific returns are plain sequential `if`s; `pref` is never consulted again after line 189 and the function's only other exit is `return null` at :195. So pref='openai' with no OpenAI key falls straight into the auto cascade at :191-193 and returns claude-cli/claude with the Anthropic key.

Refutations attempted and failed: (1) No caller guard — pickBackend has exactly two call sites, graphify.ts:205 (graphifyStatus) and graphify.ts:296 (buildGraph); neither compares pref to picked.backend. buildGraph's only gates are graphifyRefusalReason (encryption) and confidentialGraphRefusal — neither concerns provider identity. (2) No sanitizer — graphifyBackend appears repo-wide only at graphify.ts:183, Settings.tsx:5548-5549, ipc.ts:705/1090; the IPC.setApiKey handler (index.ts:2103-2126) has no reset side effect, so deleting the key leaves the pin stale. (3) No test — ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/graphify.test.ts passes 9/9 but covers only computeRelated, windowsPythonDirs, and MI-5 refusal/source-dir routing; pickBackend is untested. (4) Quotes verified verbatim (graphify.ts:190, :184-185; Settings.tsx:5553-5555) and independently corroborated by src/shared/ipc.ts:700-702, which binds the cascade to one option: "backend 'auto' = local Claude Code CLI -> stored Claude key -> stored OpenAI key". The presence of a distinct 'auto' option is what makes 'claude'/'openai' exclusive contracts. (5) Strongest counterargument — brain/ingest.ts:84-122 and index.ts runImportedRecap both intentionally waterfall from s.provider across all configured providers, so "preference then waterfall" is a house pattern. Rejected: those settings have no separate 'auto' alternative, and ingest.ts:79-81 states the opposite rule for an explicit user pick (local-summary "is the ONLY candidate whenever active — never waterfalls into a cloud provider, since that would silently upload a transcript the user chose to keep on-device").

Severity medium is correct, not higher: ok() gates every cascade branch, so an org allowedProviders pin fails closed to null (graphify.ts:186-187) — only the individual user's UI choice is unenforced; and the fallback target is always a vendor the user already keyed in this app. Not lower, because graphifyEnabled/graphifyAutoRebuild both default true (ipc.ts:703-704) so full transcripts (or the wiki/ mirror) ship to the unchosen vendor silently in the background. Finder understated one point: there is zero user-visible signal — status.backend is consumed in the renderer only as a boolean (Settings.tsx:5523, :5562) and the engine name is never rendered. Fix is trivial: make lines 188-189 exhaustive for non-'auto' prefs (return null rather than falling through).

### MQA-059 — A revoked API key on the active provider is silently absorbed by cross-provider failover — the user is never told, and providerReady stays true forever

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:3055` · workflow: ask a question / get an answer when your key stops working · fix size: small

**Intended.** docs/asktoto-architecture.md:224 (Section B.9 Failure States) — "| **Invalid / expired API key** | Answer error block | \"Your API key may be invalid or expired. Update it in Settings → Your AI.\" | Retry + settings |", plus the B.9 design rule at docs/asktoto-architecture.md:240 — "Failure copy names the cause and points at the exact setting to fix it."

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:3054-3055 — "// Retries exhausted or non-transient: fall over to another provider (pre-token only)." then `if (!gotToken && provider !== 'local' && failover(attempted.concat(provider))) return`. A pre-token 401 is non-transient (src/main/llm/retry.ts:57-59), so it goes straight to failover and NO streamError is ever sent. The only suppression is src/main/llm/local-routing.ts:169-171 `allowCrossProviderFailover` = `!req.agentOverride`, i.e. it only protects pinned Dust-agent requests (the QA-024 fix), not ordinary asks. Meanwhile `providerReady` (src/main/index.ts:844-853) is derived from `hasApiKey(s.provider)`, which is `getApiKey(provider).length > 0` (src/main/store.ts:891-893) — a key STRING check, never a key WORKS check — so nothing in the app ever downgrades it. The Bar setup CTA is gated on `!settings.providerReady` (src/renderer/src/App.tsx:2771) and therefore never appears. The answering provider from streamMeta is only rendered in Answer.tsx's pre-first-token 'thinking' branch (src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:305-316), so once text arrives there is zero indication of who answered.

**Repro.** Settings → provider = Anthropic (the default, src/shared/ipc.ts DEFAULT_SETTINGS.provider = 'anthropic') with a key you then revoke at console.anthropic.com; also have an OpenAI key saved. Ask "summarise this call". Anthropic returns a pre-token 401 → isTransient false → failover('openai') → the answer streams from GPT. Result: a normal-looking answer, no error, no hint, Settings still shows Anthropic active with a saved key and 'ready' state, no Bar CTA. Every subsequent ask silently runs on OpenAI (different model, different vendor, different cost/data path) and the user never learns the Anthropic key is dead.

**Suggested fix.** Track a per-provider auth-failure latch in main: on a pre-token failure classified as auth (reuse retry.ts's AUTH_PATTERN / status===401), record `{provider, at}` and expose it on PublicSettings (e.g. `keyFailedProviders`). Make providerReady false (or add a distinct `providerKeyFailed`) for that provider until a successful request or a successful key test clears it, so the existing Bar CTA and requireProvider() path fire. Even if failover still answers, send a one-shot non-terminal notice (the Answer captureNotice pattern already exists) saying "Your <Provider> key was rejected — answered with <Fallback> instead. Fix it in Settings → AI."

**Verifier.** Reproduced the full chain. src/main/llm/retry.ts:58-59 makes a pre-token 401 non-transient, so src/main/index.ts:3099's retry gate is skipped and 3107 (`if (!gotToken && provider !== 'local' && failover(attempted.concat(provider))) return`) returns BEFORE the streamError at 3121 — the MQA-005 auth copy at 3119 is only reachable when pickFailover finds nothing. allowCrossProviderFailover (src/main/llm/local-routing.ts:186-188) is `!req.agentOverride`, i.e. pinned-Dust only, so an ordinary ask is unprotected. providerReady (src/main/index.ts:852-861) derives from hasApiKey = getApiKey(provider).length > 0 (src/main/store.ts:891-893), a string check with no health input; the Bar CTA at src/renderer/src/App.tsx:2771 is gated on !providerReady and so never fires. Answer.tsx uses the streamMeta `provider` in exactly one place (line 310, the pre-first-token `thinking` branch) — no header/footer chip.

Best refutation attempt: the MQA-003/004 fix DOES exist — src/main/llm/provider-health.ts, unhealthyProviders() wired into the snapshot at index.ts:907, schema at src/shared/ipc.ts:1014, and 33 tests pass (provider-health.test.ts + provider-health-ux.contract.test.ts, run green). It dies on one fact: `grep -rn "unhealthyProviders" src/renderer` returns ZERO consumers. The signal is computed and shipped over IPC and no component renders it. src/shared/ipc.ts:1009-1013 states the field's own purpose ("without this the UI reports a provider as ready forever while every ask silently degrades") and that UI was never built. docs/qa/BUG-LEDGER.md:33 marks MQA-004 FIXED while its own suggested fix (:119-121) required a banner "and reflect it in providerReady" — neither shipped. No OS-notification path either (the only three `new Notification` sites in main are import-done at index.ts:447, meeting-soon at 1651, Dust-connected at 2231). Settings has no health badge.

One caveat on the finder's citation: the docs/asktoto-architecture.md:224 row quotes verbatim, but it governs the "Answer error block" case, which IS correctly implemented (index.ts:3119 + Answer.tsx:37) whenever no failover target exists — a single-provider user is told properly. The stronger in-repo intent anchors are ipc.ts:1009-1013 and BUG-LEDGER MQA-004 itself. The behavior survives either way.

Severity corrected high -> medium: the two damaging halves of the original pair are genuinely fixed (cooldown at index.ts:3155 kills the 6.5-9.3s per-ask stall; 3119 gives actionable copy when failover is exhausted). What remains is a transparency defect on a path that still returns a correct answer, requires >=2 keyed providers, is session-scoped (COOLDOWN_MS, never persisted), and has a manual detection path (testApiKey rejects the dead key). Residual harm is real: false "ready" state, no CTA, and every later ask silently runs on a different vendor/cost/data path with only a transient "Asking ChatGPT..." thinking label as a signal.

Fix: render settings.unhealthyProviders as a banner beside the existing CTA at App.tsx:2771 and refresh settings on stream end (the focus-refetch at state.ts:539 would otherwise delay it). Folding health into providerReady itself is riskier — it feeds ~10 gates (App.tsx:707, 736, 1491, 2146; BrainView.tsx:403) that currently succeed via failover.

**FIXED (2026-08-17).** Exactly the remedy this entry names, and only that one. `settings.unhealthyProviders` — computed and shipped since MQA-004, with ZERO renderer consumers until now — is rendered beside the existing setup CTA in App.tsx, scoped to the ACTIVE provider and to the act-on-it reasons (`auth`, `quota-exhausted`). The second half of the same remedy: settings are re-fetched when a visible ask stops streaming (a `wasStreamingRef` transition guard, never on mount), because provider health is session state main computes as a side effect of answering and the snapshot was otherwise only re-read on window focus — so the ask that discovered the dead key would finish, failover would answer it correctly, and the notice would stay invisible until the user happened to alt-tab away and back. `providerReady` is deliberately left alone: folding health into it is the change the verifier flagged as riskier, because ~10 renderer gates currently succeed via failover and would start failing closed. CLI providers get the remedy that actually exists for them ("Reconnect it"), not "update your key" — the wrong-remedy-text problem this entry's verifier called out under REFUTATION 3.

### MQA-060 — The Settings "Test" button can never test the key that is actually stored — the exact remedy the error hint points at is a dead end

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:862` · workflow: diagnose / fix a key that stopped working from Settings → AI · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/lib/dust-live-check.ts:4-5 states the app's own principle for saved credentials: "Persisted state can lie: the user may have run `dust logout`, cleared the keychain, or the CLI session may be gone — so opening Settings must verify the real session instead of taking \"already connected\" for granted." And src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:37 sends the user there for exactly this: "Your API key may be invalid or expired. Update it in Settings → AI."

**Actual.** src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:859-865 — `const onTest = async (): Promise<void> => { const trimmed = key.trim(); ... if (!trimmed) { setTest({ status: 'error', message: 'Paste a key above to test it.' }); return }`. The `key` state is the input box, which is cleared on mount/provider change (Settings.tsx:774) and after every save (Settings.tsx:837); the stored key is never rendered (placeholder is `'•••••• saved (paste to replace)'`, Settings.tsx:943). The main-process handler has the same floor: src/main/store.ts:713 `if (!trimmed) return { ok: false, error: 'No API key provided.' }`, and the preload signature requires a key (src/preload/index.ts:78-79). The Test button itself is rendered enabled whenever a key is saved (Settings.tsx:957-965, disabled only while loading or when an env key is active). Unlike Dust, which gets a live session probe on Settings open, no API-key provider is ever re-probed.

**Repro.** Save a valid Anthropic key, use the app, then revoke the key at the provider. Ask a question → red error + hint "Your API key may be invalid or expired. Update it in Settings → AI." Open Settings → AI → the key field shows '•••••• saved (paste to replace)' → click **Test** → red "Paste a key above to test it." Anthropic/OpenAI display a key exactly once at creation, so the user cannot re-paste the stored secret; there is no in-app way to answer "is my saved key still valid, or is the provider down?" The only path forward is minting a brand-new key on faith.

**Suggested fix.** Allow testApiKey to validate the STORED key: accept an empty/omitted key in the IPC payload and have store.ts's testApiKey fall back to `getApiKey(provider)` (still rejecting when neither exists). In Settings, when `settings.hasKeys[provider]` is true and the input is empty, label the button "Test saved key" and call it with no key; keep the paste path for replacing.

**Verifier.** I could not refute the mechanism; I could partly refute the framing, so I am downgrading high -> medium.

WHAT REPRODUCES (all independently verified):
1. The renderer never holds the stored key. `const [key, setKey] = useState('')` (Settings.tsx:725), wiped on provider change (Settings.tsx:774) and after every save (Settings.tsx:837). The placeholder is literally `'•••••• saved (paste to replace)'` (Settings.tsx:943). I grepped the preload for `getApiKey|revealKey|apiKeyGet` — zero matches, so there is no IPC that can hydrate the field from the stored secret (correct security posture, but it means the field is always empty on open).
2. `onTest` hard-floors on the empty input: Settings.tsx:860-865 `const trimmed = key.trim(); if (!trimmed) { setTest({status:'error', message:'Paste a key above to test it.'}); return }`.
3. The main process has the same floor with no stored-key fallback: store.ts:712-713 `const trimmed = key.trim(); if (!trimmed) return { ok:false, error:'No API key provided.' }`. The handler passes the renderer's key straight through — index.ts:2138-2139 `const parsed = TestApiKeyPayloadSchema.parse(payload); return testApiKey(parsed.provider, parsed.key)`. Preload signature requires the key (preload/index.ts:78-79).
4. The button is enabled in exactly the state where it can only fail: Settings.tsx:957-965 `disabled={test.status === 'loading' || envKeyActive}` — nothing checks `key` or `settings.hasKeys[provider]`.
5. The asymmetry with Dust is real: Settings.tsx:2668-2672 probes `window.toto.dustProbeSession()` on mount and feeds `decideDustLiveCheck`. `testApiKey` is called from exactly ONE place in the whole main process — the IPC handler at index.ts:2139. (docs/asktoto-architecture.md:473 claims a startup `testApiKey()` ping is "already wired in index.ts" — that is stale; it is not.)
6. Both cited "intended" quotes are verbatim and accurate (dust-live-check.ts:4-5; Answer.tsx:37).

REFUTATIONS I TRIED AND WHAT SURVIVED:
- Provider-health mitigation: `unhealthyProviders()` exists (llm/provider-health.ts:128), is put on the settings snapshot (index.ts:907) and schema'd (shared/ipc.ts:1014) precisely as the "your key stopped working" surface, and `provider-health-ux.contract.test.ts:37` pins it. But a case-insensitive grep for /unhealthy/ across `src/renderer` returns ZERO matches — the renderer never consumes it. So this does NOT rescue the case.
- Existing tests: Settings.contract.test.ts and dust-live-check.test.ts both pass (16/16 via ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run) and neither covers the Test button's empty-input path. No guard exists.

WHERE THE FINDER OVERSTATES (why medium, not high):
- The title says the remedy the hint points at is a dead end. It isn't. The hint says "Update it in Settings → AI", and updating works and self-verifies: onSave auto-runs testKey and reports "Key is valid and working." (Settings.tsx:823-830). Only the *Test* affordance dead-ends.
- "no in-app way to answer 'is my saved key still valid, or is the provider down?'" is too strong: Answer.tsx:295-299 renders the RAW provider error next to the hint, so a `401 invalid x-api-key` is distinguishable from a network/5xx failure at ask time. What genuinely does not exist is any Settings-side verification of the stored credential.
So the true defect is: a control that presents itself as "verify my key" is enabled in a state where it can only produce a confusing error, and the capability to verify a stored key (store.ts testApiKey) is unreachable for the stored key. That is a real degrade-UX dead-end costing an unnecessary key rotation — not data loss, not security, and not a blocked recovery path. Medium.

FIX: small. Either disable Test when `!key.trim() && settings.hasKeys[provider]` with a "paste a key to test" title, or make the key optional end-to-end (TestApiKeyPayloadSchema -> preload sig -> store.testApiKey falling back to `getApiKey(provider)`) so Test probes the stored credential. Four small edits, no architectural change.

### MQA-061 — A network outage on the default provider shows a bare, unclassified "Connection error." — no retry, no friendly rewrite, and errorHint() matches nothing

**Where.** `src/main/llm/retry.ts:42` · workflow: ask a question while offline / on a broken network · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/llm/retry.ts:6-7 — "\"Transient\" = a connection/transport failure or a server-side hiccup that a retry can plausibly clear (dropped socket, DNS blip, connect timeout, 5xx, 429)." And docs/asktoto-architecture.md:226 (B.9) — "| **Network offline** | Answer error block | \"Looks like a network problem. Check your connection, then retry.\" | Retry button |". src/main/index.ts:2973 even names the exact string this failure produces: "while a silent-drop network surfaces the \"Connection error.\" in seconds."

**Actual.** Both SDKs the app uses throw APIConnectionError whose message defaults to the literal 'Connection error.' (node_modules/openai/core/error.js:78-80 and node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/core/error.js:76-78; the throw sites at openai/client.js:435-438 and @anthropic-ai/sdk/client.js:562 pass no message for ordinary transport failures). src/main/llm/shared.ts:59 `errMsg = (e) => (e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e))` drops the undici `cause` (ENOTFOUND/ECONNREFUSED), so main only ever sees the string. src/main/llm/retry.ts:41-42's TRANSIENT_PATTERN has no `connection error` alternative — I verified `isTransient('Connection error.') === false`. Consequences: (a) the same-provider retry at index.ts:3047 never runs; (b) the friendly rewrite at index.ts:3058-3059 ("Connection issue — couldn't reach the provider after retrying…") is skipped and the raw string is sent (index.ts:3063-3064); (c) errorHint (src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:34-43) matches nothing — its network branch is `/network|fetch failed|enotfound|econnrefused|getaddrinfo|offline|dns/`, none of which appear in "Connection error." — verified, returns null.

**Repro.** Provider = Anthropic (the shipped default) or any OpenAI-compatible provider. Disconnect WiFi. Ask anything. The app tries every other keyed provider in turn (each also failing), then renders a red box containing exactly "Connection error." and nothing else — no cause, no hint, no "check your connection". The one failure the user can actually fix themselves is the one the app describes least, and it is indistinguishable at a glance from a broken key.

**Suggested fix.** Two fixes, both one-liners: add `|connection error` to TRANSIENT_PATTERN in src/main/llm/retry.ts:41-42 (so the retry and the friendly rewrite both engage), and add `connection error` to the network branch of errorHint in src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:39. Better still, have shared.ts's errMsg append `e.cause?.code` (ENOTFOUND/ECONNREFUSED) so the classification has the signal the SDK already captured.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; every link independently reproduced. Chain: default provider is 'anthropic' (src/shared/ipc.ts:1074) → src/main/llm.ts:23-24 routes to streamAnthropic → on an offline DNS failure the SDK's isTimeout check (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/client.js:517-518) is false, so client.js:562 throws `new Errors.APIConnectionError({ cause: response })` with NO message, and core/error.js:76-78 defaults it to the literal 'Connection error.' → MessageStream.js:46-47 emits it as-is because APIConnectionError instanceof AnthropicError → src/main/llm/anthropic.ts:30 calls onError(errMsg(e)), and src/main/llm/shared.ts:59 errMsg returns only e.message, discarding the .cause that carries ENOTFOUND. I executed the actual TRANSIENT_PATTERN from src/main/llm/retry.ts:41-42 against 'connection error.' — false (no alternative matches; 'network error' != 'connection error', 'internal server error' is a literal). So at src/main/index.ts:3099 the same-provider retry never fires, and at index.ts:3110 the friendly rewrite is skipped: isTransient is false and provider-health.ts:60-74 isAuthFailure('Connection error.') is also false (no 401/403/402, no 'unauthor'), so the raw string is sent. src/renderer/src/state.ts:349 passes it through verbatim, and I ran Answer.tsx:39's network regex against it — false, so no hint renders. Refutations attempted and failed: no preflight offline gate anywhere on the ask path (grep for onLine/offline/isOnline across src/main + src/renderer/src); nothing in src/ rewrites the string (grep "Connection error" hits only the index.ts:3004 comment); the OpenAI 6.45.0 half is identical because client.js:781-785 getConnectionErrorMessage returns undefined for every non-undici-dispatcher failure; the existing src/main/llm/retry.test.ts (9 tests, all pass under ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run) deliberately covers real SDK message strings but has no 'Connection error.' case, so no test guards it. The intended-behavior quotes are accurate verbatim (docs/asktoto-architecture.md:226; retry.ts:6-7). Two finder inaccuracies that do not sink it: a manual Retry button IS rendered (src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:233 wired from App.tsx:2430), so B.9's "Retry button" affordance survives and only the AUTOMATIC retry is missing; and the index.ts:2973 cite is actually index.ts:3004. Severity corrected high -> medium: the missed isTransient match is a genuine functional gap in the module's own stated contract ("dropped socket, DNS blip, connect timeout"), and the specified B.9 copy never appears, but the flow degrades rather than breaking — the message literally reads "Connection error.", a Retry button is present, and there is no data loss or security impact. Fix is trivial: add a `connection error` alternative to TRANSIENT_PATTERN (and `connection` to errorHint's network branch), or preserve the SDK `cause` in errMsg so ENOTFOUND survives to the classifier.

### MQA-062 — A `claude logout` / `codex logout` is never detected — cliConnected stays true forever, so Métis keeps reporting the CLI provider as ready

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:2236` · workflow: ask a question with Claude Code / Codex CLI as the provider after the CLI session ends · fix size: medium

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/lib/dust-live-check.ts:3-5 states the rule for exactly this class of credential: "Persisted state can lie: the user may have run `dust logout`, cleared the keychain, or the CLI session may be gone — so opening Settings must verify the real session instead of taking \"already connected\" for granted." Dust implements that probe; the two CLI providers do not.

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:2236-2239 is the ONLY writer that sets the flag true: `if (r.ok) { const s = getSettings(); setSettings({ cliConnected: { ...s.cliConnected, [p]: true } }) }`. Nothing ever sets it back to false on a failed ask — the only false-writer in the codebase is the user's own Disconnect button (src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:1672-1674). Readiness reads the stale flag directly: src/main/index.ts:847 `? !!s.cliConnected[s.provider]` inside the providerReady derivation, and src/main/index.ts:2903 exempts the provider from the ineligible chain whenever the flag is set. The Settings card's state is `const isConnected = !!cliConnected[id]` (Settings.tsx:1698) with no re-probe on open, and startup only warms the binary path — src/main/cli.ts:1164-1168 `prewarmCli()` just calls `resolveBin('claude')`/`resolveBin('codex')`, no auth check.

**Repro.** Connect Claude Code in Settings (cliConnected['claude-cli'] = true, provider becomes claude-cli). In a terminal run `claude logout` (or let the CLI's OAuth expire, or uninstall the CLI). Reopen Métis: the card still reads Connected/Active, providerReady is true, so the "Connect Claude Code in Settings" CTA (App.tsx:2771-2793) never renders and requireProvider() (App.tsx:762-784) lets every ask through. Each ask spawns `claude -p`, fails on auth, and either silently falls over to another keyed provider (see finding 1) or dumps the raw CLI stderr at the user. Nothing in the app ever says "your Claude Code session ended — sign in again".

**Suggested fix.** Mirror the Dust live-probe: run `testCli(p)` for any provider with `cliConnected[p] === true` when the Settings AI tab opens (and once on startup), and clear the flag on failure so the existing Connect card and Bar CTA take over. Additionally, on a pre-token CLI failure whose stderr matches the not-logged-in shape, write `cliConnected[p] = false` before failing over.

**Verifier.** I tried four independent refutation routes and all failed. (Line numbers in the finding are ~8 lines stale vs the working tree; the code is identical.)

REFUTATION 1 — "some other writer resets the flag." Dead. A full sweep of main/shared (`grep -rn cliConnected src/main src/shared`) yields exactly one true-writer: `src/main/index.ts:2260-2263` (the `IPC.cliTest` handler, `if (r.ok) { setSettings({ cliConnected: {...s.cliConnected, [p]: true} }) }`). Every other main-process reference is a *read* (678, 855, 898, 2830, 2880, 2934, 3136, 3973, brain/ingest.ts:104). The only false-writer in the repo is `src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:1673` (`disconnectCli`), user-initiated. No migration, no schema default, no store.ts hook (`store.ts` only mentions CLI at 714 to reject API-key tests for CLI providers).

REFUTATION 2 — "something re-probes on startup or on Settings open." Dead. Startup: `src/main/index.ts:3973` calls `prewarmCli()`, which is `src/main/cli.ts:1164-1168` — `Promise.all([resolveBin('claude'), resolveBin('codex')])`, a PATH lookup only; `detectCli` (cli.ts:599) is documented "Does NOT test authentication". Settings open: `Settings.tsx` calls `window.toto.cliTest` only from `runInstall` (1625) and `connect` (1652), both click-driven. The only mount-time live probe in that file is the Dust one (`liveCheckedRef`, 2667-2701), gated on `settings.dustTokenMintedAt`. So the CLI cards render off the persisted flag alone: `const isConnected = !!cliConnected[id]` (1698), which only flips the button label to "Reconnect" and reveals Disconnect (1798-1811); the "Active" pill (1725) keys off `provider === id`.

REFUTATION 3 — "provider-health already handles it (MQA-004)." This was the strongest candidate and it still dies. `src/main/llm/provider-health.ts` exists precisely for "providerReady is derived from 'a key string exists', never from whether that key works" — but (a) it never touches `cliConnected`; (b) its output field `unhealthyProviders` is produced at `index.ts:907` and typed at `src/shared/ipc.ts:1014`, yet `grep -rin unhealthy src/renderer` returns ZERO matches — the renderer never renders it, so it produces no user-visible signal; (c) its message mapping (`index.ts:3118-3119`) is API-key-shaped: a logged-out `claude` whose stderr matches `isAuthFailure` (e.g. "Invalid API key · Please run /login" hits `/invalid[_\s-]*api[_\s-]*key/`) is told "Claude Code rejected your API key … Open Settings → AI to re-enter it" — actively wrong for a CLI provider that has no key; and (d) that message is only reached when `failover(...)` at index.ts:3107 finds nothing, so with any second keyed provider the ask silently reroutes. Non-auth stderr falls through raw at `cli.ts:569` (`fail(stderr.slice(-500) || ...)`). I ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/provider-health-ux.contract.test.ts src/main/llm/provider-health.test.ts` — 33/33 pass, confirming the machinery is intentionally scoped to API keys (`'${def.label} rejected your API key'`, `resetProviderHealth` on `setApiKey`/`clearApiKey`), never to CLI sessions.

REFUTATION 4 — "the intended-behavior quote is misrepresented." Dead. `src/renderer/src/lib/dust-live-check.ts:3-5` reads verbatim: "Persisted state can lie: the user may have run `dust logout`, cleared the keychain, or the CLI session may be gone — so opening Settings must verify the real session instead of taking \"already connected\" for granted." Settings.tsx:2652-2701 implements that probe for Dust and nothing else. It is Dust-scoped prose, but it states the rule for the identical credential class, and the repo has no equivalent for claude-cli/codex-cli.

CAUSAL CHAIN CONFIRMED: `cliConnected[p]=true` (index.ts:2262, write-once) → `providerReady` (index.ts:855) → App.tsx:772 `requireProvider` returns true and App.tsx:2771 (`!settings.providerReady`) never renders the "Connect Claude Code in Settings" CTA → index.ts:2934 exempts the provider from the ineligible chain → every ask spawns a dead CLI. Also reachable with no auth involved at all: uninstall the CLI and `resolveBin` returns null (cli.ts:446-449) while Settings still shows Reconnect/Active.

SEVERITY CORRECTED high → medium. It is a real, unhandled degrade path with an in-repo precedent, but: the state is fully recoverable with one "Reconnect" click; when no failover target exists the ask does fail loudly (wrong remedy text, not silence); and there is no data loss or security exposure. The worst variant — silent cross-provider reroute — is the finder's separate finding 1, not this one.

FIX COMPLEXITY medium, not small: `testCli` spawns a real `claude -p` with a 45 s timeout (cli.ts:633-704), so a naive mount-effect probe mirroring the Dust one would spawn a child process on every Settings open. A correct fix needs a cheap/throttled probe plus a main-side path that clears `cliConnected[p]` (today nothing outside the renderer can), touching index.ts, cli.ts and Settings.tsx.

**FIXED (retire-on-rejection 2026-08-08, live probe 2026-08-17).** Two halves. The ask path retires the flag at the same pre-token seam that records the auth verdict (`retireCli`, gated on `!exhaustion` so a spent Claude Pro / Codex window — a temporary lockout, not a dead login — does not disconnect anything), and the CLI remedy copy no longer sends a CLI user to re-enter an API key they never had. That still only fires AFTER the user has asked something and watched it fail, so the second half finds out first: `verifyCliSessions()` runs once at launch beside the existing CLI prewarm, and the CLI Integration card calls it on mount through `cli:verify-sessions` — the same "opening Settings must verify the real session" rule dust-live-check.ts states for this credential class.

The verifier's objection to the ledger's own suggested fix is respected in full: this does NOT use `testCli`, which spawns a real one-turn completion with a 45s timeout and bills the user's own subscription.
