Both CLIs ship a documented, zero-token status command that reads their stored credential and prints — `claude auth status` (JSON carrying `loggedIn`) and `codex login status` — and both were exercised against the installed CLIs on this machine before the code was written, which is how the initial `--output-format json` guess was caught and dropped: `claude auth status` takes no such flag, it is already JSON.

`checkCliSession` returns `'live' | 'signed-out' | 'unknown'` and only an explicit negative retires anything. That is the load-bearing decision: a false "signed out" disconnects a working provider and sends the user to reconnect for nothing, so an unrecognised output shape, a CLI version without the subcommand, a timeout, or a claude invocation that fails to run all answer `'unknown'` and change nothing. The probe also runs under `cliEnv`, so an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment cannot make a logged-OUT CLI report itself authenticated. The sweep is single-flighted and throttled per provider (60s), re-reads the flag after its await so a user Disconnect during the probe is not undone, and its IPC handler carries the same main-window + `requireAuth()` gate every settings-writing handler carries (MQA-129).

### MQA-063 — FFmpeg spawn failure during the duration probe escapes as an uncaught main-process exception (fatal crash dialog) instead of a failed import

**Where.** `src/main/ffmpeg-decoder.ts:126` · workflow: import an audio/video recording (every import, ffmpeg path) · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/ffmpeg-decoder.ts:102-111 wraps the decode spawn so a spawn failure becomes a HANDLED import failure: `} catch (error) { const completed = callbacks.onError(error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error))); return { cancel: () => {}, completed } }`. The same file, lines 129-133, shows the authors explicitly reasoning about early error events: "'error' can fire before 'close', rejecting this promise while nothing awaits it yet (the stdout for-await loop below runs first). Observe it immediately so that isn't an unhandled rejection". And src/main/index.ts:455-458: "A synchronous throw in an ipcMain.on handler isn't caught by Electron like an ipcMain.handle throw is — it escalates to a main-process uncaughtException, which brings up the app's fatal crash dialog."

**Actual.** The decode child is spawned at src/main/ffmpeg-decoder.ts:103-107, but its `child.once('error', ...)` listener is only attached at src/main/ffmpeg-decoder.ts:126 — AFTER `await probeDurationSeconds(executable, sourcePath)` at line 114, which itself spawns a second child and waits for its `close` (20 ms-5 s). Node emits an async spawn error (ENOENT/EACCES) on nextTick, i.e. inside that window, with zero listeners on the ChildProcess. EventEmitter re-throws unhandled 'error' events, so it reaches `process.on('uncaughtException', ...)` at src/main/index.ts:3965 -> onFatal (index.ts:1194-1216): a crash-*.log, an `app.crash` audit entry, and the modal "Métis hit a problem" dialog. The try/catch at ffmpeg-decoder.ts:102-111 only catches the SYNCHRONOUS spawn error class (verified: a non-PE file throws EFTYPE synchronously and is caught; a missing path does not).

**Repro.** `bundledFfmpegPath` (ffmpeg-decoder.ts:83-88) only does `existsSync`, and `bundledImportFfmpeg()` (index.ts:505-508) is re-evaluated on EVERY import start, so any state where resources/ffmpeg/win32-x64/ffmpeg.exe passes existsSync but is not spawnable at spawn time triggers it (AV/EDR quarantining the unsigned ffmpeg.exe mid-session, an auto-update replacing it, WDAC/AppLocker execution denial). Verified empirically on this machine with Node: spawning a non-existent path with the exact ffmpeg-decoder.ts ordering (spawn -> await a probe that spawns+closes its own child -> attach 'error') prints `>>> UNCAUGHT: ENOENT | spawn ... ENOENT` before the late listener is attached. Inputs: click Import audio, pick any file -> expected "Import failed: spawn ENOENT" card; actual: main-process uncaughtException, crash dump written, fatal error dialog.

**Suggested fix.** Attach `child.once('error', (e) => { spawnError = e })` (and the stderr reader) synchronously, immediately after the spawn on line 107 and before the `completed` IIFE awaits the probe — or run probeDurationSeconds first and spawn the decode child only after it resolves.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED. src/main/ffmpeg-decoder.ts:103-107 spawns the decode child, then the async IIFE at :113 suspends at `await probeDurationSeconds(...)` (:114) before `child.once('error', ...)` is attached at :126 — the child has zero listeners across that window. Node emits ENOENT/EACCES/EAGAIN/EMFILE/ENFILE spawn failures async on process.nextTick (only other errnos throw synchronously), so the try/catch at :102-111 cannot catch this class. The probe's own child IS protected (`child.once('error')` at :62 runs synchronously inside the `new Promise` executor), which is precisely why the probe resolves after the decode child has already thrown. Reproduced empirically on Node v24 with the exact ordering: prints ">>> UNCAUGHT: ENOENT | spawn ... ENOENT" before "probe error observed"; also reproduced with a path that passes existsSync but is unspawnable (a directory), so bundledFfmpegPath's existsSync-only check (:83-88, re-evaluated per import at index.ts:555) is not a guard. The throw reaches process.on('uncaughtException') at src/main/index.ts:4011 -> onFatal (index.ts:1205-1227): crash-*.log, `app.crash` audit entry, modal "Métis hit a problem" dialog. Aggravating factor the finder missed: `completed` never settles (verified over 9s — neither onError nor completion fires), so ffmpegDecoders keeps the entry, the job stays in `decoding`, the stale reaper at index.ts:561-568 only reaps failed/cancelled/done/undefined and won't free it, and closeImportDecoder's `await ffmpeg.completed` (index.ts:509) hangs — import is permanently wedged with "Another audio decoder is already active." until restart. It is a regression: `git show 34ad395^:src/main/ffmpeg-decoder.ts` shows `child.once('error')` used to be the IIFE's first statement with no preceding await, capturing the async spawn error into spawnError and surfacing it via onError; commit 34ad395 inserted the duration probe as the new first await. Refutation attempts that failed: no runtime preflight/spawn-check of the sidecar exists (ffmpeg appears in index.ts only at 193/372/506-593); no test covers spawn failure — ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/ffmpeg-decoder.test.ts passes 2/2 happy-path tests only. Corrections: the index.ts line cites are stale (uncaughtException is 4011 not 3965; the ipcMain.on comment is 470-473 not 455-458; bundledImportFfmpeg is 520-523 not 505-508) though the quoted text is verbatim correct; ffmpeg-decoder.ts cites are exact. Severity lowered high->medium: the finder's "every import" is wrong — it needs an environment where the binary passes existsSync but is not spawnable (AppLocker/WDAC execute-deny, missing +x on macOS/Linux per docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:44-50 "copy one from a teammate's" guidance, directory/dangling symlink); the existsSync->spawn race is sub-millisecond and not a realistic trigger. Low likelihood, severe impact when hit. Fix is trivial: hoist `child.once('error', ...)` (and ideally the stderr listener plus `once(child,'close')` + its `.catch(() => {})`) above the `await probeDurationSeconds(...)` at ffmpeg-decoder.ts:114.

### MQA-064 — Saving the CRM connection wedges the Settings card in "saving" forever when the key write throws — the user-facing error is written but never shown

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:2272` · workflow: connect Polo Pre-Sales (Settings → Mantu Intelligence → Set up → Save) · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/mcp/bidstackSecrets.ts:53-59 throws a message written verbatim for the user: "Couldn't save the Polo Pre-Sales API key — Métis can't write to its data folder(...)", and :44-48 throws "Encryption is unavailable on this machine. Métis cannot safely store the Polo Pre-Sales API key." bidstackClient.ts:15-16 states the module contract as "every network call is wrapped so a failure returns { ok: false, error } — never throws into an unhandled rejection", and every other failure in this flow is surfaced through the `{ok:false,error}` channel the Settings card renders at Settings.tsx:2092-2097.

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:2272 calls `setBidstackApiKey(parsed.data.apiKey)` with no try/catch inside the `ipcMain.handle(IPC.mcpCrmSaveConnection, ...)` body (2265-2280), so the throw propagates out of the handler and rejects the renderer's `invoke`. src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:1983-1998 `saveConnection` has no try/catch and is fired as `void saveConnection()` at :2122, so the rejection is unhandled (there is no window unhandledrejection handler in src/renderer — the ErrorBoundary in main.tsx:50 only catches render errors) and `testState.phase` stays `'saving'`.

**Repro.** Windows packaged build whose userData already holds a `secret-key.bin` this account's DPAPI cannot unwrap (profile restored from another Windows account / reimaged machine). setBidstackApiKey -> prepareFileKeyForWrite (bidstackSecrets.ts:39) -> secrets.ts:260-262 -> getOrCreateKey(true) -> secrets.ts:183-186 throws KeychainKeyRecoveryError. Same wedge with a read-only or full userData folder (bidstackSecrets.ts:52 writeFileSync -> EACCES/ENOSPC). Sequence: enter endpoint + key, click "Test connection" (succeeds, phase='tested'), click "Save" -> spinner spins forever, no error text ever appears; "Test connection" is disabled (Settings.tsx:2114 `testState.phase === 'saving'`) and "Save" is disabled (:2123 `testState.phase !== 'tested'`), so only Cancel works and the connection is never established.

**Suggested fix.** Wrap the persistence step in the handler: `try { setBidstackApiKey(...) } catch (e) { return { ok: false, error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Could not store the Polo Pre-Sales API key.' } }`, and add a `.catch()` in Settings.tsx's saveConnection/testConnection that sets `{phase:'error', error: ...}` so a rejected invoke can never leave the card in a non-terminal phase.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED — I could not refute the causal chain.

CALL SITE VERIFIED. `git show HEAD:src/main/index.ts` line 2272 is exactly `setBidstackApiKey(parsed.data.apiKey)` (the working tree has drifted +32 lines to 2304, explaining an initial mismatch). It sits inside `ipcMain.handle(IPC.mcpCrmSaveConnection, async (e, payload) => {...})` with no try/catch in the handler body. `connectBidstack` has already returned ok:true by that point, so nothing short-circuits it.

THROWS VERIFIED, all three quotes verbatim. bidstackSecrets.ts:39 -> prepareFileKeyForWrite -> secrets.ts:260-262 -> getOrCreateKey(true), which throws KeychainKeyRecoveryError at secrets.ts:183, :186, :202, :207 and :215. bidstackSecrets.ts:44-48 throws "Encryption is unavailable on this machine. Métis cannot safely store the Polo Pre-Sales API key." bidstackSecrets.ts:51-59 wraps writeFileSync and re-throws "Couldn't save the Polo Pre-Sales API key — Métis can't write to its data folder(...)" on EACCES/ENOSPC — a broader trigger than the DPAPI case and not Windows-specific.

REFUTATIONS ATTEMPTED AND FAILED:
1. No wrapper on ipcMain.handle anywhere in src/ (grep for reassignment/wrapHandler/safeHandle found only unrelated `wrapHandlers` in llm/local.ts:148).
2. Preload src/preload/index.ts:303-304 is a bare `ipcRenderer.invoke`, no catch, no generic api wrapper.

6. src/main/mcp/bidstackSecrets.test.ts — ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run`, 7/7 pass, but covers only happy paths. No test exercises any throw. windows-keystore-dpapi.test.ts has zero bidstack references.

DECISIVE CONFIRMATION OF INTENT — the codebase's own precedent. src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:807-817, the analogous provider-key save, wraps the identical class of throw: `try { await saveKey(provider, trimmed) } catch (e) { // e.g. OS encryption unavailable — store.setApiKey throws; don't fail silently.` then renders it via setTest({status:'error', message}) and even offers recovery via isProfileUnlockError. store.ts:666 and :685 throw the same two message shapes that bidstackSecrets.ts:46/55 mirror. So catch-and-render is not inferred intent — it is already implemented once for this exact failure class, and the BidStack card omits it. saveConnection (Settings.tsx:1983-1998) is bare and fired as `void saveConnection()` at :2122, leaving phase='saving' set at :1984, which disables Test connection (:2114) and Save (:2123).

CORRECTION TO THE FINDER: "forever" overstates it. Cancel at Settings.tsx:2132-2135 resets testState to idle, so the card recovers on cancel/reopen. The substantive damage stands — the deliberately user-authored diagnostic never reaches the user and the connection can never be established, with zero feedback.

SEVERITY high -> medium: requires a degraded precondition (unwritable/full userData, DPAPI-unwrappable secret-key.bin, or safeStorage unavailable); scoped to one optional CRM integration, not core function; no state corruption (setSettings at :2305 never runs, so bidstackConnected is not falsely set); Cancel recovers the UI. It is a real diagnosability dead-end on an anticipated Windows field scenario, not a broad-impact or security defect.

FIX: trivial — wrap the setBidstackApiKey/setSettings block in try/catch returning { ok: false, error: e.message } to match the {ok,error} channel Settings.tsx:2092-2097 already renders (and/or add a try/catch in saveConnection mirroring Settings.tsx:807-817).

### MQA-065 — CONNECT/CALL_TIMEOUT_MS never bound the actual MCP request — a stalled tool call blocks for 60s and is then reported as "failed for an unknown reason"

**Where.** `src/main/mcp/bidstackClient.ts:170` · workflow: test the CRM connection / push a recap to the CRM · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/mcp/bidstackClient.ts:17 — "a hard timeout bounds every call (BidStack may be unreachable, slow, or hung) via AbortController." and :28-30 — "/** Bound every BidStack round-trip so an unreachable/hung server never blocks the main process. */ const CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000; const CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000". classifyError's first branch (:128-130) exists to turn a timeout into "Timed out connecting to Polo Pre-Sales at ${endpointUrl}. Check the endpoint is reachable."

**Actual.** withClient (bidstackClient.ts:169-173) passes `{ signal: controller.signal }` only to `client.connect(transport, ...)`. The SDK applies that signal to the `initialize` request alone (node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/cjs/client/index.js:296-305); `fn(client)` then calls `client.listTools()` / `client.callTool({...})` with no options, so those requests fall back to DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MSEC = 60000 (dist/cjs/shared/protocol.js:12, 716). The resulting SDK error message is "MCP error -32001: Request timed out", which contains neither 'abort' nor any of classifyError's network substrings, so it falls through to the generic return at :149.

**Repro.** I proved the signal gap empirically with a local Streamable-HTTP MCP mock whose tool sleeps 6s: connect at 100ms, `controller.abort()` fired at 1511ms, `callTool` still RESOLVED at 6136ms (abort had no effect). Applied to the product: a Polo Pre-Sales server that completes `initialize` but stalls on `tools/call` keeps the Review "Pushing…" spinner up for 60s (not the advertised 30s), then shows "Polo Pre-Sales connection failed for an unknown reason. Check the endpoint and API key." instead of the timeout message — pointing the user at the key rather than at reachability. Same for "Test connection" stalling on `tools/list`: 60s, not 15s. Separately, the 30s abort fires while the tool call is in flight and makes the SDK send a `notifications/cancelled` for the already-completed initialize request.

**Suggested fix.** Thread the bound into the request itself: pass `{ signal: controller.signal, timeout: timeoutMs }` to `client.listTools(undefined, opts)` and `client.callTool({name, arguments}, undefined, opts)` (i.e. give withClient's `fn` the RequestOptions), and add `'timed out'`/`'timeout'` to classifyError's first branch so an SDK RequestTimeout maps to the timeout message.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; independently reproduced. CHAIN: src/main/mcp/bidstackClient.ts:169-173 passes `{signal: controller.signal}` only to `client.connect(transport, ...)`. In node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/cjs/client/index.js:289-305, `Client.connect` calls `super.connect(transport)` with NO options and forwards `options` solely to the `initialize` request — the transport never receives the signal (its own `_abortController`, streamableHttp.js:96/308/445, is aborted only by transport.close()). `fn(client)` then runs `client.listTools()` (bidstackClient.ts:198) and `client.callTool({...})` (:257) with no options, so shared/protocol.js:716 resolves `options?.timeout ?? DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MSEC` = 60000 (protocol.js:12) and the abort listener at protocol.js:713 is never attached. The resulting error is exactly `MCP error -32001: Request timed out` (types.js:2067-2073 + :197), which contains none of classifyError's substrings (bidstackClient.ts:128-144), so it hits the generic branch at :149.

EMPIRICAL (my own run, local Streamable-HTTP MCP mock with a 6s tool, withClient mirrored with a 1.5s bound): connected at 406ms, controller.abort() at 1696ms, callTool RESOLVED at 6447ms — abort had zero effect. Same script confirmed zero classifyError substring hits on the timeout message.

REFUTATIONS TRIED AND FAILED: (a) no outer bound exists — src/main/index.ts:2288-2350 bare `await`, src/preload/index.ts:301-307 bare `ipcRenderer.invoke`, Review.tsx:419-429 and Settings.tsx:1973-1980 have no client-side timeout; (b) no test covers it — src/main/mcp/bidstackClient.test.ts (13 tests) passes fully under ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run but never exercises a stalled response; (c) client/index.js:127 listTools is inside _setupListChangedHandlers, dead here (no listChanged config at bidstackClient.ts:161); (d) undici's 300s default headers/body timeout is far above 60s, so the SDK timeout is what actually fires.

The intended-behavior quotes at bidstackClient.ts:17 ("a hard timeout bounds every call ... via AbortController") and :28-30 are verbatim and mean what the finder says. The finder correctly scoped it: the CONNECT leg IS bounded (protocol.js:672-689 rejects with String(reason) = "AbortError: This operation was aborted", which does match the 'abort' branch at :128), so a fully-down server still gets the right message. The gap is exactly the server that completes `initialize` then stalls on tools/list or tools/call.

SEVERITY: medium confirmed, not raised. No data loss, no security impact, no main-process freeze (all async). Impact is a 60s spinner instead of the advertised 15s/30s plus an actively misdirecting message ("Check the endpoint and API key") when the real problem is server responsiveness — and a stalled `tools/call` is the realistic case for a CRM write (slow DB, loaded Azure host, buffering proxy), since `initialize` is trivial and fast. The stray `notifications/cancelled` for the already-completed initialize (protocol.js:672-686, listener never removed) is real but cosmetic.

FIX: pass a RequestOptions through withClient's `fn` (e.g. `fn(client, { signal: controller.signal, timeout: timeoutMs })`) into listTools/callTool, plus optionally add 'timed out'/'-32001' to classifyError's timeout branch — ~4 lines across 3 spots in bidstackClient.ts plus a regression test.

### MQA-066 — With requireAuth enforced but SSO unconfigured, SignInWall tells the user to open Settings → Account — a screen the wall itself makes unreachable

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1952` · workflow: first launch on an enterprise-managed machine (managed-config requireAuth:true, or ASKTOTO_REQUIRE_AUTH=1) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/SignInWall.tsx:52-58: "signIn() short-circuited: `ok:true` here means \"nothing to do\" (SSO isn't actually configured), NOT \"you're signed in\" … Treating this as success would silently strand the user behind the wall with a stopped spinner and no feedback or way forward." followed by `setErr("Microsoft sign-in isn't configured. Set it up in Settings → Account, or contact your admin.")` — i.e. the stated remedy is Settings → Account.

**Actual.** That remedy is unreachable while the wall is up. App.tsx:2535-2541 returns <SignInWall/> in place of the entire tree when `(configured || enforced) && !signedIn`; `enforced` is true from authEnforced() alone (auth.ts:595, 600-619) even with no azure config. App.tsx:1950-1952 (`if (a !== 'hide' && (onboardingGate || signInGate)) return`) drops every hotkey action including 'settings', and the tray's "Settings…" item goes through the same path (index.ts:1672-1675 `sendHotkey('settings')`). The Bar's Métis-mark → Settings affordance is not rendered at all. There is no other route to Settings.

**Repro.** Deploy `%ProgramData%\Métis\managed-config.json` containing only `{"requireAuth": true}` (a supported shape — auth.ts:605-617 and asktoto-hardening-backlog P1 both treat it as the org override; the shipped enterprise example sets it). Launch Métis: the SignInWall renders. Click "Sign in with Microsoft" → main returns {ok:true, configured:false} → the wall shows "Microsoft sign-in isn't configured. Set it up in Settings → Account…". Press the Settings hotkey → nothing. Tray → Settings… → nothing. The app is permanently unusable on that machine.

**Suggested fix.** Allow a restricted Settings surface (Account tab only) to open from the SignInWall — either an explicit button on the wall or by letting the 'settings' hotkey through the signInGate at App.tsx:1952 — and reword the not-configured message to name the actual reachable path. Alternatively, when authEnforced() is true but readConfig() is null, fall back to the pre-config Settings screen instead of a wall with no forward action.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED — I reproduced the full causal chain independently and could not refute it.

CHAIN VERIFIED:
1. auth.ts:600-619 authEnforced() returns true from ASKTOTO_REQUIRE_AUTH or managed-config {"requireAuth":true} ALONE, with no azure config required. Its own comment concedes the state: "privileged IPC is blocked until the user signs in, even if SSO is unconfigured." Surfaced at auth.ts:596 as `enforced: authEnforced() || isStickyConfigured()`.
2. auth.ts:651-653: `signIn()` opens `const cfg = readConfig(); if (!cfg) return { ok: true, configured: false }`. With no azure config in env (149-154), managed (155), Settings (157), or LKG (161-166, gated on sticky which is unset on first launch), this branch fires permanently.
3. state.ts:651-655 useAuth().signIn returns `r` verbatim, so configured:false reaches the wall. SignInWall.tsx:52-58 sets exactly the quoted string. The finder's "intended" quote is accurate line-for-line, and the remedy it names is REAL: Settings.tsx:6052-6053 renders the client/tenant ID fields and readConfig honors readSettingsAzure() at auth.ts:157. The fix genuinely works — it is only unreachable.
4. App.tsx:2536 returns <SignInWall/> as the entire tree on (configured || enforced) && !signedIn. Unlike the onboarding gate 15 lines below (2551: `if (view === 'settings')`, added precisely because a fix-link dead-ended), this branch has NO view==='settings' escape.
5. App.tsx:1952 drops every action including 'settings' (the handler's own `else if (a === 'settings') guardReviewNav(openSettingsDefault)` at 1975 is downstream of the gate). All routes funnel through it: window.toto.onHotkey (1985), Desk Tap (comment at 1987 states it reuses the same router), and the tray's "Settings…" -> sendHotkey('settings') (index.ts:1683-1685). Tray menu (index.ts:1681-1694) has no sign-out/reset item. Only renderer keydown listener is Escape->hide (App.tsx:2065-2072). openSettings (App.tsx:749-754) and the Bar affordance (2265) both live below the early return.

REFUTATIONS ATTEMPTED AND FAILED: managed-config CAN supply azure (readManagedAzure, auth.ts:64-79) but the trigger is precisely its absence; the LKG recovery fallback exists but is gated on isStickyConfigured(), unset before any successful sign-in; auth.test.ts passes (4 tests) but no test touches SignInWall, signInGate, or `enforced` (grepped *.test.ts* across src).

WHERE THE FINDER OVERREACHED: build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json:18-21 sets requireAuth:true TOGETHER with the three azure fields, so a by-the-book enterprise deploy does not hit this. Its placeholders ("REPLACE-WITH-AZURE-APP-CLIENT-ID") also pass isSafeConfigValue (auth.ts:105-110, /^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$/), yielding configured:true and a different failure mode. The state requires admin error — omitted, partial, or metachar-bearing azure fields alongside requireAuth:true (or ASKTOTO_REQUIRE_AUTH=1 without AZURE_* vars). Also "permanently unusable" overstates it: the same sentence offers a valid second remedy ("contact your admin") and a one-line managed-config change restores the machine.

SEVERITY corrected high -> medium: a real dangling-remedy dead-end that the code explicitly anticipates in two places, but reachable only via misconfiguration, fully recoverable out-of-app, with a working escalation path already named in the message. No data loss, no security hole.

FIX small: mirror the onboarding gate's existing pattern at App.tsx:2551 — allow `view === 'settings'` to render inside the SignInWall branch and pass an onOpenSettings affordance to SignInWall (or let action 'settings' through the App.tsx:1952 gate, since opening Settings has no capture/LLM/recording side effect, unlike the actions that gate was written to block).

**FIXED (2026-08-17).** Both halves, because the renderer half alone would have been a lie — that is what the note in app-audit-fixes.contract.test.ts said when this was deferred, and it was correct: letting `view === 'settings'` render over the wall opens a panel that cannot complete the remedy, since `settingsSet` starts with `if (!requireAuth()) return publicSettings()` and requireAuth() is false in exactly the state that raises the wall. The IDs would be typed and silently not persist.

**Main.** `auth.ts` exports `ssoBootstrapAllowed()`, and `settingsSet` uses it as the ONE exception to its blanket unauthenticated refusal. Two conditions, both load-bearing: no live session with enforcement actually on (otherwise the normal authed path applies, or the wall is self-serve and already has MQA-107's reset hatch), and never once sticky-configured — a device where a genuine sign-in has succeeded must never let an unauthenticated renderer repoint SSO at another tenant, which is the attack `isStickyConfigured` exists to stop.

**It is deliberately NOT also gated on `readConfig() === null`,** and that correction came from re-reviewing the fix rather than from the finding. Closing the bootstrap the moment any config resolved only moved the brick one step later: the user types the tenant GUID, fat-fingers one digit, and now a config resolves — so the carve-out shuts, every sign-in fails the tenant compare forever, and MQA-107's reset hatch is unavailable because it correctly refuses an `authEnforced()` fleet. Bricked again, further along. The fields stay writable until a sign-in actually succeeds, which is what makes the remedy the wall names a real one. Widening it is still safe and the tests pin all three reasons: writing these fields cannot lift enforcement (`authEnforced()` reads env and managed-config only, never these), cannot override an org deployment (`readConfig` resolves env -> managed -> settings, so on a managed fleet the write is inert), and cannot touch a device that has ever signed in. The patch is then narrowed key-by-key to `azureClientId` / `azureTenantId` / `azureAllowedDomain` (copied from a whitelist, never spread), and audited as `reason: 'sso_bootstrap'`. env and machine-wide managed-config still outrank settings inside `readConfig()`, so this cannot loosen an org deployment — it can only fill a vacuum.

**Renderer.** The wall branch gains the same `view === 'settings'` escape the onboarding gate 15 lines below already has (added there for the identical dead-link reason), the hotkey/tray router lets `'settings'` — and only `'settings'` — through the sign-in gate (it is the one action with no capture/LLM/recording side effect, the class that gate exists to block), and SignInWall takes an `onOpenSettings` affordance shown once sign-in has actually reported not-configured.

One correction to the finding while implementing it: the remedy it quotes — "Set it up in Settings → Account" — named a screen that does not exist. There is no Account tab; the Entra client/tenant/domain fields live on the **Calendar** tab (`CalendarTab`, alongside the Outlook connection). The copy now says Settings → Calendar and the button opens exactly that tab with a notice explaining why the user is there.

### MQA-067 — One-click "Mantu Dust" setup connects, but onboarding's readiness row never notices and mislabels it as a missing API key

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/Onboarding.tsx:577` · workflow: first-run onboarding — choosing "Mantu Dust · One-click setup" as the provider · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/Onboarding.tsx:570-575: "'Mantu Dust' isn't just a preference — kick off the one-click setup right here so onboarding ends CONNECTED, not just with Dust selected. Import an existing Dust CLI session, or auto-run the installer + `dust login` if there's none; the main-process poll then connects on its own and the readiness step reflects it."

**Actual.** The readiness step cannot reflect it. chooseDust (Onboarding.tsx:575-579) calls `choose('dust')` — which does `patch({ provider })` and jumps to step 6 — BEFORE `await window.toto.dustImportCli()`, so the settings snapshot the renderer holds predates the credential write. dustImportCli (index.ts:2148-2156) writes the key and dustWorkspaceId in MAIN only; there is no settings push channel (no webContents.send for settings anywhere in index.ts). Step 6's own effect (Onboarding.tsx:343-377) polls only `window.toto.getPermissions()`, never getSettings(). App's useSettings only refetches on the window 'focus' event (state.ts:539-541) — and the overlay never loses focus on this path. So settings.providerReady stays stale. Separately, PROVIDERS.dust.kind is 'dust' (shared/providers.ts:247), not 'cli', so Onboarding.tsx:705-706 renders the label "Dust · your agents API key" with hint "add your key to get live answers" — wrong copy for an OAuth/CLI flow with no key to paste.

**Repro.** Machine that already has a `dust` CLI session in the OS secret store. Onboarding step 5 → click "Mantu Dust". dustImportCli succeeds in main (key + workspaceId persisted). Step 6 nonetheless shows the amber row "Dust · your agents API key — add your key to get live answers" with the "Open Settings → AI" fix link, and never clears while the user sits there. Only after pressing "Get started" (whose patch returns fresh settings) does the app agree Dust is connected — Settings → AI then shows it as Connected all along.

**Suggested fix.** In chooseDust, await dustImportCli()/dustSetupCli() and then force a settings refresh (thread the parent's `refresh` in, or `await patch({})`) before/after `choose('dust')`; and have the step-6 effect at Onboarding.tsx:343-377 re-read settings alongside permissions so a main-process connection lands live. Also special-case provider 'dust' in the label/hint at Onboarding.tsx:705-706 ("Dust workspace connected" / "finish the one-click sign-in") instead of the API-key wording.

**Verifier.** I tried to kill this on six separate fronts and it survived all of them.

VERIFIED CHAIN
1. Ordering is as claimed. `src/renderer/src/components/Onboarding.tsx:575-579` — `chooseDust` calls `choose('dust')` first, and `choose` (Onboarding.tsx:539-542) is `patch({ provider }); setStep(6)` with no await. `await window.toto.dustImportCli()` runs after. The `settings:set` IPC is dispatched synchronously before the import IPC, so the snapshot main returns is computed pre-import regardless of promise resolution order.
2. No settings push channel. `src/main/index.ts:2172-2180` `dustImportCli` does `setApiKey('dust', s.token)` + `setSettings({dustWorkspaceId, dustBaseUrl, dustTokenMintedAt})` in MAIN and returns only `{ok, workspaceId, baseUrl}`. Every `webContents.send` in index.ts is importAudioProgress / hotkey / cliInstallProgress / parakeetProgress / stream* — none carries settings.
3. No renderer refetch. `src/renderer/src/state.ts:500-547`: settings load once at boot (retry loop) and refetch only on the window `focus` event (state.ts:539-542). Step 6's effect (Onboarding.tsx:342-377) polls `getPermissions`/`requestPermissionsUpfront` only. `App.tsx` has no settings poll (the only `refresh()` calls are `recheckLicenseGate` at App.tsx:178, user-triggered, and `onDone` at App.tsx:2569). Onboarding is passed no `refresh` prop (OnboardingExperience.tsx:474-489).
4. Nothing steals focus on this path, so the focus-refetch never fires: `dust status` runs with `windowsHide: true` (src/main/dustcli.ts:112), the session permission handler auto-allows with no dialog (index.ts:4202-4205), and `requestPermissionsUpfront` is a darwin no-op on Windows.
5. The row is genuinely STALE, not honestly-not-ready. index.ts:852-861 requires `hasApiKey('dust') && dustWorkspaceId.trim() && providerModels.dust`. I specifically hunted for a missing third condition — `providerModels.dust` defaults to `DUST_BASE_AGENT_ID` (`src/shared/ipc.ts:1076`, healed again at store.ts:548-551), so after the import all three hold and main would report `providerReady: true`. The renderer just never asks.
6. Copy claim confirmed: `PROVIDERS.dust.kind === 'dust'` (src/shared/providers.ts, dust entry), so Onboarding.tsx:705-706 takes the non-'cli' branch → label "Dust · your agents API key", hint "add your key to get live answers", and CheckRow (Onboarding.tsx:172-198) renders the amber warn box plus the "Open Settings → AI" link.
7. The intended-behavior quote is verbatim at Onboarding.tsx:570-574, including "the readiness step reflects it".
8. Corroborating contrast: `Settings.tsx:2463-2517` `connectCli` awaits `dustImportCli()` and THEN patches — that patch's return value is the fresh snapshot. Onboarding omits exactly that step.

REFUTATIONS I TRIED AND REJECTED
- "Onboarding.tsx is dead code, App renders OnboardingV2": false — OnboardingExperience.tsx:19 imports it and OnboardingV2 renders it at `initialStep: 5` (OnboardingExperience.tsx:474-489), i.e. this is THE provider/readiness screen.
- "Main auto-connects Dust at launch so the snapshot is already ready": the eager refresh (index.ts:4316-4342) is gated on `process.platform === 'darwin' && hasApiKey('dust')` — false on first run.
- "A test covers it": none. No test in the repo references `chooseDust`, `dustImportCli` in a renderer test, or `providerReady` in Onboarding. Ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/components/Onboarding.helpers.test.ts src/main/onboarding-dedup.contract.test.ts` — 7 passed, and neither touches this path.

SCOPE CAVEATS (narrow the blast radius but do not refute)
- Only the import-success path is broken. On the `dustSetupCli` fallback a Terminal opens, the overlay blurs, and the user's return fires `focus` → refresh → the row clears. So the code comment is true for the setup path and false for the "already has a dust CLI session" path — exactly the repro the finder chose.
- Requires the user to be signed in; `dustImportCli` returns early on `!requireAuth()` (index.ts:2174), in which case nothing was written and the amber row is honest.
- Not a functional break: "Get started" persists fine and the app really is connected. The cost is a misleading final onboarding screen on the flagship one-click corporate path, plus copy telling the user to paste a key that doesn't exist in this flow — and the offered remediation prematurely ends onboarding (finish() runs inside onFix at Onboarding.tsx:711).

Severity medium stands: user-visible wrong state on the primary Mantu path, self-healing only on an incidental window focus. Fix is small — await the import, then patch (mirroring Settings.tsx connectCli), with the same `mountedRef`/`stepRef` guard chooseCli already uses at Onboarding.tsx:558, and branch the CheckRow label on `kind === 'dust'` too.

### MQA-068 — licenseGateEnabled is a complete no-op — the shipped enterprise policy turns on licensing that has no gate, no activation UI, and no heartbeat

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:155` · workflow: enterprise rollout with device licensing (managed-config licenseGateEnabled:true) and license activation/revocation · fix size: small

**Intended.** docs/license-platform-plan.md:61-64: "`checkLicenseGrace()` is already wired into a real startup gate in `src/renderer/src/App.tsx` (~lines 1746-1773): when `settings.licenseGateEnabled` is true and the verdict says blocked, the app shows a blocking activation screen instead of the bar". src/main/license.ts:5-8 says the same: "Wired into real enforcement: main/index.ts's license:gate IPC handler calls checkLicenseGrace() for the renderer's boot gate (App.tsx's <LicenseGate/>), and a 12h background interval re-validates via heartbeat() whenever licenseGateEnabled && licenseValid." build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json ships `"licenseGateEnabled": true` and locks the key.

**Actual.** src/renderer/src/App.tsx:155-156 hardcodes `const LICENSE_ENFORCEMENT = false` / `const licenseEnforced = LICENSE_ENFORCEMENT && settings?.licenseGateEnabled === true`, so the <LicenseGate/> branch at App.tsx:2520-2528 can never render and window.toto.licenseGate() is never even called (App.tsx:161-164 early-returns). src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:143 `const LICENSE_UI_ENABLED: boolean = false` hides the whole LicenseSection (used at Settings.tsx:4990), so the Activate form is unreachable too. index.ts:4292 gates the 12h heartbeat on `licenseGateEnabled && licenseValid`, and licenseValid can only become true via activateLicense — which now has no reachable UI. Net effect: gate off, activation impossible, heartbeat never fires.

**Repro.** Deploy build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json as machine-wide managed-config.json (it sets licenseGateEnabled:true and locks it). Launch Métis on an unlicensed machine: no activation screen, no blocking, full app access. Open Settings: there is no License section anywhere to paste a key. Revoke the license in the admin dashboard: nothing happens on the device — no heartbeat runs, so the documented kill-switch ("revoke = blocked at next heartbeat", license-platform-plan.md:74-76) never fires.

**Suggested fix.** Pick one and make the sources agree: either flip LICENSE_ENFORCEMENT (App.tsx:155) and LICENSE_UI_ENABLED (Settings.tsx:143) together and re-verify the gate end to end, or remove `licenseGateEnabled` from build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json and update docs/license-platform-plan.md §Phase 3 + the src/main/license.ts header to state plainly that enforcement is currently compiled out. Add a contract test asserting that the doc's claim and App.tsx's constant cannot drift again.

**Verifier.** Could not refute it; the chain reproduces exactly as claimed. src/renderer/src/App.tsx:155 `const LICENSE_ENFORCEMENT = false` makes `licenseEnforced` (App.tsx:156) a constant false, so the effect at App.tsx:162-165 early-returns and window.toto.licenseGate() is never invoked, `licenseGatePending` (App.tsx:2476) is always false, and the <LicenseGate/> branch at App.tsx:2521-2525 — the only render site of that component in the repo — is unreachable. No build-time substitution rescues it: electron.vite.config.ts has no `define`. The activation path is equally dead: Settings.tsx:143 `LICENSE_UI_ENABLED = false` guards the sole <LicenseSection/> render at Settings.tsx:4990, and the only two callers of window.toto.licenseActivate (LicenseGate.tsx:79, Settings.tsx:5734) sit behind those two dead flags. licenseValid can only be set by activateLicense (src/main/license.ts:104,136) and is explicitly stripped from renderer settings patches (src/main/index.ts:1936), so the heartbeat guard at src/main/index.ts:4352 (`licenseGateEnabled && licenseValid`) can never be satisfied — the documented revoke kill-switch never fires. No main-side backstop exists: checkLicenseGrace() has exactly one non-test caller, the license:gate IPC handler at src/main/index.ts:2098, which only answers a renderer that never asks. The "intended" quotes are verbatim and the drift is wider than claimed: docs/license-platform-plan.md:60-64, src/main/license.ts:5-8, docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1252-1254, README.md:192, and docs/ENTERPRISE_RELEASE.md:133 ("A fresh install blocks when licenseGateEnabled is true and no license is activated" — a pre-ship proof that can never pass), while build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json:8,23 ships licenseGateEnabled:true AND locks the key (already copied into release/win-unpacked/resources/). Root cause of the drift is commit 596c17a ("license enforcement master switch (off)"), which touched only App.tsx and state.ts and updated no doc or example config. Ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/license.test.ts: 21/21 pass, but every test exercises checkLicenseGrace/heartbeat/activateLicense in isolation and none asserts the renderer gate, so no test prevents this. Severity medium is right: the off-switch itself is deliberate and commented (Phase 1 licensing off, Phase 2 public license-server deploy still open per license-platform-plan.md), so there is no security or data impact — but a shipped, locked enterprise policy plus four docs and a release checklist assert enforcement that cannot occur, which is a real trap for the licensed-rollout workflow. Not high (the whole licensing platform is pre-deployment); not low (the contradicting artifact is shipped, not just prose). Fix is small: either flip/derive the two constants and re-verify the activation UI end to end, or correct the example config and the four doc sites to state that enforcement is compiled off.

**FIXED (2026-08-17).** Took the second branch of the ledger's own choice: enforcement stays compiled off — the public license-server deploy is still open (license-platform-plan.md Phase 2), so flipping the constants would ship a blocking gate for a platform that is not deployed — and every artifact that contradicted that now states it.

The SHIPPED one first, because it is the one that could reach a customer: `build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json` no longer sets `licenseGateEnabled` and no longer locks it. It carried a `_comment_license` in its place explaining why, so the next person does not helpfully add it back. Then `docs/ENTERPRISE_RELEASE.md` — its "Customer Control Proof" list contained six licensing proofs ("a fresh install blocks when licenseGateEnabled is true", seat consumption, seat cap, revocation, offline grace) that no shipped build can produce; a pre-ship proof that can never pass is worse than no proof, because it gets ticked off. Removed, with the reason recorded in place. `src/main/license.ts`'s header, `README.md`, `docs/asktoto-architecture.md` and `docs/license-platform-plan.md` all said the subsystem went live when the SETTING was turned on; they now name the two renderer constants that actually decide, and the plan gained a step 0 (flip both, together, and re-verify end to end) that every other step depends on.

The part that stops this recurring is `src/renderer/src/license-enforcement-drift.contract.test.ts`. It does not pin any single file — it pins the RELATIONSHIP the root-cause commit (596c17a: flipped the constant, updated nothing else) broke. It reads both constants and asserts that while enforcement is compiled off no artifact may claim otherwise; flip them and the same tests demand the artifacts move with them. It also asserts the two constants agree with each other, since one on and one off is the brick state (a gate with no activation form). Verified by regression: re-adding `licenseGateEnabled: true` to the example config fails the suite.

### MQA-069 — Base/Thinking model fields write settings.json on every keystroke through a controlled IPC round-trip, so fast typing drops characters and can persist a garbled model id

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:1077` · workflow: set a custom model id in Settings → AI → Advanced · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:203-206 — "Debounced text field — shows keystrokes instantly but only commits (which persists settings.json to disk over IPC) ~350ms after typing stops, and on blur. Stops every keystroke from hitting disk." That helper (LazyInput/useLazyText) is used for the sibling field in the very same Advanced block — customBaseUrl at Settings.tsx:1126-1133.

**Actual.** The Base model input (Settings.tsx:1067-1085) and Thinking model input (:1093-1108) are plain controlled `<input>`s whose `value` is `settings.providerModels[provider] ?? ''` / `settings.providerModelsThinking[provider] ?? ''` — i.e. state that only updates after the IPC round-trip completes (state.ts:548-550 `setSettings(await window.toto.setSettings(p))`) — and whose onChange calls `patch({ providerModels: { ...settings.providerModels, [provider]: e.target.value } })` on every keystroke. Each of those keystrokes runs a full prepareFileKeyForWrite + readUserRaw (AES decrypt) + AES encrypt + tmp-write + rename + re-parse cycle in store.ts:518-573 plus getLockedKeys/validatedManaged.

**Repro.** Provider = OpenAI, Advanced open, Base model empty. Type g,p,e faster than the settings round-trip. Keystroke 1 issues patch('g'); keystroke 2 issues patch('gp'); patch('g') then resolves and React re-renders the controlled input with value='g', resetting the DOM from 'gp' back to 'g' and moving the caret; keystroke 3 is now typed against 'g' and issues patch('ge'). Handlers resolve in issue order, so the persisted value is 'ge' — the 'p' the user typed is gone. The result is a silently truncated model id (e.g. 'gpt-41' or 'gt-4.1'), which resolveModelTier then hands to the provider verbatim (it beats every registry default, providers.ts:484/493) and every request 400s with an unrecognised-model error the user reads as "my key stopped working". The window is proportional to the round-trip, and on the managed-Windows path in finding #1 that round-trip is seconds, making this near-certain there.

**Suggested fix.** Wrap both model fields in the existing LazyInput/useLazyText helper exactly as customBaseUrl at Settings.tsx:1126 does, so the field is locally controlled while typing and only commits on the 350 ms idle/blur boundary.

**Verifier.** SURVIVES. I tried four refutations and all failed.

1) "The intended-behavior quote is misread." It is not. `D:\Asktoto\src\renderer\src\components\Settings.tsx:203-206` is verbatim: "Debounced text field — shows keystrokes instantly but only commits (which persists settings.json to disk over IPC) ~350ms after typing stops, and on blur. Stops every keystroke from hitting disk." `useLazyText` (207-235) keeps a `local` state and only calls `onCommit` on a 350ms timer or blur, and its effect at 214-220 syncs only on EXTERNAL changes so in-flight typing isn't reverted. `LazyInput` (272-299) wraps it, and it IS used for the sibling field in the same Advanced block — `customBaseUrl` at 1126-1133. So the two model fields are the odd ones out, not the debounced ones.

2) "patch is optimistic / wrapped somewhere." It is not. `D:\Asktoto\src\renderer\src\state.ts:548-550` is exactly `const patch = useCallback(async (p) => { setSettings(await window.toto.setSettings(p)) }, [])` — no local pre-update. `D:\Asktoto\src\renderer\src\App.tsx:2232` passes that raw `patch` straight into `<Settings>`; `Settings` (root props) and `AiSection` (Settings.tsx:709-722) both take `patch: (p) => void` as a plain prop and never shadow `settings`. `D:\Asktoto\src\preload\index.ts:71-72` is a bare `ipcRenderer.invoke(IPC.settingsSet, patch)` — no coalescing/debounce. So the controlled `value` at Settings.tsx:1075 (`settings.providerModels[provider] ?? ''`) and :1096 genuinely only advances after a full main-process round-trip, while onChange at :1077-1079 / :1098-1102 fires per keystroke.

3) "React won't stomp the DOM." It will, on both paths. React 18 restores a controlled input's DOM value to the last-committed `value` prop at the end of the change event (restoreStateIfNeeded → updateWrapper) when no synchronous state update occurred, and on commit of the later re-render `commitUpdate` calls `updateWrapper` again with the stale-by-one value. Either way a keystroke typed while a patch is in flight is issued against a stale DOM value, so an intermediate character is dropped and the LAST resolving patch wins. The finder's trace ('g','p','t' → persisted 'ge'/'gt') is the mild version; with React's synchronous restore a fast burst can persist only the final character. Same defect class, same outcome.

4) "Something downstream sanitises the model id." Nothing does. `D:\Asktoto\src\shared\providers.ts:497-514` `resolveModelTier` returns `const base = (providerModels[id] || '').trim()` first for base tier (line 513 `return base || def.fastModel || def.defaultModel || ''`) and `think || base || …` at 510 — a custom id beats every registry default and is sent verbatim. `migrateRetiredModelId` (476-481) explicitly passes unknown/custom ids through unchanged ("a user pointing at their own fine-tune must never be rewritten"). `applyInteractiveGuardrail` only pins `anthropic`/`claude-cli` — and the anthropic field is `disabled` anyway (Settings.tsx:1076), so the affected surface is exactly the non-anthropic providers this field exists for. The finder's providers.ts line numbers (484/493) are ~13 lines stale vs. the current 510/513, but the code is what they describe.

Corroboration from the codebase itself: `D:\Asktoto\src\main\store.ts:545-547` says "Invariant enforced at the persistence boundary (not just in the Settings UI) … Covers per-keystroke UI commits, IPC callers, and hand-rolled patches alike" — the main process already knows this UI commits per keystroke.

The per-keystroke cost is also worse than the finder stated. Beyond store.ts:518-573 (prepareFileKeyForWrite → getLockedKeys → readUserRaw AES-decrypt → writeFileSync tmp + renameSync → cache-invalidate → getSettings re-read/decrypt/zod-parse), the handler at `D:\Asktoto\src\main\index.ts:1952-2000` additionally runs `auditLog('settings.changed')` (disk), `refreshScreenPreprocess()`, `win.setContentProtection()`, `syncIntelContentProtection()`, and — per keystroke — `registerShortcuts()` (which starts with `globalShortcut.unregisterAll()` at index.ts:1535) and `rebuildTrayMenu()` (index.ts:1707). Then the resolved `PublicSettings` re-renders the whole ~5000-line Settings tree (App.tsx:2218 comment). That makes the round-trip window large enough for the race to be hit by ordinary fast typing, not just on the slow managed-Windows path.

No guard, no caller mitigation, no schema default, no test covers it. `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/components/Settings.contract.test.ts src/renderer/src/components/Settings.helpers.test.ts` → 21 passed, and neither file mentions providerModels, debounce, or LazyInput.

Severity: medium is right. It is confined to a non-default workflow (Advanced panel, non-anthropic provider, typing rather than picking from the `datalist` at Settings.tsx:1116-1120), the field visibly misbehaves so it is not wholly silent, and it is user-recoverable by retyping slowly. But the outcome is a persisted garbled model id that makes every subsequent request 400 with an error the user reads as a broken key. Not high (no data loss, not security, recoverable), not low (persists bad state that breaks the provider).

Fix: give `LazyInput` an optional `list?: string` passthrough (it lacks one today, Settings.tsx:272-299) and swap the two inputs at Settings.tsx:1067-1085 and :1093-1108 to `LazyInput` + `onCommit`, mirroring customBaseUrl at :1126-1133.

### MQA-070 — Turning on "Encrypt transcripts" leaves the already-published plaintext wiki/ mirror in place and keeps rewriting it — no purge, no consent, no audit

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:1962` · workflow: publish meeting intelligence / encrypt transcripts at rest · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:1959-1961 — "// At-rest encryption just turned on → purge any previously-built CLEARTEXT knowledge graph so it // can't leak meeting topics/entities the encryption is meant to protect."  src/main/index.ts:1923-1927 — "Task MI-5 consent gate: turning publishBrainPages ON while transcripts stay encrypted writes readable meeting intelligence outside the encryption boundary — require an explicit, unmissable confirmation before it takes effect".  src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:4946-4947 — "Encrypted at rest. Even if the folder syncs to the cloud, contents stay locked to this device."

**Actual.** The consent gate at src/main/index.ts:1929 only fires on the publishBrainPages false->true transition (`'publishBrainPages' in p && p.publishBrainPages && !cur.publishBrainPages && willEncrypt`). The encryption transition at src/main/index.ts:1962-1965 purges ONLY graphify artifacts (`purgeGraphArtifacts()`), never the wiki mirror. The wiki branch at src/main/index.ts:1968-1976 keys exclusively off publishBrainPages changes, so nothing runs on encryptTranscripts false->true. src/main/brain/publish.ts:72-74 `writeWikiFile` hard-codes `writeSaved(path, content, false)`, so every later ingest (publishForExtraction, publish.ts:780-798) rewrites the pages in plaintext.

**Repro.** Settings -> Privacy: leave "Encrypt transcripts at rest" OFF. Settings -> Published wiki: turn "Publish meeting intelligence" ON (no dialog fires, because willEncrypt is false at index.ts:1929). wiki/index.md, wiki/deals/*.md, wiki/meetings/*.md are written in plaintext with meeting titles, TL;DRs, decisions, action items and deal amounts. Now turn "Encrypt transcripts at rest" ON. Result: index.ts:1962 purges graph.json/graph.html only; every wiki/*.md stays on disk in cleartext inside the OneDrive-synced meetings folder, keeps being regenerated in cleartext on every new meeting, no 'brain.publish.consent' audit line is ever written, and the Settings copy still tells the user "contents stay locked to this device".

**Suggested fix.** In settingsSet, treat the encryptTranscripts false->true transition the same way as the publish false->true transition: if `!wasEncrypted && next.encryptTranscripts && next.publishBrainPages`, run the same native consent dialog; on decline, force `publishBrainPages:false` and call `removeWiki(next)` (audit `brain.publish.disabled`); on accept, log `brain.publish.consent` and republish. Extend the existing purge block at index.ts:1962-1965 to cover the wiki mirror, not just graph artifacts.

**Verifier.** Could not refute the causal chain; every proposed escape hatch is absent.

VERIFIED: (1) The MI-5 consent gate at src/main/index.ts:1947 is `'publishBrainPages' in p && p.publishBrainPages && !cur.publishBrainPages && willEncrypt` — scoped to the publish OFF->ON edge only. The encryption OFF->ON edge reaches the identical end state (readable intelligence outside the encryption boundary) with no dialog and no 'brain.publish.consent' audit entry (only the generic auditLog('settings.changed') at index.ts:1984). (2) index.ts:1980-1983 purges graph artifacts only; its own parenthetical "Builds are already blocked while encryption is on" is false when publishing is on, since graphifyRefusalReason (src/main/graphify.ts:242) refuses only on `encryptTranscripts && !publishBrainPages`. (3) index.ts:1986-1993 keys the wiki branch exclusively off publishBrainPages transitions. (4) removeWiki has exactly ONE production caller, index.ts:1987 (publish ON->OFF) — grep-confirmed. No boot/poll-time reconciliation exists for the wiki, in pointed contrast to purgeGraphIfEncryptedAndStale at index.ts:1823-1828, which the codebase did build for the graph and runs on every settingsGet. That asymmetry is the strongest evidence the wiki case was never considered. (5) publish.ts:72-74 writeWikiFile -> writeSaved(path, content, false), and writeSaved (transcripts.ts:278-285) encrypts only when the flag is true; publishForExtraction (publish.ts:786) gates on publishBrainPages alone and runs from ingest.ts:1348 on every merge, so post-encryption meetings keep producing cleartext pages. (6) Renderer offers no confirmation or warning: Settings.tsx:4940 is a bare `patch({ encryptTranscripts: v })`, and the Privacy section has no publishBrainPages-aware warning. (7) No test guards it: publish.test.ts has no encryption-transition case (ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/publish.test.ts -> 20/20 pass, all publishBrainPages-only), and there is no settings:set handler test file.

REACHABILITY: encryptTranscripts defaults true (src/shared/ipc.ts:715), publishBrainPages defaults false (ipc.ts:723, hardened in store.ts:478-482), so the repro needs encryption OFF -> publish ON -> encryption ON. Non-default but plausible, and graphify.ts:243's refusal copy actively steers users toward the publish+encrypt combination.

WHERE THE FINDER OVERREACHES: the "purge the wiki" remedy is not the documented intent. publish.ts:36-38 states the mirror is plaintext "regardless of encryptTranscripts", and graphify.ts:249-257 treats encrypted+published as the supported configuration. Deleting a consented feature's output as a side effect of an unrelated toggle is the exact anti-pattern store.ts:478-482 (QA #9) exists to prevent. The cited index.ts graph-purge comment is about the knowledge graph, not the wiki, so it supports the claim only by analogy; the load-bearing intent quote is the consent-gate comment at index.ts:1941-1946, which justifies the modal by the STATE (publishing on while encrypted), not by the transition — and only one of the two transitions into that state is gated.

SEVERITY CORRECTED critical -> medium: the flip exfiltrates nothing new at that instant (the wiki files already existed under explicit consent), publishBrainPages remains visible with accurate copy in that state (Settings.tsx:5431-5433), and one toggle deletes the mirror. Real harm is (a) the false assurance at Settings.tsx:4946-4947 ("contents stay locked to this device") over a folder that literally contains plaintext wiki/ — wikiDir = join(resolveMeetingsFolder(s), 'wiki') at publish.ts:43-45 — and (b) continued cleartext regeneration of NEW meeting intelligence the user now believes is encrypted.

FIX (small): extend the index.ts:1947 condition to the encryption OFF->ON edge when cur.publishBrainPages is true (same native dialog, decline = drop encryptTranscripts or offer removeWiki), and/or render a publishBrainPages-aware warning next to the green banner in Settings.tsx:4943-4949.

### MQA-071 — Keyless profile saves every meeting twice — clicking "New meeting" from Review writes a duplicate .md, index row and brain ingest

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1424` · workflow: save a meeting (no AI provider configured) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1494-1496 — "No recap means no recap-time auto-save fires — persist the transcript NOW (empty recap) so a keyless 'Done' never discards the meeting. **Idempotent via savedRef, so the later leave-Review rescue won't double-save.**"  src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1421 — "Idempotent via savedRef, so normally-saved meetings never double-save."

**Actual.** The claimed idempotence does not exist: saveMeetingNow (App.tsx:1544-1575) never assigns savedRef — its own comment at App.tsx:1552-1554 says it "deliberately does NOT write the live session's savedRef/savedPath". savedRef is only written by the autosave effect (App.tsx:567) and by discardMeeting (App.tsx:1706), neither of which runs on the keyless path. So the guard `savedRef.current === String(started)` at App.tsx:1558 is false on the second call, and reset()'s rescue at App.tsx:1423-1425 saves the same lines/startedAt again.

**Repro.** No AI provider connected. Run a meeting with speech, press Stop -> App.tsx:1497 writes `<folder>/20260807-141500-<slug>.md`. On the Review screen click **New meeting** -> reset() reaches App.tsx:1423, `listen.listening` is false and `listen.lines.length > 0`, savedRef.current is '' -> saveMeetingNow fires again with the same startedAt -> saveMeeting's collision loop (src/main/transcripts.ts:671-674) writes `20260807-141500-<slug>-2.md`. Two identical meetings appear in History, two rows in index.md, and both are ingested into the brain and published as two separate wiki note cards.

**Suggested fix.** Have saveMeetingNow pin `savedRef.current = String(started)` on a successful write (it is already keyed per meeting, so this cannot collide with the autosave path), or pass an explicit already-saved marker back from the keyless branch at App.tsx:1497 that reset()'s rescue at App.tsx:1423 checks.

**Verifier.** MECHANISM CONFIRMED, TRIGGER REFUTED, so the finding survives with a corrected repro and lower severity.

Confirmed: saveMeetingNow (src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1544-1575) only READS savedRef at :1558 and never writes it — its own comment at :1552-1554 states this deliberately. savedRef is written only at :513 (manualSave), :567 (recap autosave) and :1706 (discardMeeting). On the keyless path maybeFireRecap calls ask.clear() (:1493; state.ts:456-460 sets answer=null), so the autosave effect's `settled = !answerStreaming && (!!answerText || !!answerError)` (:543) is false and savedRef stays ''. Therefore the intended-behavior comment at :1494-1496 ("Idempotent via savedRef, so the later leave-Review rescue won't double-save") is factually false, and the guard at :1558 cannot stop a second call.

Refuted — the finder's named trigger: Review's "New meeting" chip is onDone -> `reset` (App.tsx:2392-2398 -> :1648). reset saves only inside `if (wasListening)` (:1653-1654), and on a post-Stop Review listen.listening is already false (maybeFireRecap only runs when !listen.listening, :1479), so reset saves nothing and then listen.clear()s. The cited :1423-1425 is inside startListen, which reset never calls. Bar's "New meeting" pill only renders while listening (components/Bar.tsx:675-685), so it is not reachable from Review. The stated repro produces exactly ONE file, and the title claim "saves every meeting twice" is overstated.

Survives via the real "leave-Review rescue" sites the comment itself names: (a) Escape from Review — App.tsx:2045-2046, guarded only by `!pastMeeting && listen.lines.length`, recap resolves to '' since ask.answer is null; (b) starting a session while Review is open (bar rec-dot / toggle-listen hotkey, :1965 and :2697 -> toggleListen -> startListen's rescue at :1423-1425). Escape does not clear listen.lines, so Stop -> Esc -> start next meeting yields THREE saves. Both fire with the same meetingStartRef.current (startListen only resets it at :1428, after the rescue call at :1424).

No downstream dedupe: IPC.saveTranscript (src/main/index.ts:3175-3190) -> saveMeeting always writes a new file via the collision loop (src/main/transcripts.ts:671-674, "-2" suffix), then appendIndexRow (:709), scheduleRebuild (:3187) and enqueueIngest (:3190) — so duplicate .md, duplicate index row, duplicate brain ingest / wiki card, exactly as claimed. Grep shows no test references saveMeetingNow / maybeFireRecap / recapSkipped anywhere, so nothing guards it.

Severity corrected high -> medium: it does not fire on the primary exit (Done/"New meeting" -> reset), requires the keyless config plus an Escape or re-listen exit, and the impact is silent duplication rather than data loss or corruption.

Fix: pin savedRef.current = String(meetingStartRef.current) after the keyless save at App.tsx:1497 succeeds (or have saveMeetingNow pin when started === meetingStartRef.current), mirroring the recap autosave at :567.

### MQA-072 — Retroactive "Generate recap" treats a rejected disk write as success — the generated recap is shown, then lost forever

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1866` · workflow: generate a recap for a past/imported meeting · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1875-1878 — "Persistence failure is rare. Deliberately do NOT clear recapGenTarget here: doing so would flip Review's view back to the still-empty saved recap and the freshly generated text — the only copy of it left — would vanish. Leaving the target set keeps recapGen's generated text on screen instead".

**Actual.** src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1866 `await window.toto.recallUpdateRecap(action.file, action.text)` discards the return value. recallUpdateRecap RESOLVES with `{ok:false, error}` (it never throws) on every real failure — zod rejection for a recap over 20000 chars (src/shared/ipc.ts:1359-1362 + src/main/index.ts:2440-2441 returning 'Invalid edit request.'), 'Meeting file not found.', 'Meeting file could not be decrypted on this device.', and 'Could not save your changes.' when writeSaved throws (src/main/recall.ts:449-455, 482-486). Because nothing throws, the try block at App.tsx:1864-1873 continues down the SUCCESS path: setPastMeeting paints action.text into memory (line 1870) and setRecapGenTarget(null) releases the target (line 1873). The catch block that implements the quoted intent is unreachable for these cases.

**Repro.** Open a past meeting saved without notes, click **Generate recap**. While the model streams, the meeting's .md is locked by OneDrive sync / an open editor (routine on Windows), so writeSaved's rename fails and updateMeetingRecap returns `{ok:false, error:'Could not save your changes.'}`. Review renders the fresh recap, no error appears anywhere, and Copy/Export use it. Click "Back to history" and reopen the same meeting: the Summary section shows "No notes saved for this meeting. Select Edit to add some." — the generated recap is gone. Same outcome deterministically for any generated recap longer than 20000 characters (Anthropic recap runs get max_tokens 8192, src/main/llm/anthropic.ts:39).

**Suggested fix.** Capture the result: `const r = await window.toto.recallUpdateRecap(action.file, action.text)`; if `!r.ok`, take exactly the branch the catch already documents (leave recapGenTarget set, keep the generated text on screen) and surface r.error to the user; only run setPastMeeting/setRecapGenTarget(null) when `r.ok`.

**Verifier.** Reproduced the causal chain end to end and could not refute it.

1. src/preload/index.ts:197-198 — `recallUpdateRecap: (file, recap) => ipcRenderer.invoke(IPC.recallUpdateRecap, {file, recap})` typed `Promise<{ok:boolean;error?:string}>`; contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('toto', api) at :317 exposes it raw. No renderer-side wrapper that converts ok:false into a throw (grepped all call sites).
2. src/main/index.ts:2469-2479 — handler RETURNS `{ok:false,error}` for requireAuth (:2471), zod failure (:2473; UpdateRecapPayloadSchema caps recap at `z.string().max(20000)`, src/shared/ipc.ts:1369), and returns `result` from updateMeetingRecap (:2474,:2479). It never throws for these, so `invoke` resolves.
3. src/main/recall.ts:423-487 — every failure is `return {ok:false,...}`: invalid name (:430-432), reserved '## Full transcript' heading (:437-439), read error/ENOENT (:446-452), decrypt failure (:455), non-meeting file (:475), and `try { await writeSaved(...) } catch { return {ok:false, error:'Could not save your changes.'} }` (:482-486).
4. src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1866 — `await window.toto.recallUpdateRecap(action.file, action.text)` discards the result. Because nothing rejects, control continues down the success path: setPastMeeting paints action.text in memory (:1870) and setRecapGenTarget(null) releases the target (:1873). The catch at :1874 — whose comment (:1875-1878) I read verbatim and which does say exactly what the finder quoted ("Deliberately do NOT clear recapGenTarget here… the freshly generated text — the only copy of it left — would vanish") — is only reachable when invoke itself rejects (assertMainWindow, missing handler), i.e. never for the documented ok:false paths. Intent is real and unmet.
5. Loss is permanent: nothing else ever writes pastMeeting.recap back (only Review.tsx's manual edit path), and openPastMeeting re-reads from disk via recallRead (App.tsx:1898-1913), so reopening shows the empty recap. reviewBody (:2323, :2341-2346) falls back to pm.recap once the target is cleared, so the in-memory copy dies on navigation.

Refutation attempts that failed: no guard/default anywhere (recapPersistAction, src/renderer/src/lib/transcript.ts:29-36, is pure and knows nothing about writes); no test covers it — ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/lib/transcript.test.ts, 13/13 pass but only exercise the pure decision function; no other caller re-persists.

Counter-evidence that this is an oversight, not deliberate: both sibling callers handle ok:false — Review.tsx:269-273 branches on r.ok and sets recapEditError; main/index.ts:809-811 converts `!result.ok` into `throw new Error(result.error || 'Could not save the imported summary.')` for the import path.

Severity corrected high -> medium: writeSaved (src/main/transcripts.ts:290-305) already retries EPERM/EBUSY 5x with backoff (~600ms), so the OneDrive/AV lock repro needs a lock that outlasts the retry ladder; the >20000-char zod case is possible (recap runs get max_tokens 8192, src/main/llm/anthropic.ts:39) but atypical for a recap. The lost artifact is a derived summary, regenerable with one click, and remains on screen/copyable/exportable for the rest of the session. Silent, real data loss — but bounded and recoverable, not high.

Fix is small: capture the result at App.tsx:1866, and on !ok return before :1870/:1873 (leaving recapGenTarget set, which is what the existing comment already intends) plus a surface for r.error mirroring Review.tsx's recapEditError; the finally at :1879-1881 already releases recapPersistingRef.

### MQA-073 — After editing a past meeting's notes, Regenerate rewrites the file on disk but the screen (and every export) keeps showing the old edited text

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/Review.tsx:232` · workflow: regenerate a past meeting's summary after editing it · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/Review.tsx:211-215 — "`recapText` is the single value every consumer below (Markdown render, Copy Summary, Export JSON/PDF, CRM payload) reads, so an edit reflects everywhere at once."  src/renderer/src/components/Review.tsx:661-663 — "Regenerate — re-run the recap from the same transcript when the generated summary is wrong or thin… a past meeting regenerates + overwrites the saved one."

**Actual.** `const recapText = editedRecap ?? recap?.text ?? ''` (Review.tsx:232) gives the local post-edit copy absolute priority over the incoming recap prop. `editedRecap` is only cleared by the effect at Review.tsx:221-225, which is keyed on `[savedPath]` — regeneration does not change savedPath. So once saveRecap has set editedRecap (Review.tsx:276), the streaming recapGenDisplay and the later regenerated pastMeeting.recap (App.tsx:2341-2347, 1870) are both masked. The disk write still happens (App.tsx:1866).

**Repro.** History -> open a past meeting with notes -> **Edit** -> change the Overview line to "EDITED BY ME" -> **Save** (editedRecap = the edited text). Click **Regenerate**. The recap regenerates and recallUpdateRecap overwrites '## Notes & follow-ups' on disk with the new AI text. On screen the Summary still shows "EDITED BY ME" — no spinner, no new text, the button looks dead. Copy Summary, Export JSON, Export PDF and the CRM payload preview (Review.tsx:411-418) all emit "EDITED BY ME", which no longer exists in the file or in the brain re-ingest. Navigating to History and reopening the meeting reveals the regenerated text.

**Suggested fix.** Clear the local override whenever a new generation takes over: add `setEditedRecap(null)` when `recap?.id` changes to a non-'past' id (or when `recap.streaming` becomes true), so recapText falls back to the live/regenerated prop; keying the existing reset effect on `[savedPath, recap?.id]` is the minimal change.

**Verifier.** I tried to refute this five ways and could not. Every link in the chain reproduces in the code.

1. `setEditedRecap` has exactly three call sites (grep over Review.tsx): the `useState` init at Review.tsx:219, the reset inside the effect at Review.tsx:221-225, and the success branch of `saveRecap` at Review.tsx:277. The reset effect's dep array is literally `[savedPath]`. There is no other clearing path.

2. `savedPath` does not change on regenerate. App.tsx:2349 passes `savedPath={pm ? pm.file : savedPath}`, and `onRetryRecap` for a past meeting is `() => { if (requireProvider()) generateSavedRecap(pm.file, pm.lines) }` (App.tsx:2360). `generateSavedRecap` (App.tsx:1826-1843) only calls `recapGen.run(...)` and `setRecapGenTarget({ file })` — it never touches `pastMeeting`, so `pm.file` is the same string before and after. The reset effect therefore never re-fires.

3. No remount escape hatch. `Review` is `memo(...)` (Review.tsx:85) and is rendered unkeyed via `reviewBody` at App.tsx:2470; the only `key=` in App.tsx is on `<Answer>` at App.tsx:2415. `view` stays `'review'` throughout. So the component instance — and `editedRecap` — survives.

4. `recapText = editedRecap ?? recap?.text ?? ''` (Review.tsx:232) masks both incoming values: the streaming `recapGenDisplay` (App.tsx:2335-2343) and, after settle, the regenerated `pastMeeting.recap` written by `setPastMeeting((prev) => ... { ...prev, recap: action.text })` at App.tsx:1870. The render branch at Review.tsx:741 (`recapText ? <Markdown>{recapText}</Markdown>`) short-circuits before the streaming branch at 743, so the stale text stays painted. Every downstream consumer reads `recapText`: `copyNotes` (338), `exportJson` (351), `exportPdf` (365), `crmPayload.summary` (415).

5. The disk write is unconditional. `recapPersistAction` (src/renderer/src/lib/transcript.ts:29-36) returns `{file, text}` for any settled, non-empty, non-errored answer — it does not skip when a recap already exists — and App.tsx:1866 calls `recallUpdateRecap(action.file, action.text)`. So the file genuinely diverges from the screen.

Intended-behavior quotes check out verbatim: Review.tsx:212-214 says "`recapText` is the single value every consumer below (Markdown render, Copy Summary, Export JSON/PDF, CRM payload) reads, so an edit reflects everywhere at once", and Review.tsx:661-664 says a past meeting "regenerates + overwrites the saved one."

No test guards this: there is no Review.test.* (only ReviewEntityStrip.test.ts), and App.local-gates.test.ts:115-116 only asserts the provider-gate arg shape for `onGenerateRecap`, not state.

One finder detail is wrong: the repro claims "no spinner, the button looks dead." The `recap` prop during regeneration IS `recapGenDisplay` with `streaming: true`, so Review.tsx:671-675 does disable the button and render `<Spinner/> Regenerating`. The user sees a spinner, then the text is unchanged when it finishes — misleading in a different way (reads as "regeneration produced the same output"), but not a dead button. The core defect is unaffected.

Severity corrected high -> medium. The overwrite itself is documented intent, so this is not unexpected data destruction; the defect is the stale display plus stale exports, it needs the specific edit-save-then-regenerate sequence, and it fully self-heals on navigating to History and reopening. Fix is small: key the reset (or a targeted clear) on the incoming recap identity as well, e.g. `[savedPath, recap?.id]`, since the prop's id flips from `'past'` to the run id when regeneration starts.

Relevant files: D:\Asktoto\src\renderer\src\components\Review.tsx, D:\Asktoto\src\renderer\src\App.tsx, D:\Asktoto\src\renderer\src\lib\transcript.ts

### MQA-074 — A meeting file that cannot be read at publish time is published as non-confidential — the confidential flag fails open

**Where.** `src/main/brain/publish.ts:138` · workflow: exclude a confidential meeting from published intelligence · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/brain/publish.ts:129-130 — "An unreadable/undecryptable meeting file **is never treated as confidential (nor as safe** — it simply can't be read at all here)."  src/main/brain/publish.ts:651-659 (README_MD) — "Meetings flagged confidential in Métis are excluded from every page here."

**Actual.** The catch at src/main/brain/publish.ts:138-140 (and the `if (md && …)` guard at 137, where decodeSaved returns '' for an undecryptable envelope, src/main/transcripts.ts:256-258) simply skips the file, so its basename never enters the returned Set. Everything downstream reads absence-from-the-set as "safe to publish": NOT_CONFIDENTIAL (publish.ts:158) returns true, timelineRows (publish.ts:234-238) keeps the row, renderNumeric (publish.ts:184-188) renders the deal amount/close date sourced from it, changelogEntries (publish.ts:221-222) keeps its superseded values, and `confidentialOnly` (publish.ts:429) evaluates false so the entity page is written with its real name. The parenthetical claim "nor as safe" is not implemented.

**Repro.** Windows profile with the meetings folder on OneDrive (Files On-Demand is the Windows 11 default). Meeting `2026-06-12-acme-pricing.md` is flagged Confidential and has been dehydrated to a cloud-only placeholder; the machine is offline (or the file is momentarily locked by an antivirus/OneDrive sync handle -> EBUSY on Windows). Toggle Confidential on any other meeting -> publishAll runs -> readConfidentialMeetings' readFileSync for the Acme file throws, is swallowed at publish.ts:139, and that meeting is absent from the set. wiki/deals/acme-*.md is then regenerated WITH the Acme timeline row, its verified Amount and Close date, and wiki/index.md lists it — exactly the data the flag exists to suppress, written in plaintext.

**Suggested fix.** Return an explicit tri-state (or a second `unreadable: Set<string>`) from readConfidentialMeetings and fail CLOSED: treat an unreadable/undecryptable meeting as confidential for render purposes, or abort the publish run with a surfaced error rather than emitting pages built from an incomplete exclusion set.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED — could not refute. (1) Causal chain reproduced in code: readConfidentialMeetings (src/main/brain/publish.ts:131-143) is the sole confidentiality source at publish time; readSavedFile (src/main/transcripts.ts:261-263) calls readFileSync which throws on EBUSY/EACCES/ENOENT/cloud-placeholder, swallowed at publish.ts:138-140, and decodeSaved returns '' for an undecryptable envelope (transcripts.ts:256-258) so the `if (md && …)` at publish.ts:137 skips it. The basename then never enters the Set, and every consumer reads absence as "safe": NOT_CONFIDENTIAL (:158), renderNumeric (:186), renderNonNumeric (:168), changelogEntries (:222), timelineRows (:236), openCommitmentRows (:241), topByActivity (:699), confidentialOnly (:429). (2) No other gate exists: `grep -c confidential src/main/brain/ingest.ts` = 0 and store.ts has no confidentiality concept — the brain store deliberately retains the data (publish.ts:164), so render-time filtering is the only control.
