(3) The intended-behavior quotes are accurate and unqualified: README_MD publish.ts:658-659 and CLAUDE_MD publish.ts:687 both promise exclusion from every page; QA #11 (publish.ts:424-433) shows identity leakage was explicitly designed against; and graphify.ts:283 ("Confidentiality fail-closed") is the same codebase choosing fail-closed for the identical concern, so fail-open here is a genuine inconsistency, not intended design. (4) Reachability is wider than claimed: readConfidentialMeetings is recomputed per-entity in publishEntity (:411) and in publishMeetingCard (:503), both invoked on every ingest merge via publishForExtraction (:788-806), not only on the toggle (index.ts:2496 `void publishAll(s)`); a transient read error therefore writes a durable plaintext leak into wiki/ that persists until the next successful publish. (5) Extra consequence the finder missed: with the flag lost, publishMeetingCard passes the guard at :504 and then returns at :517-519 on the read failure, so a stale note card written before flagging is never deleted either. (6) `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/publish.test.ts` → 20/20 pass; no test simulates an unreadable/undecryptable meeting file, so nothing prevents this. Partial refutation considered and rejected: on a foreign machine the undecryptable path partly self-neutralizes because entity JSON is equally undecryptable (store.ts:230-234 returns null), but that blunts only one of the two triggers — a throwing read (locked/dehydrated .md while the freshly-rewritten .brain JSONs under the same folder, store.ts:33, remain readable) leaves the brain fully publishable. Severity medium stands: fail-open of the only confidentiality control into an explicitly agent-readable plaintext mirror, but triggered by an environmental I/O fault, not an attacker, and confined to the user's own folder. Fix is small: add the basename to the same Set in the catch and on empty `md` (fail closed), which also makes publishMeetingCard drop the stale card; call sites need no change, only new tests.

### MQA-075 — Confidential toggle reports success before the republish that actually enforces it — a failed publishAll leaves the meeting in the wiki and writes a bogus crash dump

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:2472` · workflow: flag a meeting confidential · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:2458-2462 — "Task MI-5: flag/unflag a saved meeting as confidential — excludes it from every published wiki surface (note card, entity timelines/current-facts, indexes)… **A full republish is the simplest correct way to make the exclusion (or its reversal) take effect everywhere at once**".  src/renderer/src/components/Review.tsx:567 renders "Confidential: excluded from published intelligence." purely on `r.ok`.

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:2469-2474: the handler returns `result` from setMeetingConfidential (which only rewrote the frontmatter) and fires the republish as `void publishAll(s)` at line 2472 — unawaited, result discarded, no try/catch. publishAll (src/main/brain/publish.ts:803-814) is a plain sequential loop with no per-page error handling, so the first throw (ensureWikiDirs mkdirSync EPERM, or writeSaved's tmp+rename failing on a locked wiki file) aborts every remaining page. The rejection escapes to `process.on('unhandledRejection', …)` (src/main/index.ts:3966), which runs onFatal -> persistCrash, writing a crash-*.log and an app.crash audit entry for a non-crash.

**Repro.** Publishing is on and the meetings folder is on OneDrive. Open a meeting in Review and switch **Confidential** on. setMeetingConfidential succeeds, so recallSetConfidential returns `{ok:true}` and Review paints "Confidential: excluded from published intelligence." (Review.tsx:178-179, 567). Meanwhile publishAll throws on the first wiki file OneDrive currently holds open — say wiki/people/anna-müller.md — so wiki/accounts/*, wiki/deals/*, every remaining note card and wiki/index.md are never regenerated and still contain that meeting's title, date, TL;DR, decisions and deal facts. The user gets no error; the only trace is a crash-*.log and an app.crash audit line.

**Suggested fix.** Await the republish inside the handler and fold its outcome into the returned result (`{ok:false, error:'Flag saved, but the published pages could not be updated.'}`), wrapping publishAll in try/catch so it can never surface as an unhandledRejection; make publishAll itself resilient per page (collect failures, continue) and re-attempt the republish on the next publish trigger.

**Verifier.** Survived every refutation attempt; only the line number was wrong (handler is src/main/index.ts:2487-2499, `void publishAll(s)` at 2496, not 2472).

CHAIN VERIFIED END TO END:
1. src/main/index.ts:2493-2498 — `const result = await setMeetingConfidential(s, ...)`; on ok, `auditLog(...)` then `void publishAll(s)` (detached, no await, no catch), then `return result`. The returned ok reflects only the frontmatter write.
2. src/main/recall.ts:554-600 — setMeetingConfidential rewrites ONLY the leading frontmatter block via writeSaved; it never touches wiki/.
3. src/main/brain/publish.ts:131 (readConfidentialMeetings) — the confidential set is read at publish time and applied during render. The wiki is static markdown, so already-written pages keep the meeting until regenerated. Republish is the sole enforcement mechanism, exactly as index.ts:2484-2486 states.
4. src/main/brain/publish.ts:803-814 — publishAll is a bare sequential loop (`for kind → for id → await publishEntity`, then meeting cards, then publishIndexes) with no try/catch and no per-page tolerance. First throw aborts all remaining pages, leaving a partially-regenerated wiki.
5. Throwing paths confirmed: ensureWikiDirs (publish.ts:62-67) calls mkdirSync unguarded; writeWikiFile → writeSaved ends in `throw e` at src/main/transcripts.ts:312.
6. src/main/index.ts:4012 registers `process.on('unhandledRejection', reason => onFatal('unhandledRejection', reason))`. onFatal (1205-1208) calls persistCrash FIRST (1207), which writes mainLog.error + `auditLog('app.crash', ...)` + a `crash-<ts>-<seq>.log` file (1185-1198). Line 1208 (`if (kind !== 'uncaughtException' || fatalHandled) return`) means the rejection path deliberately shows NO dialog — so the user genuinely sees nothing. Both halves of the claimed consequence confirmed.
7. src/renderer/src/components/Review.tsx:176-179 sets confidentialFlag optimistically and reverts only when `!r.ok`; 567-568 then renders "Confidential: excluded from published intelligence." purely off that flag.
8. Intended-behavior quote is verbatim at src/main/index.ts:2482-2486.

REFUTATIONS I TRIED AND THEY FAILED:
- No secondary republish: this handler has no enqueueIngest, unlike its siblings recallRename (2459) and recallUpdateRecap (2477). Only publishAll callers are ingest.ts:1731 (rebuildAll completion) and index.ts:1993 (publishing turned on) — neither periodic nor triggered here.
- No test coverage: grep for setMeetingConfidential/recallSetConfidential hits only index.ts, recall.ts, preload/index.ts, Review.tsx, shared/ipc.ts — zero test files. recall.test.ts has 0 mentions of "confidential". publish.test.ts covers filtering only (28 confidential assertions); ran it — 20/20 pass in 7.5s — and nothing exercises an error path or the IPC handler.
- Not suppressed by Node: the unhandledRejection listener is registered, so it fires rather than being warn-only.
- ipcMain.handle does not catch it: `void` explicitly detaches the promise from the handler's returned promise.

CORROBORATION FROM THE CODEBASE: src/main/index.ts:1660-1661 comments "rather than letting the rejection escape as an unhandledRejection → bogus crash audit" — the project already treats this exact pattern as a defect and guards against it elsewhere.

SEVERITY — held at medium, not raised. Impact argues higher (a confidentiality control reports success while the meeting's title/TL;DR/decisions/deal facts remain in wiki/accounts/*, wiki/deals/*, remaining note cards and wiki/index.md — the surface the AGENTS.md contract feeds to agents — with no user-visible error). But the trigger requires a durable filesystem failure, and writeSaved already retries EPERM/EBUSY on rename 5x with backoff (transcripts.ts:296-304), which specifically blunts the finder's headline OneDrive-lock repro. Exposure remains via the un-retried writeFile(tmp), the unguarded mkdirSync in ensureWikiDirs, exhausted retries, and non-EPERM/EBUSY codes. Two things must go wrong (publishing on + persistent I/O error), so medium is right.

FIX: await publishAll inside try/catch in the handler and downgrade result.ok (or return a warning) when the republish fails, so the renderer stops asserting exclusion took effect; optionally make publishAll tolerate per-page failures and report a partial result. Small — one handler plus a renderer message path. Note index.ts:1993 has the same fire-and-forget shape and should be fixed alongside. READ-ONLY: nothing changed.

### MQA-076 — Crash-recovery promotion re-encrypts a recovered meeting by the LIVE encryptTranscripts toggle, not the draft's own encryption — turning the toggle off downgrades an already-encrypted recording to cleartext and leaks its title into index.md

**Where.** `src/main/transcripts.ts:929` · workflow: Crash / force-quit recovery of an in-progress meeting at next launch · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/transcripts.ts:779-783 states the rule for every write to an existing saved recording: `// Preserve the file's ORIGINAL at-rest encryption exactly as found (mirrors updateMeetingRecap / renameMeeting), NOT the live encryptTranscripts toggle. Otherwise appending a debrief to a file that was saved while encryption was on would rewrite the whole transcript as plaintext once the toggle is later turned off — a silent at-rest downgrade of already-recorded third-party speech.` src/main/recall.ts:315-316 repeats it: `Encryption is preserved exactly as found: isEncryptedFile (not the current settings.encryptTranscripts toggle, which may have changed since this file was saved)…`

**Actual.** recoverOrphanDrafts writes the promoted meeting with the live setting: src/main/transcripts.ts:929 `await writeSaved(out, promoted, settings.encryptTranscripts)`. It never calls isEncryptedFile(draftPath), even though it has just proved the draft was encrypted by successfully decrypting it at transcripts.ts:921 `const text = decodeSaved(readFileSync(draftPath))`. The plaintext index.md row that follows is gated on the same live toggle (transcripts.ts:940 `if (!settings.encryptTranscripts)`), so the recovered meeting's title and date are appended to the cleartext index too. Neither transcripts.test.ts:561-635 nor any other test asserts encryption preservation for this path (86 tests in recall.test.ts + transcripts.test.ts all pass today).

**Repro.** 1. Settings → Encrypt transcripts = ON. 2. Start a meeting; the 60s autosave (App.tsx:473-491 → transcripts.ts:843) writes `.autosave-draft-2026-08-07_141500-312.md` as an ATKENC2 envelope. 3. Force-quit / crash before the meeting ends, so the draft survives. 4. In Settings turn Encrypt transcripts OFF — exactly what the app's own UNDECRYPTABLE_MSG advises at transcripts.ts:225-226 ("turn off at-rest encryption in Settings before saving if you need transcripts portable across devices"). 5. Relaunch. index.ts:3972 runs recoverOrphanDrafts, which decrypts the draft and writes `2026-08-07_141500-312-recovered.md` as UNMARKED CLEARTEXT into the OneDrive-synced meetings folder, and appends `| 2026-08-07 14:15 | <meeting title> | meeting | 0 min | [open](…) |` to the plaintext index.md. The full recorded third-party speech from an encrypted session is now on disk and in the sync queue in the clear, with no prompt and no log.

**Suggested fix.** Mirror renameMeeting/appendDebrief: capture `const wasEncrypted = isEncryptedFile(draftPath)` before decoding and pass that to writeSaved at transcripts.ts:929; gate the index.md row on `wasEncrypted` rather than `settings.encryptTranscripts` at transcripts.ts:940. Add a regression test to the recoverOrphanDrafts describe block (transcripts.ts:561) covering encrypted-draft + toggle-since-turned-off.

**Verifier.** I tried to refute this four ways and it survives all four.

1) The code says what the finder says. `src/main/transcripts.ts:929` is literally `await writeSaved(out, promoted, settings.encryptTranscripts)`, and `settings` is the LIVE settings object — `src/main/index.ts:4026` calls `recoverOrphanDrafts(getSettings())` at `app.whenReady()`. `isEncryptedFile(draftPath)` is never called anywhere in `recoverOrphanDrafts` (transcripts.ts:896-961), even though the function is defined in the same file (transcripts.ts:266) and used by every sibling write path. `writeSaved(..., false)` writes raw utf8 with no envelope (transcripts.ts:278-285), so an ATKENC2 draft that `decodeSaved` just decrypted at transcripts.ts:921 is rewritten as unmarked cleartext.

2) The "intended behavior" quotes are verbatim and do say what the finder claims. transcripts.ts:779-783 is exactly the quoted comment plus `const wasEncrypted = isEncryptedFile(path); await writeSaved(path, updated, wasEncrypted)`. recall.ts:314-316 is verbatim, and recall.ts:341/363, 453/483, 520/540, 575/596 all follow the same `wasEncrypted = isEncryptedFile(fullPath)` pattern. So the promotion path is the sole outlier among writes that produce a `type: meeting-transcript` file.

3) No guard/caller/default prevents it. `encryptTranscripts` defaults to `true` (shared/ipc.ts:715, :1093), so the encrypted-draft state is the default state. `settingsSet` (index.ts:1925-2011) has no conversion pass on the toggle — turning it OFF does nothing to existing files (the only branch, index.ts:1980, fires when turning it ON, and only purges graph artifacts). Nothing else touches `.autosave-draft-*` (grep: only recall.ts:54's exclusion regex and transcripts.ts:796/903/907). The index.md row is genuinely cleartext-always: `appendIndexRow` (transcripts.ts:423-433) uses raw `writeFileSync`/`appendFileSync`, and it is reached at transcripts.ts:940 under `!settings.encryptTranscripts`, so the recovered meeting's title lands in plaintext index.md in the (default) OneDrive-synced folder.

4) No test covers it. transcripts.test.ts:561-635 only exercises matched pairs — plaintext draft + plaintext settings (:620) and encrypted draft + encrypted settings (:628). I ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/transcripts.test.ts src/main/recall.test.ts`: 86/86 pass, confirming the mismatch case is untested.

Where I do correct the finder: the stated repro (crash → toggle off → relaunch) is sloppy, because after a full app crash the user must relaunch to reach Settings, and `recoverOrphanDrafts` runs at whenReady BEFORE they can flip the toggle — that launch promotes the draft while encryption is still ON. The bug still reaches, via paths the code itself documents: (a) `clearDraftTranscript`'s bounded unlink retry can still exhaust ("a genuinely stuck file still degrades to the old behaviour", transcripts.ts:855-858), leaving a stale draft alive through the running session while the user turns the toggle off, downgraded on the next launch; (b) `recoverOrphanDrafts` no-ops when the meetings folder isn't present yet (transcripts.ts:900) — realistic at launch-at-login before OneDrive mounts — deferring promotion past a toggle flip; (c) a renderer-only crash orphans the draft with the app still running. So the causal chain is real but needs a compound precondition, and the artifact class involved (the rolling draft) is already written by the live toggle by design at transcripts.ts:843. That plus "user consciously disabled encryption" is why I drop high → medium; it is a genuine silent at-rest downgrade of recorded third-party speech, not a theoretical one.

Fix is two lines inside the existing try block: `const wasEncrypted = isEncryptedFile(draftPath)` before transcripts.ts:921, pass it to `writeSaved` at :929, and gate the index row at :940 on `!wasEncrypted` instead of `!settings.encryptTranscripts` (otherwise a preserved-encrypted recovery would still leak its title into cleartext index.md).

### MQA-077 — The confidential flag fails OPEN: any meeting file the publisher cannot read is treated as non-confidential, so its extracted facts, quotes and timeline rows are published to the wiki anyway

**Where.** `src/main/brain/publish.ts:137` · workflow: Flag a meeting confidential so it is excluded from the published wiki · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:5433 is the user-facing guarantee: `'Publishes readable meeting intelligence to your OneDrive folder. Meetings you flag confidential are always excluded.'` src/renderer/src/components/RecallView.tsx:575 repeats it on the row chip: `title="Confidential: excluded from published intelligence"`, and src/main/recall.ts:548-550 states `a confidential meeting is excluded from every published wiki surface (note card, entity timelines/current-facts, indexes)`.

**Actual.** readConfidentialMeetings only adds a file to the exclusion set on a SUCCESSFUL read: src/main/brain/publish.ts:136-140 `const md = readSavedFile(join(folder, f)); if (md && readFrontmatterFlag(md, 'confidential')) out.add(f)` with `catch { /* unreadable on this device — skip, never guess */ }`. readSavedFile returns '' (never throws) for any envelope decodeSaved cannot open. Everything downstream then treats absence-from-the-set as permission to render: src/main/brain/publish.ts:158 `const NOT_CONFIDENTIAL = (sf, confidential) => !sf || !confidential.has(sf)`, consumed at publish.ts:168, 186, 222, 236, 242. The doc comment at publish.ts:129-130 acknowledges the file is "never treated as confidential", but the shipped product copy promises "always excluded", and nothing surfaces the gap to the user.

**Repro.** macOS, encryptTranscripts ON. src/main/index.ts:275 forces `process.env.ASKTOTO_LOCAL_KEYSTORE ??= '1'`, so every bulk read goes through decodeSaved with allowKeychainRecovery=false. A meeting saved before that forcing (kLocal starts with 'S:') hits src/main/transcripts.ts:180-182 `if (process.env.ASKTOTO_LOCAL_KEYSTORE && !canRecover) throw new Error('Keychain-wrapped transcript is unavailable while the local keystore is active')` → tryDecodeSaved returns null → readSavedFile returns ''. That meeting was extracted into `.brain/` while it was still readable and it was flagged `confidential: true` in its frontmatter. On the next publishAll it is absent from the confidential set, so its deal/person/account pages render its timeline rows, its quotes and its current facts into `<meetingsFolder>/wiki/` — a plaintext, OneDrive-synced, agent-readable surface — while History still shows the red "Confidential" chip. The same fails-open outcome occurs transiently on Windows: setMeetingConfidential fires `void publishAll(s)` immediately (index.ts:2461-2464) against the file it just wrote via tmp+rename, and that file is exactly the one transcripts.ts:292-304 documents as routinely EPERM/EBUSY-locked by OneDrive upload hashing and AV right after the rename.

**Suggested fix.** Fail closed: have readConfidentialMeetings return `{ confidential: Set, unreadable: Set }` and make NOT_CONFIDENTIAL (publish.ts:158) also return false for any source_file in `unreadable`, so an unreadable source is never rendered. Give readSavedFile a bounded EPERM/EBUSY retry for this call site, and surface a publish warning (or refuse the publish) when the unreadable set is non-empty, instead of silently publishing.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED, with two corrections to the finder's repro and blast radius.

Causal chain, independently reproduced by reading:
1. src/main/transcripts.ts:232-252 tryDecodeSaved returns null for any envelope it cannot unwrap (foreign keychain, wrong backend, malformed); :256-258 decodeSaved maps null to ''; :261-263 readSavedFile returns that ''. So "could not decrypt" is byte-identical to "empty file".
2. src/main/brain/publish.ts:131-143 readConfidentialMeetings adds to the set ONLY when the read succeeded AND the flag parses: `if (md && readFrontmatterFlag(md,'confidential')) out.add(f)`, with `catch { /* unreadable on this device — skip, never guess */ }` swallowing readFileSync errors (EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES, un-hydrated OneDrive Files-On-Demand placeholder, file replaced mid-loop).
3. Absence from the set is unconditionally read as "safe to render": publish.ts:158 NOT_CONFIDENTIAL, consumed at 168 (non-numeric facts), 186 (amount/close_date), 222 (changelog), 236 (timeline rows), 242 (open commitments, which carry verbatim promise text), 247 (newestDate), 429 (the confidential-only no-page rule), 699 (index.md listing). So an unreadable-but-flagged meeting's derived facts, commitment text, title and date render into <meetingsFolder>/wiki/ — plaintext, OneDrive-synced, agent-readable — and index.md lists it.

No other guard exists. src/main/brain/ingest.ts contains zero `confidential` references, so confidential meetings are always fully extracted into .brain; publish-time filtering is the ONLY control. There is no sidecar/index of confidential meetings — the flag lives only in the meeting file's own frontmatter (recall.ts:579-593). setMeetingConfidential fails closed only for its own write (recall.ts:577 returns "Meeting file could not be decrypted on this device"). The intended-behavior quotes are verbatim accurate: Settings.tsx:5433 "Meetings you flag confidential are always excluded.", RecallView.tsx:575 title chip, recall.ts:548-550, and publish.ts's own shipped README_MD (:658) "Meetings flagged confidential in Métis are excluded from every page here" and CLAUDE_MD (:687). graphify.ts:283 literally labels this same helper "Confidentiality fail-closed" while it is fail-open here.

Tests do not cover it: ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/publish.test.ts passes 20/20, but every test meeting is plaintext (writeMeetingFile -> writeFileSync, settingsFor sets encryptTranscripts:false), so no test ever hands readConfidentialMeetings an undecryptable file.

Corrections to the finder:
(a) Blast radius is narrower than claimed. The meeting NOTE CARD surface is accidentally protected: publishMeetingCard (publish.ts:514-520) reads the file itself and `if (!raw) return`, so no new card is written (a stale card is merely left behind rather than removed — a smaller, separate leak). The confirmed leak is entity pages (timeline, current facts, changelog, open commitments) + index.md.
(b) The claimed repro is shaky as written. The macOS forced-keystore path (index.ts:283, darwin-only, not :275) usually self-cancels: .brain lives under the same meetings folder and inherits the same at-rest encryption (store.ts:23-34), so whatever makes the old transcript unreadable normally makes the entity JSON unreadable too — store.ts:229-233 returns null and publishEntity then REMOVES the page instead of publishing it. Likewise "History still shows the red Confidential chip" is wrong: recall.ts's readMeetingUncached turns an undecryptable meeting into a lockedStub titled "Locked — …" with no `confidential` field, so the chip disappears.
The reachable shape is one where .brain is readable while the .md is not: (i) at-rest encryption toggled OFF after the confidential meeting was saved — later merges rewrite the entity JSON as plaintext (store.ts:242 writeJson passes settings.encryptTranscripts) while the old .md keeps its ATKENC wrap — followed by a keychain/DPAPI identity change (the codebase ships recoverEncryptedProfile for exactly this) or a OneDrive sync to a second machine, which transcripts.ts:219-226 documents as the common undecryptable case; or (ii) any transient read failure at publish time (AV/OneDrive lock, cloud-only placeholder), including right after setMeetingConfidential's tmp+rename fires `void publishAll(s)` (index.ts:2496).

Severity medium is right: it is a privacy control failing silently open, but it needs an I/O/decryption failure to trigger, it leaks derived summary content rather than verbatim transcript, and nothing about it is attacker-controlled in the normal case. Fix is small: have readConfidentialMeetings distinguish "read failed" from "read OK, no flag" and add unreadable files to the exclusion set (fail closed), rather than silently dropping them.

### MQA-078 — A meeting title containing a double quote or backslash never round-trips: History shows the YAML escapes, and every rename doubles them

**Where.** `src/main/recall.ts:18` · workflow: Save a meeting / rename a meeting from History · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/recall.test.ts:459-461 states the contract for this exact path: `// Regression test: a title containing $-replacement patterns ($&, $1, $\`, $$) used to corrupt the frontmatter and H1 … Fixed by using replacement functions instead, so it must round-trip verbatim.` and asserts it at recall.test.ts:476 `if (read.ok) expect(read.title).toBe(title)`. src/main/recall.ts:351-353 repeats the intent: a title "would otherwise mangle the output (or splice in the old title / whole match) instead of being written verbatim."

**Actual.** The writers escape for YAML — src/main/transcripts.ts:565-566 `const yamlSafeTitle = (s) => s.replace(/\\/g, '\\\\').replace(/"/g, '\\"')…` and src/main/recall.ts:304-306 `yamlSafeRenameTitle` — but the single reader never unescapes. src/main/recall.ts:18 `if (kv) out[kv[1]] = kv[2].replace(/^["[]|["\]]$/g, '').trim()` strips only the outer quote characters, leaving every `\"` and `\\` literal in the value that becomes MeetingSummary.title (recall.ts:132) and RecallReadResult.title (recall.ts:247). RecallView's rename input is pre-filled from that same escaped value (RecallView.tsx:605 `onStartEdit(m.file, m.title)`), so each commit re-escapes what was already escaped. Verified by running the two functions verbatim: 'Renault "Phase 2" renewal' → after rename #1 `Renault \"Phase 2\" renewal`, #2 `Renault \\\"Phase 2\\\" renewal`, #3 `Renault \\\\\\\"Phase 2\\\\\\\" renewal`. 'C:\Users share' behaves the same. The existing regression test only covers `$`-patterns, which contain no quote or backslash, so it passes.

**Repro.** A recap returns `## Title: Renault "Phase 2" renewal` (parseRecapMarkdown at transcripts.ts:1063-1068 strips only LEADING/TRAILING quotes, so the inner pair survives). saveMeeting writes `title: "Renault \"Phase 2\" renewal"`. History immediately shows `Renault \"Phase 2\" renewal`. Click the pencil, press Enter without editing: recallRename writes `title: "Renault \\\"Phase 2\\\" renewal"` and the row now shows `Renault \\\"Phase 2\\\" renewal`. Each subsequent rename doubles the backslashes again; the true title is unrecoverable from the file without knowing how many rename cycles occurred.

**Suggested fix.** Unescape in frontmatter() (src/main/recall.ts:12-21): when the value is a double-quoted scalar, strip the outer quotes and then apply `.replace(/\\(["\\])/g, '$1')` before returning. Extend the recall.test.ts:459 regression block with titles containing `"` and `\` asserting `read.title === title` after two consecutive renames.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED by executing the real code, not just reading it. I bundled src/main/transcripts.ts + src/main/recall.ts with esbuild (electron and ./store stubbed; nothing written into the repo) and drove the actual saveMeeting -> listMeetings/recallRead -> renameMeeting path. Output: title 'Renault "Phase 2" renewal' is written correctly as `title: "Renault \"Phase 2\" renewal"` (src/main/transcripts.ts:689 via yamlSafeTitle at :565-566) with a correct unescaped H1, but listMeetings and recallRead both return `Renault \"Phase 2\" renewal`; feeding that back through renameMeeting yields `title: "Renault \\\"Phase 2\\\" renewal"`, then 8 backslashes, then 16 — doubling on every rename. 'C:\Users share' behaves identically. Refutation attempts all failed: (1) no unescaper exists anywhere — the only \\/\" regexes in the repo are the two writers, src/main/transcripts.ts:565-566 and src/main/recall.ts:304-306; (2) src/main/recall.ts:18 `kv[2].replace(/^["[]|["\]]$/g,'').trim()` strips only the outer quote/bracket, verified live; (3) no schema guard — RenameMeetingPayloadSchema at src/shared/ipc.ts:1358-1361 only caps length 120, and cleanTitle/sanitizeRenameTitle strip control chars only; (4) the renderer does not sanitize — RecallView.tsx:554 renders {m.title} raw and RecallView.tsx:605 prefills the rename input from that same escaped value, so each Enter re-escapes; (5) renameMeeting's regex ^title:\s*"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"\s*$ (recall.ts:354) keeps matching after every escalation, so the growth is unbounded; (6) reachability is real — parseRecapMarkdown at transcripts.ts:1063-1068 strips only LEADING/TRAILING quotes so an inner pair survives, and a user typing a straight quote into the rename box triggers it directly. The intended-behavior citation is slightly over-broad (recall.test.ts:459-461 is scoped to $-replacement patterns), but the write-side escaping is deliberate and tested (transcripts.test.ts:246 asserts `title: "Said \\"hello\\" to the team"` on disk), so the missing inverse on the read side is unambiguously a defect. Extra blast radius the finder missed: src/main/brain/publish.ts:462-470 is a byte-identical copy of the same parser, so the escaped title also reaches the published wiki note card, and index.ts:2459 re-ingests on rename, propagating it into the knowledge graph; index.md (written unescaped at recall.ts:376) diverges from the frontmatter. Baseline `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/recall.test.ts` passes 27/27, consistent with the finder's note that the existing regression test only covers $-patterns (which contain no quote or backslash). Severity stays medium: display/metadata corruption with unbounded per-rename growth (and the 120-char cap eventually truncates the real title away), but no transcript-data loss and no security impact. Fix is small: one unescape step (strip outer quotes, then replace /\\(["\\])/g with '$1') applied to both duplicated parsers at recall.ts:18 and publish.ts:468, plus a quote/backslash round-trip test next to recall.test.ts:459. One incidental observation: renaming a plain title to the identical string returns 'Could not find a title to rename in this file.' because the replacement produces an identical block (recall.ts:355) — a separate minor no-op quirk, not this bug.

### MQA-079 — Manual "Check for updates" bypasses all three update-channel guards (Cahê edition, Microsoft Store package, IT disableAutoUpdate kill-switch)

**Where.** `src/main/updater.ts:74` · workflow: Settings → About → Updates on a Cahê pilot, a Store/AppX package, or a fleet frozen by managed-config · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/cahe-edition.ts:84 — "/** Cahê is an isolated pilot package and must never consume the shared Métis release feed. */". docs/cahe-windows-edition.md:11 — "The Cahê app does not use the shared Métis auto-update feed. New Cahê builds must be distributed as new Cahê installers." src/main/updater.ts:9-11 — "Enterprise governance: IT can freeze the version fleet-wide by deploying an admin managed-config with `{ \"disableAutoUpdate\": true }` … so a standard user cannot turn their own updates on or off." src/main/updater.ts:122-124 — "The Store (MSIX/AppX) build must never self-update: updating a packaged app is the Store's job, and a packaged app installing software outside its own package is a certification violation."

**Actual.** All three guards (`shouldDisableAutoUpdate()` at updater.ts:109, `process.windowsStore` at updater.ts:130, `autoUpdateDisabledByPolicy()` at updater.ts:135) live only inside `initAutoUpdate`. `checkForUpdateNow()` (updater.ts:74-96) queries `RELEASES_API` = the shared `mysticalsin/Metis-Releases` feed (updater.ts:35) with no edition, Store, or policy check. It is exposed unconditionally at src/main/index.ts:3844 (`ipcMain.handle(IPC.updateCheck, ...)`) and the renderer runs it automatically, not just on click: src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:3411-3413 `useEffect(() => { check() }, [check])`. There is no `isCaheEdition` reference anywhere in Settings.tsx or App.tsx.

**Repro.** Install Metis-Windows-Cahe-Setup-1.5.3.exe (its profile lives in %APPDATA%\Metis Windows Cahe with the seeded Kimi key). Publish 1.5.4 to Metis-Releases. Open Settings → About: the Updates row auto-fires and renders "Version 1.5.4 is available — open the download page" linking to the standard Métis Setup (Settings.tsx:3425-3433). The pilot user installs it and now runs standard Métis (appId com.mantu.asktoto, profile %APPDATA%\Metis) — a different app with an empty profile, no seeded key, and none of their pilot state — while the Cahê install sits unchanged. Same row on a fleet where IT deployed `{"disableAutoUpdate": true}`: the frozen version is advertised as out-of-date with a working download link, so any standard user can defeat the fleet freeze. Same row on the Store/AppX package: it advertises the out-of-band NSIS installer.

**Suggested fix.** Move the three guards into a shared `updatesAllowed()` predicate used by BOTH initAutoUpdate and checkForUpdateNow. Have checkForUpdateNow return a distinct non-error result (e.g. `{ ok: true, current, managed: true }`) so the Settings row can say "Updates are managed by your organisation" / "Update this pilot with a new Cahê installer" / "Updates come from the Microsoft Store" instead of linking to the wrong feed. Add a test alongside the existing configDisablesAutoUpdate cases in updater.test.ts.

**Verifier.** Could not refute it. Reproduced the full chain at HEAD.

checkForUpdateNow (src/main/updater.ts:74-96) fetches RELEASES_API (updater.ts:35 = the shared mysticalsin/Metis-Releases feed, a plain module const with no build-time define override — electron.vite.config.ts has no define block, and the const is referenced only at updater.ts:79) with no edition, Store, or policy check. All three guards are strictly inside initAutoUpdate: shouldDisableAutoUpdate() at updater.ts:109, process.windowsStore at updater.ts:130, autoUpdateDisabledByPolicy() at updater.ts:135. Repo-wide grep: shouldDisableAutoUpdate has exactly one call site (updater.ts:109); isCaheEdition appears only under src/main/, never in the renderer.

Exposure is unconditional: src/main/index.ts:3913 (finder cited 3844 — line drift, same handler) does `ipcMain.handle(IPC.updateCheck, (e) => { assertMainWindow(e); return checkForUpdateNow() })`; assertMainWindow validates the sender, not policy. src/preload/index.ts:294 exposes it unconditionally. Settings.tsx:3411-3413 auto-fires on mount, 3422-3431 renders the download anchor, and Settings.tsx:5008 renders <UpdatesSection /> inside `{tab === 'about' && …}` with no conditional wrapper.

Cahê really does hit the case: electron-builder.cahe.win.yml does `extends: ./electron-builder.win.yml` and inherits package.json "version": "1.5.3", so a 1.5.4 Métis release makes isNewerVersion true for the pilot. Both intent quotes are verbatim and mean what the finder says (cahe-edition.ts:84 "must never consume the shared Métis release feed"; docs/cahe-windows-edition.md:11 "does not use the shared Métis auto-update feed").

Tests do not cover it: ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/updater.test.ts src/main/cahe-edition.test.ts => 14/14 pass, but they only exercise pure semver/parse/never-throw behavior. Nothing asserts an edition/Store/policy guard on the manual path.

Severity corrected high -> medium. Two of the three legs are weaker than claimed. (a) disableAutoUpdate: the quoted intent ("a standard user cannot turn their own updates on or off") remains true — the auto-download/install path IS frozen; the row only surfaces a public GitHub link the user could reach in a browser regardless. perMachine: false (electron-builder.yml:204) means self-install needs no admin, so the row lowers friction rather than breaking a technical control. (b) Store: the finder's own quote says "installing software outside its own package is a certification violation" — rendering a hyperlink is not installing. (c) The Cahê leg is solid and unrefuted: a documented, code-commented invariant is violated unconditionally, the feed is contacted on every About open, and the pilot is offered a different app's installer (com.mantu.asktoto / %APPDATA%\Metis vs com.mantu.metis.windows-cahe / %APPDATA%\Metis Windows Cahe). No data loss though — initializeCaheEditionIdentity() keeps the pilot profile isolated, so the outcome is a confused user in an empty second app. No auto-install, no code execution, no security boundary broken => medium, not high.

Fix: guard checkForUpdateNow (or the IPC handler) with the same three conditions; a clean fix also wants a renderer-visible flag so the Updates row is hidden rather than showing an error, which is the only reason this is small rather than trivial.

### MQA-080 — redactSecrets misses every sk- key with a dashed prefix (sk-kimi-, sk-proj-, sk-or-v1-), so the app's own shipped Kimi key survives into crash-*.log and audit.log

**Where.** `src/shared/redact.ts:44` · workflow: Writing a crash dump / audit line after a provider failure; redacting a transcript before cloud egress · fix size: trivial · **regression**

**Intended.** docs/asktoto-hardening-backlog.md:35 (item marked `[x]` done) — "_accept:_ A crash whose error message embeds an `sk-`/Bearer token writes `[redacted key]` to the dump, and stale crash logs are capped." src/main/index.ts:1161-1164 — "Redact BEFORE writing to any sink — an error stack/message routinely embeds the data involved in the failing operation, so mainLog and auditLog (both persistent) must never see the raw value, same as the crash-*.log dump below."

**Actual.** src/shared/redact.ts:44 is `/\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b/g` — the character class excludes `-`, so it only matches flat `sk-<20+ alnum>` keys. The repo's own Kimi key format is `sk-kimi-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}` (src/main/cahe-embedded-key.ts:11; placeholder `'sk-kimi-…'` at src/shared/providers.ts:171), and Kimi is a first-class provider in the standard build, not just Cahê. Only the `sk-ant-` prefix (line 43) is special-cased. Line 50's Bearer pattern catches the key ONLY when it is literally preceded by `Bearer `.

**Repro.** Verified by running the three redact.ts key patterns against sample inputs: `"sk-kimi-AbCdEf0123456789xyz"` → unchanged; `"sk-proj-AbCdEf0123456789xyzQWERTY"` → unchanged; `"sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123"` → unchanged; `"Bearer sk-kimi-AbCdEf0123456789xyz"` → `"[redacted key]"`; `"sk-0123456789abcdefghijklmno"` → `"[redacted key]"`. So a Kimi 4xx whose error message embeds the bare key (or a stack frame carrying the request URL/config object) reaches persistCrash (src/main/index.ts:1166-1177) and is written verbatim to `<userData>\crash-<ts>-<seq>.log` (mode 0o600 is a no-op on Windows per win-security.ts:13) and to `logs/audit.log`. On the Cahê pilot that key is the shared, installer-embedded one.

**Suggested fix.** Broaden the generic pattern to cover dashed prefixes, e.g. `/\bsk-(?:[A-Za-z0-9]+-)*[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\b/g` (or add explicit `sk-kimi-`, `sk-proj-`, `sk-or-v1-` alternatives), and add redact.test.ts cases for each shipped provider's documented key shape in src/shared/providers.ts so a new provider prefix cannot be added without redaction coverage.

**Verifier.** Could not refute. (1) The regex is exactly as claimed: src/shared/redact.ts:44 is /\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b/g, whose character class excludes '-'. Running the three key patterns standalone confirms sk-kimi-…, sk-proj-…, and sk-or-v1-… all pass through unchanged, while flat sk-<20 alnum> and "Bearer sk-kimi-…" are redacted. Only sk-ant- is special-cased (line 43). Line 44's own comment claims "OpenAI + generic sk- keys", which is false for OpenAI's current sk-proj- project keys.

(2) The intended-behavior quotes check out verbatim. docs/asktoto-hardening-backlog.md:35 is marked [x] with "_accept:_ A crash whose error message embeds an sk-/Bearer token writes [redacted key] to the dump". src/main/index.ts:1161-1164 carries the "Redact BEFORE writing to any sink" comment as quoted.

(3) The key format is confirmed in-repo: src/main/cahe-embedded-key.ts:11 KIMI_KEY_PATTERN = /sk-kimi-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}/; src/shared/providers.ts:171-172 keyHint 'sk-kimi-…' / keyPattern '^sk-kimi-'; openrouter at :192-193 is '^sk-or-'. Kimi is a first-class provider, not Cahe-only.

(4) No other guard exists. redactSecrets is the only scrubber in the repo (grep for scrub/mask/sanitize yields only unrelated recall/transcript title sanitizers). src/main/logger.ts applies no redaction — mainLog and auditLog write raw. src/shared/redact.test.ts passes 7/7 (vitest run, green) but has zero sk-kimi/sk-proj/sk-or coverage, so nothing regression-guards it.

(5) redactSensitive defaults to true (src/shared/ipc.ts:840 schema default, :1138 defaults object), so the egress path is live by default rather than opt-in.

(6) The strongest reachable sink is cloud egress, not the crash log. src/main/index.ts:2783 redacts the screen-OCR description under an explicit comment: "the description can be a VERBATIM OCR extract of the screen — an open password manager or API key must be stripped before this text reaches a cloud answer provider." A key visible on screen or spoken into the transcript (:2748) reaches a third-party model unredacted. That requires no assumption about error-message contents.

Where the finder overreaches: the headline "the shipped Kimi key survives into crash-*.log" needs an error object to embed the bare key, which I could not demonstrate. src/main/cahe-embedded-key.ts never logs the key value (comment at :91 states this and the code honors it); OpenAI SDK APIError messages carry a response body that upstream providers usually mask, and stack frames carry no values. When a key does appear as apiKey: "…" rule 3 (redact.ts:57-60) catches it — though util.inspect's single-quoted apiKey: 'sk-kimi-…' escapes rule 3 too, since [^\s"'] cannot start on a quote. So the crash-dump framing is plausible-but-unproven while the egress framing is solid; the defect itself (the redactor fails the exact behavior its acceptance criterion and inline comment assert) survives either way.

Supporting detail also holds: src/main/win-security.ts:12-14 documents that mode 0o600 is a no-op on Windows, and persistCrash (src/main/index.ts:1186-1195) never calls lockPathToCurrentUserWin32 on the crash file.

Severity medium is correct — defense-in-depth redaction gap, conditional exposure, no direct exploit, but default-on and covering the exact key format the product itself ships. Fix is trivial: widen the class to [A-Za-z0-9_-] (ordering with the sk-ant- rule is already safe) plus a unit test for sk-kimi-/sk-proj-/sk-or-v1-.

### MQA-081 — Screen capture can send the wrong monitor with no notice — displayMismatch is never emitted, so the documented soft "captured a different monitor" warning is dead code and the dispId guard is a tautology

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:1261` · workflow: ask about my screen on a multi-monitor setup · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/shared/ipc.ts:1624-1626 — "/** True when the captured monitor didn't match the cursor's display (fell back to sources[0]); the renderer surfaces a soft \"captured a different monitor\" notice. */ displayMismatch: z.boolean().optional()".  And src/main/index.ts:1259-1260 — "Surfaced to the caller (not just audited) so the renderer can show a soft \"wrong screen?\" notice instead of silently answering about a monitor the user didn't ask about."  The renderer half already exists: src/renderer/src/App.tsx:59-64 (`CAPTURE_DISPLAY_MISMATCH_NOTICE`, `hasDisplayMismatch`) consumed at App.tsx:864 and App.tsx:947.

**Actual.** `displayMismatch` is computed at src/main/index.ts:1261 and then thrown away: the >1-source branch throws (index.ts:1267) instead of falling back to sources[0], and the flag is never put on the returned object. `CapturedScreen` (index.ts:1223) has no such field and `getScreenshot` (index.ts:1304, return at 1346) returns only `{image, width, height, capturedAt}`, so `hasDisplayMismatch(shot)` at App.tsx:864/947 is always false and the notice can never render. Separately, `captureScreenshotOnce` returns `dispId: disp.id` (index.ts:1289) — the REQUESTED id, never the captured source's id — so the safety check `if (shot.dispId !== disp.id) throw ...` at index.ts:1333 can never fire.

**Repro.** Two monitors, cursor on monitor B, screen-ask enabled. `getScreenSourcesWithRetry` (src/main/screen-capture.ts:33-49) drops zero-pixel sources and returns as soon as `usable.length` is non-zero — so if B's thumbnail comes back 0x0 on the first attempt (display asleep/waking, HDR mode switch, protected content) while A's is fine, it returns `[A]` with length 1. At index.ts:1258 `matched` is undefined; at 1261 `displayMismatch = !matched && sources.length > 1` = false (length is 1); at 1269 `src = sources[0]` = monitor A. Line 1289 stamps `dispId: disp.id` (= B), so index.ts:1333 passes and the frame is cached under B's id. Monitor A's screenshot is uploaded to the vision provider, labelled "Viewed screen", with zero indication the wrong screen was sent. The complementary case (3 monitors, cursor's source filtered out, 2 usable sources left, no match) takes index.ts:1267 and hard-fails the ask with "Métis could not identify the selected display" — which App.tsx:891 does not classify as a permission error, so it silently degrades to a text-only answer (App.tsx:899).

**Suggested fix.** Make `CapturedScreen`/`getScreenshot`/`CaptureResult` actually carry the flag: set `displayMismatch = !matched` (any source count), return `dispId: src.display_id` (the id actually captured, not the requested one) so the index.ts:1333 guard becomes real, and replace the index.ts:1267 throw with the documented `sources[0]` fallback + `displayMismatch: true`. Add a unit test that a 2-source list with no matching display_id yields `displayMismatch: true` rather than a throw, and one that a filtered single-source list from a different display also flags the mismatch.

**Verifier.** I tried to refute this three ways (another emitter, a caller/handler that enriches the payload, a test or schema default) and could not.

VERIFIED — `displayMismatch` is never emitted:
- Repo-wide grep for `displayMismatch` returns exactly four sites: src/shared/ipc.ts:1634 (schema field), src/renderer/src/App.tsx:64/864/947 (consumer), and src/main/index.ts:1272-1273 (producer). Nothing else.
- src/main/index.ts:1272 `const displayMismatch = !matched && sources.length > 1` is consumed ONLY by the `if` on 1273, which audits and throws (1278). It never reaches a return value.
- `CapturedScreen` (index.ts:1234) is `{image, width, height, dispId}` — no such field. `captureScreenshotOnce` returns exactly that shape at index.ts:1300. `getScreenshot`'s signature (index.ts:1315) and both returns (1330, 1357) are `{image, width, height, capturedAt}`.
- The IPC handler is a bare pass-through: `ipcMain.handle(IPC.captureScreen, … => getScreenshot())` at index.ts:2684-2688. No enrichment, no schema default (the field is `.optional()` with no `.default()`).
=> `hasDisplayMismatch(shot)` at App.tsx:864/947 is unconditionally false; CAPTURE_DISPLAY_MISMATCH_NOTICE is unreachable. The renderer's own comment at App.tsx:61-63 admits it ("isn't declared on CaptureResult yet … once main starts sending it") — main never started.

VERIFIED — the guard is a tautology: index.ts:1300 stamps `dispId: disp.id`, where `disp` is looked up by the `displayId` argument (1237). `captureScreenshot` is keyed single-flight on that same id (1304, screen-capture.ts:55-71), and `getScreenshot` calls it with `disp.id` (1334). So `shot.dispId === disp.id` always, and `if (shot.dispId !== disp.id) throw` at index.ts:1344 can never fire. It cannot catch the wrong-monitor case it exists for.

VERIFIED — git shows this is a half-landed change, not a deliberate design: `git log -S displayMismatch` returns ONE commit (4b2a98a) touching all three files. Its main-process diff is a pure rename of the existing `if (!matched && sources.length > 1)` into a named const plus the comment "Surfaced to the caller (not just audited)…" — the throw was left in place and the field was never threaded through. So the intended-behavior quotes say what the finder claims, and the code contradicts both of them (the schema even documents a "fell back to sources[0]" path that main deliberately does not take).

PLAUSIBLE (not provable from source) — the wrong-monitor send: `getScreenSourcesWithRetry` (screen-capture.ts:41-42) filters zero-pixel sources and returns on the first non-empty result, so a multi-monitor box where only the cursor's source comes back 0x0 yields `usable.length === 1`; then `matched` is undefined, `displayMismatch` is false (length not > 1), and index.ts:1280 `src = sources[0]` sends the other monitor. index.ts:1266-1268's stated invariant ("With one available source it is necessarily the requested display") was true before the usable-source filter (added later, commit 5715d00) and is no longer enforced. The repo believes 0x0 sources are real (that's why isUsableScreenSource exists, screen-capture.ts:22-26), but nothing proves the per-source-asymmetric case occurs, and no test covers the matching logic at all (src/main/screen-capture.test.ts — 6 tests, all pass, none touch display routing).

FINDER OVERSTATEMENT (does not kill the finding): the ">1 sources, no match" branch is NOT a silent degradation. App.tsx:892-900 sets a visible captureError ("Couldn't capture your screen. Answering from context only.") on the non-permission path, and App.tsx:910 strips a screen-asserting label so the UI never claims "Viewed screen". `isScreenCapturePermissionError` (src/shared/screen-capture.ts:5-7) indeed doesn't match that message, but the consequence is an announced text-only answer, not a silent one.

Severity corrected high -> medium: the certain half (dead notice + tautological guard + schema comment describing behavior that doesn't exist) has no runtime harm, and the half that does carry harm — a silent upload of the wrong monitor to a vision provider, then cached under the wrong dispId at index.ts:1354 for CAPTURE_TTL_MS — depends on a narrow, unproven precondition. Fix is small: add the field to CapturedScreen/getScreenshot's return, stamp dispId from the captured source rather than the request, and treat a single surviving source whose non-empty display_id doesn't match as a mismatch instead of assuming it must be right.

### MQA-082 — A desk-tap zone bound to "Hide / show Métis" can only hide — the renderer's 'hide' branch calls the one-way hide IPC instead of the toggle

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1963` · workflow: hide/show the overlay with a desk tap · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/TapCalibration.tsx:28 — "{ value: 'hide', label: 'Hide / show Métis' }".  The same HotkeyAction is a toggle everywhere else: src/main/index.ts:1503 — "hide: () => toggleVisible()," and the tray item "{ label: label('Show / Hide', 'hide'), click: toggleVisible }" (src/main/index.ts, buildTrayMenu). Settings labels it "Show / hide" (src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:6239).

**Actual.** src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1963 — `else if (a === 'hide') void window.toto.hide()`. `window.toto.hide()` (src/preload/index.ts:279) invokes `IPC.windowHide`, whose handler is `win?.hide()` (src/main/index.ts:3831-3834) — a one-way hide with no show branch. The toggle IPC exists and is unused here: `toggle: () => ipcRenderer.invoke(IPC.windowToggle)` (src/preload/index.ts:280) → `toggleVisible()` (src/main/index.ts:3835). This branch is only reachable from Desk Tap Control, because the keyboard/tray paths handle 'hide' entirely in main and never send it to the renderer.

**Repro.** Settings → Desk Tap Control: calibrate 2 zones and set zone 2's action to "Hide / show Métis". Start a meeting (default `armOnlyWhileListening`). Tap zone 2 → App.tsx:1963 → `win.hide()`; the overlay disappears along with the recording timer and Pause/Stop. Tap zone 2 again → the renderer is still running (`backgroundThrottling:false` + `disable-renderer-backgrounding`), so the tap is recognized and dispatches again, but `win?.hide()` on an already-hidden window is a no-op. The overlay never comes back by tap; recovery requires the Ctrl+\ global hotkey or the tray.

**Suggested fix.** Change App.tsx:1963 to `void window.toto.toggle()` so the renderer-side 'hide' action matches the keyboard/tray semantics of the same HotkeyAction. Add a contract test asserting that the renderer's 'hide' hotkey branch calls the toggle channel, not the hide channel.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; reproduced the full chain independently. (1) Code confirmed verbatim: src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1963 `else if (a === 'hide') void window.toto.hide()`; src/preload/index.ts:279 `hide: () => ipcRenderer.invoke(IPC.windowHide)` vs :280 `toggle: () => ipcRenderer.invoke(IPC.windowToggle)`; src/main/index.ts:3884-3887 `ipcMain.handle(IPC.windowHide, ...) { win?.hide() }` vs :3888-3891 `ipcMain.handle(IPC.windowToggle, ...) { toggleVisible() }` (finder cited 3831-3835 — line numbers drift ~53, content exact). toggleVisible() itself is at src/main/index.ts:1496-1510. (2) Intended-behavior quotes are accurate: src/renderer/src/components/TapCalibration.tsx:28 `{ value: 'hide', label: 'Hide / show Métis' }`; src/main/index.ts:1514 `hide: () => toggleVisible(),`; :1682 tray `{ label: label('Show / Hide', 'hide'), click: toggleVisible }`; Settings.tsx SHORTCUT_LABELS `hide: 'Show / hide'`. (3) Reachability confirmed: grep across src/main finds no `sendHotkey('hide')` and no other send of IPC.hotkey 'hide' — keyboard and tray resolve 'hide' entirely in main, so App.tsx:1998-2004 (useTapControl onZone -> handlersRef.current) is the only caller of the renderer's 'hide' branch. (4) No guard/schema stops it: src/shared/ipc.ts:933 `zoneActions: z.array(z.string()).max(4)` has no action allowlist, HOTKEY_ACTIONS includes 'hide' (ipc.ts:1175), and App.tsx:1952/:1956 explicitly exempt 'hide' from both dispatch gates. (5) Tap stays armed while hidden: no `win.on('hide')` handler exists in src/main/index.ts, `disable-renderer-backgrounding` is set at :331 and `backgroundThrottling: false` at :609, and useTapControl's effect (src/renderer/src/lib/tap/tap-control.ts:209-238) keys only on active/profile/micDeviceId/sensitivity — nothing tears it down or stops listening on hide. The visibilitychange listener at src/renderer/src/state.ts:684 is the permissions poll, irrelevant. (6) No recovery path in the renderer: grep for `toto.toggle` / `windowShow` across src/renderer and src/preload shows `toggle` is exposed but never called anywhere, and no other zone action calls show — so a second tap is a genuine no-op and only Ctrl+\ or the tray restores the overlay. (7) No test pins it: no test file references toto.hide, windowToggle, windowHide, handlersRef, onZone, or tapControl, so there is nothing to run that covers this. Severity medium is right: opt-in, calibration-gated feature with an easy escape hatch (global hotkey/tray), but the action's own label promises a toggle and mid-meeting it hides the recording timer and Pause/Stop with no tap-based way back. Fix is trivial and must be scoped to the tap path only — special-case 'hide' in onZone to `window.toto.toggle()` — because the other two `window.toto.hide()` sites (App.tsx:2062 Escape, :2684) are correctly one-way dismissals.

### MQA-083 — Changing the microphone silently kills Desk Tap Control — onProfileMismatch is never passed, so the documented "recalibrate" prompt never appears

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1991` · workflow: use Desk Tap Control after switching microphones · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/lib/tap/tap-control.ts:192-193 — "/** Profile was calibrated on a different mic/rate — surface a \"recalibrate\" prompt. */ onProfileMismatch?: () => void". The hook honours it at tap-control.ts:212-215: "// Mic identity is part of the acoustic model — a different mic has a different transfer function." then `mismatchRef.current?.(); return`.

**Actual.** The single production call site, src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1991-2005, passes only `active`, `profile`, `micDeviceId`, `sensitivity` and `onZone` — `onProfileMismatch` is omitted, so `mismatchRef.current` (tap-control.ts:204-205) is `undefined` and tap-control.ts:213 is an optional-call no-op. Grep across src/renderer confirms `onProfileMismatch` appears nowhere outside tap-control.ts, and TapCalibration.tsx computes no mic-mismatch state of its own. The effect then `return`s without starting a session and without any cleanup, so the feature is simply off.

**Repro.** Enable Desk Tap Control and calibrate while on the system default mic — TapCalibration.tsx:123 stamps `profile.micDeviceId = settings.micDeviceId || 'default'` = 'default'. Later pick an explicit input (e.g. a USB headset) in Settings → Audio, so `settings.micDeviceId = 'abc123'`. On the next render App.tsx:1996 passes `micDeviceId: 'abc123'`; tap-control.ts:212 evaluates `'default' !== ('abc123' ?? 'default')` → true → calls the undefined `mismatchRef.current` → returns. From then on no desk tap does anything, while Settings still shows Desk Tap Control enabled with a saved profile and no warning anywhere in the UI.

**Suggested fix.** Pass an `onProfileMismatch` from App.tsx that sets a state flag surfaced in the Bar/Settings ("Desk Tap Control is paused — recalibrate for this microphone"), and mirror it in TapCalibration.tsx so the Recalibrate button is the obvious next step. Add a test that a profile/mic mismatch invokes the callback and starts no capture session.

**Verifier.** Could not refute. (1) Intended-behavior quote verified verbatim at src/renderer/src/lib/tap/tap-control.ts:192-193 ("Profile was calibrated on a different mic/rate — surface a \"recalibrate\" prompt." / onProfileMismatch?: () => void), honoured at 212-215 by an early `return` that skips startTapControl. (2) Grep over all of src/ finds `onProfileMismatch` at only tap-control.ts:193,204,205 and `useTapControl` at only App.tsx:32 (import) and App.tsx:1991 (single production call site) — that call passes active/profile/micDeviceId/sensitivity/onZone and omits onProfileMismatch; the prop is optional so TS raises nothing, and mismatchRef.current is undefined making tap-control.ts:213 a no-op. (3) The id divergence is real: TapCalibration.tsx:123 stamps `settings.micDeviceId || 'default'` while App.tsx:1996 passes `settings?.micDeviceId || undefined`; Settings.tsx:3357-3363 uses value="" for "System default" and a real deviceId otherwise, and ipc.ts:759 defaults micDeviceId to ''. Calibrating on default stores 'default'; later selecting a device makes tap-control.ts:212 evaluate 'default' !== ('abc123' ?? 'default') → true → early return, feature permanently off. (4) No compensating path: `tapControl` appears outside the tap files only at App.tsx:1990 and the ipc.ts schema (925-955) — no main-process invalidation or normalization; TapCalibration.tsx:168 renders "Calibrated and ready." purely on `tc.profile` truthiness and compares nothing against settings.micDeviceId; the only "recalibrate" strings are the button label (236, 310) and the separability-failure copy (307), neither reachable here. (5) No test guards it — there is no tap-control.test.ts; the seven tap tests cover calibrate/classify/features/fft/gates/onset/worklet only, none import useTapControl. Minor correction to the finder: "returns ... without any cleanup" is imprecise — React runs the prior effect's cleanup (tap-control.ts:233-237) before re-running, so the old session is stopped and the mic released; nothing leaks, the feature is just dead. Bonus defect in the same expression (out of scope): the reverse switch passes undefined and `micDeviceId ?? profile.micDeviceId` makes the check self-equal, so a profile calibrated on a USB mic silently runs against the default mic. Severity medium confirmed — silent permanent loss of an opt-in feature while the UI asserts it works, no data loss or security impact. Fix is small: the mismatch is a pure derived value TapControlCard can compute from settings.tapControl.profile.micDeviceId vs settings.micDeviceId || 'default', plus normalizing the ''/'default'/undefined comparison across App.tsx:1996, TapCalibration.tsx:123 and tap-control.ts:212.

### MQA-084 — Tap Control tears down and re-acquires its microphone on every settings refresh, and leaks a capturing keydown listener each time the capture fails

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/lib/tap/tap-control.ts:238` · workflow: keep Desk Tap Control armed during a meeting · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/lib/tap/tap-control.ts:196-198 — "Lifecycle hook: arms/disarms the pipeline as `active`/profile/mic/sensitivity change." The session owns exactly one release path for the keydown listener — tap-control.ts:177-181: "stop() { window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey, true); cap.stop() }" — and the hook's failure comment at tap-control.ts:230-232 assumes it happens at most once: "/* mic denied or worklet failed — feature silently unavailable this session */". The session also exposes `setSensitivity` (tap-control.ts:124, 176) for in-place adjustment, which the hook never calls.

**Actual.** The effect deps are `[active, profile, micDeviceId, sensitivity]` (tap-control.ts:238) where `profile` is `settings.tapControl.profile` (App.tsx:1995) — an object that comes fresh over IPC on every settings read. `useSettings` replaces the whole settings object on every `refresh()` (src/renderer/src/state.ts:504) and every `patch()` (state.ts:549), and `refresh()` is wired to the DOM `focus` event (state.ts:541-542). So each window focus / settings save gives `profile` a new identity, re-running the effect: cleanup stops the session and `startTapControl` re-runs `getUserMedia` + `new AudioContext()` + `audioWorklet.addModule` (tap-control.ts:65-78). `window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey, true)` is registered at tap-control.ts:139 BEFORE the awaited capture; when that capture rejects, the `.catch` at tap-control.ts:230 swallows it and no `stop()` ever runs, so the listener is never removed.

**Repro.** (a) Churn: enable Desk Tap Control with `armOnlyWhileListening` on, start a meeting, then click the Métis overlay (Pause, a quick action, the eye button — each fires a DOM focus and/or a `patch()`). Every one of those replaces `settings`, re-runs the effect, closes the AudioContext and re-opens the mic; taps in the ~100-400 ms re-acquisition window are dropped and `makeTrainGate()` (tap-control.ts:134) restarts its typing-train state from scratch. (b) Leak: deny microphone permission with Desk Tap Control enabled and armed. Every focus event adds one more capturing `keydown` listener on `window` that is never released — 50 focus events leave 50 listeners, all invoked on every keystroke.

**Suggested fix.** Depend on stable primitives, not object identity — key the effect on `profile.version`/`profile.calibratedAt` (or a memoized JSON hash) plus `micDeviceId`, and drop `sensitivity` from the deps in favour of a separate effect that calls the already-exposed `sessionRef.current?.setSensitivity(sensitivity)`. In `startTapControl`, register the keydown listener only after `startTapCapture` resolves, or wrap the await in try/finally and remove the listener on the failure path.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; both mechanisms independently reproduce in the code.

CHURN CHAIN (all links verified):
- src/shared/ipc.ts:934-948 — `tapControl.profile` is a nested zod object (version/sampleRate/mean/std/zones/negatives/dAccept/levelRange/createdAt), not a scalar, so it carries object identity.
- src/preload/index.ts:64 — `getSettings: () => ipcRenderer.invoke(IPC.settingsGet)`; structured clone across processes yields a brand-new object graph on every call. No caching layer.
- src/renderer/src/state.ts:504 (`refresh` → `setSettings(await window.toto.getSettings())`) and :549 (`patch` → `setSettings(await window.toto.setSettings(p))`) both replace the whole settings object. state.ts:541-542 registers `window.addEventListener('focus', onFocus)` where `onFocus = () => void refresh()`; `refresh` is `useCallback([])`-stable so it is attached once and lives for the app's lifetime.
- src/renderer/src/App.tsx:1990 `const tapCfg = settings?.tapControl` and :1995 `profile: (tapCfg?.profile as TapProfile | null) ?? null` — passed straight through, no useMemo/memoization anywhere.
- src/renderer/src/lib/tap/tap-control.ts:238 — deps `[active, profile, micDeviceId, sensitivity]`. `active` is boolean, `micDeviceId` string, `sensitivity` number — all stable by value. Only `profile` is unstable, and it is unstable on EVERY settings read. Effect re-runs → cleanup `sessionRef.current?.stop()` → `startTapControl` → `startTapCapture` re-runs `getUserMedia` (tap-control.ts:65-70), `new AudioContext()` (:71), `ctx.audioWorklet.addModule` (:73).

Two facts strengthen it beyond the finder's claim: (1) `patch()` fires unattended during a live listening session — App.tsx:212 `asrLastFallbackAt`, :226 `asrWebgpuFallbackAt`, :243 `micOnlyFallbackAt` — so the re-arm churn does not require any user click; (2) `makeTrainGate()` (gates.ts:153-165) holds `times[]` + `coolUntil` typing-train state that is discarded on every re-arm, so an in-progress typing cooldown is dropped. That is a correctness effect (a keystroke-adjacent false-positive tap can slip through right after a focus/patch), not merely a dropped-tap window.

LEAK CHAIN (verified): tap-control.ts:139 `window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey, true)` runs synchronously BEFORE `await startTapCapture(...)` at :141. The only removal is inside `stop()` at :178, reachable only via a resolved `TapControlSession`. When capture rejects (both getUserMedia attempts fail, or `addModule` throws at :73-78), the `.catch` at :230-232 swallows it, `sessionRef.current` is never assigned at :228, and the cleanup's `sessionRef.current?.stop()` at :235 is a no-op. One orphaned capturing listener per effect run, unbounded, each retaining the closure over `train`/`opts` (profile + onEvent → App scope).

REFUTATIONS ATTEMPTED AND FAILED:
- No memoization of settings/tapCfg/profile in App.tsx (read 1960-2005; grep for useMemo around it found none).
- Overlay window is focusable: src/main/index.ts:960-985 has no `focusable: false`, and `acceptFirstMouse: true` — Chromium fires window `focus` on activation, so state.ts:541 genuinely triggers.
- The mic-mismatch early return at tap-control.ts:212 does not short-circuit the normal case: `profile.micDeviceId !== (micDeviceId ?? profile.micDeviceId)` is false when micDeviceId is undefined or equal.
- The `gen` counter at :217/:227 does correctly stop late-resolving sessions, so AudioContexts do NOT accumulate — but it does nothing for the keydown listener, which is added outside the session object's lifetime.
- `setSensitivity` (tap-control.ts:124, 176) has zero callers outside onset.test.ts (grep across src), confirming the hook never uses the in-place adjustment path the API exists for.
- No test guards this: `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/lib/tap` → 7 files / 50 tests all pass, and none import `startTapControl` or `useTapControl` (only calibrate.test.ts imports the `TapCandidatePayload` type).

SEVERITY: medium is correct. Not high — the feature is off by default (ipc.ts:927 `enabled: false`), requires successful calibration for `profile` to be non-null, and the listener leak additionally requires mic denial/device-busy after calibration. Not low — in the feature's primary armed workflow the mic is torn down and re-acquired on every window focus and every settings patch (including unattended ones), dropping taps and resetting the anti-typing gate.

FIX COMPLEXITY: small. Memoize/key the effect on a stable profile identity (e.g. `profile.createdAt` + `micDeviceId`, or a `useMemo` on the serialized profile) instead of the raw object; and either move the `addEventListener` at :139 to after the await, or wrap the capture in try/catch that removes the listener on failure.

### MQA-085 — settleCommitment and setDealOutcome bypass withEntityLock, so an in-flight ingest silently reverts a just-settled promise or a just-closed deal

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:981` · workflow: settle a promise / mark a deal won-lost while a meeting is being indexed · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/brain/store.ts:249-255 — "MI-2.5 Fix C: the ONE serialization lane every read-modify-write mutation of `.brain/` entity files (account/person/deal/graph — none of which have their own per-file lock the way index.json has via ingest.ts's own indexLock) must go through. Before this fix, ingest.ts's in-flight backfill/ingest jobs serialized against a PRIVATE module-level `ingestChain` promise that corrections.ts's five correction mutations … never joined — a correction running concurrently with an in-flight backfill could lose an update or resurrect a tombstoned entity."

**Actual.** grep for `withEntityLock` over src/ (tests excluded) shows it wrapping only corrections.ts's five mutations (878, 1093, 1176, 1368, 1435), replayCorrections (1470) and ingest.ts's job-finishing lane (1624). `settleCommitment` (ingest.ts:974-997) does `readDeal` → mutate `row.status` → `await writeDeal`, then loops `listEntities`/`readPerson` → `await writePerson`, entirely outside the lane; `setDealOutcome` (store.ts:444-454) does `readDeal` → `deal.outcome = outcome` → `await writeDeal` outside it too. Their IPC handlers (index.ts:2511, index.ts:3278) add no lock. Meanwhile mergeExtraction, which DOES hold the lane, reads the deal at ingest.ts:788 and only writes it at ingest.ts:903, with `await writeAccount` (ingest.ts:900) in between — a yield point the unlocked handler can run inside.

**Repro.** A meeting finishes transcribing and its live ingest job starts; mergeExtraction has read deal `acme-renewal` (ingest.ts:788) and is awaiting `writeAccount` at ingest.ts:900. In that window the user clicks ✓ (Mark kept) on one of that deal's open promises. settleCommitment reads acme-renewal from disk, sets that row to 'kept', writes it, returns { ok: true }; BrainView refreshes and the row leaves "Open promises". The ingest job then resumes and executes `await writeDeal(s, dslug, deal)` (ingest.ts:903) with its stale in-memory copy — the row is 'open' again. The next 3-10s poll puts the promise back in the rail with no error shown. Identical window for setDealOutcome: a deal marked 'won' reverts to 'open'.

**Suggested fix.** Wrap both bodies in store.ts's `withEntityLock`, matching the five correction mutations: `export async function settleCommitment(...) { return withEntityLock(async () => { … }) }` (ingest.ts:974) and the same for `setDealOutcome` (store.ts:444). While there, clone before mutating (`cloneEntity`, corrections.ts:696-703) — both currently mutate the object readJson returned from its shared cache, so a failed writeDeal leaves the cached entity showing a value that was never persisted.

**Verifier.** STRUCTURAL CLAIM — verified. `grep withEntityLock` over src/ hits only corrections.ts (878, 1093, 1176, 1368, 1435, 1470) and ingest.ts:1624 (`void withEntityLock(() => finishJob(result))`). `settleCommitment` (src/main/brain/ingest.ts:974-997) is readDeal -> `row.status = status` -> `await writeDeal`, then a listEntities/readPerson/`await writePerson` loop, all unlocked; `setDealOutcome` (src/main/brain/store.ts:449-452) is readDeal -> `deal.outcome = outcome` -> `await writeDeal`, unlocked. Their IPC handlers add no lock (src/main/index.ts:2510-2525 for brainCommitmentSettle; the setDealOutcome handler likewise just calls the store fn). The "intended" quote at src/main/brain/store.ts:249-255 does say what the finder claims — every read-modify-write of account/person/deal/graph must go through the one lane. Both run on the same event loop as the ingest pump (ingest.ts:1593-1637, no worker/utility process), and mergeExtraction reads the deal at ingest.ts:788 and writes it at ingest.ts:903 with `await writeAccount` (ingest.ts:900) in between. src/main/transcripts.ts:286-288 even documents "two concurrent writers to the SAME target (e.g. a background brain ingest and an IPC-driven edit both updating one entity file)" — atomicity per write, no RMW serialization.

REFUTATION ATTEMPT — the finder's stated mechanism is WRONG in the default path. store.ts:214-237 returns the CACHED OBJECT BY REFERENCE on a (mtimeMs,size) hit (`return hit.value as T`, and `jsonCache.set(p, {..., value}); return value`), and mergeExtraction mutates that very instance. So in the claimed window the handler's readDeal returns the SAME object the merge holds; `row.status = 'kept'` is therefore included in merge's own writeDeal snapshot. The merge's copy is not stale. `pushUnique` (store.ts:97-99) skips duplicates rather than replacing, so merge's commitment loop cannot overwrite a settled row either.

BUT IT SURVIVES. I wrote a throwaway vitest file (src/main/brain/zz-verifier-scratch.test.ts, run then deleted; `git status` confirms no residue) replicating ingest.ts:788->900->903 with settleCommitment fired in the window: (A) cache warm -> final status 'kept' (finder's repro fails, as predicted); (B) deal cache entry invalidated between the two reads -> 'open' (revert reproduces); (C) using the REAL production trigger — 2100 readJson calls overflowing `JSON_CACHE_MAX` and hitting `if (jsonCache.size >= JSON_CACHE_MAX) jsonCache.clear()` (store.ts:234) inside the window -> final status 'open', the settled promise silently reverted, exactly as claimed. The store.ts:201-206 comment says three pollers re-read the whole dataset every 3-10s, so that clear fires continuously once a brain exceeds ~2000 distinct cached files (entities + one meeting-extraction file per meeting + index/graph/corrections). Nothing else guards it: no busy-check in the handlers, no schema default, no test (outcome.test.ts and e2e-proof.test.ts are single-threaded; corrections.test.ts:949 covers only the corrections side of Fix C). Second, cache-independent window: `.brain` lives inside the meetings folder (store.ts:32-34), which transcripts.ts:292-304 says routinely sits under OneDrive/AV and retries rename on EPERM/EBUSY for up to ~600ms — two unserialized writers to one deal file can then land out of order, and the later rename wins with the older snapshot (losing the ingest's merged meeting/signals instead).

SEVERITY corrected medium -> low: real, but not the "every click during an ingest" exposure the finder describes — it needs a >2000-entry cache clear (or a rename-retry reorder) inside a sub-second window. Worth fixing anyway because the only thing preventing it today is an accidental, undocumented aliasing side effect of a perf cache; the obvious hardening of that cache (clone on read) would turn this into an always-live silent revert. Fix is trivial: wrap both bodies in `withEntityLock` — ingest.ts already imports it (ingest.ts:52), store.ts defines it, and neither function is called from inside the lane, so there is no re-entrancy/deadlock risk.

**FIXED (2026-08-17).** `settleCommitment` took the lane in the 2026-08-08 pass; `setDealOutcome` (src/main/brain/store.ts) now does too — same lane, same reasoning, and its only caller is the `brain:setDealOutcome` IPC handler, never the lane itself, so there is no re-entrancy risk. Both also **clone before mutating** now, which is the part that matters beyond the lock: the verifier showed the current code only survives by accident, because readJson's cache aliases the very object the merge holds, and that the obvious hardening of that cache would turn this into an always-live silent revert. `cloneEntity` moved out of corrections.ts (where it was private) into store.ts beside `withEntityLock` and is now the one implementation all three mutation sites share — store.ts, ingest.ts and corrections.ts — for the same import-cycle reason the lock lives there. Regression tests name MQA-085 for the lane ordering on both mutations and for the aliasing: a reader holding the pre-mutation reference still sees the on-disk value after a settle and a won-mark.

### MQA-086 — testCli(claude-cli) spawns the CLI without `--disallowedTools '*'` and without `--model`, relaxing the file's own "never relax" security invariant and billing the user's default (possibly Opus) model

**Where.** `src/main/cli.ts:653` · workflow: Settings → CLI Integration → Connect / Test connection, and onboarding's CLI tile · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** cli.ts:4-11 header — "SECURITY INVARIANTS (never relax): … - claude-cli: --allowedTools '' --disallowedTools '*' so the agent can never execute arbitrary tools." cli.ts:317-319 — "'--model' is unconditional: an empty model must never silently inherit the user's own CLI default (which can be a premium model) — floor to the cheapest current model instead." cli.ts:652 states the intent to match: "'-p' with no positional arg reads the prompt from stdin (consistent with runCliStream)".

**Actual.** src/main/cli.ts:653 — `testArgs = ['-p', '--output-format', 'text', '--max-turns', '1', '--allowedTools', '']`. Both `--disallowedTools '*'` and `--model` are absent, so the invariant declared for the claude-cli backend holds on the runCliStream path (cli.ts:320-334) but not on the testCli path, even though both spawn the same binary with the same live user login. The codex branch degrades similarly: cli.ts:656-661 falls through to "proceed without a dedicated cwd" when mkdtemp fails, dropping the header's "codex-cli: … runs in a throwaway tmp cwd" guarantee.

**Repro.** A developer whose ~/.claude/settings.json contains `{"permissions":{"defaultMode":"bypassPermissions"}}` (or an explicit `allow` list) clicks Settings → CLI Integration → Connect for Claude Code. testCli spawns `claude -p --output-format text --max-turns 1 --allowedTools ''` in the app's cwd with no deny list, so the auto-approved tools from the user's own config are live for that turn — the exact condition the header forbids. Independently, with the user's Claude Code default model set to Opus, every Connect/Test click (and Onboarding.tsx:555's automatic cliTest) runs a full Opus turn against their subscription instead of the pinned Sonnet that applyInteractiveGuardrail forces on every real ask.

**Suggested fix.** Make testCli reuse the same locked-down arg list: `['-p','--output-format','text','--max-turns','1','--allowedTools','','--disallowedTools','*','--model', PROVIDERS['claude-cli'].fastModel || 'haiku']`. For codex, fail the test with a clear error when mkdtemp fails rather than silently running in the app's cwd. Add a contract test asserting that every claude-cli spawn site in cli.ts contains both `--disallowedTools` and `--model`.

**Verifier.** I tried to refute this and could not. Every factual claim checks out.

CODE AS CLAIMED. `src/main/cli.ts:653` is verbatim `testArgs = ['-p', '--output-format', 'text', '--max-turns', '1', '--allowedTools', '']` — no `--disallowedTools`, no `--model`. The claude-cli branch also leaves `testCwd` undefined (cli.ts:648, 651-653), so the spawn at cli.ts:692-693 inherits the Electron main process cwd.
