INTENT QUOTES ARE ACCURATE, NOT PARAPHRASED. cli.ts:11 reads exactly "claude-cli: --allowedTools '' --disallowedTools '*' so the agent can never execute arbitrary tools" under a "SECURITY INVARIANTS (never relax)" header that scopes the whole file, not just `CLI_CONFIGS`. cli.ts:318-319 reads exactly "'--model' is unconditional: an empty model must never silently inherit the user's own CLI default (which can be a premium model) — floor to the cheapest current model instead." The "pinned Sonnet" claim is also real: `src/shared/providers.ts:523-524` `applyInteractiveGuardrail` returns Sonnet for claude-cli on every tier, under a comment at providers.ts:517-518 saying "the CLI provider only ever answers as Sonnet in the interactive ask flow, never Haiku, never Opus."

NO GUARD ANYWHERE ELSE. (a) `cliEnv()` (cli.ts:180-196) only deletes `CLAUDE_CODE*`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` — it sets no model and no permission mode, so it cannot compensate. (b) The IPC handler `src/main/index.ts:2237-2248` only zod-parses the provider id. (c) Callers `src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:1625` and `:1652` and `src/renderer/src/components/Onboarding.tsx:555` and `:563` pass only an id. (d) No test covers `testCli` at all — `grep -rl testCli --include=*.test.ts src/` returns nothing; `src/main/cli.test.ts:51-73` asserts both flags only on `CLI_CONFIGS['claude-cli'].buildArgs`. Ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/cli.test.ts` — 19/19 pass, none touch this path.

SUBSTITUTE-DEFENSE REFUTATIONS FAILED. `--allowedTools ''` is not a deny-all (Claude Code's allow list is additive over settings.json), and the codebase concedes this: if the empty allowlist sufficed, `--disallowedTools '*'` at cli.ts:330-331 would be dead weight and cli.test.ts:56 would not assert it separately. `--max-turns 1` is not the substitute either — buildArgs uses it *alongside* the deny list.

NOT A DELIBERATE EXCEPTION. `git log -L 645,665:src/main/cli.ts` shows commit 37a9226 only moved the positional prompt to stdin on both branches; the deny-list and `--model` were added to `buildArgs` and never backported here. There is no comment claiming an exemption.

SEVERITY CORRECTED medium -> low. The security half is hardening-only: the prompt is the hardcoded constant "Reply with OK" (cli.ts:710), so no untrusted input reaches this spawn. Exploitation needs the model to spontaneously call a tool on a trivial prompt AND the user to run bypassPermissions — the second is plausible for this audience, the first is not. The cost half is certain but tiny: one `claude -p` turn per Connect click, plus an unprompted one at Onboarding.tsx:555, on subscription auth (cliEnv strips the API key), so it burns quota rather than dollars. Real divergence from two stated policies, minor blast radius.

Worth adding for the fixer: pinning `--model sonnet` here is not only cost hygiene — testing on the user's default model can report "connected" while the model the real ask actually uses (Sonnet, per providers.ts:524) is unavailable, i.e. a false green.

The codex sub-claim also reproduces (cli.ts:656-661 swallows an mkdtemp failure and proceeds with the app cwd, degrading the cli.ts:12 "throwaway tmp cwd" half of the invariant while `features.shell_tool=false` survives), but mkdtemp-on-tmpdir failure is rare enough that it does not lift the severity.

Fix is one line: append `'--disallowedTools', '*', '--model', 'sonnet'` to cli.ts:653. The codex fallback is a separate small change.

### MQA-087 — codex-cli leaks its sandbox temp directory (and reports a confusing error) whenever the Windows shim guard rejects an argument

**Where.** `src/main/cli.ts:471` · workflow: codex-cli ask on Windows when the model id contains a cmd.exe metacharacter (e.g. a brain-ingest model string, which bypasses the interactive guardrail) · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** cli.ts:451-452 — "codex needs a throwaway working directory so it never mutates the user's project", paired with the `cleanup()` contract at cli.ts:574-583 (`rm(tmpCwd, { recursive: true, force: true })`). cli.ts:219-223 states the guard exists precisely because "the model id can be free text a user typed into Settings (codex-cli has no fixed model list, and the brain-ingest path can deliver a model string without going through the interactive guardrail)".

**Actual.** src/main/cli.ts:455 creates `tmpCwd` via mkdtemp, and only THEN does cli.ts:468 call `resolveSpawnTarget`, whose cmdShimSpawn guard (cli.ts:238-244) can throw. The catch at cli.ts:469-472 does `wd.clear(); return fail(...)` and never calls `cleanup()` — the only `cleanup()` call site is inside `child.on('close')` at cli.ts:561, which is unreachable because no child was ever spawned. Each failed ask therefore leaves an `asktoto-cli-*` directory behind in %TEMP% forever.

**Repro.** Windows, codex installed via npm (codex.cmd). Set a codex model id containing a cmd.exe metacharacter — e.g. `gpt-5-codex(preview)` in Settings, or any such string arriving from the brain-ingest path that skips applyInteractiveGuardrail. Each ask: mkdtemp creates C:\Users\<u>\AppData\Local\Temp\asktoto-cli-XXXX, cmdShimSpawn throws on the `(`/`)`, fail() reports "Codex · OpenAI CLI: refusing to spawn: an argument contains a quote, newline, or cmd.exe metacharacter (unsafe for cmd.exe)" — which does not tell the user the model id is the cause — and the directory is never removed. Repeat per ask.

**Suggested fix.** Move the `resolveSpawnTarget` call above the mkdtemp block (it needs neither cwd nor the temp dir), or `await cleanup()` in the catch at cli.ts:469-472 before returning. Also include the offending argument's role in the message (e.g. "the model id contains a character that can't be passed safely on Windows") so the user knows what to change.

**Verifier.** I tried to refute this on four fronts and it survived all of them.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED, line by line (D:\Asktoto\src\main\cli.ts):
- 423: `let tmpCwd: string | undefined` declared in runCliStream's closure.
- 453-461: `if (cfg.useTmpCwd) { tmpCwd = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'asktoto-cli-')) }`. `CLI_CONFIGS['codex-cli'].useTmpCwd === true` (cli.ts:393), claude-cli is false (365) — so this is codex-only, as claimed.
- 463-472: args are built (`...(model ? ['-m', model] : [])`, cli.ts:379), then `resolveSpawnTarget(absBin, args)` at 468 inside a try. The catch at 469-472 is exactly `wd.clear(); return fail(...)` — no cleanup.
- resolveSpawnTarget → cmdShimSpawn (283-291) throws on `/["\r\n&|^%<>()!]/` in any arg (238-244) or `/["\r\n%]/` in bin (249-253).
- Grep for `cleanup|tmpCwd|mkdtemp` over the whole file returns exactly one call site: `void cleanup()` at 561 inside `child.on('close')`. No child exists on the throw path, so the rm at 577 never runs. The returned `abort()` (586-589) only clears the watchdog and aborts the controller — it does not clean up either. Directory leaks.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED:
1. "Something else sweeps %TEMP%." No. Grep of `tmpdir()` across all non-test src/main code hits only cli.ts (455, 657), apple-speech.ts, selftest.ts. No `asktoto-cli-*` sweeper anywhere (only test files use that prefix for their own dirs). Node/Electron do not delete mkdtemp dirs.
2. "Some other error path already covers it." No. Node emits 'close' after a spawn 'error', and the watchdog path aborts → kills child → 'close' → cleanup. The resolveSpawnTarget throw is the *only* post-mkdtemp exit that bypasses 'close'.
3. "It's intended / not a contract." The opposite: the sibling function testCli handles the identical case correctly at cli.ts:671-674 — `catch (e) { if (tmpDir) await rm(tmpDir, { recursive: true, force: true }).catch(() => {}); return {...} }`. Same guard, same throw, same temp dir, cleanup present. runCliStream is the asymmetric one. The finder's "intended" quotes are accurate (cli.ts:451-452 comment, cleanup() at 574-583, and the free-text-model rationale at 219-223 verbatim).
4. "A schema/guardrail blocks a metachar model." No. `providerModels: z.record(z.string(), z.string())` (src/shared/ipc.ts:662) — no character constraint. `applyInteractiveGuardrail` (src/shared/providers.ts:523-528) is a pass-through for codex-cli, so it does not sanitize on any path, interactive or brain-ingest. resolveBin does return `.cmd` on Windows (parseWhereOutput, cli.ts:92-98; npmGlobalBinCandidates, 104-108).

Ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/cli-win.test.ts src/main/cli.test.ts` — 53 tests pass. cli-win.test.ts:234 tests that the metachar arg is *rejected*, but nothing asserts temp-dir cleanup on that path, so no test refutes or covers this.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE FINDER'S REPRO (does not change the ruling): the codex model id cannot be typed in Settings. The model `<input>` lives inside `keyEntrySection`, which is `null` for CLI providers (`!CLI_PROVIDERS.has(provider)`, src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:926, with CLI_PROVIDERS including 'codex-cli' at :138). PROVIDERS['codex-cli'].defaultModel is `''`, so by default `-m` is omitted entirely and the guard never fires. Reaching it requires a hand-edited settings.json / managed-config.json `providerModels['codex-cli']`, or a resolved codex.cmd path containing `"`/newline/`%`. So the trigger is narrower than "type it in Settings" — but the code's own comment (219-223) declares this path reachable by design, and the defect is real whenever it is reached.

IMPACT: one *empty* directory per failed ask in %TEMP% (no child ran, nothing written). Accumulates only while the CLI is in an already-broken state where every ask errors — e.g. a brain-ingest run over many meetings would leak one per attempt. Disk cost is negligible; low severity is correct.

FIX: one line — `await cleanup()` (or `void cleanup()`) before the `return fail(...)` at cli.ts:470-471, mirroring testCli:672. `cleanup` is a hoisted function declaration in the same closure, so it is already in scope there.

### MQA-088 — Diagnostics "Fallbacks" counter conflates same-provider retries with cross-provider failovers and double-counts provider requests

**Where.** `src/main/metrics.ts:60` · workflow: read Settings → Diagnostics to find out whether provider failover is working · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/metrics.ts:9-11 — "Surfaces the section-H/D quality + latency numbers from the product brief: ... provider failure + fallback rates, and a per-provider request count." docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1077 — "| Provider-fallback success rate (failover resolves the ask) | ≥ 95 % | — | `audit.log fallbacks / (failures + fallbacks)` |".

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:2951 logs `auditLog('provider.request', { provider, ..., retry: attempted.length > 0 })`, but a same-provider transient retry re-enters `attempt(provider, attempted, retryCount + 1)` (index.ts:3050) with `attempted` UNCHANGED — so a retry emits another `provider.request` carrying the same `retry` value as the original attempt. src/main/metrics.ts:59-60 then does `if (r.provider) byProvider[r.provider]++; if (r.retry) fallbacks++`, counting a same-provider retry of any non-first provider as a fallback, and missing every same-provider retry of the first provider.

**Repro.** One ask, primary = DeepSeek (revoked/rate-limited), NVIDIA keyed. deepseek 429 -> retry deepseek (provider.request retry:false -> byProvider.deepseek = 2, fallbacks = 0) -> failover to nvidia (retry:true -> fallbacks = 1) -> nvidia 429 -> retry nvidia (retry:true -> fallbacks = 2) -> nvidia answers. Settings.tsx:5270 renders "Fallbacks 2" for a single ask that failed over exactly once, and the per-provider card shows 2 DeepSeek requests for 1 user question.

**Suggested fix.** Emit a distinct signal for a cross-provider hop: at index.ts:2951 log `retry: retryCount > 0` (same-provider) and `failover: attempted.length > 0` as separate fields, then count `fallbacks` from `r.failover && r.retry !== true` in metrics.ts:60 and exclude same-provider retries from `byProvider`. Update src/main/metrics.test.ts:30 accordingly.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED, with one sub-claim rejected.

Causal chain independently reproduced:

1. src/main/index.ts:2958 emits `auditLog('provider.request', { provider, model, mode: req.mode, tier, retry: attempted.length > 0 })` with no guard on retryCount.
2. The same-provider transient retry at src/main/index.ts:3066 is `setTimeout(() => attempt(provider, attempted, retryCount + 1), delayMs)` — `attempted` is passed UNCHANGED; only retryCount advances. Only `failover()` (src/main/index.ts:2832-2838) grows it: `attempt(next, tried)` with `tried = attempted.concat(provider)` from the call sites at index.ts:2927/3070. So `retry` literally encodes "this is not the first provider tried", and a same-provider retry of provider #2+ re-emits `retry: true`.
3. src/main/metrics.ts:59-60 `if (r.provider) byProvider[r.provider]++; if (r.retry) fallbacks++` has no disambiguation. The distinct `provider.retry` event (emitted index.ts:3065, declared src/main/logger.ts:85) is never consumed by aggregateMetrics — there is no branch for it (metrics.ts:50-67 handles only provider.request / provider.failed / answer.feedback).
4. Reachability of the repro trigger is locked by an existing test: `isTransient('429 Too Many Requests') === true` at src/main/ask-freshness.contract.test.ts:124, and the retry gate is `!gotToken && retryCount < retryBudget && isTransient(message)` (index.ts:3063).
5. No compensating code anywhere: grep for `fallbacks` across src hits only ipc.ts:200 (type), metrics.ts:44/60/78, and Settings.tsx:5270 (`card('Fallbacks', String(m.fallbacks))`). src/main/logger.ts:125-137 does no dedup on audit writes.
6. No test prevents it. Ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/metrics.test.ts — 2 passed — but it feeds only hand-written records (metrics.test.ts:10-21) and never models a retry sequence.

Intended-behavior quotes check out verbatim: metrics.ts:9-11 says "provider failure + fallback rates, and a per-provider request count"; docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1077 says "Provider-fallback success rate (failover resolves the ask) | >= 95 % | - | `audit.log fallbacks / (failures + fallbacks)`". So `fallbacks` is unambiguously intended as a cross-provider failover count, and a same-provider retry inflating it is a real defect.

REJECTED sub-claim: the "double-counts provider requests" half. metrics.ts:11 defines the counter as "a per-provider REQUEST count", and a retry genuinely is another request issued to that provider, so byProvider.deepseek = 2 for one user question is defensible rather than wrong. The metrics.ts:52 comment "Count requests on the pre-request record so each ask counts once" is about not also counting the phase:'done' record, not about collapsing retries. The finder's framing of the per-provider card as a bug does not survive.

Severity: low is correct. This is a read-only local diagnostics panel (Settings.tsx:5241-5290); no effect on routing, answers, privacy, or persisted data — only a misleading integer.

Fix complexity: trivial — one-line change at index.ts:2958 (e.g. `retry: attempted.length > 0 && retryCount === 0`, or emit a separate `attemptIndex`/`failover` field) so a same-provider retry stops carrying the failover flag; metrics.ts needs no change if the emit is corrected.

### MQA-089 — A Dust CLI session expiry is overwritten with "update your API key" advice — sending the user to re-enter a key that does not exist

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:37` · workflow: ask a question after the Dust CLI OAuth session expires · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:3056-3062 deliberately crafts the precise remedy for this case: "// Replace raw client transport strings … with a clean message; keep the Dust-auth one-click reconnect path" → `'Your Dust session expired and could not refresh automatically. Open Settings and reconnect Dust once.'` The whole point is that the fix is a reconnect, not a key edit — the Dust credential is an OAuth token minted by the Dust CLI (src/main/index.ts:2988-2997 refreshDustAuth), never something the user types.

**Actual.** src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:37 — `if (/invalid.*(key|api)|incorrect api key|unauthor|\b401\b|expired/.test(e)) return 'Your API key may be invalid or expired. Update it in Settings → AI.'`. The bare `expired` alternative matches main's own Dust copy, so the hint is appended under it. I verified this against the exact string: errorHint('Your Dust session expired and could not refresh automatically. Open Settings and reconnect Dust once.') returns the API-key hint.

**Repro.** Connect Dust via the CLI, leave the app idle past the ~1 h token life with the CLI session gone (e.g. run `dust logout`), then ask a question. The red box reads "Your Dust session expired and could not refresh automatically. Open Settings and reconnect Dust once." followed by "Your API key may be invalid or expired. Update it in Settings → AI." The two lines prescribe different actions; a user who follows the second one goes hunting for a Dust API key to re-paste — the failure mode of sending someone to replace a perfectly good credential.

**Suggested fix.** Tighten the key branch so a bare `expired` can't claim a session/OAuth failure — e.g. require it to co-occur with key/api/token wording (`/(api|key|token).*expired|expired.*(api|key|token)/`) — and add an earlier Dust branch returning null (main's message is already complete and actionable, exactly as the vision case is skipped at Answer.tsx:41-42).

**Verifier.** Survives. I reproduced the chain end-to-end and could not find any guard.

INTENDED (quote is accurate; finder's line numbers drifted ~50 lines but text is verbatim): src/main/index.ts:3108-3114 holds the exact comment "Replace raw client transport strings ... with a clean message; keep the Dust-auth one-click reconnect path" and emits 'Your Dust session expired and could not refresh automatically. Open Settings and reconnect Dust once.' src/main/index.ts:2806-2811 (pickFailover) independently confirms intent: "letting the flow fall through to the reconnect-Dust message instead."

REACHABLE: src/main/llm/retry.ts:57-59 excludes auth from isTransient ("Auth is not transient - a 401 must never be retried here"), so the isTransient branch at index.ts:3110 does not swallow it. src/main/llm/dust.ts:25,38 surfaces expired_oauth_token / "valid authentication credentials" text matching main's dust regex at index.ts:3113. failover at index.ts:3107 returns false for a Dust-only install (and pickFailover returns null for agent-pinned requests), so the friendly string is sent.

VERBATIM TRANSPORT: src/renderer/src/state.ts:348 sets `error: aborted ? null : e.message`; src/renderer/src/App.tsx:2418 passes `error={ask.answer?.error ?? null}`; Answer.tsx:282 calls errorHint(error) with no provider argument and renders {error} then {hint} in the same alert box (Answer.tsx:295-300). No Dust guard exists in errorHint (Answer.tsx:34-44) or the render path.

REPRODUCED BY REAL RENDER (esbuild-bundled SSR of the actual component, repo untouched): the role="alert" block contains BOTH "Your Dust session expired and could not refresh automatically. Open Settings and reconnect Dust once." and "Your API key may be invalid or expired. Update it in Settings -> AI." The bare `expired` alternative at Answer.tsx:37 is the matcher.

NO EXISTING GUARD/TEST: src/main/provider-health-ux.contract.test.ts (9 tests, ran green) asserts main keeps the three causes distinct - its own comment says "sending a user to re-enter a perfectly good key because their WiFi dropped is its own bug" - but it only greps main's source. src/renderer/src/components/Answer.test.tsx covers only the capture-notice case. The renderer re-collapses at the UI layer what main deliberately separated.

FINDER OVERSTATEMENT (does not refute): "never something the user types" is wrong - Settings.tsx:2906-2950 has a manual "Paste your Dust API key (sk-...)" step 3. It does not rescue the hint: with a CLI token stored, keySaved is true so that input is replaced by "Saved on this device" + a Remove button (Settings.tsx:2910-2924), so the user following the hint finds nothing to update and only a destructive action.

SEVERITY CORRECTED medium -> low: the correct remedy renders first in larger high-contrast danger text; the contradictory hint is smaller muted secondary text below it, and both point at the same panel where the Dust card's prominent Reconnect button lives (Settings.tsx:2761). No data loss; recovery stays one click away. The same echo is benign for main's other crafted strings (the transient message maps to the consistent network hint). Real contradictory-guidance defect, but low blast radius. Fix is trivial: tighten the `expired` alternative at src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:37 to require key/token context (or bail on the Dust reconnect message).

### MQA-090 — On the ffmpeg-less fallback path, one import's transcription failure cascade-fails every queued import with the wrong error "Another audio decoder is already active."

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:581` · workflow: queue several imports at once · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:542-545 documents the mechanism and the required fix for the ffmpeg branch: "A transcription failure inside acceptDecodedChunk marks the job terminal and pumps the next FIFO job synchronously (fail() -> pump() -> here), before this decoder's own onError callback — which normally deletes the map entry — has had a chance to run. Reap any decoder whose job already finished so it can't block the next job with a false 'already active'." The in-repo adversarial test src/main/import-jobs.verify-cascade.scratch.test.ts:22-54 pins the hidden-window variant of the same cascade ("hidden-window ordering: completing job A fails queued job B") and currently PASSES, i.e. it asserts the broken behaviour rather than guarding against it.

**Actual.** The equivalent reaping was added only to the ffmpeg branch (index.ts:546-554). The hidden-window branch at src/main/index.ts:581 is still a bare `if (decoderWin && !decoderWin.isDestroyed()) throw new Error('Another audio decoder is already active.')` with no check of whether the job that owns `decoderWin` (`decoderJobId`) is already terminal. The importDecoderComplete/importDecoderFailed handlers were fixed by closing the window first (index.ts:3549-3553, 3564-3565), but the acceptDecodedChunk failure path never reaches those handlers before pump() runs.

**Repro.** On a machine where `bundledFfmpegPath()` returns null (ffmpeg.exe absent/quarantined -> hidden-window OfflineAudioContext fallback), queue imports A, B, C. A's chunk 0 fails transcription twice (transcribeWithRetry, import-jobs.ts:385-395 — e.g. the Whisper transformers backend fails to load AND the Parakeet fallback at index.ts:783-785 also throws). fail(A) -> pump() -> decode(B) runs in the same await chain, while A's decoderWin is still alive because A's renderer has not yet received the submitChunk rejection -> index.ts:581 throws -> pump's catch fails B with "Another audio decoder is already active.", then the same for C. Two imports the user queued die with a message naming the wrong cause; each needs a manual Resume.

**Suggested fix.** Mirror the ffmpeg reaping loop before the guard at index.ts:581: if `decoderJobId` is set and `importJobs?.get(decoderJobId)?.state` is terminal/undefined, `await closeImportDecoder(decoderJobId)` first, then re-test `decoderWin`.

**Verifier.** CONFIRMED, though the finder's line numbers are stale by ~15 and one piece of its evidence is bogus.

Line-number corrections: the bare guard is src/main/index.ts:596, not 581; the quoted comment is 557-560; the ffmpeg reaping loop is 561-569; the two already-fixed handlers are 3600-3613 (importDecoderComplete) and 3615-3625 (importDecoderFailed). The quoted "intended behavior" comment at 557-560 matches the finder's quote verbatim, so that citation is accurate.

Bad evidence, discarded: src/main/import-jobs.verify-cascade.scratch.test.ts passes only because its mocks encode PRE-fix code. Its own header comment ("the importDecoderComplete handler awaits finishDecoding() FIRST and closes the decoder window only afterwards") is now false — index.ts:3608 closes the window before finishDecoding. Its ffmpeg case (line 62) also omits the reaping loop. That file is stale scratch, not a pin on live behavior. I ran it (2 passed) and then ignored it.

Independent reproduction: I bundled the REAL src/main/import-jobs.ts with esbuild and drove it with a decode mock mirroring index.ts:596 exactly (throw if decoderWin alive; assign decoderJobId/decoderWin only past the guard; onCancel -> closeImportDecoder). Result with 3 queued jobs and a failing transcribe:
  A -> failed | ASR crashed
  B -> failed | Another audio decoder is already active.
  C -> failed | Another audio decoder is already active.
  started = [A], decoderWinAlive = true
Control run in the same script using the ffmpeg branch's reaping loop (index.ts:561-569): B -> decoding, started2 = 2, i.e. no cascade. The asymmetry between the two branches is real and load-bearing.

Causal chain verified hop by hop:
1. src/main/index.ts:3594-3599 (importDecoderChunk) is the ONLY decoder IPC handler that does not free the decoder before the manager can pump — unlike 3608 and 3620 which both call closeImportDecoder first.
2. import-jobs.ts:291 fail() -> 424-426 pump() -> 411 deps.decode(B) -> index.ts:766-771 -> startImportDecoder(B).
3. bundledImportFfmpeg() null -> falls past 555-595 to the bare guard at 596, which throws BEFORE assigning decoderJobId (so decoderJobId still names A).
4. pump's catch (413) fails B; recursion fails C. All of this settles before acceptDecodedChunk rethrows at 292, so the renderer only learns of the error afterwards (src/renderer/src/import-decoder.ts:62-66 -> importDecoderFailed) — far too late.
5. Nothing else closes decoderWin: onCancel: closeImportDecoder (index.ts:813) fires only from cancel(); the 'closed' handler (616) never runs.
Note the trigger is broader than transcription failure — import-jobs.ts:268 (out-of-order seq) and :272 (chunk-count change) hit the same fail()->pump() path.

The fallback is live maintained code, not dead: src/renderer/src/lib/import-audio.ts:22-29 documents it as "used only when the bundled ffmpeg sidecar ... is unavailable", with its own memory bound, preload, decoder.html and build input.

Severity corrected medium -> low. Production reachability is gated hard: resources/ffmpeg/* is gitignored (.gitignore:60-62, only manifest.json + LICENSE tracked), and scripts/after-pack.mjs:42 plus scripts/check-packaged-runtime.mjs:444-458 fail the build if the sidecar is missing, so every shipped install takes the already-fixed ffmpeg branch. The hidden-window path is reached on unseeded dev checkouts and on post-install removal (AV quarantine/deletion of the 15MB ffmpeg.exe). Impact is fully recoverable — every job is checkpointed and importJobResume (index.ts:3556) restores it — so the damage is a misleading error message plus one manual Resume per queued job.

Fix: mirror the ffmpeg reap at the guard — before index.ts:596, if decoderJobId names a job whose state is terminal/undefined, await closeImportDecoder(decoderJobId). ~3-5 lines; closeImportDecoder already sets closingDecoderJobId so the 'closed' handler at 626 won't spuriously failDecoder, and the 619 identity check keeps A's late 'closed' from tearing down B's window. Needs a real regression test (the existing scratch file should be replaced, not kept).

### MQA-091 — Disconnect reports success even when the CRM API key file survives on disk — the renderer discards the ok:false the handler was built to return

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:2001` · workflow: disconnect Polo Pre-Sales / remove the stored CRM API key · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:2288-2291 — "// Don't falsely report a clean disconnect when the secret is still on disk — the connection is marked off, but the user needs to know the key file survived so they can remove it manually." followed by `if (!keyRemoved) return { ok: false, error: 'Disconnected, but the stored BidStack key file could not be deleted — remove it manually.' }`. src/main/mcp/bidstackSecrets.ts:93-95 — "Returns false if the on-disk key file could not be deleted (...) so the disconnect handler can tell the user their key wasn't actually removed instead of falsely reporting success while the secret survives on disk."

**Actual.** src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:2000-2007 does `await window.toto.mcpCrmDisconnect()` and throws the result away — no `r.ok` check, no error state set — then unconditionally patches the card to disconnected and closes it. The preload signature makes the error unreachable by construction: src/preload/index.ts:305 types it `mcpCrmDisconnect: (): Promise<{ ok: boolean }>` with no `error` field. The entire !keyRemoved branch in main is dead code.

**Repro.** On Windows, have `%APPDATA%/Metis/key-bidstack.bin` held open by AV/EDR/backup (or make it read-only) so `rmSync` throws EPERM/EBUSY. Click Settings → Polo Pre-Sales → Disconnect: `clearBidstackApiKey()` logs the warning and returns false (bidstackSecrets.ts:99-107), the handler returns `{ok:false, error:'… could not be deleted — remove it manually.'}`, and the UI silently shows the card as fully disconnected. The plaintext-equivalent CRM bearer token is still on disk, and because clearBidstackApiKey sets `_cache = null` (not `''`) on that path, the next `getBidstackApiKey()` re-reads it from disk successfully.

**Suggested fix.** Widen the preload/IPC type to `{ ok: boolean; error?: string }`, and in Settings.tsx's disconnect check the result: on `!r.ok` still flip the card to disconnected but render `r.error` in the existing error strip (Settings.tsx:2092-2097) instead of closing silently.

**Verifier.** Could not refute — the full chain reproduces on current HEAD.

PRODUCER CONFIRMED: src/main/index.ts:2320-2324 contains verbatim the quoted comment ("Don't falsely report a clean disconnect when the secret is still on disk…") followed by `if (!keyRemoved) return { ok: false, error: 'Disconnected, but the stored BidStack key file could not be deleted — remove it manually.' }`. src/main/mcp/bidstackSecrets.ts:93-95 carries the quoted docstring verbatim. (Finder's cited lines 2288-2291 are stale — that's the .claude/worktrees copy, where the handler sits at index.ts:1883 — but the quoted text is accurate, so the "intended behavior" quote stands.)

REACHABLE: clearBidstackApiKey (bidstackSecrets.ts:96-111) returns false only from the rmSync catch at :101-107; a locked or read-only key-bidstack.bin on Windows (EPERM/EBUSY) reaches it. Not dead in main.

CONSUMER DISCARDS IT: src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:2000-2007 does `await window.toto.mcpCrmDisconnect()` with no r.ok check, then unconditionally `patch({ bidstackConnected: false, bidstackEndpointUrl: '', bidstackTools: [] })` and setOpen(false). Verified this is the ONLY CRM disconnect call site in src/ (other 'disconnect' hits are disconnectCli / disconnectDust, unrelated channels).

NO ALTERNATE SURFACE: grep for the error string finds exactly one occurrence — the producer. Nothing consumes it. auditLog('bidstack.disconnected', {keyFileRemoved}) at index.ts:2319 writes only to the audit log. src/preload/index.ts:305 is a bare ipcRenderer.invoke with no generic ok-checking wrapper.

UNREACHABLE BY TYPE: src/preload/index.ts:305 declares `mcpCrmDisconnect: (): Promise<{ ok: boolean }>` — no error field — and src/preload/index.d.ts binds window.toto to that same TotoApi, so the renderer cannot even read r.error. Finder's claim is exact.

NO DOWNSTREAM GUARD: bidstackConnected is a plain persisted boolean (src/shared/ipc.ts:865, default false at :1147), never derived from hasBidstackApiKey(), written only at index.ts:2307/2318. So the card really does render fully disconnected while the blob survives. mcpCrmPush (index.ts:2336) does block pushes on !s.bidstackConnected, which caps blast radius but does not address the false success.

TESTS: ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/mcp/bidstackSecrets.test.ts → 7/7 pass, but the suite only asserts the happy path ('clearBidstackApiKey removes the key file and cache', :56-64). Nothing asserts the false return or an undeletable file. No renderer test exists for disconnect.

SEVERITY CORRECTED medium -> low. The finder overstates the impact: the surviving file is NOT "plaintext-equivalent" — it is the same AES-256-GCM (ATKBID1) or DPAPI/safeStorage machine-bound blob it was before disconnect, so at-rest protection never regresses, and no unauthorized push is possible since bidstackConnected is false. The `_cache = null` re-read observation is correct but is deliberate design documented at bidstackSecrets.ts:104-105, not a second defect. Trigger also requires an OS-level delete failure, not any normal flow. What remains genuinely real: a documented, security-motivated failure signal is silently swallowed and the user is told a credential was deleted when it was not.

FIX: widen preload signature at src/preload/index.ts:305 to Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> and check r.ok in Settings.tsx:2000-2007 before collapsing the card (reuse the existing testState error slot).

### MQA-092 — Re-opening an already-pushed meeting re-arms "Push to CRM", and the payload carries no idempotency key — a second identical record lands in the CRM

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/Review.tsx:402` · workflow: push a meeting recap to Polo Pre-Sales (CRM) · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/Review.tsx:399-401 — "A different meeting loaded into this reused Review instance → drop any in-progress/finished CRM push state (...) Without this, navigating from a pushed meeting to an unpushed one via 'Recent meetings' kept showing 'Pushed to Polo Pre-Sales.' for the wrong meeting." The stated contract is that the "Pushed to Polo Pre-Sales." indicator reflects whether THIS meeting was pushed.

**Actual.** The reset effect at Review.tsx:402-406 keyed on `[savedPath]` makes `pushState` per-mount, not per-meeting: nothing about a completed push is persisted anywhere (grep of src/ for crmPushed / pushedAt / bidstackPushed: no result found — scope: whole src/ tree; the only bidstack settings are bidstackEndpointUrl / bidstackConnected / bidstackTools, shared/ipc.ts:864-868). The payload built at Review.tsx:411-418 is `{title, date, summary}` only — no meeting file name, no id, no client-generated idempotency token — so the receiving MCP tool has nothing to dedupe on.

**Repro.** Connect Polo Pre-Sales. Open saved meeting A in Review, Push to CRM → Confirm push → "Pushed to Polo Pre-Sales." and the chip disappears. Click "Recent meetings" and open meeting B (savedPath changes → effect resets pushState to idle), then open meeting A again (savedPath changes back → reset again). Meeting A now shows the "Push to CRM" chip as if never pushed; clicking Confirm push sends a byte-identical `{title, date, summary}` tool call, producing a second CRM record for the same meeting. Same result via "Back to history" → reopen A.

**Suggested fix.** Persist the push per meeting — either a `crmPushedAt` frontmatter field on the saved meeting (same mechanism as recall.ts's `confidential` flag) that seeds pushState on mount, or at minimum include a stable idempotency key in the payload (e.g. the meeting file basename, which is already unique per meeting) so the CRM side can dedupe.

**Verifier.** MECHANISM CONFIRMED — I could not find any guard, caller, schema default, or test that prevents a second identical push.

What I checked, in order:
1. Component guard — `sendToCrm` (src/renderer/src/components/Review.tsx:420-430) only guards `pushState.phase === 'sending'` (concurrent double-click) and `!pushTool`. Nothing checks "already pushed".
2. UI gate — the chip is hidden by `pushState.phase !== 'sent'` (Review.tsx:841) and the success line renders at 852-855. That is the ONLY memory of a completed push, and it is plain `useState` (Review.tsx:395-398) wiped by the effect at Review.tsx:402-406 on every `savedPath` change. Since App renders Review with `savedPath={pm ? pm.file : savedPath}` (src/renderer/src/App.tsx:2349), opening meeting B then re-opening A flips savedPath twice and re-arms the chip. Switching to the history/settings view unmounts the memoized `reviewBody` entirely, which loses the state even without the effect.
3. Main-process dedupe — the `mcpCrmPush` handler (src/main/index.ts:2330-2349) checks auth, connection, and a tool allowlist, then forwards `parsed.data.args` verbatim to `pushToBidstack`. `auditLog('bidstack.push', ...)` at index.ts:2347 is write-only and never read back. `pushToBidstack` (src/main/mcp/bidstackClient.ts:241-271) self-describes as "a thin, defensive transport wrapper" and adds nothing to args.
4. Schema default — `McpCrmPushPayloadSchema` (src/shared/ipc.ts:1534-1539) is `z.record(string, string|number|boolean|null)` with a ≤20-key cap. No id, no token, no default.
5. Persistence — settings carry only `bidstackEndpointUrl` / `bidstackConnected` / `bidstackTools` (src/shared/ipc.ts:864-868, defaults 1146-1148). A repo-wide grep for idempot/dedup/pushedAt/crmPushed finds hits only in src/main/brain/* (unrelated entity merging) — nothing on the CRM path.
6. Tests — there is no Review test file (only ReviewEntityStrip.test.ts). src/main/mcp/bidstackClient.test.ts has 14 cases (auth, SSRF denylist, timeouts, missing args); none assert dedupe or idempotency. Nothing to run that bears on this.

EXTRA TRIGGER the finder missed, which strengthens it: no navigation is even required. In a live session `savedPath` starts null and becomes a path only when autosave lands (App.tsx:382, 2349), and that save can be deferred behind up to 5 retries with backoff (App.tsx MAX_SAVE_RETRIES=5). The push panel only requires `recapText` (Review.tsx:835), not a saved path — so a push completed while a save is still retrying has its "Pushed to Polo Pre-Sales." wiped by the same effect, on the SAME meeting, with the user sitting still.

WHERE THE FINDER OVERREACHES (why I dropped medium → low):
- The cited "intended behavior" (Review.tsx:399-401) does NOT say what the finder claims. It documents only the false-positive direction — a pushed indicator following the user to a *different* meeting. It never promises the indicator persists for a meeting that was pushed. This is a design gap, not a violation of a stated contract.
- "keyed on [savedPath] makes pushState per-mount, not per-meeting" is imprecise: the reset IS per-meeting; what is absent is durable memory.
- The proposed fix (add the meeting file name / id to the payload) directly collides with a documented constraint three lines above: "Payload is deliberately thin: title, date, and the already-AI-summarized recap text — never raw transcript lines or file paths (see the confidentiality note...)" (Review.tsx:389-392). The absent idempotency key is at least partly a deliberate tradeoff, not pure oversight — a content hash would be the only fix that respects it.
- Impact is bounded and user-visible: the duplicate requires the user to deliberately re-open the panel and click "Confirm push" past a preview that renders the full title/date/summary (Review.tsx:886-899). Result is one duplicate CRM record, manually deletable — no data loss, no security exposure, and the feature is gated on a niche self-hosted MCP connection.

Fix complexity small: hold a `Set<savedPath>` of pushed meetings in App (survives Review unmount/remount within a session), or persist a per-file marker; a durable cross-restart fix plus a content-hash dedupe token would push toward medium.

**FIXED (session memory 2026-08-08, durable marker 2026-08-17).** The first pass added `pushedCrmPayloads`, a module-scope Set keyed on the payload rather than the meeting file — deliberately, because `savedPath` is still null while a live meeting's autosave is retrying, so a file key would miss a push made in that window. That closed the in-session re-arm (leave for History, open another meeting, come back) and the extra trigger the verifier found.

It could not survive a relaunch, which is what kept this row open: push a recap, quit, reopen the meeting tomorrow, and the chip is armed again over a record the CRM already holds. The meeting's own frontmatter now carries `crm_pushed: <fingerprint>` (recall.ts's `setMeetingCrmPushed`, built on the exact mechanism and guards `setMeetingConfidential` uses — basename-constrained, encryption preserved as found, only the frontmatter block rewritten), `recallRead` returns it, and Review seeds the session Set from it on mount. It stores the payload FINGERPRINT, not a timestamp, so it shares one identity with the session Set and an edited recap still re-arms the chip — that is a different record, not a duplicate.

The key is interpolated into a YAML scalar, so its shape (`/^[a-z0-9]{1,32}$/`, a base-36 FNV-1a) is enforced in the zod payload AND re-checked in recall.ts: a value carrying a newline or a colon could otherwise forge frontmatter — `confidential: true`, or a bogus `type:` — from the renderer. Refused, never escaped. The write is best-effort after a successful push: failing to record a dedupe marker must never be reported as a failed push. It also covers the EXTRA TRIGGER the verifier added to this finding — a push needs only `recapText`, not a saved path, so a LIVE meeting's push can land while `savedPath` is still null behind autosave's retry ladder, with no file to stamp. That fingerprint is parked in a single slot (only the live meeting can lack a path) and written when the path arrives, guarded on it still matching the CURRENT payload — which makes stamping a different meeting's file impossible by construction, since navigating away changes the payload and therefore the hash.

**Deliberately NOT done: the idempotency token in the payload.** The verifier already showed the finding's own proposal (put the meeting file name in the payload) collides with the documented thin-payload constraint three lines above it. A content hash would respect that constraint — it is derived from `{title, date, summary}`, which the CRM already receives — but `pushToMcp` forwards args verbatim to an EXTERNAL, user-configured MCP tool, and a strict server would reject an argument its schema does not declare. Trading a working push for a dedupe hint on a low-severity duplicate is the wrong trade, and this machine cannot verify any given customer's tool accepts it. The client-side memory is now durable, which closes the repro; the server-side token stays available if a receiving tool ever declares the key.

### MQA-093 — Onboarding's "Allow Microphone" button is a permanent no-op once mic access is denied, and offers no path to OS privacy settings

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/OnboardingExperience.tsx:298` · workflow: first-run onboarding, "Your setup" scene — granting the microphone · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:1865-1867 (permissionsOpenSettings): "Deep-link to the relevant macOS Privacy pane once a permission has been denied — getUserMedia never re-prompts after a Deny, so without this a denied user has no in-app path back to granting it." The legacy checklist honours this (Onboarding.tsx:148-151 CheckRow doc: "`onFix` renders an inline 'Open System Settings' link — only meaningful when the OS has recorded an explicit Deny") and the sibling *screen* row in the same scene does too (OnboardingExperience.tsx:317-323 calls openPermissionSettings('screenRecording')).

**Actual.** OnboardingExperience.tsx:110-111 collapses denied and not-determined into the same state: `set('mic', perms?.microphone === 'granted' ? 'ready' : 'action', …)`. The mic 'action' block (OnboardingExperience.tsx:298-311) renders only an "Allow Microphone" button wired to requestMic() (line 179-192), which calls window.toto.requestPermissionsUpfront(). That handler (src/main/index.ts:1895-1896) only prompts `if (systemPreferences.getMediaAccessStatus('microphone') === 'not-determined')` — for a denied mic it does nothing and returns the same 'denied' status. openPermissionSettings('microphone') is never called anywhere in this scene.

**Repro.** macOS first run: reach the "Your setup" scene, click Deny on the microphone prompt that fires automatically (OnboardingExperience.tsx:132-134). The Microphone row stays "needs permission / needed" with an "Allow Microphone" button. Every click on it is a no-op — no OS prompt, no System Settings deep link, no error, row state unchanged — and the scene's Continue button stays in the ghost 'needsPerms' style with no explanation. Same on Windows: getUserMedia rejects (line 184-188), requestPermissionsUpfront is a darwin-only no-op, the row stays 'action', and there is no link to ms-settings:privacy-microphone. The user completes onboarding believing they granted the mic; Listen then fails on the first meeting.

**Suggested fix.** Track the denied status separately (e.g. state 'blocked' when perms.microphone === 'denied') and, in that state, render the same recovery control the screen row already has: a button calling window.toto.openPermissionSettings('microphone') with copy that says the OS will not re-ask. Keep "Allow Microphone" only while the status is not-determined/unknown.

**Verifier.** MECHANISM CONFIRMED. OnboardingExperience.tsx:111 and :153 both collapse denied/not-determined/unknown into a single 'action' state (SetupRow's enum at :63 has no denied discriminator). The mic 'action' block (:298-311) renders only "Allow Microphone" -> requestMic() (:179-192) -> window.toto.requestPermissionsUpfront(). src/main/index.ts:1906 gates askForMediaAccess on `=== 'not-determined'`, so a denied mic gets nothing and getPlatformPermissions() returns 'denied' again; :191 re-sets the row to the identical state. Observably zero effect. openPermissionSettings('microphone') is indeed never called in this file (grep: only line 319, the screenRecording sibling), so the mic/screen asymmetry the finder flags is real and the quoted intent at index.ts:1873-1875 is accurately transcribed.

IMPACT CLAIM REFUTED. The finder stopped quoting one sentence too early. index.ts:1899-1901 says: "Never re-prompts after an explicit Deny (macOS suppresses those anyway); the checklist's 'Open System Settings' link stays the recovery path." That checklist is unavoidable in this exact flow: OnboardingV2 (OnboardingExperience.tsx:462-489) enters Onboarding with initialStep=5, and EVERY exit from step 5 goes to step 6 -- choose() at Onboarding.tsx:551, chooseCli, chooseDust, and "Decide later" at :653 all setStep(6). finish(), the only writer of onboardingDone, is reachable solely from step 6's "Get started" (:742). Step 6 re-runs requestPermissionsUpfront + polls every 2.5s (:341-375) and renders the mic CheckRow (:714-725) with ok=false (warning border) and denied={perms?.microphone === 'denied'}, which satisfies CheckRow's link gate at :189 (`!ok && onFix && (denied || fixLabel)`) and calls openPermissionSettings('microphone'). Windows 'unknown' gets fixLabel "Check Windows Settings", unlocking the same link; index.ts:1888-1892 has a real win32 branch emitting ms-settings:privacy-microphone, contradicting the repro's "no link to ms-settings:privacy-microphone". Two more recovery paths exist afterwards: Settings.tsx:6183-6222 (correctly splits denied -> deep link vs not-determined -> "Request permission") and Copilot.tsx:256-259 (mic-error deep link at Listen time). So "user completes onboarding believing they granted the mic; Listen then fails on the first meeting" is false.

TESTS: no coverage of this path -- ask-freshness.contract.test.ts:17 only asserts the literal string requestPermissionsUpfront() exists in the file. Ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/components/Settings.permissions.test.ts src/renderer/src/App.capture-permission.test.ts src/main/platform-perms.test.ts: 23/23 pass, none exercise OnboardingExperience.

SEVERITY: downgraded high -> low. It is a dead control (a button that produces no prompt, no link, no error, no state change) and a real inconsistency with the sibling screen row in the same scene, but the Continue button is never blocked and three documented recovery paths sit downstream inside the same first-run flow. FIX: thread the raw status into SetupRow (or add a 'denied' state) and mirror lines 312-325 with openPermissionSettings('microphone'); touches the two setRows sites at :111 and :153 plus the render block, so small rather than trivial.

### MQA-094 — Onboarding's "Sign in with Microsoft" silently advances when SSO isn't configured, presenting a no-op as a successful sign-in

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/Onboarding.tsx:397` · workflow: first-run onboarding, legacy welcome slide (reached via "Skip the tour") — signing in with a work account · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/SignInWall.tsx:52-58 states the rule for exactly this return value: "signIn() short-circuited: `ok:true` here means \"nothing to do\" (SSO isn't actually configured), NOT \"you're signed in\" … Treating this as success would silently strand the user…" — and SignInWall accordingly branches on `r.configured === false` and surfaces a message.

**Actual.** src/renderer/src/components/Onboarding.tsx:397-407 does the opposite: `const r = await window.toto.signIn(); if (!r.ok) { setErr(...); return } … setStep(2)`. It inspects only `r.ok` and never `r.configured`, so main's unconfigured short-circuit (src/main/auth.ts:653 `if (!cfg) return { ok: true, configured: false }`) is consumed as success and the walkthrough advances with no browser opened, no session created, and no message. The footer at Onboarding.tsx:857-859 then still reads "Restricted to your Mantu Microsoft account" because `signedIn` is false.

**Repro.** Fresh install with no AZURE_* env vars, no managed-config azure block, and no Settings SSO (the shipped default). Onboarding hero → "Skip the tour" → tick the consent box → click "Sign in with Microsoft". No browser opens; the screen advances straight to "Ask + capture". Finish onboarding, open Settings → Account: Microsoft is Not connected. The user believes they signed in with their work account and did not.

**Suggested fix.** Mirror SignInWall: in advance(), after `const r = await window.toto.signIn()`, add `if (r.configured === false) { setErr("Microsoft sign-in isn't set up on this device — continuing without it."); }` before advancing (or hide/disable the Microsoft button entirely when auth.status.configured is false, since App already knows that value and passes signedIn/signedInEmail down).

**Verifier.** Could not refute it. Causal chain reproduces independently: src/main/auth.ts:653 returns `{ ok: true, configured: false }` when readConfig() (auth.ts:140-168) resolves nothing, which is the shipped default (no AZURE_* env, no managed azure block — build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json holds only placeholders, no bundled config). src/renderer/src/components/Onboarding.tsx:397-407 reads only `r.ok` and then setStep(2); `configured` appears nowhere in Onboarding.tsx. The button at Onboarding.tsx:821-832 is rendered unconditionally and the component is never passed auth status. Reachability confirmed: OnboardingExperience.tsx:470 (onSkip -> 'legacy-full') -> :484 initialStep={1} -> the legacy welcome slide.

No guard/caller/default/test prevents it. The codebase has exactly two mitigations for this return value and Onboarding uses neither: (a) handle it in the handler — SignInWall.tsx:52 and AgendaView.tsx:78 (`if (r.configured === false) { setNotConfigured(true); return }`); (b) gate the button on configured — Settings.tsx:6001 (`!isOutlookConnected && authStatus?.configured && !showOutlookSetup`), which is why Settings.tsx:5916's `!r.ok`-only check is safe. Ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/auth.test.ts src/main/onboarding-dedup.contract.test.ts — 6/6 pass; onboarding-dedup only counts the "Continue without signing in" label, auth.test.ts only covers authStatus()/requireAuth(). Neither pins this path.

Attempted refutation via unreachability backfired: App.tsx:2536 renders SignInWall BEFORE the onboarding gate at App.tsx:2550, so a configured-or-enforced + signed-out user never reaches onboarding. Every reachable render of slide 1 is thus either unconfigured (signIn short-circuits) or already signedIn (Onboarding.tsx:397 `viaSso && !signedIn` deliberately skips the call) — the primary CTA effectively never launches OAuth.

Two corrections to the finder. (1) The quoted "intended" text at SignInWall.tsx:52-58 is verbatim accurate about the return-value semantics, but its rationale ("silently strand the user behind the wall with a stopped spinner") is wall-specific and does not transfer — onboarding's advance() comment (Onboarding.tsx:379) calls SSO here "optional" and auth.ts:653's own comment says "let the user proceed", so advancing is intended; the defect is the missing feedback, corroborated instead by the generic convention at AgendaView.tsx:78. (2) "The footer at Onboarding.tsx:857-859 then still reads…" is imprecise — slide 1 unmounts on setStep(2), so that caption is pre-click, not post-click.

Severity confirmed low: unconfigured is fail-open by design (requireAuth() auth.ts:633-638), no privileged surface is opened, no data is lost; the only harm is a misleading affordance on the skip-the-tour path. Fix is trivial: add the `else if (r.configured === false)` branch at Onboarding.tsx:401 mirroring SignInWall.tsx:52.

### MQA-095 — Pasting a key auto-switches the active provider without checking the org allowlist, stranding the user on a provider every ask rejects

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:791` · workflow: add/replace an API key in Settings → AI · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:897-898 — "When the org sets a data-residency allowlist, only approved providers are offered — mirroring what the main process enforces at request time, so the UI can't offer a provider every ask would then reject." and :911-914 — "gate it here too so an org allowlist that omits 'anthropic' can't be bypassed via this separate control."

**Actual.** src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:786-795 `onKeyChange` checks only `locked` (managedKeys.includes('provider')) and CLI_PROVIDERS, then calls `patch({ provider: id })` at :793 with no reference to `orgAllowed`/`settings.allowedProviders` (computed at :899, used only for the tile grid at :900-906 and the Anthropic row at :914). Main does not reconcile it either: setSettings (src/main/store.ts:518-555) drops only LOCKED keys, and `allowedProviders` is a policy key, not a locked key.

**Repro.** managed-config.json with {"allowedProviders": ["openai"]}. Provider is 'openai'; the Anthropic row shows "Restricted by your organization" and the tile grid contains only GPT · OpenAI. The user pastes a Grok key (`xai-...`) into the OpenAI key box by mistake → detectProvider returns 'grok' (providers.ts:360-368) → patch({provider:'grok'}) is persisted. providerReady goes false (index.ts:838), the key card relabels to "Grok · xAI key", and every question now returns "Grok · xAI is not on your organization's approved provider list. Switch to GPT · OpenAI in Settings." (index.ts:2847) — a state no tile in the grid represents. The same gap exists in `pickReadyProvider` (Settings.tsx:156-169), which onRemove uses at :879 to pick a replacement provider from PROVIDER_IDS with no allowlist filter.

**Suggested fix.** Guard the auto-switch: `if (id && id !== provider && !CLI_PROVIDERS.has(id) && (!orgAllowed || orgAllowed.includes(id)))`, and show the existing 'tip' hint ("restricted by your organization") when detection lands on a blocked provider so the paste isn't silently ignored. Pass `settings.allowedProviders` into pickReadyProvider and filter there too. Belt-and-braces: have main's settings:set reject a `provider` outside getAllowedProviders() the same way it strips license fields (index.ts:1918-1920).

**Verifier.** Could not refute it. Chain reproduced end to end. Settings.tsx:786-795 `onKeyChange` gates only on `locked` (:789) and `CLI_PROVIDERS` (:791) before `patch({provider: id})` at :793 — `orgAllowed`/`settings.allowedProviders` (computed at :899, reachable from that closure) is never consulted. detectProvider returns 'grok' for `xai-…` (providers.ts:239,360-368; asserted providers.test.ts:195). The patch persists unchecked: state.ts:548 -> ipcMain.handle(IPC.settingsSet) at index.ts:1914-1952 (strips only license fields) -> setSettings store.ts:518-544 (drops only LOCKED keys) -> getSettings repair store.ts:504-509 (validates the schema enum only, never the allowlist). Locked and allowlist are provably independent: getLockedKeys/parseLockedContent (store.ts:195-200, 133-145) read only `locked`/`lockedKeys`, getAllowedProviders (store.ts:207-217) reads `allowedProviders`, so `{"allowedProviders":["openai"]}` gives managedKeys [] and `locked === false`. Downstream, providerReady goes false (index.ts:844-845) and the ask path rejects at index.ts:2845-2868.

Refutations tried and failed: (1) Cahê edition does NOT bundle an allowlist with locks — caheEditionPolicy() returns {allowedProviders:null, lockedKeys:[]} (cahe-edition.ts:80-82), and its comment states the allowlist only ever comes from IT managed-config. (2) No reconciliation exists anywhere — Settings.tsx:1199-1201 says so outright: "the active provider was never reconciled against the allowlist (see store.ts getSettings)". (3) No other caller gates it: Settings.tsx:786 is the app's only detectProvider auto-switch (Onboarding.tsx has none). (4) No test covers it — ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run Settings.contract.test.ts Settings.helpers.test.ts providers.test.ts: 57 passed, none exercises onKeyChange or allowlist+auto-detect.

Intended-behavior quotes are accurate as written (Settings.tsx:897-898, :911-914), and the intent is corroborated by two further gated controls the finder didn't cite: CLI cards at :1551-1555 ("so a disallowed provider can't be activated from here either") and Dust at :2440-2441. onKeyChange is the sole ungated provider-activating control. Secondary claim also holds: pickReadyProvider (Settings.tsx:156-169) has no allowlist filter and is used at :879, :1676, :2586.

Severity corrected medium -> low. It is a UI-consistency defect against a stated invariant, not an enforcement or data-residency bypass: egress is still blocked at index.ts:2845, testApiKey refuses at Save (store.ts:724-727), detectHint announces the switch (:693), App.tsx:772-782 intercepts asks with "Your organization restricts which providers you can use. Switch to an approved provider here.", and one click on the still-rendered allowed tile recovers. It needs the intersection of an org allowlist deployment and a mistyped/mismatched key prefix. Real aggravator confirmed: grok.tier is 'more' (providers.ts:232), so the key card renders at Settings.tsx:1302 inside an ExpandableSection whose `open` defaults false (:500) — the panel then shows no active provider at all.

Fix is small: add `(!orgAllowed || orgAllowed.includes(id))` to the :791 condition; threading the allowlist through pickReadyProvider's three call sites is the remaining work.

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/components/Onboarding.tsx:629` · workflow: first-run onboarding, step 5 provider choice · fix size: trivial

Clicking "Something else (DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, and more). Pick it in Settings" persists provider='anthropic'. Step 6's readiness checklist and every subsequent ask then fail with "Claude · Anthropic is not on your organization's approved provider list." (index.ts:2847) — the user finishes onboarding on a provider the org blocked, chosen by a control that exists inside the block whose comment promises this cannot happen.

**Suggested fix.** Make the link target the first approved API-key provider rather than a literal: `const fallbackApi = filterAllowedProviders(['anthropic','openai','nvidia','minimax'], settings.allowedProviders)[0]`, then `onClick={() => fallbackApi && choose(fallbackApi)}`, and hide the link entirely when that list is empty (the tile is already inert in that case per :538).

**Verifier.** I tried to refute this at five seams and could not.

Code chain verified verbatim:
- `D:\Asktoto\src\renderer\src\components\Onboarding.tsx:614-616` — comment does say exactly what the finder quotes ("Honor the org data-residency allowlist (null = unrestricted) so onboarding never offers a provider every ask would then reject — same source main enforces"), and the tile grid it guards is `filterAllowedProviders(['anthropic','openai','nvidia','minimax'], settings.allowedProviders)`.
- `Onboarding.tsx:627-633` — the escape-hatch button inside that same block is `onClick={() => choose('anthropic')}` with no allowlist test.
- `Onboarding.tsx:539-542` — `choose` = `patch({ provider }); setStep(6)`.
- `Onboarding.tsx:538` — `apiPathAllowed` is `.length > 0`, so an allowlist of `["openai","dust"]` leaves the "An API key" tile enabled and the picker reachable while anthropic is excluded. Repro stands.

Refutation attempts that failed:
1. Main-side drop? `src\preload\index.ts:72` → `IPC.settingsSet` → `src\main\index.ts:1914-1952`, which strips only license keys, then `setSettings` (`src\main\store.ts:518-545`) drops only `getLockedKeys()` entries. `allowedProviders` is a separate policy key (`store.ts:155-212`) and is never consulted on write. The provider persists.
2. Read-time clamp? `getSettings` (`store.ts:500-512`) only repairs a provider that fails the zod enum; `anthropic` is valid. `publicSettings()` (`index.ts:843-916`) uses the allowlist only to compute `providerReady:false` and to surface `allowedProviders` — it never rewrites `s.provider`.
3. `providerLocked` guard? `settings.managedKeys` = `getLockedKeys()`, which excludes `allowedProviders`. It correctly disables the tile (so the picker is unreachable when `provider` is locked), but is orthogonal to the allowlist.
4. Existing test? `Onboarding.helpers.test.ts` only covers `providerTileDisabledReason`; nothing touches the escape hatch. Ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/components/Onboarding.helpers.test.ts src/shared/providers.test.ts` — 41 passed, so the bug is simply unpinned, and `filterAllowedProviders` (`src\shared\providers.ts:346-351`) behaves as claimed.
5. Downstream sink? `index.ts:2845-2867` blocks the ask with the quoted message (line numbers are 2845/2862-2863, finder cited 2847 — close enough), `store.ts:724-726` blocks Test Key. So it fails closed; no egress to a blocked provider.

Severity corrected medium → low. Two reasons the blast radius is smaller than claimed: (a) the schema default is already `anthropic` (`src\shared\ipc.ts:657`), so on a plain first run the click is a no-op relative to the state "Decide later" would leave anyway — the control fails to help rather than introducing a new broken state; (b) the failure is a clear, actionable error ("Switch to <approved> in Settings"), not a policy bypass. It is still a real defect, because two paths do produce a genuine downgrade: an org that sets a managed *default* `provider` (e.g. openai) without locking it, and — since `setShowApiPicker` is never reset to `false` (only `Onboarding.tsx:307` and `:640`, contradicting the comment at :305-306 that it "closes again if the user backs out of step 5") — a user who picks OpenAI, hits step 6, presses Back (`Onboarding.tsx:763-769`), and clicks the still-open escape hatch, flipping an approved provider to a blocked one.

Fix is trivial: hide the link when `anthropic` isn't allowed, or route it to the first entry of the already-computed filtered list.

### MQA-097 — recallRead's midnight-crossing guard misfires on sub-second start times, shifting every reconstructed line of an imported meeting one full day forward

**Where.** `src/main/recall.ts:216` · workflow: Reopen a saved (especially imported) meeting from History; Speaker Intelligence backfill · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/recall.ts:222-224: `// If the reconstructed time is before the previous line's timestamp (midnight crossing), push to the next day — compares against the previous line rather than startedAt so this still works when startedAt is unavailable.` The stated trigger is a real midnight crossing, not a sub-second rounding difference.

**Actual.** prevT is seeded with the full-millisecond frontmatter start — src/main/recall.ts:216 `let prevT: number | undefined = startedAt` (parsed from the ISO `date:` written by saveMeeting at transcripts.ts:688, which keeps milliseconds) — while every reconstructed line time is floored to whole seconds at src/main/recall.ts:221 `d.setHours(Number(hh), Number(mm), Number(ss), 0)`. So whenever the first line falls in the SAME wall-clock second as the start, `d.getTime() < prevT` is true for a purely sub-second reason and recall.ts:225 `d.setDate(d.getDate() + 1)` fires; prevT is then a day ahead, so every subsequent line is pushed too. Imported meetings always hit this: src/main/import-jobs.ts:333 `startedAt: job.sourceMtimeMs` and src/main/import-jobs.ts:284 `t: job.sourceMtimeMs + seq * CHUNK_MS`, so line 0's timestamp equals startedAt exactly, and a real file mtime almost never lands on a whole second.

**Repro.** Import `call.wav` whose mtime is 2026-08-01 12:34:56.437. saveMeeting writes `date: 2026-08-01T16:34:56.437Z` and the first line as `**[12:34:56] Speaker:** …`. Verified with a standalone Node replay of transcripts.ts's line rendering plus recall.ts:211-232: recallRead returns line 0 at `Sun Aug 02 2026 12:34:56` and lines 1-2 at `Sun Aug 02 12:35:26 / 12:35:56` — the entire transcript sits one calendar day after the meeting's own date. Downstream, backfillSpeakerNames computes `const endedAt = read.lines[read.lines.length - 1].t` (src/main/index.ts:1773) ≈ startedAt + 24h and calls findJoinUrlFromCalendar, which queries Graph calendarView over `[startedAt - 15min, endedAt + 15min]` — a ~24.5-hour window — and takes the FIRST event with a joinUrl (src/main/graph-transcript.ts:44-55), i.e. very likely an unrelated meeting whose Teams transcript is then fetched; the 24h offset then defeats the time-proximity match, so the result is always `named: 0`. Re-deriving duration from these lines yields 1441 minutes for a one-minute recording.

**Suggested fix.** Floor the seed to the same resolution as the reconstructed times: `let prevT = startedAt !== undefined ? Math.floor(startedAt / 1000) * 1000 : undefined` at src/main/recall.ts:216 (or compare with a 1000ms tolerance before pushing the day at recall.ts:225). Add a recall.test.ts case saving with a startedAt whose ms component is non-zero and a first line in the same second, asserting `lines[0].t` stays on the meeting's own calendar day.

**Verifier.** Could not refute; reproduced the full chain. (1) transcripts.ts:688 writes `date: <ISO with milliseconds>`; recall.ts:181-184 parses it back at full ms precision (frontmatter() at recall.ts:12-21 strips nothing from that value). (2) recall.ts:217 seeds `prevT = startedAt` at ms precision, while recall.ts:221 `d.setHours(hh,mm,ss,0)` floors to the whole second because formatTranscriptLine (transcripts.ts:587-593) only renders HH:MM:SS. (3) recall.ts:225 therefore fires `d.setDate(d.getDate()+1)` on a pure sub-second rounding difference, and prevT then carries the day shift to every later line. Imported meetings hit it deterministically: import-jobs.ts:333 `startedAt: job.sourceMtimeMs` and :284 `t: sourceMtimeMs + seq*CHUNK_MS` make line 0's t equal startedAt exactly; sourceMtimeMs is raw statSync().mtimeMs (import-audio.ts:69/89) and ipc.ts:327 is only z.number().finite() with no int coercion. Empirically sampled 15 real files: 15/15 had a non-zero sub-second component. Verbatim replay of transcripts.ts:587-593 + recall.ts:180-232 with IMPORT_CHUNK_SECONDS=12 and mtime 2026-08-01 12:34:56.437 returns all lines at Sun Aug 02, delta exactly +24.000h; with .000 ms it does not fire, and a genuine 23:59:30 crossing still works, so the guard's stated purpose (recall.ts:222-224, quoted accurately) is intact and only the sub-second case misfires. No guard/caller/schema/test prevents it: recallRead's only callers are App.tsx:1898 and index.ts:1780, and all 27 tests in src/main/recall.test.ts (run green via node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs) use startedAt=1_700_000_000_000, i.e. ms%1000===0, the one value that escapes. Severity stays low because two of the finder's downstream claims do not hold: nothing re-derives duration against startedAt on this path (Review.tsx:306-318 uses max(times)-min(times), invariant under a uniform shift; saveMeeting's durMin at transcripts.ts:676-677 is never re-run on recalled lines since resumePastMeeting at App.tsx:1922-1933 discards them), and the shift is invisible in the UI (Review.tsx:13-19 clock() renders time-of-day only) and never corrupts the file (updateMeetingTranscript -> formatTranscript re-emits identical HH:MM:SS). The one live consequence is real but narrow: backfillSpeakerNames (index.ts:1784, not 1773) computes endedAt from the shifted last line, widening findJoinUrlFromCalendar's window to ~24.5h (graph-transcript.ts:44-48, first joinUrl wins at :52-55) and guaranteeing named:0 via MATCH_WINDOW_MS=45_000 (shared/transcript-align.ts:83/145) — but imports bypass the auto-backfill (they call saveMeeting directly at index.ts:804, not the IPC handler at index.ts:3194) and recallBackfillSpeakers has no wired UI caller yet, so it is reachable only through the preload IPC. Fix is trivial: seed the guard at the comparison's own resolution, e.g. `Math.floor(startedAt/1000)*1000`.

### MQA-098 — docs/cahe-windows-edition.md tells the pilot security reviewer the Kimi key is not in the installer, while the build hard-fails without it and embeds it

**Where.** `docs/cahe-windows-edition.md:16` · workflow: Cahê pilot security / compliance review and first-run setup · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/cahe-embedded-key.ts:69-73 — "Cahê pilot builds ship with a Kimi API key baked into the installer — this is an intentional, user-authorized embed for the Cahê pilot only, disclosed (not sneaky): electron-builder.cahe.win.yml's extraResources copies the locally-provided build/cahe-kimi.local.json to resources/cahe/kimi.json…" electron-builder.cahe.win.yml:16-17 — "The key IS extractable from the installer by anyone who has it."

**Actual.** docs/cahe-windows-edition.md:16 instructs the pilot user to "enter Cahê's Kimi Code key" by hand and states "It is not included in this installer or source tree" — the opposite of what ships. scripts/build-cahe-windows.mjs:45-51 throws unless `build/cahe-kimi.local.json` exists (only `METIS_CAHE_ALLOW_KEYLESS=1` opts out), and line 44/56 then sets METIS_CAHE_EMBED_KEY=1 so the key is packed. docs line 30 repeats the check-cahe-package.mjs claim that the gate "fails if a Kimi-shaped secret is found in the app archive or installer", which cannot fire (see the check-cahe-package finding).

**Repro.** A reviewer performing the "Pilot boundary" assessment (docs/cahe-windows-edition.md:34) reads line 16, concludes no credential ships in the artifact, and approves distribution. The delivered Metis-Windows-Cahe-Setup-1.5.3.exe installs resources/cahe/kimi.json containing a live `sk-kimi-…` key readable by any local user, and src/main/cahe-embedded-key.ts:115-127 seeds it into the profile on first run. The doc also mis-describes first run: the user is told to paste a key that is already configured.

**Suggested fix.** Rewrite the first-run and pilot-boundary sections to state plainly that the installer embeds a scoped, rotatable Kimi key, that it is extractable by anyone with the installer, and how to rotate/revoke it — mirroring the disclosure text already in cahe-embedded-key.ts:69-77 and electron-builder.cahe.win.yml:13-18. If a keyless pilot is what the doc describes, build with METIS_CAHE_ALLOW_KEYLESS=1 instead.

**Verifier.** Could not refute the core factual claim; I did refute part of the repro narrative, which is why I lower the severity.

VERIFIED — the doc statement is false for the default build path:
- D:\Asktoto\docs\cahe-windows-edition.md:16 reads verbatim: "In Métis Settings → AI, enter Cahê's Kimi Code key. When entered there, it is saved in the app's encrypted local profile. It is not included in this installer or source tree."
- D:\Asktoto\scripts\build-cahe-windows.mjs:27-51 throws when build/cahe-kimi.local.json is absent or lacks an sk-kimi- token; the only opt-out is METIS_CAHE_ALLOW_KEYLESS=1 (line 25). Line 44/56 then sets METIS_CAHE_EMBED_KEY=1 in the child env for the electron-builder run at line 77-87.
- D:\Asktoto\electron-builder.cahe.win.yml:19-21 extraResources copies build/cahe-kimi.local.json → cahe/kimi.json, so the key ships inside the artifact. build/cahe-kimi.local.json exists on this machine (102 B), so `npm run installers:win:cahe` here embeds a real key.
- D:\Asktoto\src\main\cahe-embedded-key.ts:115-127 reads process.resourcesPath/cahe/kimi.json on first run and calls setApiKey('kimi', …); wired at src\main\index.ts:3981. So the user is told to paste a key that is already seeded.
- The cited "intended behavior" quotes are accurate, not paraphrase: cahe-embedded-key.ts:69-74 says pilot builds "ship with a Kimi API key baked into the installer"; electron-builder.cahe.win.yml:16-17 says "The key IS extractable from the installer by anyone who has it."

Provenance confirms staleness rather than a deliberate statement: the doc was created at commit e3dbc57 when nothing was embedded (the line was true then); the embed landed in 63c5638 and was hardened in 67ca37f, and `git show --stat` shows neither commit touched docs/cahe-windows-edition.md.

No guard exists. `grep` for "cahe-windows-edition" across the repo hits only docs/WINDOWS.md — no doc-lint, no contract test. I ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/cahe-embedded-key.test.ts scripts/cahe-package.contract.test.ts (9 tests, all pass): they assert the embed/packaging contract and never look at the doc.

Second stale claim in the same doc holds too: line 30 says the build "fails if a Kimi-shaped secret is found in the app archive or installer", but check-cahe-package.mjs:66,89-93 downgrades that to a warning whenever METIS_CAHE_EMBED_KEY=1 — which build-cahe-windows.mjs:56 sets automatically on every keyed build. So the stated verification guarantee does not apply to any shipped Cahê installer.

WHY SEVERITY DROPS TO LOW: the finder's repro ("reviewer concludes no credential ships and approves distribution") is undercut by the same 35-line doc. Line 9 already states Kimi is "seeded once on first run from a bundled key" — the embed is disclosed seven lines above the contradiction, so the doc is self-contradictory rather than concealing. docs/WINDOWS.md:145-190 documents the extraResources embed, the METIS_CAHE_EMBED_KEY=1 requirement, and the one-time seed accurately, and check-cahe-package.mjs:69-79 prints a loud extractability warning at packaging time. Real harm is a wrong first-run instruction plus one false sentence a reviewer could quote — documentation-only, no code path affected. Fix is rewriting two sentences (lines 16 and 30).

### MQA-099 — capturingRef double-capture guard is never armed — a double-click or hotkey+click fires two screen captures and two billed vision requests

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:819` · workflow: capture the screen and ask about it · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/App.tsx:302-307 — "Synchronous in-flight guard for askScreen(): capturing (state) only flips true via startTransition, so two fast triggers (double-click / hotkey-plus-click) both read the OLD `capturing` and both start a capture before the deferred state update ever commits — mirrors listen.ts's startingRef pattern. Set at the very top of askScreen, before any `await`; cleared in its `finally`. `capturing` (state) still drives the UI exactly as before."

**Actual.** `capturingRef` is declared at App.tsx:307 and cleared at App.tsx:915, but is never set to `true` anywhere (grep over App.tsx returns exactly those two occurrences) and is never read. The only guard in `askScreen` is App.tsx:819 `if (capturing) return null` — the state value the comment explicitly says is insufficient — and `setCapturing(true)` sits inside `startTransition` at App.tsx:828-833, so it has not committed when the second trigger runs.

**Repro.** Configure any vision-capable provider. Double-click the Bar's camera button (two clicks inside ~50 ms), or press the Capture hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+S) while clicking the camera button. Both invocations read `capturing === false` from the same render's closure, both pass App.tsx:819, both call `await window.toto.capture()` (App.tsx:860) and both call `ask.run({mode:'vision', ...})` (App.tsx:866). Result: two OS captures, two image uploads billed to the provider, and the first run's `finally` (App.tsx:914-917) clears `capturing` while the second is still in flight, so the busy state disappears early.

**Suggested fix.** Do what the comment says: add `if (capturingRef.current) return null; capturingRef.current = true` as the first statements of `askScreen` (before `requireProvider`'s await-free check is fine, but definitely before the first `await`), keep the `finally` clear, and drop `capturing` from the useCallback dep array so the guard cannot go stale. Add a test that two synchronous `askScreen` calls produce exactly one `window.toto.capture()` call.

**Verifier.** CORE DEFECT CONFIRMED — I could not refute it.

1. The ref really is inert. Grep over all of src/ returns exactly two hits: `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:307` (`const capturingRef = useRef(false)`) and `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:915` (`capturingRef.current = false`). Never assigned `true`, never read.

2. The "intended behavior" quote is verbatim and does say what the finder claims. App.tsx:302-307 states the ref must be "Set at the very top of askScreen, before any `await`; cleared in its `finally`." Only the second half was implemented. `git show 6b75daf -- src/renderer/src/App.tsx` (the commit that introduced it) adds exactly two lines: `+ const capturingRef = useRef(false)` and `+ capturingRef.current = false`. The arm and the read were never written — a half-implemented guard that contradicts its own documented contract.

3. No other layer closes it. The only guard is App.tsx:819 `if (capturing) return null`, against state that flips inside `startTransition` at App.tsx:828-833 — precisely the insufficiency the comment describes. Bar's capture button is never disabled (Bar.tsx:556-558 only swaps the icon to `<Spinner>`; `onClick={props.onCapture}` stays live). The hotkey path App.tsx:1969 → `capture` (App.tsx:1397) → `askScreen` has no debounce. Main's `IPC.captureScreen` handler (index.ts:2684-2688) has no dedupe. The window is genuinely widened on the first screen-ask of a session: per App.tsx:820-827 and state.ts:391-393, React always suspends the lazy `<Answer>`'s first render, so the transition does not commit and `capturing` stays false in the committed tree for the whole chunk-resolution window.

IMPACT MATERIALLY OVERSTATED — two of the three claimed harms die:

- "two OS captures" is REFUTED. index.ts:1304 wraps `captureScreenshotOnce` in `createKeyedSingleFlight` keyed by display id (screen-capture.ts:55-71), and `getScreenshot` serves a TTL cache at index.ts:1328 with `CAPTURE_TTL_MS = 1500` (index.ts:1232).
