Two `capture()` calls tens of ms apart on the same display coalesce into ONE native capture; both callers get the identical JPEG.
- "two billed vision requests" is WEAKENED to at most one aborted duplicate. state.ts:376 (`if (idRef.current) void window.toto.cancel(idRef.current)`) fires before the second ask. Main's `askStart` handler (index.ts:2712) is a NON-async arrow, and it reaches `attempt(...)` synchronously at index.ts:3156, which registers `streams.set(req.id, handle)` at index.ts:3125. So the follow-on `askCancel` (index.ts:3165-3168) definitively finds and aborts stream A. Realistic outcome: one vision request dispatched then aborted within ~ms (possible partial input-token billing, not a guaranteed double charge) plus the one real request.
- "busy state disappears early" is negligible: both invocations resolve from the SAME single-flight promise, so their `finally` blocks (App.tsx:914-917) run microseconds apart, not with a visible gap.

VERDICT: real bug (a guard documented and half-wired, leaving a genuine re-entrancy hole), but the blast radius is one redundant, promptly-aborted provider request — not duplicate screen captures and not a clean double charge. Severity corrected medium → low.

FIX NOTE (read-only, nothing changed): the arm must go immediately before the `try` at App.tsx:834, not before the early returns at 818-819 — the `finally` at 914 only covers the try block, so arming above those bare `return null` paths would latch the ref permanently and dead-lock all future screen asks.

### MQA-100 — on-device extraction returns invalid JSON often enough to fail real meetings

**Intended.** `brain/ingest.ts` parses the model reply as JSON and throws `No complete JSON object in
model output` when it cannot. With `localLlm.fallback` defaulting on, on-device extraction is now the
DEFAULT path for anyone without a working cloud key, so it has to be dependable, not merely usually right.

**Actual.** The bundled Qwen3.5-0.8B intermittently emits an unterminated object. Nothing constrained the
decoding, so validity was left to chance.

**Repro (observed live, not theorised).** A physical run of `scripts/qa/e2e-workflows.mjs` against a cold
zero-key profile indexed the same fixture meeting successfully on three earlier runs and failed on the
fourth: `brainStatus.failedDetails` = `[{ file: "2026-08-07-acme-renewal.md", error: "No complete JSON
object in model output", exhausted: false }]`, and the commitments check went from 3 extracted to 0. The
error string predates this session (present at 4245cbf), so it is a long-standing reliability limit that
only became load-bearing when local became the default fallback.

**Fix.** `response_format: { type: "json_object" }` on the local extraction call only. llama-server
compiles it into a GBNF grammar and masks every token that would break JSON syntax, so an unterminated
object stops being representable rather than merely unlikely. It joins openai.ts's existing
drop-on-rejection ladder, so a runtime without the feature degrades to today's behaviour instead of
failing the request. Cloud providers are deliberately excluded: they already return well-formed JSON, and
sending a param some proxies reject would risk a working path to fix one that is not broken.

**Model note.** Replacing the 0.8B with a larger model (Qwen3.5 2B/4B, Phi-4-mini 3.8B) would raise raw
quality, but the app deliberately moved DOWN to 0.8B (a retired `qwen3.5-2b` id still appears in the
settings migration), and a 2B/4B Q4 would roughly double-to-triple the ~730 MB installer payload and the
RAM floor. Constrained decoding fixes the actual failure — JSON validity — at zero size cost, so it is
the right first move; a model upgrade remains a separate, size-budget decision.


> MQA-101..MQA-110 came from a 5-Sonnet re-audit (2026-08-09) of the state after the first 100
> findings were logged and 88 fixed. It verified the 88 fixes hold under adversarial re-tracing and found
> 10 new issues — 7 of them gaps or regressions in this session's own fixes, which is exactly what a
> re-audit exists to catch.

### MQA-101 — The circuit breaker's own auth-failure detector doesn't recognize the current, documented Dust auth-rejection phrasing — cooldown never trips for a genuinely dead Dust session, and the raw provider string reaches the user instead of the friendly message

**Where.** `src/main/llm/provider-health.ts:60` · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/llm/dust.ts:27-31 (module comment, right above the function the codebase already built for exactly this): "A Dust OAuth token that has expired surfaces as a 401 before any answer token — but the exact wording drifts across Dust API versions ... and (current) 'the user request does not have a valid authenticated credential'." src/main/llm/provider-health.ts:52-58 states isAuthFailure's job is to answer "Does this failure mean 'your credentials were rejected'?" for exactly this class of message, and the module doc (lines 4-11) says MQA-003/004 exist so a dead credential is remembered and the UI stops claiming providerReady:true.

**Actual.** src/main/llm/provider-health.ts:60-74 `isAuthFailure()` has no pattern matching Dust's own documented "authenticat...credential" phrasing (no 401/403/402 digits, no "unauthor", no "invalid api key", no "key...invalid/expired/revoked", no "insufficient quota/credit", no "permission denied"). src/main/index.ts:3239 `if (!gotToken && isAuthFailure(message)) recordAuthFailure(provider, String(message))` therefore never fires for this message, so src/main/index.ts:3315's `isCoolingDown(primary)` check never demotes Dust. The SAME gap exists one level up: index.ts:3267-3269's Dust-specific friendly-message regex (`/oauth|unauthor|expired|authentication credential|invalid.*(token|credential)/i`) also does not match "authenticated credential" (it only matches the literal noun "authentication credential", not the adjectival "authenticated credential" Dust's current API actually emits), so the raw string falls through to index.ts:3280's `: message` and is shown to the user verbatim. Meanwhile `isDustAuthError` (llm/dust.ts:34-41, used only for the refresh-and-retry decision at dust.ts:268-274 and for the unrelated Settings agent-picker at index.ts:2266) and retry.ts's `AUTH_PATTERN` (retry.ts:50-51, via `authenticat\w*\s+credential`) BOTH already recognize this exact phrasing — isAuthFailure is the only one of the three that doesn't.

**Repro.** Verified by executing the real exported functions against the module's own documented "(current)" Dust phrasing (not simulated): `isDustAuthError({ message: 'The user request does not have a valid authenticated credential.' })` -> true; `isAuthFailure('The user request does not have a valid authenticated credential.')` -> false (ran both via `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run` against a temporary co-located test file importing the two real modules, then removed the file — repo left clean, confirmed via `git status --porcelain`). Chain: Dust session is dead and `refreshDustAuth()` fails (dust.ts:270-271 `if (!fresh) return false`) -> dust.ts:385 `fail(created.error.message)` hands index.ts this exact raw string -> index.ts:3239 never calls recordAuthFailure -> index.ts:3315 `isCoolingDown('dust')` stays false forever -> Dust is retried FIRST on every single ask (typed question, screen vision, and the ~15s live-suggest loop), each paying a doomed round trip plus a failed refresh attempt, and if Dust is the only configured provider the user sees the literal string "The user request does not have a valid authenticated credential." with no Settings pointer, on every ask, indefinitely.

**Suggested fix.** Reuse the already-broadened `isDustAuthError` from llm/dust.ts instead of the narrower `isAuthFailure` when provider === 'dust' (index.ts already imports it at line 120) — e.g. at index.ts:3239 use `(provider === 'dust' ? isDustAuthError({ message }) : isAuthFailure(message))`, and apply the same swap to the friendly-message branch at index.ts:3267-3269 (or simplest: fold Dust's `authenticat\w*\s+credential|credential.*authenticat` pattern directly into provider-health.ts's isAuthFailure so all three call sites agree on one definition).

**Verifier.** Fully reproduced the causal chain, not just read the code.

1. src/main/llm/dust.ts:27-31 (module comment) documents the exact current Dust auth-rejection phrasing: "the user request does not have a valid authenticated credential." isDustAuthError (dust.ts:34-41) matches it via `authenticat\w*\s+credential` — verified true by executing the real function.

2. src/main/llm/provider-health.ts:60-74 isAuthFailure has no pattern that matches "authenticated credential" (no digits, no "unauthor", no "invalid...token/credential", no "key...invalid/expired/revoked", nothing). Verified false by executing the real function against the exact documented string.

3. src/main/index.ts:3239 `if (!gotToken && isAuthFailure(message)) recordAuthFailure(...)` therefore never fires for this message → src/main/index.ts:3315 `isCoolingDown(primary)` never trips for Dust on this failure mode → the circuit breaker (MQA-003/004, whose own module doc at provider-health.ts:4-11 says this is its entire purpose) is dead for the documented-current Dust error.

4. src/main/index.ts:3268's Dust-specific friendly regex `/oauth|unauthor|expired|authentication credential|invalid.*(token|credential)/i` also does not match "authenticated credential" (adjectival form vs. the regex's literal noun-phrase "authentication credential") — verified false by executing the actual regex against the actual string. Since def.kind for 'dust' is 'dust', not 'cli' (confirmed in src/shared/providers.ts), the CLI branch at index.ts:3273 is skipped, isAuthFailure(message) at 3278 is also false, so control falls through to index.ts:3280 `: message`, surfacing the raw provider string to the user with no Settings pointer.

5. Confirmed retry.ts's AUTH_PATTERN (line 50-51) DOES already contain `authenticat\w*\s+credential|credential.*authenticat` — i.e., the exact fix already exists elsewhere in the codebase but was never applied to provider-health.ts's isAuthFailure or index.ts's friendly-message regex, making this a genuine, narrow, easily-fixable inconsistency rather than a design choice.

6. Checked src/main/llm/provider-health.test.ts and src/main/provider-health-ux.contract.test.ts — neither tests isAuthFailure against the Dust "authenticated credential" phrasing, so no existing guard/test catches this gap.

7. Ran the exact repro via a temporary co-located vitest file (removed after, confirmed via git status --porcelain — clean): isDustAuthError → true, isAuthFailure → false, friendly regex → false. All three match the finder's claims exactly.

Severity: "high" is justified, not inflated — this disables the circuit breaker entirely for the single most common real-world Dust failure (dead session + failed refresh), on every ask (typed, vision, and the ~15s live-suggest loop), and leaves the user staring at a raw, unhelpful provider string instead of the "reconnect Dust" guidance the codebase clearly intended (mirrors the historical MQA-003/004/005 bug class already fixed for other phrasings). Not "critical" since no data loss/security impact, so "high" is the correct tier as claimed.

Fix is small: add the same regex fragment already present in retry.ts's AUTH_PATTERN to provider-health.ts's isAuthFailure pattern list, and extend index.ts:3268's friendly-message regex the same way.

### MQA-102 — MQA-020's belt-and-braces fix explicitly excludes Métis Local, but nothing else surfaces a local zero-content completion as an error — the exact blank-bubble bug MQA-020 fixed for cloud/CLI is still live for the on-device last-resort fallback

**Where.** `src/main/index.ts:3218` · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:3212-3217 (the handler's own comment): "a provider that completes with ZERO content deltas has not answered — the user gets a blank bubble and the waterfall stops, because 'done' reads as success. ... ANY strategy that reaches onDone pre-token has the same effect, so treat it as a pre-token failure here ... Only for cloud/CLI: a local no-output must surface rather than silently upload the request." — i.e. local must still surface an error, just never fail over to cloud.

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:3218 `if (!gotToken && provider !== 'local' && failover(attempted.concat(provider))) return` is the ONLY branch guarding the blank-onDone case; for `provider === 'local'` this condition is unconditionally false (regardless of `gotToken`), so execution falls straight through to line 3231's unconditional `win?.webContents.send(IPC.streamDone, { id: req.id, ...u })` — a normal success message, not an error. Nothing else in the onDone handler, and nothing in src/main/llm/openai.ts's streamOpenAI (which streamLocal delegates to per llm/local.ts:177-186), converts a plain empty completion (sawContent=false AND sawReasoning=false) into an error — openai.ts:198-201 only special-cases `sawReasoning && !sawContent` (the Kimi-reasoning-exhausted-budget case), not the reasoning-free empty-completion case. On the renderer, src/renderer/src/state.ts:321-329 confirms there is no fallback: `onDone` with `noOutput = pendingReplaceRef.current === true` sets `text: ''` and leaves `error` unset entirely — the exact "no error, no hint" outcome MQA-020 rated high for cloud/CLI.

**Repro.** Local fallback engaged after every cloud provider is exhausted (the lens's own 'my API key died' end state) or local used directly. The on-device model (per this repo's own docs the smallest bundled model already shown to misbehave under tight output budgets — MQA-100, MQA-006) returns a completion with zero content deltas and zero reasoning deltas (plausible under LOCAL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_BUDGETS.suggest=96 or a sampling quirk producing an immediate stop token) -> streamOpenAI's for-await loop finishes with sawContent=false, sawReasoning=false -> openai.ts:203 `opts.handlers.onDone({...})` fires with gotToken never having been set true -> index.ts:3218's guard is skipped for 'local' -> index.ts:3231 sends a normal IPC.streamDone -> state.ts:327-329 sets `text: ''` with no `error` -> the user sees the idle 'Ask a question...' placeholder, indistinguishable from never having asked, exactly on the path this whole lens traces (everything else already failed, local was the last hope, and it fails silently too).

**Suggested fix.** In the onDone handler, branch explicitly on `provider === 'local'` instead of letting the existing `provider !== 'local'` guard silently no-op: when `!gotToken && provider === 'local'`, send `IPC.streamError` with an actionable message (e.g. "Métis Local produced no answer — try again.") instead of falling through to `IPC.streamDone`. Add a regression test alongside the existing MQA-020 cli.test.ts coverage that drives a local zero-delta completion through index.ts's onDone and asserts an error reaches the renderer, not a blank success.

**Verifier.** Verified the full causal chain in the repo.

1. src/main/index.ts:3210-3231 (onDone handler): the comment at 3212-3217 is quoted verbatim by the finder and matches the file exactly ("a provider that completes with ZERO content deltas has not answered... Only for cloud/CLI: a local no-output must surface rather than silently upload the request."). The code at 3218 is `if (!gotToken && provider !== 'local' && failover(attempted.concat(provider))) return` — for provider==='local' this is always false regardless of gotToken, so execution falls straight through to the unconditional `win?.webContents.send(IPC.streamDone, { id: req.id, ...u })` at line 3231. Grepped the whole file for every `=== 'local'` occurrence (lines 709, 724, 2968, 3037, 3043, 3069, 3160) — none of them add any post-onDone check that would convert a local zero-content completion into an error. The comment's stated intent ("a local no-output must surface") is not actually implemented anywhere; only the failover-suppression half of the sentence is coded.

2. src/main/llm/local.ts:117-187 (streamLocal/runLlama) confirms local delegates straight to `streamOpenAI` from openai.ts with only a wrapped onDone/onError for idle-timer bookkeeping (lines 148-160) — it does not inspect content/reasoning at all.

3. src/main/llm/openai.ts:146-203 confirms `sawContent`/`sawReasoning` are tracked per-chunk, and the ONLY place they gate onDone vs onError is line 198: `if (usageResult.sawReasoning && !usageResult.sawContent)` → onError. When BOTH are false (a genuinely empty completion — zero content, zero reasoning), execution falls through to `opts.handlers.onDone(...)` at line 203, exactly as claimed. No other branch handles sawContent===false && sawReasoning===false.

4. src/renderer/src/state.ts:321-329 confirms the renderer's onDone handler: `noOutput = pendingReplaceRef.current`, then `setAnswer((a) => (a ? { ...a, streaming: false, text: noOutput ? '' : a.text } : a))` — error is never touched/set on this path, so it stays whatever it was (null on a fresh answer).

5. src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:352-361 confirms that `!text` with `streaming=false` and `error=null` renders literally "Ask a question or press ... to capture your screen." — the idle placeholder, indistinguishable from never having asked, exactly as the finder describes.

6. Ran the relevant test suites (`local-cloud-boundary.contract.test.ts`, `index-audit-fixes.contract.test.ts`, `llm.test.ts`, `local.engine.test.ts`) — all 54 tests pass with the code as-is, confirming no existing test catches or exercises this exact gap (sawContent=false && sawReasoning=false routed through local). `local-cloud-boundary.contract.test.ts`'s "never sends a failed local request to a cloud failover provider" test only pins the onError-path failover guard (line 3262), not the onDone-path error-surfacing gap at 3218.

7. Cross-checked docs/qa/BUG-LEDGER.md's MQA-020 entry (line 49, 607-615): confirms MQA-020's origin was specifically claude-cli's is_error mis-settlement, and the index.ts:3218 guard is described in-code as the generalized "belt-and-braces half" — a defense-in-depth extension to ANY strategy reaching onDone pre-token. The ledger does not show a separate fixed MQA entry for the local-specific "must surface" half described in the same comment, consistent with this being a genuine unimplemented half of that comment's stated intent rather than something already covered elsewhere.

I could not refute any link in the chain: the quoted comment is verbatim and accurately located, the guard demonstrably never fires for provider==='local' regardless of gotToken, no downstream code (local.ts, openai.ts, index.ts, state.ts, Answer.tsx) converts a reasoning-free empty completion into an error for local, and no test currently exercises or prevents this path. The repro condition (zero content AND zero reasoning deltas) is a real, if narrower, subset of "provider completes pre-token" — plausible under the documented tight local suggest budget (96 tokens) or an immediate-EOS sampling quirk on the already-flagged-flaky bundled model (MQA-100/MQA-006 precedent for this model misbehaving under tight budgets).

Severity: keeping HIGH as claimed. This is the same UX-failure class as MQA-020 (rated high) — a blank bubble indistinguishable from never asking — but occurring on the terminal/last-resort step of the degradation waterfall where, by design, there is no further failover to rescue the user (unlike cloud providers, which can still fail over or retry). That makes the user-facing consequence at least as severe as the bug MQA-020 fixed elsewhere.

### MQA-103 — GDPR/CCPA 'Delete all my data' silently SKIPS a real, hand-renamed meeting transcript hit by a transient read error, and still reports success

**Where.** `src/main/recall.ts:661` · regression of MQA-032 · fix size: unknown

**Intended.** src/main/recall.ts:654-660 (isOwnedMeetingFile's own doc comment, written for this fix): 'True when this file is one of Métis's own... Used as the ownership check for a file whose NAME no longer matches Métis's own shape (a transcript the user renamed by hand), so an erasure request still erases it.' The same file establishes, two functions earlier (recall.ts:106-112, the MQA-033 UNREADABLE sentinel), the invariant a 'could not read it right now' error must never be treated the same as a confirmed negative verdict.

**Actual.** src/main/recall.ts:661-670: `if (DRAFT_FILENAME.test(file) || FILENAME_TIMESTAMP.test(file)) return true` only fast-paths Métis's own standard `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS-*.md` filenames without reading them. For any file that does NOT match that shape — precisely the hand-renamed-transcript case the doc comment calls out — isOwnedMeetingFile falls to `try { readFile... } catch { return false }` (line 668-669). A THROWN read (EBUSY/EPERM from the same OneDrive/AV lock class this codebase documents as routine in this exact folder, transcripts.ts:292-295) is indistinguishable from 'confirmed not ours' and returns false. deleteAllMeetings (recall.ts:696-698) then adds the file to `skipped`, never unlinks it, and still returns `ok: true` (recall.ts:712, `ok: failed.length === 0` — skipped files don't count as failed). Settings.tsx:5728-5729 renders the success path ('Deleted N meetings.') with zero mention of `skipped`.

**Repro.** Save a meeting (default flow gives it `type: meeting-transcript` frontmatter). Rename the file via File Explorer (not the app's in-app rename, which only edits the frontmatter title — the file is never renamed by the app, recall.ts:459) to something that no longer matches the timestamp pattern, e.g. `renault-kickoff.md`, keeping its frontmatter. While the file is transiently locked (OneDrive upload-hash lock, AV/EDR real-time scan, or a Files-On-Demand dehydrated placeholder while offline — the same trigger class MQA-033's own fix targets in this file), trigger 'Delete all my data'. Empirically confirmed with a scratch vitest test mirroring recall.test.ts's existing MQA-032/MQA-033 test infrastructure (its `unreadablePaths` EBUSY-injecting fs mock plus the `renault-kickoff.md` renamed-file fixture from recall.test.ts:624-625, combined — a combination neither existing test suite exercises): `deleteAllMeetings()` returned `{ ok: true, deleted: 1, failed: [], skipped: ['renault-kickoff.md'] }` and the renamed meeting file was still present on disk after the wipe. The scratch test file was deleted afterward per the read-only constraint; git status is clean of it.

**Suggested fix.** Distinguish 'confirmed not ours' from 'could not read it right now' the same way MQA-033's UNREADABLE sentinel already does two functions above this one in the same file: on a thrown read, return an explicit tri-state (or push the file into a new `unreadable: string[]` used by the caller as `failed`, not `skipped`) rather than collapsing to `false`. deleteAllMeetings should surface an unreadable-but-plausibly-owned file as a genuine failure (so `ok` goes false and the renderer's error path fires) rather than silently folding it into the same `skipped` bucket as the user's own unrelated markdown.

**Verifier.** Traced the full chain and reproduced it empirically.

Code: isOwnedMeetingFile (recall.ts:661-671) fast-paths only Métis's own filename shapes (DRAFT_FILENAME/FILENAME_TIMESTAMP, line 662). For anything else — including a hand-renamed transcript — it falls into `try { readFile...; check frontmatter } catch { return false }` (668-669). A THROWN read (not a decode failure, an fs-level throw) is caught by the same generic catch and collapses to `false` — i.e. "not ours" — with no distinction from a confirmed non-owned file. This directly contradicts the tri-state discipline the same file already established two functions earlier: readMeetingUncached (144-153) and the UNREADABLE sentinel (106-112) explicitly split "could not read it right now" from "confirmed not a meeting," specifically because a thrown read is not a negative verdict. isOwnedMeetingFile does not reuse that sentinel/retry pattern at all (grep for EBUSY/EPERM/retry in recall.ts finds nothing outside the MQA-033 machinery).

deleteAllMeetings (696-698) treats `isOwnedMeetingFile === false` as "skip, don't unlink" and pushes to `skipped`, which is NOT counted toward `failed`. `ok: failed.length === 0` (712) stays true. index.ts:2711-2720 passes the result straight through with no additional check. Settings.tsx:5717-5734 renders `result.ok ? 'Deleted N meetings.' : ...` — the `skipped` array is never read or surfaced in the UI at all, success or failure branch.

Verified transcripts.ts:290-305 independently documents that this exact folder (OneDrive-synced by default) "routinely" throws EPERM/EBUSY from AV/EDR or upload-hashing — the same trigger class the finder invokes, and the codebase's own justification for MQA-033's UNREADABLE handling — so the read-throw precondition is not far-fetched, it's a documented recurring condition in this exact code path's neighborhood.

Empirical reproduction: wrote a scratch vitest file (`src/main/recall.mqa034-verify.test.ts`, deleted after, git status confirmed clean) mirroring recall.test.ts's existing `unreadablePaths` EBUSY-injection mock. Created `renault-kickoff.md` with `type: meeting-transcript` frontmatter (a filename that fails both DRAFT_FILENAME and FILENAME_TIMESTAMP), added its path to unreadablePaths, called the real `deleteAllMeetings()`. Result: `{"ok":true,"deleted":0,"failed":[],"skipped":["renault-kickoff.md"]}` and the file was confirmed still on disk (`existsSync === true`) after the wipe — exactly the claimed outcome.

No guard, caller, or test in the repo prevents this: recall.test.ts's MQA-032 renamed-file test (line 619-637) exercises the renamed-filename ownership path but never combines it with a read failure; MQA-033's tests (from line 644) exercise the read-failure sentinel but only through listMeetings/searchMeetings, never through isOwnedMeetingFile/deleteAllMeetings. The intersection is genuinely untested and genuinely broken.

Severity: the finder's "high" is defensible — this is a GDPR/CCPA erasure primitive that (a) leaves a real, sensitive meeting transcript un-erased and (b) actively reports success with zero UI signal of the gap, directly regressing the stated purpose of MQA-032's own fix ("so an erasure request still erases it"). The trigger requires two conditions to coincide (hand-renamed file + transient lock), which is a real but non-trivial precondition — I considered downgrading to medium for that narrowness, but the transient-lock condition is independently documented in this codebase as routine on this exact folder, and the consequence (silent, unrecoverable-looking compliance failure with no retry signal) is severe enough that high is the more defensible call than medium. Fix is medium complexity: extend isOwnedMeetingFile to a tri-state (owned/not-owned/unreadable) mirroring the existing UNREADABLE sentinel, thread a distinct 'skipped due to read error' bucket through deleteAllMeetings's return shape and index.ts's audit log, and update Settings.tsx to surface skip-with-uncertainty distinctly from skip-because-foreign-file (and probably make `ok` false, or at least the headline copy conditional, when any file was skipped for read-failure reasons).

### MQA-104 — Cancel racing the ingest-queue write resurrects the job as 'done' and never deletes the meeting file — the opposite of what the user clicked

**Where.** `src/main/import-jobs.ts:374` · regression of MQA-024 · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/import-jobs.ts:456-459 (abandonIfCancelled's own doc comment, written for the MQA-024 fix): 'Every bail-out after saveMeeting() has landed must go through here. cancel() has already erased the checkpoint and the renderer hides cancelled cards, so a bare `return` would strand the meeting file and its index.md row on disk — a transcript of exactly the recording the user asked to discard, with nothing left to reconcile it.'

**Actual.** src/main/import-jobs.ts:373-379: `if (await this.abandonIfCancelled(job, file)) return` checks cancellation ONLY before `await this.deps.enqueueIngest(file)` (line 374). enqueueIngest performs real file I/O (readIndex + updateIndex's tmp-write+rename of index.json, ingest.ts:1804-1810), so it is a genuine await window, not an instant no-op. After it resolves, the code falls straight through to `job.progressPct = 100; job.state = 'done'; await this.persist(job); await this.removeCheckpoint(...)` with NO subsequent cancellation check — violating the comment's own 'every bail-out... must go through here' invariant, which this success path isn't even a bail-out of. If cancel() runs concurrently while enqueueIngest is in flight (cancel() sets state='cancelled', deletes the checkpoint, and — since `this.activeJobId === jobId` is still true mid-finishDecoding — nulls activeJobId and re-pumps), the unconditional `job.state = 'done'` write that follows overwrites the 'cancelled' state back to 'done', re-persists a checkpoint cancel() had just deleted (via onChange it also resurrects the card in the renderer, which had already dropped it per RecallView.tsx:1125's `state !== 'cancelled'` filter), and never deletes the orphaned meeting file/index.md row the user explicitly cancelled.

**Repro.** Empirically confirmed with a scratch vitest test built on the existing import-jobs.test.ts harness (createManager/MemoryStore pattern, same shape as the file's own MQA-024 describe block at lines 238-297): make `enqueueIngest` return a controllable pending Promise, run finishDecoding to the point where it's awaiting enqueueIngest, call `manager.cancel('job-1')` (confirmed state is 'cancelled' immediately after), then resolve enqueueIngest and await finishDecoding's return. Result: `manager.get('job-1')?.state` was `'done'`, not `'cancelled'`, and `deleteMeeting` was never called — reproducing exactly the MQA-024 defect (orphaned meeting file, silently un-cancelled job) through the one checkpoint window the fix's three explicit checks (after generateRecap, after updateRecap, before enqueueIngest — import-jobs.ts:360/363/373) don't cover: during/after enqueueIngest itself. Scratch test deleted after confirming; git status clean of it.

**Suggested fix.** Add one more `if (await this.abandonIfCancelled(job, file)) return` immediately after `await this.deps.enqueueIngest(file)` (line 374), before the `job.progressPct = 100 / job.state = 'done'` finalization at lines 376-377 — mirroring the three checkpoints the MQA-024 fix already added elsewhere in this same function.

**Verifier.** Read src/main/import-jobs.ts:337-388 in full. Confirmed the code matches the claim exactly: line 373 `if (await this.abandonIfCancelled(job, file)) return` is the LAST cancellation check before `await this.deps.enqueueIngest(file)` (374), and nothing checks cancellation again before the unconditional `job.progressPct = 100; job.state = 'done'; await this.persist(job); await this.removeCheckpoint(...)` at 376-379. The abandonIfCancelled doc comment at 456-459 states "Every bail-out after saveMeeting() has landed must go through here" — the done-path assignment at 377 is not routed through it.

Confirmed `cancel()` (230-244) and `finishDecoding()` (312) both call `this.requireJob(jobId)`, which returns the live object reference from the `jobs` Map (not a copy) — so a concurrent `cancel()` call mutates the exact same object `finishDecoding` is holding. `cancel()` sets `job.state = 'cancelled'` synchronously before its first `await`, so it takes effect immediately regardless of what `finishDecoding` is awaiting.

Confirmed `enqueueIngest` is a genuine async I/O op in production, not a no-op: src/main/index.ts:838 wires the real `enqueueIngest` from src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1780, whose non-tracked/non-previous path (1804-1810) calls `updateIndex()` (ingest.ts:1150-1158), which chains onto a serialized `indexLock` promise and does `await writeIndex(s, idx)` — real file I/O. This is a real await window, not instantaneous.

Confirmed reachability: src/main/index.ts:3725-3731 wires `IPC.importJobCancel` directly to `importJobs.cancel(jobId)` with no mutex/lock against a concurrently-running `finishDecoding` for the same job — a user can click Cancel at any point in the pipeline.

Confirmed the renderer drops cancelled cards: src/renderer/src/components/RecallView.tsx:1125 filters `job.state !== 'cancelled'`, so a job flipped back to 'done' via `onChange` would resurface in that list.

Checked existing test coverage: src/main/import-jobs.test.ts's MQA-024 describe block (238-297) covers cancel during generateRecap, during updateRecap, and during a failing recap — all of which route through checkpoints at 359-360, 362-363. None test cancel landing during/after the `enqueueIngest` await (374), confirming this is a genuine gap left by that fix.

Empirically reproduced with a scratch vitest test built on the exact createManager/MemoryStore harness pattern already in import-jobs.test.ts: made `enqueueIngest` return a controllable pending promise, ran `finishDecoding` up to the point it was awaiting `enqueueIngest`, called `manager.cancel('job-1')` (confirmed state flipped to 'cancelled' immediately), then resolved `enqueueIngest` and awaited `finishDecoding`'s return. Result matched the claim exactly: `manager.get('job-1')?.state === 'done'`, `job.file` still `'saved-import.md'`, and `deleteMeeting` was called 0 times — the checkpoint's own invariant violated on its own test harness. Ran via `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run`, not npx. Scratch file deleted afterward; git status confirms it left no residue in my session's changes.

Nothing refutes this: no lock serializes cancel() against finishDecoding, no guard re-checks cancellation after enqueueIngest, and the existing MQA-024 tests structurally cannot catch this gap because they all cancel before hitting line 373-374. The finding's severity (high) is justified — this is a silent data-integrity violation (cancelled import silently becomes 'done', orphaned file never deleted, card resurrected) that reopens the exact defect class MQA-024 was written to close, reachable via a real, unguarded IPC path, gated only by winning a real (if narrow) async file-I/O race. The fix is trivial: add one more `if (await this.abandonIfCancelled(job, file)) return` between the enqueueIngest await (374) and the done-state assignment (376), mirroring the three existing checkpoints exactly.

### MQA-105 — recover()'s crash-safety guard only matches state 'recapping' — a crash in the narrower window between saveMeeting() landing and the following persist (still state 'saving', file not yet recorded) replays the decoder and duplicates the meeting

**Where.** `src/main/import-jobs.ts:154` · regression of MQA-025 · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/import-jobs.ts:151-153: 'The meeting file is already durable once `file` is present. A crash during recap must not replay the decoder and create a duplicate meeting; surface it as a completed transcript so the user can open the note and retry its summary manually.' The stated invariant is about the underlying fact (the meeting file already landed on disk), not about the bookkeeping field lagging behind it.

**Actual.** src/main/import-jobs.ts:341-357: `job.state = 'saving'` is persisted (line 343) BEFORE `saveMeeting()` is called (line 344); `job.file = file` is only assigned and persisted AFTER saveMeeting resolves AND the abandonIfCancelled check passes (lines 354-357). So there is a real window — from the moment saveMeeting() physically writes the meeting file to disk, through the following persist — where the LAST DURABLE checkpoint on disk is still `{state: 'saving', file: undefined}` even though the meeting file genuinely already exists. recover()'s guard at line 154, `if (job.file && job.state === 'recapping')`, cannot match this shape (file is undefined, state is 'saving', not 'recapping'), so it falls through to the generic non-terminal branch (lines 167-177): `job.state = 'queued'` and the decoder is re-enqueued from scratch. On replay, saveMeeting() runs again against a source whose meeting file already exists on disk; transcripts.ts's collision-avoidance (`for (let n = 2; existsSync(file); n++)`) creates a second, differently-named file rather than overwriting — the exact duplicate-file/duplicate-index-row/duplicate-ingest outcome MQA-025 was filed against.

**Repro.** Empirically confirmed with a scratch vitest test mirroring the file's own 'does not decode or duplicate a meeting after a crash during recap' test (import-jobs.test.ts:299-316), but seeding the store with the checkpoint shape a crash in the 'saving' window actually leaves — `{ state: 'saving', cursor: 1, totalChunks: 1, lines: [...], file: undefined }` (no `file` field, matching finishDecoding's real persist at line 343) — on a fresh manager instance (simulating app restart), then calling `manager.recover()`. Result: the mocked `decode` function WAS called (job transitioned to `state: 'decoding'`), proving the decoder is replayed from scratch for this checkpoint shape, whereas the sibling 'recapping'-state test at the same location asserts (and gets) zero decode calls. Since saveMeeting is mocked to always return the same filename in this harness, a full end-to-end run would call the real saveMeeting a second time against an already-existing file. Scratch test deleted after confirming; git status clean of it.

**Suggested fix.** Either (a) record `job.file` durably as soon as saveMeeting() resolves — before the abandonIfCancelled check — so the 'saving' checkpoint can never be persisted without it once the file exists, or (b) widen recover()'s guard to also treat a checkpoint whose state is 'saving' (a non-terminal state that only exists between two persists straddling saveMeeting) the same conservative way as 'recapping' when a way to confirm the file already exists on disk is available (e.g. checking existsSync against the deterministic path saveMeeting would have produced, or persisting the target filename before calling saveMeeting).

**Verifier.** Verified line-by-line and reproduced empirically.

Code trace confirms the exact causal chain claimed: finishDecoding() at import-jobs.ts:342-343 sets `job.state = 'saving'` and persists it (file still undefined at this point — the filename doesn't exist until saveMeeting resolves) BEFORE calling `saveMeeting()` at :344. Only after saveMeeting() resolves and passes the cancellation check does the code assign `job.file = file; job.state = 'recapping'` and persist again (:355-357). recover()'s only crash-safety guard, at :154, is `if (job.file && job.state === 'recapping')` — it does not match a checkpoint shaped `{state: 'saving', file: undefined}`, so it falls into the generic non-terminal branch (:167-177), resets to 'queued', and re-enqueues the decoder.

Reproduced empirically with a scratch vitest test (written, run, then deleted — tree confirmed clean via `git status --porcelain`) seeding exactly the checkpoint shape a crash during the saving-window leaves: `{state:'saving', file: undefined, cursor:1, totalChunks:1, chunkSec:12, lines:[...]}`. Calling `manager.recover()` on a fresh manager instance produced `state: 'decoding'` and called the mocked `decode` function once — proving the decoder is unconditionally replayed for this checkpoint shape. Since cursor/totalChunks/lines were preserved (chunkSec matched, so the unrelated mismatch-reset branch didn't fire), a real replay would have the decoder re-submit already-transcribed chunks (harmlessly skipped by `seq < job.cursor` at :280), hit EOF, and call finishDecoding() again with `job.lines` already populated from the checkpoint — driving straight into a second `saveMeeting()` call. transcripts.ts:672's `for (let n = 2; existsSync(file); n++)` confirms saveMeeting never overwrites, so this second call produces a second file — the exact duplicate outcome claimed.

This is not new: it's the documented "SECONDARY HOLE" from the original MQA-025 investigation (docs/qa/BUG-LEDGER.md:764), which explicitly says "recover()'s guard at import-jobs.ts:154 is job.file && job.state === 'recapping'. The 'saving' checkpoint is persisted... BEFORE saveMeeting, so a kill anywhere in saveMeeting's tail... leaves a durable 'saving' checkpoint with no file -> non-terminal -> requeued... -> full decoder replay -> duplicate. Narrower crash window, same defect," and its own suggested fix (BUG-LEDGER.md:770) explicitly called for widening recover()'s guard to include 'saving' state. I checked `git log --oneline -- src/main/import-jobs.ts` and `git show 0f28626` (the commit that closed the 23 MQA findings including MQA-025's primary resume() bug) — that commit added the `if (job.file)` short-circuit to `resume()` and the `abandonIfCancelled` helper for the cancel-during-recap orphan issue, but did NOT touch recover()'s guard at :154, which is unchanged since. No commit since 0f28626 touches import-jobs.ts. Grepped both import-jobs.ts and import-jobs.test.ts for `state: 'saving'` / `'saving'` checkpoints — zero matches; no test seeds this shape, confirming the gap is untested exactly as claimed.

Location, intended quote (verbatim at :151-153), and actual mechanism (:341-357) are all accurate as cited. Severity 'high' matches the repo's own established precedent for this exact class of bug — MQA-024/MQA-025 (silent duplicate meeting file + duplicate index.md row + duplicate brain ingest, durable across restarts) were both rated 'high', and the ledger's own prior analysis of this specific secondary hole explicitly concluded "SEVERITY: keeping 'high'." No correction needed. Fix complexity: matches the ledger's own "FIX: small" assessment (widen the recover() guard condition; true correctness likely needs job-identity-based idempotency in saveMeeting/finishDecoding rather than a bare state check, since `file` is undefined during 'saving', but the surface-level guard fix is a small, contained change).

### MQA-106 — MQA-012's language-probe fix was never mirrored to the Import path — whisper-import.ts still retires the probe after 5 windows, forcing a non-English recording to English for its entire duration

**Where.** `src/main/whisper-import.ts:216` · regression of MQA-012 · fix size: small

**Intended.** docs/qa/BUG-LEDGER.md:431 (MQA-012's own 'Suggested fix', which the FIXED row is scored against): 'Fix complexity: small. Either stop consuming a slot unless the probe returned >= PROBE_MIN_WORDS, or keep probing on the PROBE_EVERY cadence while un-pinned instead of retiring (listen.ts:534-539) — plus mirroring in whisper-import.ts:216...'. whisper-import.ts:164-174 itself states the reason the retirement is unsafe: 'transformers.js's whisper does NOT auto-detect language on an un-pinned call — it logs "No language specified - defaulting to English" and decodes ENGLISH... once a language is known ... whisper NEVER decodes un-pinned again'.

**Actual.** src/main/whisper-import.ts:216 `if (!probe || userLanguage !== 'auto' || probePinned || windowCount >= PROBE_WINDOW_BUDGET) return` — the exact MQA-012 pattern (a hard `>=` cutoff with no fallback cadence) that was fixed in the live path via listen.ts's `shouldProbeLanguageWindow` (burst-then-PROBE_EVERY) was never ported here. Once `windowCount` passes 5 while still un-pinned, `probeLanguage` can never fire again for that import job.

**Repro.** Import a Portuguese or French recording whose first ~5 transcribed windows are short openers/greeting/hold-music (each under PROBE_MIN_WORDS=8 words, whisper-import.ts:226). Each of the first 5 calls to probeLanguage is consumed but discarded by the substance gate, so `probePinned` never flips true. From window 6 on, line 216's guard blocks every future probe call. `nextDecodeOptions` (whisper-import.ts:175-187) then decodes un-pinned whenever `activeLang` is null, and transformers.js forces those decodes to English (per the file's own header PROVEN FACT). `followLanguage`'s text-side fallback (line 129) reads that forced-English junk, confidently detects 'English' (MIN_HITS=2 stopwords), and latches it — the entire rest of the imported recording, and any recap generated from those lines (App.tsx's generateSavedRecap), is transcribed/summarized in English throughout. This is not hypothetical: the existing regression test src/main/whisper-import.test.ts:204-212 ('gives up after the probe window budget and leaves auto in place') feeds exactly 7 non-substantive ('Hello') windows, asserts `probe` was called only 5 times, and asserts `nextDecodeOptions().language` stays undefined — i.e. it codifies the bug as the intended, tested behavior. Ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/whisper-import.test.ts` — 26/26 pass, confirming the buggy behavior is what ships.

**Suggested fix.** Port listen.ts's `shouldProbeLanguageWindow` cadence into whisper-import.ts's `probeLanguage` guard at line 216: keep probing on the PROBE_EVERY cadence after the initial PROBE_WINDOW_BUDGET burst instead of a hard cutoff (e.g. `if (!probe || userLanguage !== 'auto' || probePinned) return; if (windowCount > PROBE_WINDOW_BUDGET && windowCount % PROBE_EVERY !== 0) return`). Update the comment at whisper-import.ts:206-207 ('give up after PROBE_WINDOW_BUDGET windows and leave auto — the follow machine's own probes still apply later') which repeats the exact reasoning MQA-012 already proved false, and rewrite whisper-import.test.ts:204-212 so it asserts probing continues instead of asserting it stops.

**Verifier.** Verified the full causal chain and could not refute it.

1. src/main/whisper-import.ts:216 — `if (!probe || userLanguage !== 'auto' || probePinned || windowCount >= PROBE_WINDOW_BUDGET) return`. Confirmed via read: this is a hard, permanent retirement — once windowCount passes 5 while probePinned is still false, probeLanguage becomes a permanent no-op for the rest of the job (module state only resets via resetLanguageFollow, called once per job in index.ts:801).

2. Compared to the live path's actual fix: src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts:86-88 `shouldProbeLanguageWindow` — `if (pinned) return windowIndex % PROBE_EVERY === 0; return windowIndex <= PROBE_WINDOW_BUDGET || windowIndex % PROBE_EVERY === 0`. This never permanently gives up — after the initial dense burst it falls back to a steady PROBE_EVERY cadence until a pin lands. listen.ts's own comment (lines 78-84) states explicitly: "The un-pinned budget is an opening BURST, not a retirement... a probe that never landed must keep trying — an un-pinned whisper decode is hard-coded to English by transformers.js, so 'give up and stay auto' silently means 'transcribe the rest of a Portuguese meeting as English'." whisper-import.ts was never updated to match this shape — it kept the pure `>= budget` cutoff the live path moved away from.

3. docs/qa/BUG-LEDGER.md:399-431 (MQA-012, status FIXED) is the exact prior finding for the live path, and its own text explicitly flags this gap: line 427 "the budget is clearly deliberate and mirrored in src/main/whisper-import.ts:207-216 with the same rationale. But imports feed ... the constant was ported without recalibrating," and line 431's Suggested/Fix-complexity note explicitly requires "mirroring in whisper-import.ts:216" as part of closing MQA-012 out — confirming this exact spot was known to need the same fix and, per current code, was not done.

4. Mechanism check: whisper-import.ts:164-174's own header comment states the "PROVEN FACT" that transformers.js's whisper forces English on any un-pinned decode. Once probeLanguage permanently retires without ever setting probePinned, activeLang stays null (nextDecodeOptions only sets `opts.language` when `activeLang` is truthy), so every remaining window decodes fully un-pinned/forced-English. finalizeDecodedText (line 282) still feeds that forced-English text into followLanguage() since `!probePinned && userLanguage === 'auto'` holds, and followLanguage's stopword-based detector (shared/lang-id.ts, MIN_HITS=2) will converge to 'english' after 2 consecutive forced-English-shaped decodes — locking the rest of the recording (and any downstream PROBE_EVERY-th "probe" window, which is also un-pinned and therefore also forced-English) permanently to English. This is the same mechanism the ledger's MQA-012 analysis independently verified against the installed @huggingface/transformers dependency for the live path.

5. Test confirms no guard exists: ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/whisper-import.test.ts --reporter=default` → 26/26 pass. The specific test at lines 204-212 ("gives up after the probe window budget and leaves auto in place") only asserts probe call count (5) and that nextDecodeOptions().language stays undefined immediately after — it never drives real decoded text through followLanguage()/finalizeDecodedText() to observe the subsequent false-English convergence, so the regression is not caught by any existing test.

I could not find any mitigating caller-side logic: index.ts:794-835 wires whisperImportTranscribe with a Parakeet-backed probe callback and a per-job resetLanguageFollow, nothing else. A stale comment at index.ts:816-817 ("calls this at most once per job... window 1 only") is itself inaccurate against the real budget=5 logic, further evidence the import path's probe design was not kept in sync with the live-path fix, not evidence of a mitigation. No other BUG-LEDGER entry tracks this gap (only the two MQA-012 self-references at lines 427 and 431), so this is a live, unfixed regression-of-MQA-012 rather than a duplicate.

Severity: agree with "high" — matches MQA-012's own severity rating for the structurally identical bug and impact (silent, unrecoverable mistranscription/mis-summarization of an entire non-English import in the shipped default 'auto' mode). Fix complexity is small, as the ledger itself already prescribed: port shouldProbeLanguageWindow's burst-then-PROBE_EVERY cadence into whisper-import.ts's probeLanguage guard.

### MQA-107 — MQA-027's fix closes the free-text tenant-ID vector but leaves a syntactically-valid, factually-wrong Entra tenant GUID as a full-app brick with zero in-app recovery — the ledger's own "add an escape hatch" remedy was never implemented

**Where.** `src/main/auth.ts:121` · regression of MQA-027 · fix size: small

**Intended.** docs/qa/BUG-LEDGER.md:810 (the same MQA-027 entry's suggested fix, item 2) — "Add an escape hatch on SignInWall — a 'Reset Microsoft sign-in setup' action ... when there is no live session AND enforcement does not come from admin-trusted managed config." auth.ts:126-128 itself frames the design goal as preventing exactly this: a bad tenantId must not be "an unrecoverable lockout" and must leave the install "unenforced and usable" — i.e. the whole point of the fix is that a bad config can never brick the app with no way back.

**Actual.** The shipped fix (TENANT_GUID_RE at auth.ts:121, isPlausibleAzureConfig at :129-131) only rejects tenantId values that AREN'T shaped like a GUID. A value that IS a well-formed GUID but names the WRONG tenant (a digit-swap typo, or a different Azure subscription's GUID that happens to be copy-pasted by mistake) passes isPlausibleAzureConfig, so readConfig() (auth.ts:157-185) reports configured:true, and signIn()'s tenantMatches() (:137-139, :776) permanently fails on every attempt. App.tsx:2640-2646 renders <SignInWall/> with no bypass; SignInWall.tsx has exactly two buttons ("Sign in with Microsoft" and a local "Cancel and start over" that only resets component state, lines 67-70/108-114) — no sign-out, no settings link, no reset. Settings.tsx:5949-5953 sets `azureLocked = ... || !!authStatus?.configured`, which is true here, locking the three ID fields (and Save, :6124) forever; main independently refuses the write (`if (!requireAuth()) return publicSettings()`, index.ts, since requireAuth() at auth.ts:650-655 returns `!s.configured || s.signedIn` = false). The LKG recovery path (auth.ts:176-184) only helps a device that had a PRIOR successful sign-in — inert for a first-time typo, which is exactly when this fires.

**Repro.** Fresh install, Settings → Account → Change IDs. Enter a valid clientId, paste a syntactically valid Entra tenant GUID with one digit wrong (e.g. transpose two hex characters of the real Mantu tenant GUID), a valid allowedDomain, Save. TENANT_GUID_RE passes (it only checks shape), so configured becomes true. On the next sign-in attempt, Microsoft authenticates the user fine, but auth.ts:776's tenantMatches(tid, cfg.tenantId) fails (wrong tenant) → "That account is outside your organization." Every retry gives the same result. Settings ID fields are locked, tray → Settings routes through the same blocked hotkey path, and there is no in-app action that clears azureTenantId or bypasses the wall — the only recovery is editing userData/settings.json by hand or deleting the profile, exactly the outcome MQA-027's own suggested fix (item 2) was written to eliminate for the already-bricked population.

**Suggested fix.** Implement the ledger's own item 2: add a 'Reset Microsoft sign-in setup' action on SignInWall, gated on no live session AND enforcement not coming from admin-trusted managed-config (so a genuine IT-locked fleet still can't be talked out of it from the UI), that clears azureClientId/azureTenantId/azureAllowedDomain and any sticky flag via a dedicated main handler reachable even while requireAuth() is blocking settingsSet.

**Verifier.** Verified the full causal chain in the current tree (branch fix/windows-audit-and-release-gate). auth.ts:121 TENANT_GUID_RE and auth.ts:129-131 isPlausibleAzureConfig only check that tenantId is GUID-*shaped* (hex+hyphens) — they cannot and do not check that it names the *correct* tenant, so a well-formed-but-wrong GUID passes. readConfig()'s settings tier (auth.ts:174) accepts it, authStatus() (auth.ts:604) reports configured:true, and signIn()'s tenantMatches() (auth.ts:137-139, called at auth.ts:776) permanently returns false for every retry since the id-token `tid` will never equal the wrong configured GUID — no normalization can fix a genuinely wrong value. Confirmed App.tsx:2640/2643 unconditionally renders <SignInWall/> whenever (configured||enforced) && !signedIn, with zero exceptions. Read SignInWall.tsx in full: exactly two buttons exist — 'Sign in with Microsoft' (onSignIn) and 'Cancel and start over' (cancel(), lines 67-70/108-114) which only resets local busy/err state, no sign-out/reset/settings link. Read Settings.tsx:5949-5953: azureLocked = ... || !!authStatus?.configured, and confirmed at 6004/6016 this disables every idField input, and at 6124 disables the Save button — once configured flips true there is no in-app way to overwrite the bad tenantId. Confirmed main independently blocks the write: requireAuth() (auth.ts:650-655) with sticky=false (never set because signIn() only calls writeStickyConfigured() in its success branch, auth.ts:806-807, unreachable when tenantMatches always fails) falls to `!s.configured || s.signedIn` = `!true || false` = false, so requireAuth-gated handlers (e.g. settingsSet) reject the write. Confirmed LKG recovery (auth.ts:176-184) is gated on isStickyConfigured(), false for a first-time typo — inert. Checked signOut() (auth.ts:820-835): unreachable from the gated UI anyway, and would no-op since wasSignedIn is false (never had a session), so it would not clear the bad Settings values even if triggered. Grepped the entire src tree for any 'Reset SSO'/resetSso/clearAzure/escape-hatch implementation — none exists, only comments. Ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/auth.test.ts — 10/10 pass; its MQA-027 describe block (lines 66-135) only covers format-rejection and case-folding, never a well-formed-but-wrong-tenant scenario or any recovery path. The cited 'intended' text at BUG-LEDGER.md:810 is verbatim, and item 2 of that suggested fix (the SignInWall escape hatch) was genuinely never implemented, unlike item 1 (GUID-shape check, done) and item 3 (expectedTenant/attemptedTenant audit logging at auth.ts:778-783, done). This isn't a newly-introduced defect — the original MQA-027 verifier itself already flagged (BUG-LEDGER.md:816: 'this also fires on any GUID typo... a wider trigger than the finder claimed') that a wrong-but-valid GUID would brick identically even pre-fix, and rated that class of issue 'high, not critical' for the same reasons this finding carries (fail-closed, no data loss/bypass, requires operator misconfiguration, out-of-app recovery exists via hand-editing settings.json, deleting the profile, or the higher-precedence AZURE_*/ASKTOTO_ALLOWED_DOMAIN env vars). I adopt that same 'high' severity precedent. Fix is straightforward: add a 'Reset Microsoft sign-in setup' action on SignInWall backed by a main handler that clears the three azure* settings fields (plus sticky/LKG) when there's no live session and enforcement isn't admin-managed — exactly the ledger's own still-open suggested item 2.

### MQA-108 — brainStatus's `topError` ships the raw, unredacted fs-error string (full local path + Windows username) straight into the dashboard — the redaction its sibling function exists for is silently skipped

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1291` · fix size: trivial

**Intended.** src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1312-1316 (the docstring on the very next function, `redactPathsInError`, which reads the SAME `record.error` field): "Raw exception messages can embed full absolute paths (fs errors like ENOENT quote the whole path, Windows username included)... a tooltip screenshot pasted into a support channel would leak the local directory layout. Collapse any drive-rooted or home-rooted path down to its basename before the string leaves the main process." The sibling consumer of the identical data, `ingestFailureDetails` (line 1330-1343), honors this by calling `redactPathsInError(record.error ?? 'Unknown error')` at line 1340 before returning to the IPC layer.

**Actual.** `ingestFailureCounts()` (src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1291-1310) aggregates `record.error` completely raw — `byError.set(record.error, ...)` at line 1299, then `topError = error` at line 1305, returned verbatim at line 1309 with zero call to `redactPathsInError`. This value flows straight through the `brainStatus` IPC handler at src/main/index.ts:3420 (`...(failure.topError ? { topError: failure.topError } : {})`) with no redaction step in between, and is rendered directly in the UI at src/renderer/src/components/BrainView.tsx:706-708: `` `Your AI provider is failing: ${topError} — check Settings → AI` ``. `brainStatus` is polled every few seconds (per the comment at ingest.ts:1327), so once the condition triggers it stays visible on the dashboard.

**Repro.** Cause 3+ meeting files to fail `finishJob` (src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1517-1542) with byte-identical error text that embeds a full path — the simplest trigger is a shared per-account/per-deal `.brain/` entity file that multiple meetings' extractions all try to write and that a locked-down Windows profile denies (AV/EDR handle lock, permission ACL, OneDrive sync lock), or the local sidecar binary being unreachable so every local-fallback extraction throws the identical `spawn ENOENT 'C:\Users\<user>\AppData\...\llama-server.exe'`. `e.message` is stored raw at ingest.ts:1533 into `idx.ingested[key].error`. With ≥3 records sharing that exact string (the `minTopErrorCount` default at line 1291), `ingestFailureCounts(idx)` returns `topError` equal to that raw string (proved by the existing unit test at src/main/brain/ingest-resilience.test.ts:217-228, which never exercises a path-bearing message). BrainView then literally renders the full absolute path and Windows username in the dashboard banner text — the exact disclosure the adjacent `redactPathsInError` function was written to prevent for the (redacted) per-file detail list, on the same underlying field.

**Suggested fix.** Call `redactPathsInError(topError)` before returning it from `ingestFailureCounts` (or redact once at the `byError.set` call site so both the count and the detail list share one sanitized value), and add a regression test mirroring ingest-resilience.test.ts:217 but with a path-bearing shared error, asserting `ingestFailureCounts(...).topError` never contains a drive-rooted or `/Users//home/`-rooted path.

**Verifier.** Traced the full chain in src/main/brain/ingest.ts. ingestFailureCounts (line 1291-1310) aggregates record.error verbatim into byError map (line 1299) and returns topError raw (line 1309) with zero call to redactPathsInError. redactPathsInError (line 1317-1322) exists specifically to strip drive-rooted/home-rooted paths per its own docstring (1312-1316), and its ONLY caller is ingestFailureDetails (line 1330-1343), which calls it at line 1340 — confirming the redaction step is real but skipped for topError. Confirmed the raw error text comes from e.message (line 1533, finishJob catch block), which for fs/spawn errors on Windows does embed the full path + username (e.g. ENOENT, spawn ENOENT quote the full path per Node's error format). Confirmed IPC flow: src/main/index.ts:3420 spreads failure.topError straight into the brain:status payload with no redaction call anywhere in between. Confirmed shared/brain.ts:534 documents topError's intended UI string ('Your AI provider is failing: <topError>') with no redaction mention, unlike failedDetails just below it. Confirmed renderer: BrainView.tsx:706-708 interpolates topError directly into the alert text. Ran the actual test file (./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/brain/ingest-resilience.test.ts) — all 9 tests pass, and the topError-specific tests at lines 216-242 only use path-free strings ('404 page not found', 'network error'), never a path-bearing error, so no test would have caught this and none contradicts the claim. Also checked ingest-audit-fixes.test.ts:187, same pattern — plain strings only. No guard, schema transform, or caller-side redaction intervenes anywhere between record.error's raw storage and the renderer. The finder's causal chain, quotes, and line numbers are all accurate.

### MQA-109 — armThemProbation (added by the MQA-011 fix) can recycle a perfectly healthy 'them' channel — its own comment claims a quiet stretch 'must never' do that

**Where.** `src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts:788` · regression of MQA-011 · fix size: medium

**Intended.** src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts:780-781: 'Armed only by a device change — a naturally quiet stretch (you talking for 20 s) must never tear down a healthy loopback.'

**Actual.** The devicechange effect (listen.ts:1020-1038) computes `themDeviceChangeAction(wantsSystemRef.current, !!channels.current.them, null)` for EVERY 'devicechange' event (the Web API fires this for ANY audio/video device add or remove, with no detail on which device or whether it's relevant) — when a 'them' channel is already open this always returns 'watch' (listen.ts:109) and calls `armThemProbation()` (listen.ts:1029), unconditional of whether the change had anything to do with system-audio loopback. armThemProbation's 20s timer (listen.ts:785-802) then evaluates `themDeviceChangeAction(wantsSystemRef.current, !!channels.current.them, themWindowSeenRef.current)`, and `themDeviceChangeAction` returns 'recycle' (listen.ts:110) whenever no window arrived in that window — which is exactly what happens during an ordinary 20-second stretch where only the local user is talking or there is a natural pause, with the channel perfectly healthy the whole time. Confirmed by the shipped unit test itself: listen.test.ts:100 `expect(themDeviceChangeAction(true, true, false)).toBe('recycle')` — the function cannot distinguish 'channel actually died' from 'device event coincided with normal silence'.

**Repro.** Live meeting, source 'both', 'them' channel already open and healthy (themHeardRef true — the remote side was heard earlier in the call). At T=0 any unrelated 'devicechange' fires (e.g. a Bluetooth peripheral wakes, a USB device is plugged in, a virtual-audio-cable app toggles, a laptop dock/undock event) — none of which affected the system-audio loopback. 800ms later the effect arms armThemProbation(). For the next 20s the remote participant doesn't speak (e.g. the local user is mid-monologue or presenting) — a completely normal occurrence, so zero 'them' windows are emitted (windows are VAD-gated). At T=20s the probation timer fires, themWindowSeenRef.current is still false, verdict='recycle' → listen.ts closes the healthy channel (`closeChannel('them')`), sets `error: THEM_LOST_MSG` and `captureDegraded: {side:'them', ...}`, and calls `recoverSystemAudioRef()` to re-run the full getDisplayMedia() acquisition. Bar.tsx:452-457 immediately flips the persistent 'Heard live' chip to an incorrect amber 'Mic only' even though the remote side was being captured fine seconds earlier, and on macOS the teardown/reacquire risks rebuilding the shared ScreenCaptureKit session mid-meeting (per the file's own SCStream-fragility comments around line ~1259-1266), losing whatever the remote side says during the reconnect window.

**Suggested fix.** Don't treat 'no window since an unrelated device change' as proof of death for a channel that was already confirmed healthy (themHeardRef true). Either scope probation to device changes plausibly relevant to the them side (e.g. only re-arm when the change coincides with an actual RMS/track anomaly), or require positive evidence of silence (e.g. check the worklet is still receiving zero-filled/near-zero buffers) rather than merely 'no window emitted', before recycling an already-healthy loopback.

**Verifier.** Traced the full chain and it holds. (1) listen.ts:1021-1038 — the devicechange listener has no filtering on device kind/relevance; the DOM 'devicechange' event itself carries no such detail, and the code never calls enumerateDevices() to diff/compare. After an 800ms debounce it unconditionally calls themDeviceChangeAction(wantsSystemRef.current, !!channels.current.them, null) at line 1028. (2) themDeviceChangeAction (listen.ts:102-111): with hasThemChannel=true and sawWindow=null, it always returns 'watch' (line 109). (3) 'watch' triggers armThemProbation() (line 1029), which resets themWindowSeenRef.current=false (listen.ts:784) and starts a fresh 20s timer WITHOUT consulting themHeardRef — grepped every use of themHeardRef in the file; it's read/written only by armThemWatchdog and the first-emission handler, never by armThemProbation or its timeout callback. So a channel that has been healthy and heard for the whole meeting gets no special treatment once a device change fires. (4) themWindowSeenRef.current is set true only inside the worklet's onmessage handler (listen.ts:843), which fires only when the AudioWorklet posts a message — confirmed in whisper-worklet-src.ts:41-56 that postMessage only happens after vad.step() signals end-of-turn AND the window passes the RMS floor AND isSpeechLikeWindow (vad.ts), i.e. genuinely VAD-gated on real speech. A 20s stretch with no remote speech (ordinary — local user presenting, or a pause) produces zero postMessage calls, so themWindowSeenRef stays false. (5) At timeout, listen.ts:788-792 recomputes themDeviceChangeAction(true, true, false), which returns 'recycle' per line 110 — this exact input is the literal shipped unit test at listen.test.ts:100, whose own comment (lines 98-99) states 'Without the probation this state is unreachable', confirming this is a deliberately reachable, tested code path. (6) Verdict 'recycle' triggers closeChannel('them'), sets error:THEM_LOST_MSG and captureDegraded (listen.ts:794-801), and calls recoverSystemAudioRef — Bar.tsx:452-457 confirms the persistent chip flips to amber 'Mic only' off captureDegraded, and the macOS SCStream-fragility comment the finder cites is real and adjacent (listen.ts:1254-1266, describing the shared video+audio SCStream session). Ran vitest run src/renderer/src/lib/listen.test.ts — 21/21 pass, including the recycle-on-sawWindow-false assertion, confirming this is today's shipped behavior, not something a guard already blocks. The doc comment at listen.ts:780-781 ('a naturally quiet stretch... must never tear down a healthy loopback') is only true in the absence of any devicechange event; once ANY devicechange fires — including ones fully unrelated to the loopback device, since the code cannot distinguish relevance — the probation logic applies the same 'prove it again within 20s or die' rule regardless of how long the channel was already proven healthy, so the invariant the comment asserts does not actually hold end-to-end. Real gap between stated invariant and implemented heuristic, with concrete (if self-healing) user impact: false degraded-UI state plus an unnecessary loopback teardown/reacquire mid-meeting that risks briefly losing the remote side's audio. Bounded — auto-recovers, no crash, no permanent data loss, no security impact — which supports keeping severity at medium.

### MQA-110 — Screen-capture readiness never re-validates after a successful probe, so revoking the OS permission later in the same session leaves the checklist reporting a stale 'granted' — reintroducing MQA-002's own bug for the revoke-after-grant case

**Where.** `src/main/platform-perms.ts:77` · regression of MQA-002 · fix size: small

**Intended.** src/main/platform-perms.ts:27-28 — "Null means \"never probed\"; callers fall back to \"unknown\" rather than guessing \"granted\"." And :74-77 (windowsScreenStatus) — "Windows exposes no queryable screen-capture permission, so the only honest answer is whatever an actual capture attempt produced ... Unprobed stays 'unknown' — never assume 'granted', or the readiness UI would promise a capability it has not demonstrated." src/main/platform-perms.test.ts:99 pins the macOS analogue as "falls back to probe evidence only while TCC is non-committal (not-determined)".

**Actual.** screenProbeResult (platform-perms.ts:29) is a module-level cache written only by probeScreenCapture() (:41-54) and read forever after by windowsScreenStatus() (:77, `return screenProbeResult ?? 'unknown'`) with NO live OS query behind it on Windows (there is none). Grepping every call site of probeScreenCapture confirms it fires at exactly three points in the whole app: onboarding's permissionsRequestUpfront (src/main/index.ts:1987 macOS, :1997 win32) and the one-shot boot probe (index.ts:4570-4572). clearScreenProbe() — the only thing that can invalidate the cache — is called nowhere in production code, only in tests. Nothing re-probes before an actual screenshot capture, on a timer, or on window focus. Windows genuinely does expose a live per-app toggle for this (index.ts:1963-1969 itself opens `ms-settings:privacy-graphicscaptureprogrammatic`, "the App graphics capture privacy page"), so a 'granted' cached at boot is silently wrong the moment that toggle is flipped off later in the same run. On macOS the same staleness manifests narrower but by the identical mechanism: macStatus() (platform-perms.ts:56-63) collapses BOTH 'not-determined' and 'restricted' into 'unknown' (only 'granted'/'denied' are special-cased), so getPlatformPermissions()'s fallback-to-probe branch (:84-88) — documented as reserved for the 'not-determined' case only — also fires when TCC's live answer is 'restricted' (e.g. an MDM Privacy Preferences Policy Control profile), letting a stale in-session 'granted' probe outrank a live administrative deny.

**Repro.** Windows: launch Métis, let the boot probe succeed (screenProbeResult='granted', confirmed by platform-perms.test.ts's own 'reports granted once a probe returns at least one source' case). Complete onboarding; the readiness checklist (Settings → Permissions) shows Screen/system audio: granted. Without restarting Métis, open Windows Settings → Privacy & security → App permissions → Graphics capture (the exact URI index.ts:1969 links to) and turn off access for Métis. Ask a screenshot question mid-meeting: getPlatformPermissions().screenRecording still returns 'granted' (verified by code trace — no call path re-invokes probeScreenCapture between boot and this ask), so Settings' PermissionsSection (Settings.tsx:6224-6231) keeps showing a green dot and gives no warning, while the actual desktopCapturer call the ask uses fails/returns nothing — silently, exactly the discovery-only-mid-meeting failure MQA-002 was written to eliminate.

**Suggested fix.** Re-probe screen capture opportunistically rather than trusting a single boot-time snapshot for the life of the process: at minimum call probeScreenCapture() again immediately before the real capture path runs (captureScreenshotOnce/getScreenshot) so a stale 'granted' can never gate a UI promise without being checked at point of use, and/or periodically re-probe on an interval or on window-focus the same way usePermissions() already polls. On macOS, make macStatus() distinguish 'restricted' from 'not-determined' (or have getPlatformPermissions() only fall back to the probe for 'not-determined', never for 'restricted') so a live administrative deny can never be shadowed by an earlier successful probe.

**Verifier.** Verified the core mechanism by code trace: platform-perms.ts:29's `screenProbeResult` is written only inside probeScreenCapture (:41-54) and read forever after by windowsScreenStatus (:77). Grepped every call site — probeScreenCapture fires only at index.ts:1987/1997 (onboarding) and :4570-4572 (boot), and clearScreenProbe (:32) is called nowhere in production (only in platform-perms.test.ts). Settings.tsx's PermissionsSection (6184-6232) reads this via usePermissions, which polls every 1000ms (state.ts:663/687) but on win32 getPlatformPermissions() just re-reads the same stale cache — polling never re-probes. So the readiness checklist genuinely can show a stale 'granted' after an OS-level revoke, with no production code path that invalidates it. That part of the finding is correct.

However, the finding's severity-defining claim collapses on inspection: it says the actual desktop-capture call the ask uses "fails/returns nothing — silently, exactly the discovery-only-mid-meeting failure MQA-002 was written to eliminate." This is false. captureScreenshotOnce (index.ts:1298-1373) performs its OWN live desktopCapturer.getSources call, completely independent of screenProbeResult — it never consults the cache. When sources come back empty it throws screenCaptureUnavailableMessage('win32', ...) (screen-capture.ts:74-81) = "No screen source available. Check your system's screen-capture permissions for Métis, then try again." App.tsx's askScreen catch block (899-952) classifies this via isScreenCapturePermissionError (shared/screen-capture.ts:5-7, whose regex matches "screen-capture permissions"), surfaces the raw message verbatim to the user, and — critically — for a bare "look at my screen" ask with no allowTextFallback, returns null instead of silently degrading to a text-only answer (comment at 940: "A denied Screen Recording grant must not SILENTLY become a cloud text request"). So the live-use path is exactly the opposite of silent; it re-validates for real and gives an actionable, correctly-diagnosed error every time. Ran src/main/platform-perms.test.ts (11/11 pass), which also shows macOS correctly lets a live TCC 'denied'/'granted' override a stale probe (only 'restricted' — a rare status for screen recording in practice, atypical for MDM screen-recording restrictions which normally report 'denied' — falls through to stale-probe fallback, and even that's untested/speculative).

Net: the architectural claim (cache never invalidates) is real, but the concrete harm is far narrower than described — it's a passive Settings/onboarding status-dot staleness in the revoke-after-grant-without-restart case, not a functional regression that reintroduces MQA-002's silent mid-meeting failure. The actual ask path already re-validates live and reports failures loudly and specifically, which is exactly what MQA-002 was fixing. Correcting severity down substantially; a mislabeled status dot that self-corrects the moment the user actually tries the feature (with clear guidance) is a low-severity UX polish gap, not high.
