> isolated running app instance over CDP across routing, brain, and settings domains. It confirmed the
> shipped features work (zero-key on-device suggest/summary/vision, degradation, quick actions, meetings,
> indexing, time-saved, settings/security) and found 6 real issues.

### MQA-131 — new Settings sections are invisible to settings search

**Repro.** Open Settings, type `Plane` (or `ClickUp`, `NVIDIA`, `Race a backup provider`) into the
search box. Expected: the tab holding that card. Actual: no result, even though the card renders on the
Intelligence tab (Plane/ClickUp) or the AI tab (Backups & limits).

**Intended behavior**, quoted from the code that defines the rule —
`src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx`, the comment above `TABS`: "INVARIANT: ... a Section's exact
title is only findable if some keyword in its tab's list is at least that long and contains it verbatim.
Whenever a `<Section title=\"...\">` is added or renamed under a tab, add that exact title text to this
tab's `keywords` too."

**Actual behavior.** The `intelligence` tab's keyword list carried only
`['mantu intelligence','meetings & follow-up','published wiki','polo pre-sales','crm','knowledge graph']`
while rendering `<Section title="Plane">` and `<Section title="ClickUp">`; the `ai` tab rendered
`<Section title="Backups & limits">` (via `ResilienceSection`) with no matching keyword either. The
Backups & limits gap predates this session; Plane/ClickUp arrived with the task-manager connectors.

**Why unit tests missed it.** `searchSettingsTabs` had tests, but only for sections that were already
listed — nothing asserted the invariant across the sections that actually render. Found by driving the
real renderer over CDP and searching for the cards I had just watched render.

**Fix.** Added the missing titles to both tabs' keywords, plus `searchSettingsTabs` cases naming MQA-131
that assert every connector card and the resilience section are findable, so a future Section added
without its keyword breaks a test instead of shipping unsearchable.

### MQA-132 — a dead primary leaves the hedge backup waiting out the full delay

**Repro.** Configure the primary provider so it cannot run (here: `provider: 'custom'` with
`customBaseUrl: https://10.255.255.1/v1`, a non-routable address, and no model set), keep a second
working provider configured, leave `resilience.hedge` on, and ask a base-tier question. Expected: the
backup answers about as fast as it normally would. Actual: the answer took **3673 ms** — the primary leg
died at ~0.4s, then nothing happened until the `HEDGE_DELAY_MS` timer fired at 3000ms and finally started
the backup.

**Intended behavior**, from `src/main/llm/hedge.ts`'s own contract for `markDead`: it returns `'suppress'`
only while some other leg "could still answer", i.e. suppressing this leg's error is a promise that
another leg will produce the answer instead.

**Actual behavior.** `markDead('primary')` returned `'suppress'` (correctly — the hedge leg had not been
ruled out) but nothing started the hedge leg early, so the promise was only honoured once the delay timer
happened to fire. `HEDGE_DELAY_MS` exists to give a *slow* primary a head start; a primary that is already
dead has nothing left to win with, so the remaining delay is pure added latency.

**Why unit tests missed it.** Every `HedgeRace` unit test asserted the surface/suppress accounting, which
was correct in isolation; the defect is that the dispatcher had no path to act on it early. It only shows
up as wall-clock latency in a running app. Found by physically driving the app over CDP with a
deliberately stalled primary.

**Fix.** `HedgeRace` gained `setHedgeStarter`/`markHedgeStarted` and now pulls the backup forward from
`markDead('primary')`; `main/index.ts` puts the delay timer and the pull-forward behind one
`startHedgeLeg()` launcher so neither can start the backup twice. Same scenario after the fix: **854 ms**,
one `streamMeta` leg, no error surfaced. Healthy-primary asks are unchanged (512-1023 ms against live
NVIDIA NIM; the backup never starts). Regression tests naming MQA-132 cover early start, double-start
from both triggers, an already-won race, an unavailable backup, and a dying hedge leg.

### MQA-133 .. MQA-138 — the 2026-08-15 hardening audit

Six defects found by a six-lens adversarial audit (auth/token handling, MCP + IPC trust boundary, hedge
concurrency, secrets at rest, crash safety, renderer correctness), each put through a skeptic told to
refute by default. Findings that did not survive that pass are deliberately not recorded here.

The common shape of MQA-133, MQA-135, MQA-137 and MQA-138: **a guarantee stated in one handler's comment
was reachable around through a different channel.** mcpPush says "a compromised renderer can't redirect
the push to an attacker-controlled MCP endpoint" — true of its own payload, false once settings:set could
rewrite the saved endpoint. dustLoginBegin gates on requireAuth() — irrelevant once the pair that
actually writes the credential (poll -> pickWorkspace) did not. The lesson worth keeping: an invariant
belongs at the place that ENFORCES it, and a comment asserting one is a claim to re-test whenever a new
write path appears.

MQA-134 and MQA-136 are the opposite class — correct-looking code with an unconsidered branch. The hedge
leg's terminal path had a gate on every sibling case but that one; the Dust refresh assumed a field the
spec marks optional. Both were only observable as behaviour (a spinner that never ends, a session that
never recovers), which is why they survived a green suite.

Verification for all six: both typechecks clean, full suite green, and — for the reachable ones — a
physical check against the running app (Dust login shape against the live WorkOS endpoint; the hedge
paths driven with a deliberately stalled primary, both with and without an eligible backup).

### MQA-139 .. MQA-142 — second pass over the hardening audit's candidate list

The 2026-08-15 audit produced 18 candidates but only verified the 8 highest-severity ones; these four came
from re-checking the remainder by hand rather than letting them lapse.

MQA-139 is the one with real blast radius. redact.ts advertises that it strips "recognised API-key
formats" before text leaves the device, but the list was hand-maintained and had drifted behind
providers.ts: `nvapi-`, `gsk_` and `xai-` were never added. NVIDIA NIM had just become the DEFAULT
provider, which made its key the single most likely one to be present on this machine. Fixed by DERIVING
the rules from providers.ts's own `keyPattern` prefixes, so the class is closed rather than the three
instances — a provider added later is covered the moment it is declared, and the test walks every declared
prefix to prove it. The conservative bias is preserved: ordinary text like "ask nvidia about pricing" is
still untouched.

MQA-140/141/142 are all in the Review panel and all share a shape: state that was correct for the case it
was written for and wrong for a case nobody enumerated — a second click in the same tick, a coaching run
that never started, a recap edited after its action items were parsed. Two of the three end in the user's
external tracker (duplicate tasks, stale wording), which is why they are worth more than their severity
labels suggest: they are silent and they are outbound.

### MQA-146 — the compliance one-pager describes an installer that no longer exists

**Where.** `docs/compliance/data-flow-onepager.md` · workflow: an enterprise security review of Métis, and any air-gapped deployment decision made from it · fix size: small

**Found by** running `npm run dist:win` during a full QA pass and looking inside the artifact, rather than by reading source. Every automated gate passed — `check:packaged-runtime` OK pre- and post-sign, `check:update-metadata` OK, `check:launch` OK — because none of them asserts anything about a document.

**Intended.** `docs/compliance/data-flow-onepager.md` (Local LLM bullet): "The macOS arm64 and Windows x64 packages include Qwen3.5 0.8B (quantized GGUF plus its multimodal projector) and the pinned llama.cpp `llama-server` b9957 sidecar... The installed app does not download a model or inference runtime."

**Actual.** `find release/win-unpacked -name '*.gguf'` returns **zero files**; the only thing under `resources/local-llm/` is `LICENSE.QWEN3.5-APACHE-2.0.txt`. `electron-builder.yml` says why, deliberately and in its own comment: "The Qwen WEIGHTS are deliberately NOT packaged. At ~728 MB they dominated the installer, and a universal (Intel + Apple Silicon) package carrying them would exceed GitHub's 2 GB per-asset release limit." `src/main/llm/local-model-download.ts` fetches them on first run, and `scripts/check-offline-package.mjs` has already been updated to allowlist that URL in exactly two reviewed files. So the ENGINEERING is coherent and gated — it is only the compliance document that was left behind. Corroborating evidence: `Metis-Setup-1.5.4.exe` is 733.7 MB where 1.5.3 was 1393.2 MB, a ~660 MB drop matching the excluded weights almost exactly.

**Why it matters more than its severity suggests.** This is the document that goes to a customer's security review, and both false halves point the same way — they understate the app's network behaviour. A reviewer approving an air-gapped or egress-restricted deployment on the strength of "does not download a model" would be approving something the build cannot honour. Exactly the MQA-068 shape (a shipped artifact asserting behaviour the build cannot produce), one class of document more sensitive.

**Not everything in the claim was wrong.** The `llama-server` sidecar genuinely ships — verified in the artifact at `resources/llama/win/{cpu,vulkan}/`, 132 MB of thin exe plus per-microarch ggml DLLs, sha256-pinned. So the inference RUNTIME is never downloaded; only the weights are.

**Fix.** The bullet now states the split plainly (runtime bundled, weights fetched once on first run) and, in their place, gives the mitigations a reviewer actually needs: the URL is a **commit-pinned** Hugging Face revision rather than a mutable tag, both byte size and SHA-256 are enforced before use, the fetch goes to Hugging Face rather than to Mantu or any Métis service, and it carries no meeting content, telemetry or identifiers. It also answers the question the exclusion creates and the old text hid — in an air-gapped install there is no local LLM until the file is placed by other means, while **ASR is unaffected** because those weights ARE bundled, so transcription still works with no network at all.

`src/main/packaged-model-claims.contract.test.ts` pins the RELATIONSHIP rather than the prose, the same way `license-enforcement-drift.contract.test.ts` does for MQA-068: while `electron-builder.yml` does not package `resources/local-llm/models`, the compliance doc may not claim it does — and package them again and the same tests demand the doc move with it. It also asserts the mitigations the corrected text now offers are real (commit-pinned URL, not `resolve/main`). Verified by regression: restoring the old sentences fails the suite.

### MQA-147 — F3 hedge race bypasses the on-device-only screenshot pin and uploads the capture to a cloud provider

**Repro.** Default install: `settings.resilience.hedge` = true (shared/ipc.ts:1004/1209), Métis Local enabled with `localLlm.useFor.vision` on, plus any keyed vision-capable cloud provider (Claude/GPT/Grok/Gemini/OpenRouter/Kimi). First screen-capture hotkey press after launch. `localVisionPrivacyRequired` -> `pickPrimaryProvider` returns 'local' (local-routing.ts:202). `routeTier` = 'base' for a plain screen glance (shared/routing.ts:108-112), `isCoolingDown('local')` false -> `skipDeadPrimary` null -> `hedgeEligible` true. The cold sidecar needs ~730 MB of GGUF loaded before its first token (the code itself budgets `LOCAL_COLD_START_IDLE_MS` = 90s, index.ts:3504), so at t = HEDGE_DELAY_MS (3000 ms) it has emitted nothing. Timer fires -> `startHedgeLeg()` -> `pickFailover(['local'])` -> 'anthropic' -> `attempt('anthropic', ['local'], 0, {leg:'hedge'})` with the unmodified `req`. streamAnthropic embeds `req.image` (anthropic.ts:8-15) and the base64 screenshot is POSTed to api.anthropic.com. Aborting the loser later does not un-send it. Faster variant, no 3s wait: when the pin is set but local is not ready, `attempt('local')` builds the ineligible string at index.ts:3410-3411, skips the `provider !== 'local'`-guarded block at 3445-3452 and reaches `race.gate.markDead(race.leg)`; `markDead` calls `startHedgeEarly()` BEFORE judging viability, so the cloud leg starts in well under a second and then 'suppress' swallows the message entirely.

**Intended.** local-routing.ts:143-147: "The screenshot toggle is a privacy policy, not only a routing preference... the request must fail locally with no upload instead of quietly selecting a cloud provider." index.ts:3396-3400: "Opted-in vision deliberately stays local at every tier so prompt complexity cannot silently turn a screenshot into a cloud upload." User-facing string at index.ts:3411 promises "Nothing was sent to a cloud provider." MQA-124 closed the same leak at the skip-cooling-primary seam.

**Actual (before).** index.ts:3786-3791 — `hedgeEligible = s.resilience.hedge && !skipDeadPrimary && routeTier(...) === 'base' && (mode in {answer,vision,suggest}) && allowCrossProviderFailover(req)`. `localVisionRequired` (declared 3764) was consumed ONLY at 3770 by `pickPrimaryProvider` and was absent from the gate. index.ts:3803 `pickFailover([primary])`'s `eligible()` (3262-3280) applies only `req.mode !== 'vision' || providerVisionOk(p)`, so any keyed vision-capable cloud provider qualified. The hedge leg is a FRESH dispatch, not a failover out of the local leg, so neither `provider !== 'local'` guard (3564, 3700) ever saw it.

**Fix.** One conjunct added to the gate at index.ts:3786 — `primary !== 'local'`. It subsumes the vision pin (pickPrimaryProvider returns 'local' whenever `localVisionRequired`, local-routing.ts:202) and also closes the sibling hole for an in-scope local `suggest` (mode 'suggest' is in the hedge mode set and routeTier is unconditionally 'base' for it). With `hedgeEligible` false the else branch at 3823 dispatches `attempt(primary, [])` with NO race, so the local leg's own terminals run un-suppressed and "Nothing was sent to a cloud provider" is actually delivered instead of markDead-swallowed. The belt-and-braces `primary === 'local'` guard inside `startHedgeLeg` was deliberately NOT added: `primary` is a const and `startHedgeLeg` is defined inside the `if (hedgeEligible)` block, so that branch is provably unreachable dead code.

### MQA-148 — Private View's env kill-switch is not gated to unpackaged builds

**Repro.** Packaged install, `privateView` ON. Any process running as the user (no elevation) runs `setx ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP 1`; Métis relaunches. `privateViewOn()` returns false unconditionally from then on: `getScreenshot()` stops throwing PrivateViewBlockedError at its pre-check and post-capture re-check, `capture.blocked` is never audited, the 6 s background describe keeps capturing, and `currentFreshContext()` hands the screen description to whatever cloud provider answers the next ask. Settings -> Privacy still renders the toggle ON.

**Intended.** The sibling function nine lines above states and implements the rule — src/main/index.ts:402-408: "Disable via env for dev/screenshots ONLY — gated to unpackaged builds so a packaged process can never have capture protection stripped by `setx ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP 1` + relaunch" -> `if (!app.isPackaged && process.env.ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP) return false`. src/main/intelligence.ts:10-13 repeats it verbatim. .forge/qa-r5sec.mjs:2 pins it for a packaged build. index.ts:1026-1029 states the UI-honesty half: "Reflect the value actually applied to the window, not the raw stored setting."

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:414-417 — `function privateViewOn(): boolean { if (process.env.ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP) return false; return getSettings().privateView }`, no `!app.isPackaged` term, and it is the single authority behind index.ts:1497 / :1529 / the `deps.privateViewOn` wiring at :1560 (screen-preprocess.ts:198 and :318). src/main/index.ts:1023-1029 — publicSettings() spread `...s` and overrode only `contentProtection`, so `privateView` rode through untouched to Settings.tsx.

**Fix.** New src/main/dev-env.ts owns the one gate: `devEnv(name)` returns the variable's value only when `isPackagedBuild()` is false, and `isPackagedBuild()` reads `app.isPackaged === true` inside a try/catch that fails CLOSED (a throw counts as packaged). `privateViewOn()` now does `if (devEnv('ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP')) return false`; `contentProtectionOn()` was moved onto the same helper so there is one mechanism, not two spellings. publicSettings() now returns `privateView: privateViewOn()` next to `contentProtection: contentProtectionOn()`, so the Privacy toggle shows what capture actually obeys. Dev/screenshot workflows are unaffected — unpackaged runs still honor the variable.

### MQA-149 — "Delete all Métis data" never removes the published wiki/ mirror

**Repro.** Publishing on, 30 meetings ingested → `<meetingsFolder>/wiki/` holds meetings/*.md note cards, people/accounts/deals pages with named individuals and `${c.by} owes: ${c.text}` commitment lines, plus index.md/AGENTS.md/README.md/CLAUDE.md. History → Delete all Métis data → confirm. Result: every .md transcript unlinked, `.brain/` wiped, `graph.json`/`graph.html` gone, audit says `transcript.deleted {bulk:true, brainPurged:true}`, handler returns ok. `wiki/` untouched — and now unprunable forever, because publishAll iterates listEntities/listMeetingExtractions, which both return [] once the brain is gone. Second repro: delete the meetings one at a time first, then run Delete all — `if (meetings.length === 0) return { ok:true, deleted:0 }` returned before purgeBrain/purgeGraphArtifacts too, so `.brain/` AND `wiki/` both survived while the UI said success.

**Intended (quoted).** Dialog detail, src/main/index.ts:3005-3006: "This permanently removes every saved transcript, note, and the knowledge graph from this device. This cannot be undone." purgeBrain's doc, src/main/brain/store.ts:499-503: "the brain IS the knowledge graph now … A wipe that leaves it on disk would break the dialog's promise"; store.ts:510-512 names this exact call site: "recallDeleteAll's full-erasure call site leaves this false on purpose: that flow's explicit promise is 'every transcript, note, and the knowledge graph' gone, corrections included." The mirror is that same derived data in cleartext by design — publish.ts:36-38: writes are "always with `encrypt: false` — the wiki mirror's whole purpose is plaintext readability".

**Actual (pre-fix).** src/main/index.ts recallDeleteAll did deleteAllMeetings() → purgeGraphArtifacts() → purgeBrain(getSettings()) and nothing else; removeWiki (src/main/brain/publish.ts:958 pre-fix) had exactly ONE production caller, index.ts:2236, on the publishBrainPages ON→OFF edge. deleteAllMeetings cannot reach the mirror: meetingFiles filters `e.isFile() && e.name.endsWith('.md')` on a single non-recursive readdir (recall.ts:37-40), so the `wiki` dirent is skipped. brainDir = `<folder>/.brain`, wikiDir = `<folder>/wiki` (publish.ts:49-51) — siblings, so purgeBrain's rmSync misses it. Single-delete path: recallDelete only called deleteMeeting + requestSourceRefresh, and maybeStartSourceRefresh bails on a busy queue / pending replay / no usable provider (ingest.ts:1999-2002), so the orphan `wiki/meetings/<slug>.md` could outlive its transcript indefinitely.

**Fix.**
1. src/main/index.ts recallDeleteAll: `const wiki = removeWiki(getSettings())` beside purgeBrain — unconditional, NOT gated on publishBrainPages (a mirror survives the OFF edge whenever that removal returned ok:false). Folded into the audit line as `wikiRemoved: wiki.ok`, and a failed removal now returns `{...result, ok:false, error:'Deleted the transcripts, but the published wiki pages could not be removed. Close anything using the meetings folder, then try again.'}` so the renderer's error branch (Settings.tsx:6367-6382) has real text instead of a causeless "failed".
2. Deleted the `meetings.length === 0` early return; the dialog message now reads "Delete all Métis data on this device?" when the count is zero, so the derived artifacts are purged for a profile whose meetings were already deleted one-by-one.
3. src/main/brain/publish.ts removeWiki no longer rm -rf's `wiki/`. `wiki/` sits inside the user's own (often OneDrive) meetings folder, so it now deletes exactly what this module authors — WIKI_DIRS (`people`, `accounts`, `deals`, `meetings`, derived from KIND_DIR) + WIKI_ROOT_DOCS (`index.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) — then removes the root only when nothing else is left in it; `ok` means no published page survived. This is MQA-032's isOwnedMeetingFile lesson applied to the same handler. publishIndexes now writes those four docs from a `Record<(typeof WIKI_ROOT_DOCS)[number], string>` so the published set and the erased set cannot drift (a fifth doc is a type error, not a survivor). Coverage proof: every wiki write in publish.ts goes through entityPagePath (:54), meetingCardPath (:65) or the WIKI_ROOT_DOCS loop (:908) — the only writeWikiFile call sites are :551, :733, :908.
4. src/main/index.ts recallDelete: after a successful deleteMeeting, `await publishMeetingCard(getSettings(), safeName)` — publish.ts:631-634 already unlinks the card when the source file is absent and publish.ts:616 no-ops when publishing is off, so this closes the single-delete orphan with zero new deletion code and no dependence on a rebuild running.

### MQA-151 — A hedge winner that fails mid-stream is suppressed to silence

**Repro.** Default settings (`resilience.hedge` = true, default provider NVIDIA NIM per shared/ipc.ts:721). User asks a base-tier question. NIM emits its first token at ~1.2s -> onDelta -> `race.gate.declareWinner('primary')` (index.ts:3545); the 3000 ms hedge timer then finds `isDecided()` true and returns at index.ts:3802 WITHOUT touching `hedgeMayStart` or `deadLegs`. NIM streams ~200 tokens, then the connection black-holes. openai.ts:77-80's idle watchdog fires at +45s (`baseIdleMs` for a base answer, index.ts:3485) and calls `onError('Stream timed out — no response from the model.')` before aborting, so it IS delivered; a mid-stream socket reset reaches the same place via openai.ts:220-223. In index.ts's onError `gotToken` is true, so the exhaustion (3624), retry (3689) and failover (3700) branches are all skipped and control reaches index.ts:3735 `if (!race || race.gate.markDead(race.leg) === 'surface')`. `markDead('primary')` returned 'suppress' -> neither `streams.delete(req.id)` (3739) nor `IPC.streamError` (3740) ran. No terminal event of any kind. Renderer: `streaming: true` is set at state.ts:398 and cleared only by onDone/onError/user-cancel, so the partial answer sits under a live pulsing spinner forever (Answer.tsx:224-226) and the `streams` map holds the HedgeRace plus both handles until the next ask.

**Intended.** hedge.ts:29-31 — "markDead() only says 'surface this' once every leg (including a backup that hasn't started yet) is confirmed unable to answer." hedge.test.ts:150-152 names the failure mode: "The worst possible outcome: no answer AND no error... the ask spins forever." MQA-144 requires every terminal path under a race to delete the combined streams entry.

**Actual (before).** hedge.ts:112-124 — `markDead` never consulted `this.winner`. `startHedgeEarly()` (hedge.ts:102) returns immediately when a winner exists, so it does not flip `hedgeMayStart`; line 122 then computed `otherStillViable = this.hedgeMayStart && !this.deadLegs.has('hedge')` = `true && true` and line 123 returned 'suppress' — on the strength of a backup that `startHedgeLeg` had already refused to launch. hedge.test.ts:118-125 set up exactly this state but asserted only that the starter was not called, never the return value, which is why the suite was green.

**Fix.** hedge.ts, after `deadLegs.add(leg)` and the `startHedgeEarly()` call: `if (this.winner !== null) return this.winner === leg ? 'surface' : 'suppress'`. Winner-scoped rather than the blunt unconditional 'surface': a LOSER can still re-enter `markDead` un-gated (the same-provider retry timer at index.ts:3689 is not cleared by `declareWinner`, and the ineligible branch at index.ts:3453/3457 has no `isLoser` check), and an unconditional surface would fire `IPC.streamError` over the winner's live stream. index.ts:3739's `if (race) streams.delete(req.id)` now runs on the winner path, closing the handle leak in the same change. The renderer keeps the partial text (state.ts:337 `flush()`, and `noOutput` is false once deltas arrived) and shows the real error instead of an endless spinner.

### MQA-152 — publishMeetingCard rebuilds the whole alias map per meeting — publishAll is O(meetings × entities) uncached blocking decrypt reads (MQA-031 fix is half-done)

**Where.** `src/main/brain/publish.ts:555` (pre-fix) · workflow: flag a meeting confidential / rebuild the brain with wiki publishing on · fix size: small

**Intended.** publish.ts:836-838 states the rule MQA-031 established, in code, for the confidential set: "One scan for the whole regeneration: a full-corpus rescan per page is O(pages × meetings) synchronous read+decrypts on the main process, which is what froze the app for minutes on one Confidential toggle." corrections.ts:482-488 justifies readRawEntityFile's deliberate bypass of store.ts's jsonCache on the premise "it's not a hot path (once per meeting ingest, same order of cost as lintBrain's own full entity scan)."

**Actual.** Only the confidential half was threaded. `publishMeetingCard` (publish.ts:523 pre-fix) had no `knownAliases` parameter and ran an unconditional `const aliasMap: AliasMap = readAliasMap(s)` at publish.ts:555. `readAliasMap` (corrections.ts:688-692) = `readEntityAliasMap` (corrections.ts:565-591, loops every slug of all three ENTITY_KINDS calling `readRawEntityFile` — corrections.ts:493-499, a readFileSync + AES-GCM decrypt + JSON.parse that bypasses jsonCache) ∪ `aliasMapFromJournal(readCorrectionsJournal(s))` (corrections.ts:302-313, another readdirSync + uncached decode). `publishAll` (publish.ts:841-844) calls publishMeetingCard once per meeting extraction, so the per-page full-corpus rescan MQA-031 removed for confidential flags was still there for entities. `publishForExtraction` (publish.ts:806-828) already receives the `aliasMap` ingestExtraction built one statement earlier (ingest.ts:1495 → :1503) and forwards it to publishEntity, but not to publishMeetingCard — so every ingested meeting paid two full entity-corpus scans.

**Repro.** 300 saved meetings / ~1000 entities, encryptTranscripts on. Review → Confidential → IPC.recallSetConfidential (index.ts:2887) awaits `publishAll(s)` (index.ts:2903) → 300 note cards × ~1000 uncached readFileSync+decrypt+JSON.parse of entity files, plus 300 readdirSync and 300 uncached journal decodes, all synchronous on the main process. Pinned mechanically instead of by wall clock: with 3 note cards, readAliasMap was called 3 times per publishAll (test asserts 1) and once inside publishForExtraction despite the caller passing a map (test asserts 0).

**Fix.** `publishMeetingCard` takes `knownAliases?: AliasMap`, resolved lazily as `knownAliases ?? readAliasMap(s)` and ONLY when the card actually has an extraction (all three consumers — attendee/account/deal links — are extraction-gated, so an extraction-less card now pays nothing at all; `resolveEntitySlug` already accepts `undefined`). `publishAll` builds the map once beside `confidential` and threads it into every card (safe: nothing between :940-950 mutates an entity). `publishForExtraction` forwards the map it already holds, which also makes the card's links resolve through the SAME map mergeExtraction routed the entities with. Single-card callers that pass nothing keep today's fresh-read behavior.

**Deliberately NOT done** (per the verifier's fixReview): the proposal's "hoist readConfidentialMeetings across a backfill batch" was rejected. That set is a fail-closed security gate, not a perf cache (publish.ts's own doc comment: "Read fresh on every publish call (no cache)… correctness… matters far more than the cost"), and a batch spanning minutes would publish a meeting flagged confidential mid-batch. It stays per-merge.

### MQA-153 — Transcript escrow public key honored from the environment in packaged builds

**Repro.** Attacker gets one-shot code execution as the user and sets `HKCU\Environment\ASKTOTO_ESCROW_PUBKEY` to a base64 RSA PEM whose private key they hold — no elevation, no Métis file touched, no ACL-gated path involved. The next launch inherits it. From then on every save with `encryptTranscripts` on (the schema default, src/shared/ipc.ts:786) — saveMeeting, saveNote, saveDraftTranscript, recoverOrphanDrafts, plus every brain entity via brain/store.ts:242 and every recall edit — reaches transcripts.ts:142-149 and writes `kEscrow` = RSA-OAEP(per-file AES content key) into the envelope in the OneDrive-synced meetings folder. A copy of the .md file is then enough to recover the full transcript offline: no keychain, no DPAPI, no further device access. There is no signal — auditLog fires only on the `escrowFailed: true` branch at :155, and no UI shows escrow is active — so the channel survives key rotation, settings:recoverProfile, and the attacker losing code execution. On macOS this bypasses the Keychain ACL that otherwise blocks a foreign same-user process.

**Intended.** src/main/transcripts.ts:84-88, verbatim: "SECURITY: escrow decides WHO can decrypt every future transcript, so it must never be honored from a user-writable source. The per-user `userData/managed-config.json` is writable by the current user (and anything running as them), so a planted `escrowPubKey` there would silently wrap every transcript to an attacker key (readable off OneDrive). Escrow is therefore admin-machine-path-only (ACL-gated by trustedAdminManagedPath) or env (dev) — the per-user tier is deliberately NOT consulted here." Line 80 labels the env tier "(dev)". docs/solutions/2026-07-05-windows-enterprise-port.md:41-44 grades the same planted-key threat CRITICAL. docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1171 documents escrowPubKey only as a managed-config key — the env var appears in no deployment doc.

**Actual.** src/main/transcripts.ts:91 was `const fromEnv = resolveEscrowPem(process.env.ASKTOTO_ESCROW_PUBKEY)`, read FIRST and returned, with no dev gate; `app` is imported at :1 but `app.isPackaged` was never consulted in this file. The process environment is user-writable on exactly the terms the comment rejects (HKCU\Environment, `launchctl setenv`), and nothing strips it — index.ts gates only `loadDotEnv()`, which does not affect an inherited env.

**Fix.** `resolveEscrowPem(devEnv('ASKTOTO_ESCROW_PUBKEY'))` — the shared gate in src/main/dev-env.ts, whose `isPackagedBuild()` reads `app.isPackaged === true` inside a try/catch that fails CLOSED. The read is deliberately NOT bare: an unguarded `app.isPackaged` here throws out of readEscrowPubKey -> encryptEnvelopeV2 -> writeSaved and would FAIL THE SAVE when app is not ready, which is why secrets.ts:79 already wraps the same read. Added a once-per-process `mainLog.warn` for the case where ASKTOTO_ESCROW_PUBKEY is set but ignored because the build is packaged, so an install that had been configured through the dev variable does not lose escrow in silence (the existing warn at :154 fires only for a MALFORMED key). The admin machine-path tier is untouched.

### MQA-154 — Sign-out never stopped background screen pre-analysis

**Repro.** Entra SSO configured (or sticky-configured, so `requireAuth()` follows `signedIn`), `backgroundScreenContext` on and Métis Local provisioned (or macOS Vision OCR). Sign in -> `IPC.authSignIn` calls `refreshScreenPreprocess()` (src/main/index.ts:2761 pre-fix), which spawns the long-lived foreground-watcher child (foreground-watcher.ts:166-205) and arms `setInterval(onRefreshTick, 6000)` (screen-preprocess.ts:282). Click Sign out -> `IPC.authSignOut` (src/main/index.ts:2768-2772) does `assertMainWindow(e)` -> `await importJobs?.cancelAll()` -> `return authSignOut()` and nothing else. Wrong result: the watcher child and the 6 s tick survive; every tick still screenshots the full screen, OCRs/captions it and writes `capture.screen` + `screen.preprocess.describe`. No in-app stop existed — `IPC.settingsSet` returns early at `if (!requireAuth())` ~90 lines before its own `refreshScreenPreprocess()` call, so a signed-out user could not turn it off, and the only other `stop()` caller was `will-quit`.

**Intended (quoted).** src/main/index.ts, on `refreshScreenPreprocess`: "(Re)start or stop background screen preprocessing to match current auth + settings eligibility", body `if (!requireAuth()) { screenPreprocess.stop(); return }`. src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:83 on `stop()`: "Tear down: kill the watcher, clear timers, drop any cached description." Sign-in calls it for exactly this reason.

**Actual (pre-fix).** src/main/index.ts:2768-2772 — the sign-out handler never called it; repo-wide grep showed only three call sites (definition, `IPC.settingsSet`, `IPC.authSignIn`). Nothing inside the engine re-checks auth: `eligible()` (screen-preprocess.ts:148-149) tests only `backgroundScreenContext` + `localReady()/ocrAvailable()`, and `getScreenshot()` checks only Private View.

**What sign-out tore down vs. missed (enumerated).** Tore down: the session + MSAL/Graph token cache + sticky-configured + LKG config (auth.ts `signOut()` -> `clearSession()`), and in-flight import decode/transcription jobs (`importJobs.cancelAll()`). Missed: the screen-preprocess engine (this row) and the Mantu Intelligence window (MQA-169) — and it missed both entirely on the two paths that clear a session with no IPC call at all (max-age eviction in `loadSession`/`authStatus`, and the background re-validation sweep's expiry/revocation).

**Fix.** Closed in one place instead of at the handler. src/main/auth.ts: new `setSessionClearedHandler(fn)`, fired at the end of `clearSession()` inside a try/catch (teardown must never leave a half-cleared session). src/main/index.ts: `revokePrivilegedSurface()` next to `refreshScreenPreprocess()` — it calls `refreshScreenPreprocess()` (which stops the watcher child, the 6 s tick and the cached description once `requireAuth()` is false) and `closeIntelligenceWindow()` when `!requireAuth()` — registered with `setSessionClearedHandler(revokePrivilegedSurface)`. The sign-out handler is unchanged: it reaches the revoke through `authSignOut()` -> `clearSession()`, and so do expiry and admin revocation. `eligible()` was deliberately NOT auth-gated (the verifier's fixReview: that stops captures but leaks the watcher child and timer forever); the real `stop()` is what runs.

### MQA-155 — Retention sweep's detached source refresh has no rejection handler

**Repro.** `transcriptRetentionDays` set (e.g. 30). Six-hour interval armed at `src/main/index.ts:4848` fires; `sweepExpiredMeetings` deletes >=1 expired meeting so the `r.deleted > 0` branch runs. At that instant `.brain/index.json` is locked (OneDrive sync client / on-access AV → EBUSY/EPERM on the tmp+rename, or ENOSPC/EACCES). `writeIndex` rejects → `updateIndex`'s `run` rejects → the `await` inside `requestSourceRefresh` re-throws into ITS returned promise, which nothing chains onto. → `process.on('unhandledRejection')` (index.ts:4809) → `onFatal` → `persistCrash` writes `crash-<ts>-<seq>.log` into userData AND an `auditLog('app.crash', …)` record. **Wrong result: a fabricated crash event in the audit trail for an app that never crashed, while the real fs failure is silently discarded.** Because `reconcileMeetingsInBackground` re-enters the same bare `void requestSourceRefresh(s)` on its 60s tick, the false records repeat for as long as the fs fault lasts.

**Intended (quoted).** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1188-1193`, the house rule for exactly this call: "`updateIndexDetached(...)` reads as 'deliberately not awaited', but `void` does NOT attach a rejection handler — only the internal `indexLock` chain above is caught, and the promise handed back to the caller still rejects. … Log and swallow instead." Restated at the already-fixed sibling `src/main/index.ts:2266-2268`: "Deliberately not awaited …, but the rejection is observed: escaping as an unhandledRejection writes a crash-*.log + an app.crash audit line for a failed publish that never crashed anything (MQA-075…)", and at index.ts:1875-1876 for the notifier tick ("rather than letting the rejection escape as an unhandledRejection → bogus crash audit").

**Actual (pre-fix).** `src/main/index.ts:4833-4845` — `const runRetentionSweep = (): void => { sweepExpiredMeetings(...).then((r) => { if (r.deleted > 0) { auditLog('transcript.deleted', …); void requestSourceRefresh(getSettings()) } }).catch(() => {}) }`. The trailing `.catch` binds to the OUTER `.then` chain; line 4837's `void` is a statement in a block-bodied arrow, so the inner promise is never returned and never chained in. `requestSourceRefresh` (ingest.ts:2004-2009) is `async` with no try/catch, so it cannot throw synchronously either. Same shape at `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:2085` (`startBackfill`) and `:2300` (`reconcileMeetingsInBackground` — whose `try/catch` catches only synchronous throws).

**Fix.** index.ts:4841 now `void requestSourceRefresh(getSettings()).catch((e) => mainLog.warn('[brain] source refresh after retention sweep failed:', …))`, matching the blessed sibling at index.ts:2270. The same one-line `.catch` added at ingest.ts:2085 and ingest.ts:2302. Nothing else changed: the resolved value was already unused, and the refresh flag is re-requested by the 60s reconcile tick, so no signal is suppressed.

**Test.** `src/main/main-lifecycle.contract.test.ts` lifts the real `runRetentionSweep` closure out of index.ts and executes it against a `requestSourceRefresh` stub whose promise stand-in records whether `.catch` was ever called — an untouched spy is precisely the unhandledRejection path. A second assertion pins that no bare `void requestSourceRefresh(...)` remains in brain/ingest.ts.

### MQA-156 — captureDegraded is a single slot: a mic drop-and-recover erases a still-live 'them' degradation

**Repro (macOS, defaults: audioSource 'both', Screen Recording NOT granted).** Press Listen → start() falls through to the mic-only fallback and sets `captureDegraded = { side:'them', note:'System audio needs Screen Recording permission…', permission:true }` (listen.ts:1389 pre-fix). Bar shows the honest amber "Mic only" chip. Twenty minutes in the mic track fires 'ended' (lid-close sleep/wake, AirPods drop) → openChannel's `t.onended` writes `{ side:'you', note:MIC_LOST_MSG }` **over** the them entry (listen.ts:918 pre-fix). recoverMic re-acquires the default mic ~200 ms later and clears the slot: `captureDegraded: s.captureDegraded?.side === 'you' ? null : s.captureDegraded` → **null** (listen.ts:966 pre-fix). From that moment the Bar chip shows the red dot + "Heard live" and the minimized pill shows the confident pulsing red dot, while the loopback was never acquired and never will be — the macOS permission watcher (listen.ts:1093-1099 pre-fix) only calls recoverSystemAudio once `screenRecording === 'granted'`, which never happens. The user finishes the meeting believing both sides were transcribed.

**Intended (quoted, listen.ts:201-207).** "A capture side the session REQUESTED but is NOT currently hearing, while Listen stays active … Exposed as its own structured field — separate from the sticky `error` note … so persistent chrome (the Bar's \"Heard live\" chip, the minimized control pill) can show a truthful degraded state **for the entire mic-only stretch**. Tony sat through a whole meeting on 2026-07-20 with Screen Recording off and only found out from the unusable transcript." Consumers: Bar.tsx:439-464 (amber "Mic only"/"No mic" vs. the red "Heard live" chip), App.tsx:2984 `captureDegraded={listen.captureDegraded}`, App.tsx:2957 `degradedNote={listen.captureDegraded?.note ?? null}`.

**Actual (pre-fix file:line).** One slot, every writer wholesale: listen.ts:918 (mic 'ended' → `{side:'you'}`, no read of the previous value), listen.ts:966 (recoverMic success → null). Nothing anywhere derives the field from live capture state (`wantsSystemRef` / `channels.current.them`), so the them fact is simply gone.

**Fix.** The them-side cause is now remembered independently of the single exposed slot, and the mic-recovery clear can no longer speak for the other side.
- New pure decision `degradedAfterMicRecovery(current, themDegraded, wantsSystem, hasThemChannel)` (listen.ts:246): a mic recovery only retires a `{side:'you'}` entry, and while the session still wants system audio with no 'them' channel it re-exposes the remembered them cause (keeping the specific Screen-Recording copy and `permission:true`).
- New `themDegradedRef` (listen.ts:404) written at every site that degrades 'them' — the start-time mic-only fallback (listen.ts:1454), a mid-session 'them' track death (listen.ts:975-976), the probation recycle (listen.ts:885-886) — and dropped only when 'them' is genuinely capturing again (listen.ts:1078) or a fresh session starts (listen.ts:1222).
- recoverMic's success path (listen.ts:1020-1026) now routes its clear through the helper instead of `? null : s.captureDegraded`.
The shipped `CaptureDegraded` shape is unchanged, and all six anchor assertions in App.mic-only-visibility.test.ts still pass. No UX state added: during the mic outage the chip still reads "No mic"; after recovery it correctly returns to "Mic only" instead of "Heard live".

### MQA-157 — a language probe from the previous session pins the new session's Whisper worker

**Repro.** Meeting 1 is Portuguese; Settings → Audio spoken language = 'auto', engine Whisper (all defaults). pump() fires a probe: `window.toto.parakeetFeed(job.audio, 'them')` (listen.ts:598-603 pre-fix). Main-side this is the session's first Parakeet call, so parakeetFeed → getRecognizer() constructs the sherpa OfflineRecognizer and loads the ONNX weights (main/parakeet.ts:99-114; parakeetRelease() nulls the recognizer at every setListeningState(false), main/index.ts:4517) — a multi-second round trip with no timeout on the probe path (unlike the parakeet ENGINE feed, which races PARAKEET_FEED_TIMEOUT_MS). Inside that window the user hits Stop then "New meeting" (App.tsx:1713-1716 toggleListen → endReview → startListen; startListen's own comment names "A rapid Stop → New meeting" as a real user action). Session 2 is English. The stale probe resolves, and because start() re-raised `liveRef.current = true` (listen.ts:1145) the guard passes; `probePinnedRef.current` was reset to false (listen.ts:1157), so the probe takes the initial-pin branch and posts `{type:'pinLanguage', language:'Portuguese'}` to session 2's freshly `resetFollow`-ed worker. whisper.worker.ts:275-289 latches `probePinned = true` and never un-pins, so session 2's English audio decodes as Portuguese until two consecutive confirming re-probes land (SWITCH_AFTER=2 on the PROBE_EVERY=4 cadence) — roughly the opening minute. The same warm worker spans both sessions (WORKER_IDLE_RELEASE_MS = 180_000; start() cancels the pending release).

**Intended (quoted, listen.ts:462-464, immediately above the guard).** "The session may have moved on (stopped, switched engine, or the user set an explicit language) by the time this async round trip resolves — **a stale probe must not touch the current state**." And listen.ts:388-391 on the probe refs: "Reset on every start() and on a real setLanguage() change so **a new/changed session never inherits a previous pin**." The file already carries the correct primitive: `sessionEpochRef` (declared listen.ts:1492, bumped listen.ts:1142), used by stop()'s drain at :1546 and :1574 — "A new start() ran while we were draining — it already owns the session; do not clobber it."

**Actual (pre-fix file:line).** listen.ts:465 was the whole guard: `if (!liveRef.current || engineRef.current !== 'whisper' || asrLanguageRef.current !== 'auto') return`. `liveRef` is not session identity — start() sets it true again for the NEXT session — and `sessionEpochRef` appeared nowhere in probeLanguageWindow.

**Fix.** probeLanguageWindow now stamps the session epoch synchronously at dispatch (`const epoch = sessionEpochRef.current`, listen.ts:505) and the `.then` runs the new pure predicate `probeResultIsStale(dispatchEpoch, currentEpoch, live, engine, language)` (listen.ts:101, wired at listen.ts:512-521). The epoch check is **added to** the existing live/engine/language checks, which still cover mid-session fallBackToWhisper and setLanguage — those do not bump the epoch. Same-session probes see an unchanged epoch, so the MQA-012 opening-burst behavior is untouched.

### MQA-158 — The Desk Tap Control "paused — recalibrate" banner is cleared by every routine settings re-fetch and never re-raised

**Repro.** Calibrate Desk Tap Control on the system default mic (TapCalibration stamps `profile.micDeviceId = 'default'`), then pick an explicit USB headset in Settings → Audio. useTapControl detects `p.micDeviceId !== (micDeviceId ?? p.micDeviceId)`, returns without starting a capture, and raises the flag — correct so far. Now click anywhere on the overlay, or let any routine refresh fire: `useSettings`'s window-'focus' listener, App's streaming→idle `refresh()`, or any `patch()` — including the unattended `asrLastFallbackAt` / `asrWebgpuFallbackAt` / `micOnlyFallbackAt` writes a live meeting makes on its own.
→ `settings` is replaced, `tapCfg?.profile` gets a new object identity, the clearing effect sets `tapMismatch` back to false, and **nothing re-raises it**: the hook keys its own effect on `[active, profileKey, micDeviceId]`, a string built precisely to absorb that identity churn, so `mismatchRef.current?.()` does not re-fire. The amber banner disappears within seconds, Settings still shows "Calibrated and ready.", and no desk tap ever works again — the exact silent-dead-feature state MQA-083 was written to close.

**Intended.** The banner's own comment (App.tsx): "Not dismissible: it isn't a one-off event, it's a standing state that lasts until the user recalibrates." The clearing effect's comment claimed "on a still-mismatched profile the hook re-raises the flag straight after" — false for every trigger except a genuine profile/mic change or an `active` flip, since MQA-084 replaced the hook's object-identity dep with the stable `profileKey`.

**Actual (pre-fix).** `App.tsx:2230` was verbatim `useEffect(() => setTapMismatch(false), [tapCfg?.profile, settings?.micDeviceId])`, with `onProfileMismatch: () => setTapMismatch(true)` as the only raiser. `profile` arrives as a fresh structured clone from every `settings:get` / `settings:set` round trip (preload `ipcRenderer.invoke`, stored raw by state.ts with no deep-equal and no memo), so the effect re-ran on every settings read while `tap-control.ts`'s `profileKey = ${version}|${sampleRate}|${micDeviceId}|${createdAt}` deliberately did not.

**Fix.** Per the fixReview: delete the state and derive the value, which is what the banner's own "standing state, not an event" comment already describes. Removed the `useState`, the clearing effect, and the `onProfileMismatch` wiring; added exported pure `tapProfileMismatch(tap, micDeviceId)` = `Boolean(tap?.enabled && tap.profile && micDeviceId && tap.profile.micDeviceId !== micDeviceId)`, read as `const tapMismatch = tapProfileMismatch(tapCfg, settings?.micDeviceId)`. It cannot desynchronize (recomputed from the same snapshot the hook reads), mirrors tap-control.ts:238's semantics including "no explicit device selected (system default) is never a mismatch", and is automatically correct on recalibration, on switching back to the calibrated mic, and on turning the feature off — the last of which the fixReview flagged as a regression in the finder's proposed dependency-array fix. The finder's variant also dropped `profile.version` from the key; deriving removes the key entirely. `onProfileMismatch` had no other caller, so it is deleted from `UseTapControlArgs` and the hook body in the same change (Build Law rule 1) — the mismatch branch there now just returns.

### MQA-159 — The confidential flag is never evaluated for team-folder transcripts — a teammate's confidential meeting is published to the plaintext wiki

**Where.** `src/main/brain/publish.ts:149` (pre-fix) · workflow: ingest a shared team transcript folder with wiki publishing on · fix size: small

**Intended.** publish.ts:126-128 — readConfidentialMeetings returns the meetings "that must be kept OUT of the published wiki: those flagged `confidential: true` in their frontmatter, PLUS every meeting this device cannot read." The published corpus asserts it unconditionally to its readers: publish.ts README_MD "Meetings flagged confidential in Métis are excluded from every page here" and CLAUDE_MD "Meetings I flagged confidential are already excluded from this folder." recall.ts:655-657 — "a confidential meeting is excluded from every published wiki surface (note card, entity timelines/current-facts, indexes)." Team folders are a first-class ingest source (ingest.ts:2150-2196, Settings.tsx:5418-5463).

**Actual.** Two independent breaks. (1) `readConfidentialMeetings` (publish.ts:146-160 pre-fix) built its set only from `listSavedMeetingFiles` — a single readdirSync of `resolveMeetingsFolder(s)`, the user's OWN folder; `grep -n team src/main/brain/publish.ts` returned 0 matches. (2) Even if it had scanned them, the key shape was wrong: a team meeting's `MeetingRef.file` is the namespaced ingest key, not a basename — ingest.ts:1431 `const key = indexKey ?? basename(file)`, ingest.ts:1453 `const ref: MeetingRef = { file: key, … }`, with `indexKey = \`team/${owner}/${f}\`` (ingest.ts:2158-2161). Every exclusion gate compares that key — `confidential.has(m.file)` in timelineRows (publish.ts:253) and newestDate (:264), `confidential.has(c.meeting)` in openCommitmentRows (:259), `NOT_CONFIDENTIAL(field.source_file, …)` at :175/:185/:203, confidentialOnly (:453), topByActivity (:704) — and a basename-keyed Set can never contain `team/alice/2026-02-01_140000-pricing.md`, so every gate answered "safe to publish".

**Repro.** Alice flags her pricing meeting confidential (recall.ts:690-693 writes `confidential: true`) and shares her meetings folder; Bob adds it under Settings → team folders. Bob's backfill ingests it as `team/alice/…-pricing.md` (ingest.ts:2183-2191) and publishForExtraction publishes the touched entities. Bob's `<meetingsFolder>/wiki/` — plaintext, OneDrive-synced, and explicitly handed to Claude/Dust by wiki/CLAUDE.md — then contains the meeting's title + date in the account/deal timelines (publish.ts:284-288), its open commitments rendered verbatim as "<person> owes: <text>" (publish.ts:290-297), its stage/win-likelihood fact rows, and the title again in index.md "Recent meetings". Bob has no mitigation: recall.ts only ever lists `resolveMeetingsFolder`, so he cannot see or flag the file himself. Pinned by test: a deal carrying `{ file: 'team/<owner>/alice-pricing.md', title: 'Alice Pricing Negotiation' }` plus a commitment "drop the floor price to 40k" on that key — both strings appeared in the swept wiki corpus after publishAll, with the team file flagged confidential on disk.

**Fix.** publish.ts only.
- New `addConfidentialTeamMeetings(s, out)` runs after the own-folder loop inside `readConfidentialMeetings`. For each `settings.teamTranscriptFolders` entry it enumerates `.md` files with the same predicate ingest uses (`isMeetingFileName`, extracted from listSavedMeetingFiles) and derives the SAME key ingest does (`teamMeetingKey` = `` `team/${basename(folder) || 'team'}/${f}` ``).
- Fail CLOSED by inversion, not by scanning: a team key is publishable only if it was positively **cleared** (file read here, complete frontmatter block present, no `confidential: true`). Everything else is added to the exclusion set — unreadable file, unparsable/encrypted head, readdir throw, folder missing. The universe of keys is `keys seen on disk now` ∪ `keys in the brain ingest index` (`readIndex(s).ingested`, filtered on the `team/` prefix), so an **unreachable share still fails closed**: the refs persist in `.brain` after the folder is gone, and the index is the durable record that says those keys are team keys. The on-disk half is what covers a meeting being ingested for the first time (ingestExtraction publishes BEFORE it writes `idx.ingested[key]`).
- Cost guard (the hazard the verifier flagged): team files are read through a new bounded `readTeamFrontmatterHead` (openSync/readSync of the first 8 KiB, frontmatter sits at byte 0) instead of `readSavedFile`'s whole-file read+decrypt, because this scan runs on EVERY merge via publishForExtraction and pulling whole transcripts down a network/OneDrive share would reintroduce exactly the MQA-031 main-process stall. Anything that is not plaintext frontmatter — including a teammate's ATKENC envelope, which readSavedFile could not decrypt on this device either — is simply not cleared, i.e. fails closed.
- `publishMeetingCard` now returns immediately for a `team/`-prefixed key. Previously it reduced the key to a basename and, if the user happened to own a same-named `.md`, wrote THAT meeting's card under the shared slug (or deleted that card). Team meetings get no note card here — their transcript is not in this device's folder.

Matches the fail-CLOSED direction MQA-074/MQA-077 established for own meetings (publish.ts:151-157).

### MQA-160 — an edited team transcript is never re-ingested, and the comment that says otherwise was the only thing guarding it

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:1641-1677` (drift detection) · workflow: Bob adds Alice's shared OneDrive folder under Settings → team transcript folders, Alice later edits a transcript in it · fix size: small

**Repro.** Alice's `weekly-sync.md` ingests OK, so `idx.ingested["team/alice/weekly-sync.md"] = { ok: true, sourceVersion: "<mtime>:<size>" }`. Alice then rewrites the file in place (a 90-second debrief appended, a mis-heard name corrected, a Teams speaker backfill) and OneDrive syncs the new bytes to Bob. Bob's 60-second reconcile tick → `reconcileMeetingsInBackground` (ingest.ts:2285) → `hasMeetingSourceDrift` → `startBackfill`. Wrong result: nothing happens. The pre-edit extraction keeps driving Bob's account/deal/person entities through every reconcile, every relaunch and every "Index meetings" click; only an unrelated own-source drift or a manual `brain:rebuildAll` (which purges `idx.ingested`) ever picks the change up.

**Intended.** ingest.ts:1668-1672 stated the design in its own words: team keys are skipped by the drift detector because `currentMeetingSourceVersions` (keyed by basename) never has them, and "**A changed team file re-ingests via its own sourceVersion check in the team scan.**" The `Job` doc at ingest.ts:1104-1105 states the general guarantee: "mtime/size snapshot at queue time; a later edit must not be merged incrementally."

**Actual.** No such check existed. `hasMeetingSourceDrift` excluded every team key at ingest.ts:1672 (`if (file.includes('/')) continue`; team keys always contain '/' by construction at ingest.ts:2161), and the team scan skipped on identity alone one level down — ingest.ts:2162 `if (already.has(key) || inFlight.has(key)) continue`, with `already` built from every `ok:true` record at ingest.ts:2075. The `sourceVersion` the team loop recomputes at ingest.ts:2165 was only ever compared inside the `!record.ok` retry-backoff branch (ingest.ts:2167-2175), i.e. for FAILED records. So an `ok:true` team record had no drift path at all — and a DELETED team file was equally invisible.

**Fix.** Drift detection now owns team sources instead of a comment promising someone else does. `currentMeetingSourceVersions` (ingest.ts:1641) also walks each `s.teamTranscriptFolders` entry and emits the same namespaced `team/<owner>/<file>` identity `startBackfill` writes into the index, so a changed or deleted team transcript routes through the existing `requestSourceRefresh` → `startRebuild` purge-and-rebuild that own meetings already use. The naive alternative — a version-aware skip in the team loop — was rejected: `mergeExtraction` is purely additive (`pushUnique` de-dups identical facts, it cannot retract one), so an incremental re-merge of a corrected transcript would leave BOTH the wrong and the right person node, which is worse than stale. The false comment at ingest.ts:1668-1672 and its `file.includes('/')` skip are deleted, not amended. Unavailable shared folders stay conservative (`return null`, never read as a deletion), matching `hasIncompleteMeetingSource`'s `if (!existsSync(teamFolder)) return true`. Price accepted, knowingly: a teammate's edit now costs a full purge + re-extract, the same cost the own path already pays, serialized by `sourceRefreshRunning`.

### MQA-161 — Hedge backup picked against the ORIGINAL primary id, so it can duplicate the provider the primary already failed over to

**Repro.** Default install, `s.provider` = 'nvidia' (ipc.ts:721-722 documents NIM as the hedge-raced default) with an Anthropic key configured; the NIM key is revoked. t=0 `attempt('nvidia', [], 0, {leg:'primary'})` -> 401 at ~0.4s -> non-transient (retry.ts:60-62) -> `failover(['nvidia'], false, race)` -> `pickFailover` returns 'anthropic' -> `attempt('anthropic', ['nvidia'], 0, {leg:'primary'})` — SAME leg identity (index.ts:3315-3322 doc: the cascade "stays part of the SAME leg"). Nothing on the failover path clears `hedgeTimer`. t=3000 ms the timer fires: `race.isDecided()` false, `pickFailover([primary])` = `pickFailover(['nvidia'])` and, `pickFailover` being pure with byte-identical inputs, deterministically returns 'anthropic' again. `attempt('anthropic', ['nvidia'], 0, {leg:'hedge'})` -> two byte-identical Anthropic requests in flight for one ask: the full system prompt + transcript (and on a vision ask the whole base64 screenshot) billed twice, the rate-limit budget spent twice, and the "hedge" buys nothing because both legs share one failure mode. A plain transport blip collides the same way: `hasFailoverTarget` sets `retryBudget` = 1 (index.ts:3668) and `nextBackoff(0)` is 250-500 ms, so the failover lands ~0.7s, 2.3s before the hedge fires.

**Intended.** hedge.ts:4-9 — HEDGE_DELAY_MS is "how long the primary provider gets before a backup starts racing it"; hedge.ts:14-16 — "Exactly two legs ever compete — the primary provider and the one backup started after HEDGE_DELAY_MS"; index.ts:3781-3785 — "races a backup provider against the primary". The `[primary]` argument exists only to stop the hedge racing the primary's own provider.

**Actual (before).** index.ts:3803 `const backup = pickFailover([primary])` where `primary` is the const captured at 3765 — the provider the leg STARTED on, never reassigned. `pickFailover` (3239-3305, documented "Pure (no side effect)") filters solely on `tried.includes(p)` / `isCoolingDown` / `budgetBlocked`; nothing tracks in-flight legs. index.ts:3813 then passed `[primary]` as the hedge leg's own `attempted`, so a failing hedge could ALSO fail over straight back onto the provider the primary was streaming from.

**Fix.** Added `const primaryChain: ProviderId[] = []` next to the `AttemptRace` type (index.ts ~3309) and, on entry to `attempt()`, `if (race?.leg === 'primary' && !primaryChain.includes(provider)) primaryChain.push(provider)` — recorded before any eligibility work, so a provider the primary merely bounced off still counts. `startHedgeLeg` now snapshots `const tried = primaryChain.slice()`, picks with `pickFailover(tried)`, and passes `tried` into `attempt(backup, tried, 0, {gate: race, leg: 'hedge'})` so the hedge's own failover cascade carries the same exclusion. `pickFailover(tried)` returning null still routes to `race.markHedgeUnavailable()`, which is what lets `markDead('primary')` surface honestly. The finder's stated alternative (cancel the hedge on failover) was NOT taken: `startHedgeLeg` never consults `hedgeMayStart`, so the timer would still fire, and flipping `hedgeMayStart` false would make `markDead('primary')` return 'surface' and push an error toast over a live hedge stream — regressing MQA-132/MQA-134.

### MQA-162 — a failed entity write left the in-memory cache advertising facts that never reached disk

**Where.** `src/main/brain/ingest.ts:756-988` (`mergeExtraction`) · workflow: Index meetings / any ingest, with `.brain` inside a OneDrive-synced folder · fix size: small

**Repro.** Meeting M2 merges onto an account/person/deal that M1 already created. `mergeExtraction` reads each entity, mutates it, then awaits the write. `writeSaved` bounds its rename retry to 5 attempts over ~600 ms and rethrows EPERM/EBUSY past that, rethrowing any other errno immediately (transcripts.ts:296-305), so an AV/OneDrive lock throws out of `writeAccount` (ingest.ts:800). `finishJob` catches it and records `ingested[M2] = { ok:false, retryAfter… }` (ingest.ts:1553-1567) — the file on disk is untouched, so its (mtimeMs, size) is unchanged and `jsonCache` keeps serving the object that was mutated in place. For the rest of the process `brainRead` (index.ts:3980-3994) shows M2 on the person/account/deal rails, `buildBrainContext` cites it in live answers, and `publishEntity` writes it into the wiki timeline — while `index.json` says M2 was never ingested and `brainRead` hides M2's own card. Restart the app and all of it silently vanishes.

**Intended.** store.ts:259-264, verbatim: "readJson's cache returns the SAME object reference on a repeat read of an unchanged file (keyed by path+mtime+size, not by caller) — mutating it in place silently edits every other holder of that reference, and **leaves the cache advertising a value that was never persisted if the write then fails**. Every read-modify-write below and in corrections.ts clones first, so it only ever owns the copy it writes."

**Actual.** `mergeExtraction` cloned nothing. `readJson` returns the cached instance on a hit and caches the very object it returns on a miss (store.ts:214-236), and `writeJson` only does `jsonCache.delete(p)` AFTER its await (store.ts:239-246). Six reads were mutated in place: `readGraph` at ingest.ts:756 (mutated by addNode/addEdge for the whole function, written only at :987 — so ANY earlier write failure stranded it), the account at :767 (written :800), the person at :806 (written :864), the second account at :858 (written :861), the deal at :869 (written :984) and the third account at :978 (written :981). `settleCommitment` (ingest.ts:1075-1076, 1083) was the only site in the file that honoured the rule; the MQA-085 regression test (ingest-audit-fixes.test.ts:282-307) pinned only that one.

**Fix.** The write is the point of truth: every one of the six reads is now `cloneEntity(...)`, so the function mutates a copy and the cache only ever gains the new state through `writeJson`'s post-write invalidation plus a fresh parse. No invalidation call was bolted onto each failure site, and `readJson` was deliberately NOT made clone-on-read — three pollers re-read the whole dataset every 3-10s (store.ts:201-206), which is exactly the cost the cache exists to avoid. Success-path behaviour is unchanged: `cloneEntity(null)` is `null`, so the `?? { …seed }` fallbacks still work, and the clone is what gets written.

`src/main/brain/ingest-merge-cache.test.ts` fails one target write through `writeSaved` (the single lane every brain write takes) and asserts the account, graph, person and deal readers still return only the persisted meeting afterwards. Restoring any of the six in-place reads fails it.

### MQA-163 — Windows system-audio recovery retries a full display-capture acquisition every 3 s for the whole meeting, with no backoff and no attempt cap

**Repro.** Windows, audioSource 'both' → `wantsSystemRef.current = true` is set in start() before `listening: true`, so the watcher effect exists for the session. WASAPI loopback cannot start for the whole call (VDI/RDP with no render endpoint, every output disabled, or another app holding the render endpoint exclusively). Start-time grab fails → UI falls back to mic-only; `channels.current.them` stays null and `state.listening` stays true, so the tick guard never short-circuits.
→ The interval fires every 3000 ms for the entire meeting and calls recoverSystemAudio unconditionally: ~2400 attempts in a 2 h call, each `armAudio(true)` → `getDisplayMedia({audio:true})` → on reject `getDisplayMedia({video:{frameRate:1},audio:true})`, which reaches the main handler's video path and runs `getScreenSourcesWithRetry(() => desktopCapturer.getSources({types:['screen']}))` — up to 3 enumerations with 250/500 ms sleeps (src/main/screen-capture.ts:33-48), each reading `source.thumbnail.getSize()`, i.e. a real thumbnail grab of every screen. Every rejected attempt also spread a fresh state object, re-rendering App (useListen is called at App.tsx:248) on a 3 s cadence for the whole meeting.

**Intended.** The watcher's own comment scopes this to a recoverable blip: "a transient start-time loopback failure (default output mid-switch, another app holding the render endpoint) left the meeting mic-only until the user stopped and restarted Listen". The main handler documents the audio-only request as the cheap path and the video path as the unvalidated fallback: "Skip desktopCapturer entirely in that case: no screen source is grabbed for a request that never wanted one. CAVEAT: Chromium's support for Windows loopback-audio-without-video hasn't been validated on real hardware yet" (src/main/index.ts:4859-4869).

**Actual (pre-fix, verified against `git show HEAD:src/renderer/src/lib/listen.ts`).** The Windows arm of the watcher was literally `if (isWindows) { void recoverSystemAudioRef.current?.(); return }` — no attempt counter, no backoff, no terminal state anywhere in the effect or in recoverSystemAudioRef (whose only early returns are `!liveRef.current || sysRecoveringRef.current` and `channels.current.them`, with `sysRecoveringRef` cleared in `finally` so the next tick re-enters). The macOS arm IS gated on `p?.screenRecording === 'granted'`; Windows had no equivalent gate. The catch spread `{ ...s, error: s.error === null ? THEM_LOST_MSG : s.error, captureDegraded: s.captureDegraded ?? {...} }` on every failure, even when both fields were already value-identical (`??` returns the same identity on repeat failures).

**Fix.**
(a) New exported pure `sysRetryDelayMs(consecutiveFailures) = Math.min(3000 * 2 ** n, 30_000)`. The Windows arm now skips ticks until `sysRetryNextAtRef` passes and arms the next delay off `sysRetryAttemptsRef++`, leaving `setInterval(…, 3000)` alone: 3s → 6s → 12s → 24s → 30s ceiling, ~243 attempts in 2 h instead of ~2400. Deliberately **not** terminal — the headline case in the watcher's own comment (another app holding the render endpoint) emits no 'devicechange', so a give-up cap would re-open MQA-041 for exactly the scenario MQA-041 names. Counters reset in the three places recovery becomes plausible again: start() (fresh session), the successful `openChannel('them')` path, and the devicechange `'recover'` branch (a real device change is new evidence and gets an immediate attempt rather than waiting out the backoff).
(b) New exported pure `themRecoveryFailureIsNoop(error, captureDegraded)`; the failed-retry catch returns the previous state object unchanged once both are already set, so a permanently-stuck retry no longer re-renders the App tree. The write still only ever RAISES, so an existing `captureDegraded` (carrying the more specific start-time Screen-Recording copy) survives.
(c) MQA-041's regression test asserted the literal source text of the old `if (isWindows) { … }` block. It now anchors on the branch's CONTENT — that the Windows tick re-acquires off capture state (`void recoverSystemAudioRef.current?.()`) and never reaches `getPermissions` — so it still guards MQA-041 while allowing the pacing.

### MQA-164 — A failed update download never reaches the renderer: the Settings row is stuck on a fake progress bar with the download-page fallback hidden

**Repro.** Packaged install, Settings → About. Manual check reports 1.5.5 available; user clicks "Download & install version 1.5.5". `startDownload` sets `phase='downloading'` synchronously (Settings.tsx:3911) and main answers `{started:true}` (updater.ts:175, pre-fix) — which it returned the moment `checkForUpdates()` resolved, i.e. before the download ran (`node_modules/electron-updater/out/AppUpdater.js:422` puts `downloadPromise` into the result WITHOUT awaiting). The download then dies for an ordinary reason (proxy 403 on objects.githubusercontent.com, laptop sleep, sha512 mismatch, or `verifyUpdateCodeSignature` rejecting the .exe — electron-builder.yml:221). electron-updater routes it to `dispatchError` → `emit('error')` (AppUpdater.js:449-460, 476-478).

→ Wrong result: the row keeps "Downloading update… 41%" forever and the download-page link stays hidden, because it renders only for `phase === 'blocked' || 'idle'` (Settings.tsx:3965). Second wrong result: the discarded `downloadPromise` rejection reaches `process.on('unhandledRejection')` (index.ts:4733) → `onFatal` (index.ts:1368) → `persistCrash` (index.ts:1348-1357), writing a `crash-*.log` and an `app.crash` audit line for something that is not a crash. The boot / 6-hourly path leaked the same way through electron-updater's own unreachable `void it.downloadPromise.then(...)` (AppUpdater.js:294).

**Intended (quoted).** Settings.tsx:3963-3964 — "Download-page fallback: a build that cannot self-install (portable / Store / managed / unsigned mac), or any download-start failure. Always reachable so the user is never stranded." And updater.ts:156-159 — "…this just kicks a fresh find-and-download, so the Settings row can show 'Downloading… X%' and then 'Restart & install'."

**Actual (pre-fix).** src/main/updater.ts:236-243 was the ONLY 'error' handler and both branches ended in `log.warn` with no `webContents.send`, unlike the sends at :259/:265. src/shared/ipc.ts:178-182 had no error channel at all (repo-wide grep for `update:error|updateError|onUpdateError` returned zero hits), and src/preload/index.ts:306-310 exposed only onUpdateReady/onUpdateProgress/installUpdate/downloadUpdate — main had no way to tell the renderer anything had failed.

**Fix.**
- `src/shared/ipc.ts`: new `updateError: 'update:error'` channel (main → renderer, same class as updateDownloaded/updateProgress; no ipcMain.handle needed).
- `src/main/updater.ts`: module flag `downloadInFlight`, set only by `startUpdateDownload` and cleared when the download settles. The 'error' listener forwards `IPC.updateError` ONLY while that flag is set, so the silent boot/6-hourly check can never flip an untouched Settings row into an error; the 404 early-return still forwards nothing. The payload is a fixed human string ("The update download failed. Open the download page to install manually.") — electron-updater's own message embeds the feed URL and request context, and this process redacts before every sink (index.ts:1350), so it stays in `log.warn` only.
- `src/main/updater.ts`: `startUpdateDownload` now reads `(await checkForUpdates())?.downloadPromise`, returns `{started:false, reason}` when there is no download to watch, and holds the promise (`then(settle, settle)`) so a failure is no longer an unhandledRejection.
- `src/main/updater.ts`: `initAutoUpdate`'s `check()` no longer calls `checkForUpdatesAndNotify()` — that method fires its notification from a derived promise it never handles and we cannot reach, so a failed BACKGROUND download wrote a fake `app.crash` too. It now calls `checkForUpdates()` and catches `result?.downloadPromise`; the OS "update ready" notification moved into the existing `update-downloaded` listener (which already has version + notes) and is skipped when the user started the download themselves, preserving exactly the prior user-visible behaviour.
- `src/preload/index.ts`: `onUpdateError` next to onUpdateProgress.
- `src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx`: UpdatesSection subscribes to it, `setPhase('blocked')` + `setDownloadError(message)`, so the existing fallback link (whose other conditions `result?.ok && result.available` are already true in this scenario) renders as "Open the download page instead".

**Tests.** `src/main/updater.test.ts` seeds the CJS require cache with a fake AppUpdater (vi.mock cannot intercept updater.ts's deliberate lazy `require('electron-updater')`) and drives the real `initAutoUpdate` + `startUpdateDownload`: forwarding on a mid-flight failure, no raw feed URL/token in the payload, no unhandled rejection, no error for a background-check failure, and the OS notification still shown. `src/renderer/src/components/Settings.contract.test.ts` pins the renderer half (source-contract pattern already used in that file).

### MQA-165 — The Cahê embedded-key gate scans app.asar and the compressed installer — never resources/cahe/kimi.json, the only file that holds the key

**Repro.** Build a keyed Cahê package (`electron-builder --config electron-builder.cahe.win.yml --win nsis --x64` with `build/cahe-kimi.local.json` holding a live `sk-kimi-…`), then run `node scripts/check-cahe-package.mjs <out>` with `METIS_CAHE_EMBED_KEY` unset. `<out>/win-unpacked/resources/cahe/kimi.json` contains the key → gate exits **0** and prints `…distinct identity, no embedded Kimi key`. The documented hard refusal never fires. Same on the sanctioned CI path (.github/workflows/cahe-windows.yml:97 writes the real key, :103 sets `METIS_CAHE_EMBED_KEY=1`): the ⚠️ extractability warning at check-cahe-package.mjs:69-79 cannot print because nothing ever matched, so the run log again ends in "no embedded Kimi key" for a build that ships one.

**Intended.** docs/WINDOWS.md:176-183 — "Without `METIS_CAHE_EMBED_KEY=1`, `scripts/check-cahe-package.mjs` hard-refuses the package the moment it finds an `sk-kimi-` pattern … **With** the flag set, the same scan still runs but tolerates the key, printing a loud multi-line warning that names the file it found the key in". Same promise in electron-builder.cahe.win.yml:17-18 ("the packaging-time scan only allows it through with METIS_CAHE_EMBED_KEY=1 set, printing a loud warning when it does") and docs/cahe-windows-edition.md:32. check-cahe-package.mjs:61-65 calls the flag "the one, deliberate way" past a gate that otherwise "never allow[s] an embedded Kimi key".

**Actual.** scripts/check-cahe-package.mjs:105-106 called `assertNoEmbeddedKimiKey` on exactly two paths — `appAsar` (:32, win-unpacked/resources/app.asar) and `installer` (:22, the NSIS .exe). The key is in neither: electron-builder.cahe.win.yml:19-21 copies build/cahe-kimi.local.json to `cahe/kimi.json` as an **extraResource**, i.e. to win-unpacked/resources/cahe/kimi.json, outside app.asar (corroborated by src/main/cahe-embedded-key.ts:115 reading `join(process.resourcesPath, 'cahe', 'kimi.json')`; electron-builder.win.yml's `files:` allowlist is `out/**/*` + package.json, so build/ can never enter the archive). Inside the .exe the file exists only within the LZMA-compressed app-64.7z payload (no `compression:` override anywhere → app-builder-lib defaults to `-mx=9`; NsisTarget sets `SetCompress off` because the payload is already compressed), so the latin1 substring scan at :86-98 cannot match plaintext `sk-kimi-…` there either. Nothing else covered it: check-packaged-runtime.mjs inventories models/asr/ort, local-llm, llama and ffmpeg subtrees but never resourcesRoot itself, so the extra `cahe/` directory is neither inventoried nor scanned.

**Fix.** scripts/check-cahe-package.mjs now also scans the packaged extraResources destination — every regular file under `<out>/win-unpacked/resources/cahe/`, `existsSync`-guarded so a deliberately keyless build (`METIS_CAHE_ALLOW_KEYLESS=1`, which produces no `cahe/` directory) still passes instead of throwing ENOENT out of the read stream. The app.asar and installer scans stay, re-labelled in a comment as a net for a key landing where it was never meant to be rather than coverage of this one. No whole-`resources` walk: that tree is the multi-GB runtime payload (models/asr/ort/llama/ffmpeg/local-llm) and streaming it through a latin1 regex on every build is not affordable. docs/WINDOWS.md:176-183 rewritten to name the bundle that is actually scanned and to say plainly that the compressed `.exe` scan cannot see `cahe/kimi.json`.

**Pinned by.** `scripts/check-cahe-package.test.ts` drives the real script as a subprocess against a synthetic package: keyed → non-zero exit + `Refusing Cahê package with an embedded Kimi API key: kimi.json`; keyed with `METIS_CAHE_EMBED_KEY=1` → exit 0 + `Found in: kimi.json`; keyless → exit 0 + `no embedded Kimi key`; plus an assertion that the gate's scan root still matches the builder config's `to: cahe/kimi.json`, so moving the destination cannot silently un-reach the refusal again.

### MQA-166 — CI "Secret scan" could not match this product's own sk-kimi- key shape and never looked at scripts/, build/ or intelligence/

**Repro (real grep, clean `git worktree add --detach HEAD` checkout, pre-fix step body).** Write `const k = 'sk-kimi-A1b2C3d4E5f6G7h8xyzQWERTY'` into `src/leak-probe.ts` — i.e. inside the one root and one include the old scan actually covered — and run the step body from `.github/workflows/build.yml`. Result: `No committed secrets found.`, exit 0. The Security job goes green on a committed key. Same file at `scripts/leak-probe.mjs`: same green, for a second independent reason (wrong root AND `*.mjs` not in `--include`). Control: `sk-ant-…` exits 1, so the harness was correct.

**Intended.** build.yml:70 — "Secret scan: fail if a key-shaped string is committed to source", and the step prints "No committed secrets found." only when nothing matched. This is the repo's ONLY committed-credential gate: no husky/git hooks, no gitleaks/trufflehog, no npm script does it, and `scripts/check-cahe-package.mjs` is not a substitute (it inspects a BUILT installer, runs only in the Cahê Windows chain, and merely warns).

**Actual.** Two independent holes.
(a) Prefix. build.yml:75 was `grep -rInE '(nvapi-|sk-ant-|sk-or-|gsk_|fw_|tgp_v1_)[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}'`. `sk-kimi-` absent, and `sk-or-` requires that literal, so nothing substituted. `sk-kimi-` is a first-class shipped format: `src/main/cahe-embedded-key.ts:11` `KIMI_KEY_PATTERN = /sk-kimi-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}/`, `scripts/build-cahe-windows.mjs:23` same pattern embedding it into the Cahê installer, `src/shared/providers.ts:178-179` `keyHint: 'sk-kimi-…'` / `keyPattern: '^sk-kimi-'`. Three further declared prefixes were equally uncovered: `^xai-` (:249), `^AIza` (:314), `^eyJ` (:160).
(b) Scope. build.yml:78 roots were `src .github electron-builder.yml`; :76 includes had no `*.mjs`. Never scanned: `scripts/` (the whole .mjs build/release chain), `build/` (where `cahe-kimi.local.json` lives), `intelligence/src` (a real source tree shipped as extraResources per electron-builder.yml:64-65), `electron-builder.win.yml`, `electron-builder.cahe.win.yml`, `package.json`. Corollary: line 70's ".env.example placeholders" carve-out was vacuous — repo root was never scanned and `.env.example` matches no `--include`.
