**Reachable.** `build/cahe-kimi.local.json` exists in the working tree and is kept out of git only by `.gitignore:17` (`git check-ignore -v` confirms; `git ls-files build/` does not list it). A deleted ignore line, a `git add -f`, or a key pasted into any `scripts/*.mjs` or `intelligence/src/*.ts` all reached a green Security job.

**Fix.** build.yml's Secret scan step body now reads `\b(nvapi-|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]+-|gsk_|xai-|AIza|eyJ|fw_|tgp_v1_)[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}` over roots `src scripts build intelligence/src .github electron-builder.yml electron-builder.win.yml electron-builder.cahe.win.yml package.json`, with `--include='*.mjs'` added and `--exclude-dir=qa` added.
- The literal `sk-ant-`/`sk-or-` terms are DELETED, not kept alongside — `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]+-` subsumes both and adds sk-kimi-, sk-proj-, sk-or-v1-.
- The finder's proposed generic term `sk-[A-Za-z0-9-]{20,}` was rejected as dead code: inside the group it inherits the trailing `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}`, demanding 36+ chars. The verifier's replacement `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}` is dead for the same reason (verified: it does NOT match `sk-kimi-AbCdEf0123456789xyzQWERTY`, needing 32 chars after the prefix). Moving the generic term to the PREFIX half, where it shares the group's single `{16,}` suffix, is what actually fires.
- `\b` is new and load-bearing: without it `sk-` matches inside ordinary words, so `risk-management-configuration-value` is a hit. Same anchor `src/shared/redact.ts:70` already uses.
- `--exclude-dir=qa` ships WITH the widened roots, not after: `scripts/qa/e2e-workflows.mjs:301` (`DEAD_NVIDIA = 'nvapi-dead0…'`) and :195 (a fake `sk-` probe) are deliberate degrade-path fixtures. Without the carve-out the first push after this change fails CI for a non-defect.

**Pinned by** `scripts/ci-secret-scan.contract.test.ts` (7 tests), following `scripts/ci-cost-gates.contract.test.ts`: it extracts the regex/includes/excludes/roots out of build.yml as text and EXECUTES them. The prefix expectation is derived from `providers.ts`'s own `keyPattern` declarations rather than re-listed — the same move `redact.ts` made for MQA-080 ("deriving them closes the class instead of the instances") — so a provider added later with a new prefix fails this test until the CI gate learns it. A final test models a CI checkout (`git ls-files` + the declared include/exclude flags) and asserts zero hits, so a future widening cannot silently turn the Security job red.

### MQA-167 — ASKTOTO_SELFTEST is honored in packaged builds and destroys the user's real profile

**Repro.** Métis is a launch-at-login tray app. Any code running as the user (no admin) runs `setx ASKTOTO_SELFTEST %TEMP%\r.json`; the shipped app relaunches. index.ts:4753 fires -> runSelfTest operates on the LIVE profile: selftest.ts:25-28 resolves `<userData>/settings.json` and `<userData>/managed-config.json`, :32 overwrites the enterprise policy file, :52 replaces the safeStorage-encrypted settings.json with 62 bytes of plaintext, :65 and :98 delete it, :47 deletes managed-config.json; index.ts:4759 quits with no window shown. store.ts's `.recovered` backup never triggers because :52 writes syntactically valid plaintext JSON that readUserRaw parses happily. Because `setx` persists, this repeats on EVERY launch: permanent silent DoS plus irreversible loss of meetingsFolder, profile PII, context docs, mcpConnections, teamTranscriptFolders, transcriptRetentionDays, and the per-user `allowedProviders`/`locked` policy read by store.ts:212/220/235.

Second defect, same trigger: suites 1 and 2 restore in a `finally` (selftest.ts:46-48, :64-66) but suite 3's cleanup at :96-98 sat INSIDE the `try` (catch at :99). Any throw between :74 and :96 (unwritable tmpdir, saveMeeting failure) was swallowed and left the profile on `encryptTranscripts: false` with `meetingsFolder` pointing at a directory the function then deletes — every later meeting written as cleartext.

**Intended.** src/main/index.ts:402-406: "Disable via env for dev/screenshots ONLY — gated to unpackaged builds so a packaged process can never have capture protection stripped by `setx ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP 1` + relaunch" -> `if (!app.isPackaged && process.env.ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP)`. The line immediately AFTER the defect applies the same discipline: index.ts:4762 `if (!app.isPackaged) loadDotEnv() // dev convenience only; never read a stray .env in production`.

**Actual.** src/main/index.ts:4753 was `if (process.env.ASKTOTO_SELFTEST) {` with no `app.isPackaged` term and no requirement that ASKTOTO_USERDATA isolate the profile. `runSelfTest` is a static import (index.ts:241) so it is bundled into the packaged main; no dead-code elimination is possible on a runtime env check.

**Fix.** index.ts now reads `const selfTestOut = devEnv('ASKTOTO_SELFTEST')` (the shared gate in src/main/dev-env.ts) and branches on that, so the suite cannot run in a packaged build. selftest.ts hoists `const folder = ...` above the suite-3 `try` — required, because `folder` was declared inside it — and moves `setSettings({ meetingsFolder: '', encryptTranscripts: true })` plus the two `rmSync` calls into a `finally`, so a mid-suite throw can no longer leave the borrowed profile unencrypted. The only recorded ASKTOTO_SELFTEST usage anywhere is an unpackaged `electron .` run, so no workflow is broken.

### MQA-168 — METIS_CAHE_EDITION=1 is honored in packaged builds and kills the update path

**Repro.** Shipped enterprise install. A local user sets `METIS_CAHE_EDITION=1` (setx persists across reboots) and the tray app relaunches. `initializeCaheEditionIdentity()` runs at index.ts:346, before any userData read: `app.setName('Métis')` and `app.setPath('userData', %APPDATA%\Metis Windows Cahe)`, and index.ts:366 then skips the rename migration. `shouldDisableAutoUpdate()` -> `blockedUpdateChannel()` (updater.ts:52) returns 'cahe', which turns the silent electron-updater flow off AND makes Settings -> About's manual "Check for updates" answer with the BLOCKED_MESSAGE (updater.ts:66) rather than an error — so the install stops receiving security patches for as long as the variable is set, and the UI reports that as normal. `seedCaheLocalAiForBackgroundScreen()` additionally flips `localLlm.enabled: true` and `backgroundScreenContext: true` on the new profile unrequested. The env branch carries no platform term either, so a packaged macOS build flips too. (Not permanent: %APPDATA%\Metis is untouched and unsetting the variable restores everything.)

**Intended.** src/main/cahe-edition.ts:27-30, verbatim: "The Cahê edition is a separately packaged Windows executable. The environment switch is deliberately limited to local test/build harnesses; installed copies identify themselves from their executable name." The file's own exe-name branch at :34 already carries the guard (`platform === 'win32' && packaged && executable === CAHE_EXECUTABLE_NAME.toLowerCase()`). updater.ts:9-11 states the stronger invariant: "IT can freeze the version fleet-wide ... Only the ADMIN (machine) policy is honored ... so a standard user cannot turn their own updates on or off."

**Actual.** src/main/cahe-edition.ts:32 was `if (environment.METIS_CAHE_EDITION === '1') return true` — the FIRST statement of detectCaheEdition, evaluated before the guarded exe-name branch, with no `packaged` term even though `packaged` is destructured at :31. cahe-edition.test.ts:17-50 covered win32/packaged/cahe-exe, darwin/packaged, win32/unpackaged and darwin/unpackaged/env — never packaged+env, which is exactly why it survived review.

**Fix.** :32 becomes `if (!packaged && environment.METIS_CAHE_EDITION === '1') return true`. `isCaheEdition()` now supplies `packaged: isPackagedBuild()` (the shared fail-closed read in src/main/dev-env.ts) instead of a bare `app.isPackaged`, because it runs at module load before app ready. The shipped pilot is unaffected: electron-builder.cahe.win.yml:7 sets `executableName: Metis-Windows-Cahe`, so it still identifies via the exe-name branch — pinned by the second assertion in the new test. The darwin+unpackaged+env case stays true, as cahe-edition.test.ts:42-49 deliberately asserts.

### MQA-169 — Sign-out never revoked the open Mantu Intelligence dashboard window

**Repro.** SSO-configured or sticky-configured install. Open Mantu Intelligence (`IPC.brainOpenDashboard`), then sign out from Settings — or let an admin revoke the seat. The overlay drops to the SignInWall. Wrong result: `intelWin` is a separate top-level BrowserWindow (`skipTaskbar: true`, but reachable on Alt-Tab) and keeps rendering the full decrypted brain — every person, account, deal, verbatim quote and open commitment — with no error banner. intelligence/src/lib/useDashboardData.ts:60 swallows the thrown 'Not signed in.' whenever data is already on screen (`error: prev.data ? null : err.message`), and its status poll self-terminates after 3 consecutive nulls (:87-91), so it never retries. `window-all-closed` is a deliberate no-op, so the stale render survives until the process quits.

**Intended (quoted).** Every brain channel requires a live session: src/main/index.ts:3957 `if (!requireAuth()) return null` (brain:status), :3991 and :4032 `if (!requireAuth()) throw new Error('Not signed in.')` (brain:backfill / brain:read), and even opening it at :3940. src/main/intelligence.ts:8-9: "The dashboard aggregates the most sensitive cross-meeting data (people/accounts/deals/quotes/commitments)." The sign-out handler already tears down other in-flight work — src/main/import-jobs.ts:266 "Sign-out boundary: stop any decoder/transcription work before the auth session is cleared."

**Actual (pre-fix).** src/main/index.ts:2768-2772 cancelled import jobs and called `authSignOut()`, nothing else. src/main/intelligence.ts exported only `syncIntelContentProtection`, `isIntelligenceSender` and `openIntelligenceWindow` — there was no close/destroy path in the file at all, `intelWin` was nulled only by its own `closed` listener, and no auth-change broadcast reached that window.

**Fix.** src/main/intelligence.ts: `export function closeIntelligenceWindow(): void { if (intelWin && !intelWin.isDestroyed()) intelWin.destroy() }` — Electron guarantees `closed` still fires, so the existing listener nulls `intelWin` and `isIntelligenceSender()` fails closed for the dead webContents (pinned by the test). src/main/index.ts: it is called from `revokePrivilegedSurface()` (guarded by `if (!requireAuth())`, so an unconfigured self-serve install that never gates the dashboard does not lose its window), which src/main/auth.ts's new `setSessionClearedHandler` fires from `clearSession()`. That funnel is why the fix is not at the IPC handler: `clearSession()` is also the expiry path (`loadSession`/`authStatus` max-age eviction) and the background re-validation sweep's revoked-refresh-token path — the "admin frees the seat" case named in the repro, which never reaches an IPC handler. Polling brain:status was not used as the trigger (fixReview's alternative): that would leave a ~2 s window and put teardown inside a read handler; the clearSession hook is instant and covers every path.

### MQA-170 — the graph purge left graphify's manifest behind

**Repro.** Encryption OFF + graphifyEnabled/graphifyAutoRebuild (defaults) + the third-party `graphifyy` package installed. Meetings save under readable names (`transcripts.ts:619 namePart = settings.encryptTranscripts ? opaqueNamePart() : slug(title)`), e.g. `2026-08-19_143000-acme-q3-renewal-pushback.md`. Every save schedules a build; the runner writes `<userData>/graph/graphify-out/manifest.json` = a JSON map of every scanned file's ABSOLUTE path → {mtime, md5}. User then turns "Encrypt transcripts at rest" ON → index.ts removed graph.json + graph.html and audited `graph.purged {reason:'encryption-enabled'}`; manifest.json stayed on disk with the dated list of meeting titles, and because the boot/poll reconciler was gated on `graphHtml()` still existing (index.ts:2013 pre-fix) it never fired again. Same residue survives the more reachable path with no encryption toggle at all: recallDeleteAll → purgeGraphArtifacts, under a dialog promising "every saved transcript, note, and the knowledge graph" is gone.

**Intended (quoted).** src/main/graphify.ts:465-472 (pre-fix): "Delete the plaintext graph artifacts (graph.json + graph.html) from userData/graph. Called when at-rest encryption is toggled ON … a previously-built CLEARTEXT graph would otherwise linger on disk … leaking exactly the meeting content the encryption is meant to protect." And filenames are explicitly sensitive in this codebase — transcripts.ts:687-688: "Encrypted at rest → the filename must not leak the plaintext title either (see opaqueNamePart above)."

**Actual (pre-fix).** src/main/graphify.ts:475 iterated exactly `[graphJsonPath(), graphHtmlPath()]` — two hardcoded names under `outDir()` = `<userData>/graph`. But resources/graphify_runner.py:77-79 chdirs INTO that directory under its own comment "graphify keeps its manifest + cache under the cwd's graphify-out/. Run from the output dir so those artifacts stay in AskToto's app data", then line 120 `save_manifest(...)`. `graphify-out` appeared zero times in src/, so nothing ever removed it.

**Fix.** graphify.ts: added `runnerOutDir()` = `join(outDir(),'graphify-out')` and purgeGraphArtifacts now removes graph.json, graph.html AND that directory (recursive, still inside the per-path try/catch — the contract is "best-effort: never throws", and a recursive rmSync on Windows can throw EBUSY/EPERM). Deliberately targets `graphify-out` rather than `outDir()` itself, because the spawned python has chdir'd into outDir() and Windows cannot delete a live process's cwd. Signature changed `void → boolean`: true when something existed and was removed. Both audit sites now key off that return — index.ts:2013 `if (getSettings().encryptTranscripts && purgeGraphArtifacts()) auditLog('graph.purged', {reason})` and index.ts:2227 `if (!wasEncrypted && next.encryptTranscripts && purgeGraphArtifacts())`. That is what let the reconciler's `graphHtml()` precondition be dropped safely: the reconciler runs on EVERY settingsGet poll plus boot, so widening the predicate without gating the audit would have written a `graph.purged` record forever (the hazard the fixReview flagged). The doc comment's two-file scope was rewritten to the real set.

### MQA-171 — MCP API key and OAuth refresh token are written with a truncating writeFileSync despite the function's "Never partially writes" contract

**Repro (inputs/state -> wrong result).** User has ClickUp connected: `key-mcp-clickup.bin` + `key-mcp-clickup-refresh.bin` on disk, both valid. A 401 self-heal or a Reconnect calls `setMcpRefreshToken('clickup', …)`. Node's `writeFileSync` opens with `'w'` (O_TRUNC), so the existing ciphertext is destroyed before the first new byte lands; ENOSPC / EIO / an EDR-AV handle denial / a hard kill in that window leaves a 0-byte or partial file exactly where the previous ciphertext was. The user sees "Couldn't save the refresh token — Métis can't write to its data folder", which reads as "nothing changed". Next read: `readKeyFile` (mcpSecrets.ts:131-152) — a 0-byte file fails `buf.length > marker.length` at :135 and falls to the safeStorage branch which throws and is swallowed at :144; a truncated ATKMCP1 body fails the GCM tag at :137-139 and is set to `''`. So the still-valid token is *destroyed*, not merely unsaved, and recovery is a full ClickUp OAuth re-consent. Worse than it first looks: clickupOAuth.ts:103 makes `refresh_token` optional in the refresh response, so index.ts:2705 evaluates `refreshed.refreshToken ?? refreshToken` and rewrites the SAME unchanged token on every 401 — a credential that had not changed at all gets destroyed. Same shape destroys `key-mcp-bidstack.bin` / `key-mcp-plane.bin` on a kill mid-write.

**Intended (quoted).** mcpSecrets.ts:71-72: "Encrypt+write one secret to `p`, using the same file-backend/safeStorage choice and error message shape store.ts's setApiKey and the rest of this module already use. **Never partially writes.**" Module header, mcpSecrets.ts:9-12: it "reuses the exact same on-disk primitive store.ts uses for provider keys … so MCP keys are stored with identical at-rest protection". That primitive is explicit about why it is atomic — src/main/store.ts:752-753: "Atomic write: a crash mid-write must not leave a truncated/corrupt key file (which would silently read back as 'no key'). Mirrors the tmp-file + rename pattern already used in setSettings." src/main/secrets.ts:118-125 (persistKeyFileAtomically) says the same: "A plain writeFileSync truncates before it writes, so a crash, an EDR/AV handle denial or ENOSPC in that window leaves a 0-byte or partial key file … rename() is atomic, so the old key survives any failure before it."

**Actual (before fix).** src/main/mcp/mcpSecrets.ts:87-95 was a bare `writeFileSync(p, blob, { mode: 0o600 })` inside a try whose catch only rewrote the message — no tmp, no rename, no cleanup. It was the only credential writer in the repo that was non-atomic; store.ts:752-761 (setApiKey), store.ts:1006-1015 (Dust refresh token) and secrets.ts:118-140 all use tmp+rename. Both `setMcpApiKey` (:104) and `setMcpRefreshToken` (:117) route through it, and none of the three callers (index.ts:2625 mcpSaveConnection, index.ts:2704-2705 the 401 refresh+retry, index.ts:2731-2732 mcpClickupConnect) re-writes, verifies, or restores.

**Fix.** `writeSecretFile` now writes `${p}.tmp` then `renameSync(tmp, p)`, and in the catch does a best-effort `if (existsSync(tmp)) rmSync(tmp)` (wrapped in its own try) before throwing the same user-facing "Couldn't save the <label> …" message the renderer already renders. Byte-for-byte the store.ts:754-761 shape; `renameSync` added to the `node:fs` import. Mode `0o600` survives rename, and on Windows a rename blocked by an AV handle fails with the OLD file still intact — the desired failure direction. The orphan-tmp name `key-mcp-clickup-refresh.bin.tmp` is already matched by store.ts:69's `/^key-.+\.bin(?:\.tmp)?$/` in `encryptedProfileFiles()`, so profile archive/recovery still picks it up.

**Regression test.** src/main/mcp/mcpSecrets.test.ts, describe "durable writes — a failed save must not destroy the credential it was replacing": mocks `node:fs`'s `writeFileSync` to truncate the target to 0 bytes (the O_TRUNC half that already landed) and then throw ENOSPC, then reloads the module from disk. `MQA-171 — a write that fails after the file is opened leaves the previous refresh token intact` asserts the on-disk bytes are unchanged, the token still reads back, and no orphan `.tmp` remains; `MQA-171 — a failed API-key save leaves the previously saved key readable` does the same for `setMcpApiKey`.

### MQA-172 — `second-instance` does not self-heal a null window

**Repro.** `createWindow()` throws during boot (the case index.ts:1179-1186 anticipates: it destroys the partial window, sets `win = null`, rethrows). `runStep('createWindow', createWindow)` at index.ts:5175 swallows that into a log + audit line, and `app.on('window-all-closed')` is a deliberate no-op, so the process lives on with `win === null`. The window is `skipTaskbar: true` (index.ts:1125) and the dock is hidden on macOS, so the only visible surface is the tray. User double-clicks the Métis shortcut → the new process fails `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` and `app.quit()`s (index.ts:4733-4734) → the running instance's `second-instance` handler evaluates `if (win)` as false. **Wrong result: nothing happens. No window, no error, no log line. Repeated launches keep doing nothing.** (Windows/Linux only — macOS `app.on('activate')` at index.ts:5218 already self-heals.)

**Intended (quoted).** `src/main/index.ts:1332-1335`: "Self-heal a null `win` (e.g. a one-time createWindow() throw during boot) by retrying the window creation once at call time, instead of leaving window-dependent hotkeys dead for the process lifetime. **Callers that previously did `if (!win) return` should call this instead.**" Every other user-facing entry point obeys it — `sendHotkey` (1349), `moveBy` (1665), `toggleVisible` (1717), and the import-complete notification click (539, `if (!win || win.isDestroyed()) createWindow()`).

**Actual (pre-fix).** `src/main/index.ts:4736-4741`: `app.on('second-instance', () => { if (win) { if (!win.isVisible()) win.show(); win.focus() } })`. No `ensureWindow()`, and no `isDestroyed()` check before `isVisible()`.

**Fix (three parts — the naive one-liner alone would have shipped a regression).**
1. index.ts:4736 — handler now `const w = ensureWindow(); if (!w) return; if (!w.isVisible()) w.show(); w.focus()`. `ensureWindow()` returns only a non-destroyed window, so this also closes the `isDestroyed()` gap.
2. index.ts:1104 — `createWindow()` given the idempotence it already assumed: `if (win && !win.isDestroyed()) return` at the top. The handler is registered BEFORE `app.whenReady()` while boot's own `runStep('createWindow')` sits behind many awaits, so a user double-clicking twice during a slow boot would otherwise have `second-instance` create window A and the boot step then overwrite `win` with window B — leaving A visible, always-on-top and unreferenced.
3. index.ts:1202 — the `'closed'` handler now does `if (win === self) win = null`, implementing the guard its own comment at 1198-1200 already described. `const self = win` was declared and never read, so closing any stale window nulled the ref to the LIVE one and aborted every in-flight stream.

**Test.** `src/main/main-lifecycle.contract.test.ts` executes the real `app.on('second-instance', …)` registration lifted from source against a fake `app`/`ensureWindow`, asserting the recovered window is shown and focused when `win === null` (and that an existing hidden window is still merely raised, not rebuilt). Two source-contract assertions pin the `createWindow` idempotence guard and the `self === win` guard.

### MQA-173 — The ASR correction + entity-casing regexes are recompiled on EVERY App render, not once per list change

**Repro.** A meeting is live and the copilot streams a suggestion. `useAsk`'s flush is rAF-batched and returns a fresh object so React cannot bail out, so App re-renders ~60×/s for the whole stream. `useListen` is called from App.tsx:248, and both regex lists were bare assignments in the hook body → both recompiled on every one of those renders. `compileEntityCasingCandidates` NFKD-folds every name, sorts, and builds one `new RegExp('(?<![\\p{L}\\p{N}])(?:…)(?![\\p{L}\\p{N}])', 'gu')` per name; `brain:entityNames` returns up to 500 (src/main/index.ts:4010) and `asrEntityBias` defaults to true (src/shared/ipc.ts:921). Measured ~2.5-2.6 ms per call at the 500-name cap → ~150 ms of renderer main-thread work per second of streaming, and 500 RegExp objects allocated and discarded per frame. Reproduced mechanically: 61 renders with an unchanged array identity = 61 compiles of each list.

**Intended.** listen.ts: "Compiled once per corrections-list change (not per line) — word-boundary + case-insensitive so correcting \"Toto\" never also corrupts \"Tomato\"." and "Compiled once per entityNames-list change (not per line), same idiom as correctionsRef above." src/renderer/src/lib/entity-casing.ts:66-67: "Exported so callers (useListen) can compile once per entityNames change instead of per transcribed line — the same idiom listen.ts already uses for asrCorrections' correctionsRef."

**Actual (pre-fix listen.ts).** `correctionsRef.current = (corrections ?? []).filter(…).map((c) => ({ re: new RegExp(…, 'gi'), to: c.to }))` and `entityCasingRef.current = compileEntityCasingCandidates(entityNames ?? [])` — bare render-body assignments, no useMemo, no identity guard, no ref gate. Once per render, which is neither "per list change" nor "per line".

**Fix.** Both assignments are wrapped in an identity guard against a companion ref (`compiledCorrectionsForRef` / `compiledCasingForRef`) holding the array the current compile was made from — the fixReview's preferred form over `useMemo`, because useMemo is an explicit performance hint React may discard, so it would leave the comments only usually-true. Both inputs really are referentially stable between fetches (App.tsx's `entityNames` useState, replaced only by the mount/savedPath effect, and `settings?.asrCorrections` off the settings useState), so identity is exactly "the list changed". A real edit still recompiles: patch → refresh → new settings object → new array identity. `commitLine` is byte-for-byte unchanged — it still reads `correctionsRef.current` / `entityCasingRef.current`, and the `entityCasingRef.current.length` gate is untouched.

### MQA-174 — Dashboard slug() omits slugify()'s Windows-reserved-name branch, breaking every entity join for those names

**Repro.** Account named `AUX` (AUX Group is a real multinational; CON/NUL/PRN/COM1-9/LPT1-9 behave identically).

- Ingest side: `resolveEntitySlug` -> `slugify('AUX')` -> base `aux` -> reserved -> `aux-x`. Entity file `aux-x.json`, entity `id` `aux-x`, graph node minted as `account:aux-x` (src/main/brain/ingest.ts:796).
- Dashboard side: `slug('AUX')` -> `aux`. `brainAdapter.ts:416` keys `accountBySlug` by `aux`; the node's stripped id at `brainAdapter.ts:437` is `aux-x`, so `accountBySlug.get('aux-x')` (:440) misses and `cold.touch.get('account:aux-x')` (:438) misses (buildGoingCold keyed it `account:aux`, goingCold.ts:122).
- Wrong result: that GraphNode ships with `last_touch`, `days_quiet`, `freshness`, `ref`, `date`, `is_client_facing` all undefined and `unmapped === false`. `GraphView.tsx:56-57` returns opacity 1 when freshness is undefined — byte-identical to `FRESHNESS_OPACITY.fresh` — so the account and its whole edge thread render permanently fresh and are never faded. Its Going-Cold rail row carries nodeId `account:aux`, which fails `nodeIds.has(r.nodeId)` at `BriefingView.tsx:302`, so the row renders with correct copy but loses its `/graph?focus` deep link and is silently unclickable.

**Intended (quoted).** intelligence/src/lib/slug.ts:4-5 — "MUST match the host store's slugify (src/main/brain/store.ts) byte-for-byte in behavior — these slugs join adapter-side entities to graph node ids minted at ingest." src/main/brain/store.ts:62-64 states why the branch exists — "A slug that's a bare Windows reserved device name (CON, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9) can't be opened as a file on Windows … Suffix deterministically so the slug stays stable."

**Actual (before fix).** src/main/brain/store.ts:64 carries `if (base && WIN_RESERVED_NAMES.has(base)) return \`${base}-x\`` (set at store.ts:38-45). intelligence/src/lib/slug.ts went straight from `const base = …` (:25) to `if (base) return base` (:26). Every other token of the two bodies is identical, so this was the sole divergence. Drift, not design: the store gained the branch in f924d8a (2026-07-10), five days after the mirror was last touched (cd5b9a5, 2026-07-05). The branch is unconditional in store.ts (no `process.platform` gate), so macOS ids carry `-x` too.

**Why the existing test could not catch it.** intelligence/src/lib/slug.test.ts:16-27 did not import slugify; it was a hand-written copy used as the oracle, and that copy had ALREADY drifted twice — no reserved branch, and `.slice(0, 60)` where store.ts:57-60 truncates to 51 chars plus an 8-hex sha256. Its five cases were all short and non-reserved, so both drifts were invisible and the suite certified a parity that did not exist.

**Fix.** (1) intelligence/src/lib/slug.ts: added `WIN_RESERVED_NAMES` (verbatim from store.ts:38-45) and `if (base && WIN_RESERVED_NAMES.has(base)) return \`${base}-x\`` immediately before `if (base) return base`. Bodies are now token-identical. (2) Deleted the drifted `storeSlugify` hand copy from intelligence/src/lib/slug.test.ts — it is the thing that masked the bug — and replaced its vacuous `it.each` with direct behavioral assertions on the new branch. (3) New src/main/brain/slug-parity.test.ts imports BOTH real functions (`slugify` from ./store, `slug` from ../../../intelligence/src/lib/slug) and asserts equality across 13 names including all reserved-name shapes, the near-misses `Con Edison` / `Auxilium`, and a >60-char name that exercises the hashed truncation the old oracle also got wrong. Any future drift in either direction now fails.

> MQA-147 .. MQA-174 came from a 41-agent hardening audit (2026-08-19): 8 independent lenses over the
> IPC boundary, crypto/secrets, main-process lifecycle, renderer races, brain data integrity, LLM
> failover, performance and packaging, each finding then adversarially verified by a skeptic told to
> refute it by default. 28 of 32 candidates survived verification; 4 were refuted and are recorded as
> such rather than fixed.

### MQA-150 — alignQuote's fuzzy fallback is cubic in quote length and runs synchronously on the main process

**Repro.** `verifyExtraction()` in `src/main/brain/ingest.ts` calls `alignQuote` synchronously on the main process for every unaligned quote, twice per ingest (`ingest.ts:478`, `:503`, `:512`). With a 120 KB meeting transcript and one 28-token quote that does not align, the fuzzy fallback executed **193,888,628** DP cell comparisons — measured, not estimated, by counting the `Math.max` calls of the LCS recurrence (`src/shared/grounding.mqa150.test.ts:30-43`). A quote entirely absent from the same transcript still cost 19,498,391. Because the main process is blocked for the whole call, every renderer window and every IPC reply stalls with it.

**Intended vs actual.**
- Intended: locate a quote in a transcript, at cost proportional to the number of places the quote could plausibly be.
- Actual (pre-fix `src/shared/grounding.ts:116-127`): the scan built a full LCS table at **every** transcript token position. The table is O(quote × window) and was rebuilt for ~0.3·quote window widths at each of the transcript's tokens — O(transcript × quote³) overall. Growing a transcript 8× with text sharing no vocabulary with the quote multiplied the work by 8.01, exactly linear in transcript length, even though the added text could not contain the quote.
- Additionally, each window was materialized with a `slice()` + `map()` allocation per window on top of the table.

**What changed** (`src/shared/grounding.ts`, +52/-18):
1. **Anchor guard** (`:127-149`). A prefix-sum `Int32Array hits[]` counts how many of the first *i* transcript tokens appear in the query's vocabulary. For each start, the widest enumerable window's hit count gives `min(hits, qLen)/qLen` — a proven upper bound on the score of *every* window at that start, because LCS length can never exceed the count of window tokens present in the query, and the score divisor `max(qLen, len)` is always ≥ `qLen`. A start whose upper bound is below `threshold` is skipped without building any LCS table (`:149`).
   This is **verdict-preserving, not a narrowing**: the only windows skipped are ones that scored below `threshold`, and `alignQuote` already discards those at `:167`. If the true best clears the threshold it is still enumerated, in the same start/len order, so equal-scoring ties still resolve to the same earliest window.
2. **Early exit at a perfect score** (`:163`). `overlap ≤ qLen` and the divisor is `≥ qLen`, so no score can exceed 1, and a later tie would lose to the incumbent on the strict `>` anyway — the remaining scan cannot change the answer.
3. **`lcsLen` takes a range, not an array** (`:83-98`). The window is passed as `[from, to)` into the caller's flat token array, deleting the per-window `slice()` + `map()`, and the DP uses two swapped rows instead of allocating a fresh row per query token.

**Result.** 193,888,628 → 1,640,214 comparisons on the worst case; 19,498,391 → 0 on the absent-quote case (no table is built at all); the 8× transcript-growth case is now flat instead of 8.01×.

**Fidelity is pinned, because correctness outranks speed here.** `src/shared/grounding.mqa150.test.ts` carries 31 named goldens (exact match, reflowed line break, casing drift, ASR filler insertion, drifted numeral, accented French, tie-resolution, leading/trailing noise, empty/whitespace/absent quote, quote longer than transcript, single-token, thresholds 0.1/0.2/0.85/1.0, vulgar fraction, enclosed digit + squared unit, NNBSP thousands grouping, astral emoji, ligature fold, scrambled tokens) plus a 900-trial seeded corpus whose entire result set is pinned by FNV-1a digest and by non-null/fuzzy counts. Every one of those expectations was captured by running the pre-fix implementation and **all of them pass against pre-fix code as well as post-fix code** — a differential proof that nothing `alignQuote` could match before was narrowed away. The work bound is measured as a deterministic comparison count, never wall-clock, per the repo's documented history of load-sensitive timing gates (`vitest.config.ts` MQA-007 note).

### MQA-175 — An undecryptable brain-index envelope terminates the app with an uncatchable native exception

**Repro.** Put an `ATKENC2` v2 envelope that cannot be decrypted at `<meetingsFolder>/.brain/index.json` (a torn or sync-conflicted write — the field copy was 418 bytes, `S:`-wrapped content key, ciphertext failing GCM auth), then launch the packaged app. `app.whenReady()` schedules `resumeBackfillIfPending()` on a 15 s timer (src/main/index.ts:5243); it calls `readIndex(s)` (src/main/brain/ingest.ts:2049), which decrypts that file. The process vanishes 15-20 s after launch — no window, no dialog, no `crash-*.log`, no `app.crash` audit line — on every launch. Bisection on the real profile isolated it to that one file: with `.brain` moved aside the app survived 100 s+; with only `index.json` swapped fresh it survived 60 s+ and completed the backfill resume; restoring the bad `index.json` killed it again.

**Intended vs actual.**
1. src/main/brain/ingest.ts:2064-2066 wraps the whole resume in `try { … } catch { /* brain store unreadable — a manual backfill will surface the real error */ }`. Intended: an unreadable brain store degrades. Actual: the failure was not a JS throw. Crashpad captured a minidump for all six launches with exception code `0xE06D7363` (MSVC C++ throw, magic `0x19930520`), flags `0x81` (NONCONTINUABLE|SOFTWARE_ORIGINATE), raised from `KERNELBASE!RaiseException`, with an identical `ThrowInfo` inside the Metis.exe image every time. A native C++ exception unwinds past V8, so that catch — and `process.on('uncaughtException')`/`unhandledRejection` at src/main/index.ts:4826-4827, and `onFatal`'s dialog and `crash-*.log` — never ran.
2. src/main/transcripts.ts (pre-fix) called `safeStorage.decryptString(Buffer.from(raw, 'base64'))` with whatever the envelope's `kLocal` happened to contain. Chromium's `OSCryptImpl::DecryptString` (components/os_crypt/sync/os_crypt_win.cc) slices a `'v10'`-prefixed blob with `ciphertext.substr(15)` and no length check; `std::string::substr` throws `std::out_of_range` past the end. A blob that is merely wrong returns false (ordinary JS error); a SHORT one raises the native exception. That is the one call in this path that can kill the process rather than fail.
3. src/main/brain/store.ts (pre-fix) `readIndex` was `readJson(…) ?? BrainIndexSchema.parse({})`. `readJson`'s single catch-all (src/main/brain/store.ts:230-233) collapses absent / unreadable / corrupt into `null`, so an undecryptable index was silently indistinguishable from "no brain yet": the whole ingest log was discarded with no log line, the poisoned bytes were left in place to be re-decrypted on every 3-10 s poll, and the next successful ingest would have overwritten them. src/main/brain/corrections.ts:143-190 already documents this exact hazard for its own journal ("not store.ts's cached readJson, whose single catch-all collapses every outcome to `null`") and handles it properly; index.json never got the same treatment.
4. `crashReporter.start({ uploadToServer: false })` (src/main/index.ts:404) had been writing minidumps to `<userData>/Crashpad/reports` all along. Nothing in the app has ever read one.

**What changed.** One mechanism, three effects.

*Degrade.* src/main/transcripts.ts — the single native boundary is now `unwrapWithKeychain()` (transcripts.ts:141), which refuses an empty blob and a `'v10'`-prefixed blob shorter than the position os_crypt_win.cc indexes to (3 + 12 = 15 bytes) as an ordinary JS `Error` before crossing into native code. The bound is the throw boundary, not a well-formed-blob size, so real Windows (≥31 B) and macOS AES-128-CBC (≥19 B) envelopes are untouched. Both `safeStorage.decryptString` sites (v2 `S:` and the v1 legacy branch) go through it. `tryDecodeSaved` now returns a typed `SavedDecode = { ok: true; text } | { ok: false; reason }` (transcripts.ts:276) instead of `string | null`, exported as `decodeSavedResult()` (transcripts.ts:307): "cannot be decrypted here" is a value, not an exception, and is distinguishable from an empty file. `decodeSaved()` and `decryptToTemp()` are thin wrappers over it — no second path.

*Preserve.* src/main/brain/store.ts — `readIndex` (store.ts:462) now calls `quarantineUnusableIndex` (store.ts:438) when `readJson` yields null. It reads the raw bytes; ENOENT/unreadable and 0-byte files are left alone (never a corruption, matching corrections.ts's classification), and a present-but-unusable file is renamed to `index.corrupt-<ISO>.json`, logged through `mainLog.warn` with the decode reason, and the app continues on a rebuildable empty index. Same shape as the corrections journal's quarantine, with one deliberate difference stated in the comment: corrections.json is irreplaceable human input so an undecryptable one is refused transiently, while index.json is derived state rebuildable from the transcripts. Nothing is deleted — the bytes are renamed — which is strictly better than the old behaviour of reading it as empty and then overwriting it. One attempt per path per process bounds a rename that keeps failing under an AV/OneDrive hold.

*Trace + recover.* New src/main/boot-sentinel.ts (dependency-free, node:fs/path only). `beginBootWatch()` writes `<userData>/boot-incomplete.json` before the dangerous work and reports any record a previous run left behind, together with the newest `<userData>/Crashpad/reports/*.dmp` and a consecutive-death count; `endBootWatch()` clears it. Nothing inside a natively-dying process can report on itself, so the surviving file IS the report. Wired at src/main/index.ts:4820 (records the death through the existing `persistCrash` → `mainLog` + `app.crash` audit + `crash-*.log` sink), at index.ts:5243-5249 (when the previous launch died early the brain backfill resume and its reconcile interval are skipped for this session only — safe start — and the watch closes only after the resume has actually survived), and at index.ts:5296 (a graceful quit inside the watch window clears it, so quitting fast is never mistaken for a death).

**Regression test.** `src/main/mqa-175-brain-index-poison.test.ts`, 6 tests. Fixtures are byte-equivalent to the recovered field file: a real `ATKENC2/n` v2 envelope with an `S:`-wrapped content key and one flipped ciphertext byte (GCM auth fails while the wrapped key still unwraps), plus a `'v10'`+4-byte truncated wrapped key for the native-boundary case. Proves: the read path hands the keychain nothing that could throw natively; the bad file is preserved as an `index.corrupt-*.json` sibling with identical bytes while `readIndex` returns a rebuildable empty index that is immediately writable again; a healthy index is never quarantined; an unclosed boot watch is reported on the next launch with its Crashpad dump and a consecutive count; a closed one never is; and the boot sequence routes the resume through the early-death check before clearing the watch.

### MQA-177 — the test suite wrote into the real user profile's log

**Repro (live, on this machine, before the fix).** `C:/Users/Tony/AppData/Roaming/asktoto/logs/main.log` — the file a support engineer reads to diagnose a field crash — held **4331** `[updater]` lines plus a 1.0 MB rotated `main.old.log`. They are provably test output, not field output: the log contains `[updater] error Error: sha512 checksum mismatch` and `[updater] downloaded 1.5.5`, and those exact strings are fixtures inside `src/main/updater.test.ts:282` (`new Error('sha512 checksum mismatch')`) and `src/main/updater.test.ts:304` (`fake.emit('update-downloaded', { version: '1.5.5', … })`). A probe test importing only `./win-security` resolved electron-log's file transport to `C:/Users/Tony/AppData/Roaming/asktoto/logs/main.log`; the same probe through `./dust-secret-store` and `./updater` resolved identically.

**Intended.** `src/main/logger.ts:14-20` already carries the correct guard: electron-log resolves its own path and, outside an Electron main process (`process.type !== 'browser'`), falls back to `NodeExternalApi`, whose log dir is `<appData>/<package.json name>/logs` (`node_modules/electron-log/src/node/NodeExternalApi.js:12-18`) — byte for byte the installed app's directory. So `logger.ts` overrides `log.transports.file.resolvePathFn` to `<tmpdir>/asktoto-nonapp-logs/main.log` whenever it is not the app, and pins `audit.log` the same way at `src/main/logger.ts:52-53`.

**Actual.** That guard is a **module-load side effect of `logger.ts`**, so it only exists in a process whose import graph actually reaches `logger.ts`. Two main-process modules bypassed the module that owns logging policy and grabbed the electron-log singleton directly:
- `src/main/updater.ts:4` — `import log from 'electron-log'`, then nine `log.info` / `log.warn` calls (`updater.ts:212, 219, 228, 255, 268, 274, 326`).
- `src/main/win-security.ts:22` — `import log from 'electron-log'`, used by `warnUntrusted` (`win-security.ts:196`).

Neither file imports `./logger`, and neither does anything else in `updater.test.ts`'s graph (`./cahe-edition` → `./dev-env`, `./win-security`). Result: every `updater.test.ts` run appended real lines into the real user's production log, and a test run mutated real user state on any developer's machine. The same shape explains the `[auth] session teardown failed: window already gone` line reported in the ticket.

**What changed.**
- `src/main/updater.ts:4-8` and `src/main/win-security.ts:22-23` now import the shared logger from the module that owns it — `import { mainLog as log } from './logger'` — with a comment naming the reason (the redirect is a load-time side effect, so reaching the singleton around `logger.ts` writes into the real user's log). No call sites changed; it is the same electron-log singleton, so transport level / 5 MB rotation / `mode: 0o600` are unchanged. No new file, no config, no dual path — `logger.ts`'s existing single guard now covers 100% of the surface because there is exactly one door to it.
- New `src/main/logger.single-owner.test.ts` locks both halves: a behavioural case that imports `./updater` **without** importing `./logger` and asserts the resolved `main.log` is `<tmpdir>/asktoto-nonapp-logs/main.log` and not under the installed-app log dir; and a structural case that walks every non-test `.ts` under `src/main` and asserts `logger.ts` is the only file matching `from 'electron-log'`, so a future module cannot silently reopen the hole.

**The other two log surfaces, checked as asked.**
- `audit.log` — already closed by `src/main/logger.ts:52-53` (`isAppMainProcess ? userData/logs/audit.log : <tmpdir>/asktoto-nonapp-logs/audit.log`), and the `audit` child logger is created inside `logger.ts` so it can never be reached around it. Verified live: the real `%APPDATA%/asktoto/logs/audit.log` (1.9 KB) contains **0** test markers (`MQA`, `asktoto-corrections-test`, `Temp`); its tail is genuine `local.runtime.start` / `brain.ingest` records.
- `crash-*.log` — written at `src/main/index.ts:1378` to `app.getPath('userData')`. `index.ts` is never imported by a test (its contract tests read it as source text), and every test that does load `electron` gets `__mocks__/electron.ts`, whose `getPath('userData')` returns `/tmp/asktoto-test-userdata`. Verified live: **no** `crash-*.log` exists in the real `%APPDATA%/asktoto/`. Nothing to close.

**End-to-end proof.** With the real `main.log` at 554 526 bytes, running `updater.test.ts`, `win-security.test.ts`, `dust-secret-store.test.ts` and `logger.profile-isolation.test.ts` left it at **554 526 bytes — byte for byte unchanged**, while `%TEMP%/asktoto-nonapp-logs/main.log` picked up the very lines that used to pollute it (`[updater] error Error: sha512 checksum mismatch`, `[updater] downloaded 1.5.5`).

### MQA-176 — ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP does not lift the overlay's capture exclusion in a packaged build

**Repro (as reported):** launch the shipped 1.5.4 Windows build with `ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP=1` in the environment; `GetWindowDisplayAffinity` on the overlay HWND still reads 17 (`WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE`). A cross-process `SetWindowDisplayAffinity(hwnd, WDA_NONE)` returns FALSE, so only this process can change it.

**Verdict: not a defect. This is the gate working as designed, and it predates the 1.5.4 release.**

**1. Why the env var did nothing in that build.** None of the three hypotheses hold — it is not a persisted setting winning, not an ordering problem, not a missing re-apply on recreate. `contentProtectionOn()` has short-circuited the hatch to unpackaged builds since commit `1c4421d` (2026-07-06). Verified directly against the 1.5.4 version-bump commit, `git show 52b03046:src/main/index.ts` lines 350-353:

```
function contentProtectionOn(): boolean {
  if (!app.isPackaged && process.env.ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP) return false
  return getSettings().contentProtection
}
```

`git log -S'!app.isPackaged && process.env.ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP' -- src/main/index.ts` returns exactly one commit (1c4421d, 2026-07-06, an ancestor of HEAD per `git merge-base --is-ancestor`), and the gate is still present at HEAD — so it was continuously in force across the whole 1.5.4 lineage. In a packaged process the expression is `false && …`, the raw setting is returned, and the window is constructed with `setContentProtection(true)`. Affinity 17 is the only possible outcome.

**Corroborating detail worth recording:** at that same 1.5.4 commit, `privateViewOn()` (index.ts:359-362) was `if (process.env.ASKTOTO_DISABLE_CP) return false` — **ungated**. So in the shipped build the planted env var did nothing to window affinity but *did* silently open the app's own capture side (getScreenshot pre/post checks, screen-preprocess describe) while Settings still read "on". That asymmetry is the real hole, it is MQA-148, and the sibling agent closed it this run with `src/main/dev-env.ts` (a single fail-closed `devEnv()` gate). Post-MQA-148 the observed behaviour is doubly intended.

**2. The supported path is correct and durable — full audit, intended vs actual.**

| Path | Intended | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Overlay at construction | decide at creation | `src/main/index.ts:1170` `win.setContentProtection(contentProtectionOn())` ✅ |
| Overlay rebuilt after crash / second-instance / boot retry | re-decide | `ensureWindow()` `src/main/index.ts:1342-1352` recreates via `createWindow()`, which re-reads live ✅ |
| Renderer crash (`render-process-gone`, index.ts:1236) | keep the exclusion | reloads the SAME BrowserWindow; affinity is a native window property, untouched by a renderer reload ✅ |
| User flips the toggle (bar eye button `App.tsx:2005-2006`, Settings → Privacy `Settings.tsx:5280-5282`) | reach every live window | both go through the one `patch({contentProtection})` → `IPC.settingsSet` → `src/main/index.ts:2279-2280` `win?.setContentProtection(...)` + `syncIntelContentProtection()` ✅ — there is no second write path |
| IT-managed config change | apply without restart | `IPC.settingsGet` drift check `src/main/index.ts:2062-2063` re-applies to both windows ✅ |
| Window created LATER (Intelligence dashboard) | created with current state | `src/main/intelligence.ts:91` at construction; `intelCpOn()` reads `getSettings()` live so every reopen (incl. after sign-out destroys it, MQA-169) re-decides ✅ |
| Remaining windows | none unprotected | `decoderWin` (index.ts:701) and `pdfWin` (index.ts:4439) are `show:false`, never composited; no `BrowserView`/`WebContentsView`/`openDevTools` anywhere; both visible windows deny `window.open` and `will-navigate`, so no child window can appear ✅ |
| Turning it OFF | user is reliably visible again | packaged `contentProtectionOn()` returns the raw setting, and `publicSettings()` (index.ts:1047) reports the **effective** value, so the UI cannot claim "on" while capture is off ✅ |

**3. The one real gap found — in the regression pin, not the product.** `auditWindows()` in `src/main/content-protection.contract.test.ts` accepted any `<var>.setContentProtection(` occurring **anywhere** in the module. Deleting the dashboard's construction-time call at `src/main/intelligence.ts:91` therefore still passed the audit, because `syncIntelContentProtection()` at `src/main/intelligence.ts:18` mentions the same call — a helper that only runs on the *next* settings save, by which time the dashboard has already been on screen and capturable. That is precisely the "opened later, came up unprotected" regression the audit exists to catch, so the pin had a hole on the exact half of the invariant this ticket is about.

**What changed:** test-only. `src/main/content-protection.contract.test.ts` — `auditWindows()` now searches `source.slice(match.index)` (the construction site forward) instead of the whole module, with a comment explaining why an earlier re-sync-helper mention must not count; plus a new negative control, `MQA-176 — the audit fires if the DASHBOARD stops applying it at construction`, which deletes that one line and asserts `['intelligence.ts: intelWin']` while the helper's mention deliberately survives. The strip uses a regex rather than a literal slice because `src/main/intelligence.ts` is CRLF in the tree while `src/main/index.ts` is LF. No product source was touched; the tightened audit still reports `violations: []` against the real tree.

> MQA-147 .. MQA-174 came from a 41-agent hardening audit (2026-08-19): 8 independent lenses over the
> IPC boundary, crypto/secrets, main-process lifecycle, renderer races, brain data integrity, LLM
> failover, performance and packaging, each finding then adversarially verified by a skeptic told to
> refute it by default. 28 of 32 candidates survived verification; 4 were refuted and are recorded as
> such rather than fixed.

### MQA-178 — Background screen pre-analysis never starts at boot

**Repro:** Enable Local AI + "Preload screen context (on-device)" (or run the Cahê pilot, which seeds both at `src/main/cahe-embedded-key.ts:52-55`). Quit Métis, relaunch, ask "what's on my screen". `IPC.screenContext` (`src/main/index.ts:3192-3196`) returns null on every probe for the whole session, so `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:920-940` falls through to `window.toto.capture()` + a full-image `mode:'vision'` cloud upload, and the audit log records zero `screen.preprocess.describe` lines.

**Intended:** `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:81-82` — "(Re)start or stop the engine to match current eligibility. **Call on startup** and after settings change."

**Actual:** `refreshScreenPreprocess()` (`src/main/index.ts:1609-1615` pre-fix) had three call sites — `revokePrivilegedSurface` (which only ever stops it), `IPC.settingsSet`, and `IPC.authSignIn`. The `app.whenReady()` body (`src/main/index.ts:4746`→`5254`) never called it, and neither sign-in nor a settings write happens on a normal relaunch. `started` stayed false (`screen-preprocess.ts:140`), so no watcher, no 6 s tick, `cache` null, `currentFreshContext()` null forever. The Cahê seed made it worse: it writes `backgroundScreenContext: true` through the store directly at boot, bypassing the IPC handler that would have armed the engine.

**What changed:**
- `src/main/index.ts` — added `runStep('refreshScreenPreprocess', refreshScreenPreprocess)` to the boot sequence, deliberately **after** `runStep('createWindow', createWindow)` (the eligibility read pulls in the local-model trust probe, which must not sit on first paint) and **before** `registerIpc`, so the renderer's first `getSettings()` already sees a reconciled readiness flag.
- `src/main/index.ts` — `void ensureLocalModel(LOCAL_MODELS[0].id)` now chains `.then(() => refreshScreenPreprocess()).catch(mainLog.warn)`. Without it a first-run user is still dead all session: the boot reconcile runs while the ~760 MB download is in flight, `localReady` is false, and nothing else notices when the weights land.
- `src/main/index.ts` — `refreshScreenPreprocess()` is now the ONE reconcile point (boot / settings write / sign-in / session clear / model download). Its duplicated `requireAuth()` gate was deleted; auth is now a dep of the engine's own eligibility, so the lifecycle and the flag Settings renders read one expression.
- `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts` — new `authorized: () => boolean` dep folded into `eligible()`, and `canRun()` exported as the single authority (see MQA-179).

### MQA-179 — macOS: the background screen reader runs while Settings says it cannot

**Repro:** macOS, Local AI not provisioned (`localReady` false), turn on "Preload screen context (on-device)". Settings renders "Enable Local AI (below) to use this" while `eligible()` is satisfied by OCR alone, `setInterval(onRefreshTick, 6000)` is armed and a real `getScreenshot('bg-screen')` runs every six seconds; the OCR text is then injected into the cloud answer request at `src/main/index.ts:3273-3286`.

**Intended:** one question, one answer. `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:148-149` — `backgroundScreenContext === true && (deps.localReady() || ocrAvailable())`; `src/shared/ipc.ts:1149-1151` declares the UI mirror of exactly that.

**Actual:** `src/main/index.ts:1079` computed a second, independent expression — `s.backgroundScreenContext && localReady` — with the OCR half missing. On darwin `src/main/index.ts:1602` wires `extractScreenText` unconditionally, so `ocrAvailable()` is true on every Mac and the two expressions disagreed on every Mac without a local model.

**What changed:**
- `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts` — new `canRun()` on the `ScreenPreprocess` interface: session + setting + an on-device reader (local model OR OCR) + a live foreground-window signal. `refresh()` drives the lifecycle from it.
- `src/main/index.ts:1079` — `backgroundScreenReady: screenPreprocess.canRun()`. The second expression is deleted, not shimmed.
- `src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:5236-5246` — copy fixed on BOTH sides, per the fixReview. The "on" branch no longer says "reads your screen **with the on-device model**" (false on a Mac where Vision OCR does the work) — now "reads your screen **on this device**". The "off" branch is now two honest cases: with `settings.localReady` true the reason is the missing OS window signal ("Métis can't tell when you switch windows, so screen asks capture live instead"), otherwise the original "Enable Local AI (below)".
- `src/shared/ipc.ts:1149` — the field doc now describes what the flag actually reports and how to pair it with `localReady`.

### MQA-180 — Retry / "Go deeper" re-asks with ZERO screen data while the UI keeps the "Viewed screen" badge

**Repro.** `backgroundScreenContext` on, a keyed cloud provider active. T=0: screen hotkey → the fast path hits, a grounded answer renders with "Viewed screen" and "Seen 1s ago". Then either flip Private View on (one gesture, deterministic — `currentFreshContext()` drops the cache at `screen-preprocess.ts:318`), or simply let the description expire (`CONTEXT_TTL_MS` = 12s) or change foreground window (`handleWindowChange` nulls the cache; focusing Métis to click the button is itself a foreground change). T=25s: click "Go deeper". The ask reaches the provider carrying only `req.prompt`, while the badge and the "Seen 25s ago" chip still assert the screen.

**Intended.** `state.ts:462-463` — "Replay the last request EXACTLY (same mode + screenshot + prompt) so retrying a vision answer re-sends the image instead of silently re-asking text-only". `index.ts:3269-3272` documents the missing-cache fall-through as best-effort for a *millisecond* race between the renderer's probe and askStart — not for an arbitrarily delayed replay.

**Actual (pre-fix).** On the fast path the renderer sends an INTENT flag only (`App.tsx:925-933`, `wantsScreenContext: true` — no image, no description). `state.ts:375` stores that request; `retry()` (:467) and `deeper()` (:471-474) replay it verbatim with no re-probe. Main clears `req.screenContext` unconditionally (`index.ts:3252`) and re-fills it only `if (ctx?.description)` (`index.ts:3276`) — there was no else branch, so a stale cache meant zero screen data reached `llm/shared.ts`. Meanwhile `state.ts:403` set `usedScreen` from the intent flag alone and nothing ever corrected it, so `Answer.tsx:140/160` rendered "Viewed screen" and `App.tsx:567/2884` kept the freshness chip counting from the ORIGINAL capture.

**What changed.** One truthful story: main is now the authority on whether an answer saw the screen, and the UI obeys it.
- `src/main/index.ts:3319-3327` — after the injection block, `const screenGrounded = req.mode === 'answer' && req.wantsScreenContext ? !!req.screenContext : undefined`. `undefined` for every other ask (a vision ask carries its own image), so main only speaks where it is the authority.
- `src/main/index.ts:3580` and `:3659` — both `IPC.streamMeta` announcements (the per-attempt one and the hedge winner's re-assert) now carry `usedScreen: screenGrounded`. `stream:meta` was already the per-request main→renderer channel the renderer merges into the live answer, so no new IPC channel was added.
- `src/shared/ipc.ts:681-686` — `StreamMetaSchema` gains optional `usedScreen`. Absent = no verdict; the existing provider/tier contract is unchanged.
- `src/renderer/src/state.ts:337-354` — `onMeta` applies the verdict: `usedScreen` follows main, and `screenMissed` records "asked for the screen, didn't get it". The badge (`Answer.tsx`) and the "Seen Ns ago" chip (gated by `showingScreenChip`, `App.tsx:567`) therefore clear themselves off one field.
- `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:61-66, 574-585` — the degrade is announced, not silent: `SCREEN_CONTEXT_LOST_NOTICE` ("Métis couldn't see your screen for this answer. Answering from context only — ask again to re-capture.") shows in the existing amber capture-notice banner whenever `screenMissed` is set, and clears only its own notice when a later answer is grounded again. This mirrors the live capture path's own contract (`App.tsx:960-963`) of degrading loudly rather than substituting silently.

The finder's first proposal — a hard `streamError` when `currentFreshContext()` is null — was rejected per the fixReview: main cannot distinguish a replay from a first ask, so it would also hard-fail the acknowledged millisecond race that today still answers.

### MQA-181 — When the foreground watcher dies, screen pre-analysis keeps serving the PREVIOUS app's description

**Repro:** Windows enterprise install where the watcher cannot run (AppLocker/WDAC Constrained Language Mode rejects the script's `Add-Type`, or EDR blocks the `-EncodedCommand` spawn), Local AI provisioned, `backgroundScreenContext` on. User is in Excel; the 6 s tick caches a description of Excel under `windowId: ''`. Alt-tab to Outlook, press the screen hotkey → the fast path serves the Excel description with no capture at all, badged "Viewed screen" / "Seen 3s ago", and the model answers about Excel.

**Intended:** `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:326-327` — "If focus has moved to a different window since the describe, the description is about the wrong screen — treat it as absent so the ask falls back to a live capture"; `:265` — "cache = null // the cached description belonged to the window we just left".

**Actual:** both guards are fed by the watcher, and neither degraded safely. `activeWindowId()` (`:151`) was null forever when the watcher never emitted, so `handleWindowChange`'s `cache = null` never fired and the read guard `if (wid && c.windowId && wid !== c.windowId)` short-circuited on `wid`. It was doubly dead: `onRefreshTick` passed `activeWindowId() ?? ''` (`:274`) and the commit guard at `:240` explicitly waved a null window through, so every timer-committed entry carried the falsy `windowId: ''`. After a MID-session death `currentWindowId` instead froze at the last observed id, so stale matched stale and the guard passed anyway. `start()` armed the 6 s interval regardless of whether the spawn worked, and `ScreenPreprocessDeps` had no channel to learn the signal was gone. On the watcher side, an ENOENT/EACCES spawn lands on the async `'error'` handler where node emits `'close'` and never `'exit'` — the only restart path hung off `'exit'`, so the watcher was permanently dead on the first attempt while still claiming to watch.

**What changed:**
- `src/main/foreground-watcher.ts` — `ForegroundWatcher` gains `healthy(): boolean`. The inert handle (linux, or a mac install without the bundled helper) returns false. A live watcher returns `!stopped && !gaveUp`.
- `src/main/foreground-watcher.ts` — one `failed(message)` path now owns the restart budget for all three death modes (sync spawn throw, async `'error'`, `'exit'`), guarded by a per-attempt `settled` flag so a failure never double-counts. Budget exhausted → `gaveUp = true` + `onError`. This is where the fixReview said the missing budget actually belongs; a bare `setTimeout` in the sync-throw catch would have bypassed `MAX_RESTARTS` and spun forever.
- `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts` — `windowSignalOk()` reads `watcher?.healthy()`. `start()` refuses to run (and latches `windowSignalDead`) when the producer is inert; `onRefreshTick` drops the cache and stops the engine when the signal dies mid-session; `currentFreshContext()` drops the cache and returns null whenever the signal is not healthy, then requires a known window id (`wid === null || wid !== c.windowId → null`).
- `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:240` — the commit guard is now `if (activeWindowId() !== forWindowId) return`; nothing is ever cached under a blank window id again.
- The user-visible state follows, as the fixReview required: `windowSignalDead` feeds `canRun()`, so `backgroundScreenReady` goes false and Settings says "Métis can't tell when you switch windows, so screen asks capture live instead" instead of silently claiming the feature is on.

### MQA-182 — "Retry" / "Go deeper" re-sends the stored screenshot to the cloud after Private View is turned on

**Repro.** Private View OFF (default), any keyed vision provider. Ctrl+Shift+S → screenshot captured, answer streams with the "Viewed screen" badge and the Retry / Go deeper buttons. Open Settings → Privacy → Private View ON (main now throws `PrivateViewBlockedError` from `getScreenshot()`), close Settings (the answer survives — no `ask.clear()` on that path), click "Go deeper". The renderer replays `{mode:'vision', image:<stored JPEG>, depth:'deeper'}` from `state.ts` `lastReqRef` and main ships the whole screenshot to the provider again.

**Intended.** `src/shared/ipc.ts:824-825` — "Private View: Métis itself won't look at (or send) YOUR screen while this is on"; `src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:5290` — "Métis won't look at or capture your screen while this is on." `getScreenshot()` already re-checks the switch AFTER its own async capture (`src/main/index.ts:1556`) precisely so a frame grabbed a moment before the toggle cannot still be sent.

**Actual (pre-fix).** `IPC.askStart` (`src/main/index.ts:3225`) never called `privateViewOn()` — the only call sites were `publicSettings` (:1049) and the two inside `getScreenshot` (:1524, :1556). `req.image` was forwarded verbatim to `llm/anthropic.ts:7-14` / `llm/openai.ts:12-18`. No `capture.blocked` audit line, no notice, and the buttons stayed live. A stored frame is still the screen, so a re-send after the toggle broke the literal promise.

**What changed.**
- `src/main/index.ts:3243-3247` — new guard at the trust boundary, immediately after `AskStartSchema.parse`: `if (req.image && privateViewOn()) { auditLog('capture.blocked', { reason: 'private_view', at: 'ask' }); send(IPC.streamError, PRIVATE_VIEW_BLOCKED_MESSAGE); return }`. Keyed on the payload, not on `mode === 'vision'` — the schema permits an image on a non-vision mode, so gating on mode would be narrower than the invariant.
- `src/main/index.ts:1509-1512` — the refusal copy is now the single `PRIVATE_VIEW_BLOCKED_MESSAGE` const that `PrivateViewBlockedError` also throws, so the live-capture path and the replay path speak with one wording (and both match the renderer's `/private view/i` copy paths).
- `src/renderer/src/state.ts:366-381` — a stream error that arrives with zero output now clears `usedScreen` alongside the stale text it already discarded. Without it the rejected replay still rendered the "Viewed screen" badge (and the Bar's "Seen Ns ago" chip it gates) over a request that sent nothing. A partial answer keeps its badge — it really did see the screen.

The renderer half proposed by the finder (clearing `lastReqRef` on a privateView false→true transition) was deliberately NOT applied: it would kill Retry for plain text asks too and leave a live-looking button that silently does nothing, which is the dead-button bug `App.tsx:2693-2696` exists to prevent.

### MQA-183 — The cached screen description is captured from the cursor's display but keyed by the foreground window

**Repro:** Dual monitor. Keyboard alt-tab from a window on monitor 2 to a window on monitor 1 — a keyboard alt-tab moves no cursor. `handleWindowChange` clears the cache, and 700 ms later `describeForWindow` captures whatever is under the pointer (monitor 2) and commits `{description:'<monitor 2>', windowId:<monitor 1 window>}`. Move the mouse to monitor 1 and ask within the 12 s TTL: both guards pass and main injects the other monitor's description. The identical ask with the feature off captures monitor 1.

**Intended:** the entry is documented and guarded as a description of the focused window (`src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:325-328`, the commit guard at `:238-241`, `CacheEntry` at `:98-103`).

**Actual:** the description was never bound to a display. `deps.getScreenshot('bg-screen')` (`:209`) took no display argument and `ScreenShot` (`:29-34`) carried no display id, while the only display selector in the pipeline is the cursor (`src/main/index.ts:1528`, `screen.getDisplayNearestPoint(screen.getCursorScreenPoint())`). `getScreenshot` even returned `displayMismatch` (`src/main/index.ts:1563`) — MQA-081's own wrong-monitor signal — and the cache discarded it, so a frame main had already flagged as the wrong monitor was cached as a screen description with no trace.

**What changed:**
- `src/main/index.ts` — `getScreenshot()` now returns `dispId` on BOTH paths (cache hit and fresh capture); `captureScreenshotOnce` already computed it, it just never travelled.
- `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts` — `ScreenShot` gains `dispId` + `displayMismatch`; `CacheEntry` gains `dispId`; new injected dep `currentDisplayId: () => number` (wired in index.ts from Electron's `screen`, keeping the engine Electron-free per its own header contract).
- `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:209` — a `displayMismatch`-flagged frame is dropped before hashing: the live capture path can tell the user it grabbed a different monitor, a background describe cannot.
- `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts:311-329` — `currentFreshContext()` returns null when `deps.currentDisplayId() !== c.dispId`, so the ask falls back to the live capture at `App.tsx:941`.
- The hash dedupe now also requires the same `dispId`, so an unchanged-looking frame from another monitor cannot refresh the wrong entry's freshness stamp.
- `src/main/index-audit-fixes.contract.test.ts:342` — MQA-081's contract pinned the two `getScreenshot` return literals verbatim; updated to the new shape (both `dispId` and `displayMismatch` must travel on both paths) with a comment recording why.

### MQA-184 — Settings → Shortcuts key recorder was a keyboard trap (WCAG 2.1.2)

**Repro (keyboard only):** Settings → Shortcuts → Tab to the "Capture screen" row → Enter. The row shows "Recording… press keys". Tab: nothing happens, no message, focus stays. Shift+Tab: instead of leaving, `capture: 'Shift+Tab'` is persisted and `globalShortcut.register('Shift+Tab')` claims reverse-tab navigation process-wide, for this run and every launch after. Esc (the only working exit) is named in no user-visible string, and taking it dropped focus to `<body>` AND closed the entire Settings panel.

**Intended vs actual:**
- Settings.tsx KeyRecorder `onKeyDown` ran `e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation()` on every key except Escape, so Tab/Shift+Tab could never move focus (trap). Shift+Tab additionally reached `keyEventToAccelerator`, which mapped `Tab` → `'Tab'` and produced `'Shift+Tab'` → `onChange` → `set()` (collision check only) → `patch()`.
- `src/shared/ipc.ts` accepts any string for `shortcuts`, and `registerShortcuts()` (src/main/index.ts) passed it straight to `globalShortcut.register(accel, fn)` with no validation of any kind.
- The Escape branch deliberately did not `stopPropagation`, so it bubbled to App.tsx's window-level Escape handler; by then the input had unmounted, so that handler's INPUT guard missed and it ran `setView('answer')`, closing all of Settings.

**What changed:**
1. `Settings.tsx` KeyRecorder `onKeyDown` now returns on `e.key === 'Tab'` **before** any preventDefault/stopPropagation — the browser moves focus natively and the resulting blur ends recording. (Per fixReview: a guard inside `keyEventToAccelerator` alone would NOT have lifted the trap, only silenced the key.)
2. The now-unreachable `else if (key === 'Tab') main = 'Tab'` mapping is deleted from `keyEventToAccelerator`.
3. Escape is now `stopPropagation`'d — a deliberate reversal of the old comment's rationale, because Esc is now the *documented* cancel and an exit that also throws away the user's place is not an exit. The comment says why.
4. The recording field renders a visible hint: "Press Esc to cancel · Tab to move on".
5. `triggerRef` + a `returnFocus` flag return focus to the row's trigger button whenever a keypress (cancel or commit) ends recording — never on blur, where the user already chose where focus went.
6. New `src/shared/accelerator.ts` `isSafeAccelerator()` validates accelerator *shape* (≥1 real modifier, main key not a modifier, no reserved navigation key) and `registerShortcuts()` (src/main/index.ts) refuses anything failing it, pushing it into `shortcutFailures` so the Settings banner offers a rebind. This covers an already-persisted or hand-edited `settings.json`, which the renderer-side fix cannot.
7. The failures banner no longer claims "Another app likely owns the key combo" as the single cause — that would be untrue for a binding Métis itself refused. It now names both causes.

### MQA-185 — the only path to the weights was the one request a corporate proxy could not carry

**Repro.** Machine where direct outbound 443 is blocked and all egress goes through a PAC-configured proxy — the exact network `src/main/net/install-proxy.ts:16-17` names as "the common corporate case and the real gap". Dust/OpenAI/Anthropic asks work (patched `fetch`), but Métis Local never provisions. Covered by a unit test that stubs `net.fetch` and asserts the weights land: pre-fix it returned false because the request never went through that transport.

**Intended vs actual.** `src/main/net/install-proxy.ts:31/46/55` install undici dispatchers, which rebind `fetch` only — never `node:https`. Every other outbound call in `src/main` is proxy-aware (`updater.ts:130` `net.fetch`, `license.ts`, `calendar.ts`, `dust-oauth.ts`, `cli-installer.ts` on the patched `fetch`). `local-model-download.ts:3` imported `get as httpsGet` from `node:https` and `openResponse` (:49) called it with no agent, so this one request honoured neither `HTTP(S)_PROXY` nor the OS/PAC proxy. Since `local-models.ts:11-13` records that the weights are no longer in the installer, this was the sole provisioning path — permanently dead on those networks, with one `auditLog('local.model.download_fail')` line as the only trace.

**What changed.** `local-model-download.ts` now imports `net` from `electron` and fetches with `net.fetch(spec.url, { signal })`. That resolves the proxy per request host, which also covers a PAC routing `huggingface.co` differently from the `https://dust.tt` probe `install-proxy.ts:41` uses — the reason the verifier rejected the "reuse the patched global fetch" and "build an https-proxy-agent" alternatives. Redirect following moves to `net.fetch` (`redirect: 'follow'` is the default), replacing the hand-rolled 5-hop loop. Every integrity invariant is untouched: the `content-length` pre-check still reads off the Response before a byte is written, and size → sha256 → `renameSync` ordering into `.partial` is unchanged. The idle-stall guard `res.setTimeout(IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, …)` had no Response-body equivalent, so it is rebuilt as one `AbortController` carrying both deadlines: a 60 s header deadline, then a rolling 120 s window every chunk re-arms. The body is drained with `res.body.getReader()` inside an async generator piped to the write stream — the same shape `cli-installer.ts:267` already uses — so backpressure is preserved.

### MQA-186 — the 763 MB first-run transfer was unconditional, invisible and undeclinable

**Repro.** Fresh 1.5.4 install on any machine. `src/main/index.ts:4816` fired `void ensureLocalModel(LOCAL_MODELS[0].id)` inside `app.whenReady()` with no guard, no `onProgress`, and no reference to `settings.localLlm.enabled` or `totalmem()`. The two pinned files are 558,772,480 + 204,987,232 = 763,759,712 bytes from `huggingface.co` (`local-models.ts:41-48`).

**Intended vs actual.** The module shipped a complete progress contract — `DownloadProgress` (`local-model-download.ts:35-41`), `ProgressListener` (:43), `ensureLocalModel(modelId, onProgress?)` (:138) emitting per chunk — and `isLocalModelMissing` (:211) documented as "used to decide whether to announce the download". A repo-wide grep found zero callers for either: nothing in the product ever mentioned the transfer. Meanwhile `local-models.ts:39` sets `minTotalRamGB: 8` and `assertRamOk` refuses every load below it, so a 4 GB machine paid for bytes `listModels()` then reported `insufficient-ram`.

**What changed.**
- `local-model-download.ts` exports `shouldFetchWeights(modelId, localAiEnabled)`: false when Local AI is off, false when `assertRamOk` throws. `index.ts:4816` is now wrapped in it (the MQA-178 anchor `ensureLocalModel(LOCAL_MODELS[0].id)` → `refreshScreenPreprocess()` is preserved).
- The gate is armed on the OFF→ON edge in the `IPC.setSettings` handler (`index.ts`, right after `refreshScreenPreprocess()`), because the boot call is the only other trigger. Without it, gating on `enabled` would have created a new permanent dead end.
- The unwired `ProgressListener`/`onProgress` parameter and the zero-caller `isLocalModelMissing` are deleted. In their place the module publishes `localModelDownloadState()` — `{ modelId, status: 'idle'|'downloading'|'failed', progress }` — which the existing `localModels:list` handler folds into the summary. No new IPC channel, so `scripts/check-offline-package.mjs`'s ban on runtime local-model mutation IPC and `ipc.local-models.test.ts`'s "only the read-only channel" assertion both still hold.
- Settings' Local AI card renders `Downloading… N%` with a progress bar off `downloadProgress` (see MQA-187/188).
- `docs/ENTERPRISE-DEPLOY-WINDOWS.md` gains a **Required egress** section naming `huggingface.co`, when it is contacted, what breaks if blocked, and how to deploy without it. Line 17 is untouched — it is about the ASR models, which genuinely are packaged.

### MQA-187 — a normal first-run download was rendered as a broken installation

**Repro.** (a) Healthy fresh install: for the whole 763 MB transfer, Settings → AI → Local AI showed a red destructive-bordered "Unavailable" card reading "The bundled model files are missing or incomplete. Reinstall Métis to restore them." Reachable during onboarding (App.tsx renders `<Settings>` inside the onboarding gate for the Step 6 fix-link), and obeying the instruction quits mid-download — `local-model-download.ts` rmSyncs the `.partial`, so the next launch restarts from zero. (b) Proxy blocks huggingface.co: `run()` burns 3 attempts per file, returns false, writes one audit line, and the red reinstall card is the terminal state for that session and every session after.

**Intended vs actual.** `electron-builder.yml:76-83` — "The Qwen WEIGHTS are deliberately **NOT packaged** … `local-model-download.ts` fetches them once on first run" — so a missing weight file means "not downloaded yet", never "damaged install". But the verdict came from file presence alone: `local-models.ts:153-161` set `unavailableReason: 'missing-files'` from a bare `statSync().size` check, and `Settings.tsx:1543/1589` rendered that as an install defect. No `downloading` branch existed anywhere, and no data existed to write one: `index.ts:4816` passed no `onProgress`, and `src/shared/ipc.ts:162` defined only `localModels:list`. `Settings.tsx:1505-1518` also fetched the list once with `[]` deps.

**What changed.** `LocalModelSummary` (`local-models.ts`) gains `downloadProgress: number` and its `unavailableReason` becomes `'insufficient-ram' | 'downloading' | 'download-failed' | 'not-downloaded' | null`, fed from `localModelDownloadState()` which `index.ts`'s `localModels:list` handler folds in. `Settings.tsx` renders each case distinctly: a downloading card is neutral-bordered with a spinner, a `Downloading N%` pill and a progress bar — not the destructive treatment — while `download-failed` says the fetch could not complete, names `huggingface.co` as what must be reachable, and says Métis retries on the next launch. The card re-polls every 1.5 s while any model reports `downloading`, so it reaches Ready on its own instead of freezing on its mount snapshot.

### MQA-188 — the in-app card said the opposite of what the product does

**Repro.** Open Settings → AI → Local AI on any 1.5.4 install, ready or not. The toggle description read: "The model is Included with Métis. There is no separate model download after installation." (`Settings.tsx:1531`), with "Included with Métis. Needs N GB RAM." at `:1570`.

**Intended vs actual.** `src/main/llm/local-models.ts:11-13` — "These weights are NO LONGER embedded in the installer … They are fetched once, on first run, by local-model-download.ts." `electron-builder.yml:76-83` copies only `resources/local-llm/LICENSE.QWEN3.5-APACHE-2.0.txt`, and `scripts/check-packaged-runtime.mjs:430` fails the build if a `.gguf` ever returns. The main process already tells the truth where it owns the message (`local-models.ts:199`: "is not downloaded yet. Métis fetches it automatically on first run; check the connection if this persists."). MQA-146 corrected the compliance one-pager but its regression test reads only `electron-builder.yml`, that doc and `local-models.ts` — never the renderer. Worse, `Settings.contract.test.ts:38` asserted `/Included with Métis/` under a describe block titled "Local AI is a bundled, read-only capability", so a green test held the false claim in place.

**What changed.** The toggle description now reads "Métis downloads the model (~730 MB) once, on first run — it is not part of the installer. Turning this off skips that download."
