The card subtitle becomes "Downloaded once on first run. Needs N GB RAM.", borrowing the voice `local-models.ts:199` already uses. The stale premise in `src/shared/ipc.ts` — the `localLlm.enabled` default-TRUE rationale claiming "the model + runtime ship inside every installer … so there is nothing to download", and the `LocalModelSummarySchema` doc calling it "the installer-owned model" — is corrected to name the runtime, which genuinely does ship. `packaged-model-claims.contract.test.ts` is extended with a second describe block that reads `Settings.tsx` and, while `weightsArePackaged` is false, forbids "Included with Métis" / "no separate model download" and requires "first run" — so the UI is now bound to the builder config exactly the way the compliance doc is, and packaging the weights again would demand the copy move with them.

### MQA-189 — calendarToday's Graph fetch had no timeout, so a stalled socket left "Loading agenda…" spinning for undici's 300 s default

**Repro.** Sign in (Graph token still cached, so `getGraphToken` returns without touching the network), then put the machine behind anything that completes the TLS handshake to `graph.microsoft.com` and then silently drops the socket — an enterprise proxy, a captive portal, a wifi roam or a resume-from-sleep mid-request. Open the tray → "Today's agenda". The panel renders `Spinner` + "Loading agenda…" (`src/renderer/src/components/AgendaView.tsx:113-118`) and stays there for five minutes, with no error, no cancel and no timeout; the Refresh button (`:100-108`) only re-enters the same unbounded call. Covered by tests: the mocked fetch resolves only when its `signal` aborts, which is precisely what a black-holed socket does.

**Intended vs actual.** `src/main/calendar.ts:1-8` promises `needsConsent` "instead of erroring", and `AgendaView.tsx:49-50` promises the view "degrades gracefully when … the calendar is unreachable" — and the code for that already existed: `calendar.ts:96` returns `{ ok:false, error:'Calendar unavailable — try again.' }`, which AgendaView's final branch (`:151-176`) renders with a working "Try again" button. That branch could never fire on a stall. `calendar.ts:85` called `fetch(url, { headers })` with no `signal`, and nothing above it bounded the call either: the IPC handler (`src/main/index.ts:2823-2826`), preload (`src/preload/index.ts:137`) and both renderers (`AgendaView.tsx:57-67`, `RecallView.tsx:356-366`) just await. `src/main/net/install-proxy.ts` sets a dispatcher but never `headersTimeout`/`bodyTimeout`, so undici 7.29.0's 300 s default applied (`node_modules/undici/lib/dispatcher/client.js:262`). Every other outbound call in main already bounds itself — `license.ts:78` `AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)`, `updater.ts:127-128`, `llm/local-runtime.ts:155`, `mcp/clickupOAuth.ts:90` — calendar.ts was the outlier.

The same unbounded shape existed on all four fetches in `src/main/graph-transcript.ts` (`:49/:62/:73/:93`), which run **sequentially** inside `fetchTeamsTranscriptForMeeting`. That chain is awaited by `backfillSpeakerNames` (`index.ts:2022`), reachable as a user-invoked Review action via `recall:backfillSpeakers` — so the worst case there was ~4 × 300 s ≈ 20 minutes of a held user action.

**What changed.**
- `src/main/calendar.ts`: new `GRAPH_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000` (the same bound `license.ts:25` uses for its own POST — not a new number) and `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(GRAPH_TIMEOUT_MS)` on the calendarView fetch. The abort rejects with a `TimeoutError` DOMException, which the existing `catch` converts to the already-written, already-rendered "Calendar unavailable — try again." — a real, actionable state with a retry, not a vaguer message. The signal also covers the `res.json()` body read, so a headers-then-stall server is bounded too.
- `src/main/graph-transcript.ts`: one `AbortSignal.timeout(CHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS)` created once in `fetchTeamsTranscriptForMeeting` and threaded through all four helpers, so the budget covers the whole chain rather than each hop (four per-hop bounds would still stack to 4×). `CHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000` matches `mcp/clickupOAuth.ts:58`'s `FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`. Overrunning it degrades to the same quiet `null` every other failure in that file already produces — speaker enrichment is best-effort and `named: 0` is a normal outcome.

**Tests.** `src/main/calendar.test.ts` — "MQA-189 aborts a black-holed Graph request and reports it as unavailable instead of spinning": stubs a fetch that only ever settles on abort, asserts the request carries an `AbortSignal`, that the bound is 10 s, and that the call resolves to the actionable error. `src/main/graph-transcript.test.ts` (new) — "MQA-189 bounds the whole four-call chain with one deadline and degrades to null when it fires": asserts all four fetches receive the *same* signal instance, that `AbortSignal.timeout` is called exactly once with 15 s, and that the aborted chain resolves to `null`.

### MQA-190 — one unbounded await sat in front of every user-visible surface

**Repro.** Machine configured with "Use an automatic configuration script" pointing at an internal PAC URL, used off the corporate network (home, hotel, guest SSID) where that host black-holes. A Finder/Explorer launch inherits no shell env (`install-proxy.ts:15`), so `detectProxyFromEnv` returns null and the `resolveProxy` branch is taken. For the whole PAC-resolution stall the boot callback is parked: `index.ts:4785` `await installProxyAwareFetch()` is the first await inside `app.whenReady()`, and `runStep('createTray')` / `registerShortcuts` / `createWindow` are at `:5237-5239`. Reproduced as a unit test with a `resolveProxy` stub that never settles — it hung the call for the full 30 s test timeout.

**Intended vs actual.** `install-proxy.ts:41-43` awaited `session.defaultSession.resolveProxy('https://dust.tt').catch(() => 'DIRECT')`. The `.catch()` and the outer `try/catch` handle a *rejection*; neither bounds a promise that simply stays pending. There was no `AbortSignal`, no `Promise.race`, and no test for the file. The codebase already knew the window existed — `index.ts:1108-1110` notes `second-instance` can call `ensureWindow()` while boot's own `runStep('createWindow')` is still queued behind its awaits; without a stalling await that window is milliseconds.

**What changed.** The probe races a 2 s deadline (`OS_PROXY_DEADLINE_MS`). On expiry, boot proceeds immediately on the direct keep-alive agent — but the resolver is deliberately NOT abandoned: `void resolving.then((answer) => installSystemProxy(answer, true))` upgrades the global dispatcher to a `ProxyAgent` in place when a slow PAC finally answers, logged and audited as `source: 'system-late'`. `installSystemProxy()` and `directAgent()` are extracted so the immediate and late paths cannot drift apart. The module doc records that "must never block startup" is a latency promise, not only an exception one. Two tests pin both halves: a never-settling resolver still lets `installProxyAwareFetch()` resolve (with a direct agent installed), and a resolver that answers `PROXY corp-proxy.internal:8080` after the deadline still ends with `http://corp-proxy.internal:8080` installed.

### MQA-191 — the product offered a remedy the build gate guarantees cannot work

**Repro.** Fresh enterprise install behind a proxy that blocks huggingface.co (or a laptop with no network on first launch). Boot fires `ensureLocalModel`; all 3 attempts per file fail; only `auditLog('local.model.download_fail')` is written. Settings → AI → Local AI shows a red "Unavailable" badge and "The bundled model files are missing or incomplete. Reinstall Métis to restore them." (`Settings.tsx:1543`, repeated at `:1589`). The user reinstalls from an installer containing zero `.gguf` files and lands in the identical state. `scripts/check-packaged-runtime.mjs:430-440` runs `requireExactInventory(resources/local-llm, ['LICENSE.QWEN3.5-APACHE-2.0.txt'])` and FAILS THE BUILD if a weight file ever reappears — so this dead end is enforced by CI, not merely likely.

**Intended vs actual.** Main already words it correctly where it owns the message (`local-models.ts:199`). MQA-146 found this drift class and closed it in `docs/compliance/data-flow-onepager.md` only; its test never touches the renderer, so the in-app copy was left behind. A second instance sat in main itself: `src/main/index.ts:3521` told the user on the screenshot path to "Restart Métis, or reinstall it if the bundled model is missing."

**What changed.** Both reinstall sentences are gone. `Settings.tsx` now renders, per state: `insufficient-ram` → the RAM floor; `download-failed` → "Could not download the on-device model. Métis retries on the next launch — check that huggingface.co is reachable from this network."; `not-downloaded` → "Not downloaded yet. Métis fetches the on-device model automatically on first run."; `downloading` → progress. The manifest-read failure branch now says "could not read the on-device model status. Restart Métis if this persists." `index.ts:3521` becomes "…Open Settings → AI → Local AI to see whether the on-device model is ready" — which now points at a card that can actually answer. `src/shared/ipc.ts` drops `'missing-files'` outright rather than aliasing it (no back-compat), and `ipc.local-models.test.ts` pins that it no longer parses. `packaged-model-claims.contract.test.ts` forbids any reinstall wording in the Local AI block while the weights are excluded.

**Deliberately not built:** a Retry button. `local-model-download.ts`'s `inFlight` coalescing would make one safe, but per fixReview the copy change alone closes the defect and boot already retries every launch — which the new copy states truthfully. Adding a retry IPC would have pushed against `check-offline-package.mjs`'s ban on runtime local-model mutation channels for no additional truth.

### MQA-192 — Transcript-save failure showed the raw Electron IPC/OS error and then falsely claimed it was still retrying, forever

**Repro.** End a meeting whose transcripts folder is held by OneDrive/AV (or whose session has dropped). The auto-save effect in `src/renderer/src/App.tsx` runs its backoff ladder (1+2+4+8+16s, 6 attempts) and every attempt rejects. Review settles on:

> Couldn't save the transcript: Error invoking remote method 'transcript:save': Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, open 'C:/Users/jdoe/OneDrive/Métis Meetings/2026-08-19_143000-acme.md.tmp'
> Retrying… attempt 5 / 5

and stays there for the rest of the session.

**Intended vs actual.**

1. *Raw error.* `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:659-660` (pre-fix) stored the unmodified `e.message`. `src/preload/index.ts:164-165` invokes `IPC.saveTranscript` bare and `src/main/index.ts:3979-3984` has no try/catch, so main's `throw new Error('Not signed in.')` (`index.ts:3982`), `SaveMeetingSchema.parse`, and `saveMeeting`'s raw fs throw all reject through Electron's `Error invoking remote method 'transcript:save': …` wrapper, printed verbatim at `Review.tsx:825`. The same file already strips exactly that wrapper for `capture:screen` at `App.tsx:984-989` under the comment "strip the plumbing before showing anything to the user" — the save path did not. A dropped session and a locked file were also indistinguishable at a glance, and neither named an action.
2. *Permanent false status.* `App.tsx:661-663` incremented `saveAttempts` only while `saveAttempts < MAX_SAVE_RETRIES` (=5, `App.tsx:474`), and `saveAttempts` is the effect's only re-trigger (dep list `App.tsx:679`). After the last failure nothing was ever scheduled again, but `Review.tsx:826` gated the status line on `saveAttempts > 0`, so the present-tense "Retrying… attempt 5 / 5" (`Review.tsx:828`) stayed up permanently while nothing retried. `manualSave`'s catch (`App.tsx:603-606`) set `saveError` without touching `saveAttempts`, so a failed manual retry left the false line up too.

**What changed.**

- `App.tsx`: new exported pure `saveFailureReason(err)` — strips the IPC wrapper via a new module-level `IPC_INVOKE_WRAPPER` const (the two screen-capture catches now reuse it instead of each carrying their own copy of the same regex), then maps `Not signed in.` / `ENOSPC` / `EPERM|EACCES` / `EBUSY` / `ENOENT` to a short line naming the one action that clears each, all ending at the Save chip. An undiagnosable cause keeps the OS's own words minus the plumbing — deliberately not flattened into a vaguer line. Routed into all three writers of the banner: `doSave`'s catch, `manualSave`'s catch, and `saveMeetingNow`'s definitive give-up (`App.tsx:1806`).
- `App.tsx`: new `saveGaveUp` state, set only in `doSave`'s catch on the rung where the ladder actually stops (`else` of `saveAttempts < MAX_SAVE_RETRIES`), cleared on every save success (auto + manual) and in `startListen`'s reset. Passed to Review (`saveGaveUp={pm ? false : saveGaveUp}`) and added to the Review element's memo dep list.
- `Review.tsx`: new exported pure `saveStatusLine(attempts, max, gaveUp)` — `null` before the first retry, `Retrying… attempt N / M` only while one is genuinely scheduled, and `Automatic retries have stopped. Press Save to try again.` once the ladder is spent. The banner now calls it instead of hardcoding the retry claim.

### MQA-193 — A per-window ASR decode exception painted the raw transformers.js error into the live-meeting banner and never cleared it

**Repro.** Long meeting on a memory-pressured machine. One 6s VAD window trips an onnxruntime-web WASM fault inside `asr()` (`src/renderer/src/lib/whisper.worker.ts:322`). The exception text — e.g. `Aborted(). Build with -sASSERTIONS for more info.` or `RuntimeError: memory access out of bounds` — is rendered verbatim in the red danger banner under the overlay (`App.tsx:3058-3062`, no dismiss control). The very next window transcribes normally and lines keep appearing, but the banner stays up for the rest of the meeting.

**Intended vs actual.**

1. *Raw error.* `whisper.worker.ts:259-262` states the rule for this exact surface: the raw transformers.js message "is meaningless to a user mid-meeting — surface a human line instead, and keep the raw detail in a log post for diagnostics". The load-failure branch (`whisper.worker.ts:263-269`) obeys it and `whisper.worker.test.ts:64` pins that wording. The decode branch at `whisper.worker.ts:325-328` did the opposite: `post({ type: 'error', message: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err), speaker })` — no log post, no humanization. `listen.ts:748-750` put it straight into live state because `armNetworkRetry` declines a post-ready failure by design (`listen.ts:832`). The two sibling engines handle the identical per-window failure with no user-facing banner at all (`listen.ts:638-645`, `676-683`), so Whisper's decode path was the only one painting engine internals into the live UI.
2. *Sticky.* Enumerating every `error:` write in `listen.ts` confirmed it is only cleared at `741` (OFFLINE_MSG/RECONNECTING_MSG), `982` (THEM_SILENT_MSG), `1063` (MIC_LOST_MSG), `1289` (start) and `1683` (stop). The `m.type === 'text'` handler never touched `error`, so a one-window failure outlived the recovery that happened milliseconds later.

**What changed.**

- `whisper.worker.ts`: the decode catch now mirrors the load branch — `post({type:'log', message: 'ASR window failed: …raw…'})` for diagnostics, then one fixed user line, `Part of the audio could not be transcribed. Transcription is continuing.` Still exactly one terminal reply per window, so the renderer queue cannot wedge.
- `listen.ts`: new exported pure `noteAfterDecodedWindow(current, decodeNote)` and a `decodeNoteRef`. The `error` handler records the exact note only when `readyRef.current` is true (a per-window decode failure — a genuine *load* failure stays sticky, because nothing recovers it on its own); the `text` handler retracts that exact string on the next window that decodes, and returns the previous state object untouched when there is nothing to clear.

### MQA-194 — "Meetings per week" bars read zero for every week on the far side of a DST change

**Repro:** In any DST-observing zone, open Brain and look at the "Meetings per week" histogram within ~11 weeks of a transition. Pinned as a test: TZ=America/New_York, now = Mon 2026-11-16 (US DST ended 2026-11-01), four meetings on 2026-09-15 / 10-06 / 10-20 / 11-03 — all inside the 12-week window. Only the post-transition one is drawn; the other three bars read 0 under correctly-labelled Monday headings.

**Intended vs actual:** `weekStart()` (BrainView.tsx:69-76) buckets each meeting under a *local* Monday midnight — it uses `setHours(0,0,0,0)` / `setDate()`, which preserve wall-clock fields. The 12 rendered columns were built with fixed arithmetic instead — `const w = now - (WEEKS_SHOWN - 1 - i) * WEEK_MS` (BrainView.tsx:198, `WEEK_MS = 7*24*60*60*1000` at :78) — and read back with `counts.get(w)` at :199. Consecutive local Monday midnights are 7d ± 1h apart across a transition, so every synthetic column key on the far side is an hour off the real bucket key and the lookup misses. The same skew was in the range guard at :194, and `max`/`maxIdx` (the highlighted "busiest week") were computed from the wrong counts. Going *into* spring-forward the skew runs the other way: keys land on Sunday 23:00, so `fmt(w)` (:210) labelled the wrong day as well.

**What changed:** `WeeklyBars`'s `useMemo` body is extracted to an exported pure `computeWeeklyBars(meetings, now)` (BrainView.tsx) so the bucketing is testable with an injected clock. The columns are now built by stepping a Date back seven **calendar** days at a time from `weekStart(now)` (`cursor.setDate(cursor.getDate() - 7)`), which keeps every column a real local Monday 00:00 in both directions. The skewed range guard is deleted rather than rebuilt — a bucket outside the 12 columns is simply never read — and the now-unused `WEEK_MS` constant is deleted with it.

### MQA-195 — Mars weekly draft dates every meeting by UTC calendar day, so evening meetings are reported on the wrong day

**Repro:** TZ=America/Los_Angeles, draft opened Fri 2026-08-14 19:00 PDT. A meeting held Wed 2026-08-12 18:15 PDT is saved as `date: 2026-08-13T01:15:00.000Z`; History labels it 2026-08-12 (`localDateKey`), the Mars draft rendered `- 2026-08-13: …` — Thursday, a day the user had no meetings. The header read `# Mars week draft: 2026-08-09 → 2026-08-15`, a window that begins a day late and ends tomorrow, and a Saturday-morning meeting (Sat 2026-08-08 09:00 PDT) fell out of the week entirely — including the deal it touched, so a won deal was reported as untouched this week.

**Intended vs actual:** RecallView.tsx:55-66 states the rule and implements `localDateKey` with `toLocaleDateString('en-CA')`; Review.tsx:41-50 repeats it; History keys the same instant through it. mars.ts:45 was `const isoDay = (t: number) => new Date(t).toISOString().slice(0, 10)` (UTC day), feeding the window bounds at :59-60, and four raw truncations of the meeting date did exactly what RecallView warns against — `x.date.slice(0, 10)` at :64 (window membership), :74 (first-seen per account), :83 (the row date rendered at :145) and `m.date.slice(0, 10)` at :98 (`touchedThisWeek`, which drives won/lost). `x.date` is the raw frontmatter value, written by transcripts.ts:769 as `date: ${new Date(started).toISOString()}` — a UTC instant.

**What changed:** `isoDay` is replaced by a `localDay(when: string | number)` helper using `toLocaleDateString('en-CA')`, and all five call sites (mars.ts:59, 60, 64, 74, 83, 98 in the old numbering) go through it, so the draft's dates are identical to the ones History shows. It carries the NaN guard its RecallView/Review siblings have — load-bearing at `touchedThisWeek`, whose deal meeting refs never pass the `Number.isFinite(parse(x.date))` filter, so an unparseable date would otherwise become the literal string "Invalid Date" in the `>=`/`<=` comparisons. It also returns a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` frontmatter date unchanged: ingest.ts documents bare `date:` frontmatter as "common", and parsing one would read it as UTC midnight and shift it a day west of UTC — inventing an offset that was never in the data. The `MarsWeek.weekStart`/`weekEnd` comments now say "local calendar day" instead of "ISO date".

### MQA-196 — Renderer-crash recovery leaves the overlay stuck at mini-pill width

**Repro:** Collapse the overlay to the control mini-pill (App.tsx → `IPC.windowMinimize` → `setMinimizedWidth(true)`: `isMinimized = true`, `currentWidth = PILL_WIDTH`, then narrowed to ~130px by the pill's own `[data-hug-width]` report through `IPC.windowResize`). Kill the renderer — the causes the handler itself names at src/main/index.ts:1241-1243, a GPU/compositor crash or OOM in the in-renderer ASR worker.

**Intended:** createWindow's crash/recovery guard states the hazard verbatim at src/main/index.ts:1113-1122 — a recovered window must start full-size because the mount effect's `setBounds({ width: currentWidth })` would otherwise squeeze the Bar to the pill width, "with resizable:false blocking any manual fix" — and resets both variables.

**Actual (before):** `render-process-gone` recovers by reloading the SAME window (src/main/index.ts:1263-1265), so createWindow never re-runs; its idempotence guard at index.ts:1112 returns the surviving window even via `ensureWindow()`. The handler's reset block cleared only the renderer-owned MEETING state from MQA-038 (`resetDustConversation`, `listeningActive`, `lastPlainAskAt`, `audioArmed`, `setTrayRecording(false)`, `setRecordingPowerSaveBlock(false)`) and left the geometry alone. `isMinimized` (index.ts:453) and `currentWidth` (index.ts:449) are assigned nowhere else except createWindow and `setMinimizedWidth`, whose only caller is a user gesture. The remounted App boots `minimized = false` (App.tsx:355, `useState`, never persisted), renders the full 880px Bar, and its mount effect fires `windowMode('bar')` → `setWindowMode()` → `setBounds({ width: currentWidth })` with the surviving ~130px pill width; every later `resizeTo` re-applies it, and `isMinimized` staying true also freezes `lastBarHeight` tracking. With `resizable: false` (index.ts:1147) the user cannot drag it back — the overlay stays a sliver until the app is restarted.

**Changed:** src/main/index.ts:1261-1262 — `isMinimized = false` and `currentWidth = BAR_WIDTH` added to the `render-process-gone` reset block, the same two lines createWindow's crash guard uses, applied on the reload path that never reaches it. Main's geometry state now matches the state the remounted renderer actually boots into.

### MQA-197 — Window height is never re-clamped when the overlay changes display

**Repro:** 4K external (workArea 2112px tall) plus a 1080p laptop (workArea 1032). Open the post-meeting Review on the external — Panel caps itself at `availHeight - 160` ≈ 1960 and the window grows to `resizeTo`'s ceiling, `workArea.height - 48` = 2064. Then either drag the overlay onto the laptop, or undock/unplug the external.

**Intended:** `resizeTo` documents the invariant at src/main/index.ts:1301-1303 ("Clamp + reposition against the display the OVERLAY is actually on"), and `registerScreenListeners` at index.ts:1744-1750 exists so a topology change cannot strand the window "off-screen with no fix but a restart".

**Actual (before):** the ceiling lived only inside `resizeTo`, whose two call sites are `setMinimizedWidth` and the renderer's content-height IPC — neither fires on a display change. Every setBounds that can change the window's display preserved the old height by spreading `...b`: `moveBy` (index.ts:1732, 1741) and `reanchor` (index.ts:1765) overrode x/y only, and `setWindowMode` (index.ts:1350) wrote `height: lastBarHeight` with no clamp at all. `reanchor` additionally early-returned whenever the window still overlapped its matched display's work area — which is the normal state after a shorter monitor takes over — so it skipped exactly this case. There is no `move`/`resize` listener on the overlay. Result: a 2064px window on a 1032px work area, covering the whole laptop screen and extending ~1000px below the bottom edge; `resizable: false` (index.ts:1147) leaves no manual fix, and the renderer will not re-push because its content height has not changed (state.ts dedups on `lastSentRef`).

**Changed:**
- src/main/index.ts:1671-1675 — new `clampHeight(height, areaHeight)`, the `Math.max(BAR_MIN_HEIGHT, Math.min(h, areaHeight - 48))` ceiling lifted out of `resizeTo` so there is exactly one definition of it. `resizeTo` (index.ts:1304) now calls it.
- src/main/index.ts:1704-1716 — new `refitToDisplay(next, fromDisplayId)`: re-applies the ceiling only when a move lands the window on a DIFFERENT display than it left, re-checking y with `clampAxisMargin` because the caller validated y against the old, taller height.
- src/main/index.ts:1725, 1732, 1741 — `moveBy` captures the pre-move display id and routes both of its setBounds calls (free-drag and the flung-off-screen fallback) through `refitToDisplay`. The renderer's pointer drag goes through `IPC.windowMoveBy` → `moveBy`, so this covers the real drag, not just the scroll hotkeys.
- src/main/index.ts:1757-1776 — `reanchor` computes the clamped height BEFORE the reachability early-return, applies it with the same 8px bottom slide `resizeTo` uses when the window is still visible, and includes it in the off-screen branch.
- src/main/index.ts:1346-1350 — `setWindowMode` clamps `lastBarHeight`, which is measured on whatever display the bar was on; the renderer sends `windowMode('bar')` on every mount, including the reload after a renderer crash.
- src/renderer/src/components/Panel.tsx — the panel's own cap now follows the move. `subscribeMaxHeight()` re-reads `panelMaxHeight()` on the viewport resize that main's new clamp produces, and `Panel` holds it in state. Without this the main-side clamp alone leaves the panel laid out ~1000px taller than the window it lives in, clipping at the frame with no scrollbar — a worse outcome than the original defect.

### MQA-198 — The answer surface's `76vh` cap is self-referential in a content-sized window

**Repro.** Ask anything that produces a long answer. The overlay ratchets open in seven successive native `setBounds` steps and parks at a 384px-tall window — about 275px of readable answer — and it is the *same* 384px on a 3840x2160 monitor as on a 1366x768 laptop. The window never uses the height main already provisions for it (`workArea.height - 48`, ~990px on a 1080p work area), and the reading area does not grow with the display. The sibling Panel surface (Review / History / Agenda) does grow correctly, which is the visible inconsistency.

**Intended vs actual.** The overlay window is *content-sized*: `useAutoResize` measures the content root (`src/renderer/src/state.ts:137`), quantizes the grow path onto a 24px grid (`state.ts:148`), pushes it over IPC (`state.ts:94`), and main's `resizeTo` sets the window bounds to it (`src/main/index.ts:1289-1311`, clamped only to `[BAR_MIN_HEIGHT, workArea.height - 48]`). So the window height *is* the renderer's viewport. `src/renderer/src/components/Bar.tsx:769` capped the answer body with `max-h-[76vh]`, and `vh` resolves against that same viewport — making the cap a function of its own output. `H = chrome + 0.76·H` has a fixed point at `H = chrome/0.24`; simulating the real loop (chrome 86px, 24px grow quantization, main's clamp) gives 384px after 7 grow steps for `availHeight` 728, 1400 and 2100 — identical on every display. The documented intent for the sibling surface is the opposite: `src/renderer/src/components/Panel.tsx:3-13` caps against the *screen* (`Math.max(460, availHeight - 160)`), "computed PER RENDER … so it tracks the current display", and `src/renderer/src/App.tsx:2891-2893` confirms answer/copilot are the in-bar surface while only settings/history/review/agenda use the panel. Nothing in the tree documented what `76vh` was meant to be relative to; `76vh` appeared exactly once in the whole repo and no test or QA check pinned it.

**What changed.** `Bar.tsx` gains an exported `answerBodyMaxHeight(availHeight = window.screen?.availHeight)` — `Math.max(320, Math.round(availHeight * 0.76) - 96)` — read per render (so it tracks the display the overlay was moved to, same as `panelMaxHeight`), and the `.aw-body` element now carries that pixel `maxHeight` instead of the `max-h-[76vh]` class. The 76% ratio the author chose is kept deliberately: it is now 76% *of the screen* rather than of itself, so the always-on-top overlay stays compact over the user's meeting instead of filling the display (the literal "cap at `availHeight - chrome`" proposal would have made it larger than Panel's own cap — a product change, not a bug fix). Because the cap no longer depends on the window height, the loop closes in a single grow step. Simulated over the real loop: window settles at 552px on a 728px work area (1 step), 1056px on 1400, 1608px on 2100 — versus 384px / 7 steps everywhere before. The arithmetic keeps it under main's ceiling on any real display (`0.76·avail ≤ avail - 48` for `avail > 200`; the 320px floor stays under it for `avail ≥ 464`).

### MQA-199 — A transient read error on settings.json makes the next settings write erase every persisted user override

**Repro (regression test, `src/main/settings-persistence.mqa.test.ts`).** Persist real overrides (`meetingsFolder`, `suggestEverySec`), then make `readFileSync` throw `EPERM` for `settings.json` only — at the syscall boundary, the way a Windows AV/EDR lock or a broken ACL on a redirected profile actually presents — and issue a one-key patch. Pre-fix, `setSettings({ autoSuggest: false })` returned ok and the persisted file afterwards contained only `autoSuggest`: `expected undefined to be 'D:/Meetings'`. A second test showed the read path memoising the resulting fresh-install-shaped profile under the live file's unchanged mtime, so it survived the lock: `expected 15 to be 42`.

**Intended.** Every other unreadable-settings branch in `readUserRaw` preserves the bytes first (`preserveUnreadableSettings`, store.ts:296-311: "Without this, the very next settings write would permanently overwrite the only copy of the user's settings"), and `setSettings`'s own comment (store.ts:660) says a failed write must not "wipe every setting + context doc". The project already codifies this exact error class elsewhere — recall.ts:729-737, "A THROWN read is a transient 'can't read it right now' ... NOT 'not a meeting file'".

**Actual (pre-fix).** `store.ts:338-345` caught *every* `readFileSync` error with a bare `catch {}` and returned `tryRecoveredSettings() ?? {}`, so EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY/EIO were indistinguishable from ENOENT. `setSettings` then built `{ ...readUserRaw(), ...allowed }` (store.ts:632) and `renameSync`'d it over settings.json (store.ts:638-639) — a full-file replacement containing one key, with no `.recovered` backup on that path because nothing was ever read to preserve. `getSettings` (store.ts:496) cached the same misread under the live file's mtime (store.ts:472-491).

**What changed.**
- `readUserRaw()` now returns `Record<string, unknown> | null` (store.ts:337-360). Only `code === 'ENOENT'` falls through to `tryRecoveredSettings() ?? {}` (store.ts:353); any other errno returns `null`. The `.recovered` fallback is deliberately *not* consulted on that branch — merging a stale recovery copy over a live-but-unreadable settings.json is the same loss with extra steps.
- `getSettings` (store.ts:509-514) keeps degrading to DEFAULT+managed so boot, the tray, shortcut registration and every IPC handler still work, and skips the memo when the read failed (store.ts:593-594) so the defaults snapshot cannot outlive the lock.
- `setSettings` (store.ts:652-660) fails closed on `null` with a message that names the real cause: "Couldn't save settings — Métis can't read its existing settings file at <path>, and saving now would erase everything already saved there. This is usually antivirus, a backup tool, or a synced profile folder holding the file open. Try again in a moment."

### MQA-200 — Clearing or resetting a keyboard shortcut is a silent no-op

**Repro (regression test, `src/main/settings-persistence.mqa.test.ts`).** `setSettings({ shortcuts: { capture: 'CommandOrControl+Shift+K' } })`, then `setSettings({ shortcuts: { capture: '' } })` — exactly what Settings' Clear button sends (Settings.tsx:7241 → `set(action, '')` → `patch({ shortcuts: { ...user, [action]: '' } })` at :7194). Pre-fix the returned and persisted value was still `CommandOrControl+Shift+K`.

**Intended.** `''` is the codebase's unbind sentinel: `resolveShortcut` is `user[action] ?? DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS[action] ?? ''` (index.ts:1772-1774 — `??`, so a stored `''` deliberately survives) and `registerShortcuts` does `if (!accel) continue` (index.ts:1791-1793). `DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS` ships `''` for five actions (whatnext, explain, summarize, spotlight-ref, settings). Downstream UI is already written for it — Bar.tsx:555 branches `props.captureAccel ? ... : ...`, and the tray's `fmtAccel` starts `!a ? '' : ...` (index.ts:1910).

**Actual (pre-fix).** `src/shared/ipc.ts:843` declared `shortcuts: z.record(z.string(), z.string().min(1)).default({})`, so any map containing an empty value failed validation as a whole. `store.ts`'s `validKeysOnly` (store.ts:103-110) drops a key when its `safeParse` fails, so the entire `shortcuts` patch was discarded and `{ ...readUserRaw(), ...allowed }` re-persisted the old binding — while main still audit-logged `settings.changed { keys: ['shortcuts'] }` (index.ts:2260). Same for Reset on the five actions whose shipped default is `''`.

**What changed.**
- `src/shared/ipc.ts:848` — `shortcuts: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).default({})`, with a comment recording why the value may be empty. The record *key* is unchanged.
- `src/renderer/src/components/Answer.tsx:358-363` — the empty-state hint used `accelLabel(captureAccel ?? 'CommandOrControl+Shift+S')` (`??`, not a truthiness check), so with Capture now genuinely clearable it would render "Ask a question or press  to capture your screen." It now branches like Bar.tsx:555 and points at the bar's camera button when nothing is bound.

### MQA-201 — the magic moment's first row was fabricated

**Repro.** Run onboarding on any Windows machine (x64 is the only Windows arch shipped) or the universal DMG on an Intel Mac. Scene 4 spins for 500 ms and then renders "Hardware acceleration ✓ detected" / "Apple Silicon acceleration ✓ detected" having consulted nothing.

**Intended vs actual.** `docs/ONBOARDING-EXPERIENCE.md` scene 4: "Rows animate from spinner → state, using REAL signals … (only show rows that are actually true — **never fake a check**.)" and "Every row must reflect reality — the honesty rule." The component's own header at `OnboardingExperience.tsx:8-10` names the three real signals — getPermissions / requestPermissionsUpfront / asrBundled — and silicon is conspicuously not among them. `:116` was an unconditional `set('silicon', 'ready', 'detected')` with the comment "this build only ships arm64; reaching here IS the check". That premise is false at the build level: `dist`/`release:build:mac` run `electron-builder --mac --universal` and verify with `check-packaged-runtime.mjs --macho-arches=arm64,x64`, and `dist:win` is `--win --x64`. The app's own runtime disagrees too — `local-runtime.ts:107-109` ships separate `win/vulkan` and `win/cpu` llama-server binaries and pins CPU after a Vulkan crash "common on older Intel iGPU drivers". The row fed `allReady` (`:219`), which gates the "Everything's ready. Nothing to configure." headline, so the fabricated row is what let that headline render.

**What changed.** The row is deleted from the base array and its `set()` call removed, taking the false comment with it. The four remaining rows are all genuinely derived: `asrBundled()`, the brain path, `micRowStatus(perms?.microphone)`, and the screen-permission check. `Cpu` is dropped from the lucide import and the `SetupRow.icon` type moves to `typeof Sparkles`. The staggered 500 ms opening beat is preserved, so the scene's rhythm is unchanged.

### MQA-202 — FieldHint promised a control that did not exist, and clicking it flipped the setting

**Repro:** Settings → Privacy → click the ⓘ glyph next to "Hide from screen capture" to read its description. No popover opens; the click is forwarded by the enclosing `<label htmlFor={toggleId}>` to the `role="switch"` button, flipping the privacy flag. With a screen reader, the same glyph is announced as a multi-sentence label followed by "button", but Enter and Space do nothing.

**Intended vs actual:** `src/renderer/src/components/ui.tsx:136` was `<span className="group focus-ring relative inline-flex" tabIndex={0} role="button" aria-label={text}>` with no `onClick`/`onKeyDown`/`onKeyUp` anywhere in the component (ui.tsx:134-143). A `<span>` has no native activation behaviour, so the declared role was a promise the element could not keep; and because a span is not *interactive content*, Blink's label activation forwarded clicks on it to the labelled control (ToggleRow, Settings.tsx ~601/612-616/621). ToggleRow renders `desc` ONLY inside FieldHint, so the description was unreachable any other way.

**What changed:** FieldHint now renders the trigger as a real `<button type="button" aria-label={text}>` — the exact shape the component's own docstring cites as its reference (Bar.tsx IconTool, Bar.tsx:256-277). This fixes both halves with one change: native Enter/Space activation makes the announced role honest, and a `<button>` IS interactive content, so the label stops forwarding the click — no `preventDefault` workaround needed. The tooltip reveal moved from `group-focus:` to `peer-focus-visible:` (the button carries `peer`), matching Bar.tsx:314, since focus now sits on the inner button.

### MQA-203 — a multi-day reset was phrased as a bare clock time

**Repro:** Claude Code CLI connected; the account hits its WEEKLY limit Monday morning. The CLI returns "Claude AI usage limit reached|<epoch>" ~6.8 days out (or the prose "resets in 164h27m24s"); `classifyExhaustion` → `recordExhausted` keeps it (provider-health clamps only at 8 days). Settings → Backups & limits showed "Claude Code — usage limit reached — resets ~9:14 AM" and the failed ask said "…hit its usage limit (resets 9:14 AM)". The user retries at 9:14 AM, hits the same wall, and repeats every morning for a week.

**Intended vs actual:** `providerLimitLabel` (src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx:1407) and the failed-ask message (src/main/index.ts:3834) both rendered `toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit' })` — time of day only, no day, no date — while the underlying value is documented and tested to reach 8 days (provider-health.ts:42/130, exhaustion.ts:124-126/133/139). The paired contract test (exhaustion-routing.contract.test.ts:75) pinned the literal `toLocaleTimeString`, locking the defect in.

**What changed:** new `src/shared/reset-time.ts` `formatResetPhrase(until, now)` — the one phrase both surfaces use:
- reset is today → `resets ~3:40 PM` (a bare clock time is unambiguous here, so it is kept)
- tomorrow → `resets tomorrow ~9:14 AM` (covers exhaustion.ts's 24h weekly default, which used to render as the exact clock time it already was)
- beyond → `resets in 7 days — Mon, Aug 24` (distance first; a weekday qualifier alone collides at the 7-8 day end of the supported range, which is the ambiguity the change exists to remove)
Calendar-day arithmetic is midnight-anchored so a DST shift cannot shave a day. Both call sites now delegate, and the exhaustion-routing contract test was relaxed to pin the day-aware phrasing (and its header now lists MQA-203).

### MQA-204 — The legacy BidStack→mcpConnections migration re-inserts a user value after locked keys are stripped

**Repro (regression test, `src/main/settings-persistence.mqa.test.ts`).** Write `managed-config.json` with a `plane` connection plus `locked: ["mcpConnections"]`, and a `settings.json` carrying only the pre-v1.5.4 `bidstackEndpointUrl` / `bidstackConnected` fields. Pre-fix, `getSettings().mcpConnections` was the synthesized BidStack entry pointing at `https://bidstack-old.internal/mcp`, not the org's pinned Plane endpoint.

**Intended.** store.ts's own comment above the strip: "Locked keys are authoritative on READ too, not just on write: a value persisted before a lock (or a hand-edited settings.json) must not override the managed/default value." `mcpConnections` is main-owned enough that the settings:set handler unconditionally strips it from every renderer patch (index.ts:2203-2205).

**Actual (pre-fix).** `migrateLegacyBidstackConnection(raw)` ran at store.ts:537, *after* the locked-key strip at store.ts:525-526. Its only guard is `if ('mcpConnections' in raw) return` (store.ts:434) — and for the dominant case (a pre-v1.5.4 profile) that key was never persisted at all, so the strip had nothing to delete and the guard could never fire. The final merge `SettingsSchema.safeParse({ ...base, ...raw })` (store.ts:543) then let the synthesized user-layer array beat the managed value on every read. Hardening the strip alone could not fix it; the migration had to insert first.

**What changed.** `src/main/store.ts` — `migrateLegacyBidstackConnection(raw)` now runs at store.ts:550, immediately *before* the locked-key strip at store.ts:552-556, so `delete raw['mcpConnections']` removes the synthesized value along with any persisted one and `base`'s managed array wins. The strip's comment records the new invariant ("Runs AFTER every migration above so a migration's synthesized value is stripped too"). Unlocked behavior is unchanged — the strip is a no-op for that key when nothing is locked, and the `'mcpConnections' in raw` guard still correctly no-ops for a modern profile because the persisted key has not been stripped yet at that point. A second test pins that unchanged behavior.

> MQA-147 .. MQA-174 came from a 41-agent hardening audit (2026-08-19): 8 independent lenses over the
> IPC boundary, crypto/secrets, main-process lifecycle, renderer races, brain data integrity, LLM
> failover, performance and packaging, each finding then adversarially verified by a skeptic told to
> refute it by default. 28 of 32 candidates survived verification; 4 were refuted and are recorded as
> such rather than fixed.

### MQA-205 — the darwin-x64 FFmpeg sidecar had no provisioning path at all

**Repro (before the fix).** On any machine that does not already hold the untracked binary, `node scripts/check-ffmpeg-sidecar.mjs mac x64` — the SECOND command of `predist` (package.json) — died with `Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat 'resources/ffmpeg/darwin-x64/ffmpeg'`. Nothing could supply that file: `.github/workflows/build.yml` cached only `resources/ffmpeg/darwin-arm64` and downloaded only `--pattern 'ffmpeg-darwin-arm64'`, `release.yml` repeated the same arm64-only block, and the one documented seed (`docs/ENTERPRISE_RELEASE.md`, "ffmpeg Sidecar Provisioning") created the `ffmpeg-sidecar-v1` release with two assets — arm64 and win32 — so the release could not contain a mac x64 asset either.

**Intended behaviour, quoted from the repo itself.** `predist` runs `check-ffmpeg-sidecar.mjs mac arm64 && … mac x64`; `dist` packages `--universal` with `ASKTOTO_MAC_ARCHES=arm64,x64`; `scripts/check-packaged-runtime.mjs mac --arches=arm64,x64` hashes both `darwin-<arch>/ffmpeg` files back out of the finished `.app`; `scripts/after-pack.mjs` throws `Missing reviewed FFmpeg sidecar for darwin-x64` inside electron-builder. The x64 requirement entered with cc9faf5 ("feat(mac): build a universal (Intel + Apple Silicon) package"), which touched no `.github/` and no `docs/` file — so the requirement shipped without its supply.

**Fix.** The arm64 provisioning block is mirrored for darwin-x64 in `build-macos` and `release-macos`: its own `actions/cache` entry (`id: ffmpeg-cache-x64`, key `ffmpeg-sidecar-v1-darwin-x64-${{ hashFiles('resources/ffmpeg/manifest.json') }}`) so an arm64 cache hit cannot skip the x64 download, `gh release download … --pattern 'ffmpeg-darwin-x64'`, `mv` + `chmod +x`, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine`, then a hard gate that names the cross-build prerequisites (nasm + Rosetta 2), prints the full three-asset seed, and prints the single-asset `gh release upload … /tmp/ffmpeg-darwin-x64 --clobber` for a release that already exists. The seed command in all four workflow gates and in `docs/ENTERPRISE_RELEASE.md` now stages and uploads all three binaries the manifest pins. Writing the x64 quarantine strip exposed that `release.yml`'s arm64 step never had one — a quarantined download would have been killed by Gatekeeper when the licence banner is read — so that line was added there too, and the two mac gates were renamed `… (darwin-arm64)` / `… (darwin-x64)` so a failing job log names the arch.

**What a maintainer must still do (impossible from Windows).** Build the binary on a Mac — `./scripts/build-ffmpeg-sidecar-mac.sh x64`, which needs nasm and Rosetta 2 — and upload it to `ffmpeg-sidecar-v1` as `ffmpeg-darwin-x64`. Until that asset exists the mac jobs still fail, deliberately: the gate was not weakened, only made self-explanatory.

**Regression test.** `scripts/ffmpeg-provisioning.contract.test.ts` derives the arch list from `package.json`'s own `check-ffmpeg-sidecar.mjs mac <arch>` calls, so adding a third arch to `predist` fails the file until CI can provision it, and asserts per arch: a dedicated cache entry with a unique id and key, a download of the matching asset gated on THAT id, `mv`/`chmod`/`xattr`, and a hard gate ordered before `npm run dist` / `npm run release:build:mac`. It also asserts every printed seed command (both workflows, plus the ENTERPRISE_RELEASE.md block) creates one asset per binary in `resources/ffmpeg/manifest.json`.

### MQA-206 — a missing sidecar reported a raw ENOENT instead of where the file comes from

**Repro (before the fix).** `scripts/check-ffmpeg-sidecar.mjs:18` did `const stat = statSync(file)` with no existence guard, so on a fresh clone or a cold runner the very first command of `npm run dist` aborted with `Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat 'resources/ffmpeg/darwin-arm64/ffmpeg'` and a Node stack. The reviewed sidecars are untracked by design (`.gitignore` keeps only `manifest.json` and the licence), so absence is the NORMAL first state — and nothing in that stack trace says the file comes from the `ffmpeg-sidecar-v1` release, or that `docs/ENTERPRISE_RELEASE.md` explains how it is seeded. `.github/workflows/build.yml`'s own comment already recorded the problem — "Without this, predist's check-ffmpeg-sidecar.mjs throws a raw ENOENT before the build even starts" — but only the runner had a gate that said what to do; a human at a Mac had nothing.

**Fix.** An `existsSync` guard before the `statSync` (the shape `scripts/check-mac-helper.mjs` already uses) that names, for the requested platform/arch: the missing path, the fact that these binaries are untracked and come from this repo's `ffmpeg-sidecar-v1` release, the exact `gh release download ffmpeg-sidecar-v1 --pattern '<asset>' --dir resources/ffmpeg --clobber` plus the `mv`/`chmod +x` that puts it in place, and `docs/ENTERPRISE_RELEASE.md` -> "ffmpeg Sidecar Provisioning" for the case where the release has no such asset yet. The asset name is derived per target (`ffmpeg-darwin-arm64`, `ffmpeg-darwin-x64`, `ffmpeg-win32-x64.exe`), and the macOS branch adds `scripts/build-ffmpeg-sidecar-mac.sh <arch>` / `docs/MAC_SIDECAR_REBUILD.md` with the warning that a rebuild also means re-reviewing the manifest sha256. Paths in the remedy are rendered with posix separators because it is a bash command line.

**What deliberately did NOT change.** A PRESENT binary is verified exactly as strictly as before: the same sha256 comparison against `resources/ffmpeg/manifest.json`, the same Mach-O non-system-dylib gate, the same executable-bit and licence-banner checks. The guard only replaces the failure mode for a file that is not there; it never lets a build proceed without a reviewed binary.

**Regression test.** Two cases in `scripts/check-ffmpeg-sidecar.test.ts` seed a manifest entry with no file on disk and assert the message names the path, the release, the per-arch asset, `gh release download` and the seed doc — and that the string `ENOENT` is absent, so the raw failure cannot creep back. Both run on Windows and Linux CI.

### MQA-208 — release:mas was the one mac chain that never staged Electron

**Repro.** `npm run release:mas` on a Mac with a cold Electron cache. Every other mac chain calls `scripts/provision-electron-dist.mjs` and passes `-c.electronDist=resources/electron-dist` (package.json: `dist` via `predist`, `dist:local`, `release:build:mac`); release:mas did neither, so electron-builder used its own bundled @electron/get 3.1.0. The failure lands only after the whole expensive provisioning phase — Swift mac-helper compile, `fetch-llama-server`, `fetch-local-model`, `fetch-speaker-model`, `fetch-models`, `build:intelligence`, the bytecode build — because electron-builder is the last step in the chain.

**Intended behaviour (quoted).** `scripts/provision-electron-dist.mjs:6-14` — electron-builder 26.15.3's bundled @electron/get "fails for any mac arch it has to fetch fresh: it reports `No checksum found in checksum file for /"electron-v<version>-darwin-x64.zip/"` … It is a defect in that dependency, not in this project's configuration." The whole script exists so no mac chain has to rely on that downloader.

**Actual behaviour.** The only remaining escape hatch was the pin at electron-builder.yml:37-39, which lists exactly two archives (`electron-v39.8.10-darwin-arm64.zip`, `electron-v39.8.10-win32-x64.zip`) — and the Mac App Store target uses neither. app-builder-lib's `macPackager.getPlatformConfig` sets `platformName = "mas"` for the mas target, and `ElectronFramework` resolves the archive as `electron-v${version}-${platformName}-${arch}.zip`, i.e. `electron-v39.8.10-mas-arm64.zip`. @electron/get synthesises a SHASUMS file from only the pinned keys and never fetches the real one, so that name misses and the build stops.

**Fix.** `provision-electron-dist.mjs` gained a `--platform=darwin|mas` flag (default darwin, unknown values rejected with exit 1 *before* any download, so an unrecognised name cannot surface as a confusing SHASUMS miss mid-build). `release:mas` now runs `node scripts/provision-electron-dist.mjs --platform=mas arm64` in the same slot the sibling chains use — right after `check-sherpa-platform.mjs mac arm64` — and its electron-builder invocation carries `-c.electronDist=resources/electron-dist`. Verification is unchanged and still explicit: the mas zip is fetched from Electron's own release and refused unless its sha256 matches the published SHASUMS256.txt entry.

**Why the platform is an explicit flag rather than inferred.** Staging the darwin zip for a mas build would not fail loudly. `ElectronFramework.selectElectron` only extracts directly when the directory contains the exact `defaultZipName`; otherwise it falls through to the "custom already-unpacked Electron distribution" branch, does `emptyDir` + `copyDir`, and produces a broken .app with no error. Passing `-c.electronDist` without teaching the script about `mas` would therefore have been worse than the original bug.

**Not verified on a Mac.** `electron-v39.8.10-mas-arm64.zip` is confirmed to exist upstream from `node_modules/electron/checksums.json` (asserted by the regression test, mirroring how release-gates.test.ts already reads that file), and the archive name is confirmed against app-builder-lib's own resolution code. The end-to-end mas build itself cannot be run from Windows.

### MQA-209 — arming the background screen reader at boot can raise the macOS Screen Recording prompt unattended

**Repro (regression test, `src/main/screen-preprocess.test.ts`, "MQA-209 — darwin without the Screen Recording grant: nothing starts and nothing captures").** Mac profile, signed in, `backgroundScreenContext: true` (opt-in but sticky, so it survives from an earlier session), Screen Recording still `not-determined`. Pre-fix `canRun()` was true, `refresh()` armed the engine, and the describe path called `getScreenshot('bg-screen')` — the harness counts that capture and it was 1 where it must be 0. On a real Mac that capture IS the permission request, so the system dialog appears roughly 6 s after launch with nothing on screen that asked for it. A second test pins the other half: with the grant in place the engine still arms at boot and caches a description, so MQA-178 is not reintroduced.

**Intended vs actual.** The rule is stated 21 lines below the step that broke it, at `src/main/index.ts` (boot sequence): "Deliberately NOT run at boot on macOS: there the same call raises the TCC prompt, which belongs in onboarding (permissionsRequestUpfront) where it is explained, not as an unattended pop-up seconds after launch" — enforced for `probeScreenCapture` by `if (process.platform === 'win32')`. `runStep('refreshScreenPreprocess', refreshScreenPreprocess)` (index.ts:5337), added this session for MQA-178, carried no such gate, and the engine's own eligibility (`screen-preprocess.ts` `eligible()`) never mentioned capture permission at all. `captureScreenshotOnce` (index.ts:1454-1458) deliberately lets `not-determined` fall through to `desktopCapturer` *because* that is what registers the app with TCC. On darwin the OCR dep is wired by platform rather than by helper presence (`extractScreenText: process.platform === 'darwin' ? … : undefined`), so the loop was eligible on a Mac with Local AI switched off entirely.

**What changed.** `src/main/screen-preprocess.ts` gains one optional dep, `screenCaptureGranted?: () => boolean` (:100), folded into eligibility through `captureAllowed()` (:194) at `eligible()` (:196-200) — placed in eligibility rather than in the capture so `canRun()`, which `publicSettings().backgroundScreenReady` reports to Settings, stays the single truth (MQA-179). `src/main/index.ts:1634` wires it darwin-only: `process.platform === 'darwin' ? () => systemPreferences.getMediaAccessStatus('screen') === 'granted' : undefined` — the same preflight read the capture path already performs at index.ts:1456, which reports status and never prompts. Off darwin the dep is undefined and eligibility is byte-identical to before. `IPC.permissionsRequestUpfront` (index.ts:2228) now reconciles after asking for the grant (macOS usually defers a fresh grant to the next launch, where the boot reconcile catches it; this covers the case where the status already flipped). Finally, because the gate adds a SECOND way to be off on a Mac, the Settings toggle's "not running" copy no longer asserts the window-signal reason on darwin (`src/renderer/src/components/Settings.tsx`, the `isWindows` branch keeps the Windows string byte-identical) — same rule as MQA-179: never describe a state the engine is not in.

### MQA-210 — the boot sentinel looked for crash dumps in the Windows-only Crashpad directory

**Repro (regression test, `src/main/boot-sentinel.crash-dumps.test.ts`).** Seed `<userData>/Crashpad/pending/mac-early-death.dmp` — Crashpad's macOS layout — then call `beginBootWatch(userData, '1.6.0')` twice so the second call reports the first as an early death. Pre-fix `death.crashDump` was `null` and `describeEarlyDeath(death)` ended "newest Crashpad minidump: none". Same for `completed/`. Five of the file's seven cases failed that way; the two that passed are the Windows `reports/` layout and the no-database case, both of which had to keep passing.

**Intended vs actual.** `src/main/boot-sentinel.ts:40` was `const dir = join(userData, 'Crashpad', 'reports')` with no platform branch, and its docstring asserted that layout as *the* location ("Newest `.dmp` under `<userData>/Crashpad/reports`"). `reports/` is `CrashReportDatabaseWin`'s shape; the macOS/Linux database uses `new/`, `pending/` and `completed/`, so `readdirSync` threw ENOENT and the catch returned `null` on every Mac. The dumps really are produced there — `crashReporter.start({ uploadToServer: false })` (index.ts:407) runs at module scope on all platforms — and the scan is reached unconditionally on darwin via `beginBootWatch(app.getPath('userData'), app.getVersion())` (index.ts:4952). The module was written entirely from Windows evidence (its own header cites six 1.5.4 Windows launches), and the existing MQA-175 test cannot catch the difference because it creates `Crashpad/reports` itself before asserting.

**What changed.** `newestCrashDump()` (`src/main/boot-sentinel.ts:48-83`) now scans the Crashpad database root at `<userData>/Crashpad` plus one level of subdirectories for `*.dmp`, newest by mtime, instead of naming a single platform's directory. A directory this platform does not use is skipped exactly as before (`listOrNull` returns null), an entry Crashpad's own cleanup deletes mid-scan is skipped (`statOrNull`), and non-minidump bookkeeping (`settings.dat`, `attachments/`, `*.meta`) is ignored. Windows behaviour is unchanged, macOS/Linux start working, and the return contract is unchanged — the bare file name, or null — so `describeEarlyDeath` and the MQA-175 assertion need no edit. Still `node:fs`/`node:path` only: this module must never be the reason a boot fails.

### MQA-207 — the mac release path has no launch gate, and the universal DMG's second slice is the part that needs one

**Repro.** On a Mac, run `npm run dist`. The chain (package.json:46) ends `… electron-builder --mac --universal … && node scripts/check-packaged-runtime.mjs mac --arches=arm64,x64 --macho-arches=arm64,x64 --post-sign && node scripts/check-update-metadata.mjs release/latest-mac.yml`. Every one of those gates inspects files; none starts the app. `release:build:mac` (package.json:54) ends at `verify-signing.mjs --require-notarized`, same story. Both Windows chains do start it: package.json:49 and :55 end with `node scripts/check-packaged-launch.mjs release/win-unpacked/Metis.exe`.

**Intended behaviour (quoted).** `scripts/check-packaged-launch.mjs:5-9` — "Every other release gate inspects files … None of them start the app, so a build whose main process dies on the first require() passes all of them. That is exactly how 1.5.3 shipped to Windows dead with `cachedDataRejected` … and how 1.2.0 shipped before it." Its own platform guard already said macOS needs an equivalent "before the mac release path can claim this coverage".

**Actual behaviour, and why the mac case is worse than a missing duplicate.** `electron.vite.config.ts:13` sets `bytecode: true`, and electron-vite compiles bytecode exactly once by spawning the build host's own Electron (node_modules/electron-vite/dist/chunks/lib-q6ns0vZr.js, `compileToBytecode` → `spawn(getElectronPath(), [bytecodePath])`); its runtime loader hard-throws `Invalid or incompatible cached data (cachedDataRejected)` on mismatch. electron-builder then packages that single `out/main/index.jsc` into both slices of `--universal`. So the slice that is not the build host's architecture executes bytecode it did not produce — the exact DOA class this gate exists to catch — and nothing in the mac chain exercises it. The Intel slice is a live target, not hypothetical (electron-builder.yml:116-119, scripts/build-mac-helper.mjs:22-23 "an arm64-only helper is simply not executable on an Intel Mac", MQA-201's workflow cell).

**Why it is OPEN rather than fixed.** Two mechanisms the Win32 gate depends on have no clean darwin counterpart that can be written correctly without a Mac to test on:
1. *Window assertion.* The Win32 path uses PowerShell + UI Automation. The macOS equivalents (`osascript` / System Events) require a TCC Automation grant; from an unattended shell the call errors (-1743) rather than answering, so the gate would fail builds for a permissions reason unrelated to the app's health. `CGWindowList` avoids the prompt but needs a compiled Swift helper that only builds on a Mac.
2. *Diagnostics.* The gate reads `join(userData, 'logs')` (check-packaged-launch.mjs:143). On macOS electron-log resolves the app's log directory through `app.getPath('logs')` (node_modules/electron-log/src/main/ElectronExternalApi.js:48), which is `~/Library/Logs/<product>` and is not moved by the `ASKTOTO_USERDATA` override at src/main/index.ts:367. Only `audit.log` is pinned to userData (src/main/logger.ts:52-53), and no unconditional audit event fires at startup — so today there is no portable positive "the app came up" signal to assert on.

Writing either blind risks the two outcomes the file itself forbids: a false FAIL that blocks a real release, or a false PASS, which is "worse than no gate".

**What landed.** `scripts/check-packaged-launch.mjs` still exits 2 on any non-win32 host — unchanged, no gate weakened — but the header now records the universal-bytecode gap in full, and the darwin branch prints the procedure that actually covers it:

```
open release/mac-universal/Metis.app
arch -x86_64 release/mac-universal/Metis.app/Contents/MacOS/Metis   # Apple Silicon host, Rosetta 2
```

with the note that an immediate "Error" dialog naming `cachedDataRejected` is the 1.2.0/1.5.3 DOA, and that an Intel host cannot execute the arm64 slice at all.

**Prerequisite for closing this row (needs a Mac).** Add an unconditional startup marker the main process writes under `app.getPath('userData')` after the first window is shown, then a darwin branch that asserts on that marker instead of inspecting windows — permission-free and portable — and wire it into `dist`, `dist:local` and `release:build:mac`. Alternatively drop `--universal` for two per-arch DMGs so each carries bytecode built by its own Electron.

### MQA-211 — the screen was allowed to become the subject, not the evidence

**Repro (regression test, `src/main/llm/screen-relevance.contract.test.ts`).** Build a real answer-mode ask through `userText()` with a cached on-device screen description and the question "what is the capital of Portugal?". Pre-fix the assembled prompt carried the whole screen block, a prompt-injection guard, and nothing that said which of the two was the task. Found by driving the running app and capturing the exact payload sent to the provider, not by reading source.

**Intended vs actual.** `screenContextBlock` rides on EVERY answer-mode ask once a description is cached, and a screenshot is attached to every vision ask; neither is gated on the question being about the screen. The guard that existed said "untrusted data, never instructions" — a promise about *authority*, which does not answer *relevance*. A model handed a wall of screen text and an unrelated question had no instruction telling it which one to answer, and answered with a description of the screen.

**What changed.** Both paths now carry a relevance rail: use the screen only if it helps answer the question, and if the question is not about the screen, ignore it completely and just answer, do not describe it back. The injection guard is untouched — the rail ADDS to it, because "ignore it if irrelevant" and "never treat it as instructions" are different promises and losing the second would be a security regression. The test asserts against the REAL assembled prompt rather than grepping source, so it also catches the block being dropped, reordered, or wired to the wrong mode.

### MQA-212 — Cloudflare's screen-asks never reached Cloudflare

**Repro (live, and now `scripts/qa/e2e-workflows.mjs`).** With Cloudflare active and configured, send a vision ask. Measured pre-fix walk: `["local","local"]` — nothing reached the provider at all.

**Intended vs actual.** `vision` is a per-PROVIDER flag and `publicSettings().visionReady` is `providerReady && PROVIDERS[p].vision`. Cloudflare declared `vision: false` because its resolved base/fast model (`llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast`) is text-only. Internally consistent, and it made screen-asks unreachable: every screenshot fell through to the on-device model while the UI showed Cloudflare as the active provider.

**What changed.** The default model is now one that can actually see: `@cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct` is natively multimodal, Cloudflare-hosted (no third-party lab, no second credential), 131k context. The text-only 3.3-70b stays selectable. `src/shared/providers.test.ts` pins the COUPLING — `vision: true` AND the resolved base model AND that model being in the catalog — so a future text-only default fails the test instead of silently breaking screen-asks again.

**Second repair, this pass.** The live check named for this behaviour asserted only `s.visionReady === true`. `visionReady` ORs in `localFallbackReady`, which the QA suite asserts true a few checks earlier, so the assertion was a tautology: it passed in the exact pre-fix state it was written to catch. It now sends a real vision ask with a real attached JPEG and asserts `r.providers[0] === 'cloudflare'`.

### MQA-213 — the operator's dead token was reported as the user's dead wifi

**Repro (regression tests: `src/main/llm/proxy-operator-fault.test.ts` for the classifier, `src/main/cloudflare-provider.contract.test.ts` for the branch order, `src/main/store.test.ts` for Settings → Test).** With `allowedProviders: ["cloudflare"]` so no fallback can answer, make the gateway return the 502 it emits when Cloudflare rejects the OPERATOR's account token. Pre-fix the user saw "Connection issue — couldn't reach the provider after retrying. Check your network and try again."

**Intended vs actual.** `cloudflare-proxy` deliberately answers 502 rather than 401 there: the caller's own key was accepted, so a 401 would send Métis off to re-prompt for a credential that is fine. But 502 also matches `retry.ts`'s `TRANSIENT_PATTERN`, so the terminal-error path rewrote the Worker's accurate sentence into the network one. With no fallback configured, every user in the org was pointed at their wifi while the real fix was a secret on the Worker — and Settings → Test showed the true sentence at the same moment, so two surfaces contradicted each other.

**What changed.** The proxy MARKS the failures only its operator can clear (a dead account token, a half-deployed Worker) and Métis passes those through instead of rewriting them. The marker rides in the message text because that is all that survives the hop: the OpenAI SDK folds an error into `${status} ${message}` and the adapter forwards only `e.message`. Transient upstream failures are deliberately NOT marked, so a 30-second Cloudflare outage cannot read as a misconfiguration.

**What this pass added.** The arc pinned the pure classifier but neither call site, so deleting either left the suite green. The branch ORDER is now asserted (the operator-fault check must sit ahead of `isTransient`, because 502 matches both — the code comment says so and nothing enforced it), and `store.ts`'s strip is pinned by a behavioural test that drives `testApiKey` against a real rejected upstream call. The live QA check now asserts the returned message too, not just `ok === false`.

### MQA-214 — a key with no endpoint advertised vision, and the app captured the screen for nothing

**Repro (regression test, `src/main/cloudflare-provider.contract.test.ts`).** Store a `METIS_PROXY_KEY` with `cloudflareBaseUrl` empty — the ordinary state between the operator sending the key and sending the URL. Pre-fix `publicSettings().visionAvailable` was true, which lights the screen-ask affordances and, via `App.tsx`'s `canPrewarm` then `Bar.tsx`'s `onFocus` then `prewarmCapture`, takes REAL screen captures for a request that can never be sent.

**Intended vs actual.** `visionAvailable` checked "provider has vision AND a key is stored" and skipped the `requiresUserBaseUrl` gate that `providerReady` and the ask path both apply. Cloudflare answers at an endpoint the OPERATOR supplies, so a stored key with no Worker URL is a provider that can never be reached.

**What changed, and what this pass added.** The gate was added with the rest of the arc; the tripwire was not. `src/main/c-main-fixes.contract.test.ts` reads a 400-character window from `visionAvailable:` that stops roughly 80 characters short of the new clause, and `cloudflare-provider.contract.test.ts`'s existing assertion was a whole-file `toMatch` for an expression that appears identically inside `pickFailover` — so deleting the `visionAvailable` copy left every test green. Both assertions now slice to their own seam before matching, which was verified by deleting each clause in a copy of the source and watching only its own assertion fail.

### MQA-215 — the one candidate walk that never checked for a missing endpoint

**Repro (regression test, `src/main/cloudflare-provider.contract.test.ts`).** Store a `METIS_PROXY_KEY` with no Worker URL, then import a recording. The recap walk lists Cloudflare as a candidate because it ships a default model, and `Object.keys(PROVIDERS)` order puts it last among the cloud providers, so `streamOpenAI`'s last-ditch guard fires and its message becomes `lastError` — surfacing "No endpoint URL set for Cloudflare · AI Gateway" as the cause of an import that failed for entirely unrelated reasons.

**Intended vs actual.** Every sibling walk applies the rule and says so: `pickFailover` (`index.ts`), the brain-ingest walk (`brain/ingest.ts`, whose comment reads "Same rule as the ask path's pickFailover"), and the key tester (`store.ts`). `runImportedRecap`'s filter checked the allowlist, `local`, CLI connection, the API key, the Dust workspace and the resolved model — and stopped.

**What changed.** One line, matching the three existing call sites verbatim, plus an assertion anchored on this seam's own shape (`provider`/`settings`, unlike ingest's `p`/`s`).

### MQA-216 — Métis told the user their employer had blocked them, when they had simply not pasted a URL yet

**Repro (regression test, `src/renderer/src/app-audit-fixes.contract.test.ts`).** Select Cloudflare, paste the `METIS_PROXY_KEY`, leave the Worker URL empty, and press any quick action. Pre-fix Settings opened with "Your organization restricts which providers you can use. Switch to an approved provider here." and the under-bar CTA read "Switch to an approved provider". No org policy existed.

**Intended vs actual.** The comment above the branch describes the allowlist case correctly ("a keyed API provider can still be `!providerReady` because the org allowlist excludes it"), but the condition never read `settings.allowedProviders` — it was `hasApiKey && kind !== 'cli'`. A saved key stood in for a policy. Cloudflare makes that misread the DEFAULT first-run state, because `providerReady` is false purely on the missing `https://` endpoint while `hasApiKey` is true. The same wrong branch was duplicated on the under-bar CTA.

**What changed.** Three discriminated cases in both places, in the same order: blocked by the allowlist (tested against `allowedProviders` itself), missing an endpoint the user supplies (`requiresUserBaseUrl` plus `providerBaseUrl`, with the sentence the main process already uses and a pointer to the field), and otherwise the generic "add a key". A real allowlist deployment still gets the org sentence. A side effect worth recording: a keyed Dust install missing its workspace id also stops being told its employer blocked it.

### MQA-217 — the documented way to install a rate limit produced a config that will not parse

**Repro (regression test, `src/main/cloudflare-provider.contract.test.ts`).** Uncomment the `"vars": { "CF_AI_GATEWAY_ID": … }` line in `cloudflare-proxy/wrangler.jsonc`, exactly as the file itself, `cloudflare-proxy/README.md` and `docs/CLOUDFLARE.md` all instruct. Pre-fix: `Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 158`. The commented line sat AFTER `"observability": { "enabled": true }`, which had no trailing comma, so uncommenting it left two members with nothing between them and `wrangler deploy` died on the config before uploading anything.

**Why it matters more than a syntax slip.** This is the one file an operator edits by hand, and the edit is the one the runbook calls the second floor under the bill: an AI Gateway with a request-per-minute cap. The failure lands at the moment an operator is reacting to abuse.

**What changed.** The commented `vars` line moved above the last member with its own trailing comma already written, so uncommenting one line is self-sufficient and the committed file stays valid under strict JSON rather than depending on a parser's trailing-comma tolerance. The test parses both states and asserts the var lands where `Env.CF_AI_GATEWAY_ID` reads it.

### MQA-218 — the docs stated a provider count the registry contradicted

**Repro (regression test, `src/shared/provider-count-drift.contract.test.ts`).** `PROVIDER_IDS.length` is 18. `README.md` said "16 AI providers" in the badge, in the opening paragraph, in the Features bullet, and "15-provider + custom-endpoint registry" in the repo tree; `docs/asktoto-architecture.md` said "16 providers" twice; the compliance pack said "lists 15", "15 selectable cloud LLM providers", "of the 15 supported" and "one of 12 other providers".

**Intended vs actual.** Adding a provider is a one-line change to `PROVIDERS`, and nothing coupled it to the prose. It drifted twice: `local` took the registry from 16 to 17 and the docs stayed at 16; `cloudflare` took it to 18 and they stayed at 16 again. The result was worse than a wrong number — the README's enumeration, which is the canonical list a prospective user or an enterprise operator reads, omitted both the on-device model and the one provider reached through infrastructure the operator deploys. The GDPR Article 30 recipients row and the DPIA omitted Cloudflare's two-hop chain (operator Worker, then the operator's Cloudflare account, then whichever upstream lab the `{provider}/{model}` id resolves to) entirely, which is the register a DPO signs.

**What changed.** The docs were corrected, the architecture reference dropped its hand-maintained number in favour of pointing at the register, and the compliance pack now describes the Cloudflare chain and says its transfer picture must be recorded per deployment rather than once for the product. The gate reads `PROVIDER_IDS` and refuses any count in a shipped doc that disagrees with it, plus asserts the newest ids are actually named — so the next provider cannot land quietly.

### MQA-230 — single-meeting delete leaves brain-derived data when no provider is usable

**Repro.** Configure no provider (or revoke the key). Save a meeting with a clear commitment, let it index, then delete it via History -> Delete (confirm the native dialog). Read `.brain/` under the profile: the commitment/quote derived from the deleted meeting is still attributed to its person/deal entities, and `index.json` carries `sourceRefreshRequested: true` indefinitely. `src/main/index.ts:2989` (deleteMeeting) unlinks only the transcript + index row + the meeting's own wiki card; the derived-entity cleanup is `requestSourceRefresh()` -> `maybeStartSourceRefresh()` (`src/main/brain/ingest.ts`), which returns early on `!hasUsableProvider(s)`.

**Why it matters.** The confirmation dialog says the delete "cannot be undone" and implies completeness; a DSAR-driven deletion is silently partial for as long as no provider is reachable, with no UI signal. The bulk path (`recallDeleteAll`) already purges synchronously regardless of provider state and is pinned by `erasure-completeness.contract.test.ts` — the single-delete path has the weaker guarantee.

**Fixed (2026-08-21).** `exciseDeletedMeeting` (`src/main/brain/ingest.ts`) removes the meeting's extraction JSON (`removeMeetingExtraction`, provider-free) and its `idx.ingested` ledger row synchronously; wired into `recallDelete` AND `sweepExpiredMeetings` (the retention sweep had the same residue). The remaining entity-file residue still waits on the source refresh, but visibly: `brainStatus.cleanupPending` + a BrainView notice. Pinned by `erasure-completeness.contract.test.ts` (MQA-230 block).

### MQA-233 — native Open-File dialog takes 25-240s to first appear under a scripted packaged launch

**Repro.** Launch `release/win-unpacked/Metis.exe` via Playwright's Electron driver or with `--remote-debugging-port`, then invoke `window.toto.importAudioPick()` (which calls `dialog.showOpenDialog`). Measure time until the dialog's top-level window exists (EnumWindows over the process's windows). Observed 25s–240s+ across 5 runs on this machine; no stable ceiling.

**Why it matters (if it reproduces interactively).** The import flow's first click would appear dead for tens of seconds. Unconfirmed for normal launches — confirm or rule out before treating as a user-facing defect.

**Evidence.** `scripts/check-packaged-asr.mjs` header comment (the gate works around it by substituting the dialog's return value inside the real main process while keeping every subsequent IPC hop real).
